The current version has limited interface customization functionality, only supporting basic options like adjusting message font size, message style, and font style. This cannot meet users' personalized needs for interface presentation. If users wish to further customize the interface appearance, they currently must rely on the custom CSS injection feature provided by the software. However, this approach has obvious limitations. The process of writing and maintaining CSS code is tedious and presents a high usage barrier for users unfamiliar with front-end technology. More importantly, software updates may cause component structures or class names to change, causing users' self-injected CSS code to become ineffective and requiring them to troubleshoot and modify the code again. This unstable implementation method increases users' maintenance costs and cannot serve as a long-term reliable solution. Therefore, it is recommended that the official version provide richer native customization options in the settings interface, allowing users to complete interface configuration without relying on CSS injection. ### Desired Solution It is recommended to add the following customization options based on the existing interface settings: ### 1. **Avatar Display Control** - User avatar display toggle - Model avatar display toggle - --- ### 2. **Provider Name Display Control** - Whether to display provider names in the message area, such as OpenAI, Gemini, Anthropic, etc. - --- ### 3. **Message Background Display Control** - User message background display toggle - Model message background display toggle (the current version has no background for model messages, it is recommended to support user configuration) - - --- ### 4. **Message Timestamp Display Control** - User message time display toggle - Model message time display toggle - --- ### 5. **UI Component Spacing Adjustment** - Customizable top and bottom spacing for thinking component - Customizable top and bottom spacing for search component - The default spacing in the current version is quite large; it is recommended to support user adjustment according to preference - - --- ### 6. **Other Potential Options** - In addition to the above, it is recommended to continuously collect user feedback in subsequent versions and gradually open up more display and style configuration options for interface elements ### Alternative Solutions The currently available alternative solution is to achieve interface customization through the custom CSS injection feature provided by the software. Although this solution can meet some personalized needs, it has the following problems: - Users need to have certain CSS writing skills, with high learning costs - Maintenance of custom CSS code depends on users themselves, lacking official support - Software version updates may cause changes in component structures or class names, and the injected CSS code becomes ineffective and needs to be fixed by users themselves In comparison, providing native customization options officially can ensure the stability and ease of use of the feature. Users do not need to pay attention to underlying implementation details, nor do they need to worry about compatibility issues caused by version updates. ### Additional Information None ---

### Bug Description

(Generated by Kimi K2 Thinking with logs uploaded: )

Cherry Studio v1.7.18 experiences repeated Out-of-Memory (OOM) crashes in the Electron renderer process, forcing the application to restart. The crash signature is:

```json
{"reason":"oom","exitCode":-536870904}
```

**Root Cause:** Multiple memory leaks accumulate over time:
- Agent session messages grow indefinitely (observed up to 14+ messages per session)
- Failed tool call results and JSON parsing errors are cached but never released
- MCP server (SequentialThinkingServer) thinking logs are retained in memory
- Knowledge base file locks (EBUSY errors) prevent resource cleanup
- Long-running SDK queries (2+ minutes) hold memory without timeout/gc

**Impact:** Application becomes unusable after ~10-15 minutes of active agent usage, requiring manual restart. All in-progress agent tasks and session state are lost.

[app-error.2026-02-14.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/25310786/app-error.2026-02-14.log)

[app.2026-02-14.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/25310787/app.2026-02-14.log)

Execute a complex, multi-turn task involving multiple tool calls while performing a multi-turn web-search assistant.

[web search assistant prompt.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/25310778/web.search.assistant.prompt.txt)

### Expected Behavior

(Generated by Kimi K2 Thinking with logs uploaded: )
- Renderer process memory should stay below 500MB during normal usage
- Old session messages should be auto-truncated (e.g., keep last 5 messages)
- Failed tool calls should be garbage collected immediately
- MCP server logs should not accumulate in memory
- Renderer should implement memory pressure monitoring and trigger GC before OOM
- Application should gracefully degrade (show warning) instead of crashing

### Problems Encountered

As a user of Cherry Studio, I would like to customize the application's background picture to enhance my personal experience and create a more pleasant working environment. Customizable backgrounds can significantly improve user satisfaction and allow for personal expression within the application.

Currently, I have attempted to use the built-in CSS editor to implement background images, but this approach has several significant limitations and issues:

1. **CSS Complexity**: Implementing a proper background requires extensive CSS knowledge and trial-and-error
2. **Inconsistent Results**: Even with careful CSS styling, elements like the sidebar, settings panels, and message bubbles don't always display correctly with background transparency
3. **Maintenance Burden**: Custom CSS needs to be maintained across updates and can break when the application's structure changes
4. **Performance Issues**: CSS-based solutions may not be optimized for performance, especially with large background images
5. **Missing Features**: Basic features like image scaling, positioning, and opacity control require complex CSS workarounds

The main pain points include:
- Sidebar and UI elements not properly adapting to background transparency
- Text readability issues when background images have varying brightness/contrast
- No easy way to preview or adjust background settings
- Compatibility issues across different themes (light/dark mode)

### Desired Solution

I would love to see an official, user-friendly option to customize the background picture directly within Cherry Studio's settings. This would provide a much better experience than the current CSS workaround approach.

**Core Needs:**
1. **Simple Background Selection**: Ability to choose a background image from local files or via URL
2. **Basic Image Controls**: Options to adjust how the background displays (scaling, positioning, opacity)
3. **UI Adaptation**: The interface should automatically adjust to maintain readability and usability with custom backgrounds
4. **Theme Compatibility**: Background customization should work well with both light and dark themes

**Why This Would Be Valuable:**
- Makes customization accessible to all users, not just those comfortable with CSS
- Ensures consistent and reliable results across the entire application
- Provides a more polished and integrated user experience
- Reduces the need for users to maintain custom CSS code

**Considerations (if helpful):**
- A preview feature would be great to see changes in real-time
- Options to adjust background brightness/blur could help with text readability
- Default background options could provide inspiration for users

This feature would greatly enhance the user experience and make Cherry Studio more customizable and personal for all users. Thank you for considering this suggestion!

## Inter-Agent Coordination Question

I've been exploring Cherry Studio's autonomous agent capabilities, and I noticed the impressive scale of your user base (39k+ stars). With that many users, I'm curious about multi-instance coordination scenarios.

Have you considered coordination between multiple Cherry Studio agent instances? I'm specifically interested in cases like:

- Agents discovering each other's capabilities across different deployments
- Verifying outputs from unknown agents
- Persistent identity across sessions
- Cross-framework agent communication

I built [Agora](https://github.com/rookdaemon/agora) to explore this problem space. It's a coordination protocol with cryptographic identity, relay-based messaging (works behind NATs/firewalls), and a reputation system for trust.

Not promoting, genuinely curious: is this a problem space Cherry Studio users run into? If so, I'd be interested in collaborating on integration patterns.

### Platform

Windows

### Version

v1.7.19

### Is your feature request related to an existing issue?

Currently, the Quote feature in Selection Assistant works by adding a `> ` Markdown quote symbol to the beginning of each line of the selected content and appending `-------------` at the end. This implementation has the following drawbacks:

1. It disrupts the original formatting. For instance, code blocks are quoted into an absurd format like this:

```txt
> def estimate_token(file_path: str, MOONSHOT_API_KEY: str, moonshot_timeout=3) -> int:
>     import json
>     import urllib.request
>     import urllib.error
>     import socket
-------------
```

2. It wastes tokens. Every `> ` adds up to the total token count.

### Desired Solution

A possible solution is simple: change the implementation of the Quote feature to wrap the quoted content in XML tags, as shown below:

```txt
<quote>
def estimate_token(file_path: str, MOONSHOT_API_KEY: str, moonshot_timeout=3) -> int:
    import json
    import urllib.request
    import urllib.error
    import socket
</quote>
```

This approach is more predictable, aligns better with how LLMs process information, and saves tokens.

Note: It is best to use XML tags because they strictly distinguish between start and end markers. Using Markdown code blocks (```) lacks explicit start and end delimiters and is more susceptible to having its logic broken by the content being quoted.

目前Selection Assistant的Quote功能的效果是对选中的内容每行添加一个`> `markdown引用符号并在末尾添加`-------------`，这种实现方式有如下缺点：

1. 破坏原文格式。如代码会被Quote成以下荒谬的格式

```txt
> def estimate_token(file_path: str, MOONSHOT_API_KEY: str, moonshot_timeout=3) -> int:
>     import json
>     import urllib.request
>     import urllib.error
>     import socket
-------------
```

2. 浪费tokens。每个`> `都会增加总token数

---

解决办法很简单：把Quote的实现方式改成在被quote的内容前后加xml标签，效果如下：

```txt
<quote>
def estimate_token(file_path: str, MOONSHOT_API_KEY: str, moonshot_timeout=3) -> int:
    import json
    import urllib.request
    import urllib.error
    import socket
</quote>
```

### Platform

macOS

### Version

v1.7.19

### Bug Description

**Bug Description**

The Quick Assistant (macOS 15.1, build 24B83) invoked via the menu bar shortcut ⌘ + E behaves inconsistently:

1. When the HerryCStudio desktop app is **not minimized** and is in the foreground, the Quick Assistant dialog appears correctly on the first invocation.
2. On subsequent invocations with the same shortcut, the dialog flashes briefly and then disappears behind the active window.
3. If the desktop app is **minimized**, the Quick Assistant dialog appears on top of whatever window is currently active, regardless of which app is in the foreground.

Thus, the dialog only stays visible when the desktop app is both **unminimized** and **in the foreground**; otherwise it is hidden or disappears immediately.

**Steps to Reproduce**

1. Open the HerryCStudio desktop app on macOS 15.1.
2. Ensure the app is **not minimized** and is the active (foreground) window.
3. Press ⌘ + E. The Quick Assistant dialog appears.
4. Press ⌘ + E again (without changing any windows). The dialog appears briefly then vanishes behind the current window.
5. Minimize the HerryCStudio app.
6. Press ⌘ + E. The Quick Assistant dialog now appears on top of the currently active window, regardless of which app is in the foreground.

**Expected Behavior**

The Quick Assistant dialog should consistently appear on top of the active window each time the shortcut is pressed, independent of the desktop app’s minimized state.

**Observed Behavior**

The dialog’s visibility depends on whether the desktop app is minimized and in the foreground, leading to intermittent disappearance.


### Steps To Reproduce

1. Open the HerryCStudio desktop app on macOS 15.1.

4. Press ⌘ + E again (without changing any windows). The dialog appears briefly then vanishes behind the current window.

The Quick Assistant dialog should consistently appear on top of the active window each time the shortcut is pressed, independent of the desktop app’s minimized state.

## Is your feature request related to an existing issue?

Gemini 模型返回的 `thoughtSignature` 目前未被持久化存储。在请求时通过中间件注入了跳过验证的魔串，但在响应时 aisdk 解析出的 providerMetadata 被丢弃了。

## Desired Solution

将 Gemini 的 thoughtSignature 持久化存储到 MessageBlock 的 metadata 中：

1. **Chunk 层**：修改 `AiSdkToChunkAdapter.ts` 保留 providerMetadata
2. **类型定义**：修改 Chunk 类型（TextStartChunk/TextDeltaChunk/ThinkingDeltaChunk 等）添加 providerMetadata 字段
3. **Callbacks 层**：修改 textCallbacks/thinkingCallbacks 接收并存储 metadata
4. **存储层**：在 createMainTextBlock/createThinkingBlock 或更新时写入 metadata

## Alternative Solutions

暂无

**数据流问题**：
```
aisdk google provider
    ↓ (每个text-start/text-delta都有providerMetadata)
AiSdkToChunkAdapter.convertAndEmitChunk()
    ↓ (只取chunk.text，丢弃chunk.providerMetadata!)
CherryStudio Chunk
    ↓
textCallbacks/thinkingCallbacks
    ↓
MainTextMessageBlock/ThinkingMessageBlock (metadata未使用)
```

title: Feature Request: Per-Minapp Proxy with Partition Reuse (HTTP/SOCKS)
body:
# Feature Request: Per-Minapp Proxy with Partition Reuse (HTTP/SOCKS)

## Summary
Support assigning proxy behavior per mini-app webview, while maximizing session reuse:
- `inherit` (use global app proxy)
- `system` (OS proxy)
- `direct` (no proxy)
- `custom` (HTTP/SOCKS with optional bypass rules)

To avoid unnecessary session explosion, webview partitions should be reused by **proxy profile** instead of by app id.

## Problem / Motivation
Today, mini-app webviews effectively share one session/proxy context. This makes it impossible to:
- route only selected mini-apps through a proxy,
- mix proxied and non-proxied mini-apps reliably,
- isolate different proxy endpoints per workload.

A naive “one app = one partition” solution works functionally, but has higher memory/storage cost and weak reuse.

## Proposed Design

### 1) Proxy model (per mini-app)
Add per-mini-app fields:
- `proxyMode`: `inherit | custom | system | direct`
- `proxyUrl?: string` (for custom mode)
- `proxyBypassRules?: string`

Semantics:
- `inherit`: follow global app proxy settings
- `custom`: use `fixed_servers` with `proxyUrl` + optional bypass rules
- `system`: Chromium `system` mode
- `direct`: Chromium `direct` mode

### 2) Partition reuse strategy
Compute partition by proxy profile, not by app id:
- `inherit` -> `persist:webview` (existing shared partition)
- `system` -> `persist:webview:proxy:system`
- `direct` -> `persist:webview:proxy:direct`
- `custom` -> `persist:webview:proxy:<hash(proxyUrl + normalizedBypassRules)>`

This yields:
- same proxy profile => same partition/session (reuse)
- different proxy profiles => isolated sessions (correctness)

### 3) Apply proxy before navigation
Before assigning `webview.src`, configure partition proxy via IPC in main process:
- renderer sends `{ partition, proxyConfig }`
- main process calls `session.fromPartition(partition).setProxy(proxyConfig)`
- then load URL

### 4) Persistence
Store per-mini-app proxy overrides in a dedicated local file:
- `minapp-proxy-overrides.json`

Load flow:
1. load built-in + custom mini-apps
2. apply proxy overrides by app id

### 5) UI / UX
In mini-app context menu, add **Proxy Settings** dialog:
- Mode selector (inherit/custom/system/direct)
- custom proxy URL input (HTTP/SOCKS)
- bypass rules input (optional)

Validation:
- `custom` mode requires URL with scheme (`http://`, `https://`, `socks5://`, etc.)

### 6) Compatibility
- Existing users default to `inherit` (no behavior change)
- No migration needed; missing fields are treated as inherit

## Why This Design
Compared to per-app partitions:
- lower memory/storage overhead
- better cookie/cache reuse for apps sharing same proxy profile
- preserves isolation when proxy profiles differ

Compared to one global partition:
- supports mixed proxied / non-proxied usage
- avoids proxy leakage between unrelated mini-apps

## Risks & Mitigations
- **Partition proliferation** if many unique custom proxies
  - acceptable and bounded by actual user configs
  - can add optional cleanup later for stale proxy partitions
- **User confusion about effective routing**
  - can add future debug tooltip showing current partition + proxy mode

## Acceptance Criteria
- User can configure proxy mode per mini-app.
- Two mini-apps with same custom proxy share one partition.
- Mini-apps with different proxy profiles are isolated.
- `inherit` mini-apps continue to use existing global behavior.
- Build/typecheck/tests pass.

## Optional Future Enhancements
- UI indicator: show effective partition/proxy mode in toolbar.
- “Apply to selected mini-apps” batch operation.
- Partition housekeeping for orphaned proxy partitions.

However, it completely **fails to pass the actual image data to the LLM**. Instead of sending the base64 image payload in the API request to the model, Cherry Studio strips the image data and replaces it with a literal text placeholder: `[Image: image/jpeg]`. As a result, the LLM is completely blind to the image generated/read by the tool. ### Screenshots ### Steps To Reproduce 1. Connect an MCP tool that reads or generates images and returns them as `image` content blocks (e.g., my custom markdown reader: https://github.com/YifeiDevs/mcp-file-reader). 2. Prompt the LLM with the following request: ```text Use file-reader’s `read_markdown` with `include_images=true` to open `D:\Ivey\Pictures\image_test\test.md`. Then, based ONLY on what you actually see in the tool output (not on how Markdown would normally render), report: 1) The exact text content shown. 2) Whether an image is displayed, what it depicts. 3) Where the image appears relative to the text in the tool output (e.g., after which line/paragraph, or at the end). ``` 3. Observe the Tool Response captured in the Cherry Studio UI. It shows that the actual image data was replaced by a text string `[Image: image/jpeg]`: ```text file-reader : read_markdown Arguments md_path: D:\Ivey\Pictures\image_test\test.md include_images: true --- Response this is a cat: ![](pic.jpeg) [Image: image/jpeg] the black cat ``` 4. Look at the LLM's final answer. Because the LLM only received the literal string `[Image: image/jpeg]`, it will state that it cannot see the actual picture (even though Cherry Studio's UI successfully renders the picture on the screen for the human user). ### Expected Behavior Cherry Studio should pass the actual image data returned by the MCP tool directly into the tool response payload sent to the LLM Provider. For example, when communicating with OpenAI-compatible endpoints, the MCP `image` block should be translated into a valid image content object in the messages array: ```json { "type": "image_url", "image_url": { "url": "data:image/jpeg;base64," } } ``` The LLM must be able to "see" the exact image the tool returned, just as the human user can. ### Actual behavior The image data is intercepted for UI rendering, but the LLM only receives a string placeholder `[Image: image/jpeg]` inside its context window. This breaks any multimodal MCP tools (like visual file readers, chart generators, screen scrapers, etc.). ### Relevant Log Output ```shell ``` ### Additional Context _No response_ ---

### Platform

Windows

### Version

1.7.20 

### Bug Description

In Cherry Studio version 1.7.20 (Windows 11 25H2), when using the MinerU knowledge base preprocessing feature to upload a PDF file, the upload consistently fails regardless of whether the API address is set to https://mineru.net or https://mineru.net/api/v4.

With API address set to https://mineru.net, the upload task hangs for about 5 minutes and eventually fails with the error "File not found in batch results". The log shows numerous warnings like Failed to check status for batch xxx, retry N/60, indicating that the file upload may not have been successful or the returned batch_id is invalid.

With API address set to https://mineru.net/api/v4, the upload fails immediately with errors "HTTP 404: Not Found" or "HTTP 405: Method Not Allowed".

After comparing with the official MinerU API documentation, it appears that the current implementation in the plugin deviates significantly from the required flow.

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Create a new knowledge base in Cherry Studio.

2. In the MinerU service configuration, test with both API addresses:

https://mineru.net

https://mineru.net/api/v4

3. Upload a PDF file that meets MinerU's restrictions (e.g., a medical textbook PDF of about 170 MB, page count under 600 pages).

4. Observe the upload result.

### Expected Behavior

1. The plugin should strictly follow the official MinerU API documentation for file upload:

2. Request upload URLs: Send a POST request to https://mineru.net/api/v4/file-urls/batch with the filename in the request body. The response should contain a batch_id and a list of upload URLs.

3. Upload the file: Use the obtained URL to upload the file via the PUT method (no additional headers required).

4. Poll for results: Poll the status using GET https://mineru.net/api/v4/extract-results/batch/{batch_id} until the state becomes done or failed.

After successful parsing, the knowledge base should display the file normally for subsequent queries.

### Relevant Log Output

```shell
When API address is https://mineru.net/api/v4:

log
{"level":"error","message":"Failed to get batch upload URLs: HTTP 404: Not Found","module":"MineruPreprocessProvider"...}
{"level":"error","message":"Failed to upload file: HTTP 405: Method Not Allowed","stack":"Error: HTTP 405: Method Not Allowed\\n    at MineruPreprocessProvider.getBatchUploadUrls ..."}

When API address is https://mineru.net:

log
{"level":"warn","message":"Failed to check status for batch xxx, retry 60/60",...}
{"level":"error","message":"MinerU preprocess processing failed for: File not found in batch results"...}
```

### Additional Context

Cherry Studio version: 1.7.20 (auto-update enabled)

Operating system: Windows 11 Home, version 25H2, OS build 26200.7840, Windows Feature Experience Pack 1000.26100.291.0

MinerU service configuration: Valid token is correctly filled; both API addresses were tested.

Official website works: The same PDF file uploaded via the MinerU official website succeeds, and the daily parsing page count updates accordingly, confirming that the account, file, and server are all functional.

Workarounds:

Use a Python script to manually implement the correct upload flow (already successfully tested).

Or download the parsed Markdown files from the official website and place them directly into the local knowledge base folder (...\\KnowledgeBase\\<knowledgeBaseID>\\) to let Cherry Studio index them.

Possible cause: MinerU's official API may have been updated recently (e.g., now requiring the /api/v4 path), but the MinerU plugin in Cherry Studio has not been updated accordingly, still using old hardcoded paths and an incorrect upload flow.

Thank you for looking into this issue.

3.上传文件：使用获得的链接通过 PUT 方法上传文件（无需额外 Header）。

4.轮询结果：通过 GET https://mineru.net/api/v4/extract-results/batch/{batch_id} 获取解析状态，直到状态变为 done 或 failed。

```shell
log
{"level":"warn","message":"Failed to check status for batch xxx, retry 60/60",...}
{"level":"error","message":"MinerU preprocess processing failed for: File not found in batch results"...}
```

### Additional Context

Cherry Studio 版本：1.7.20（启用了自动更新）

操作系统：Windows 11 家庭中文版，版本号 25H2，操作系统版本 26200.7840

临时解决方案：

使用 Python 脚本手动实现标准上传流程（已成功验证）。

或直接在官网下载解析后的 Markdown 文件，将其放入 Cherry Studio 知识库的本地文件夹（...\\KnowledgeBase\\<知识库ID>\\），让 Cherry Studio 自行索引。

可能的原因：MinerU 官方 API 近期可能有更新（例如要求使用 /api/v4 路径），但 Cherry Studio 的 MinerU 插件未同步更新，仍使用旧的硬编码路径和错误的上传流程。

希望开发者能尽快修复，感谢！

### Platform
macOS

### Version
latest

### Bug Description

In the plugin browser page (PluginBrowser.tsx), the plugin installation state management has several issues related to asynchronous operations and React component lifecycle.

**Root Cause**: The `actioningPlugin` state uses a single `string | null` type, which cannot properly track:
1. Multiple concurrent installation operations
2. Installation state after component unmount

Related code location: `src/renderer/src/pages/settings/AgentSettings/components/PluginsSettings/components/PluginBrowser.tsx:54`

```typescript
const [actioningPlugin, setActioningPlugin] = useState<string | null>(null)
```

#### Issue 1 - Concurrent Installations (UI Only)
When a user quickly clicks install buttons for multiple plugins in succession, only the last-clicked plugin shows a loading state. However, the earlier installation continues to run in the background (not cancelled).

#### Issue 2 - Component Unmount - Most Critical
When the user navigates away while an installation is in progress:

1. **Scenario A** (Works correctly):
   - User starts installation → installation completes in background → user returns → sees "Installed" ✓

2. **Scenario B** (Problematic):
   - User starts installation → user navigates away (component unmounts) → installation still in progress → user returns
   - Sees **Install button** (not loading state!)
   - User thinks installation was cancelled → clicks Install again
   - **Result: Two installation tasks running simultaneously!** ← This causes the most user confusion

This is a serious UX issue because:
- User sees "Install button" and assumes the operation was cancelled
- User triggers another installation, causing duplicate operations
- May lead to race conditions, duplicate files, or unexpected behavior

### Steps To Reproduce

**For Issue 2 (Component Unmount - Critical)**:
1. Open the plugin browser in settings
2. Click the install button of a plugin
3. Immediately navigate to a different page (causing PluginBrowser to unmount)
4. Wait a few seconds (but not long enough for installation to complete)
5. Navigate back to the plugin browser
6. Observe: You see the "Install" button, not a loading state
7. Click the Install button again
8. Now you have two concurrent installation operations!

### Expected Behavior

1. When user returns to the plugin browser after navigating away:
   - If installation completed: Show "Installed" state
   - If installation is still in progress: Show loading state (NOT install button!)
   - If installation failed: Show error state

2. When installing multiple plugins:
   - Each plugin should show its own loading state
   - User should be able to see all ongoing operations

### Additional Context

Recommended solutions:
1. Change `actioningPlugin` from `string | null` to `Set<string>` to track multiple concurrent operations
2. Persist installation state (e.g., in Redux store) so it survives component unmount
3. When component mounts, check for any in-progress installations and restore the loading state
4. Optionally: Use AbortController to cancel in-flight operations when component unmounts

### Bug Description

In the PluginBrowser component (`PluginBrowser.tsx`), when uninstalling a plugin that is part of a plugin package (e.g., a package containing multiple skills), only a single skill is uninstalled instead of the entire package.

**Root Cause**: The `handleUninstall` function in `PluginBrowser.tsx` always calls `onUninstall(filename, type)` without checking if the plugin belongs to a package. It should call `onUninstallPackage(packageName)` when the plugin has a `packageName`.

**Expected Behavior**: When uninstalling a plugin that belongs to a package, the entire package should be uninstalled (all skills/plugins in that package), not just the single item.

**Current Behavior** (buggy):
- User clicks uninstall on a plugin that is part of a package
- Only that single plugin/skill is uninstalled
- The rest of the package remains installed

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Install a plugin package that contains multiple skills (e.g., `agent-sdk-dev`)
2. Go to the plugin browser in settings
3. Find one of the skills from that package
4. Click the uninstall button
5. Observe: Only that single skill is uninstalled, not the entire package

### Expected Behavior

When uninstalling a plugin that belongs to a package:
- Either uninstall the entire package at once, OR
- Show a confirmation dialog asking if user wants to uninstall the single item or the entire package

### Additional Context

#### Architecture Issue

This bug highlights a deeper architecture problem: **`InstalledPluginsList` and `PluginBrowser` have duplicated but inconsistent plugin management logic**.

The `InstalledPluginsList` component already has the correct logic:
- It groups plugins by `packageName`
- It has a separate "Uninstall Package" button that calls `uninstallPackage`
- It distinguishes between single plugin uninstall and package uninstall

But `PluginBrowser` lacks this logic entirely.

#### Recommended Architecture Fix

Instead of fixing this bug in two places separately, consider creating a **shared hook or utility** that both components can use:

```typescript
// Proposed: shared hook usePluginUninstallLogic
const { handleUninstall, handleUninstallPackage } = usePluginUninstallLogic({
  onUninstall: (filename, type) => Promise<void>,
  onUninstallPackage: (packageName) => Promise<void>
})
```

This would ensure:
1. Consistent behavior between both components
2. Single source of truth for plugin management logic
3. Easier maintenance and testing

Related code location:
- `src/renderer/src/pages/settings/AgentSettings/components/PluginsSettings/components/PluginBrowser.tsx`
- `src/renderer/src/pages/settings/AgentSettings/components/PluginsSettings/components/InstalledPluginsList.tsx` (for reference - correct implementation)

### Platform
macOS

### Version
latest

### Bug Description

In the PluginBrowser component, after successfully installing a plugin, the loading button does not change to "Uninstall" - it changes back to "Install" instead. This is caused by the installed state not being refreshed in time.

### Root Cause

The root cause is in `usePlugins.ts`, in the `executeAction` function:

```typescript
const executeAction = useCallback(
  async <TResult>(...): Promise<...> => {
    setLoading(true)
    try {
      const result = await action()
      if (result.success) {
        onSuccess?.()  // Called WITHOUT await!
        return { success: true, data: result.data as TResult }
      }
      // ...
    } finally {
      setLoading(false)
    }
  },
  [onSuccess]
)
```

The `onSuccess?.()` (which calls `refresh()`) is called **without await**, so when `handleInstall` awaits `onInstall()`, it only waits for the installation API to complete, not for the refresh to finish.

**Timeline of the bug**:
1. User clicks Install → `setLoading(true)` in `handleInstall`
2. `await onInstall()` completes → installation API done, but `refresh()` still running
3. `setLoading({ id: loadingKey, value: false })` executes immediately
4. At this point, `installedPlugins` still has old data (refresh not complete)
5. `isPluginInstalled(plugin)` returns `false`
6. Button shows "Install" instead of "Uninstall"

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Go to the plugin browser in settings
2. Find a plugin that is not installed
3. Click the Install button
4. Observe: After installation completes, the button changes back to "Install" instead of showing "Uninstall"

### Expected Behavior

After successful installation, the button should change to "Uninstall" to indicate the plugin is now installed.

### Additional Context

The same issue likely exists for uninstall operations.

### Suggested Fix

In `src/renderer/src/hooks/usePlugins.ts`, change `executeAction` to await `onSuccess?.()`:

```typescript
if (result.success) {
  await onSuccess?.()  // Add await here!
  return { success: true, data: result.data as TResult }
}
```

This ensures that when `onInstall()` returns, the `refresh()` has already completed, and `installedPlugins` will have the latest data.

Related code location:
- `src/renderer/src/hooks/usePlugins.ts:59-80` (executeAction function)
- `src/renderer/src/pages/settings/AgentSettings/components/PluginsSettings/components/PluginBrowser.tsx:181-193`

title: [Feature]: Support Cohere Rerank provider or customizable rerank request/response mapping
body:
### Platform
Windows

### Version
v1.7.x (current stable)

I need to use Cohere Rerank for Knowledge Base / RAG.

I searched existing issues and found related but not exact requests:
- #68 (model provider collection, mentions Cohere)
- #290 (request to add Cohere AI)
- #1056 (request Cohere API support)
- #8790 (Cohere compatibility issue)

I did not find a dedicated request for **Cohere Rerank provider support** or for a fully **customizable rerank request/response mapping**.

### Desired Solution
Please consider either of these solutions:

1. Native Cohere Rerank provider support
- Add official Cohere Rerank integration (for example /v2/rerank)
- Built-in mapping for query, documents, 	op_n, and relevance score parsing

2. Advanced custom rerank adapter (more general)
- Customizable request URL path (not hardcoded to /v1/rerank)
- Customizable HTTP method and headers
- Customizable request body template (map internal fields to provider format)
- Customizable response mapping (map index/score fields to Cherry expected format, e.g. JSONPath/JMESPath)
- A Test Request button with request/response preview

This would make many rerank providers usable without building a local proxy translator.

### Alternative Solutions
Current workaround is running a local proxy to transform URL/body/response formats. It works, but adds extra complexity and maintenance overhead.

### Additional Information
Example Cohere rerank payload pattern:

`json
POST /v2/rerank
{
  "model": "rerank-v3.5",
  "query": "...",
  "documents": ["doc1", "doc2"],
  "top_n": 5
}
`

Typical response contains ranked results with document index and relevance score.

- [x] I've filled in short, clear headings so that developers can quickly identify a rough idea of what to expect when flipping through the list of issues. And not "a suggestion", "stuck", etc.
- [x] I've confirmed that I am using the latest version of Cherry Studio.

### Platform

macOS

### Version

v1.7.23

### Bug Description

The API Server (`src/main/apiServer`) does not apply any `apiHost` formatting when reading provider configurations from the Redux store. This causes requests to be sent to incorrect paths, resulting in 404 errors from upstream providers.

**Root Cause:**

In `src/main/apiServer/utils/index.ts`, `getAvailableProviders()` reads providers directly from the Redux store without formatting their `apiHost`. When the OpenAI SDK client is created in `resolveProviderContext()`, the raw unformatted `apiHost` is passed as `baseURL`:

```typescript
// Current (broken): apiHost is used as-is
const client = new OpenAI({
  baseURL: provider.apiHost,  // e.g., "http://localhost:11434" — missing /v1!
  apiKey: provider.apiKey
})
```

The renderer-side (`aiCore`) always calls `adaptProvider()` → `formatProviderApiHost()` before using a provider, which normalizes the `apiHost` (e.g., appending `/v1` for OpenAI-compatible providers). The API Server skips this step entirely.

**Inconsistency:**

| Context | Behavior |
|---------|---------|
| Renderer (aiCore) | Calls `formatProviderApiHost()`, appends `/v1` → requests go to `/v1/chat/completions` ✅ |
| API Server (main) | Uses raw `apiHost` from Redux store → requests go to `/chat/completions` ❌ |

**Additional Finding:**

`formatVertexApiHost()` in `src/renderer/src/utils/api.ts` unnecessarily reads `project` and `location` from `store.getState().llm.settings.vertexai`, even though `VertexProvider` type already contains `project` and `location` fields directly. This store dependency can be eliminated, making the function a pure function suitable for sharing.

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Enable API Server in Cherry Studio settings
2. Add a provider configured as OpenAI-compatible (e.g., Ollama with `apiHost = http://localhost:11434`)
3. Send a `POST /v1/chat/completions` request to the API Server with model `<provider-id>:<model-id>`
4. Observe 404 error

### Expected Behavior

The API Server should apply the same `apiHost` formatting as the renderer-side `adaptProvider()` / `formatProviderApiHost()`. For OpenAI-compatible providers, `http://localhost:11434` should be normalized to `http://localhost:11434/v1` before creating the OpenAI SDK client.

### Relevant Log Output

```
# Cherry Studio API Server log
{"error":{"headers":{},"requestID":null,"status":404},"level":"error","message":"Error processing streaming chat completion","model":"107a079e-a151-4795-b887-5c75737c222e:qwen3:0.6b","timestamp":"2026-03-04 12:06:07"}
{"error":{"headers":{},"requestID":null,"status":404},"level":"error","message":"Chat completion error","timestamp":"2026-03-04 12:06:07"}

# Ollama server log (confirms wrong path received)
[GIN] 2026/03/04 - 12:06:07 | 404 |      18.041µs |  127.0.0.1 | POST  "/chat/completions"
[GIN] 2026/03/04 - 12:06:22 | 200 |   2.98832025s |  127.0.0.1 | POST  "/v1/chat/completions"
```

### Additional Context

Related to #13188 — that issue describes a user failing to use the API Server with an Ollama provider. The `provider_not_found` error seen there and the 404 seen here share the same underlying cause: the API Server does not normalize provider configuration the same way the renderer does.

**Proposed Fix:**

Extract shared pure functions (no store dependency) into a new `packages/shared/aiCore/provider.ts`:
- `formatProviderApiHost(provider)` — covers all provider types including vertex (using `VertexProvider.project`/`.location` fields directly instead of store)
- `formatOllamaApiHost`, `formatAzureOpenAIApiHost`, `formatVertexApiHost` (refactored as pure functions)
- `isOllamaProvider`, `isAnthropicProvider`, etc.

Then in `src/main/apiServer/utils/index.ts`, apply formatting in `getAvailableProviders()`:

```typescript
import { formatProviderApiHost } from '@shared/aiCore/provider'

const formattedProviders = supportedProviders.map((p) => formatProviderApiHost(p))
CacheService.set(PROVIDERS_CACHE_KEY, formattedProviders, PROVIDERS_CACHE_TTL)
return formattedProviders
```

**Files to modify:**
- `packages/shared/aiCore/provider.ts` ← new file
- `src/renderer/src/utils/api.ts` ← re-export from shared
- `src/renderer/src/utils/provider.ts` ← re-export from shared
- `src/renderer/src/aiCore/provider/providerConfig.ts` ← import from shared
- `src/main/apiServer/utils/index.ts` ← apply `formatProviderApiHost`

title: [Bug]: VertexAI Provider Data Storage Architecture Flaw - Type Mismatch with Actual Storage
body:
> [!NOTE]
> This issue was translated by Claude.

## Bug Description

The VertexAI Provider object stored in Redux has a fundamental type mismatch with the `VertexProvider` type definition! This leads to code relying on false type assertions and complex runtime mappings.

### Problem Symptoms

1. **Type System Lies** - The `isVertexProvider()` function only checks the `type` field but claims to return a `VertexProvider` type containing `googleCredentials` and `project` fields
2. **Scattered Data Storage** - VertexAI configuration is stored in two places:
   - Provider object in `llm.providers[]` (basic configuration)
   - `llm.settings.vertexai` (sensitive configuration)
3. **Inconsistent Field Naming** - Redux state uses `serviceAccount`/`projectId`, but type definitions expect `googleCredentials`/`project`
4. **Manual Mapping Required** - All code using VertexAI must call `createVertexProvider()` for mapping, which is error-prone

### Proof

The following code locations all require defensive checks or explicit mapping, indicating the type system is untrustworthy:

- `src/renderer/src/utils/provider.ts:159-161` - `isVertexProvider()` false type assertion
- `src/renderer/src/hooks/useVertexAI.ts:46-59` - Must call `createVertexProvider()` for mapping
- `src/renderer/src/aiCore/legacy/clients/gemini/VertexAPIClient.ts:26-30` - Needs to check if it's really a VertexProvider, otherwise manually map
- `src/renderer/src/aiCore/provider/providerConfig.ts:321-335` - Must call `createVertexProvider()` to get configuration

### Redux Actual Storage

```typescript
// Provider object in llm.providers[]:
{
  id: 'vertexai'
  type: 'vertexai'        ✓
  apiKey: string          ✓
  apiHost: string         ✓
  // ❌ Missing googleCredentials, project, location
}

// Real configuration is in llm.settings.vertexai:
{
  serviceAccount: {           // ❌ Should be called googleCredentials
    privateKey: string
    clientEmail: string
  }
  projectId: string          // ❌ Should be called project
  location: string
}
```

### Expected Behavior

VertexAI configuration should have a single source of truth, and the type system should accurately reflect the actual data structure!

## Steps To Reproduce

1. View the `VertexProvider` type definition in `src/renderer/src/types/provider.ts`
2. View the storage structure in Redux state `src/renderer/src/store/llm.ts`
3. Check the implementation of the `isVertexProvider()` function
4. Trace all code paths using VertexAI configuration

## Expected Behavior

1. The type system should accurately reflect the runtime data structure
2. VertexAI configuration should be stored in a single, consistent location
3. No complex mapping functions and defensive checks are needed

## Additional Context

This is an **architectural design flaw**, not a user-visible bug. But it leads to:
- Difficult code maintenance
- Easy to introduce bugs (type mismatch)
- Runtime performance overhead (mapping functions)
- Poor developer experience (type system cannot help developers)

Need to refactor the VertexAI Provider data storage architecture!

### Environment

- **Cherry Studio Version**: v1.7.23

### Description

Cherry Studio crashes or becomes completely unresponsive when an Agent performs file editing or file reading operations. The crash occurs with no error dialog and no log output in `%AppData%\CherryStudio\logs\`.

1. Create one or more Agents with access to filesystem tools (e.g. MCP filesystem)
2. Instruct the Agent(s) to read or edit a file
3. The application freezes or exits without warning

**Also observed**: Single Agent crashes during file read/write, though less consistently

### Expected Behavior

Agent completes file operations without crashing the application.

### Actual Behavior

- Application freezes entirely (UI becomes unresponsive)
- Or application exits silently with no crash dialog
- No logs generated in `%AppData%\CherryStudio\logs\`

### Additional Notes

- The crash appears correlated with file I/O operations specifically, not with general Agent activity
- Switching to conversation-only tasks (no file tools) does not trigger the crash
- Workaround: run Agents serially rather than concurrently, and isolate each Agent to a separate working directory

Suspect a race condition or file lock conflict in the Electron renderer process when multiple filesystem tool calls are in flight simultaneously. Could also be related to the file watcher triggering on concurrent writes.

### Platform

Windows

### Version

v1.7.23

### Is your feature request related to an existing issue?

Yes, it is related to the current limitation of the Selection Assistant.

At present, the Selection Assistant mainly provides explanation, translation, and search functions after text is selected. However, it does not support reading the selected content aloud.

In many scenarios—such as reviewing academic papers (PDF readers), reading technical documentation, or browsing long-form content—users may want to listen to the selected text rather than only reading or analyzing it. This is particularly useful when:

Reading long or complex paragraphs that require repeated exposure for comprehension.

Reviewing foreign-language materials where pronunciation and intonation matter.

Reducing visual fatigue during extended reading sessions.

Multitasking while continuing to consume selected content.

Currently, users must rely on external software to perform text-to-speech, which breaks workflow continuity and reduces overall efficiency.

### Desired Solution

I would like the Selection Assistant to support a built-in Text-to-Speech (TTS) function triggered directly after text selection.

Proposed behavior:

When text is selected and the Selection Assistant popup appears, add a “Read Aloud” or “TTS” button alongside existing options (e.g., Explain / Translate / Search).

Clicking the button will immediately start reading the selected content.

Provide basic playback controls:

Play / Pause

Stop

Speed adjustment (e.g., 0.75×, 1.0×, 1.25×, 1.5×)

Automatically detect language where possible, or allow manual language selection.

Optionally allow users to configure a default voice in settings.

From a technical perspective, this could be implemented using:

Windows native Speech API (SAPI), or

A lightweight local TTS engine, or

An optional cloud-based TTS service (if aligned with project architecture).

The key objective is seamless integration into the existing selection workflow without requiring additional applications.

### Alternative Solutions

Relying on system-level accessibility features (e.g., Windows Narrator).
This is not ideal because it reads broader screen content and is not tightly integrated with the Selection Assistant.

Using third-party TTS software.
This interrupts workflow and requires copy-paste operations or separate hotkeys, which reduces usability.

Exporting selected text to another module for reading.
This adds unnecessary steps and increases interaction friction.

Compared to these alternatives, direct TTS integration inside the Selection Assistant would provide a more cohesive and efficient user experience.

### Additional Information

This feature would significantly enhance accessibility and reading efficiency, especially for:

Academic users reading papers and PDFs

Users consuming foreign-language materials

Users who prefer auditory learning

Users experiencing visual fatigue

The addition of TTS would transform the Selection Assistant from a purely analytical tool (explain/translate/search) into a more comprehensive reading companion.

If helpful, I am willing to provide further clarification or usage scenarios to support design decisions.

title: [Bug]: API server chat completion validation rejects valid tool calling messages
body:
### Issue Checklist

- [x] I understand that issues are for feedback and problem solving, not for complaining in the comment section, and will provide as much information as possible to help solve the problem.
- [x] My issue is not listed in the [FAQ](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/issues/3881).
- [x] I've looked at **pinned issues** and searched for existing [Open Issues](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/issues), [Closed Issues](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20state%3Aclosed), and [Discussions](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/discussions), no similar issue or discussion was found.
- [x] I've filled in short, clear headings so that developers can quickly identify a rough idea of what to expect when flipping through the list of issues. And not "a suggestion", "stuck", etc.
- [x] I've confirmed that I am using the latest version of Cherry Studio.

### Platform

All platforms

### Version

v1.7.23

### Bug Description

The API server's chat completion validation in `ChatCompletionService.validateRequest()` (`src/main/apiServer/services/chat-completion.ts:128-156`) requires every message to have a non-empty `content` field:

```typescript
request.messages.forEach((message, index) => {
  if (!message.role) {
    errors.push(`Message ${index}: role is required`)
  }
  if (!message.content) {
    errors.push(`Message ${index}: content is required`)
  }
})
```

This validation is too strict for OpenAI-compatible tool calling workflows. In the tool calling message flow, certain messages legitimately have `null` or missing `content`:

1. **`role: "assistant"` with `tool_calls`**: When the model decides to call a tool, the response has `content: null` and the tool invocation is in the `tool_calls` field. When this message is sent back in subsequent requests, the validation rejects it.
2. **`role: "tool"` messages**: Tool result messages use `tool_call_id` and `content` to return results, but the `role: "tool"` is not recognized by the current validation logic.

As a result, any client using custom `tools` parameter in `/v1/chat/completions` cannot complete a multi-turn tool calling conversation, because the follow-up request containing the assistant's tool call message and the tool result will be rejected with a 400 validation error.

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Send a POST request to `/v1/chat/completions` with a `tools` parameter and a user message.
2. The model responds with `content: null` and a `tool_calls` array.
3. Send a follow-up request including the assistant message (with `content: null` and `tool_calls`) and a `role: "tool"` message with the tool result.
4. The API server returns 400: `"Message X: content is required"`.

### Expected Behavior

The validation should allow messages where `content` is `null` or absent when `tool_calls` is present (for assistant messages), and should recognize `role: "tool"` as a valid message role. The `tools` parameter and tool calling message flow should work correctly as per the OpenAI API specification.

### Relevant Log Output

```shell
HTTP 400: Request validation failed: Message 1: content is required
```

### Additional Context

The `tools` parameter itself is correctly passed through to the upstream provider via the `...request` spread in `prepareRequest()`. The issue is solely in the `validateRequest()` method being too restrictive. The fix should relax the `content` requirement when `tool_calls` is present on an assistant message.

Related code: `src/main/apiServer/services/chat-completion.ts` lines 128-156.

### Is your feature request related to an existing issue?

Related to #12850.

Currently, base64-encoded images returned by MCP servers are directly embedded into the message body as raw JSON strings. They are neither persisted as files nor uploaded as image files when calling LLM APIs. This causes MCP servers that produce image content (e.g., Playwright screenshot MCP) to fail in multi-turn conversations, as the image data bloats the message context and is not properly handled by the API.

### Desired Solution

Properly handle image content (`image` type) in MCP tool responses according to the [MCP specification](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/server/tools#image-content):

1. **Persist MCP image responses as files**: When an MCP tool returns image content (base64-encoded), save it as an actual image file (e.g., PNG/JPEG) to local storage instead of keeping it as a raw base64 string in the message.
2. **Upload images via API file format**: When sending messages to LLM APIs, include MCP-generated images using the proper image file/URL format supported by each provider (e.g., OpenAI's `image_url` content part), rather than embedding raw base64 JSON strings as text.
3. **Support multi-turn conversations with images**: Ensure that subsequent messages in a conversation can correctly reference and display previously generated MCP images without re-embedding the full base64 data.

body:

- [x] I've confirmed that I am using the latest version of Cherry Studio.

### Platform

Windows

### Version

v1.7.23 (This issue has stably reproduced every single day for the past 4-5 months across multiple updates)

### Bug Description

When using Cherry Studio, every single day after the time crosses midnight (12:00 AM), PDF files (especially image-based scanned PDFs) uploaded within a single chat session can no longer be read by the application. This bug reproduces stably 100% of the time every day and has persisted for 4-5 months. The issue remains until I restart the application to recover.
Specifically:

If I continue chatting in an existing single conversation with a previously uploaded PDF, the AI can no longer read it and replies, "You haven't uploaded any attachments."
If I start a new single conversation and upload a new PDF, the AI still fails to read it and gives the same response.
If I don't restart the app, standard text-only API chats still work perfectly, but all PDF files uploaded in any chat will be completely ignored.
Restarting Cherry Studio immediately restores the PDF OCR and reading functionality.
Note: This is not an isolated case. I have seen similar issues reported by others on GitHub where the AI claims no file was uploaded, but they remain unresolved.

Based on the error logs, the direct cause is an ENOENT, chdir error. Regarding why this happens exactly at midnight, I have two hypotheses:
The logs show: ENOENT: no such file or directory, chdir '...' -> 'C:\Users\HASEE\AppData\Local\Temp\CherryStudio'. This means the local OCR or file processor crashes when trying to change its working directory to the Temp folder.

Hypothesis 1 (External Factor): A Windows system task or a 3rd-party PC manager routinely cleans up the system Temp folder exactly at midnight. The directory is deleted, and Cherry Studio fails to dynamically recreate it.
Hypothesis 2 (Internal Factor): There is an internal bug within Cherry Studio's file processor or local OCR module related to the midnight date/time change. The cross-day event might trigger an internal state reset, causing the subprocess to lose its target directory or crash during the chdir operation.

### Steps To Reproduce

1 Open Cherry Studio, start a single chat session, upload a PDF (an image-based PDF is recommended to trigger local OCR), and chat normally.
2 Wait until after midnight (12:00 AM).
3 Try to ask a question about the existing PDF in the chat, or start a new chat and upload a new PDF.
4 Send the message. The AI will reply that it cannot see any uploaded files.
5 Check the logs, and you will see the ENOENT, chdir error.
6 Restart the application, and the functionality recovers.

### Expected Behavior

Regardless of whether the directory was deleted by the OS or lost due to an internal state reset, the fileProcessor (and local OCR module) should check if the temporary working directory (Temp\CherryStudio) exists before initializing or executing chdir. If it's missing, the app should automatically recreate it (mkdir) instead of throwing a fatal error and ignoring the files silently.

### Relevant Log Output

```shell
<info> [Inputbar] Starting to send message
jsx-runtime-BuWXMfFD.js:440 <info> [FileManager] Uploading file: {"id":"a58d80d4-7539-40cf-9bc6-e4418d2ae3d3","origin_name":"Time_Analysis.pdf","name":"Time_Analysis.pdf","path":"C:\\Users\\HASEE\\OneDrive\\文档\\Time_Analysis.pdf","created_at":"2025-09-26T07:19:41.163Z","size":62609,"ext":".pdf","type":"document","count":1}
jsx-runtime-BuWXMfFD.js:440 <info> [FileManager] Uploaded file: Object
jsx-runtime-BuWXMfFD.js:437 <warn> [fileProcessor] Failed to extract text from document Time_Analysis.pdf: Error: Error invoking remote method 'file:read': Error: ENOENT: no such file or directory, chdir 'C:\浏览器下载\Cherry Studio' -> 'C:\Users\HASEE\AppData\Local\Temp\CherryStudio'
processLog @ jsx-runtime-BuWXMfFD.js:437
jsx-runtime-BuWXMfFD.js:437 <warn> [messageConverter] File Time_Analysis.pdf could not be processed in any format
processLog @ jsx-runtime-BuWXMfFD.js:437

```

### Additional Context

Adding a simple fault-tolerance mechanism (fs.existsSync and fs.mkdirSync) before directory switching/extraction would likely solve this robustly and close several other "AI can't see my files" phantom bug reports on GitHub.

- [x] I've confirmed that I am using the latest version of Cherry Studio.

### Platform

Windows

### Version

V1.7.24

### Bug Description

1. 问题描述 / Bug Description
在使用 Cherry Studio 的“划词助手”时，若设置为按 Ctrl 键触发工具栏，在我的笔记本自带键盘上完全无法生效（即使按住不放也无法呼出工具栏）。
仔细排查后发现，这似乎与目前软件强制绑定 Ctrl 并且无法识别特定硬件底层按键信号有关。

2. 环境信息 / Environment

设备类型： 2025款联想 AI PC 笔记本（带有微软标准 Copilot 按键的新键盘布局机型）
操作系统： Windows 11
触发方式： 划词后按下 Ctrl 键
3. 排查过程与关键线索 / Troubleshooting & Key Clues
为了定位问题是否属于 Cherry Studio 的设置或系统环境，我做了以下“控制变量”测试，得出这是特定硬件键盘的底层信号问题：

🟢 外接普通键盘测试： 完美触发。在使用外接键盘时划词并按下左 Ctrl 键，划词助手正常弹出。
🔴 自带键盘测试： 无法触发。使用联想笔记本自带键盘的左 Ctrl 键，毫无反应。
🔴 底层注册表映射测试（SharpKeys）： 我怀疑是预装软件劫持，因此未安装任何后台全局热键软件（如 PowerToys 或 AHK），而是使用了最底层的修改系统注册表工具（SharpKeys）。
尝试1：将自带键盘的 Left Ctrl 映射为纯净的 Left Ctrl，无效。
尝试2：将自带键盘的 Left Ctrl 强制映射为 Right Ctrl，依然无效。


### Steps To Reproduce

1. 使用 **2025款联想带 Copilot 键的笔记本**（或其他新款联想 AI PC）运行 Cherry Studio。
2. 在设置中开启“划词助手”，并将触发模式设置为 **Ctrl** 键触发。
3. 在任意软件中用鼠标选中文本（划词）。
4. 按住笔记本**自带键盘**的 `Ctrl` 键 👉 **结果：无任何反应，工具栏未弹出。**
5. 连接一个外接键盘，同样选中文本并按下外接键盘的 `Ctrl` 键 👉 **结果：工具栏正常弹出。**

### Expected Behavior

4. 猜测与结论 / Hypothesis
结合你们在 Issue #6505 中的 FAQ 描述（排除了其它改键软件劫持），我推测病根在于：2025 款联想 AI PC 新增了 Copilot 键后，其键盘的底层固件/驱动（或 BIOS 级的防呆机制）对自带按键的信号进行了特殊处理或包裹。
由于 Cherry Studio 识别触发键的条件可能相对严格，导致这种带有硬件厂商“杂质”的 Ctrl 信号被过滤无法识别，而修改注册表又无法越过硬件物理层的屏蔽。

5. 建议与诉求 / Suggestions & Feature Request
目前普通用户无法在硬件上修改联想的驱动，强烈建议开发者在后续版本中：
优化底层按键事件的监听逻辑，兼容新款 AI PC 设备的硬件信号。

希望能帮助到开发团队复现和排查问题，期待后续版本的优化！

### Platform

macOS

### Version

v1.7.24

### Bug Description

When using the WebDAV backup feature, the backup succeeds on the first attempt. However, subsequent backup attempts fail with a **405 Method Not Allowed** error if the target directory already exists.
The backup only succeeds again after manually deleting the backup directory through the WebDAV server.
This suggests that CherryStudio is attempting to create the backup directory (`MKCOL`) on every backup operation, but does not handle the `405` response correctly when the directory already exists. Instead of ignoring the error and proceeding with file uploads, it stops the backup process.


### Steps To Reproduce

1. Configure WebDAV backup in CherryStudio settings:
   - URL: `https://***/dav/srv/`
   - Path: `/cherry-studio`
   - Username: `admin`
   - Authentication: API Token (Bearer Token)
2. Trigger the first backup → **Success**
3. Trigger the second backup → **Fails with 405 error**
4. Delete the `/cherry-studio` directory via Filebrowser Quantum Web UI(v1.3.0)
5. Trigger the backup again → **Success**

### Expected Behavior

If the backup target directory already exists, CherryStudio should:
1. Attempt to create the directory (`MKCOL`)
2. If the server returns `405 Method Not Allowed` (directory exists), **ignore this error**
3. Continue with uploading backup files and **overwrite existing files** as needed
This would allow incremental backups to work properly without manual intervention.

And not "a suggestion", "stuck", etc. - [x] I've confirmed that I am using the latest version of Cherry Studio. ### Platform Windows ### Version 1.7.24 ### Bug Description When the model provider is set to **Anthropic** (`/v1/messages` endpoint) and the model is **claude-opus-4-6**, the **"max tokens"** setting in the assistant's model configuration behaves incorrectly: 1. When the toggle is enabled and the value is set to `128000`, the actual `max_tokens` sent in the request becomes `25396` instead of `128000`. 2. When the toggle is disabled, the request correctly uses the default value of `128000`. 3. When the configured value is below `102605`, the API returns an error: > `Invalid argument for parameter maxOutputTokens: maxOutputTokens must be >= 1` This suggests that the code applies an additional subtraction (approximately `actual_max_tokens = user_set_value - 102604`) before writing the value into the request body, rather than passing the user-configured value directly. ### Actual Behavior | Action | Actual `max_tokens` in request | Result | |---|---|---| | Toggle ON, set to `128000` | `25396` (= 128000 − 102604) | Value incorrectly reduced | | Toggle ON, set to `102605` | `1` (= 102605 − 102604) | Value incorrectly reduced | | Toggle ON, set to `≤ 102604` | `≤ 0` | Error: `maxOutputTokens must be >= 1` | | Toggle OFF | `128000` | Correct | ### Steps To Reproduce 1. Create or edit an assistant. Set the model provider to **Anthropic** and select **claude-opus-4-6** as the model. 2. In the model configuration panel, enable the "max tokens" toggle and enter `128000`. 3. Send any message (e.g., "test") and inspect the actual request body via network capture or logs. 4. Change the value to `102604` or lower, send a message again, and observe the error. 5. Disable the "max tokens" toggle, send a message, and inspect the request body again. ### Screenshots **Scenario 1: Toggle ON + value set to 128000** (actual request sends max_tokens = 25396) > Settings UI: > Actual request body: ```json { "model": "claude-opus-4-6", "max_tokens": 25396, "thinking": { "type": "adaptive" }, "output_config": { "effort": "high" }, "messages": [{ "role": "user", "content": [{ "type": "text", "text": "测试" }] }], "stream": true } ``` **Scenario 2: Toggle OFF** (request correctly sends max_tokens = 128000) > Settings UI: > Actual request body: ```json { "model": "claude-opus-4-6", "max_tokens": 128000, "thinking": { "type": "adaptive" }, "output_config": { "effort": "high" }, "messages": [{ "role": "user", "content": [{ "type": "text", "text": "测试" }] }], "stream": true } ``` **Scenario 3: Toggle ON + value set to 102605** (boundary value) > Actual request body: ```json { "model": "claude-opus-4-6", "max_tokens": 1, "thinking": { "type": "adaptive" }, "output_config": { "effort": "high" }, "messages": [{ "role": "user", "content": [{ "type": "text", "text": "测试" }] }], "stream": true } ``` **Scenario 4: Error when value is below 102605** ### Expected Behavior | Action | Expected `max_tokens` in request | |---|---| | Toggle ON, set to `128000` | `128000` | | Toggle ON, set to `50000` | `50000` | | Toggle OFF | Model default (`128000`) | The user-configured value should be passed directly as `max_tokens` in the API request body without any additional calculation. ### Relevant Log Output ```shell ``` ### Additional Context ### 📋 Environment - **Cherry Studio Version**: 1.7.24 - **Operating System**: Windows 10 - **Model Provider**: Anthropic - **Model**: claude-opus-4-6 - **API Endpoint**: `/v1/messages`

title: [Bug]: OpenAI Responses MCP image tool results are stringified in toolCallId path
body:
### Issue Checklist

- [x] I understand that issues are for feedback and problem solving, not for complaining in the comment section, and will provide as much information as possible to help solve the problem.
- [x] My issue is not listed in the [FAQ](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/issues/3881).
- [x] I've looked at **pinned issues** and searched for existing [Open Issues](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/issues), [Closed Issues](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20state%3Aclosed), and [Discussions](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/discussions), no similar issue or discussion was found.
- [x] I've filled in short, clear headings so that developers can quickly identify a rough idea of what to expect when flipping through the list of issues. And not "a suggestion", "stuck", etc.
- [x] I've confirmed that I am using the latest version of Cherry Studio.

### Platform

Windows

### Version

1.7.24

### Bug Description

When using Cherry Studio with an MCP server that returns image content in tool results, the OpenAI Responses path appears to stringify the MCP result content in the `toolCallId` branch instead of preserving multimodal content as OpenAI-native image input blocks.

This becomes a problem for vision/computer-use style MCP servers that return screenshots or annotated images. In that case, the returned MCP content can contain image blocks like:

```json
[
  {
    "type": "image",
    "mimeType": "image/png",
    "data": "<base64>"
  }
]
```

But in Cherry's OpenAI Responses client, the `toolCallId` branch currently appears to convert the result into:

```ts
{
  type: 'function_call_output',
  call_id: mcpToolResponse.toolCallId,
  output: JSON.stringify(resp.content)
}
```

instead of a multimodal OpenAI-style structure such as `input_text` / `input_image`.

Relevant code location:

`src/renderer/src/aiCore/legacy/clients/openai/OpenAIResponseAPIClient.ts`

Current behavior in the `toolCallId` branch:

```ts
return {
  type: 'function_call_output',
  call_id: mcpToolResponse.toolCallId,
  output: JSON.stringify(resp.content)
}
```

Why I believe this is a bug or incomplete implementation:

- I verified that direct image input to OpenAI Responses works normally.
- I also verified that a simulated second-turn `function_call_output` containing `input_image` works normally.
- Token usage remains in the same range in both cases.
- The model can understand the image in both cases.

Example from my tests against an OpenAI-compatible upstream:

- Direct image input:
  - `input_tokens = 2561`
- Simulated `function_call_output + input_image`:
  - `input_tokens = 2595`

So OpenAI-style multimodal tool-result input itself appears to work correctly.

However, Cherry's current `toolCallId` handling seems to stringify MCP result content, which likely turns image blocks into text payloads (including base64 data), causing:

- unexpectedly large token usage
- potential context window blowups
- degraded multimodal behavior for MCP image tool results

Important nuance:
I understand Cherry may have compatibility concerns with some OpenAI-compatible providers. If this behavior is intentional for compatibility fallback reasons, clarification would be appreciated. But in the dedicated OpenAI Responses path, this currently looks like a bug or at least an incomplete provider-aware implementation for multimodal MCP tool results.

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Configure Cherry Studio to use an OpenAI-compatible provider that supports the Responses API.
2. Add an MCP server that returns image content in tool results. A simple example is a screenshot / computer-use MCP server that returns:
   - one text block
   - one image block (`type: "image"`, `mimeType`, `data`)
3. Start a conversation with an OpenAI Responses model such as `gpt-5.4`.
4. Ask the model to call the MCP tool that returns a screenshot image.
5. Let Cherry pass the tool result back into the next model turn.
6. Observe the following behavior:
   - token usage becomes much larger than expected for image-based tool results
   - image tool results appear to be treated more like serialized text payloads than native image inputs

Additional technical reproduction / evidence:

1. I inspected Cherry's OpenAI Responses implementation and found the `toolCallId` path in:
   - `src/renderer/src/aiCore/legacy/clients/openai/OpenAIResponseAPIClient.ts`
2. In that branch, Cherry currently returns:

```ts
{
  type: 'function_call_output',
  call_id: mcpToolResponse.toolCallId,
  output: JSON.stringify(resp.content)
}
```

3. I separately tested the same upstream outside Cherry:
   - direct image input works
   - simulated `function_call_output` with `input_image` also works
   - token usage is normal in both cases

This suggests the issue is not with OpenAI Responses image support itself, but with how Cherry maps MCP multimodal tool results back into the OpenAI Responses input format.


### Expected Behavior

In the OpenAI Responses path, when an MCP tool result contains multimodal content such as text + image, Cherry should preserve that content in an OpenAI-native multimodal form instead of stringifying the entire MCP result.

For example, image tool results should ideally be mapped into something closer to:

```json
{
  "type": "function_call_output",
  "call_id": "call_123",
  "output": [
    { "type": "input_text", "text": "..." },
    { "type": "input_image", "image_url": "data:image/png;base64,..." }
  ]
}
```

rather than:

```json
{
  "type": "function_call_output",
  "call_id": "call_123",
  "output": "[{\"type\":\"image\",\"mimeType\":\"image/png\",\"data\":\"...\"}]"
}
```

Expected outcome:

- image tool results remain true multimodal inputs
- token usage stays close to normal image-input levels
- image understanding works consistently in the next model turn
- MCP screenshot / computer-use style tools become practical to use with OpenAI Responses models

I may be missing some historical compatibility context here, so if this is intentional I would appreciate clarification. If maintainers agree this is a bug or incomplete implementation, I would be happy to help prepare a PR.

title: [Feature]: Support Multi-Agent Workflow and Collaboration
body:
### Issue Checklist

- [x] I understand that issues are for reporting problems and requesting features, not for off-topic comments, and I will provide as much detail as possible to help resolve the issue.
- [x] I have checked the pinned issues and searched through the existing [open issues](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/issues), [closed issues](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20state%3Aclosed), and [discussions](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/discussions) and did not find a similar suggestion.
- [x] I have provided a short and descriptive title so that developers can quickly understand the issue when browsing the issue list, rather than vague titles like "A suggestion" or "Stuck."
- [x] The latest version of Cherry Studio does not include the feature I am suggesting.

### Platform

Windows

### Version

Latest version

### Is your feature request related to an existing issue?

Currently, Cherry Studio primarily supports the development and debugging of single agents. When dealing with complex, multi-stage tasks, single agents face the following challenges and pain points:

- **Difficulty in task decomposition**: A single agent finds it difficult to simultaneously handle multiple roles such as global planning, specific execution, code writing, and test feedback, leading to excessively long contexts, confused roles, and low efficiency.
- **Lack of professional specialization**: Unable to simulate the specialized division of different roles (such as "product manager", "development engineer", "test engineer") in team collaboration, making it difficult to efficiently advance complex projects.
- **Limited interaction and simulation**: Difficult to build complex interactions, debates, or simulate multi-party environments between agents within Studio.
- **Cumbersome operations**: If you need to simulate multi-agent behavior, you can currently only manually switch agent configurations or orchestrate externally, then import the results back into Studio, resulting in a fragmented and inefficient process.

**Summary**: The existing single-agent mode limits Cherry Studio's capability in building complex, collaborative AI applications.

### Desired Solution

I hope Cherry Studio can introduce a comprehensive multi-agent management and orchestration feature.

**Core feature concepts**:

**Agent Pool Management**: Allow users to create, configure, and manage multiple agents. Each agent can be independently configured with:

- Name, description, role definition
- Base LLM model selection
- Dedicated toolset
- Independent memory module

**Multi-Agent Workflow Orchestrator**:

- Provide a visual drag-and-drop interface to define interaction processes between agents.
- Support sequential, branching, parallel, loop, and other flow controls.
- Define communication mechanisms between agents (such as message passing, shared context).

**Runtime and Monitoring**:

- Real-time display of multi-agent collaboration dialogues, Chain of Thought (CoT), and tool call logs.
- Provide detailed debugging functionality.

**Expected Benefits**:

- Greatly enhance the capability to handle complex AI tasks.
- Improve development efficiency and reduce dependence on external tools.
- Promote agent modularity and specialized design.

### Alternative Solutions

目前 Cherry Studio 主要支持单个智能体的开发和调试。在处理复杂、多阶段任务时，单个智能体面临以下挑战和痛点：
任务分解困难： 一个智能体难以同时兼顾全局规划、具体执行、代码编写、测试反馈等多个角色，导致上下文过长、角色混乱，效率低下。
缺乏专业分工： 无法模拟团队协作中不同角色（如"产品经理"、"开发工程师"、"测试工程师"）的专业化分工，使得复杂项目难以高效推进。
交互与模拟受限： 难以在 Studio 内部构建智能体间的复杂交互、辩论或模拟多方环境。
操作繁琐： 如果需要模拟多智能体行为，目前只能通过手动切换智能体配置或在外部进行编排，再将结果导回 Studio，流程割裂且低效。 总结： 现有单智能体模式限制了 Cherry Studio 在构建复杂、需要协作的 AI 应用时的能力。

### Desired Solution

我希望 Cherry Studio 能引入一套完善的多智能体管理和编排功能。 核心功能设想：
智能体池管理： 允许用户创建、配置和管理多个智能体。每个智能体可独立配置：
名称、描述、角色设定
基础 LLM 模型选择
专属工具集
独立的记忆模块
多智能体工作流编排器：
提供一个可视化拖拽界面来定义智能体之间的交互流程。
支持顺序、分支、并行、循环等流程控制。
定义智能体间的通信机制（如消息传递、共享上下文）。
运行与监控：
实时展示多智能体协作的对话、思考过程、工具调用日志。
提供详细的调试功能。 预期收益：
极大地提升处理复杂 AI 任务的能力。
提高开发效率，减少外部工具依赖。
促进智能体模块化和专业化设计。

### Platform

### Version

### Bug Description

This is a follow-up to #11177, also mentioned in #11710. The previous issue was closed by a stale bot, but the problem persists.

As of Cherry Studio v1.7.24, when using the POE API provider and enabling the [Web Search - Model Built-in] option for models like Gemini-3-Flash, the built-in web search does not take effect. The model behaves as if it has no internet access and states it is in 2024.

According to the official [Poe API documentation](https://creator.poe.com/docs/external-applications/openai-compatible-api) and my own API testing, Poe's OpenAI-compatible API supports `web_search` and `thinking_level` parameters. However, the documentation explicitly states that custom bot parameters must be passed using the extra_body field. Currently, it appears that Cherry Studio does not correctly map the built-in web search UI toggle to the extra_body field in the API request payload for Poe. **I tested the Poe API endpoints using a local script and confirmed that the parameters work perfectly when formatted correctly.** Refer to Additional Context for full log.

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Configure the POE API correctly in Cherry Studio.
2. Select a Poe model that supports web search (e.g., Gemini-3-Flash).
3. Enable the [Web Search - Model Built-in] toggle.
4. Ask a question requiring real-time internet data (e.g., "Summarize the news from the past week.").
5. Actual Result: The model fails to fetch the latest news and returns outdated information from 2024.

### Expected Behavior

When the [Web Search - Model Built-in] option is enabled, Cherry Studio should correctly pass the web_search: true parameter inside the extra_body object when calling the Poe API, allowing the model to retrieve real-time internet data.

| Source | Value |
|---|---|
| Fallback in code (`ToolsSettings.tsx:156`) | `"Pre-approved Tools"` |
| Actual i18n value (`en-us.json:287`) | `"Tools"` |

The current i18n value `"Tools"` is misleading because it implies the switches control **tool availability** (whether a tool can be used at all). - `src/renderer/src/i18n/locales/en-us.json:287`

4. The title "Tools" gives the impression that the switches control tool availability, but they actually control pre-approval permissions

### Expected Behavior

The section title should clearly communicate that the switches control **pre-approval** status, not tool availability. The i18n value should be updated to match the more descriptive fallback text (e.g., "Pre-approved Tools") across all locales, so users understand that:
- Enabled = tool runs without asking for permission
- Disabled = tool still works but requires user confirmation each time
