The fallback text `"Pre-approved Tools"` in the code actually describes the feature correctly — it was likely the original intended title. The i18n entry appears to have been simplified to just `"Tools"` at some point, losing the important semantic meaning.

title: [Feature]: Support disallowedTools with dual-switch UI to separate tool availability from permission control
body:
### Issue Checklist

- [x] I understand that issues are for reporting problems and requesting features, not for off-topic comments, and I will provide as much detail as possible to help resolve the issue.
- [x] I have checked the pinned issues and searched through the existing [open issues](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/issues), [closed issues](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20state%3Aclosed), and [discussions](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/discussions) and did not find a similar suggestion.
- [x] I have provided a short and descriptive title so that developers can quickly understand the issue when browsing the issue list, rather than vague titles like "A suggestion" or "Stuck."
- [x] The latest version of Cherry Studio does not include the feature I am suggesting.

### Platform

macOS

### Version

v1.7.24

### Is your feature request related to an existing issue?

Related to #13319 — the current Agent Settings "Tools" UI only exposes `allowedTools` (pre-approval), but there is no way for users to **disable specific tools entirely**.

Currently, users can only toggle whether a tool is "pre-approved" (auto-allowed without permission prompt). However, they cannot prevent a tool from being used at all. This creates confusion because:

1. The UI title says "Tools", implying availability control, but it only controls pre-approval
2. Users who want to restrict an agent's capabilities (e.g., disable `WebSearch` for providers that don't support it) have no mechanism to do so

### Desired Solution

Add support for the `disallowedTools` option that the Claude Agent SDK already provides, with a **dual-switch tool card** UI design.

#### UI Design: Dual-Switch Tool Card

Each tool card has **two independent switches**, cleanly separating availability from permission:

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Bash                                       │
│  Execute shell commands                     │
│                                             │
│  Enable    [====ON====]   ← availability    │
│  Auto-run  [====ON====]   ← permission      │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────┘

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Edit                                       │
│  Edit files with string replacement         │
│                                             │
│  Enable    [====ON====]   ← available       │
│  Auto-run  [---OFF----]   ← needs approval  │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────┘

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  WebSearch                                  │
│  Search the web                             │
│                                             │
│  Enable    [---OFF----]   ← fully disabled  │
│  Auto-run  [---OFF----]   ← (greyed out)    │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

| Switch | Controls | Maps to SDK |
|---|---|---|
| **Enable** (on/off) | Whether the tool is in the model's context at all | `disallowedTools` (off → add to disallowed list) |
| **Auto-run** (on/off) | Whether the tool runs without user approval | `allowedTools` (on → add to allowed list) |

- When **Enable** is off, the **Auto-run** switch is greyed out (a disabled tool can't be pre-approved)
- This makes the two concepts visually and functionally distinct — no more confusion

#### Backend Changes

1. **Database**: Add a `disallowed_tools` field to the agent/session schema (similar to the existing `allowed_tools`)
2. **Backend**: Pass `disallowedTools` to the SDK when creating a Claude Code session (in `src/main/services/agents/services/claudecode/index.ts`)

The SDK already supports this:
```typescript
// From @anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk sdk.d.ts
disallowedTools?: string[];
// "List of tool names that are disallowed. These tools will be removed
//  from the model's context and cannot be used, even if they would
//  otherwise be allowed."
```

### Alternative Solutions

- **Three-state single switch** (e.g., a segmented control with Disabled / Ask / Auto-run) — more compact but less intuitive than two independent switches.
- **Two-panel design** — one panel for "Available Tools" and another for "Pre-approved Tools". Clearer separation but requires more UI real estate.

### Additional Information

The Claude Agent SDK provides three levels of tool control:

| SDK Option | Semantics | Currently Used |
|---|---|---|
| `tools` | Defines which built-in tools are available (currently set to preset `claude_code`) | Yes |
| `allowedTools` | Auto-approve without permission prompt | Yes (`allowed_tools`) |
| `disallowedTools` | Completely remove from model context | **No** |

Exposing `disallowedTools` would give users fine-grained control over agent capabilities, which is especially important for:

- **Provider compatibility** — some providers' Messages API does not fully support native tool calls like `WebSearch` (e.g., Chinese providers such as Qwen, MiniMax). The tool call itself goes through without error, but returns empty results — the search finds nothing. This is worse than a clear error because the model sees the empty results and gets confused, often wasting turns retrying or misinterpreting the lack of results. Allowing users to disable such tools via `disallowedTools` would remove them from the model's context entirely, so the model never attempts these unsupported calls in the first place.
- **Safety-sensitive deployments** where certain tools should be entirely unavailable for specific agents

Related issues: #12950, #13319

title: [Feature]: Convert i18n Locale Files from Nested to Flat Key Structure
body:
## Background

Cherry Studio's i18n locale files are deeply nested JSON. To add or find a translation key, both human contributors and AI agents have to navigate multiple levels of nesting and reason about key paths from indentation. As Cherry's development increasingly relies on AI-assisted workflows, this nesting becomes a per-task friction point: every "translate this UI string" or "find what's missing in Spanish" task takes more steps than it should, and agents frequently mis-place keys under the wrong parent.

## Goal

Every translation key in every locale file lives at the top level of the JSON, so locating, adding, and reviewing a key is a single, unambiguous lookup for both humans and AI agents.

## Spec

- Every locale file in the project uses a flat key structure: each key is a dot-joined path (e.g. `settings.general.language`) at the top level of the JSON, with no nested objects.
- Every UI string that renders today still renders correctly after the conversion, in every supported language — no missing translations, no fallback to raw key strings or to English where a translation existed before.
- `pnpm i18n:sync` and `pnpm i18n:check` continue to work end-to-end on the new format and correctly identify missing or inconsistent keys across locales.
- The auto-translate GitHub workflow continues to keep `translate/*.json` in sync with the source `locales/*.json` after the migration.
- Adding a new translation key in the future is a single-line addition in each affected locale file.

## Verification

- Open Cherry Studio and switch through every supported language → every UI page renders all strings translated, with no raw `key.path.like.this` text leaking through and no unexpected English fallback for previously-translated strings.
- Open any locale file in a JSON editor → no nested objects; every line at the top level is `"some.key.path": "value"`.
- Search for a known key (e.g. `settings.general.language`) in any locale file → exactly one match.
- Add a new key `foo.bar.baz` in `locales/en-us.json`, run `pnpm i18n:sync` → key appears at the top level of every other locale file (with placeholder or auto-translation per existing workflow behavior).
- `pnpm i18n:check` reports zero missing-or-inconsistent keys immediately after the migration commit.
- Trigger the auto-translate GitHub workflow on a PR that adds a new key in `locales/` → workflow output writes the key in flat form into every `translate/*.json`.

title: [Feature]: Separate Agent into an independent module from Assistants
body:
## Background

Currently Agent and Assistant are mixed in the same list (`UnifiedList`). Users report difficulty finding the Agent entry. The two have significant differences in functionality, data models, and interaction patterns:

| Dimension | Assistant | Agent |
|-----------|-----------|-------|
| Interaction | Conversational, Topic-driven | Autonomous execution, Session-driven |
| Data Model | `Assistant` + `Topic[]`, Redux store | `AgentEntity` + `AgentSessionEntity`, API Server + SQLite |
| Tool Capabilities | Manual MCP configuration | Built-in MCP + Skill + allowed_tools |
| Message/Input Components | `Messages` + `Inputbar` | `AgentSessionMessages` + `AgentSessionInputbar` |

Issues caused by mixing:
1. Users cannot intuitively find the Agent entry, low discoverability
2. Two fundamentally different models forced to share list and tab switching logic
3. Selecting an Agent requires setting a fake assistant (`id: 'fake'`) to work around null issues

## Goal

Complete separation of Agent and Assistant:
- **Assistant page (`/`)**: Only shows assistant list + Topics + assistant chat
- **Agent page (`/agents`)**: Only shows Agent list + Sessions + Agent chat
- Both sides are independent with their own data and UI
- Agent has a **fixed tab in the top navigation bar** next to "首页" for quick access

## Design

### 1. Add: Sidebar Agent entry + Route + Page

Add `agents` entry to sidebar using `MousePointerClick` icon (lucide-react), navigates to `/agents`.

```
Sidebar:
┌──────┐
│ 💬   │ ← assistants (assistants only)
│ 🖱️   │ ← agents (agents only)
│ 🏪   │ ← store
│ ...  │
└──────┘
```

title: [Bug]: OpenClaw installation fails for nvm/Homebrew users — sudo retry cannot find node
body:
### Issue Checklist

- [x] I have searched through the existing issues and did not find a similar report.
- [x] I have provided a short and descriptive title.

### Platform

macOS

### Version

v1.7.24

### Bug Description

OpenClaw 一键安装在 macOS 上失败。安装过程中出现两个错误：

1. **第一次 npm 安装失败（exit code 243）**：Electron 内部 spawn 的 npm 进程异常退出
2. **sudo 重试失败（exit code 127）**：`@expo/sudo-prompt` 提权后，root 的 PATH 不包含 nvm/homebrew 路径，导致 `env: node: No such file or directory`

### Root Cause

`OpenClawService.ts` 中构造 sudo 命令时，没有将 node 所在目录注入 PATH：

```typescript
// 当前代码
const npmCommand = `"${npmPath}" install -g openclaw@latest`
// npm 的 shebang 是 #!/usr/bin/env node
// sudo 环境的 PATH 只有 /usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin
// 找不到 node → env: node: No such file or directory
```

### Fix

在 sudo 命令前注入 node 目录到 PATH：

```typescript
const nodeDir = path.dirname(npmPath)
const npmCommand = `export PATH="${nodeDir}:$PATH" && "${npmPath}" install -g openclaw@latest`
```

### Error Log

```
Installing OpenClaw with command: /usr/local/bin/npm install -g openclaw@latest
OpenClaw install failed with code 243
Permission denied, retrying with sudo-prompt...
Sudo install failed: Command failed: "/usr/local/bin/npm" install -g openclaw@latest
env: node: No such file or directory
```

### Environment

- macOS with nvm (node v24.14.0) + homebrew (node v25.8.0)
- npm shebang: `#!/usr/bin/env node`
- `@expo/sudo-prompt` uses osascript, root PATH doesn't include nvm/homebrew dirs

### Bug Description

Cherry Studio's built-in Claude Code integration has a critical context length configuration error when handling custom AI models (such as `deepseek-reasoner`), causing process crashes instead of graceful error handling.

### Problem Overview

Claude Code incorrectly assumes all AI models have a 180,000 token context window, but many custom models (like deepseek-reasoner) have different actual limits. This leads to two error scenarios:

#### Scenario 1: Model Limit Misdetermination (128K-180K tokens)
- **Root Problem**: Claude Code hardcodes a 180K context window, but `deepseek-reasoner` actually only supports 131,072 tokens
- **Result**: When total tokens are between 128K-180K, Claude Code considers it "safe", but the deepseek API returns a 400 error, causing process crash

#### Scenario 2: Improper Handling of Overlong Prompts (>180K tokens)
- **Root Problem**: Claude Code can detect "Prompt is too long", but the handling logic is incorrect
- **Result**: The process still crashes, and all subsequent requests return the same error, leaving the conversation "stuck"

### Root Cause Analysis

1. **Hardcoded Model Specifications**: The Claude Code integration has a built-in incorrect model specification table, assigning Claude official model specifications to all models
2. **Environment Variable Ignored**: Standard Claude Code environment variables (such as `ANTHROPIC_MAX_CONTEXT_LENGTH`) are ignored in the Cherry Studio integration
3. **Missing Error Handling**: The process crashes directly on API errors instead of graceful degradation
4. **Incorrect State Management**: After detecting an overlong prompt, the process still crashes and cannot recover

### Attempted Solutions (Ineffective)

We tried setting environment variables: `ANTHROPIC_MAX_CONTEXT_LENGTH=131072`, `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONTEXT_LENGTH=131072`, and other configuration methods, but none took effect.

1. Configure Cherry Studio to use the deepseek API.
2. Prepare a sufficiently long text (approximately 550KB)

2. Paste the prepared text (approximately 130K-170K tokens) directly into the user message and send

**Key Metrics**:
- Text size: ~500-700KB plain text (approximately 125K-175K tokens)
- Total tokens: Message tokens (~137K) + Expected response tokens (~32K) = ~169K > 131K limit

1. **Correct Model Specification Recognition**: Claude Code should correctly identify that `deepseek-reasoner` has a 131,072 token limit
2. **Environment Variable Support**: Should respect environment variables like `ANTHROPIC_MAX_CONTEXT_LENGTH`
3. **Graceful Error Handling**:
   - Don't crash the process on API errors
   - Display user-friendly error messages (such as "Context too long, please shorten the content")

- [x] I've confirmed that I am using the latest version of Cherry Studio.

### Platform

macOS

### Version

v1.7.24

### Bug Description

When a link provides `og:image` metadata, the OG preview card image may overflow its container and cannot be displayed properly.

In `OGCard.tsx`, the `PreviewImageContainer` has a fixed height of `9rem` with `overflow: hidden`, and the `PreviewImage` uses `object-fit: cover`. For some images (especially those with unusual aspect ratios), the image gets heavily cropped and the important content may not be visible, making the preview card less useful.

**Related code**: `src/renderer/src/components/OGCard.tsx`

```tsx
const PreviewImageContainer = styled.div`
  width: 100%;
  height: ${IMAGE_HEIGHT};      // fixed 9rem
  min-height: ${IMAGE_HEIGHT};
  overflow: hidden;
`

const PreviewImage = styled.img`
  width: 100%;
  height: ${IMAGE_HEIGHT};
  object-fit: cover;            // crops the image
`
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. In a chat conversation, send or receive a message containing a link that provides `og:image` metadata
2. The OG preview card renders below the link
3. Observe that for some links, the `og:image` is cropped/overflowed and cannot display the full content

### Expected Behavior

The `og:image` in the OG preview card should be displayed properly without important content being cropped or overflowing. Consider using `object-fit: contain` or providing a fallback mechanism so that the image fits the container while remaining fully visible.

### Relevant Log Output

_No response_

### Additional Context

The container dimensions are fixed at `380px × 220px` with the image area taking `9rem` height. Images with significantly different aspect ratios than the expected landscape format will be heavily cropped by `object-fit: cover`.

#### og:image Size Standards

The Open Graph protocol has industry-standard recommended image dimensions:

| Platform | Recommended Size | Aspect Ratio | Min Size |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Facebook** | 1200×630 | 1.91:1 | 200×200 |
| **Twitter/X** | 1200×675 | 1.91:1 | 300×157 |
| **LinkedIn** | 1200×627 | 1.91:1 | — |
| **Pinterest** | 1000×1500 | 2:3 | — |

The dominant standard is **1200×630px (1.91:1 landscape)**. Most well-configured websites follow this convention, so the current fixed-height `object-fit: cover` approach works for them.

However, this issue is more likely to be triggered by:
1. **Non-standard og:image** — e.g., square logos or vertical images used as og:image
2. **Pinterest-style tall images** — 2:3 ratio gets severely cropped in a landscape container
3. **Fallback images** — when no og:image is set but a fallback image is used, the dimensions are unpredictable

title: [Bug]: OpenClaw install/uninstall has no timeout or cancel mechanism
body:
> [!NOTE]
> This issue was translated by Claude.

### Platform

macOS, Windows, Linux

### Version

v1.7.24+

### Bug Description

OpenClaw's `install()` and `uninstall()` execute `npm install -g` via `crossPlatformSpawn`, but there is no timeout or cancellation mechanism. If npm hangs due to network issues, dependency resolution getting stuck, or other reasons, users can only force quit Cherry Studio.

**Code Location**: `src/main/services/OpenClawService.ts` install() ~L267, uninstall() ~L374

```typescript
const installProcess = crossPlatformSpawn(processedNpmPath, npmArgs, { env: spawnEnv })
// No timeout, no cancel
```

### Impact

- When installation gets stuck, users have no cancel button and can only kill the process
- In poor network environments, npm may be unresponsive for long periods
- sudo retry (`@expo/sudo-prompt`'s `exec`) also has no timeout

### Suggested Fix

1. Add a reasonable timeout to spawn (e.g., 5 minutes), kill child process after timeout and notify the user
2. Provide a cancel button in the frontend installation UI, notify main process via IPC to kill child process

### Related

- #13333 (sudo PATH)
- #13358 (git dependency)
- PR #13356

---

[Bug]: OpenClaw garbled Chinese text on Windows
body:
## Description

OpenClaw runtime output shows garbled Chinese characters on Windows Chinese systems.

## Symptom

The chat response displays U+FFFD replacement characters instead of Chinese text. Structured fields like A=, B=, C= and the Exec section are partially readable, but all Chinese content is garbled.

## Root Cause Analysis

Likely an encoding mismatch between UTF-8 and GBK (CP936):

1. Windows Chinese systems use GBK (CP936) as the default code page
2. `crossPlatformSpawn()` uses `shell: true` on Windows, child processes inherit the system code page
3. `data.toString()` decodes Buffer as UTF-8 by default
4. When the gateway process output passes through Windows cmd shell, Chinese text may be re-encoded in GBK

This could affect:
- Gateway stdout/stderr logging (`OpenClawService.ts` lines 507, 519)
- Gateway API response content-type/encoding
- Or the gateway process itself outputting in wrong encoding

## Environment

- OS: Windows (Chinese locale)
- Cherry Studio: latest
- OpenClaw: latest

title: [Feature]: Message Queue for Agent & Chat
body:
## Background

In both Chat and Agent modes, the send button is disabled while the model is generating a response — users must wait for the current reply to finish before sending the next message. This creates a frustrating idle-wait workflow: batch tasks (e.g., translating 10 paragraphs, reviewing 5 files sequentially) require manual one-by-one sending with pauses between each. Users who think of follow-up questions while the AI is still replying have no way to queue them — the ideas must be held in the user's head until the reply completes. Agent mode is especially impacted: pre-arranging a series of instructions for unattended sequential execution is impossible, making batch automation a missed opportunity.

## Goal

Users can send multiple messages at any time — including while the model is replying — and those messages automatically queue, execute sequentially, and remain fully manageable (reorder, edit, delete, pause/resume) before processing.

## Spec

- The send button stays enabled while the model is replying. Messages sent during a reply automatically enter a per-conversation queue instead of being sent immediately.
- When the current reply completes, the next queued message is automatically sent. This continues until the queue is empty.
- A queue panel appears above the input bar whenever there are pending messages. It shows up to 3 messages by default; additional messages collapse behind an "Expand N more…" toggle.
- Users can drag-reorder queued messages to change execution priority.
- Users can inline-edit or delete any unsent queued message. A "Clear Queue" action removes all pending messages at once.
- Users can pause the queue (halting auto-send of the next message) and resume it at any time. Pausing does not interrupt a message already being processed.
- If a queued message fails (network error, model error), the queue pauses automatically and the user is prompted to choose: Skip, Retry, or Abort remaining queue.
- The queue works identically in Chat mode and Agent mode — each conversation/session maintains its own independent queue.
- Queue contents persist across app restarts within the same conversation. A per-conversation limit of 20 queued messages applies; exceeding it shows a prompt.

## Verification

- While Claude Sonnet is generating a long code response in Chat mode, type "Now summarize it in 3 bullets" and press Send → message appears in the queue panel above the input bar with a drag handle, edit icon, and delete icon. Send button remains enabled for further messages.
- Queue 3 messages: "Translate paragraph 1", "Translate paragraph 2", "Translate paragraph 3". After the first translation completes, "Translate paragraph 2" auto-sends without user action. Queue panel updates to show 2 → 1 → 0 remaining.
- With 3 messages queued, drag "Translate paragraph 3" above "Translate paragraph 2" → execution order updates accordingly and paragraph 3 is processed before paragraph 2.
- Click the edit icon on a queued message, change text from "Translate paragraph 2" to "Translate and summarize paragraph 2", confirm → updated content is what gets sent when the message is dequeued.
- Queue 5 messages. Click "Pause" → after the current reply finishes, no further messages auto-send. Click "Resume" → processing continues from the next queued message.
- Queue 3 messages. The second message triggers a model API error → queue auto-pauses, a prompt appears with Skip / Retry / Abort options. Choosing "Skip" skips message 2 and continues with message 3. Choosing "Abort" clears all remaining queued messages.
- In Agent mode, queue 3 instructions: "Review auth.ts", "Review api.ts", "Review utils.ts" for a code review Agent → Agent executes each sequentially, completing one review before starting the next.
- Queue 7 messages → panel shows 3 messages with "Expand 4 more…" link. Click expand → all 7 messages visible with drag handles.
- Queue 2 messages, close and reopen the app → the same conversation still shows the 2 queued messages in the panel.
- Attempt to queue a 21st message → a prompt appears indicating the queue limit of 20 has been reached.
- While a message is actively being processed by the model, delete it from the queue panel → nothing happens (only unsent messages can be deleted); the running message is not affected.
- Open two different conversations side by side, queue messages in both → each conversation's queue operates independently.

title: [Feature]: Smart Model Auto-Discovery & Auto-Add on Provider Setup
body:
## Summary

5 targeted changes to the existing provider settings page to improve model discovery and management. No new pages, no new routes.

> CherryAI (`CHERRYAI_PROVIDER`) is enabled by default with preset models. These changes help users get a **complete** model list automatically, rather than relying on the limited preset `SYSTEM_MODELS`.

## Changes Overview

| # | Change | User Impact |
|---|--------|-------------|
| 1 | Auto-fetch models after API Key save / OAuth login | Models appear silently — no manual action needed |
| 2 | Model list UI restructure (sections, groups, tags, action buttons) | Clear enabled/disabled separation, one-click add/remove |
| 3 | Auto-fetch when model list empty on check | One-click check, no error on empty list |
| 4 | Handle model-not-found on check failure | Prompt user to remove stale model |
| 5 | Fetch results dialog with diff view | New models auto-added, stale models selectively removable |

---

## Change 1: Auto-fetch models after API Key save / OAuth login

**Trigger**: First API Key save (empty → non-empty) OR OAuth success

**Behavior**:
```
API Key saved (first time) OR OAuth success
  → silently call ApiService.fetchModels(provider) in background
  → merge: uniqBy([...existingModels, ...fetchedModels], 'id')
  → update provider.models in Redux store
  → NO toast, NO loading — user unaware
  → models just "appear" in the list
  → if fetch fails: silently fall back to SYSTEM_MODELS preset
```

**Key points**:
- Silent background fetch — no UI feedback
- Only triggers on **first** API Key save, not subsequent edits
- CherryIN OAuth: append fetch logic after existing `updateProvider({ apiKey })` — don't modify login UI
- Merge uses `uniqBy` to preserve user's existing custom settings

**Implementation**:
```typescript
// ProviderSetting.tsx — after API Key debounce save
const isFirstKeySetup = !provider.apiKey && newApiKey
if (isFirstKeySetup) {
  const fetched = await ApiService.fetchModels({ ...provider, apiKey: newApiKey })
  const merged = uniqBy([...provider.models, ...fetched], 'id')
  updateProvider({ models: merged })
  // No toast — silent background fetch
}

// CherryINOAuth.tsx — after existing updateProvider({ apiKey }) call
// Don't modify login UI, just append fetch logic after success callback
const fetched = await ApiService.fetchModels(provider)
const merged = uniqBy([...provider.models, ...fetched], 'id')
updateProvider({ models: merged })
```

**Edge cases**:
- Provider doesn't support `/models` → silently fall back to `SYSTEM_MODELS`
- Network error → silently fall back, user can manually fetch later
- Only on **first** API Key save (empty → non-empty), not subsequent edits
- **Entire process is silent** — no toast, no loading, no UI feedback

**Files**: `ProviderSetting.tsx`, `CherryINOAuth.tsx`

---

## Change 2: Model list UI restructure

### Header action bar

| Current | New | Icon | Notes |
|---------|-----|------|-------|
| 👁 Show All | Enable All / Disable All | Lucide `Eye` | Toggles: shows "Disable All" when all enabled, otherwise "Enable All" |
| 🔗 Check | Check | `StreamlineGoodHealthAndWellBeing` (existing component from `@renderer/components/Icons`) | Health check icon already in codebase |
| ✏ Manage | **Remove** | — | No longer needed as standalone entry |
| Manage (bottom) | ↓ Fetch Models | Lucide `Download` | Moved to search bar right side |
| Add (bottom) | ＋ | Lucide `Plus` | Search bar far-right button for custom model add |

### Model list sections

The model list is split into **Enabled** and **Disabled** sections, each with provider-based groups inside.

### Model row actions

| Location | Icon | Lucide Name | Behavior |
|----------|------|-------------|----------|
| Enabled model row (right) | ➖ | `Minus` | Default opacity 0.35, hover → opacity 1 + red `#ff4d4f`, click moves to Disabled |
| Disabled model row (right) | ➕ | `Plus` | Default opacity 0.35, hover → opacity 1 + green `#00b96b`, click moves to Enabled |
| Enabled group header (right) | ➖ | `Minus` | Batch remove entire group, visible on hover |
| Disabled group header (right) | ➕ | `Plus` | Batch add entire group, visible on hover |

### Group collapsing

| Element | Icon | Lucide Name | Behavior |
|---------|------|-------------|----------|
| Group header arrow | ▸/▾ | `ChevronDown` | Points down when expanded, CSS `transform: rotate(-90deg)` when collapsed |

### Category filter tabs

Pill-shaped filter tabs above the model list using Lucide icons:

| Category | Lucide Icon | Import |
|----------|-------------|--------|
| All | No icon | — |
| Chat | `MessageSquare` | `import { MessageSquare } from 'lucide-react'` |
| Image | `Image` | `import { Image } from 'lucide-react'` |
| Code | `Code` | `import { Code } from 'lucide-react'` |
| Reasoning | `Brain` | `import { Brain } from 'lucide-react'` |

### Model capability tags

Reuse existing `CustomTag` component (`src/renderer/src/components/Tags/CustomTag.tsx`). Style: pill shape (`border-radius: 99px`), color + 12% alpha background (`color + '20'`).

| Tag | Color | Icon | Existing Component |
|-----|-------|------|--------------------|
| Vision | `#00b96b` | `Eye` (antd `EyeOutlined`) | `VisionTag.tsx` |
| WebSearch | `#1677ff` | `Globe` (antd `GlobalOutlined`) | `WebSearchTag.tsx` |
| Reasoning | `#6372bd` | `Brain` (iconfont `icon-thinking`) | `ReasoningTag.tsx` |
| Tools/Function Calling | `#f18737` | `Wrench` (antd `ToolOutlined`) | `ToolsCallingTag.tsx` |
| Free | `#7cb305` | No icon, text only | `FreeTag.tsx` |
| Embedding | `#8c8c8c` | — | `EmbeddingTag.tsx` |
| Reranker | `#8c8c8c` | — | `RerankerTag.tsx` |

> **Note**: Existing tag components already use antd icons (`EyeOutlined`, `GlobalOutlined`, etc.) — no need to replace. Only the new category tabs and action buttons use Lucide icons.

**i18n**: Update all 11+ language files.

**Files**: `ModelList.tsx`, `ModelListGroup.tsx`, `ModelListItem.tsx`

---

## Change 3: Auto-fetch when model list empty on check

**Current**: Click "Check" → select model from list → if empty → error "No models available".

**New**:
```
Click "Check"
  → if provider.models is empty:
    → auto-fetch via ApiService.fetchModels(provider)
    → if fetched > 0: merge into provider.models, pick first model, proceed
    → if fetched = 0: Toast "No models available. Add a model first."
  → if provider.models is not empty:
    → existing behavior (select model → check)
```

**File**: `ProviderSetting.tsx` → `onCheckApi()`

---

## Change 4: Handle model-not-found on check failure

**Current**: Check fails → generic error Toast.

**New**:
```
Check fails with model-not-found (404, "model not found", "does not exist", etc.)
  → show Modal:
    Title: "Model not available"
    Body: "[model-id] is no longer available from [Provider]. Remove from list?"
    Actions: [Remove] [Keep]
  → "Remove": delete from provider.models, Toast "Removed [model-id]"
  → "Keep": close dialog, no action
```

**Detection logic**:
```typescript
const isModelNotFound = (error: any): boolean => {
  const msg = (error?.message || '').toLowerCase()
  const status = error?.status || error?.statusCode
  return status === 404
    || msg.includes('model not found')
    || msg.includes('does not exist')
    || msg.includes('model_not_found')
    || msg.includes('invalid_model')
}
```

**File**: `ProviderSetting.tsx` → `onCheckApi()` catch block

---

## Change 5: Fetch results dialog

### Trigger

Click the "↓ Fetch Models" button next to the search bar.

### Behavior

```
Click "Fetch Models"
  → ApiService.fetchModels(provider)
  → compare fetched vs current provider.models
  → compute:
    - newModels: in fetched but not in current (by id)
    - expiredModels: in current but not in fetched (by id)
  → if no changes: Toast "Model list is up to date"
  → if changes:
    → new models immediately added to provider.models (no waiting for confirmation)
    → show "Fetch Results" dialog
```

### Dialog interaction logic

**New models section**:
- New models are already added to the list (cannot undo adding)
- Checkbox controls **whether to enable** (checked = enabled, unchecked = added but disabled)
- Default: all checked (all enabled)
- Top-right: "Deselect All / Select All" toggle

**Expired models section**:
- Checkbox controls **whether to delete** (checked = permanently removed from list)
- Default: none checked (kept in list)
- Top-right: "Select All to Delete" button
- Expired model names shown with strikethrough + gray text

**Footer**:
- Stats line: "Enabling 3/3 new models · Deleting 0/2 expired models" (plain text, no emoji)
- Buttons: "Cancel" + "Apply"

### Dialog UI mockup

```
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  ↓ Fetch Results                        ✕    │
│─────────────────────────────────────────────│
│                                              │
│  New Models (3) — Added to list, check       │
│  to enable                    Deselect All   │
│  ┌──────────────────────────────────────┐    │
│  │ ☑ Cherry IN 4o Mini   128K  Vision  │    │
│  │ ☑ Cherry IN Vision    256K  Image   │    │
│  │ ☑ Cherry IN Coder v2   64K  Code    │    │
│  └──────────────────────────────────────┘    │
│                                              │
│  Expired Models (2) — Check to delete        │
│  from list                  Select All       │
│  ┌──────────────────────────────────────┐    │
│  │ ☐ D̶e̶e̶p̶S̶e̶e̶k̶ ̶R̶1̶  deepseek-reasoner   │    │
│  │ ☐ D̶A̶L̶L̶-̶E̶ ̶3̶    dall-e-3             │    │
│  └──────────────────────────────────────┘    │
│                                              │
│  Enabling 3/3 new models · Deleting 0/2      │
│  expired models                              │
│  [ Cancel ]                    [ Apply ]     │
│                                              │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### Visual specs

- **Overall style**: Black/white/gray palette, only checkboxes use green (`#00b96b`) when checked
- **New model rows**: Light gray background (`rgba(0,0,0,.04)`), no color
- **Expired model rows**: No background color, name with strikethrough + gray text
- **No emoji**: Stats line uses plain text only, no ✅🗑 icons
- **Unified green checkboxes**: Both new and expired model checkboxes use green when checked

**New component**: `FetchResultDialog.tsx`
**Files**: `ModelList.tsx` (button click triggers fetch + diff + dialog)

---

## Files to modify

| File | Changes |
|------|---------|
| `ProviderSetting.tsx` | #1: auto-fetch after key save; #3: empty list handling; #4: model-not-found |
| `CherryINOAuth.tsx` | #1: append auto-fetch after OAuth success (don't modify login UI) |
| `ModelList/ModelList.tsx` | #2: list UI restructure (sections/groups/tags/buttons); #5: fetch + diff dialog |
| `ModelList/ManageModelsPopup.tsx` | #5: new/expired model diff display |
| `ApiService.ts` | #3: checkApi enhancement |
| New: `FetchResultDialog.tsx` | #5: fetch results dialog component |

## Key functions to reuse

- `ApiService.fetchModels(provider)` — fetch all models from provider API
- `uniqBy([...existing, ...fetched], 'id')` — merge strategy (from ManageModelsPopup)
- `checkApi(provider, model)` — existing connectivity check
- `window.message` / `window.toast` — notifications

## Non-functional Requirements

- Auto-fetch completes in under 5 seconds
- Fetch is async, non-blocking — show spinner where applicable
- Merge preserves user's custom model settings (display name, sort order)
- Model deletion always requires user confirmation
- All new UI text must be internationalized (11+ languages)

## Out of Scope

- Cross-provider model deduplication
- Per-model pricing/quota display
- Automatic model deletion without user confirmation
- Periodic background model sync

## Summary

When any error occurs in Cherry Studio, provide **two-layer diagnosis**: instant rule-based classification (translated error title in user's language) + optional AI-powered deep diagnosis inside ErrorDetailModal. Covers ALL error surfaces — chat ErrorBlock, ErrorDetailModal, and global Toast errors.

## Architecture

### Layer 1: Rule-Based Classification (instant, <100ms, no API call)

Parse HTTP status code + error message keywords → output **i18n-translated error title** in user's language + navigation buttons. No API call needed.

### Layer 2: AI Diagnosis (user-triggered, inside ErrorDetailModal)

User clicks "AI Diagnosis" button in ErrorDetailModal footer → sends error context to `settings.defaultModel` → returns plain-language explanation + step-by-step resolution in `settings.language`.

---

## Change 1: ErrorBlock Enhancement

### Current
```
antd Alert type="error"
  message: raw English error message (or HTTP status label)
  description: HTTP label
  action: [Detail] button
  closable: ✕
```

### New
```
antd Alert type="error"
  message: i18n-translated error summary in user's language (Layer 1 rule-based)
  description: original English error message (kept for reference)
  action: [Detail] text button (right side, antd Button variant="text")
  closable: ✕
  action row below description (only when primaryAction exists):
    [⚙ Go to Provider Settings] (green primary button, shown when applicable)
```

> **Note**: "Detail" button only appears once — in the right-side `action` area. The bottom action row only shows the primary navigation button (e.g., "Go to Provider Settings") when applicable.

### UI Mockup
```
┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ ⊘  Your OpenAI API Key is invalid, please reconfigure  Detail ✕ │
│    Incorrect API key provided: sk-proj-****xxxx.                  │
│    [⚙ Go to Provider Settings]                                    │
└───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### Error Classification (Layer 1)

```typescript
// errorClassifier.ts — rule-based, instant, no API call
function classifyError(error: SerializedError): ErrorClassification {
  const status = error.status || error.statusCode
  const msg = (error.message || '').toLowerCase()

  if (status === 401 || msg.includes('invalid_api_key'))
    return { category: 'auth', i18nKey: 'error.diagnosis.auth', navTarget: '/settings/provider' }
  if (status === 404 || msg.includes('model_not_found'))
    return { category: 'model', i18nKey: 'error.diagnosis.model', navTarget: '/settings/provider' }
  if (status === 429 || msg.includes('quota'))
    return { category: 'quota', i18nKey: 'error.diagnosis.quota', navTarget: '/settings/provider' }
  if (status >= 500)
    return { category: 'server', i18nKey: 'error.diagnosis.server', navTarget: null }
  // ... etc for network, content, knowledge, ocr, mcp
}
```

**i18n keys** for translated titles (example zh-CN / en-US):

| Key | zh-CN | en-US |
|-----|-------|-------|
| `error.diagnosis.auth` | 你的 API Key 无效，请检查并重新配置 | Your API Key is invalid, please reconfigure |
| `error.diagnosis.model` | 模型不可用或已被下线 | Model is unavailable or discontinued |
| `error.diagnosis.quota` | 账户额度已用完 | Account quota exhausted |
| `error.diagnosis.network` | 无法连接到服务器 | Cannot connect to server |
| `error.diagnosis.server` | 服务商服务器异常，建议稍后重试 | Provider server error, retry later |
| `error.diagnosis.content` | 消息内容被安全系统拦截 | Message blocked by safety system |

**File**: `ErrorBlock.tsx`, new `errorClassifier.ts`, 11+ i18n language files

---

## Change 2: ErrorDetailModal — Add AI Diagnosis

### Current
```
antd Modal (width:80%, maxWidth:1200px, minWidth:600px)
  body: ErrorDetailList (name, message, statusCode, cause, stack...)
  footer: [Copy] [Close]
```

### New
```
antd Modal (width:80%, maxWidth:1200px, minWidth:600px)
  body:
    ErrorDetailList (existing error details)
    AI Diagnosis panel (expandable, green border card)
  footer: [AI Diagnosis] [Copy] [Close]
```

### AI Diagnosis Panel (after clicking button)

```
┌─ AI Diagnosis Result ─────────────────────────────────────┐
│ ✓ AI Diagnosis Result                                      │
│                                                            │
│ Your OpenAI API Key is invalid or expired. The provider    │
│ returned HTTP 401, indicating authentication failure.      │
│                                                            │
│ ① Regenerate API Key at OpenAI platform ↗                 │
│ ② → Update API Key in Cherry Studio Settings               │
│ ③ Click "Check" to verify the new key                      │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### AI Diagnosis Model Selection

Uses `settings.defaultModel` directly. If the default model IS the failing model → button disabled (greyed out), only Layer 1 classification available.

> CherryAI (`CHERRYAI_PROVIDER`) has free preset models, so AI diagnosis is available for most users even without any provider configured.

### Diagnosis Context (sent to model)

| Field | Source | Notes |
|-------|--------|-------|
| Error Source | Call context | "chat" / "health_check" / "knowledge_base" / "ocr" / "mcp" etc. |
| Provider | `provider.name` | |
| Model ID | `model.id` | |
| Error Name | `error.name` | e.g. `AuthenticationError` |
| Error Message | `error.message` | |
| HTTP Status | `error.status` | |
| Response Body | `error.body` | Truncated to 500 chars |

**NOT sent** (privacy): Full API keys, chat history, local file paths.

### Diagnosis Prompt

```typescript
const prompt = `You are an error diagnosis assistant for Cherry Studio.
Analyze this error:
- Source: ${errorSource}
- Provider: ${provider?.name || 'N/A'}
- Error: ${error.name}: ${error.message}
- HTTP Status: ${error.status || 'N/A'}
- Response: ${JSON.stringify(error.body || '').slice(0, 500)}

IMPORTANT: Respond in ${settings.language}.

Respond in JSON:
{
  "summary": "one-line summary",
  "category": "authentication | quota | model_unavailable | network | ...",
  "explanation": "2-3 sentence plain language explanation",
  "steps": [{ "text": "step", "action": "navigate | link | info", "target": "..." }]
}`
```

**Files**: `ErrorDetailModal/index.tsx`, new `ErrorDiagnosisService.ts`

---

## Change 3: Toast — Add "View Details" Link

### Current
```
antd message.error('error string')
// or
antd message.error({ content: <ToastContent title="..." description="..." /> })
```

### New

Error-type Toasts show AI-translated title + original error + "View Details" link:

```
antd message.error({
  content: <ToastContent
    title={classifyError(error).i18nTitle}  // Translated title
    description={error.message}              // Original English
    link={{ text: t('common.viewDetails'), onClick: () => openErrorDetailModal(error) }}
  />
})
```

### UI Mockup
```
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ ⊘  MCP server connection refused, check if started   │
│    ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:3100                       │
│    View Details                                       │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

**File**: `toast.tsx`, callsites that use `window.toast.error()`

---

## Error Classification Table

| Category | Examples | Navigation |
|----------|----------|------------|
| **Authentication** | 401, invalid API key | → Provider settings |
| **Quota/Billing** | 429, insufficient quota | → Provider billing (external link) |
| **Model Unavailable** | 404, model not found | → Provider model management |
| **Network** | Timeout, ECONNREFUSED | → Proxy/network settings |
| **Content Policy** | 400, content filtered | → (no navigation, modify message) |
| **Server Error** | 500/502/503 | → (no navigation, retry later) |
| **Knowledge Base** | Embedding fail, vectorize error | → Embedding model config |
| **OCR** | Engine not initialized | → OCR settings |
| **MCP** | Connection refused | → MCP settings |

---

## Files to Modify

| File | Changes |
|------|---------|
| `ErrorBlock.tsx` | Layer 1 classification → translated title as `message`, original error as `description`, primary action button row (no duplicate Detail button) |
| `ErrorDetailModal/index.tsx` | Add AI Diagnosis button in footer + expandable diagnosis panel |
| `toast.tsx` | Error toasts: translated title + "View Details" link |
| New: `errorClassifier.ts` | Rule-based error classifier |
| New: `ErrorDiagnosisService.ts` | AI diagnosis service (calls default model) |
| 11+ i18n files | Add `error.diagnosis.*` translation keys |

## Technical References

| Component | File |
|-----------|------|
| Error serialization | `src/renderer/src/utils/error.ts` |
| Chat ErrorBlock | `src/renderer/src/pages/home/Messages/Blocks/ErrorBlock.tsx` |
| ErrorDetailModal | `src/renderer/src/components/ErrorDetailModal/index.tsx` |
| Toast | `src/renderer/src/components/TopView/toast.tsx` |
| Chat error callback | `src/renderer/src/services/messageStreaming/callbacks/baseCallbacks.ts` |
| Health check | `src/renderer/src/services/HealthCheckService.ts` |
| CherryAI default models | `src/renderer/src/config/models/default.ts` |

## Non-functional Requirements

- Rule-based classification: instant (<100ms, no API call)
- AI diagnosis: user-triggered only (not automatic)
- AI responds in user's system language (`settings.language`)
- Even if all models unavailable, Layer 1 classification still works
- Navigation actions deep-link to specific settings pages
- All new UI text internationalized (11+ languages)

## Future Plans (not in current scope)

### 1. Submit to GitHub Issue
- After AI diagnosis, offer "Submit to GitHub Issue" button
- Auto-fill issue template

### 2. Guided Auto-Fix
- For auto-fixable errors, provide "One-click Fix" button
- Fix requires user confirmation, never auto-executes

## Out of Scope

- Third-party error monitoring (Sentry, etc.)
- Error prediction/prevention

## Related Issues

- [#13418](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/issues/13418) — Smart Model Auto-Discovery (shares model-not-found handling)

title: [Feature]: New User Onboarding — Guided Setup from First Launch to First Chat
body:
## Summary

Introduce a **4-step guided Onboarding flow** for new users on first launch. Fixed 560×520 card overlay. All config writes go directly to the existing Settings Redux store — fully synced with the Settings page.

> **Important**: CherryAI (`CHERRYAI_PROVIDER`) is enabled by default with free models. Even if users skip all steps, they can immediately chat. Onboarding helps users configure *better* models, not unlock basic functionality.

## Flow

```
Step 1: Language + Theme
Step 2: Connect Provider (CherryIN OAuth + other providers via dropdown → API Key → verify → model list)
Step 3: Set Default Models (Default Assistant / Quick Model / Translation Model)
Step 4: Done → Enter main interface
```

## Design Principles

- **Full-screen independent page** — no sidebar, no chat frame on first launch
- **Fixed card size** (560×520), content scrolls inside, footer pinned
- **Every step skippable** → `onboardingCompleted = true` → enter main interface with CherryAI defaults
- **Every step has Back / Next**
- **All config writes to Settings store** — identical to manual Settings page operations
- **Reuse existing components** — no reinventing the wheel
- **i18n** — language switch updates all text instantly

---

## Step 1: Welcome — Language + Theme

| Element | Description | Reuse |
|---------|-------------|-------|
| Logo + Name | 🍒 Cherry Studio branding | — |
| Subtitle | "Your AI Desktop Assistant" (i18n) | i18n |
| Language dropdown | All supported languages, instant switch | `LanguageVip` |
| Theme picker | Light / Dark / System with mini preview | `ThemeMode` |

**Writes**: `settings.language`, `settings.theme`

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────┐
│          🍒 Cherry Studio           │
│     Your AI Desktop Assistant       │
│                                     │
│        🌐 [English ▼]              │
│                                     │
│   ┌─────┐  ┌─────┐  ┌─────┐       │
│   │Light│  │Dark │  │Sys  │       │
│   └─────┘  └─────┘  └─────┘       │
├─────────────────────────────────────┤
│ ●━━ ○ ○ ○       Skip  [Next ›]    │
└─────────────────────────────────────┘
```

---

## Step 2: Connect Provider

Subtitle hint: *"You can change these later in Settings → Model Services"*

### Layout (top to bottom)

1. **CherryIN single-row card** (top, green background)
   - Left: 🍒 icon + "CherryIN" + hint "Free models available after top-up"
   - Right: Sign in button
   - OAuth success → model list expands **below** this row (all selected by default)

2. **Added provider chips** — e.g. `CherryIN 3` `OpenAI 5 ✕`

3. **Divider**: "or add another provider"

4. **Provider dropdown** (select element, NOT card grid)
   - Select → API Key input + Verify button appears below
   - Ollama/local: no API Key needed, fetch models directly

5. **Model list** (expands after verify success)
   - Calls `ApiService.fetchModels()` to fetch all models
   - **All selected by default**, user can deselect
   - "Add selected models" → writes to provider.models → chip updates → provider removed from dropdown

6. **Toast** — based on actual API response (success/error), not hardcoded

### Interaction Flow

```
CherryIN:
  Sign in → OAuth → success
    → model list below (all selected) → "Add selected models"
    → chip: "CherryIN 3"

Other providers:
  Dropdown select OpenAI → API Key input appears
    → enter sk-xxx → click Verify
    → API error → error Toast (from API response)
    → success → success Toast → model list (all selected)
    → "Add selected models" → chip: "OpenAI 5"

Can add multiple providers
```

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────┐
│          Connect Provider            │
│  Sign in or add your API Keys       │
│  (Change later in Settings)          │
│                                     │
│  ┌────────────────────────────────┐ │
│  │ 🍒 CherryIN  top-up  [Sign in]│ │
│  └────────────────────────────────┘ │
│  (model list expands here)           │
│                                     │
│  [CherryIN 3] [OpenAI 5 ✕]         │
│  ───── or add another provider ──── │
│  [Select provider...          ▼]    │
│  [sk-xxxxx              ] [Verify]  │
│  (model list expands here)           │
├─────────────────────────────────────┤
│ ‹ Back  ○ ●━━ ○ ○   Skip  [Next ›]│
└─────────────────────────────────────┘
```

**Reuse**: CherryIN OAuth flow, `ProviderSetting` check logic, `ApiService.fetchModels()`, `ModelList` component

---

## Step 3: Set Default Models

Select from models added in Step 2. **Maps exactly to Settings → Default Models page**:

| Role | Description | Settings field | Settings page location |
|------|-------------|---------------|----------------------|
| 💬 Default Assistant | Model used when creating new assistants | `settings.defaultModel` | Settings → Default Models → Default Assistant |
| ⚡ Quick Model | Topic naming, keyword extraction, simple tasks | `settings.topicNamingModel` | Settings → Default Models → Quick Model |
| 🌐 Translation | Translation services | `settings.translateModel` | Settings → Default Models → Translation |

**Layout**: Each row = left (emoji + name + desc) + right (model dropdown). **Reuse** Settings page `DefaultModel` Select component.

**Data source**: All models from all providers added in Step 2. If none added, use CherryAI built-in models.

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────┐
│          Default Models              │
│   Choose a model for each scenario   │
│                                     │
│  💬 Default Asst  [cherry-4o     ▼] │
│  ⚡ Quick Model   [cherry-mini   ▼] │
│  🌐 Translation   [cherry-3.5   ▼] │
│                                     │
├─────────────────────────────────────┤
│ ‹ Back  ○ ○ ●━━ ○   Skip  [Next ›]│
└─────────────────────────────────────┘
```

---

## Step 4: Done

- 🎉 icon + "You're All Set!" (i18n)
- Config summary: language, theme, providers, model count
- 🚀 Start Chatting button → `onboardingCompleted = true` → enter main interface
- Back button → return to Step 3

---

## Technical Design

### State

```typescript
// Add to settings store
onboardingCompleted: boolean  // default false, set true on complete/skip
```

Redux-persist. Reset via Settings → About → "Restart Onboarding".

### Routing

```typescript
// App.tsx
if (!settings.onboardingCompleted) return <OnboardingOverlay />
return <MainApp />
```

### Components

```
src/renderer/src/components/onboarding/
  ├── OnboardingOverlay.tsx     // Full-screen container + step state machine
  ├── WelcomeStep.tsx           // Step 1: language + theme
  ├── ProviderStep.tsx          // Step 2: provider + model list
  ├── DefaultModelStep.tsx      // Step 3: default model selection
  └── CompletionStep.tsx        // Step 4: summary + start
```

### Component Reuse (DO NOT recreate)

| Need | Reuse from |
|------|-----------|
| Language dropdown | `LanguageVip` |
| Theme switcher | `ThemeMode` |
| CherryIN OAuth | Existing CherryIN login flow |
| API Key input/verify | `ProviderSetting` check logic |
| Fetch models | `ApiService.fetchModels()` |
| Model list with checkboxes | `ModelList` |
| Default model dropdown | Settings page `DefaultModel` Select |
| Toast | `window.message` |

### Config Sync (Onboarding = Settings page)

| Onboarding action | Equivalent Settings page action | Field |
|-------------------|-------------------------------|-------|
| Select language | Settings → General → Language | `settings.language` |
| Select theme | Settings → Display → Theme | `settings.theme` |
| Add provider | Settings → Model Services → Add | `settings.providers` |
| Add models | Settings → Model Services → Model list | `provider.models` |
| Set default assistant | Settings → Default Models → Default Assistant | `settings.defaultModel` |
| Set quick model | Settings → Default Models → Quick Model | `settings.topicNamingModel` |
| Set translation model | Settings → Default Models → Translation | `settings.translateModel` |
| Complete/Skip | — | `settings.onboardingCompleted = true` |

### Key Files

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `src/renderer/src/App.tsx` | Add onboarding detection |
| `src/renderer/src/store/settings.ts` | Add `onboardingCompleted` |
| `src/renderer/src/config/providers.ts` | Provider list |
| `src/renderer/src/services/ApiService.ts` | `fetchModels()` |
| `src/renderer/src/i18n/index.ts` | i18n integration |

## Non-functional Requirements

- Fast path completes in **under 2 minutes**
- Every step **skippable**
- All copy **internationalized**
- Card **fixed 560×520**
- State persisted via Redux-persist
- Animations via Framer Motion

## Skip & Revisit

- **Skip** → `onboardingCompleted = true` → CherryAI defaults
- **Revisit** → Settings → About → "Restart Onboarding"

## Out of Scope

- Video tutorials / embedded docs
- Account creation / cloud sync
- Advanced provider config (proxy, custom endpoints)
- MCP server setup
- Feature Tour (separate future task)
- Empty State enhancement (separate future task)

## Related Issues

- [#13418](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/issues/13418) — Smart Model Auto-Discovery

title: [Feature]: Add optional LLM-based semantic chunking strategy for knowledge base to improve retrieval quality

### Platform

Windows

### Version

1.7.24

### Is your feature request related to an existing issue?

Currently, Cherry Studio's knowledge base employs a fixed-length hard chunking strategy when processing documents (truncating by character count or token count). While this approach is simple to implement and fast, it has significant drawbacks: chunk boundaries are determined solely by length without regard for semantic structure, often splitting complete concepts or sentences across two chunks, which significantly degrades retrieval quality.

To this end, it is recommended to add an optional LLM semantic chunking mode on top of the existing hard chunking as a high-quality alternative.

### Desired Solution

Added a chunking strategy option in the knowledge base settings, allowing users to make their own selection:

- Fixed length (current default) – Truncate by character/token count
- Semantic Chunking (LLM-assisted) (New) – Invokes the LLM to split content based on semantic boundaries

After selecting the semantic chunking mode, you can further configure:
- LLM for chunking (uses the currently configured model by default)
- Target chunk size hint (passed to the LLM as a soft constraint)

title: [Feature]: Migrate third-party OpenAI Responses providers to @ai-sdk/open-responses
body:
### Issue Checklist

- [x] I understand that issues are for reporting problems and requesting features, not for off-topic comments, and I will provide as much detail as possible to help resolve the issue.
- [x] I have checked the pinned issues and searched through the existing [open issues](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/issues), [closed issues](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20state%3Aclosed), and [discussions](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/discussions) and did not find a similar suggestion.
- [x] I have provided a short and descriptive title so that developers can quickly understand the issue when browsing the issue list, rather than vague titles like "A suggestion" or "Stuck."
- [x] The latest version of Cherry Studio does not include the feature I am suggesting.

### Platform

Windows

### Version

v1.7.25

### Is your feature request related to an existing issue?

Yes — #13454.

Currently, Cherry Studio uses `@ai-sdk/openai`'s built-in Responses provider for third-party OpenAI-compatible providers that support the Responses API endpoint. However, `@ai-sdk/openai` internally uses a **model ID allowlist** to determine reasoning model capabilities:

```javascript
// @ai-sdk/openai/src/openai-language-model-capabilities.ts
const isReasoningModel =
    modelId.startsWith('o1') ||
    modelId.startsWith('o3') ||
    modelId.startsWith('o4-mini') ||
    (modelId.startsWith('gpt-5') && !modelId.startsWith('gpt-5-chat'));
```

When `isReasoningModel` is `false`, reasoning parameters (`reasoningEffort`, `reasoningSummary`) are **silently dropped** from the request body, even if correctly built by Cherry Studio. This causes the bug reported in #13454.

Third-party providers often use non-canonical model IDs (e.g., `openai/gpt-5.2`, `gpt-5.2-0125`, or custom aliases), which fail the `startsWith()` checks.

### Desired Solution

Migrate from `@ai-sdk/openai`'s built-in Responses provider to the dedicated **[`@ai-sdk/open-responses`](https://ai-sdk.dev/providers/ai-sdk-providers/open-responses)** provider for third-party OpenAI-compatible providers.

The `@ai-sdk/open-responses` provider is purpose-built for the OpenAI Responses API format without coupling to OpenAI-specific model ID allowlists. It should correctly pass through all provider options regardless of model ID format.

**Immediate fix**: As a stopgap, set `forceReasoning: true` in `providerOptions.openai` when `enableReasoning` is true, which bypasses the AI SDK's model ID allowlist:

```typescript
const isReasoningModel =
    openaiOptions?.forceReasoning ?? modelCapabilities.isReasoningModel;
```

### Alternative Solutions

1. **`forceReasoning: true` only** (stopgap) — add `forceReasoning: true` to `buildOpenAIProviderOptions()` when reasoning is enabled. Simple but still couples to `@ai-sdk/openai` internals.
2. **Upstream fix** — request Vercel AI SDK to make the allowlist more flexible or configurable in `@ai-sdk/openai`.
3. **Manual parameter injection** — use `openai-compatible` provider and manually construct `reasoning` block in the request body.

### Additional Information

Investigation trace:
- `buildProviderOptions()` correctly returns `{ openai: { reasoningEffort: "xhigh", reasoningSummary: "detailed" } }` ✅
- `providerOptions` passes through plugin engine → AI SDK `streamText()` → model `doStream()` intact ✅
- `parseProviderOptions({ provider: "openai" })` correctly extracts the options ✅
- `isReasoningModel` evaluates to `false` due to model ID mismatch → reasoning params dropped ❌

Log output:
```
AI SDK Warning (openai.responses / openai/gpt-5.2): The feature "reasoningEffort" is not supported. reasoningEffort is not supported for non-reasoning models
```

### Bug Description

Error occurred when using a third-party proxy. It turned out to be caused by request headers injected by Cherry Studio itself. Can an option be added in settings to remove them?
```
Conclusion

  This configuration cannot be used. The root cause is not a wrong path, but that Cherry Studio unconditionally adds two global request headers in the "actual chat/detection" Gemini route:

  - HTTP-Referer: https://cherry-ai.com
  - X-Title: Cherry Studio

  For the proxy https://co.yes.vg/gemini, these headers are fine individually, but when both appear together, they trigger 503 provider_error / All providers unavailable. This is the direct reason why "models appear but chat doesn't work" in Cherry Studio.

  Source Code Location

  - Gemini addresses are first formatted to .../v1beta, the path itself is fine, see providerConfig.ts:93 and providerConfig.ts:194.
  - Chat/detection goes through the modern route, ultimately calling AI.completions(...), see ApiService.ts:277 and ApiService.ts:684.
  - The modern route injects defaultAppHeaders(), see providerConfig.ts:261.
  - These two headers are defined in index.ts:3.
  - The model list, however, uses legacy @google/genai and does not carry these headers, so it can still list models normally, see index_new.ts:495 and GeminiAPIClient.ts:157.

  My Reproduction

  Same working request:

  POST https://co.yes.vg/gemini/v1beta/models/gemini-3.1-pro-preview:streamGenerateContent?alt=sse

  - Without these headers: Success
  - With only HTTP-Referer: Success
  - With only X-Title: Success
  - With both HTTP-Referer + X-Title: Failure, returns 503

  So this is a clear compatibility bug. In simple terms, Cherry Studio "casually stuffs two extra headers" into all modern providers, and this proxy happens to be triggered by both headers together to throw an exception.

  How to Determine Responsibility

  - Cherry Studio has a bug / design flaw: these headers should not be unconditionally injected into all modern chat requests.
  - The co.yes.vg proxy also has robustness issues: it shouldn't mark Gemini requests as provider_error just because of two non-auth headers.

  But standing on the question of "why it doesn't work in Cherry Studio", the most direct answer is: Cherry Studio's default header injection causes the failure.

  The analysis has been written to cherry-gemini-proxy-analysis.md, project documentation updated in AGENTS.md.

  If you want, my next step can directly provide a minimal fix patch for Cherry Studio: make defaultAppHeaders() no longer apply to Gemini provider, or add a toggle switch.
```

body:

- [x] I've filled in short, clear headings so that developers can quickly identify a rough idea of what to expect when flipping through the list of issues. And not "a suggestion", "stuck", etc.
- [x] I've confirmed that I am using the latest version of Cherry Studio.

### Platform

macOS

### Version

v1.7.25

### Bug Description

In Agent Settings, when attempting to delete the **only** accessible directory (working directory), the UI shows a success state but the directory is not actually removed. After the delete operation, the directory remains displayed in the list unchanged.

**Root Cause**: `BaseService.resolveAccessiblePaths()` in `src/main/services/agents/BaseService.ts` (line 269-275) treats an empty array `[]` the same as `undefined`, automatically replacing it with a default path:

```typescript
protected resolveAccessiblePaths(paths: string[] | undefined, id: string): string[] {
  if (!paths || paths.length === 0) {  // <-- Bug: empty array is treated as "not set"
    const shortId = id.substring(id.length - 9)
    paths = [path.join(getDataPath(), 'Agents', shortId)]
  }
  return this.ensurePathsExist(paths)
}
```

When the user deletes the last directory, `accessible_paths` becomes `[]`, which triggers the fallback logic that generates a new default path. This effectively makes it impossible to clear all accessible directories.

Both `AgentService.updateAgent()` and `SessionService.updateSession()` are affected since they both call `resolveAccessiblePaths()` during updates.

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Go to Agent Settings page
2. Create or select an agent that has exactly **one** accessible directory configured
3. Click the delete button next to the only accessible directory
4. Observe: The UI briefly reflects success, but the directory is still displayed in the list (or replaced by a default path)

### Expected Behavior

When the user deletes the only accessible directory, the directory should be removed and the accessible directories list should become empty. The `resolveAccessiblePaths()` should distinguish between:
- `undefined` (field not provided in update) -> keep existing paths
- `[]` (explicitly cleared by user) -> allow empty paths

### Relevant Log Output

N/A

### Additional Context

**Affected files:**
- `src/main/services/agents/BaseService.ts` - `resolveAccessiblePaths()` method (root cause)
- `src/main/services/agents/services/AgentService.ts` - `updateAgent()` calls `resolveAccessiblePaths()`
- `src/main/services/agents/services/SessionService.ts` - `updateSession()` calls `resolveAccessiblePaths()`
- `src/renderer/src/pages/settings/AgentSettings/components/AccessibleDirsSetting.tsx` - Frontend component (works correctly, issue is backend)

### Bug Description

`useUpdateSession` uses the global `mutate(listKey, ...)` from `swr` to update the session list cache after editing a session. However, `useSessions` uses `useSWRInfinite`, which stores its cache under a different internal key format (`$inf$` prefix + serialized page key), not the plain `listKey` string.

This means `mutate(listKey, ...)` in `useUpdateSession` **never actually updates the SWRInfinite list cache**. The UI shows stale session data (e.g., old name after rename) until SWR's automatic revalidation kicks in a few seconds later.

**Root cause in code:**

```typescript
// useUpdateSession.ts — uses global mutate with plain string key
mutate<ListAgentSessionsResponse['data']>(
  listKey,  // ❌ This key doesn't match useSWRInfinite's internal cache key
  (prev) => prev?.map((session) => (session.id === result.id ? result : session)) ?? []
)

// useSessions.ts — uses useSWRInfinite, cache key is [base, pageIndex, pageSize]
const getKey = (pageIndex, previousPageData) => {
  return [client.getSessionPaths(agentId).base, pageIndex, pageSize]
}
const { mutate } = useSWRInfinite(getKey, fetcher)
```

Additionally, `useUpdateSession` waits for the API response before updating the cache (no optimistic update), causing unnecessary UI delay.

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Open an Agent with multiple sessions
2. Double-click a session name to rename it
3. Type a new name and press Enter
4. Observe: the session name in the sidebar does NOT update immediately
5. Wait ~2-3 seconds, the name eventually updates via SWR revalidation

### Expected Behavior

The session name should update immediately in the sidebar after editing, without waiting for API response or SWR revalidation.

### Relevant Log Output

```shell
N/A
```

### Additional Context

The fix requires using `unstable_serialize` from `swr/infinite` to generate the correct SWRInfinite cache key, and implementing optimistic updates (update UI before API call, rollback on failure).

Each question is a valuable asset, but we are unable to handle Q&A across devices. The current backup mode is poor, and every update means losing something, leaving us helpless. Can we overwrite a question based on session ID and time, so that duplicate questions are not created?

### Desired Solution

1. **Unique Session ID**: Each session is assigned a unique ID, and all questions and answers are bound under this ID.
2. **Timestamp Management**: Each question and answer carries a timestamp. When the system receives a new question, it first checks whether the same question already exists under this session ID (can be judged by content hash or text similarity).
3. **Overwrite Update**: If a duplicate question is detected and the new question time is later, the new question overwrites the old question to avoid duplicate storage.
4. **Incremental Synchronization**: When synchronizing between devices, only newly added or updated content is transmitted, reducing data redundancy.

This design ensures that data is not lost while avoiding accumulation of duplicate questions, improving backup and recovery efficiency. If you need, I can help you write a simple pseudocode example to facilitate your understanding and implementation. What do you think?

# [Feature]: Extend Agent model support beyond Anthropic — allow Gemini, GitHub Copilot, and OpenAI-compatible providers

### Issue Checklist

- [x] I understand that issues are for reporting problems and requesting features, not for off-topic comments, and I will provide as much detail as possible to help resolve the issue.
- [x] I have checked the pinned issues and searched through the existing [open issues](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/issues), [closed issues](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20state%3Aclosed), and [discussions](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/discussions) and did not find a similar suggestion.
- [x] I have provided a short and descriptive title so that developers can quickly understand the issue when browsing the issue list, rather than vague titles like "A suggestion" or "Stuck."
- [x] The latest version of Cherry Studio does not include the feature I am suggesting.

### Platform

macOS

### Version

v1.7.24

### Is your feature request related to an existing issue?

Related to #12921, #12980, #12719, and #13444. All describe the same core limitation: Agent functionality is restricted to Anthropic-type providers only. This issue aims to consolidate and clearly define the feature request.

### Desired Solution

Currently, the Agent feature (claude-code mode) only supports Anthropic-type providers. The model selection in the Agent creation dialog filters providers via `getAnthropicSupportedProviders()`, which requires `provider.type === 'anthropic'` or a configured `anthropicApiHost`. The `AgentType` enum is hardcoded to `['claude-code']`.

This means providers like **Google Gemini**, **GitHub Copilot**, and any **OpenAI-compatible provider** cannot be used for Agents, even though they are fully configured and working for regular chat conversations.

**Requested changes:**
1. **Allow Gemini models as Agent backend** — Gemini 2.5 Pro/Flash support tool use, multi-turn conversations, and code generation, making them viable agent models.
2. **Allow GitHub Copilot models as Agent backend** — GitHub Copilot already provides access to Claude, GPT, and Gemini models via its API. Users with a Copilot subscription should be able to leverage these for Agents.
3. **More generally: support OpenAI-compatible endpoints for Agents** — Many providers (OpenRouter, Together, Groq, etc.) expose OpenAI-compatible APIs with models that support tool calling, which is the key capability needed for agentic use.

This would require abstracting the agent execution layer beyond the `@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk` to support other API formats (OpenAI Chat Completions, Gemini API).

### Alternative Solutions

- Using OpenRouter as a workaround to access non-Anthropic models — but OpenRouter currently also doesn't appear in the Agent model selection since it's not an Anthropic-type provider.
- Setting up a proxy that converts Anthropic API format to/from other formats (e.g., via newapi) — this is fragile and has known issues (see #12921).

### Additional Information

The current architecture ties agents tightly to the Anthropic SDK (`@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk`). A potential path forward could be leveraging the existing `ai-sdk` integrations (`@ai-sdk/google`, `@ai-sdk/openai`) that are already dependencies of the project, or implementing a provider-agnostic agent execution layer.

This is one of the most requested features based on the number of related issues.

title: [Bug]: API server agents handlers missing proper req.body validation
body:
### Issue Checklist

- [x] I understand that issues are for feedback and problem solving, not for complaining in the comment section, and will provide as much information as possible to help solve the problem.
- [x] My issue is not listed in the [FAQ](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/issues/3881).
- [x] I've looked at **pinned issues** and searched for existing [Open Issues](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/issues), [Closed Issues](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20state%3Aclosed), and [Discussions](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/discussions), no similar issue or discussion was found.
- [x] I've filled in short, clear headings so that developers can quickly identify a rough idea of what to expect when flipping through the list of issues. And not "a suggestion", "stuck", etc.
- [x] I've confirmed that I am using the latest version of Cherry Studio.

### Platform

All platforms (code-level issue)

### Version

main branch (latest)

### Bug Description

The API server's agents endpoints (`src/main/apiServer/routes/agents/handlers/agents.ts`) have several request body data validation gaps that could allow unvalidated or unsanitized data to reach the service layer.

**Issue 1: `createAgent` bypasses Zod-validated body**

In `handlers/agents.ts:58`, the `createAgent` handler passes raw `req.body` directly to `agentService.createAgent()` instead of using `req.validatedBody` (which is set by the Zod middleware). This means the Zod validation runs but its sanitized result is completely ignored:

```typescript
// Current (broken) - line 58
const agent = await agentService.createAgent(req.body)

// Expected (consistent with updateAgent/patchAgent)
const { validatedBody } = req as ValidationRequest
const agent = await agentService.createAgent(validatedBody)
```

In contrast, `updateAgent` (line 337-338) and `patchAgent` (line 483-484) correctly use `req.validatedBody`.

**Issue 2: `listAgents` query params `sortBy`/`orderBy` lack Zod validation**

In `handlers/agents.ts:186-189`, `sortBy` and `orderBy` are read directly from `req.query` with TypeScript `as` type assertions, but they are NOT defined in `PaginationQuerySchema`. Any arbitrary string value passes through without runtime validation:

```typescript
const sortBy = (req.query.sortBy as 'created_at' | 'updated_at' | 'name' | 'sort_order') || 'sort_order'
const orderBy = (req.query.orderBy as 'asc' | 'desc') || (sortBy === 'sort_order' ? 'asc' : 'desc')
```

**Issue 3: `reorderAgents` endpoint has no Zod middleware**

In `index.ts:391`, the reorder route is registered without any Zod validation middleware, unlike all other endpoints:

```typescript
agentsRouter.put('/reorder', agentHandlers.reorderAgents)  // No validator
```

It only has manual inline validation in the handler (lines 627-639), which is inconsistent with the codebase pattern.

**Issue 4: `validatedBody ?? {}` fallback can silently bypass validation**

In `handlers/agents.ts:338`:
```typescript
const replacePayload = (validatedBody ?? {}) as ReplaceAgentRequest
```

If `req.body` is `undefined`/`null`, the Zod middleware skips body validation (see `zodValidator.ts:20`: `if (config.body && req.body)`), and the handler falls back to `{}` — an empty object that bypasses all required field checks.

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Send a `POST /v1/agents` request — the handler uses raw `req.body` instead of `req.validatedBody`, so extra fields or unstripped data may reach the service layer.
2. Send a `GET /v1/agents?sortBy=INVALID_VALUE` — no validation error is returned despite invalid sort field.
3. Send a `PUT /v1/agents/reorder` — no Zod validation middleware runs, only manual inline checks.
4. Send a `PUT /v1/agents/:id` with `Content-Type: application/json` but empty body — falls back to `{}` silently.

### Expected Behavior

1. `createAgent` should use `req.validatedBody` (like `updateAgent`/`patchAgent` do) instead of raw `req.body`.
2. `sortBy` and `orderBy` should be added to `PaginationQuerySchema` with proper enum validation.
3. `reorderAgents` (and `reorderSessions`) should use a Zod validation middleware consistent with other endpoints.
4. The `validatedBody ?? {}` fallback should be removed — if validation didn't produce a result, the request should be rejected.

### Relevant Log Output

_No response_

### Additional Context

Affected files:
- `src/main/apiServer/routes/agents/handlers/agents.ts` — handlers
- `src/main/apiServer/routes/agents/validators/agents.ts` — validators
- `src/main/apiServer/routes/agents/validators/zodValidator.ts` — Zod middleware
- `src/main/apiServer/routes/agents/index.ts` — route registration
- `src/renderer/src/types/agent.ts` — Zod schema definitions

The same `reorderSessions` endpoint in `handlers/sessions.ts` and the `validatedBody ?? {}` pattern in session handlers likely have the same issues.

title: [Bug]: Chat history search navigates to blank page when clicking a message result
body:
## Bug Description

When using the chat history message search feature, clicking on a search result shows a blank message area instead of the message content.

## Root Cause Analysis

**Race condition** between async data loading and synchronous UI rendering.

In `HistoryPage.tsx` line 67-71, `onMessageClick` dispatches an async thunk and sets state simultaneously:

```typescript
const onMessageClick = (message: Message) => {
  dispatch(loadTopicMessagesThunk(message.topicId))  // async — blocks not yet in Redux
  setStack(['topics', 'search', 'message'])           // sync — triggers render immediately
  setMessage(message)                                  // sync — SearchMessage renders now
}
```

`SearchMessage` renders `MessageItem` → `MessageContent` → `MessageBlockRenderer`, which reads blocks from Redux store:

```typescript
// Blocks/index.tsx line 117-119
const blockEntities = useSelector(messageBlocksSelectors.selectEntities)
const renderedBlocks = blocks.map((blockId) => blockEntities[blockId]).filter(Boolean)
// → blockEntities is empty because loadTopicMessagesThunk hasn't completed yet
// → renderedBlocks = [] → blank content
```

After `loadTopicMessagesThunk` completes and Redux updates, `SearchMessage` does **not** re-render because its `message` comes from props (Dexie object), not from the Redux store.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open Cherry Studio
2. Use the chat history search
3. Type a keyword to search messages
4. Click on a search result message
5. **Expected**: Message content is displayed
6. **Actual**: Blank page — message container renders but content area is empty

## Suggested Fix

**Option A** — Await thunk before rendering:

```typescript
const onMessageClick = async (message: Message) => {
  await dispatch(loadTopicMessagesThunk(message.topicId))
  setStack(['topics', 'search', 'message'])
  setMessage(message)
}
```

**Option B** — Add loading state in SearchMessage that waits for blocks:

```typescript
const blockEntities = useSelector(messageBlocksSelectors.selectEntities)
const blocksLoaded = message?.blocks?.every(blockId => !!blockEntities[blockId]) ?? false

if (!blocksLoaded) {
  return <Spin />
}
```

## Related Files

- `src/renderer/src/pages/history/HistoryPage.tsx` (line 67-71)
- `src/renderer/src/pages/history/components/SearchMessage.tsx`
- `src/renderer/src/pages/home/Messages/Blocks/index.tsx` (line 115-119)
- `src/renderer/src/store/thunk/messageThunk.ts` (line 1792-1827)

## Environment

- Cherry Studio v1.8.0
- OS: macOS
