### Is your feature request related to an existing issue?

I sometimes mistakenly delete or modify something without a corresponding backup beforehand... because the backup interval is too high (6 hours). I thought of lowering the backup interval to solve this problem (1 minute), but this would make my storage explode...

### Desired Solution

I propose adding a "Backup Plan" feature with the following functionality:
Users can create multiple independent backup plans, each configurable with custom parameters including:
- Backup interval
- Maximum number of retained backups
- Backup storage path
- Other relevant settings

This would let me set up a high-frequency plan (e.g., 1-minute interval, max 60 backups) to prevent accidental data loss without excessive storage usage, alongside a separate low-frequency plan (longer interval, higher max backup count) for long-term archiving. This would fully resolve the tradeoff between data safety and storage consumption.

### Alternative Solutions

As a simplified alternative if full customizability is not feasible, I suggest implementing three pre-configured fixed backup plans (e.g., high-frequency, medium-frequency, low-frequency). This would significantly reduce development workload while still solving the core problem.

title: [Bug]: MCP tool result displayed as raw JSON — agentic loop terminates without natural language response
body: ### Issue Checklist - [x] I understand that issues are for feedback and problem solving, not for complaining in the comment section, and will provide as much information as possible to help solve the problem. - [x] My issue is not listed in the [FAQ](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/issues/3881). - [x] I've looked at **pinned issues** and searched for existing [Open Issues](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/issues), [Closed Issues](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20state%3Aclosed), and [Discussions](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/discussions), no similar issue or discussion was found. - [x] I've filled in short, clear headings so that developers can quickly identify a rough idea of what to expect when flipping through the list of issues. And not "a suggestion", "stuck", etc. - [x] I've confirmed that I am using the latest version of Cherry Studio. ### Platform macOS ### Version v1.9.1 ### Bug Description When using any MCP tool in a regular chat session, Cherry Studio displays the raw JSON tool response in the chat window and then terminates the process entirely. The model never receives the tool result back to interpret it and respond in natural language. The agentic loop stops after the first tool call instead of continuing to a follow-up completion. **Example output instead of a natural language response:** ``` { "params": { "query": "user preferences", "top_k": 10 }, "response": { "content": [{ "type": "text", "text": "{\"count\": 1, \"confidence\": \"low\", \"memories\": [{...}]}" }], "isError": false } } ``` The model produces no text after this. The conversation is terminated. ## Key Isolation Evidence - The **exact same MCP config works correctly in Msty Studio** — tool is called, result is fed back to the model, and the model responds in natural language. This confirms the MCP server and config are correct, and the bug is Cherry Studio's agentic loop. - Sending a follow-up message like "now summarize what you found in plain English" causes Cherry Studio to call the tool **again** from scratch, rather than using the already-returned result. ## Related Issues - Closed issue #10606 describes a related `finishReason: tool-calls` termination bug but was resolved via a workaround (hardcoding stepCountIs = 200). That fix does not address this issue — the tool call completes and returns a result, but the result is never passed back to the model. - Closed issue #9317 describes a similar symptom but the original poster's workaround does not apply here. ## Environment - Cherry Studio: v1.9.1 - OS: macOS (MacBook Air) - Model: Claude Sonnet 4.6 - Provider: Poe OpenAI-compatible API (https://api.poe.com/v1) - MCP Server: widemem-ai (Python stdio, pip install widemem-ai[mcp]) - Embedding: sentence-transformers (local) - MCP server status in Cherry Studio UI: shows as "connected" ### Steps To Reproduce 1. Configure a Python-based stdio MCP server (widemem-ai) in Cherry Studio settings 2. Start a new chat using Claude Sonnet 4.6 via a Poe OpenAI-compatible endpoint (https://api.poe.com/v1) 3. Ask the model to use a widemem tool (e.g. widemem_search or widemem_health) 4. Observe: raw JSON tool response is displayed, no natural language reply follows ### Expected Behavior After the tool result is returned, Cherry Studio should feed it back to the model for a second completion pass, so the model can interpret the result and respond in plain English — as is standard in any correct MCP agentic loop implementation. ## Actual Behavior Cherry Studio displays the raw JSON tool output and terminates the process. The model never gets a chance to interpret the result. ### Relevant Log Output ```shell See additional context for the log file. ``` ### Additional Context ### **### [cherry-studio-console-log.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/26773918/cherry-studio-console-log.txt)**

title: [Feature]: Ship generic Drawer in packages/ui and refactor Code Tool page per v2 design
body:
### Issue Checklist

- [x] I understand that issues are for reporting problems and requesting features, not for off-topic comments, and I will provide as much detail as possible to help resolve the issue.
- [x] I have checked the pinned issues and searched through the existing open issues, closed issues, and discussions and did not find a similar suggestion.
- [x] I have provided a short and descriptive title so that developers can quickly understand the issue when browsing the issue list, rather than vague titles like "A suggestion" or "Stuck."
- [x] The latest version of Cherry Studio does not include the feature I am suggesting.

### Platform

macOS

### Version

v2.0.0-alpha (branch: v2, working branch: feat/v2/code-tool-ui)

### Is your feature request related to an existing issue?

The Code Tool page on the v2 branch (`src/renderer/src/pages/code/CodeCliPage.tsx`) currently relies on antd + styled-components and diverges from the v2 design spec. It needs a Tailwind + shadcn refactor.

Multiple v2 pages also use a right-side drawer interaction (Translate, Chat, Paint, Explore, Code Tool — 6 drawers total per internal drawer-audit research). The drawers split into two distinct kinds:

1. **Viewport-modal drawers** — cover the whole screen with a backdrop. Already served by the existing shadcn `Drawer` primitive.
2. **In-page side drawers** — anchored inside the page area, surrounding layout remains visible and interactive alongside. No reusable component yet; each page would otherwise reimplement it.

This issue lands the in-page side drawer as `PageSidePanel` under `packages/ui` and uses it in the Code Tool refactor.

### Desired Solution

#### 1. Ship `PageSidePanel` under `packages/ui`

- **In-page** side drawer: positioned `absolute` within its nearest positioned parent, **not** viewport-fixed. The surrounding page layout stays visible and interactive alongside the panel.
- For a full-screen modal that covers the whole viewport with a backdrop, use the existing shadcn `Drawer` primitive instead. `PageSidePanel` is complementary, not a replacement.
- Built on `framer-motion` for enter/exit animation (already a peer dep of `packages/ui`).
- API:
  - `<PageSidePanel>` container: `open`, `onClose`, `side` (`'left' | 'right'`), `showCloseButton`, `closeLabel`
  - `header?: ReactNode` slot (single flexible slot; the earlier triple-slot `leading / title / trailing` design was dropped in favor of letting callers compose freely)
  - `footer?: ReactNode` slot
  - `children`: body (auto-scrollable)
  - Per-slot `*ClassName` override props
- A WHY comment at the top of the file explains the difference from shadcn `Drawer` so future contributors don't recreate a viewport-fixed alternative.

#### 2. Refactor the Code Tool page to match the v2 design

- **Main page** (`CodeCliPage.tsx`)
  - Top breadcrumb (`</> Code Tool  N items`)
  - Centered search input
  - Tool grid: 8 official CLI tools (Claude Code, Qwen Code, Gemini CLI, OpenAI Codex, iFlow CLI, GitHub Copilot CLI, Kimi CLI, OpenCode), each with its brand SVG icon
  - Empty state (preset + title + description)
  - Bun-missing warning banner uses the `--warning` semantic token (no hardcoded amber)

- **Detail drawer** (triggered by clicking a tool card) — built on `PageSidePanel`
  - Header: tool icon + name
  - Body: tool info card (icon + name + category tag) + fields (model / working directory / terminal / environment variables / auto-update)
  - Footer: meta row (tool · model · terminal) + primary "Launch" CTA
  - Launch button toggles between default / loading (spinner) / success ("Launched") states

#### 3. Supporting composites and assets (in scope)

Landed in `packages/ui` as general-purpose composites reused by this refactor and future pages:

- **`EmptyState`** — preset icon + title / description / primary / secondary action, supports `compact` mode
- **`SelectDropdown`** — generic (`<T extends { id: string }>`) popover select with custom `renderSelected` / `renderItem`, optional per-row `onRemove` (used for the working-directory recent list), optional empty state, and **optional virtualized rows** via `@tanstack/react-virtual` for large datasets (hundreds of models)

Landed in renderer assets:

- 8 CLI tool SVG icons under `src/renderer/src/assets/images/code-cli/` (`claude-code` / `qwen-code` / `gemini-cli` / `openai-codex` / `iflow-cli` / `github-copilot-cli` / `kimi-cli` / `open-code`)

Page-local helpers (remain in `pages/code/components/`, not promoted):

- `CliIconBadge` — tool icon tile (img or first-letter fallback)
- `FieldLabel` — compact label + info tooltip
- `ToolGrid` — icon card grid (used only by Code Tool for now)
- `CodeToolDrawer` — the Code-Tool-specific drawer built on `PageSidePanel`

### Alternative Solutions

- **Reuse shadcn `Sheet` / `Drawer` directly for the in-page drawer** — rejected. Those are viewport-fixed modals; they occupy the whole screen with an overlay and do not match the v2 design where the surrounding page stays visible.
- **Skip the shared `PageSidePanel` and implement a local drawer inside the Code Tool page** — rejected. Does not serve the reuse needs of the other v2 pages that share the in-page drawer pattern.
- **Migrate all 6 drawers to the shared component in one go** — rejected. Scope too large, conflicts with the v2 incremental migration strategy. This issue only lands the first use case on the Code Tool page.

### Additional Information

- **Tech constraints**: Tailwind CSS + shadcn (`packages/ui`); antd / HeroUI / styled-components are prohibited in the new code.
- **Tokens**: colors route through theme CSS variables (`--color-foreground`, `--color-background`, `--color-primary`, `--color-secondary`, `--color-muted`, `--color-warning`, …). ### Platform

### Bug Description

When using the DeepSeek Reasoner (deepseek-reasoner) model, MCP tool calls fail with a 400 error from the API.

Error message:
```
API Error: 400 {"error":{"message":"Failed to deserialize the JSON body into the target type: messages[5].content: unknown variant tool_reference, expected one of text, image, document at line 1 column 6755","type":"invalid_request_error","param":null,"code":"invalid_request_error"}}
```

Problem analysis:
The DeepSeek API's messages.content only supports three types: text/image/document, but Cherry Studio puts tool results in the message history as `tool_reference` type after MCP tool calls, causing the DeepSeek API to fail parsing.

Note: This issue reproduces whenever MCP tool calls are triggered, even in new conversations.

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Configure MCP servers in Cherry Studio settings (e.g., filesystem, web_search, etc.)
2. Click "New Conversation"
3. Select model as "DeepSeek Reasoner" (deepseek-reasoner)
4. Send a message that triggers a tool call, such as "Search for today's news" or "What files are in the current directory"
5. After tool execution completes, the model returns a 400 error
6. Error message: unknown variant `tool_reference`, expected one of `text`, `image`, `document`

### Expected Behavior

After MCP tool call completion, the DeepSeek model should receive tool results normally and generate a reply without API format errors.

Alternatively, if the DeepSeek model doesn't support the `tool_reference` format, Cherry Studio should perform format conversion before calling.

### Relevant Log Output

```shell
API Error: 400 {"error":{"message":"Failed to deserialize the JSON body into the target type: messages[5].content: unknown variant tool_reference, expected one of text, image, document at line 1 column 6755","type":"invalid_request_error","param":null,"code":"invalid_request_error"}}

Details:
Tokens:946↑612↓334
```

### Additional Context

- DeepSeek API documentation indicates it only supports three content types: text/image/document
- Related Issue: #3474 previously fixed tool content format issues for doubao/deepseek models, but may not have covered the deepseek-reasoner case
- Temporary workaround: Disable MCP tool calls, or switch to deepseek-chat model, or use Claude/GPT models

Reference: https://api-docs.deepseek.com/guides/function_calling

title: feat: extend mcp__claw__notify to support image/file sending via WeChat channel
body:
## Summary

Currently, the `notify` MCP tool only supports plain text messages. When using the WeChat channel adapter, `WeixinBot` already has `sendImage()` and `sendFile()` methods implemented in `WeChatProtocol.ts`, but they are never called — `WeChatAdapter.sendMessage()` only handles text, and the `notify` tool schema has no image/file parameters.

## Current Behavior

`mcp__claw__notify` only accepts `message` (string) and `channel_id` (string). Any image/file path sent as text arrives in WeChat as plain text, not as an actual image or file.

## Expected Behavior

Extend `notify` to optionally accept an image or file:

```json
{
  "message": "string (optional caption)",
  "channel_id": "string (optional)",
  "image_path": "string — absolute local file path to an image",
  "image_base64": "string — base64-encoded image data",
  "file_path": "string — absolute local file path (PDF, DOCX, etc.)"
}
```

**Why This Matters**
Agents that generate images (e.g. via Gemini image generation) or produce documents cannot deliver results to the user's WeChat. They are forced to upload to Imgur and send a URL — significantly worse UX.

WeixinBot.sendImage(userId, imageData: Buffer) is already fully implemented with AES encryption + CDN upload + iLink API. The missing piece is only the plumbing from the MCP tool down to the adapter.

**Suggested Fix (minimal, 3 files)**
1. `claw.ts` — add image_path / image_base64 / file_path to NOTIFY_TOOL inputSchema; detect in sendNotification() and call adapter.sendMedia()
2. `ChannelAdapter.ts` — add optional sendMedia(chatId, data: Buffer, mediaType: 'image'|'file', fileName?: string) to base class
3. `WeChatAdapter.ts` — implement sendMedia() calling this.bot.sendImage() or this.bot.sendFile()

title: [Feature]: v2 UI Boundary and Theme Contract Consolidation Refactoring
body:
> [\!NOTE]
> This issue was translated by Claude.

### Issue Checklist

- [x] I understand that issues are for reporting problems and requesting features, not for off-topic comments, and I will provide as much detail as possible to help resolve the issue.
- [x] I have checked the pinned issues and searched through the existing [open issues](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/issues), [closed issues](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20state%3Aclosed), and [discussions](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/discussions) and did not find a similar suggestion.
- [x] I have provided a short and descriptive title so that developers can quickly understand the issue when browsing the issue list, rather than vague titles like "A suggestion" or "Stuck."
- [x] The latest version of Cherry Studio does not include the feature I am suggesting.

### Platform

macOS

### Version

v2 branch / draft PR #14328

### Is your feature request related to an existing issue?

Yes. Currently, packages/ui and the renderer style system have long borne excessive migration responsibilities, leading to unclear boundaries, theme contracts, and style ownership. The main manifestations are:

1. @cherrystudio/ui is more like an internal migration directory within the monorepo, rather than a UI package with stable boundaries.
2. Contract drift exists between style entry points, icon entry points, and actual build artifacts.
3. On the renderer side, UI theme contract, app-shell token, and legacy compatibility variables coexist, with mixed responsibilities.
4. Some feature/component private styles are still placed in the shared assets/styles directory, increasing the global style burden.
5. Old variables still survive in large numbers in the renderer, and new usage lacks continuous constraints.

### Desired Solution

Centered on the v2 direction, complete a "UI infrastructure consolidation" refactoring, focusing on:

1. Consolidate the package boundaries of @cherrystudio/ui.
   - Align exports, build artifacts, and actual consumption patterns.
   - Clarify that tokens/* is the design source, and theme.css is the public contract.
   - Clean up issues where internal implementation paths masquerade as public APIs.

2. Clean up the penetration of old tech stack into the UI public layer.
   - Remove antd and styled-components from the formal export layer of the UI package.
   - Distinguish between "formal v2 UI capabilities" and "migration compatibility layer".

3. Reorganize the renderer's Tailwind bridge and legacy compatibility layer.
   - Keep app-shell-specific tokens.
   - Isolate legacy variable migration bridges in a centralized manner.
   - Provide lint and PR comment reminders for new legacy variable usage.

4. Consolidate the ownership of feature-scoped stylesheets.
   - Keep only truly shared styles in assets/styles.
   - Move local styles like CommandListPopover and selection-toolbar back to their component or window directories.

5. Clean up peripheral assets and documentation drift.
   - Sync README, stories, and style references.
   - Simplify duplicate files in the design reference / docs directory.
   - Clean up unused icons and related story drift.

### Alternative Solutions

1. Continue migrating file by file without first consolidating boundaries.
   - Benefit: Individual changes are smaller.
   - Problem: The responsibilities of the UI package and renderer will continue to mix, making subsequent migration costs higher.

2. Only handle the component layer, not the style contract and toolchain.
   - Problem: Theme contract, Tailwind scan sources, and legacy variable incremental governance won't truly stabilize.

3. Split more packages at once.
   - May be more ideal in the long term, but at the current stage, it's more realistic and lower risk to first stabilize the boundaries and contracts.

### Additional Information

This issue is used to record the goals and scope of this round of v2 UI consolidation refactoring, facilitating the continued advancement of remaining cleanup work.

Related documentation:
- v2-refactor-temp/docs/ui/ui-library-current-issues.md

Related PRs:
- #14328

Key areas already covered in this round:
- UI package boundary and documentation consolidation
- Theme contract build pipeline establishment
- Renderer Tailwind bridge reorganization
- Legacy var lint / PR comment reminder mechanism
- Recovery of local style files from global assets/styles to belonging modules

Items that can continue to be advanced:
- Continuously reduce actual usage points of legacy vars in renderer
- Further evaluate development assets that can be separated in packages/ui
- Continue to verify UI package contract consistency in truly independent publishing scenarios

### Is your feature request related to an existing issue?

是。当前 packages/ui 与 renderer 样式体系长期承担了过多迁移职责，导致边界、主题契约和样式归属不清晰，主要表现为：

1. @cherrystudio/ui 更像 monorepo 内部迁移目录，而不是边界稳定的 UI 包。
2. 样式入口、图标入口和实际构建产物之间存在契约漂移。
3. renderer 一侧同时存在 UI theme contract、app-shell token、legacy compatibility variable，职责混杂。
4. 一些 feature/component 私有样式仍放在共享 assets/styles 目录下，增加了全局样式负担。
5. 旧变量仍在 renderer 大量存活，新增使用缺少持续约束。

### Desired Solution

围绕 v2 方向，完成一次面向"UI 基础设施收口"的重构，重点包括：

1. 收口 @cherrystudio/ui 的包边界。
   - 对齐 exports、构建产物和实际消费方式。
   - 明确 tokens/* 是设计源，theme.css 是公开 contract。
   - 清理内部实现路径伪装成 public API 的问题。

2. 清理旧技术栈对 UI 公共层的渗透。
   - 将 antd、styled-components 从 UI 包的正式导出层移除。
   - 区分"正式 v2 UI 能力"和"迁移兼容层"。

3. 重组 renderer 的 Tailwind bridge 与 legacy compatibility layer。
   - 保留 app-shell 专属 token。
   - 将 legacy var 迁移桥接集中隔离。
   - 为新增 legacy var 使用提供 lint 和 PR 评论提醒。

4. 收口 feature-scoped stylesheet 的归属。
   - 只保留真正共享的样式在 assets/styles。
   - 将 CommandListPopover、selection-toolbar 这类局部样式移回所属组件或窗口目录。

5. 清理外围资产与文档漂移。
   - 同步 README、stories、styles reference。
   - 精简 design reference / docs 目录中的重复文件。
   - 清理未使用图标和相关 story 漂移。

### Alternative Solutions

1. 继续按文件零散迁移，不先做边界收口。
   - 好处是单次改动更小。
   - 问题是 UI 包和 renderer 的职责会继续混杂，后续迁移成本更高。

2. 只处理组件层，不处理样式契约与工具链。
   - 问题是 theme contract、Tailwind 扫描源、legacy var 增量治理不会真正稳定下来。

3. 一次性拆分更多包。
   - 长期可能更理想，但当前阶段先把边界和契约收稳更现实，风险也更低。

### Additional Information

本 issue 用于记录这一轮 v2 UI 收口重构的目标与范围，便于后续继续推进剩余清理工作。

相关文档：
- v2-refactor-temp/docs/ui/ui-library-current-issues.md

相关 PR：
- #14328

本轮已经覆盖的重点：
- UI 包边界与文档收口
- 主题 contract build 链路建立
- renderer Tailwind bridge 重组
- legacy var lint / PR comment 提醒机制
- 局部样式文件从全局 assets/styles 回收至所属模块

后续仍可继续推进的事项：
- 持续减少 renderer 对 legacy var 的真实使用点
- 进一步评估 packages/ui 中可拆离的开发期资产
- 在真正独立发布场景下继续校验 UI 包契约一致性

</details>

title: [Feature]: Redesign Translate page UI to match v2 design spec
body:
### Issue Checklist

- [x] I understand that issues are for reporting problems and requesting features, not for off-topic comments, and I will provide as much detail as possible to help resolve the issue.
- [x] I have checked the pinned issues and searched through the existing open issues, closed issues, and discussions and did not find a similar suggestion.
- [x] I have provided a short and descriptive title so that developers can quickly understand the issue when browsing the issue list, rather than vague titles like "A suggestion" or "Stuck."
- [x] The latest version of Cherry Studio does not include the feature I am suggesting.

### Platform

macOS

### Version

v2.0.0-alpha

### Is your feature request related to an existing issue?

The Translate page (`src/renderer/src/pages/translate/`) still relies on legacy stack components (antd `Modal` / `Drawer` / `FloatButton`, `styled-components`), which conflict with the v2 UI direction (`@cherrystudio/ui` + Tailwind, no antd / styled-components for new work). The visual design has also diverged from the latest spec maintained in the internal `cherry-studio-ui-design` reference repo (`src/features/translate/TranslatePage.tsx`).

### Desired Solution

Rebuild the Translate page UI to match the v2 design spec while keeping all existing business logic, data hooks, and i18n flow unchanged. **This issue covers the UI layer only** — any new data / behavior introduced by the spec is explicitly deferred (see *Deferred* below).

#### Scope

**Layout & structure**
- Two-column rounded-card layout (source / target panes) with a lightweight top bar inside the existing `Navbar`.
- Extract reusable components under `src/renderer/src/pages/translate/components/`:
  - `TranslateLanguageBar` — language row with swap button.
  - `TranslateInputPane` — source textarea, file upload, char counter, clear.
  - `TranslateOutputPane` — target textarea, copy, translate / abort.
  - `TranslateModelSelect` — redesigned model picker (340px dropdown, keyword filter, 4 capability tags: vision / reasoning / tools / free; uses `ModelAvatar`, reuses `useProviders` and existing capability predicates).

**History panel (`TranslateHistory.tsx`)**
- Replace antd `Drawer` with a motion-based floating panel; two-state list / detail.
- Native `<button>` for all icon actions (back, copy, reuse, star, delete).
- Keep `DynamicVirtualList`, starred filter, delete, and `ConfirmDialog` for clear-all.
- Remove the search input (not in spec).

**Settings (`TranslateSettings.tsx`)**
- Replace antd `Modal` with a right-side drawer.
- Inline the Prompt editor (`TranslatePromptField`) and custom language list (`CustomLanguageList`) — drop the "more settings" entry point.
- Remove emoji input from custom language form to match spec.

**Styling**
- Add `translate.css` scoped to `#translate-page` that overrides token values (`--radius-*`, `--color-primary`, `--color-muted`, `--color-accent`) locally — do **not** modify global `packages/ui` theme.
- Remove `styled-components` usage from the page.

**i18n**
- Add `translate.history.{back, source, target, reuse, copy_target, filter.starred}` in `en-us`, `zh-cn`, `zh-tw`.

#### Non-goals

- No changes to translation service, DB schema, or preference keys.
- No mock business features — anything without a backing data model is out of scope.
- `TranslateSettingsPopup.tsx` source file kept but no longer referenced (cleanup in a follow-up).

#### Deferred (follow-up PRs)

The reference design introduces capabilities that require new data models or service logic. These are **out of scope** for this UI refactor and will be tracked in separate issues / PRs:

- **Assistant selection** on the translate page (e.g. per-assistant prompt presets).
- **New fields** present in the design spec but not backed by the current data layer.

For this refactor, the UI will either omit these elements or render them as visual-only placeholders that do not dispatch any behavior, so the layout matches the spec without introducing mock data.

#### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Visual parity with the reference design for all currently-backed features.
- [ ] No `antd`, `styled-components`, or `HeroUI` imports in the translate page tree.
- [ ] All existing translate features still work: language swap, file upload, streaming output, abort, copy, history list / detail / reuse / star / delete / clear, custom language CRUD, prompt editing.
- [ ] `pnpm lint`, `pnpm test`, `pnpm format` all pass.
- [ ] Manual QA on narrow / wide window widths (verify `TranslateModelSelect` dropdown does not overflow).

### Alternative Solutions

N/A — rewriting against the v2 stack is already the agreed direction (see `CLAUDE.md` v2 Refactoring section). Incrementally patching the existing antd-based implementation was considered and rejected because it cannot satisfy the "no antd / styled-components" constraint for v2.

### Additional Information

- Branch: `feat/v2/translate-page-ui`
- Related guidance: project `CLAUDE.md` → *v2 Refactoring (In Progress)* (UI layer must use `@cherrystudio/ui` + Tailwind; antd / HeroUI / styled-components prohibited).

title: [Bug]: Local OpenAI-compatible API does not rotate/split comma-separated provider API keys, causing 403 Authorization failed for providers like NVIDIA while UI chat works
body:

- [x] I've filled in short, clear headings so that developers can quickly identify a rough idea of what to expect when flipping through the list of issues. And not "a suggestion", "stuck", etc.
- [x] I've confirmed that I am using the latest version of Cherry Studio.

### Platform

macOS

### Version

1.9.1

### Bug Description

When a custom OpenAI-compatible provider in Cherry Studio is configured with multiple comma-separated API keys, the provider works correctly in the Cherry Studio UI chat, but fails through the local OpenAI-compatible API at http://127.0.0.1:23333/v1/chat/completions.

The failure returned by the local API is:

403 {"status":403,"title":"Forbidden","detail":"Authorization failed"}
This creates inconsistent behavior between:

Cherry Studio UI chat: works
Cherry Studio local API: fails



### Steps To Reproduce


When a custom OpenAI-compatible provider in Cherry Studio is configured with multiple comma-separated API keys, the provider works correctly in the Cherry Studio UI chat, but fails through the local OpenAI-compatible API at http://127.0.0.1:23333/v1/chat/completions.

The failure returned by the local API is:

403 {"status":403,"title":"Forbidden","detail":"Authorization failed"}
This creates inconsistent behavior between:

Cherry Studio UI chat: works
Cherry Studio local API: fails



In my case, this affects a custom provider pointing to NVIDIA's OpenAI-compatible endpoint, with models such as:

moonshotai/kimi-k2.5
qwen/qwen3.5-397b-a17b
After investigation, the issue appears to be that:

the Cherry Studio UI path splits and rotates comma-separated API keys before sending upstream requests
the local API path does not, and instead forwards the full raw comma-separated apiKey string as a single key
As a result, upstream authentication fails only for the local API path.

I confirmed this by patching the local API to use the same key-rotation behavior as the UI. After that patch, the same local API requests succeeded immediately.

### Expected Behavior

The local API should behave like Cherry Studio UI chat and successfully call the upstream provider using one rotated/split API key.

### Relevant Log Output

```shell

```

### Additional Context

Important evidence
I verified all of the following:

The same nvidia models work in Cherry Studio UI chat
The same models fail via 127.0.0.1:23333/v1/chat/completions
Direct upstream call to NVIDIA succeeds when using a single Bearer key
After patching Cherry Studio local API to split/rotate comma-separated keys like the UI does, the local API succeeds immediately for:
moonshotai/kimi-k2.5
qwen/qwen3.5-397b-a17b
Root cause analysis
In Cherry Studio 1.9.1, the UI path rotates keys:

UI path uses getRotatedApiKey(provider)
it does provider.apiKey.split(",")
Relevant code from extracted app bundle:

out/renderer/assets/store-CSNQI1kC.js
around line 348969
The UI also injects the rotated key before inference:

out/renderer/assets/store-CSNQI1kC.js
around line 348646
But the local API path does not:

out/main/index.js
around line 206433
It directly does something equivalent to:

new OpenAI({
  baseURL: provider.apiHost,
  apiKey: provider.apiKey
})
So if provider.apiKey is "key1,key2,key3", the local API sends the full string upstream instead of one valid key.

Minimal fix suggestion
Please make the local API path use the same key-selection logic as the UI path.

For example, before constructing the OpenAI client, resolve:

split provider.apiKey by comma
trim/filter
select one key using the same rotation logic as UI
pass only that single key to the OpenAI client
Why this matters
This breaks Cherry Studio’s local OpenAI-compatible API for any provider using multiple comma-separated API keys, even though the provider works normally inside the Cherry Studio UI.

It also breaks downstream integrations that rely on the local API, such as OpenClaw.

Workaround
Use only a single API key in the provider config, or patch the local API to rotate/split keys like the UI path.

title: [Bug]: v2 fresh install — every message fails with "Topic not found" (stale topic id persists across assistant creation)
body:
### Issue Checklist

- [x] I understand that issues are for feedback and problem solving, not for complaining in the comment section, and will provide as much information as possible to help solve the problem.
- [x] My issue is not listed in the [FAQ](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/issues/3881).
- [x] I've looked at **pinned issues** and searched for existing [Open Issues](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/issues), [Closed Issues](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20state%3Aclosed), and [Discussions](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/discussions), no similar issue or discussion was found.
- [x] I've filled in short, clear headings so that developers can quickly identify a rough idea of what to expect when flipping through the list of issues. And not "a suggestion", "stuck", etc.
- [x] I've confirmed that I am using the latest version of Cherry Studio.

### Platform

macOS

### Version

v2.0.0-alpha (v2 branch, dev mode)

### Bug Description

On a fresh v2 dev-mode install (no previous Cherry Studio data), every attempt to send a message fails with Topic not found. The same topic id (15f44cf4-39f1-40ff-b60d-8e2f79c5799d in my session) is referenced across every send, even after creating a brand new assistant via the UI — meaning the renderer is persisting a "current topic" reference that was never inserted into the v2 SQLite topics table.
Creating a new assistant does not create an associated topic in SQLite, and the renderer's persisted topic reference does not get reset. Every send thus posts to POST /topics/15f44cf4-.../messages, which hits MessageService.create and throws DataApiError with code: 'NOT_FOUND', resource: 'Topic'.
Additional renderer warning observed during the same sessions:
[mainWindow::useAssistantPresets] Assistant preset with id default not found in state.
This may be a related symptom: renderer expects a default assistant preset that does not exist in SQLite (no seeder creates it).
Impact: The app is completely unusable on a fresh v2 install — no message can be sent. This blocks any first-time user (including every 1.9.x user after upgrade if their data is not migrated or migration fails silently).

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Check out the v2 branch on a machine that has never run Cherry Studio in dev mode (macOS in my case).
2. Run pnpm install && pnpm dev.
   - Dev mode writes its profile to <default userData>Dev (see src/main/core/preboot/userDataLocation.ts:113-116), so no existing data is migrated — this is a truly empty profile.
3. Open the app; no default assistant or topic is present in the UI.
4. Click + to create a new assistant. Assistant is created successfully.
5. Select the new assistant, type any message (e.g. Hello) in the chat input, press Enter.
6. Observe: message fails immediately; error logged as below.

### Expected Behavior

A fresh v2 install should be usable out of the box. Sending the first message should either:
- Succeed because a default assistant and topic were seeded on first run, OR
- Succeed because the renderer creates an assistant + topic (and persists them to SQLite via DataApi) when the user creates them via the UI and then sends a message.
- 
Either way, no Topic not found error should occur on first use.

### Relevant Log Output

```shell
16:37:37.947 <ERROR> [mainWindow::DataApiService] Request failed: POST /topics/15f44cf4-39f1-40ff-b60d-8e2f79c5799d/messages Error: Topic with id '15f44cf4-39f1-40ff-b60d-8e2f79c5799d' not found
    at async StreamingService.createUserMessage (http://localhost:5173/src/services/messageStreaming/StreamingService.ts:444:31)
    at async http://localhost:5173/src/store/thunk/messageThunk.ts:846:36
16:37:37.947 <ERROR> [mainWindow::MessageThunk] Error in sendMessage thunk: [Error: Topic with id '15f44cf4-39f1-40ff-b60d-8e2f79c5799d' not found]
DataApiError: { code: 'NOT_FOUND', status: 404, details: { resource: 'Topic', id: '15f44cf4-39f1-40ff-b60d-8e2f79c5799d' }, requestContext: undefined }
[mainWindow::useAssistantPresets] Assistant preset with id default not found in state.
[DataApi:Server] Topic with id '15f44cf4-39f1-40ff-b60d-8e2f79c5799d' not found
```

### Additional Context

1. No assistant/topic seeder exists. src/main/data/db/seeding/index.ts registers only PreferenceSeeder, TranslateLanguageSeeder, and PresetProviderSeeder. There is no seeder for default assistants or topics. Consequently, fresh SQLite databases start with empty assistants and topics tables.
2. Renderer references a topic id not present in SQLite. The same topic id (15f44cf4-...) is reused across message send attempts and persists across assistant creation. This suggests the id is stored in renderer-persisted state (Redux-persist / localStorage / Dexie residue) and is never reconciled against the v2 SQLite source of truth.
3. Dev mode profile isolation is working correctly. resolveUserDataLocation() correctly isolates dev-mode data under <userData>Dev, so this is not a migration bug — the profile is a clean slate with empty SQLite tables.
4. Suggested fix directions (non-exhaustive):
   - Add a seeder that creates a default assistant on first run (matches legacy 1.9.x behavior).
   - Fix the renderer to create a topic via a DataApi mutation before referencing it in StreamingService.createUserMessage — the current flow appears to rely on an existing topic that may never have been persisted.
   - Clear any Redux-persist / localStorage keys that reference topic ids absent from SQLite (defensive reconciliation at startup).

### Platform

Windows

### Version

v1.9.1

### Bug Description

## Problem Description

On Windows 11, after system restart and entering the desktop, even if I don't actively open Cherry Studio, as long as Explorer restores the desktop/opens File Explorer, Cherry Studio will be launched in the background and trigger the default agent's scheduled task/heartbeat task.

This task attempts to activate multiple `uvx/uv`-based Python MCP servers, subsequently creating a large process chain:

`explorer.exe -> Cherry Studio.exe -> uvx.exe / uv.exe -> <mcp server>.exe -> python.exe`

This leads to:
- Large numbers of `python.exe` processes
- Significantly elevated CPU usage
- High-speed fan rotation
- File Explorer (Explorer) severe lag, even approaching freeze state

### Steps To Reproduce

## Reproduction Steps

1. Install and use Cherry Studio v1.9.1 on Windows 11
2. Configure multiple `uvx/uv`-based MCP servers (actually observed on my side):
   - `mcp-server-time`
   - `awslabs.document-loader-mcp-server`
   - `arxiv-mcp-server`
   - `minimax-mcp`
3. Restart the system
4. After logging into the desktop, without actively operating Cherry Studio, just wait for the desktop to restore or manually open File Explorer once
5. Observe the process tree in Task Manager and system usage

## Actual Results

- After Explorer restores, `Cherry Studio.exe` appears in the background
- Cherry Studio then launches `uvx.exe` / `uv.exe`
- Then launches multiple Python MCP servers
- Finally generates multiple groups of `python.exe`
- System experiences lag, fan spinning at high speed, Explorer freeze, etc.

### Expected Behavior

- Cherry Studio should not automatically trigger scheduled tasks that batch activate MCP servers during background restore/tray restore
- Even if heartbeat/scheduled tasks exist, they should not cause multiple groups of Python processes to be launched, and should not affect Explorer and overall system responsiveness

### Relevant Log Output

```shell
### 1. Cherry Studio logs contain records of default agent creating heartbeat task
  Similar records can be seen in the logs:

  - `Created default CherryClaw agent`
  - `Task created`
  - `Created heartbeat task`
  - `interval: 30`

  This indicates that the default agent creates a heartbeat task that triggers every 30 minutes.

  ### 2. Subsequently, logs continuously show scheduled task execution records
  The logs repeatedly show:

  - `Found due tasks`
  - `Running scheduled task`
  - Same `taskId: task_1776342843621_44doeqnch`

  This indicates that Cherry Studio continuously executes the same scheduled task in the background.

  ### 3. The task execution calls bundled uvx/uv
  The logs also show:

  - `Using bundled uvx as fallback`
  - `Using bundled uv as fallback`

  This indicates that Cherry Studio actively uses bundled `uvx/uv` to activate MCP servers.

  ### 4. Error logs contain MCP server activation timeouts
  For example:

  - `Error activating server AWS Document Loader Connection timed out after 60s`
  - `Error activating server minimax-mcp Connection timed out after 60s`

  ### 5. Actual parent-child process chain captured locally
  The actual chain captured after my reproduction:

  `explorer.exe -> Cherry Studio.exe -> uvx.exe / uv.exe -> <mcp server>.exe -> python.exe`

  This is not mere speculation, but an actually observed result.
```

You use tools step-by-step to accomplish a given task, with each tool use informed by the result of the previous tool use. ## Tool Use Formatting Tool use is formatted using XML-style tags. In `exec`, you MUST explicitly `return` the final value. ### What `list` Returns - A paginated list of tools. - The response includes: Total / Offset / Limit / Returned. - Each tool line includes: - JS-friendly tool name (camelCase) - original tool id in parentheses (serverId__toolName) ### What `inspect` Returns - A JSDoc stub you can copy into `exec` code. ### What `exec` Provides - `mcp.callTool(name, params)` → call a tool by JS name (camelCase) or original id (serverId__toolName) - `mcp.log(level, message, fields?)` - `parallel(...promises)` → Promise.all - `settle(...promises)` → Promise.allSettled - `console.log/info/warn/error/debug` (captured) ### Example: Single Call (invoke) 1) `list({ limit: 50, offset: 0 })` 2) Pick the relevant tool name from the list. 3) `inspect({ name: "githubSearchRepos" })` 4) `invoke({ name: "githubSearchRepos", params: { query: "mcp" } })` ### Example: Multi-step Flow (exec) ```javascript const repos = await mcp.callTool("githubSearchRepos", { query: "mcp" }) console.log("found", repos) return repos ``` ``` ``` modelscope社区的这个API-Inference量是怎么计算的？怎么感觉用不完 ``` Reasoning ``` The user is asking about how ModelScope community's "API-Inference" quota is calculated, and they feel like they can't use it all up. ## Summary

- Improve the overall look, feel, and responsiveness of the side panel UI

## Problem
The side panel for managing assistants feels rough and unpolished (v1.9.1 on Windows). When you have a growing number of assistants, there's no good way to organize, tag, or sort them. The overall interaction feels "janky" — the UI lacks the smoothness and polish expected in a modern desktop app.

Specific pain points:
- No tagging or categorization system for assistants
- Limited or no sorting options (by name, last used, custom order)
- The side panel UI feels sluggish and unrefined in its current state

- **Tagging**: Allow users to assign tags/categories to assistants (e.g., "coding", "writing", "research") for filtering
- **Sorting**: Add sort options — by name, last used date, creation date, custom drag-and-drop order
- **UI polish**: Improve the side panel's visual design — smoother transitions, better spacing, cleaner layout, more responsive feel
- Consider collapsible tag groups or an inline search/filter bar

## Alternative Solutions
- Folder-based organization instead of tags
- Favorites/pinning system for frequently used assistants
- Compact vs. expanded view toggle

title: Feature: notify tool supports sending local files (images, documents, etc.) to IM platforms (WeChat, QQ, etc.)
body:
> [\!NOTE]
> This issue was translated by Claude.

# Background

Cherry Studio's notify tool is primarily used for sending text message notifications, but does not support sending local files directly (such as images, documents, compressed archives, etc.).

## Requirements

We hope the notify tool can support sending local files to IM platforms (WeChat, QQ, DingTalk, Feishu, etc.), including but not limited to:

- Images (PNG, JPG, GIF, etc.)
- Documents (PDF, Word, Excel, etc.)
- Archives (ZIP, RAR, etc.)
- Any other file types

## Use Cases

1. After AI generates an image, send it directly to WeChat/QQ via notify
2. After AI finishes processing a document, send the result file to the user
3. After a scheduled task completes, push the report file to IM

## Suggested Implementation

- Add `filePath` or `media` parameter to the notify tool to accept local file paths
- For image types, support inline preview; other files sent as attachments
- Compatible with mainstream IM platforms' file sending APIs

## Reference

OpenClaw's `message` tool already supports `filePath` / `media` parameters and can serve as a reference design.

Thank you for considering\!

---

## 背景

目前 Cherry Studio 的 notify 工具主要用于发送文本消息通知，但不支持直接发送本地文件（如图片、文档、压缩包等）。

## 需求

希望 notify 工具能够支持向 IM 平台（微信、QQ、钉钉、飞书等）发送本地文件，包括但不限于：

- 图片（PNG、JPG、GIF 等）
- 文档（PDF、Word、Excel 等）
- 压缩包（ZIP、RAR 等）
- 其他任意文件类型

## 使用场景

1. AI 生成图片后，直接通过 notify 将图片发送到微信/QQ

title: [Feature]: v2 Resource Library — unified Assistant/Agent/Skill hub
body:
### Issue Checklist

- [x] I understand that issues are for reporting problems and requesting features, not for off-topic comments, and I will provide as much detail as possible to help resolve the issue.
- [x] I have checked the pinned issues and searched through the existing open issues, closed issues, and discussions and did not find a similar suggestion.
- [x] I have provided a short and descriptive title so that developers can quickly understand the issue when browsing the issue list, rather than vague titles like "A suggestion" or "Stuck."
- [x] The latest version of Cherry Studio does not include the feature I am suggesting.

### Platform

macOS

### Version

v2.0.0-alpha

### Is your feature request related to an existing issue?

Entry points for user-authored AI resources — **Assistants**, **Agents**, and **Skills** — are scattered across the v2 app today:

- Assistants live in the Home left panel (legacy Redux store).
- Agents live in their own `/agents` page (legacy HTTP service).
- Skills live inside Settings → Skills (legacy IPC + a separate SQLite in the agents module).

This makes it hard to browse, organize, tag, and quick-manage all of these in one place. It also conflicts with the ongoing v2 migration that consolidates data access through the v2 DataApi + SQLite + Drizzle stack. The Cherry Studio UI Design prototype already ships a unified "资源库 (Library)" page, but there is no corresponding implementation in the product.

### Desired Solution

Ship a new top-level **Library** (`资源库`) page that aggregates **Assistants, Agents and Skills** behind a single browse/manage experience, aligned with the UI design prototype and the v2 data architecture. This is primarily a **frontend** PR, with one scoped backend change (tag enum extension). All three resource types must be fully functional by the time the PR merges.

**Scope (all must be functional at merge time):**

- New sidebar entry `library` (Lucide `Library` icon) routed to `/library`; coexists with Home / Agents / other existing entries.
- `LibraryPage` matching the design prototype: 200 px left sidebar (type switcher + tag list, **no folder tree**) + main grid/list view.
- Toolbar: global search, sort (updated / created / name), type filter, Grid ↔ List view toggle, "Create" dropdown.
- Tag bar: horizontal scrollable tag chips with multi-select filtering.
- Resource cards / rows with a context menu: edit, duplicate, delete, manage tags, enable/disable (Skill only).
- Dedicated editors per type (all real DataApi-backed at merge time):
  - `AssistantEditorDrawer`
  - `AgentEditorDrawer`
  - `SkillDetailDrawer` + `SkillInstallDialog`
- **Unified tagging across all three types**, delivered by extending `TaggableEntityType` in this PR (see below).

**v2 data alignment (strict):**

- All renderer data access must go through the v2 DataApi (`useQuery` / `useMutation` in `src/renderer/src/data/hooks/useDataApi.ts`).
- **No** dependencies on legacy Redux / legacy HTTP client (`AgentApiClient`) / legacy IPC (`useSkills`) at merge time.
- A common `ResourceAdapter<Dto, CreateDto, UpdateDto>` interface wraps each type's DataApi, so the `LibraryPage` UI is decoupled from whichever DataApi ships first.

### Tag system extension (in this PR)

Agents and Skills must participate in the existing tag system. The shared enum needs extending; no DB migration is required because `entity_tag.entityType` is a plain TEXT column with no DB-level enum constraint, and `TagService` is already generic over `TaggableEntityType`.

Changes included in this PR:

- `packages/shared/data/types/tag.ts` — extend `TaggableEntityType` from `assistant | topic | session` to `assistant | topic | session | agent | skill`; update JSDoc.
- `src/main/data/db/schemas/tagging.ts` — update the JSDoc on `entityTagTable` (no schema change).
- `src/main/data/services/TagService.ts` — update header JSDoc only (the service is already generic; no logic changes).
- `src/main/data/api/handlers/tags.ts` — if any hardcoded entity-type validation exists, release it (expected to auto-flow from the shared zod enum).
- Test coverage — add smoke tests for `syncEntityTags` / `getTagsByEntity` / `removeEntityTags` with `entityType: 'agent'` and `'skill'`.

Cross-PR coordination: the **upstream Agent and Skill DataApi PRs** must call `tagService.removeEntityTags('agent' | 'skill', id)` in their respective delete / uninstall flows — `entity_tag` has no FK to the entity tables, so cleanup is caller-driven. This is an explicit review item before merging the library PR, not a code change inside it.

### Merge dependencies & sequencing

This is a long-lived frontend branch. The PR can start immediately with a UI shell + the parts whose DataApi is already in place; final merge is gated on the upstream data-layer PRs landing.

| Stage | Work | Blocks merge? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1. Bootstrap | UI shell, `TaggableEntityType` extension (this PR), Assistant full CRUD via `/assistants`, Tag CRUD for all three types via `/tags`. Agent / Skill ship with adapter **stubs** (empty list; mutations throw `PendingBackendError` surfaced as toast). | No — PR kept open for review |
| 2. Agent DataApi PR lands | Rebase; replace `agentAdapter.ts` stub with real `useQuery('/agents')` + `useMutation`; Agent full CRUD live. Confirm upstream AgentService.delete invokes `tagService.removeEntityTags('agent', id)`. | Yes |
| 3. Skill DataApi PR lands | Rebase; replace `skillAdapter.ts` stub with real `/skills` DataApi (install / toggle / uninstall / file read). Confirm upstream SkillService.uninstall invokes `tagService.removeEntityTags('skill', id)`. | Yes |
| 4. Final regression | All stubs / `PendingBackendNotice` removed; `grep` confirms no legacy imports; `pnpm lint` / `pnpm test` / `pnpm format` green. | Merge |

### Current branch readiness audit

| Resource | Shared schema | Handler | Service | Final PR state |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Assistant | ✅ `packages/shared/data/api/schemas/assistants.ts` | ✅ | ✅ | Full CRUD via DataApi |
| Tag | ✅ `packages/shared/data/api/schemas/tags.ts` — **extended to include `agent` + `skill` inside this PR** | ✅ (generic, no code change) | ✅ (generic, no code change) | Unified tag CRUD for all three resource types |
| Agent | ❌ no shared schema yet | ❌ | ❌ | Adapter stub → swapped for real DataApi before merge |
| Skill | ❌ no shared schema yet | ❌ | ❌ | Adapter stub → swapped for real DataApi before merge |

### Proposed module layout (new)

```
src/renderer/src/pages/library/
  LibraryPage.tsx
  components/                 # sidebar, toolbar, grid/list, cards, menus, editors
  adapters/                   # ResourceAdapter<T> + assistant/agent/skill/tag
  hooks/                      # useResourceLibrary, per-resource mutations, useResourceTags
  types.ts
  __tests__/
```

### Out of scope (tracked as follow-up PRs)

- Folder hierarchy.
- KB / MCP as sub-resources inside the Assistant editor (blocked on their own renderer migrations).
- Import / Export (JSON / YAML).
- Marketplace subscription.
- Full Assistant settings surface (reasoning, customParameters, etc.).
- Skill marketplace browsing inside the library (phase-1 covers already-installed skills only; discovery stays in the current Skills settings entry).
- Batch `GET /tags/entities/:entityType` endpoint (only added if reviewers flag N+1 tag fetches as a blocker).

### Acceptance criteria (merge gate)

- Sidebar entry visible; `/library` loads the page.
- Type filter, search, sort, Grid/List toggle all work end-to-end.
- **Assistant**: create / edit / duplicate / delete / tag management all succeed via DataApi and refresh the list.
- **Agent**: same set of operations live via the Agent DataApi (introduced upstream).
- **Skill**: install (marketplace / zip / directory), enable/disable, detail view with file tree, uninstall — all via the Skill DataApi (introduced upstream).
- **Tag system**: `TaggableEntityType` enum extended, new smoke tests pass, tagging works for all three resource types. Upstream Agent/Skill delete flows confirmed to call `tagService.removeEntityTags`.
- `pnpm lint`, `pnpm test`, `pnpm format` all pass.
- Grep confirms no references to `AgentApiClient`, `useSkills` (legacy), or `useAssistant` Redux hook inside `src/renderer/src/pages/library/`.
- All `PendingBackendError` / `PendingBackendNotice` placeholders removed.

### Alternative Solutions

1. **Extend the existing Home left-panel Assistants tab.** Rejected — couples cleanly only to Assistants, doesn't accommodate Agents/Skills, and keeps the legacy Redux dependency.
2. **Ship an Assistant-only library first, add Agent/Skill later.** Rejected — the product value of the library comes from the unified view; releasing it one-type-at-a-time fragments the UX. The adapter-stub pattern lets the UI land immediately while the backend migrations proceed in parallel, and the PR only merges when the experience is complete.
3. **Defer the tag enum extension to a separate PR.** Rejected — tagging is a core library interaction and must work for all three types at merge; splitting it adds coordination overhead without reducing review size (the enum change is a few lines of shared types plus smoke tests).
4. **Aggregate Knowledge Base and MCP Server as top-level library resources.** Deferred — in Cherry Studio these are sub-resources consumed inside the Assistant editor, not independently authored user resources. Treating them as top-level would duplicate the Knowledge page and MCP settings.

### Additional Information

Design reference (internal): `cherry-studio-ui-design` prototype — `src/features/library/` (`LibraryPage.tsx`, `LibrarySidebar.tsx`, `ResourceGrid.tsx`, `SkillPluginDetail.tsx`, `ImportModal.tsx`).

Branch: `feat/v2/resource-library` (based on `v2`).

Constraints (per `CLAUDE.md`):
- UI exclusively from `@cherrystudio/ui` (Tailwind + shadcn); no antd / HeroUI / styled-components.
- `loggerService` only (no `console.log`).
- All user-visible strings through i18next (new `library` namespace; run `pnpm i18n:sync`).
- Renderer data access restricted to v2 DataApi.

title: [Feature]: Rationalize v2 user data storage layout and move sensitive files out of ~/.cherrystudio
body:
### Issue Checklist

- [x] I understand that issues are for reporting problems and requesting features, not for off-topic comments, and I will provide as much detail as possible to help resolve the issue.
- [x] I have checked the pinned issues and searched through the existing open issues, closed issues, and discussions and did not find a similar suggestion.
- [x] I have provided a short and descriptive title so that developers can quickly understand the issue when browsing the issue list, rather than vague titles like "A suggestion" or "Stuck."
- [x] The latest version of Cherry Studio does not include the feature I am suggesting.

### Platform

macOS

### Version

2.0.0-alpha

### Is your feature request related to an existing issue?

Cherry Studio's current v2-era storage layout mixes several different classes of data across multiple roots:

1. Preboot / machine-level configuration in `~/.cherrystudio`
2. Sensitive credentials and OAuth state also in `~/.cherrystudio`
3. User-managed content in `{userData}/Data`
4. App/runtime state in `{userData}`

From the current implementation, the main paths look roughly like this:

```text
~/.cherrystudio
├── boot-config.json
├── bin/
├── config/
│   ├── mcp/oauth/*.json
│   ├── memory.json
│   ├── oauth/anthropic.json
│   └── .copilot_token
├── trace/
└── ovms/

{userData}
├── cherrystudio.sqlite
├── version.log
├── .claude/
├── tesseract/
├── Data/
│   ├── Files/
│   ├── Notes/
│   ├── KnowledgeBase/
│   ├── Skills/
│   ├── Channels/
│   ├── Agents/
│   └── Workspace/
└── runtime state...
```

This causes several problems:

- Sensitive files are stored under `~/.cherrystudio`, which makes that directory a catch-all for both boot config and credentials.
- The storage model does not clearly separate boot config, user content, secrets, and runtime state.
- Some files that behave more like user/application content are still placed under `config`, for example `memory.json`.
- Backup/migration/export rules become harder to reason about because the directory responsibilities are not explicit.

Examples from the current codebase:

- `boot-config.json` is intentionally placed in `~/.cherrystudio` and should remain outside `userData` because it is required during preboot.
- MCP OAuth state currently lives under `~/.cherrystudio/config/mcp/oauth`
- Anthropic credentials currently live under `~/.cherrystudio/config/oauth/anthropic.json`
- Copilot token currently resolves to `~/.cherrystudio/config/.copilot_token`
- MCP memory graph currently lives at `~/.cherrystudio/config/memory.json`
- User content such as files, notes, and knowledge base assets already live under `{userData}/Data/...`

The current layout works, but it makes the long-term v2 storage model harder to maintain and document.

### Desired Solution

Define and adopt a clear v2 storage contract with distinct storage classes:

1. `boot`
   - Only preboot-critical configuration
   - Example: `~/.cherrystudio/boot-config.json`

2. `content`
   - User-managed files and application content
   - Example root: `{userData}/Data/...`

3. `secret`
   - Sensitive credentials, OAuth tokens, channel tokens, and other auth artifacts
   - Example root: `{userData}/Data/Secrets/...`

4. `runtime`
   - Chromium/runtime/session/cache/window-state data
   - Kept under existing Electron-managed locations

Concrete direction:

- Keep `boot-config.json` in `~/.cherrystudio`
- Stop placing any new sensitive files under `~/.cherrystudio`
- Move sensitive files to `{userData}/Data/Secrets/...`, including:
  - MCP OAuth files
  - Anthropic OAuth credentials
  - Copilot token
  - Channel/bot token files
- Move `memory.json` out of `~/.cherrystudio/config` into a content-oriented path under `{userData}/Data/...`
- Explicitly document `.cherrystudio` as a preboot/machine-level directory rather than a general storage root
- Update path registry naming so secrets/content/runtime are easier to identify from path keys
- Add migration logic so legacy files are discovered at old paths and moved forward automatically

Suggested target shape:

```text
~/.cherrystudio
├── boot-config.json
├── bin/
├── trace/
└── ovms/

{userData}/Data
├── Files/
├── Notes/
├── KnowledgeBase/
├── Agents/
├── Skills/
├── Workspace/
├── Mcp/
│   └── memory.json
└── Secrets/
    ├── McpOAuth/
    ├── Anthropic/
    ├── Copilot/
    └── Channels/
```

This would make v2 storage easier to reason about for:
- data migration
- backup/export rules
- future cleanup policies
- security review
- documentation
- adding new path keys safely

### Alternative Solutions

A few weaker alternatives were considered:

1. Keep using `~/.cherrystudio` for sensitive files, but document it better
   - This improves clarity slightly, but keeps the directory overloaded.

2. Only move a subset of sensitive files
   - This reduces immediate work, but preserves the inconsistency.

3. Keep `memory.json` and other function-owned files under `config`
   - This keeps historical behavior, but continues mixing configuration and content/state.

These options do not solve the main structural issue: the storage classes are still mixed.

### Additional Information

Scope for this proposal:

- Focus on file-based storage layout only
- Do not cover `LocalStorage`, `IndexedDB`, or other renderer-side browser storage in this issue
- Do not require a new encryption abstraction in the first step
- The first goal is to make path ownership and directory responsibility explicit

Implementation notes based on the current codebase:

- `boot-config.json` should remain outside `userData` because it must be readable before userData resolution.
- `CopilotService` already uses Electron `safeStorage` before persisting token bytes, but its file still lives under `~/.cherrystudio`; this issue is about file placement and storage classification first.
- Existing path keys in `src/main/core/paths/pathRegistry.ts` already make the current split visible, so this issue can be implemented by:
  - updating path keys
  - migrating old files
  - updating docs to reflect the new contract

A good outcome for this issue would be:

- a documented v2 storage taxonomy
- path registry updated to match that taxonomy
- legacy migration for current sensitive files
- `.cherrystudio` no longer used as a general-purpose sensitive data directory

No VPN, no proxy changes.** Tested multiple CherryIN models in Agent mode (glm-5, and others) — all return: ``` 响应传输中断，请检查网络稳定性或重试 Claude Code returned an error result: API Error: Unable to connect to API (ECONNRESET) ``` Meanwhile Chat mode, same provider (CherryIN), same moment → normal response. ### Steps To Reproduce 1. Configure CherryIN provider with a valid model (e.g. `agent/glm-5`, `agent/deepseek-v3.2`) 2. Open **Chat** → pick that model → send `hi` → works 3. Open **Agent** (1.9.2 default agent or any custom agent) → pick a CherryIN model → send `hi` 4. Agent returns `API Error: Unable to connect to API (ECONNRESET)` ### Expected Behavior Agent mode should connect to CherryIN successfully for the same models/credentials that Chat mode already works with. ### Screenshots **Agent mode — fails** (model: `agent/glm-5 | CherryIN`) **Chat mode — works** (model: `agent/deepseek-v3.2 | CherryIN`, same provider, same moment) ### Suspected Root Cause The error message prefix `Claude Code returned an error result: ...` indicates the Agent mode call path goes through the bundled Claude Code SDK / **OpenClaw gateway**, whereas Chat mode talks to CherryIN's HTTP endpoint directly. Two candidate causes: 1. **OpenClaw gateway not reachable / not started on this install.** Related: #14415 (OpenClaw dashboard opens without auth token, gateway unusable). If the gateway is effectively down, every Agent request will ECONNRESET at the SDK layer before reaching CherryIN. 2. **Agent path does not honor Chat's provider/proxy/auth settings**, so even if the CherryIN HTTP client works in Chat, the Agent-path client has its own broken config. Either way, the fact that Chat succeeds on the same provider proves the credentials + network are fine; the failure is local to the Agent call path. ### Additional Context - No VPN, no proxy changes between the two calls - Tested across multiple CherryIN models (not model-specific) - Related OpenClaw infrastructure issue: #14415

title: [Feature]: Scheduled reminder should be pushed by Agent, not injected as a user message
body:
> [!NOTE] > This issue was translated by Claude. Chinese original at the bottom. ### Issue Checklist - [x] Searched existing issues, no similar found. - [x] Short, clear title. - [x] Using latest version. ### Platform macOS ### Version v1.9.2 (draft) ### Feature / UX request When a scheduled reminder fires, the reminder message is currently **posted into the chat as the user**, and the Agent then *replies* to it. This role reversal makes the conversation log read backwards — it looks like the user is nagging themselves and the Agent is confirming receipt. Expected: the Agent should **proactively push** the reminder to the user (Agent-authored message), and the user can then reply if they want. ### Steps To Reproduce 1. Have the Agent set a scheduled reminder ("remind me to drink water in 4 minutes") 2. Wait for the trigger 3. Observe the new messages that land in the chat ### Observed The first bubble at trigger time shows the **user role** saying `该喝水啦，记得补充一下水分哦~`. The Agent's follow-up bubble says `哈哈，谢谢提醒！...` — as if the user had just prompted the Agent, not vice versa. ### Expected Behavior - The reminder message at trigger time should be **authored by the Agent** (Agent avatar, Agent role). - No synthetic user message should be injected. - Optional: a subtle "scheduled reminder" badge/icon on that message to distinguish it from normal Agent replies. ### Why it matters - Current behavior is confusing: reading the thread later, the user sees "themselves" sending reminders they never typed. - It also breaks Agent memory / context downstream, since a fake user turn gets persisted. - Third-party IM integrations (WeChat, Telegram) built on top of this would push reminders claiming to be from the user, not the Agent — even more confusing.
中文原文 ### 诉求 定时提醒触发时，提醒文案现在是以**用户身份**发进对话，然后 Agent 再去"回复"它。对话记录读起来是倒的——看上去像用户在催自己，Agent 只是确认收到。 预期：Agent 应该**主动推送**提醒给用户（以 Agent 身份发），用户想回复再回。 ### 复现 1. 让 Agent 建一个定时提醒（"4分钟后提醒我喝水"） 2. 等触发 3. 看新冒出的消息 ### 现象 触发时先冒出**用户身份**的气泡：`该喝水啦，记得补充一下水分哦~`。紧接着 Agent 气泡：`哈哈，谢谢提醒！...`——看起来像用户刚催了 Agent，而不是反过来。 ### 期望 - 触发时的提醒文案应由 **Agent 发**（Agent 头像 / 角色） - 不要伪造一条用户消息 - 可选：在该条 Agent 消息上加个"定时提醒"标识，和普通 Agent 回复区分 ### 影响 - 当前行为反直觉：回看记录时看到"自己"发了从没打过的话 - 污染 Agent 上下文：假的用户 turn 被持久化 - 第三方 IM 接入（微信/Telegram）会推送"伪装成用户发的"提醒，更乱

title: [Bug]: AWS Bedrock requests fail with "failed to fetch"
body:
### Issue Checklist

- [x] I understand that issues are for feedback and problem solving, not for complaining in the comment section, and will provide as much information as possible to help solve the problem.
- [x] My issue is not listed in the [FAQ](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/issues/3881).
- [x] I've looked at **pinned issues** and searched for existing [Open Issues](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/issues), [Closed Issues](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20state%3Aclosed), and [Discussions](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/discussions), no similar issue or discussion was found.
- [x] I've filled in short, clear headings so that developers can quickly identify a rough idea of what to expect when flipping through the list of issues. And not "a suggestion", "stuck", etc.
- [x] I've confirmed that I am using the latest version of Cherry Studio.

### Platform

Windows

### Version

1.9.1

### Bug Description

AWS Bedrock requests always fail with a `failed to fetch` error when using the built-in AWS Bedrock provider with its default configuration. The root cause is likely that an empty string `apiHost` (the default value in `SYSTEM_PROVIDERS` config) is passed as `baseURL: ""` into `createAmazonBedrock()` from `@ai-sdk/amazon-bedrock`, causing every request to be sent to an invalid URL.

**Root cause analysis:**

The default AWS Bedrock provider config in `src/renderer/src/config/providers.ts` has `apiHost: ""`:

```typescript
'aws-bedrock': {
  id: 'aws-bedrock',
  apiKey: '',
  apiHost: '',   // ← empty string by default
  ...
}
```

In `buildBedrockConfig()` (`src/renderer/src/aiCore/provider/providerConfig.ts`), this empty string flows through as `ctx.baseConfig.baseURL = ""` and is spread directly into the provider settings:

```typescript
// authType === 'apiKey' path:
return { ...base, providerSettings: { ...ctx.baseConfig, region, apiKey: getAwsBedrockApiKey() } }
//                                    ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
//                                    spreads baseURL: "" into providerSettings
```

Inside `@ai-sdk/amazon-bedrock`, the base URL is constructed as follows:

```typescript
const getBedrockRuntimeBaseUrl = () => {
  return withoutTrailingSlash(
    options.baseURL != null   // ← uses != null (loose), NOT !== undefined
      ? options.baseURL       // "" != null is TRUE, so "" is used as-is
      : `https://bedrock-runtime.${region}.amazonaws.com`
  ) ?? `https://bedrock-runtime.us-east-1.amazonaws.com`;
  //  ↑ this fallback also never triggers because withoutTrailingSlash("") returns ""
};
```

Because `"" != null` evaluates to `true` (loose equality), the SDK treats the empty string as a valid, intentional base URL override. `withoutTrailingSlash("")` returns `""`, and `"" ?? fallback` also keeps `""`. The final request URL becomes `""/model/{modelId}/converse` — an entirely invalid URL — causing the `failed to fetch` error.

The same issue likely affects both `apiKey` auth and `iam` auth paths. Additionally, if `region` is also left empty (the default is `""`), and `baseURL` were somehow fixed, the SDK would construct `https://bedrock-runtime..amazonaws.com` (missing the region segment), which is equally broken. Both values need to be guarded against empty strings.

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Open Cherry Studio (any recent version).
2. Go to **Settings → Providers**, find the built-in **AWS Bedrock** provider.
3. Set auth type to **API Key**, fill in a valid Bedrock API Key and a valid Region (e.g. `us-east-1`).
4. Add a AWS Bedrock model and send any message.
5. The request fails immediately with `failed to fetch`.

### Expected Behavior

When **API Host** is left empty (the default), the SDK should automatically construct the correct endpoint URL from the configured Region:
`https://bedrock-runtime.{region}.amazonaws.com`

### Relevant Log Output

```shell

```

### Additional Context

**Affected file:** `src/renderer/src/aiCore/provider/providerConfig.ts`, function `buildBedrockConfig()`

**Introduced by:** Likely to be the `refactor: migrate to ai sdk v6 Phase 3` commit (~2 weeks ago), which migrated Bedrock to use `@ai-sdk/amazon-bedrock` directly.

**Proposed fix** (2-line change):

```typescript
function buildBedrockConfig(ctx: BuilderContext): ProviderConfig<'bedrock'> {
  const authType = getAwsBedrockAuthType()
- const region = getAwsBedrockRegion()
+ const region = getAwsBedrockRegion() || undefined  // prevent empty string → malformed URL

  const base = { providerId: 'bedrock' as const, endpoint: ctx.endpoint }
+ // Empty string baseURL passes the SDK's `!= null` guard and is used as-is,
+ // resulting in invalid request URLs. Convert to undefined so the SDK
+ // constructs the correct endpoint from region automatically.
+ const baseURL = ctx.baseConfig.baseURL || undefined

  if (authType === 'apiKey') {
-   return { ...base, providerSettings: { ...ctx.baseConfig, region, apiKey: getAwsBedrockApiKey() } }
```

### Is your feature request related to an existing issue?

**Background:** When using models like Claude Opus 4.7 that support 5-minute caching, multi-tasking (opening 3-4 windows for deep analysis simultaneously) often causes a specific window to exceed 5 minutes without interaction, leading to invalidation of expensive context cache and generating significant duplicate charges.

### Desired Solution

**Requirements Details:**

**Independent Toggle:** Add a "cache expiration reminder" toggle in the toolbar or settings of each conversation window.

**Timing Logic:** Start timing from the completion of the last API interaction. When this feature is enabled, trigger a reminder when approaching 5 minutes (recommended at 4 minutes 30 seconds) and the user has not entered new content.

**macOS Native Notification:** Use macOS system beep sound to alert the user that the window's cache is about to expire and requires immediate interaction.

**Targeted Scope:** Unlike the existing "30-second response adjustment," this feature needs to be enabled individually for "specific conversations" rather than as a global setting.

**UI Representation:** Suggest adding a "breathing light progress bar" next to the avatar in the conversation list. Green represents active cache, turns yellow when 1 minute remains, and turns red at 30 seconds with a "ding" sound.

### Alternative Solutions

This feature request may partially overlap with the conversation state preservation feature I previously proposed, but they are not entirely the same.

Alright, I've submitted multiple requests in one go—these are all pain points I've encountered during intensive recent usage. Cherry Studio is indeed a fantastic and easy-to-use software, much more thoughtful than chatbox. I hope you can keep it up, and let's all continue to improve together\!

body:

- [x] I've filled in short, clear headings so that developers can quickly identify a rough idea of what to expect when flipping through the list of issues.
- [x] I've confirmed that I am using the latest version of Cherry Studio.

### Platform

Windows

### Version

v1.9.2 (Portable)

### Bug Description

When launching Code Tools (opencode, claude-code, qwen-code) from Cherry Studio's UI on Windows, the status shows ` but **no visible terminal window appears**. The CLI tool process starts headless in the background but the user never sees a terminal interface.

This affects **all terminal options** (CMD, Windows Terminal, PowerShell) when launched from the Cherry Studio Portable version.

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Use Cherry Studio **Portable** version on Windows
2. Open Cherry Studio - Code Tools
3. Select any tool (opencode / claude-code / qwen-code)
4. Select any terminal (Command Prompt / Windows Terminal / PowerShell)
5. Click ` Launch
6. Cherry Studio shows ` in the UI
7. **No terminal window appears** -- the CLI tool process runs headless in the background

### Expected Behavior

A visible terminal window should open with the CLI tool running inside it.

### Relevant Log Output

Cherry Studio logs show successful launch:

`
{"message":"Created temp bat file: C:\\Users\\paul\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\cherrystudio\\launch_opencode_1776816963095.bat","module":"CodeToolsService"}
{"message":"Using terminal: Windows Terminal (WindowsTerminal)","module":"CodeToolsService"}
{"message":"Launching terminal with command: wt","module":"CodeToolsService"}
{"message":"Launched opencode in new terminal window","module":"CodeToolsService"}
`

But opencode.exe runs HEADLESS (no MainWindowTitle):

`
Get-Process opencode | Select Id, MainWindowTitle

    Id MainWindowTitle
    -- ---------------
114728                  # Empty title = no visible window
120332                  # Empty title = no visible window
`

### Root Cause Analysis

The issue is caused by the ` option added in PR #13405.

The spawn call in CodeToolsService.ts:

`	ypescript
spawn(terminalCommand, terminalArgs, {
  detached: true,
  stdio: "ignore",
  cwd: directory,
  env: processEnv,
  shell: isWin  // Added in PR #13405 to fix ENOENT
})
`

What happens on Windows:

With `, Node.js wraps the command in `. Combined with ` + `, this creates a **headless cmd.exe process** with no console window.

For Windows Terminal (wt.exe):
`
spawn("wt", ["--", "cmd", "/c", batFile], {shell: true, stdio: "ignore", detached: true})
  -> cmd.exe /d /s /c "wt -- cmd /c batFile"   (headless cmd.exe)
    -> wt.exe (UWP app)                          (cannot create visible window from headless parent)
`

For CMD:
`
spawn("cmd", ["/c", batFile], {shell: true, stdio: "ignore", detached: true})
  -> cmd.exe /d /s /c "cmd /c batFile"           (nested headless cmd.exe, no window)
`

Experimental verification:

| Method | Result |
|--------|--------|
| Start-Process wt.exe (no hidden) | WT window appears |
| Start-Process cmd.exe -WindowStyle Hidden, then cmd /c wt ... | No WT window |
| spawn("wt", [...], {shell: true, stdio: "ignore"}) via bun | Returns PID but no WT window |
| Direct cmd.exe /c "wt ..." in visible console | WT window appears |

The key insight: **UWP apps like wt.exe cannot create visible windows when spawned from a headless parent process on Windows.**

### Why PR #13405 introduced this regression

PR #13405 correctly identified that ` loses Windows case-insensitive PATH resolution, causing ENOENT. The fix ` delegates command resolution to cmd.exe -- but the side effect is that the intermediate cmd.exe process becomes headless due to `.

### Suggested Fix

**Option A:** Use ` only for resolving the command path, then spawn the terminal directly without shell wrapping.

**Option B:** Use the ` command on Windows to create a new console window:
`
spawn("cmd", ["/c", "start", "cmd", "/k", batFile], { detached: true, stdio: "ignore", env: processEnv, shell: true })
`

**Option C:** Fix the root cause (PATH case-insensitivity) in env merging without using `:
`	ypescript
const processEnv = { ...process.env };
for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(env)) {

## Bug Description

When an assistant has built-in web search enabled, the `buildin_web_search` tool can be invoked repeatedly during a single assistant response. In the reported case, one response produced many separate search result/citation groups and consumed more than 120k tokens.

Observed symptoms:

- Multiple search result groups are shown in one response, such as 17, 20, 5, 6, 6, 3, and 20 search results.
- Multiple citation blocks are created for the same assistant response.
- Token usage can become extremely high, for example `Tokens: 122737`.

This makes web search unexpectedly expensive and can slow down or disrupt the conversation.

## Steps To Reproduce

1. Configure an assistant with a web search provider enabled.
2. Ask a question that triggers built-in web search.
3. Let the assistant stream the response.
4. Observe that `buildin_web_search` may be called repeatedly in the same response, producing many search/citation groups and very high token usage.

## Expected Behavior

Built-in web search should have a bounded per-response budget. A single assistant response should not repeatedly call `buildin_web_search` and append multiple large search result payloads unless explicitly allowed.

Expected behavior for the default path:

- Execute built-in web search at most once per assistant response.
- Reuse the first search result if the model attempts to call the tool again.
- Limit and deduplicate prepared search queries.
- Keep URLs compact in search results to reduce token overhead.
