## Version
2.0.0-alpha

## Is your feature request related to an existing issue?
This request is based on the ongoing work built on top of the `v2` branch.

The background is the current v2 data refactor and UI component refactor. Under the new conventions, renderer-side data should move to the new data layer and be consumed through DataApi-based hooks, while new UI should follow the Shadcn + Tailwind CSS component direction.

Because of that, continuing to extend the legacy model selector directly on top of the old implementation is expensive, and the final behavior cannot be expected to stay fully identical after the underlying data flow and UI conventions have changed. In this situation, it makes more sense to build a new standalone business-side selector component on top of the v2 architecture instead of patching the legacy selector in place.

The current in-progress work mainly covers two parts:

- completing missing Storybook documentation/examples during the UI component refactor
- building a standalone `ModelSelectorV2` business component using the latest `useModels` / related hooks

In this new implementation, the pinning capability is also part of the v2 data design. Pinned model IDs should be stored in user Preference data instead of remaining a purely local UI concern.

## Desired Solution
Please continue this work as a v2-aligned implementation with the following direction:

- complete the missing Storybook docs/examples needed for the refactored component system
- build a standalone `ModelSelectorV2` business component on top of the latest `useModels` / related v2 hooks and DataApi-based renderer data flow
- keep the component focused on model acquisition, selection, filtering, and search responsibilities
- store pinned model IDs in the user's Preference data under the v2 storage model
- keep the implementation aligned with the new Shadcn + Tailwind CSS conventions instead of following legacy UI patterns
- treat this as a new component built on top of the v2 architecture rather than a strict in-place port of the old selector internals

This should make the selector consistent with the current v2 migration direction while reducing the cost of forcing old assumptions into the new architecture.

## Alternative Solutions
Continue modifying the legacy selector directly and try to preserve its old internal structure while migrating it to the new data layer and new UI stack.

This may seem simpler in the short term, but it increases migration cost and makes it harder to align the selector with the current v2 data flow, UI conventions, and storage model.

## Additional Information
Relative to the `v2` branch, the current branch only has one extra committed Storybook-related documentation change. The rest of the selector-related work discussed here is mainly still in the staged changes.

So this request is specifically about the staged work being developed on top of `v2`: Storybook doc completion, the development of a standalone `ModelSelectorV2` business component, and the related migration of pinning into v2 Preference storage.

### Platform

Windows

### Version

v1.9.2

### Bug Description

问题描述 (Description)
在使用 OhMyGPT 等 OpenAI 兼容接口（或 cherryin 渠道）调用支持思考的 Gemini 模型时，桌面版 CherryStudio 无法触发/输出思考过程，而 手机版 CherryStudio 在完全相同的配置下可以正常显示思考块。
原因分析 (Root Cause Analysis)
经过对比桌面版和手机版的源码，发现两端在构建 openai-compatible 渠道下的推理参数时存在逻辑差异：
手机版 (reasoning.ts) 中，当识别为 Gemini 思考模型时，会通过 extra_body 注入特定的 Google 思考参数：
code
TypeScript
if (isSupportedThinkingTokenGeminiModel(model)) {
  if (reasoningEffort === 'auto') {
    return {
      extra_body: {
        google: {
          thinking_config: { thinking_budget: -1, include_thoughts: true }
        }
      }
    }
  }
  // ...
}
桌面版 (utils/options.ts & reasoning.ts) 中，由于渠道类型是 openai-compatible，代码走的是 buildGenericProviderOptions。桌面版并没有像手机版那样，把 Gemini 的 thinking_config 正确包装进 extra_body 交给底层 AI SDK (@ai-sdk/openai)。
无法通过自定义参数绕过：尝试在桌面版「自定义参数」中手动添加 extra_body 或 thinkingConfig，发现桌面版会直接将其作为顶层字段 (top-level field) 放入 Request Body 中发出，而不是放进 providerOptions 走 SDK 的底层透传逻辑，因此代理端（中转 API）无法识别。

### Steps To Reproduce

在桌面版添加一个类型为 OpenAI 的中转渠道（可以使用 OhMyGPT）。
添加 Gemini 支持思考的模型（如 gemini-3.0-flash ）。
在助手设置中，确保思考/推理开关处于开启状态（reasoning_effort 不为 undefined）。
发送消息，打开开发者模式查看原始响应，发现只有 main_text block，没有返回 reasoning block（即中转端未被触发思考逻辑）。

### Expected Behavior

希望桌面版能对齐手机版的处理逻辑：在 openai-compatible / cherryin / newapi 等中转渠道下，调用 Gemini 模型时能够正确构造并传递 extra_body.google.thinking_config 参数，或者让「自定义参数」能够正确合并进 AI SDK 的 providerOptions 中，以便正常触发代理端的思考过程。

body:

- [x] I have provided a short and descriptive title so that developers can quickly understand the issue when browsing the issue list, rather than vague titles like "A suggestion" or "Stuck."
- [x] The latest version of Cherry Studio does not include the feature I am suggesting.

### Platform

Windows

### Version

v1.9.2

### Is your feature request related to an existing issue?

I often feel frustrated because many mainstream models supported in Cherry Studio are text-only unimodal models (e.g., GLM-5.1) or have extremely limited, underperforming visual understanding capabilities. Currently, Cherry Studio only allows users to set one global active model for an entire conversation. When I upload image-based materials (such as academic charts, literature screenshots, data visualizations, and figure panels from research papers) for analysis, the selected unimodal model cannot parse, interpret, or extract valid information from the visual content at all, resulting in irrelevant, inaccurate, or completely invalid responses.
To handle multi-modal tasks properly, I have to manually switch the global conversation model to a multi-modal capable one every time I upload images, which is extremely cumbersome. Moreover, frequent model switching breaks the consistency of the conversation context and text interaction experience, as different models have distinct strengths in text generation, long context processing, and conversation style. This pain point is especially prominent in academic research and document processing scenarios, where I regularly need to analyze visual materials alongside ongoing text conversations.

### Desired Solution

I would like Cherry Studio to add an independent model configuration feature dedicated to multi-modal tasks, with the following core design:
Add a separate Dedicated Model for Multi-Modal Tasks option in the model settings panel. This allows users to configure two default models independently: one primary model for regular text-only conversations, and a specialized multi-modal model exclusively for processing tasks that include uploaded images, visual content in PDFs, or other vision-related inputs.
Implement automatic model routing logic: when a user uploads image materials or triggers a multi-modal task in a conversation, the system automatically routes the relevant inference requests to the pre-configured dedicated multi-modal model, with no need for the user to manually switch the global conversation model. All pure text interactions will continue to use the user's primary model to maintain a consistent conversation experience.
Add quality-of-life optimizations: clearly label which models support multi-modal/visual understanding capabilities in the model selection dropdown, to help users quickly filter and select appropriate models. Meanwhile, retain a manual override option for users to temporarily select a different multi-modal model for specific conversations, balancing ease of use and flexibility.
This feature will allow users to fully leverage the strengths of different models: using models with strong text generation and long context handling capabilities for daily text tasks, while using powerful specialized multi-modal models to process visual content. It will completely solve the pain point of unimodal models failing to understand uploaded materials, and significantly improve the experience and efficiency of multi-modal usage scenarios in Cherry Studio.

title: [Bug]: Symlink created by bun install -g points to claude.exe instead of native binary (macOS arm64)
body:
### Issue Checklist

- [x] I understand that issues are for feedback and problem solving, not for complaining in the comment section, and will provide as much information as possible to help solve the problem.
- [x] My issue is not listed in the [FAQ](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/issues/3881).
- [x] I've looked at **pinned issues** and searched for existing [Open Issues](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/issues), [Closed Issues](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20state%3Aclosed), and [Discussions](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/discussions), no similar issue or discussion was found.
- [x] I've filled in short, clear headings so that developers can quickly identify a rough idea of what to expect when flipping through the list of issues. And not "a suggestion", "stuck", etc.
- [x] I've confirmed that I am using the latest version of Cherry Studio.

### Platform

macOS

### Version

v.19.2

### Bug Description

When installing @anthropic-ai/claude-code globally via Bun, the claude symlink is created pointing to bin/claude.exe (a shell script stub) instead of the platform-specific native binary from the @anthropic-ai/claude-code-darwin-arm64 optional dependency. This results in a ENOENT or JavaScript parse error when attempting to run claude.

Environment
- OS: macOS (arm64 / Apple Silicon)
- Bun version: v1.3.1 (89fa0f34) — bundled with Cherry Studio
- Package: @anthropic-ai/claude-code@2.1.118
- Install method: bun install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code


### Steps To Reproduce

1. Install via Bun: bun install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code
2. Try to run: bun /path/to/bin/claude or execute the claude binary directly
3. Error occurs

### Expected Behavior

## Actual Behavior
The symlink created at ~/.cherrystudio/bin/claude points to:
~/.cherrystudio/bin/claude -> ../../node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-code/bin/claude.exe
The claude.exe file contains a shell script stub:

```
echo "Error: claude native binary not installed." >&2
exit 1
When Bun tries to execute this file, it attempts to parse it as JavaScript and fails with:
1 | echo "Error: claude native binary not installed." >&2
         ^
error: Expected ";" but found ""Error: claude native binary not installed.""
    at /Users/xaibael/node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-code/bin/claude.exe:1:6
1 | echo "Error: claude native binary not installed." >&2
                                                      ^
error: Unexpected >
    at /Users/xaibael/node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-code/bin/claude.exe:1:51
In other cases (after the bin directory was cleaned), attempting to run the symlink results in:
error: ENOENT reading "/Users/xaibael/.cherrystudio/bin/claude"
```

## Expected Behavior
The symlink should point to the native binary from the platform-specific optional dependency package:
~/.cherrystudio/bin/claude -> ~/.cherrystudio/install/cache/@anthropic-ai/claude-code-darwin-arm64@2.1

### Relevant Log Output

```shell

```

### Additional Context

## Workaround
Manually recreate the symlink to point to the correct native binary:
`rm ~/.cherrystudio/bin/claude`

`ln -s "~/.cherrystudio/install/cache/@anthropic-ai/claude-code-darwin-arm64@2.1.118@@@1/claude" ~/.cherrystudio/bin/claude`

`chmod +x ~/.cherrystudio/bin/claude`


## Root Cause
It appears that Bun's global install resolves the bin entry from package.json and creates a symlink to bin/claude.exe, but does not correctly resolve the optional dependency (@anthropic-ai/claude-code-darwin-arm64) that the postinstall script or runtime would normally use to replace the stub with the native binary. The postinstall script (which copies the native binary into place) may not be running during Bun's global install, or the symlink is created before postinstall has a chance to run.

title: [Bug]:  Mistral Small 4 / mistral-small-2603 is missing vision and reasoning_effort support

- [x] I've filled in short, clear headings so that developers can quickly identify a rough idea of what to expect when flipping through the list of issues. And not "a suggestion", "stuck", etc.
- [x] I've confirmed that I am using the latest version of Cherry Studio.

### Platform

Windows

### Version

v1.9.2

### Bug Description

Mistral Small 4 (`mistral-small-2603`, also exposed through `mistral-small-latest`) supports image input and adjustable reasoning according to Mistral's official docs, but Cherry Studio's built-in Mistral provider does not seem to handle those capabilities correctly.

The two problems I ran into:

1. `mistral-small-2603` is not detected as a vision model by default, so image input is not available unless I manually edit the model and enable the Vision capability.

2. Mistral Small 4 supports adjustable reasoning through the `reasoning_effort` request parameter, but setting this as an assistant custom parameter under Cherry Studio's built-in `Providers -> Mistral` does not appear to enable thinking/reasoning.

I tested this on Windows with the built-in Mistral provider using a normal local Cherry Studio setup.

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Open Cherry Studio.
2. Go to `Settings -> Providers -> Mistral`.
3. Configure the built-in Mistral provider.
4. Add or use the model `mistral-small-2603`.
5. Select this model in an assistant.
6. Try to attach/send an image.

Observed:
- Image input is not available by default for `mistral-small-2603`.

Then try to enable reasoning:

7. Open the assistant's model settings.
8. Add a custom parameter:
   - name: `reasoning_effort`
   - type: `string`
   - value: `high`
9. Send a normal chat request using `mistral-small-2603`.

Observed:
- The model does not appear to receive or apply Mistral's `reasoning_effort` setting.

### Expected Behavior

Cherry Studio's built-in Mistral provider should correctly support Mistral Small 4 capabilities:

- `mistral-small-2603` should be recognized as a vision-capable model.
- Image input should be available without manually overriding the model capability.
- The Mistral provider should support sending `reasoning_effort`, for example:
  - `reasoning_effort: "high"`
  - `reasoning_effort: "none"`

For Mistral's Chat Completions API, this parameter should be sent as part of the request body.

### Relevant Log Output

```shell

```

### Additional Context

Mistral docs:

- Mistral Small 4 announcement:
  https://mistral.ai/news/mistral-small-4

- Adjustable reasoning docs:
  https://docs.mistral.ai/studio-api/conversations/reasoning/adjustable

- Mistral chat endpoint docs:
  https://docs.mistral.ai/api/endpoint/chat

I did a quick read through Cherry Studio's source and I think this may be caused by two separate config/code-path issues.

For vision, the model detection appears to include older/current aliases such as `mistral-small-2506` and `mistral-small-latest`, but not the new explicit model id `mistral-small-2603`.

For reasoning, adding `reasoning_effort` as an assistant custom parameter does not seem to work with the built-in Mistral provider because Cherry routes built-in Mistral through the AI SDK Mistral provider. In that path, the custom parameter appears to be treated as a provider option, not necessarily as Mistral's top-level chat-completions request field.

In other words, I can add this in the UI:

```json
{
  "reasoning_effort": "high"
}

but with the built-in Mistral provider it does not look like Cherry sends it in the same way Mistral's API expects:

{
  "model": "mistral-small-2603",
  "messages": [...],
  "reasoning_effort": "high"
}

As a workaround, using an OpenAI-compatible/New API style provider pointed at Mistral may be able to pass the parameter, but the built-in `Providers -> Mistral` integration should ideally support this directly.

### Platform

macOS

### Version

v2.0.0-alpha

### Is your feature request related to an existing issue?

Every consumer that kicks off a translation (`TranslatePage`, `ActionTranslate`, `TranslateWindow`, the space-key auto-translate in `InputbarCore`, and potentially others) hand-rolls the same flow:

- call `translateText()`
- manage an `isTranslating` state
- suppress `isAbortError` on user-initiated cancels
- log the failure
- surface a toast with `formatErrorMessageWithPrefix`
- manage its own abort controller wiring

Because every consumer owns the boilerplate, they drift. Code review on PR #13871 caught `InputbarCore` and `TranslateWindow` independently mis-handling the same concerns (wrong log level, missing toast, no abort-error distinction), which each had to be patched in place. New translate entry points added in the future will repeat the drift.

### Desired Solution

Extract a single `useTranslate` hook that owns the translate flow end-to-end — the call, the loading state, the abort handling, and the standard error presentation — so each consumer just hands it input text and a target language.

Consumers that need custom behavior (e.g. a page that shows errors inline rather than as a toast) should be able to opt out of the default feedback via options, mirroring how `useMutationFeedback` works for the mutation hooks added earlier in this PR.

git log shows there used to be a `useTranslate` hook (`97af83c2f refactor: move useTranslate hook to translate module`) that has since been dissolved back into its consumers. This issue is asking to revive that direction with the benefit of hindsight.

### Alternative Solutions

Leaving the boilerplate duplicated and patching each consumer individually — current state, and what PR #13871's translate review threads made visible.

### Additional Information

Consumers that should migrate to the hook in the rollout:

- `src/renderer/src/pages/translate/TranslatePage.tsx`
- `src/renderer/src/windows/selection/action/components/ActionTranslate.tsx`
- `src/renderer/src/windows/quickAssistant/translate/TranslateWindow.tsx`

- [x] I have checked the pinned issues and searched through the existing [open issues](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/issues), [closed issues](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20state%3Aclosed), and [discussions](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/discussions) and did not find a similar suggestion.
- [x] I have provided a short and descriptive title so that developers can quickly understand the issue when browsing the issue list, rather than vague titles like "A suggestion" or "Stuck."
- [x] The latest version of Cherry Studio does not include the feature I am suggesting.

### Platform

macOS

### Version

2.0.0-alpha

### Is your feature request related to an existing issue?

This request is built on top of the ongoing work on the `v2` branch and is the assistant/agent counterpart to #14483.

The background is the same: the v2 data refactor moves renderer-side data to the new data layer (consumed via DataApi-based hooks), and the UI refactor moves new components to the Shadcn + Tailwind direction under `@cherrystudio/ui`. New consumers — chiefly the `pages/library` editor flows, which are not allowed to reuse `AgentSettings` or `pages-agents` components — need a way to pick an assistant or an agent without each editor reinventing its own popup.

Continuing to extend the legacy pickers (`AddAssistantPopup`, the `pages-agents` sidebar, etc.) directly is expensive and cannot keep behavior fully aligned once the underlying data layer and UI conventions have changed. As with #14483, it makes more sense to introduce a v2-aligned standalone selector instead of patching the legacy ones in place.

### Desired Solution

Introduce **one shared presentational selector composite in `@cherrystudio/ui`** plus **two thin business wrappers in the renderer** built on top of it.

**1. Shared selector composite (in `@cherrystudio/ui`)** — fully presentational, no business or data-layer dependency. An audit of the current `@cherrystudio/ui` surface shows that the closest existing piece (`Combobox`, which already has multi-select + search + custom trigger) does not cover the required structure: it has no per-item left/right action slots, no sticky footer row, and no filter-toggle panel. Rather than overload `Combobox` with unrelated concerns, this should ship as a new composite layered on top of the existing `Popover` / `Command` / `Button` primitives. Layout the composite must support:

- a business-supplied `trigger` slot (any node)
- on click: a popover containing
  - **top row**: search input + a filter toggle button (the filter panel expands to show tag chips + sort dropdown)
  - a multi-select toolbar with a multi-select on/off toggle (whether multi-select is allowed is decided by the consumer via prop)
  - a vertically scrollable list with a max height; **each row exposes two action affordances**: left side (pin button + selected-state mark) and right side ("jump to detail config page")
  - a bottom sticky row with a single "create new" entry that always shows and jumps to the create page
- both single-select and multi-select modes (mode is a prop)

**2. `AssistantSelectorV2`** (renderer business wrapper) — wraps the shared composite with the assistant data source, the assistant tag filter (via the existing tag system), the assistant detail/create routes, and the assistant pinning preference key.

**3. `AgentSelectorV2`** (renderer business wrapper) — wraps the shared composite with the agent data source, the agent detail/create routes, and the agent pinning preference key. The tag filter is intentionally not included in the first cut; an agent tag filter is planned as a follow-up once agent data grows a tag concept.

Pinning is part of the v2 data design, aligned with the model pinning direction in #14483: pinned IDs should be stored in user Preference under v2 storage rather than as ad-hoc local UI state, so they persist across sessions and sync across windows.

The composite and the wrappers should follow the new Shadcn + Tailwind conventions; legacy UI patterns (antd, styled-components, ad-hoc popups) must not be introduced.

### Alternative Solutions

Continue modifying `AddAssistantPopup`, the `pages-agents` sidebar, and other legacy assistant/agent pickers in place, attempting to migrate them to the v2 data layer and UI stack while preserving their old internal structure.

This is cheaper short-term but raises long-term migration cost and makes it harder to align these pickers with the v2 data flow, UI conventions, and pinning storage model. It also leaves `@cherrystudio/ui` without a reusable selector composite, which means future selectors (e.g. the `ModelSelectorV2` proposed in #14483) cannot share the same primitive.

### Additional Information

- Scope: one shared presentational composite in `@cherrystudio/ui` + two renderer business wrappers (`AssistantSelectorV2`, `AgentSelectorV2`).
- The shared composite is intentionally placed in `@cherrystudio/ui` (rather than in the renderer next to the wrappers) so future selectors — including the `ModelSelectorV2` work in #14483 — can compose the same primitive instead of duplicating the structure.
- Tag filter: Assistant-only in this iteration; Agent tag filter is a planned follow-up.
- Pinning: aligned with #14483 — pinned IDs go into Preference.
- Out of scope: migrating existing legacy call sites; agent tag filter; full batch-operation UX in the multi-select toolbar (the toolbar slot itself is in scope, but specific batch actions are deferred to consumers).

- [x] I've filled in short, clear headings so that developers can quickly identify a rough idea of what to expect when flipping through the list of issues. And not "a suggestion", "stuck", etc.
- [x] I've confirmed that I am using the latest version of Cherry Studio.

### Platform

macOS

### Version

v2.0.0-alpha

### Bug Description

The repository's pre-commit hook and the CI "Lint Check" step do not run the same set of linters, so lint failures show up in CI even when pre-commit passed locally.

The `Lint Check` job in `basic-checks` runs `pnpm lint`, whose script composition is:

```
oxlint --fix && eslint . --ext … --fix --cache && pnpm typecheck && pnpm i18n:check && pnpm format
```

The pre-commit hook (`.pre-commit-config.yaml`) only runs ESLint on staged files; there is no oxlint step:

```yaml
- id: eslint-fix
  entry: pnpm eslint --fix
```

Rules that live in oxlint but aren't enforced by the project's ESLint config therefore pass pre-commit and break CI. A concrete case hit during PR #13871: oxlint's `typescript/consistent-type-imports` rejected an import in `_mutationFeedback.ts` that used `loggerService` only inside `typeof`; pre-commit's ESLint step accepted it, CI's `pnpm lint` failed.

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Introduce a type-only import in a TS file written as a value import, e.g. `import { loggerService } from '@logger'` when `loggerService` is only referenced inside `typeof`.
2. Run `pnpm eslint --fix` (what pre-commit executes) — passes.
3. Run `pnpm lint` (what CI executes) — fails with `All imports in the declaration are only used as types. Use \`import type\`.`

### Expected Behavior

Pre-commit catches anything that CI's `Lint Check` step would catch. Either:

- add an `oxlint-fix` hook before `eslint-fix` in `.pre-commit-config.yaml`, or
- replace the current `eslint-fix` entry with `pnpm test:lint` (oxlint + eslint, aligned with the CI command), accepting the extra runtime cost.

### Relevant Log Output

```shell
X Lint Check
…
X All imports in the declaration are only used as types. Use `import type`.
basic-checks: src/renderer/src/hooks/translate/_mutationFeedback.ts#1
```

### Additional Context

Failing CI run (pre fix): https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/actions/runs/24837890810
Follow-up commit that patched it in-tree: 68f95adc6 (on PR #13871).

title: Make auto-i18n cover the v2 branch
body:
`.github/workflows/auto-i18n.yml` syncs locales nightly but its PR-creation step is hardcoded to `base: "main"` (line 88). Active v2 development lives on the `v2` branch, so any i18n key added during v2 work never gets its translations backfilled automatically — contributors must hand-run `pnpm i18n:sync` inside every feature PR that touches i18n or the `i18n Check` CI step will fail.

Hit this on PR #13871: a `translate.error.detect.failed` key added to `zh-cn` + `en-us` but missing in `zh-tw` (and the extra locales under `src/renderer/src/i18n/translate/*.json`) tripped CI until the sync was run manually.

## Desired

Auto-i18n should also cover `v2` while it's the active development line. Any of these shapes works:

- run the workflow as a matrix over `main` and `v2`, each creating its own sync PR against the corresponding base; or
- duplicate the workflow with `base: "v2"`; or
- expose a manual-dispatch input that picks the target branch on demand.

## Related

- Context PR: #13871
- Failing CI run: https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/actions/runs/24838046357

When an agent runs through external channels like QQ bots, I hope it can **automatically start a new conversation** when the conversation approaches or reaches the token limit, avoiding service interruption without requiring manual user intervention.

### Use Case
My use case is integrating the Cherry Studio agent with a QQ bot to achieve 7×24 automatic reply service. However, in practice, I encountered the following problems:

1. **Conversation interruption**: When the agent runs in the QQ bot, it cannot automatically continue after reaching the limit, causing users to not receive replies

- **Trigger condition**: When the conversation reaches a set token threshold (e.g., 80% or 90%)

    $ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'

        Title   = 'Cyan'
        Step    = 'Yellow'
        Success = 'Green'
        Warning = 'DarkYellow'
        Error   = 'Red'
        Info    = 'White'
    }

    function Write-Step { param($n, $msg) Write-Host "[$n] $msg" -f $Colors.Step }
    function Write-Success { param($msg) Write-Host "✓ $msg" -f $Colors.Success }
    function Write-Warning { param($msg) Write-Host "⚠ $msg" -f $Colors.Warning }
    function Write-Error { param($msg) Write-Host "✗ $msg" -f $Colors.Error }

    # Silent mode output
    if (-not $Silent) {
        Write-Host ""
        Write-Host "  Cherry Studio Claude Code Updater" -f $Colors.Title
        Write-Host "  ────────────────────────────────────" -f $Colors.Title
        Write-Host ""
    }

    # Check bun
    if (-not (Get-Command bun -EA SilentlyContinue)) {
        Write-Error "bun not found, please install: powershell -c 'irm bun.sh/install.ps1|iex'"
        return $false
    }

    # Step 1: Upgrade bun
    if (-not $NoBun) {
        Write-Step 1 "Checking bun version..."
        $bunCurrent = (bun --version)
        if (-not $Silent) { Write-Host "  Current: v$bunCurrent" -f $Colors.Info }

        Write-Step 1 "Upgrading bun..."
        try {
            Invoke-RestMethod bun.sh/install.ps1 | Invoke-Expression
            $bunNew = (bun --version)
            Write-Success "bun upgraded to v$bunNew"
        } catch {
            Write-Warning "bun upgrade failed, continuing with subsequent steps..."
        }
    }

    # Step 2: Update Claude Code
    Write-Step 2 "Updating Claude Code..."
    bun remove -g claude-code 2>$null
    bun install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code

    $claudeVer = & "$HOME\.bun\bin\claude.exe" --version
    Write-Success "Claude Code $claudeVer"

    # Step 3: Close Cherry Studio
    Write-Step 3 "Checking Cherry Studio..."
    $cherryProcess = Get-Process -Name "Cherry Studio" -EA SilentlyContinue
    if ($cherryProcess) {
        Write-Warning "Cherry Studio is running, closing..."
        Stop-Process -Name "Cherry Studio" -Force
        Start-Sleep -Seconds 2
        Write-Success "Cherry Studio closed"
    } else {
        if (-not $Silent) { Write-Host "  Cherry Studio not running" -f $Colors.Info }
    }

    # Step 4: Replace wrapper
    Write-Step 4 "Replacing wrapper files..."
    $bunBin = "$HOME\.bun\bin"
    $cherryBin = "$HOME\.cherrystudio\bin"

    try {
        Remove-Item "$cherryBin\claude.exe" -Force -EA SilentlyContinue
        Remove-Item "$cherryBin\claude.bunx" -Force -EA SilentlyContinue

        Copy-Item "$bunBin\claude.exe" "$cherryBin\claude.exe" -Force
        Copy-Item "$bunBin\claude.bunx" "$cherryBin\claude.bunx" -Force

        Write-Success "Wrapper replaced"
    } catch {
        Write-Error "Replacement failed: $_"
        Write-Warning "Please close Cherry Studio manually and run again"
        return $false
    }

    # Step 5: Verification
    Write-Step 5 "Verifying version..."
    if (-not $Silent) {
        Write-Host ""
        Write-Host "  bun:        v$(bun --version)" -f $Colors.Info
        Write-Host "  Claude Code: $claudeVer" -f $Colors.Info
    }

    Write-Host ""
    Write-Host "  ────────────────────────────────────" -f $Colors.Title
    Write-Success "Update complete\! Please restart Cherry Studio"
    Write-Host ""

    return $true
}`

### Platform

Linux

### Version

v2 (dev branch)

### Bug Description

In V2 dark mode, the Code Tools page (`/app/code`) has severe visibility problems:

1. **CLI tool icons**: GitHub Copilot CLI and OpenCode icons use hardcoded `fill="#000"` in their SVG, making them invisible against dark backgrounds.
2. **Text elements nearly invisible**: Many Tailwind classes apply opacity modifiers (e.g. `/30`, `/40`, `/50`) on top of semantic color tokens that already have reduced opacity in dark mode (e.g. `--cs-foreground-muted` is `oklch(1 0 0 / 0.4)`). This double-opacity reduction makes text effectively 5-12% white — nearly invisible. Affected elements include:
   - Search bar background, border, and placeholder text
   - Tool count label
   - Field labels and info icons
   - Provider names in model dropdown
   - Section title in tool grid
   - Official badge text
   - Environment variables textarea border and placeholder
   - Auto-update checkbox label
   - Drawer footer summary text and separator dots
   - Tool card border and background

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Switch to dark mode
2. Navigate to Code Tools page (`/app/code`)
3. Observe that many text labels, borders, and icons are nearly invisible
4. Open any tool's launch configuration drawer — labels, info icons, and summary text are barely visible

### Expected Behavior

All text, icons, borders, and interactive elements should have sufficient contrast against the dark background to be clearly readable and usable.

### Additional Context

Root causes:
1. SVG icons with `fill="#000"` instead of `fill="currentColor"` — only affects `githubCopilotCli.tsx` and `openCode.tsx`; other CLI icons use brand colors correctly.
2. Double-opacity problem: dark mode semantic tokens already carry reduced opacity (~40% for muted text, ~10% for borders), and Tailwind opacity modifiers further halve them. Fix is to remove or reduce the extra opacity modifiers for dark-mode-appropriate values.

title: [Bug]: useMutation refresh option silently misses useSWRInfinite cache keys
body:
### Issue Checklist

- [x] I understand that issues are for feedback and problem solving, not for complaining in the comment section, and will provide as much information as possible to help solve the problem.
- [x] My issue is not listed in the [FAQ](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/issues/3881).
- [x] I've looked at **pinned issues** and searched for existing [Open Issues](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/issues), [Closed Issues](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20state%3Aclosed), and [Discussions](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/discussions), no similar issue or discussion was found.
- [x] I've filled in short, clear headings so that developers can quickly identify a rough idea of what to expect when flipping through the list of issues. And not "a suggestion", "stuck", etc.
- [x] I've confirmed that I am using the latest version of Cherry Studio.

### Platform

macOS (cross-platform; this is a renderer framework bug)

### Version

v2.0.0-alpha (`v2` branch)

### Bug Description

`useMutation`'s `refresh` option is documented to invalidate every cache key whose path matches the supplied pattern. **It silently fails to invalidate any `useSWRInfinite` cache key**, even when the path matches.

This breaks the invariant that `useTranslateHistories` (and `useSessions`) explicitly rely on:

```
// src/renderer/src/hooks/translate/useTranslateHistories.ts
* - Mutations elsewhere (`useAddHistory`, `useDeleteHistory`, `useClearHistory`,
*   `useUpdateHistory`) call `refresh: ['/translate/histories']`, which invalidates
*   every page this hook holds because all keys share that path prefix.
```

User-visible symptom: after `useAddHistory` succeeds, the `TranslateHistoryList` drawer does not reflect the new entry — the user has to close and reopen the drawer (which re-mounts the hook) to see it.

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Open the renderer translate module.
2. Open the history drawer (`TranslateHistoryList`).
3. From `TranslatePage`, run a translation that triggers `useAddHistory().mutate(...)`.
4. Observe the drawer — the new record does **not** appear until the drawer is closed and reopened, even though `dataApiService.post('/translate/histories')` returns 200 and the row is committed in SQLite.

Same symptom applies to `useDeleteHistory` / `useUpdateHistory` / `useClearHistory` — none of them propagate to the live list.

Minimal repro outside translate:

```ts
const { items } = useTranslateHistories() // wraps useSWRInfinite('/translate/histories', ...)
const addHistory = useAddHistory()        // useMutation('POST', '/translate/histories', { refresh: ['/translate/histories'] })

await addHistory({ ... })
// → POST 200
// → server has the row
// → globalMutate(matcher) is called by the framework
// → matcher returns false for every $inf$ key
// → `items` does NOT update
```

### Expected Behavior

`refresh: ['/translate/histories']` (and `/translate/histories/*` prefix patterns) should invalidate **every** SWR cache key whose path matches, regardless of whether the consumer is `useSWR`, `useQuery`, or `useSWRInfinite`.

### Relevant Log Output

```shell
N/A — failure is silent. The mutation succeeds, the matcher runs, but no SWR
cache entry matches, so no revalidation fires.
```

### Additional Context

#### Root cause

The matcher in `useDataApi.ts` only inspects array-shaped cache keys:

```ts
// src/renderer/src/data/hooks/useDataApi.ts:1102
function createKeyMatcher(pattern: string): (key: unknown) => boolean {
  assertValidPattern(pattern)
  if (pattern.endsWith('/*')) {
    const prefix = pattern.slice(0, -1)
    return (key) => Array.isArray(key) && typeof key[0] === 'string' && key[0].startsWith(prefix)
  }
  return (key) => Array.isArray(key) && key[0] === pattern
}
```

But `useSWRInfinite` serializes its cache keys as a **string** with the form `'$inf$' + stableHash(originalKey)`. Verified empirically:

```js
// node REPL
const { unstable_serialize } = require('swr')
const { unstable_serialize: serializeInfinite } = require('swr/infinite')

unstable_serialize(['/translate/histories', 1, 50])
// → '@"/translate/histories",1,50,'

serializeInfinite(() => ['/translate/histories', 1, 50])
// → '$inf$@"/translate/histories",1,50,'
```

`Array.isArray('$inf$@"/translate/histories",...')` is always `false`, so `globalMutate(matcher)` skips every infinite cache entry. The matcher never sees the path embedded in the serialized form.

The `INFINITE_PREFIX = '$inf$'` constant is defined in `swr/_internal/constants.ts`.

#### Scope of impact

Any hook that combines `useSWRInfinite` with `useMutation`'s `refresh`. Today:

- `useTranslateHistories` + `useAddHistory` / `useDeleteHistory` / `useUpdateHistory` / `useClearHistory` (broken — this is the user-visible regression in PR #13871).
- `useSessions` (the agents module) — happens to dodge the bug by exposing `mutate` and doing optimistic updates manually instead of relying on `refresh`. The framework gap is invisible from the agents side because nobody points `refresh` at it.
- `useDataApi.ts`'s own `useInfiniteQuery` (cursor pagination wrapper) — same underlying `useSWRInfinite`, would silently miss any `refresh` aimed at it. No consumer pairs cursor endpoints with `refresh` today, so the bug stays latent.

#### Suggested fix

Extend `createKeyMatcher` / `createMultiKeyMatcher` to recognize `useSWRInfinite` cache keys by extracting the path from the serialized form:

```ts
const SWR_INFINITE_PREFIX = '$inf$'

function extractPath(key: unknown): string | undefined {
  if (Array.isArray(key) && typeof key[0] === 'string') return key[0]
  if (typeof key === 'string' && key.startsWith(SWR_INFINITE_PREFIX)) {
    const stripped = key.slice(SWR_INFINITE_PREFIX.length)
    if (!stripped.startsWith('@"')) return undefined
    const closeQuoteIdx = stripped.indexOf('"', 2)
    return closeQuoteIdx === -1 ? undefined : stripped.slice(2, closeQuoteIdx)
  }
  return undefined
}
```

Then both matchers route their `key[0] === pattern` / `key[0].startsWith(prefix)` check through `extractPath(key)`. This restores the invariant the existing JSDoc and consumer comments already promise, and fixes every current and future `useSWRInfinite` consumer in one place.

A workaround on the consumer side (mirror `useSessions`: expose `mutate`, drop `refresh` from the translate mutations, and patch the cache by hand) is possible but requires every future `useSWRInfinite` consumer to repeat the dance and contradicts the framework's documented `refresh` contract.

#### Related references

- `src/renderer/src/data/hooks/useDataApi.ts:1088-1130` — current matcher implementation
- `src/renderer/src/hooks/translate/useTranslateHistories.ts:28-32` — relied-upon (false) invariant
- `src/renderer/src/hooks/translate/useAddHistory.ts` — caller that motivates this fix
- `src/renderer/src/hooks/agents/useSessions.ts` — the consumer-side workaround pattern
- `node_modules/swr/dist/_internal/constants.{js,mjs,d.ts}` — `INFINITE_PREFIX = '$inf$'`

title: [Feature]: Brand TranslateLangCode / PersistedLangCode for compile-time validation
body:
### Issue Checklist

- [x] I understand that issues are for reporting problems and requesting features, not for off-topic comments, and I will provide as much detail as possible to help resolve the issue.
- [x] I have checked the pinned issues and searched through the existing [open issues](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/issues), [closed issues](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20state%3Aclosed), and [discussions](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/discussions) and did not find a similar suggestion.
- [x] I have provided a short and descriptive title so that developers can quickly understand the issue when browsing the issue list, rather than vague titles like "A suggestion" or "Stuck."
- [x] The latest version of Cherry Studio does not include the feature I am suggesting.

### Platform

macOS (cross-platform; this is a renderer/shared types refactor)

### Version

v2.0.0-alpha (`v2` branch)

### Is your feature request related to an existing issue?

Surfaced by PR #13871 review item #12. The repeating pain point: `PersistedLangCodeSchema` and `TranslateLangCodeSchema` in `packages/shared/data/preference/preferenceTypes.ts` are declared as

```ts
export const PersistedLangCodeSchema = z.string().regex(/^[a-z]{2,3}(-[a-z]{2,4})?$/)
export const TranslateLangCodeSchema = z.union([z.literal('unknown'), PersistedLangCodeSchema])
export type TranslateLangCode = z.infer<typeof TranslateLangCodeSchema>
// → 'unknown' | string
```

So the regex / `'unknown'`-only-as-UI-sentinel invariants exist purely at runtime. The type system cannot tell a validated lang code from any random string.

This has caused several "UNKNOWN leaks past the persistence boundary" bugs already in the v2 translate work; each was fixed reactively by adding a `coerce UNKNOWN → null` step at the boundary (e.g. commit `bc62d1138`, the entire `_mutationFeedback`-related round in PR #13871). Without compile-time branding the same class of bug is one careless caller away from coming back.

### Desired Solution

Apply `.brand<...>()` to lift the regex / sentinel invariant to compile time:

```ts
export const PersistedLangCodeSchema = z
  .string()
  .regex(/^[a-z]{2,3}(-[a-z]{2,4})?$/)
  .brand<'PersistedLangCode'>()
export type PersistedLangCode = z.infer<typeof PersistedLangCodeSchema>
// → string & { [BRAND]: 'PersistedLangCode' }

export const TranslateLangCodeSchema = z.union([z.literal('unknown'), PersistedLangCodeSchema])
export type TranslateLangCode = z.infer<typeof TranslateLangCodeSchema>
// → 'unknown' | PersistedLangCode
```

After branding, only `PersistedLangCodeSchema.parse(...)` (or an explicit `as PersistedLangCode` cast at a sanctioned helper) can produce a `PersistedLangCode`. Service / DB / DTO boundaries stop accepting raw strings, and the entire "did the caller remember to coerce 'unknown' to null?" worry goes away at compile time.

### Alternative Solutions

PR #13871 review describes this as "minimal changes." It is **not minimal** in the current codebase, because branding propagates through several long-standing patterns:

1. **`BUILTIN_LANGUAGE` (`packages/shared/data/presets/translate-languages.ts`)** uses
   ```ts
   } as const satisfies Record<string, { langCode: TranslateLangCode; value: string; emoji: string }>
   ```
   After branding, `langCode: 'en-us'` (a plain string literal) is no longer assignable to `TranslateLangCode`. The `satisfies` constraint must drop to `langCode: string` plus a module-load runtime parse check, or every entry needs a cast.

2. **`langCodeToI18nKey`** uses `satisfies Record<(typeof BUILTIN_LANGUAGE)[keyof typeof BUILTIN_LANGUAGE]['langCode'] | 'unknown', string>` for exhaustiveness checking — depends on the literal-union recovered from `BUILTIN_LANGUAGE`. Survives if `as const` is preserved, but worth verifying after the satisfies change.

3. **`BuiltinLangCodeSchema = z.enum(BUILTIN_TRANSLATE_LANGUAGES.map(l => l.langCode))`** — same dependency chain.

4. **`packages/shared/data/preference/preferenceSchemas.ts`** is **auto-generated by `v2-refactor-temp/tools/data-classify`** (see CLAUDE.md "MUST READ" rule). It currently emits string-literal defaults like
   ```ts
   'feature.translate.action.alter_lang': 'en-us',
   'feature.translate.action.preferred_lang': 'zh-cn',
   ```
   Branded `TranslateLangCode` rejects these literals, so the data-classify generator has to be taught to emit casts (or wrap defaults in `PersistedLangCodeSchema.parse(...)`).

5. **34 `: TranslateLangCode` signatures** across `src/` and `packages/`. Signatures themselves don't change, but every call site that passes a literal needs a cast or to thread the value through a parsing helper.

6. **Tests / mocks / config** — many hardcoded `'en-us'` style values, all need cast or parse.

Two ways to scope this:

- **A. Full brand.** Schema + BUILTIN_LANGUAGE satisfies relaxation + module-load runtime check + data-classify generator update + cast/parse migration across all consumers. Best end state, big mechanical PR.
- **B. Boundary-local brand.** Don't touch the public schema; declare a local `WrittenLangCode = string & { __brand: 'WrittenLangCode' }` plus an `assertWrittenLangCode(s: string): WrittenLangCode` helper inside the translate service / migrator. Forces the immediate boundary callers but doesn't propagate. Smaller, doesn't ripple through `BUILTIN_LANGUAGE` / generator, but only protects one layer.

A is the right long-term answer; B is a stepping stone if A's blast radius is too large for one PR.

### Additional Information

PR #13871 deferred this fix on the grounds that it requires touching the data-classify code generator (out of translate-renderer scope) and would balloon an already 5K-line PR. The current runtime defense (coerce-at-boundary in mutation hooks + `_mutationFeedback`) is sufficient to ship; this issue tracks the structural fix.

References:

- `packages/shared/data/preference/preferenceTypes.ts:122-145` — current schema
- `packages/shared/data/presets/translate-languages.ts:17-72` — `BUILTIN_LANGUAGE` and derived types
- `packages/shared/data/preference/preferenceSchemas.ts:395-435` — auto-generated defaults
- `v2-refactor-temp/tools/data-classify/` — code generator that owns `preferenceSchemas.ts`
- PR #13871 review #12 — original suggestion

### Platform

Windows

### Version

1.9.3

### Bug Description

I am experiencing two critical issues with the spell check functionality in version 1.9.3:

1. Focus-Dependent Highlighting: Misspelled words are no longer highlighted in real-time as I type. The red underline only appears if the input field loses focus and then regains it. This "focus-toggle" requirement makes the spell checker practically unusable for real-time editing.

2. Silent Failure in Secondary Languages: While the primary language catches errors (only after the focus-toggle mentioned above), the second or third enabled languages fail to flag misspelled words at all. They provide zero validation, treating every misspelled string in those languages as correct.

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Open Cherry Studio 1.9.3 on Windows.
2. Go to Settings and enable Spell Check, selecting at least two languages (e.g., English and Greek).
3. Start typing a misspelled word in the editor. Observe that no error highlight appears.
4. Click outside the editor window (lose focus) and then click back inside (gain focus). Observe that the error highlight now appears.
5. Type a incorrectly spelled word in the second enabled language. Observe that it is not flagged as an error despite being enabled in settings.

### Expected Behavior

1. Misspelled words should be highlighted immediately (real-time) as the user types, without requiring focus changes.

2. The spell checker should actively validate and flag misspelled words in all languages selected in the settings simultaneously. Enabling a second language should not result in a silent bypass of error detection for that language.

### Relevant Log Output

```shell

```

### Additional Context

This behavior started appearing in the 1.9.x branch. Previous versions handled real-time highlighting more efficiently. The multi-language issue suggests a logic error where the engine only initializes a single dictionary instance instead of a composite one.

title: [Bug]: useInfiniteQuery's mutate type erases extra fields beyond CursorPaginationResponse<T>
body:
### Issue Checklist

- [x] I understand that issues are for feedback and problem solving, not for complaining in the comment section, and will provide as much information as possible to help solve the problem.
- [x] My issue is not listed in the [FAQ](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/issues/3881).
- [x] I've looked at **pinned issues** and searched for existing Open Issues, Closed Issues, and Discussions, no similar issue or discussion was found.
- [x] I've filled in short, clear headings so that developers can quickly identify a rough idea of what to expect when flipping through the list of issues.
- [x] I've confirmed that I am using the latest version of Cherry Studio.

### Platform

macOS

### Version

v2.0.0-alpha

### Bug Description

`useInfiniteQuery` in `src/renderer/src/data/hooks/useDataApi.ts` types its returned `mutate` as `KeyedMutator<CursorPaginationResponse<T>[]>`, where `T` is the item type inferred from `InferPaginatedItem<TPath>`.

This shape is wrong for any endpoint whose response **extends** `CursorPaginationResponse<T>` with extra top-level fields. The most concrete case in the codebase: `BranchMessagesResponse extends CursorPaginationResponse<BranchMessage>` and adds `activeNodeId: string | null`.

When a consumer reads or writes pages via the returned `mutate`, the type system erases `activeNodeId` (and any other extras), so updater callbacks cannot read or modify the field without an unsafe cast.

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Open `src/renderer/src/data/hooks/useDataApi.ts` and look at `UseInfiniteQueryResult<T>` (around line 184) and the `useInfiniteQuery` function definition.
2. Note that the mutate field is typed `KeyedMutator<CursorPaginationResponse<T>[]>` — only the item type `T` flows through.
3. Try to consume it for a path whose schema declares `response: BranchMessagesResponse`:

```ts
const { mutate } = useInfiniteQuery('/topics/:topicId/messages', {
  params: { topicId },
  query: { includeSiblings: true },
  limit: 50
})

// Want to write a new pages array that preserves activeNodeId:
const refreshed: BranchMessagesResponse[] = await someFetch()
await mutate(refreshed)
//        ^^^^^^^^^
// Type error: BranchMessagesResponse[] is not assignable to
// CursorPaginationResponse<BranchMessage>[].
//
// Workaround that consumers end up adopting:
//   mutate as unknown as KeyedMutator<BranchMessagesResponse[]>
// — defeats type safety, has to be repeated in every consumer.
```

### Expected Behavior

The hook should preserve the **full response type** declared in the path schema, not collapse it to `CursorPaginationResponse<T>`. `mutate`, and any cache-related fields, should be typed against the actual response shape so consumers can read/write top-level extras (`activeNodeId`, custom pagination metadata, etc.) without `unknown` casts.

### Relevant Log Output

```shell
Type 'KeyedMutator<CursorPaginationResponse<BranchMessage>[]>' is not assignable to type 'KeyedMutator<BranchMessagesResponse[]>'.
  Type 'CursorPaginationResponse<BranchMessage>[]' is not comparable to type 'BranchMessagesResponse[]'.
    Property 'activeNodeId' is missing in type 'CursorPaginationResponse<BranchMessage>' but required in type 'BranchMessagesResponse'.
```

### Additional Context

The pattern affects every path whose schema response is a `CursorPaginationResponse<T>` subtype. Today it's only `BranchMessagesResponse`, but any future paginated endpoint that wants to attach top-level metadata (`totalUnread`, `cursorMode`, `lastSyncTime`, etc.) hits the same wall.

The non-paginated read hook `useQuery` does not have this problem — it correctly types `data` as `ResponseForPath<TPath, 'GET'>`. Only `useInfiniteQuery` collapses the shape.

title: [Bug]: useInfiniteQuery's items flatMap breaks ordering for newest-page-first endpoints
body:
### Issue Checklist

- [x] I understand that issues are for feedback and problem solving, not for complaining in the comment section, and will provide as much information as possible to help solve the problem.
- [x] My issue is not listed in the [FAQ](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/issues/3881).
- [x] I've looked at **pinned issues** and searched for existing Open Issues, Closed Issues, and Discussions, no similar issue or discussion was found.
- [x] I've filled in short, clear headings so that developers can quickly identify a rough idea of what to expect when flipping through the list of issues.
- [x] I've confirmed that I am using the latest version of Cherry Studio.

### Platform

macOS

### Version

v2.0.0-alpha

### Bug Description

`useInfiniteQuery` in `src/renderer/src/data/hooks/useDataApi.ts` flattens its `items` field with a single, fixed strategy:

```ts
const items = useMemo(() => data?.flatMap((p) => p.items) ?? [], [data])
```

This implicitly assumes **page load order equals desired item order** — i.e. concatenating `page0.items, page1.items, ..., pageN.items` produces a monotonically ordered list. This holds for typical feed endpoints (newest-first within page, newest page loaded first → flatMap stays newest-first overall).

It fails for endpoints that paginate **newest-page-first** but keep within-page items in **oldest→newest** order. The branch-walk endpoint `/topics/:topicId/messages` is a real example: the server walks `parent_id` from `activeNode` toward root, slices off the most recent `limit` messages as page 0 (in chronological order), and returns earlier slices on subsequent pages.

For these endpoints, `items` ends up non-monotonic — order breaks at every page boundary. Consumers that expect a monotonic message list (rendering, scroll restore, `lastMessage` lookups) get visually broken output.

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Define an endpoint where the server returns "most recent N items" as page 0 (no cursor) with **within-page items in ascending chronological order**, and earlier pages as you cursor backward.
2. Build the cursor pagination so each page's `items` is `[oldestInPage, ..., newestInPage]` and `nextCursor` points to one slice further back in time.
3. Use `useInfiniteQuery` with this endpoint, load page 0 only, then call `loadNext()` to load page 1.
4. Inspect `items`. With pages `[ [m4, m5, m6], [m1, m2, m3] ]`, the default flatMap yields `[m4, m5, m6, m1, m2, m3]` — the order is broken at the boundary between page 0's items and page 1's items.

A concrete reproduction is `useTopicMessagesV2(topicId)` consuming `/topics/:topicId/messages` (see `src/main/data/services/MessageService.ts` `getBranchMessages` for the server-side logic that produces this shape).

### Expected Behavior

`useInfiniteQuery` should either:

1. Not assume page load order matches desired item order (let the consumer specify), or
2. Document the assumption explicitly and require endpoints to conform.

For the current branch-walk endpoint, every consumer would have to manually `pages.slice().reverse().flatMap(p => p.items)` — but `pages` isn't exposed by the hook either, only the (already incorrectly-ordered) `items` array. So callers are forced to either change the server, write their own infinite-query wrapper, or live with broken ordering.

### Relevant Log Output

```shell
N/A — the bug surfaces as visually wrong message ordering after `loadNext()`,
no error is logged.
```

### Additional Context

The downstream symptom in v2 chat: after the migration of `useTopicMessagesV2` from `useQuery(limit: 999)` to `useInfiniteQuery`, the latest assistant message disappears from view once a second page loads, because the broken order combined with the `column-reverse` layout in `Messages.tsx` puts it scrolled off-screen.

This is a real correctness limitation of the hook, not an edge case — any endpoint that paginates "going further back in time" while keeping pages in chronological reading order is affected.

title: [Bug] On Windows, default Git Bash tool ignores ~/.bash_profile and ~/.bashrc, breaking fnm / nvm / mise / asdf PATH setup (affects both external CLI launch and built-in agent/assistant shell tool)
body:
> This issue is written in both English and Chinese. The English version comes first, the Chinese translation follows below.
> 本 issue 提供英文与中文两个版本,英文在前,中文翻译在后。

---

## 🇬🇧 English

### Environment
- OS: Windows 11
- Cherry Studio: latest
- Default bash: Git Bash (`C:\Program Files\Git\bin\bash.exe`)
- Node version manager: fnm (also reproducible with nvm-windows-shellinit, mise, asdf, Volta, direnv)

### Problem
On Windows, when Cherry Studio uses Git Bash as the default bash, **the user's bash profile files are never sourced**. Only `process.env` plus the Windows registry `Environment` keys are read.

This affects **two distinct usage paths**, not just one:

1. **Launching external CLI tools** (claude-code, gemini-cli, etc.) from Cherry Studio.
2. **The built-in bash tool** that Cherry Studio exposes to the **Agents** and **Assistants** modules — i.e., when an agent or assistant calls a shell command via the internal tool, the same broken environment is inherited. So if a user asks an assistant to run `node script.js`, `npm install`, `npx some-tool`, etc., it will fail with `command not found` for the same root cause.

For users who manage Node.js with `fnm` (or any tool that mutates PATH via shell init), the line in `~/.bash_profile`:

```bash
eval "$(fnm env --shell bash)"
```

…never executes. As a result, both spawned external tools **and** the built-in agent/assistant bash tool see no `node` / `npm` / `npx` on PATH, even though running `node -v` inside an interactive Git Bash window works fine.

### Root cause
`src/main/utils/shell-env.ts` — `getLoginShellEnvironment()` short-circuits on Windows:

```ts
function getLoginShellEnvironment(): Promise<Record<string, string>> {
  // On Windows, skip the shell spawn entirely — `cmd.exe /c set` just inherits
  // the (potentially stale) parent process env. Instead, read the current PATH
  // straight from the Windows registry.
  if (isWin) {
    return Promise.resolve(getWindowsEnvironment())
  }
  // macOS/Linux: spawn(shellPath, ['-ilc', 'env'], ...)
}
```

`getWindowsEnvironment()` only merges `process.env` with the registry `PATH` from `HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Session Manager\Environment` and `HKCU\Environment`. It never spawns bash, so `~/.bash_profile`, `~/.bashrc`, `~/.profile` are completely invisible.

This `getLoginShellEnvironment()` result is the env baseline used by **every code path that spawns a child process** in Cherry Studio on Windows — both the external-CLI launcher (`src/main/services/CodeToolsService.ts`) and the built-in shell tool exposed to agents/assistants. Fix it once, both paths are fixed.

Meanwhile `findGitBash()` in `src/main/utils/process.ts` already locates `bash.exe` reliably (PATH → registry → common install paths → `CLAUDE_CODE_GIT_BASH_PATH`), but that discovered path is **never used to capture the user's shell environment**.

The macOS/Linux branch *does* run `spawn(shellPath, ['-ilc', 'env'])` which sources profile files. The Windows branch should do the equivalent when Git Bash is the configured default.

### Reproduction
1. Install fnm: `winget install Schniz.fnm`
2. Add to `~/.bash_profile`:
   ```bash
   eval "$(fnm env --shell bash)"
   ```
3. In a fresh Git Bash window, install Node: `fnm install --lts && fnm use lts-latest`
4. Confirm `node -v` works in Git Bash.
5. **Path A (external CLI):** In Cherry Studio, configure Git Bash as the default bash and launch any tool that needs Node (claude-code, gemini-cli). → fails with `node: command not found`.
6. **Path B (built-in tool):** In an Assistant or Agent, ask it to run `node -v` or `npm install` via the built-in bash/shell tool. → same failure.

### Suggested fix
When `findGitBash()` succeeds on Windows, spawn the discovered bash with `['-ilc', 'env']` (same approach as macOS/Linux), parse the output, and merge with the registry PATH. Pseudocode:

```ts
if (isWin) {
  const gitBash = await findGitBash()
  if (gitBash) {
    const env = await spawnAndCaptureEnv(gitBash, ['-ilc', 'env'])
    return mergeWithRegistryPath(env)
  }
  return getWindowsEnvironment() // fallback
}
```

This single fix repairs both the external-CLI launch path and the built-in agent/assistant shell tool, since both consume `getLoginShellEnvironment()`.

### Related feature request (lower priority)
`packages/shared/config/constant.ts` — `WINDOWS_TERMINALS_WITH_COMMANDS` currently lists only `cmd`, `powershell`, `windowsTerminal`, `wsl`, `alacritty`, `wezterm`. Please consider:
- Exposing **Git Bash** as a first-class selectable shell.
- Splitting **PowerShell 5 (`powershell`)** and **PowerShell 7 (`pwsh`)** as separate options — they have different module paths and execution policies.
- Adding **WSL2** as a selectable shell (currently only `wsl` launcher, not as a CLI tool host).
- Surfacing all of the above in a UI selector in settings, so users can switch without editing config files.

> ⚠️ Priority: the **profile-loading bug is the urgent one** — it silently breaks every Node-based CLI tool **and** every agent/assistant shell call for fnm/nvm/mise users on Windows. The shell selector enhancement is nice-to-have.

Thanks for the great work on Cherry Studio!

---

## 🇨🇳 中文

### 环境
- 系统:Windows 11
- Cherry Studio:最新版
- 默认 bash:Git Bash(`C:\Program Files\Git\bin\bash.exe`)
- Node 版本管理:fnm(同样问题也会出现在 nvm-windows-shellinit、mise、asdf、Volta、direnv 等)

### 问题
在 Windows 上,当 Cherry Studio 把 Git Bash 设为默认 bash 时,**用户的 bash profile 文件根本不会被加载**。它只会读取 `process.env` 与 Windows 注册表里的 `Environment` 项。

这个问题影响**两条不同的使用路径**,而不只是其中一条:

1. **从 Cherry Studio 启动外部 CLI 工具**(claude-code、gemini-cli 等)。
2. **Cherry Studio 暴露给「智能体」与「助手」模块的内置 bash 工具**——也就是说,当智能体/助手通过内置工具调用 shell 命令时,继承的是同样残缺的环境。所以用户让助手运行 `node script.js`、`npm install`、`npx some-tool` 等时,会因同一个根本原因报 `command not found`。

对于用 `fnm` 管理 Node 的用户(以及任何依赖 shell init 修改 PATH 的工具),写在 `~/.bash_profile` 里的:

```bash
eval "$(fnm env --shell bash)"
```

……永远不会执行。结果:无论是被启动的外部工具,**还是智能体/助手的内置 bash 工具**,在 PATH 里都看不到 `node` / `npm` / `npx`——尽管手动打开一个 Git Bash 窗口运行 `node -v` 是完全正常的。

### 根本原因
`src/main/utils/shell-env.ts` 中的 `getLoginShellEnvironment()` 在 Windows 下直接走了短路逻辑:

```ts
function getLoginShellEnvironment(): Promise<Record<string, string>> {
  // 在 Windows 上完全跳过 shell spawn —— `cmd.exe /c set` 只是继承
  // (可能是过时的)父进程环境变量。改为直接从注册表读取当前的 PATH。
  if (isWin) {
    return Promise.resolve(getWindowsEnvironment())
  }
  // macOS/Linux: spawn(shellPath, ['-ilc', 'env'], ...)
}
```

`getWindowsEnvironment()` 只把 `process.env` 与注册表 `HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Session Manager\Environment` 和 `HKCU\Environment` 中的 PATH 合并,完全没有调用 bash。所以 `~/.bash_profile`、`~/.bashrc`、`~/.profile` 完全不可见。

而 Windows 上 Cherry Studio **每一处启动子进程的代码路径**都以 `getLoginShellEnvironment()` 的返回值作为环境基线——既包括外部 CLI 启动器(`src/main/services/CodeToolsService.ts`),也包括给智能体/助手用的内置 shell 工具。修这一处,两条路径都会同时被修好。

而 `src/main/utils/process.ts` 中的 `findGitBash()` 其实已经能可靠地定位 `bash.exe`(顺序为 PATH → 注册表 → 常见安装路径 → `CLAUDE_CODE_GIT_BASH_PATH`),但**这个找到的路径从未被用来加载用户的 shell 环境**。

macOS / Linux 分支会执行 `spawn(shellPath, ['-ilc', 'env'])`,这会触发 profile 文件的加载。Windows 分支在 Git Bash 被设为默认时,理应做同样的事。

### 复现步骤
1. 安装 fnm:`winget install Schniz.fnm`
2. 在 `~/.bash_profile` 加入:
   ```bash
   eval "$(fnm env --shell bash)"
   ```
3. 打开一个新的 Git Bash 窗口,安装 Node:`fnm install --lts && fnm use lts-latest`
4. 确认 `node -v` 在 Git Bash 中可正常运行。
5. **路径 A(外部 CLI):** 在 Cherry Studio 把 Git Bash 设为默认 bash,启动任意需要 Node 的工具(claude-code、gemini-cli)。→ 报 `node: command not found`。
6. **路径 B(内置工具):** 在助手或智能体里,让它通过内置 bash/shell 工具运行 `node -v` 或 `npm install`。→ 同样失败。

### 建议修复
Windows 下 `findGitBash()` 成功时,用 `['-ilc', 'env']` 启动找到的 bash(与 macOS/Linux 一致),解析输出,再与注册表 PATH 合并。伪代码:

```ts
if (isWin) {
  const gitBash = await findGitBash()
  if (gitBash) {
    const env = await spawnAndCaptureEnv(gitBash, ['-ilc', 'env'])
    return mergeWithRegistryPath(env)
  }
  return getWindowsEnvironment() // 没有 Git Bash 时回退
}
```

由于外部 CLI 启动路径和智能体/助手内置 shell 工具都使用了 `getLoginShellEnvironment()`,这一处修复就能同时修好两条路径。

### 顺带的功能请求(优先级较低)
`packages/shared/config/constant.ts` 的 `WINDOWS_TERMINALS_WITH_COMMANDS` 目前只列了 `cmd`、`powershell`、`windowsTerminal`、`wsl`、`alacritty`、`wezterm`。希望能:
- 把 **Git Bash** 作为一等公民加入可选 shell 列表。
- 把 **PowerShell 5(`powershell`)** 与 **PowerShell 7(`pwsh`)** 拆成两个独立选项——它们的模块路径与执行策略不同。
- 加入 **WSL2** 作为可选 shell(当前只是 `wsl` 启动器,不能作为 CLI 工具宿主)。
- 在设置界面提供 UI 选择器,让用户无需改配置文件即可切换。

> ⚠️ 优先级:**profile 加载这个 bug 是紧急的**——它会无声地让所有依赖 fnm/nvm/mise 的 Windows 用户:既无法启动基于 Node 的 CLI 工具,**也无法在智能体/助手中正常调用 shell**。Shell 选择器是锦上添花。

感谢你们做的 Cherry Studio!

Instead, an "AI_APICallError: Invalid JSON response" error message appeared. ### Expected Behavior It is compatible with both URL and b64_json return formats. If the server returns a URL, the client can also parse and load the image correctly. ### Relevant Log Output ```shell ``` ### Additional Context Besides Zod validation failure, an `InvalidCharacterError: Failed to execute 'atob' on 'Window'` is also triggered when attempting to bypass or forcibly returning a URL by certain APIs. This is because the `convertBase64ToUint8Array` function attempts to decode the URL string returned by the API using `atob()`. This indicates that the entire `generateImage` process completely lacks compatibility handling for URL formats. It is strongly recommended that upon receiving the return value, you first determine whether it is a URL or b64_json. If it is a URL, render it directly as the `src` attribute of an `` element, instead of forcibly going through the Base64 detection and decoding process.

## Platform

macOS

## Version

v1.9.3

## Bug Description

After switching the UI language (e.g., from Chinese to English), the built-in default assistant name and its default topic name remain in the original language instead of updating to match the new language.

- Default assistant name stays as **"默认助手"** instead of **"Default Assistant"**
- Default topic name stays as **"默认话题"** instead of **"Default Topic"**

The problem persists even after restarting the app.

**Root cause:** `getDefaultAssistant()` and `getDefaultTopic()` in `AssistantService.ts` initialize these names via `i18n.t()` at first launch, and the values are persisted to the Redux store via `redux-persist`. The `onSelectLanguage` handler in `GeneralSettings.tsx` calls `i18n.changeLanguage()` but never updates the already-persisted strings in the store.

Affected state fields:
- `state.assistants.defaultAssistant.name` (i18n key: `chat.default.name`)
- `state.assistants.defaultAssistant.topics[0].name` (i18n key: `chat.default.topic.name`)

## Steps To Reproduce

1. Launch Cherry Studio with language set to **Chinese (Simplified)**
2. Confirm the default assistant is named **"默认助手"** and default topic is **"默认话题"**
3. Go to **Settings → General → Language**
4. Switch to **English**
5. Return to the main view and observe the default assistant/topic name

The issue also reproduces in reverse: switching from English → Chinese leaves "Default Assistant" / "Default Topic" unchanged.

## Expected Behavior

After switching the UI language, the default assistant name and default topic name should update to match the new language:

- Chinese → English: "默认助手" → "Default Assistant", "默认话题" → "Default Topic"
- English → Chinese: "Default Assistant" → "默认助手", "Default Topic" → "默认话题"

## Platform

Windows (x64)

## Version

v1.9.3

## Bug Description

When running 2 Agents concurrently (code writing scenario), when both Agents are using the MCP browser screenshot function, the Cherry Studio UI becomes almost completely frozen and unresponsive.

**Key Information**: Hardware resources are extremely abundant but the application is unresponsive——

- CPU: 192 cores, very low usage rate (< 5%)
- Memory: 256GB, very low usage rate
- Disk I/O is normal

This indicates that the bottleneck is not in hardware resources, but in the software architecture layer.

**Root Cause Analysis**: Cherry Studio is an application built on Electron. Electron's renderer process main thread is single-threaded. When two Agents simultaneously call `mcp__browser__screenshot`, each screenshot (PNG, hundreds of KB to several MB) floods into the renderer process through IPC (Inter-Process Communication) channels, causing the UI main thread to be completely blocked. The extremely low CPU/memory usage also confirms that this is not a resource bottleneck, but IPC transmission blocking the UI thread.

## Steps To Reproduce

1. Create 2 Agents, both configured with MCP browser tools (browser MCP server)
2. Start both Agents simultaneously to execute code writing tasks
3. When both Agents simultaneously call the browser screenshot function (`mcp__browser__screenshot`)
4. Cherry Studio UI becomes almost completely frozen, mouse clicks and keyboard operations are unresponsive
5. Observe CPU and memory usage rates, both are at very low levels

## Expected Behavior

When multiple Agents concurrently use browser screenshots, the UI should remain responsive. Large data transfers (screenshots) should not block the UI main thread.

## Relevant Log Output

No error logs, logs output normally during the lag period, no ERROR level information.

## Additional Context

**Hardware Environment**:
- CPU: 192 cores
- Memory: 256GB
- Operating System: Windows x64

**Suggested Optimization Directions**:
1. **Asynchronous MCP Large Data Transfer** — Use Offscreen Canvas or Web Worker threads to process image decoding/rendering without blocking the UI main thread
2. **Image Lazy Loading / Streaming** — Implement progressive loading for screenshot content output by Agents, rather than transferring complete images all at once
3. **Multi-Agent Concurrent IPC Priority Queue** — When multiple Agents simultaneously generate large amounts of MCP data, add scheduling mechanisms to prevent the UI thread from being overwhelmed
4. **Screenshot Default Quality Optimization** — MCP browser screenshots use JPEG format by default instead of PNG, or limit maximum resolution to reduce IPC transmission data volume
5. **Renderer Process Isolation** — Consider using independent renderer processes for Agent output areas (similar to Chrome's Site Isolation) to prevent one Agent's large data from affecting the entire application UI

title: Bug: MCP with Claude model fails due to invalid anthropic-beta header value `structured-outputs-2025-11-13`
body:
## Describe the Bug

When using Cherry Studio v1.9.3 with a Claude model and enabling MCP (Model Context Protocol), the request fails with an error about an invalid `anthropic-beta` header value.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure a Claude model (e.g., via Vertex AI / Anthropic API)
2. Enable MCP in Cherry Studio settings
3. Send any message / trigger MCP tool call
4. Error is returned immediately

## Expected Behavior

MCP should work normally with Claude models without header errors.

## Actual Behavior

The following error is returned (repeated twice):

```json
{
  "type": "error",
  "error": {
    "type": "invalid_request_error",
    "message": "Unexpected value(s) \`structured-outputs-2025-11-13\` for the \`anthropic-beta\` header. Please consult our documentation at docs.anthropic.com or try again without the header."
  },
  "request_id": "req_vrtx_011CaTt9LEAvrJTcMDBDWasZ"
}
```

## Environment

- **Cherry Studio Version:** 1.9.3
- **Model Provider:** Claude (Vertex AI endpoint, based on request_id prefix `req_vrtx_`)
- **MCP:** Enabled

## Analysis

The app is sending `anthropic-beta: structured-outputs-2025-11-13` as a request header, but the Anthropic API (specifically the Vertex AI proxy endpoint) does not recognize this header value. This could be:

1. An outdated beta header value that has since been removed/renamed by Anthropic
2. A header value that is only valid for direct Anthropic API but not for Vertex AI proxy
3. Cherry Studio hardcoding a beta header that should be dynamically determined

## Suggested Fix

- Remove or update the `structured-outputs-2025-11-13` value from the `anthropic-beta` header
- Alternatively, only include the beta header when calling the direct Anthropic API, not when routing through Vertex AI

## Additional Context

This completely blocks MCP usage with Claude models in v1.9.3. Works fine when MCP is disabled.

title: [Bug]: Quick Assistant Window Flashes and Disappears When Main Window Is Open but Unfocused
body:
### Issue Checklist

- [x] I understand that issues are for feedback and problem solving, not for complaining in the comment section, and will provide as much information as possible to help solve the problem.
- [x] My issue is not listed in the [FAQ](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/issues/3881).
- [x] I've looked at **pinned issues** and searched for existing [Open Issues](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/issues), [Closed Issues](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20state%3Aclosed), and [Discussions](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/discussions), no similar issue or discussion was found.
- [x] I've filled in short, clear headings so that developers can quickly identify a rough idea of what to expect when flipping through the list of issues. And not "a suggestion", "stuck", etc.
- [x] I've confirmed that I am using the latest version of Cherry Studio.

### Platform

macOS

### Version

v1.9.3

### Bug Description

When Cherry Studio's main window is open but not in focus, invoking the Quick Assistant (mini window) succeeds only once. Any subsequent invocation — whether via keyboard shortcut (Option+Space) or menu bar icon — causes both the main window and the mini window to briefly flash on screen and then immediately disappear together. The problem resets (and the mini window works again for one call) only after manually switching focus back to Cherry Studio's main window.

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Launch Cherry Studio. Keep the main window open.
2. Switch focus to another application (e.g., a browser).
3. Invoke the Quick Assistant via Option+Space or the menu bar icon → works correctly (window appears, can be dismissed).
4. Without switching focus back to Cherry Studio, invoke the Quick Assistant a second time → both the main window and mini window flash briefly and then immediately disappear together.
5. Switch focus back to Cherry Studio (click Dock icon or Cmd+Tab).
6. Repeat from step 2 → the cycle reproduces reliably.

### Expected Behavior

The Quick Assistant should appear and function normally on every invocation, regardless of the main window's focus state or how many times it was previously invoked.

### Relevant Log Output

```shell
{"level":"info","message":"mini_window shortcut triggered, QuickAssistant enabled: true","module":"ShortcutService","process":"main","timestamp":"2026-04-27 08:45:03"}
{"level":"info","message":"mini_window shortcut triggered, QuickAssistant enabled: true","module":"ShortcutService","process":"main","timestamp":"2026-04-27 08:45:03"}
```

### Additional Context

Suspected Root Cause
Likely a window state management / focus-handling bug on macOS. After the mini window is dismissed the first time, the app enters a "dirty" state where subsequent show() + app.focus() calls fail to properly acquire focus on macOS 15.5. This may trigger a blur/hide handler that immediately hides the mini window (and main window) as soon as it appears. The fact that it works when the main window is minimized or closed suggests the mini window's behavior changes depending on whether the main window is in a "visible but unfocused" state.

title: [Bug]: Creating an Agent rewrites the updatedAt of all existing agents
body:
### Issue Checklist

- [x] I understand that issues are for feedback and problem solving, not for complaining in the comment section, and will provide as much information as possible to help solve the problem.
- [x] My issue is not listed in the [FAQ](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/issues/3881).
