- [x] I've filled in short, clear headings so that developers can quickly identify a rough idea of what to expect when flipping through the list of issues. And not "a suggestion", "stuck", etc.
- [x] I've confirmed that I am using the latest version of Cherry Studio.

### Platform

macOS (logic-layer bug, all platforms affected)

### Version

v2 dev branch — `feat/v2/resource-library` @ `1857b6f72` (also reproducible on `main` @ `4c264de12`)

### Bug Description

In the v2 Resource Library, creating a new Agent silently rewrites the `updatedAt` timestamp of **every existing Agent** in the database to the current time. The same problem occurs when reordering Agents via drag-and-drop.

As a result, the Agent list — when sorted or filtered by "last updated" — collapses every Agent into the same instant, making the field unusable as a recency signal and breaking any downstream cache-invalidation / incremental-sync / audit consumer that relies on `updatedAt` semantics.

The Assistant DataApi has not been observed to exhibit the same behavior, but the `AssistantService` create / reorder paths should be reviewed for the same anti-pattern.

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Have at least two existing Agents in the Resource Library; note their current "last updated" timestamps.
2. Click the **New Resource** button in the toolbar and create a new Agent (any name / model is fine), then save.
3. Return to the Agent list and refresh.
4. Observe: the "last updated" timestamp of every previously existing Agent has been rewritten to the moment the new Agent was created.
5. (Optional) Drag any Agent to a new position in the list. All agents whose `sortOrder` shifted will likewise have their `updatedAt` refreshed.

### Expected Behavior

- Creating a new Agent should only set `createdAt` / `updatedAt` on the newly inserted row. Existing rows must retain their previous `updatedAt`.
- Reordering Agents (changing only `sortOrder`) is a presentation-layer concern and should not bump the business-level `updatedAt` of the affected rows.

### Relevant Log Output

```shell
(no error log — the bug is silent and only visible by inspecting `updatedAt` values in the agent list)
```

### Additional Context

**Root cause** — two independent designs combine into the user-visible bug:

1. `AgentService.createAgent` issues an unfiltered bulk update to push every existing Agent's `sortOrder` up by one, so the newly inserted Agent (which is created with `sortOrder: 0`) ends up at the front of the list:

   `src/main/data/services/AgentService.ts:157`
   ```ts
   await tx.update(agentsTable).set({ sortOrder: sql`${agentsTable.sortOrder} + 1` })
   await tx.insert(agentsTable).values(insertData) // sortOrder: 0
   ```

   The same pattern exists in `reorderAgents` (`AgentService.ts:399`), which loops `update().set({ sortOrder: i })` over every reordered row.

2. The shared timestamp helper declares `updatedAt` with a column-level `$onUpdateFn`, so **any** `update().set(...)` that touches a row will auto-rewrite that row's `updatedAt` to `Date.now()`, regardless of which fields were actually set:

   `src/main/data/db/schemas/_columnHelpers.ts:50`
   ```ts
   updatedAt: integer().notNull().$defaultFn(createTimestamp).$onUpdateFn(createTimestamp)
   ```

The combination means: every `createAgent` call → full-table `sortOrder + 1` update → full-table `updatedAt` refresh.

**Suggested fix directions** (open for discussion):

- **A. Change the sortOrder strategy so create no longer touches other rows.** New Agent's `sortOrder` could be derived from `MIN(existing.sortOrder) - 1` (or a fractional-index midpoint), reducing `createAgent` to a single INSERT. This is the upstream fix and aligns with the project's "fix upstream, don't hack downstream" principle.
- **B. Explicitly preserve `updatedAt` in reorder updates** — e.g. `set({ sortOrder: ..., updatedAt: agentsTable.updatedAt })` to bypass `$onUpdateFn`. Smallest change, but every "passive reorder" call site has to remember to do this.
- **C. Reconsider the granularity of `$onUpdateFn`.** Move `updatedAt` maintenance to be explicit in service code (which `updateAgent` at `AgentService.ts:296` already does), and drop `$onUpdateFn` from the shared helper. Cleanest semantics, largest blast radius — needs a sweep across all v2 services first.

**Files / lines of interest**:
- `src/main/data/services/AgentService.ts:157` — `createAgent` full-table `sortOrder + 1`
- `src/main/data/services/AgentService.ts:399` — `reorderAgents` per-row `sortOrder` update
- `src/main/data/services/AgentService.ts:296` — `updateAgent` already sets `updatedAt: Date.now()` explicitly (reference)
- `src/main/data/db/schemas/_columnHelpers.ts:50` — `$onUpdateFn(createTimestamp)`
- `src/main/data/db/schemas/agent.ts:21` — agent table uses `createUpdateDeleteTimestamps`

title: Inconsistent ID generation for agents — agent_<timestamp>_<random> vs UUID in DB schema
body:
## Problem

The agent-related tables use inconsistent ID generation strategies:

### 1. `agentId` uses `agent_<timestamp>_<random>` instead of UUID

The DB table defines the ID as:
```ts
id: uuidPrimaryKey()
```

But in `createAgent(req: CreateAgentDto): Promise<AgentEntity>`:
```ts
const id = `agent_${Date.now()}_${Math.random().toString(36).substring(2, 11)}`
```

This generates a string like `agent_1734567890123_x7k2m9p4q` which does **not** conform to UUID format, conflicting with the `uuidPrimaryKey()` schema definition.

### 2. `agentSession` table explicitly bypasses UUID

```ts
'agent_session',
{
  // IDs use the app-generated "session_<timestamp>_<random>" format, not UUIDs,
  // so uuidPrimaryKey() is intentionally not used here. Callers must always supply an id.
  id: text().primaryKey(),
}
```

This works, but it's inconsistent with other tables and the codebase-wide UUID convention.

### 3. Need full audit

All agent-related tables should be reviewed for ID generation consistency. Likely tables include:
- `agent`
- `agent_session`
- Any other agent-related junction or mapping tables

## Expected Behavior

All agent-related IDs should follow a single, consistent strategy — either:
- Use `uuidPrimaryKey()` everywhere and generate UUIDs in the app layer, or
- Explicitly use `text().primaryKey()` everywhere with the `agent_<timestamp>_<random>` pattern (but this breaks consistency with the rest of the codebase)

Given the rest of the codebase uses UUIDs, the first option seems preferable.

title: [Bug]: Non-multimodal models configured as Agents cannot add image attachments in the input box
body:
> [\!NOTE]
> This issue/comment/review was translated by Claude.

## Bug Description

Non-multimodal models, after being configured to the Agent function, cannot add image-type attachments in the input box toolbar. This restriction is unreasonable for the following reasons:

1. **Agents might simply pass image files as attachments to tools for processing**, not necessarily requiring the model itself to understand image content. For example, Agents might process images through MCP tools, code execution, or other methods.
2. **Agents might use other tools to understand images**, such as calling OCR APIs, vision model APIs, etc. Restricting users from uploading images would block these workflows.
3. The use of image attachments should not be determined solely by the model's capabilities, but should be determined by the user and the Agent's toolchain.

## Steps To Reproduce

1. Select a non-multimodal model (e.g., a text-only model)
2. Configure that model to the Agent function
3. Open the Agent conversation interface
4. Attempt to add image attachments in the input box toolbar
5. Find that the image upload button is unavailable or hidden

## Expected Behavior

Regardless of whether the model supports multimodal, the input box in Agent mode should allow users to add image attachments. The model's multimodal capability should not be the condition for restricting attachment uploads, as Agents can process images through other means (tool calls, file transfers, etc.).

## Additional Context

- Platform: macOS

- ShipIt logs (`~/Library/Caches/com.kangfenmao.CherryStudio.ShipIt/ShipIt_stderr.log`) last recorded on 2026-03-17, showing the update was successful at that time, **this signature validation failure is not logged**.

- The current installation package's code signature validation passes (`codesign -dv` shows the signature is valid, Authority is Developer ID Application: Nanjing Stonecutter Network Technology Co., Ltd.).

- ShipIt update mechanism uses the Squirrel framework.

title: Suggest optimization for DeepSeek cache hit mechanism
body:
Suggest optimization for DeepSeek cache hit mechanism

> [\!NOTE]
> This issue was translated by Claude.

### Issue Checklist

- [x] I understand that issues are for reporting problems and requesting features, not for off-topic comments, and I will provide as much detail as possible to help resolve the issue.
- [x] I have checked the pinned issues and searched through the existing [open issues](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/issues), [closed issues](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20state%3Aclosed), and [discussions](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/discussions) and did not find a similar suggestion.
- [x] I have provided a short and descriptive title so that developers can quickly understand the issue when browsing the issue list, rather than vague titles like "A suggestion" or "Stuck."
- [x] The latest version of Cherry Studio does not include the feature I am suggesting.

### Platform

Windows

### Version

1.93

### Is your feature request related to an existing issue?

Regarding DeepSeek, I recently tested and found that it cannot effectively hit the cache, resulting in high costs. I suspect it is caused by the knowledge base or web search functionality. After consulting AI, it was pointed out that this is a software transmission mechanism issue. Can you provide a solution?

**Core Issue: Cherry Studio uses a "full context resend" mechanism**

The vast majority of open-source AI clients (including Cherry Studio, Lobe Chat, Chatbox, etc.) adopt this simplest context handling method:
- In each round of conversation, the complete chat history from the beginning of the session to the present is concatenated into a brand new Prompt
- Then this new Prompt is sent to the DeepSeek API all at once
- Since each round's Prompt adds "the previous round's AI response + your new question", the Prompts of two requests can never be 100% identical
- Therefore, the DeepSeek server-side cache can almost never be hit

**Combined with your data verification**

The time interval between your two screenshots is very short, with only one round of conversation:
- New cache misses: 42,681 tokens
- New cache hits: only 1,280 tokens
- New output: 2,995 tokens

These 42,681 missed tokens, more than 95% are your entire previous chat history being resent. Only those 1,280 tokens may be system prompts or fixed templates that hit the cache.

**Why the vectorized database is not responsible**

The vectorized database is only responsible for retrieving external documents and is completely unrelated to the sending method of chat history:
- Even if you store chat records in a vectorized database, Cherry Studio will still send the complete history to the API
- After enabling RAG, the external fragments retrieved each time may have slight differences, which will make the Prompt more difficult to be completely identical, further reducing the cache hit rate
- After disabling the RAG function, your cache hit rate will not be improved in any way

**Why DeepSeek official client has high cache hit rate**

DeepSeek official web and APP adopt advanced mechanisms of incremental context + server-side session caching:
- It does not resend the complete history every round, but only sends the previous round's response and new questions
- The server-side will save your session state, and the client does not need to repeatedly send history
- Therefore, the new cache miss tokens in each round are only the dozens of words you newly input, and the cache hit rate is extremely high

### Desired Solution

**1. Immediate temporary solutions**
- Regularly create new sessions: Don't chat for dozens of rounds in one session. Create a new session every 5-10 rounds to avoid history getting longer and longer
- Enable automatic context truncation: In Cherry Studio's model settings, find "Maximum context length" and set it to a reasonable value (such as 4096 or 8192) to automatically truncate the earliest history
- Disable unnecessary RAG: When you don't need to retrieve external documents, close all knowledge bases to avoid additional token consumption

**2. Medium to long-term optimization suggestions**
- Provide feedback to Cherry Studio developers and request support for "incremental context sending" or "local context caching" features. This is the fundamental way to solve the problem
- For content that requires repeated queries, copy and paste it into a new session for separate questioning to avoid carrying irrelevant history
- For long document analysis, use a "one-time question" method instead of asking multiple rounds of follow-up questions to reduce history accumulation

**Supplementary explanation**

At present, the vast majority of open-source AI clients have not implemented the incremental context function. This is a widespread problem. As the context window of large models becomes larger and larger, this problem will become more and more prominent, because the historical tokens resent in each round will become more and more.

You can submit a feature request in Cherry Studio's GitHub repository. Many developers have realized this problem, and optimization may be added in the future.

### Alternative Solutions

针对deepseek 我最近测试发现无法有效命中缓存，导致费用颇高，怀疑是知识库或者联网搜索导致的，在询问ai后，指出是软件的传送机制问题，请问能否给出解决方案。
核心问题：Cherry Studio 采用 "全量上下文重发" 机制
绝大多数开源 AI 客户端（包括 Cherry Studio、Lobe Chat、Chatbox 等）都采用这种最简单的上下文处理方式：
每一轮对话，都会把从会话开始到当前的所有历史消息，完整拼接成一个全新的 Prompt
然后把这个全新的 Prompt 一次性发给 DeepSeek API
由于每一轮的 Prompt 都比上一轮多了 "上一轮的 AI 回复 + 你新的提问"，两次请求的 Prompt 永远不可能 100% 相同
因此 DeepSeek 服务器端的缓存几乎永远无法命中
结合你的数据验证
你两张截图的时间间隔很短，只进行了一轮对话：
新增未命中缓存：42,681 tokens
新增命中缓存：仅 1,280 tokens
新增输出：2,995 tokens
这 42,681 个未命中 token，95% 以上都是你之前所有的聊天历史被重新发送了一遍。只有那 1,280 个 token 可能是系统提示词或固定模板命中了缓存。
为什么向量化数据库不背这个锅
向量化数据库只负责检索外部文档，和聊天历史的发送方式完全无关：
即使你把聊天记录存入向量化数据库，Cherry Studio 依然会把完整历史发给 API
开启 RAG 后，每次检索到的外部片段可能有细微差异，反而会让 Prompt 更难完全相同，进一步降低缓存命中率
关闭 RAG 功能，你的缓存命中率也不会有任何提升
三、为什么 DeepSeek 官方客户端缓存命中率高
DeepSeek 官方网页端和 APP 采用了增量上下文 + 服务器端会话缓存的高级机制：
它不会每轮都重发完整历史，而是只发送上一轮的回复和新的提问
服务器端会保存你的会话状态，不需要客户端重复发送历史
因此每轮新增的未命中 token 只有你新输入的几十个字，缓存命中率极高

### Desired Solution

1. 立即见效的临时方法
定期新建会话：不要在一个会话里聊几十轮，每聊 5-10 轮就新建一个会话，避免历史越来越长
开启上下文自动截断：在 Cherry Studio 的模型设置里，找到 "最大上下文长度"，设置为一个合理值（比如 4096 或 8192），让它自动截断最早的历史
关闭不必要的 RAG：不需要检索外部文档时，关闭所有知识库，避免额外的 token 消耗
2. 中长期优化建议
向 Cherry Studio 开发者反馈，请求支持 "增量上下文发送" 或 "本地上下文缓存" 功能，这是从根本上解决问题的方法
对于需要重复查询的内容，复制粘贴到新会话中单独提问，避免携带无关历史
对于长文档分析，使用 "一次性提问" 的方式，不要分多轮追问，减少历史累积
五、补充说明
目前绝大多数开源 AI 客户端都没有实现增量上下文功能，这是一个普遍存在的问题。随着大模型上下文窗口越来越大，这个问题会越来越突出，因为每轮重发的历史 token 会越来越多。
你可以在 Cherry Studio 的 GitHub 仓库里提交一个功能请求，很多开发者已经意识到了这个问题，未来可能会加入优化。

### Platform

Windows

### Version

v1.9.3

### Bug Description

When using **deepseek-v4-pro** model in the **default assistant on the home page**, the assistant stays in an infinite loading state and eventually causes the renderer process to crash.

The root cause appears to be that deepseek-v4-pro outputs `thinking` type content blocks (chain-of-thought reasoning tokens) which the standard chat UI does not handle. This leads to:

1. Warning logs: `Unhandled assistant content block type: thinking`
2. Warning logs: `Received content_block_stop for unknown index`
3. Eventually: `Renderer process crashed with: {"reason":"crashed","exitCode":-1073741819}`

**Note**: The same model works correctly in Agent mode (Claude Code SDK agent), suggesting the issue is specific to the standard chat UI's handling of `thinking` content blocks.

Additionally, the default assistant preset appears to be corrupted:
- `Assistant preset with id default not found in state` — repeated multiple times after restart

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Install Cherry Studio v1.9.3 on Windows
2. Configure a valid DeepSeek API key in Settings -> Provider -> DeepSeek
3. Fetch model list and select `deepseek-v4-pro` in the default assistant
4. Send any message to the default assistant
5. The assistant shows infinite loading with no response
6. After 5-10 minutes, the renderer process crashes completely
7. After restart, the issue persists — default assistant still cannot be used

### Expected Behavior

1. The standard chat UI should correctly handle `thinking` type content blocks from reasoning models (either display them appropriately or safely ignore them)
2. The renderer process should not crash when receiving unsupported content block types
3. The default assistant preset should persist after restart

### Relevant Log Output

```
{"level":"warn","message":"Unhandled assistant content block","timestamp":"...","type":"thinking"}
{"index":1,"level":"warn","message":"Received content_block_stop for unknown index","timestamp":"..."}
{"level":"error","message":"Renderer process crashed with: {\"reason\":\"crashed\",\"exitCode\":-1073741819}","module":"WindowService","process":"main","timestamp":"..."}
{"level":"warn","message":"Assistant preset with id default not found in state.","module":"useAssistantPresets","process":"renderer","timestamp":"..."}
```

### Additional Context

- The issue does NOT occur with non-reasoning models (e.g., deepseek-chat)
- The Agent (Cherry Assistant) works fine with deepseek-v4-pro since the Claude Code SDK handles thinking blocks correctly
- The error log file is at `%APPDATA%/CherryStudio/logs/app-error.YYYY-MM-DD.log`
- Exit code `-1073741819` = `STATUS_ACCESS_VIOLATION` (Windows memory access violation)
- Cherry Studio version: 1.9.3 (Windows, packaged install)

Windows

### Is your feature request related to an existing issue?

Cherry Studio's current context truncation strategy has an issue:

When context count is set to 20:

After 20 messages (10 user + 10 AI turns), each conversation round sends identical messages
Once the 21st round (22 messages) is sent, takeRight(messages, 20) truncates the earliest message
The 21st round request is identical to the 20th round request → server cache cannot be hit
Every round loses cache, continuously incurring full token costs
Issues caused:

Extremely low cache hit rate (near 0%)
High API costs
Slow response times


### Desired Solution

Suggest implementing a dual-threshold strategy:

Truncate Threshold: Start truncating after 30 messages
Keep Count: Keep 20 newest messages when truncating
Cache Window: 30 messages (15 conversation rounds)
Effect Comparison:

| Current Strategy | Proposed Strategy |
| ---------------- | ------------------ |
| Rounds 0-20: Cache hits | Rounds 0-20: Cache hits |
| Round 21: Truncated, cache lost | Rounds 21-30: Cache still works |
| Round 31: Truncated, cache lost | Round 31: Truncated to 20, but 21-30 rounds still hit cache |

title: [Bug]: DeepSeek V4-pro web search outputs raw DSML tool_calls tokens instead of invoking the tool
body:
> [\!NOTE] > This issue was translated by Claude. ### Platform macOS ### Version v1.9.4 (draft) ### Bug Description When using `agent/deepseek-v4-pro` (CherryIN provider) with built-in web search enabled, the model emits the raw DSML tool-call protocol syntax as plain message text instead of having the client parse it as a tool invocation. The web search itself does fire (the citations card with "5 search results / 5 cited sources" appears earlier in the message), but the final assistant turn ends up showing protocol tokens to the user with no actual answer content. Concretely the message body contains, verbatim: ``` < | DSML | tool_calls> < | DSML | invoke name="builtin_web_search"> < | DSML | parameter name="additionalContext" string="true">DeepSeek V4 发布 特性 性能 评测 2025 ``` This looks like a tool-use parser miss for DeepSeek V4-pro: the DSML wrapper tokens that should be intercepted and turned into a tool-call UI block are leaking into the rendered text. Same provider + similar request on `deepseek-v3.2` does not exhibit this — the issue appears tied to V4-pro's tool-use formatting. ### Steps to Reproduce 1. Provider: CherryIN 2. Model: `agent/deepseek-v4-pro` 3. Enable built-in web search (globe toggle in the composer) 4. Send: 搜一下 DeepSeek V4 的资料 (or any query that triggers a follow-up web search) 5. Observe the assistant turn ### Expected Behavior After the web search runs, the assistant should produce a normal natural-language summary citing the 5 sources. The DSML protocol tokens (`< | DSML | tool_calls>`, `< | DSML | invoke …>`, etc.) should never be visible in the rendered message. ### Actual Behavior - ✅ Thinking blocks render (1.5s, 1.3s) - ✅ "5 个搜索结果" / "5 个引用内容" cards appear - ❌ Final answer is replaced by raw DSML tool_calls XML — user sees protocol syntax, not an answer - ❌ The conversation turn is effectively wasted; the user has to retry ### Severity P0 — main path is blocked. The user asks a question, web search succeeds, but no answer text is produced. The visible output is internal protocol noise. Single-turn conversations using V4-pro + web search are unusable. ### Possibly Related - #14671 (DeepSeek search-result annotations not displayed) — different (annotations vs tool-call token leak), but both touch DeepSeek + web search rendering. ### Environment - App: Cherry Studio 社区版 v1.9.4 (draft) - OS: macOS - Provider: CherryIN (gateway-class) - Model: `agent/deepseek-v4-pro` ---

title: [Bug]: Agent model picker hides CherryIN provider's GPT models while AiHubMix GPT models show
body:
> [\!NOTE] > This issue/comment/review was translated by Claude. ### Platform macOS ### Version v1.9.4 (draft) ### Bug Description In the **Agent** model picker, searching `gpt` only returns AiHubMix's GPT lineup. **CherryIN's `openai/gpt-*` models are not shown at all**, even though CherryIN is enabled and those exact models are visible / enabled in the global Provider settings. In the regular Chat path the same CherryIN models work fine; the regression is scoped to the Agent picker. #### Agent picker (search "gpt") — CherryIN GPT models missing Only AiHubMix entries appear: `GPT 5.5`, `gpt-4.1`, `gpt-4o`, `gpt-5`, `gpt-5-chat-latest`, `gpt-5-mini`, `gpt-5-nano`. No CherryIN entry under any of the GPT names. #### Provider settings — CherryIN's GPT models are configured and enabled CherryIN provider is **ON**; under the `openai` group: `openai/gpt-5.1-chat`, `openai/gpt-5.1-codex`, `openai/gpt-5.2`, `openai/gpt-5.2-chat`, `openai/gpt-5.2-codex`, `openai/gpt-5.3-chat`, `openai/gpt-5.4`, `openai/gpt-5.4-mini`, `openai/gpt-5.4-nano` — all enabled. ### Likely Cause (speculation for the maintainers) #13507 extended Agent model support to OpenAI-compatible providers, but the picker's filter / capability check seems to special-case based on either provider type, model-id prefix (`openai/*` vs bare `gpt-*`), or capability tags. CherryIN-served GPT models carry an `openai/` provider-prefix and may not be recognized as tool-capable / Agent-eligible by whatever predicate gates the Agent picker, while AiHubMix's models are passing the predicate. ### Steps to Reproduce 1. Provider settings: confirm CherryIN is **ON** and at least one `openai/gpt-*` model is enabled (Cherry Studio defaults already include these). 2. Open an Agent (e.g. the default `Agent` / `DeepSeek V4 深度解析` shown in the screenshot). 3. Click the model selector and type `gpt`. 4. Observe the result list. ### Expected Behavior CherryIN's `openai/gpt-5.x` family should appear alongside AiHubMix's GPT family in the Agent picker (matching the Chat picker's behavior). ### Actual Behavior CherryIN GPT models silently absent. No error, no tooltip, nothing in the empty state to suggest filtering — they just don't render. ### Severity **P1** — feature regression scoped to Agent. Workaround exists (use AiHubMix), but CherryIN is a first-class provider and parity with Chat is expected. Selecting CherryIN GPT is not possible in Agent at all. ### Possibly Related - #13507 (closed feature: extend Agent model support to OpenAI-compatible providers) — same surface, the gating predicate appears to undercount `openai/*`-prefixed CherryIN models. ### Environment - App: Cherry Studio 社区版 v1.9.4 (draft) - OS: macOS - Providers: CherryIN (ON), AiHubMix (ON) - Surface: Agent model picker (not the Chat picker) ---
Original Content ### 现象 在 Agent 的模型选择器里搜 `gpt` 时，只列出 AiHubMix 的 GPT 系列；CherryIN 的 `openai/gpt-*` 模型一个都没出现，但在全局"模型服务"设置里 CherryIN 是开启的，`openai/gpt-5.1-chat`、`openai/gpt-5.2`、`openai/gpt-5.4` 等都已配置并启用。同样的 CherryIN 模型在普通 Chat 场景下完全可用。 ### 推测根因 #13507 已扩展 Agent 支持 OpenAI-compatible provider，但 Agent picker 的过滤/能力判定可能按 provider type、model-id 前缀（`openai/*` vs 裸 `gpt-*`）或能力 tag 做了特判。CherryIN 走的是 `openai/` 前缀，没被 Agent 选择器识别为可用，AiHubMix 通过了。 ### 复现步骤 1. 模型服务设置确认 CherryIN 已开启，且 `openai/gpt-*` 启用（默认即如此） 2. 打开任意 Agent 3. 点模型选择器，搜 `gpt` 4. 看结果列表 ### 期望 CherryIN 的 `openai/gpt-5.x` 应该和 AiHubMix 的 GPT 同时出现，与 Chat 行为一致。 ### 实际 CherryIN GPT 全部不展示，无报错无提示。 ### 优先级 P1：Agent 内 CherryIN GPT 整条路径不可达；有 workaround（AiHubMix），但 CherryIN 是默认 provider，与 Chat 行为不一致是明显回归。 ### 相关 - #13507（closed，扩展 Agent 对 OpenAI-compatible provider 支持的 feature）

title: [Feature]: Auto-Memory in Agent Mode (User-Level)
body:
## Background

Cherry Studio's Agent mode currently keeps any learned context scoped to each individual agent's workspace, so anything the agent figures out (the user's setup, recurring fixes, environment quirks) is invisible to other agents and lost when the user starts a new agent. Anthropic's Claude Code recently shipped Auto Memory: the agent autonomously writes durable notes during work and recalls them in future sessions, with each session surfacing "recalled N memories, wrote M memories" inline and the user able to expand to see what was written. Cherry users running multiple agents do not get this — every new agent starts cold.

## Goal

Cherry Studio's agents autonomously remember durable user-level facts and recall them in any later session — across all of the user's agents — so the user does not have to re-explain the same setup, preferences, or recurring fixes.

## Spec

- Agents autonomously decide when to write to user-level memory during a session, without the user needing to issue a "remember this" command.
- At the start of every session, the agent automatically reads relevant entries from user-level memory and applies them as context.
- Each session surfaces a transparent inline status showing how many memory entries were recalled and how many were written, with an action to expand and view the actual entries.
- User-level memory is shared across all of the user's agents — what one agent writes is visible to all others. Each agent's per-agent (workspace) memory continues to exist for context that should not leak across agents.
- Users can directly view and edit the underlying memory file at any time; deletions take effect on the next session.
- The agent decides what is durable enough to write to user-level memory (long-lived user facts, environment quirks, recurring fixes) versus what stays in per-agent memory (project-specific details).

## Verification

- Inline status visibility: open a fresh Agent session → status line near the assistant turn shows `recalled 0 memories`. After interaction in which the agent autonomously commits a fact, status updates to show `wrote N memories` with an affordance to expand and inspect the entries.
- Autonomous write: in agent A, user mentions a durable fact about themselves (e.g. "I work in TypeScript on Next.js projects, prefer pnpm over npm"). Without the user issuing a "remember this" command, the agent commits relevant facts to user-level memory; the inline status reflects `wrote N memories`.
- Cross-agent recall: open a fresh agent B (different agent, never used) and ask "what should I keep in mind when working with me?" → status shows `recalled N memories`; agent's response references the TypeScript / Next.js / pnpm facts established in agent A.
- Edit-via-file: user opens the underlying user-level memory file, manually removes the "pnpm preference" entry → start a new session in any agent → agent does not recall that preference; if a relevant scenario arises, agent does not assume pnpm.
- Per-agent isolation: while working in agent A on a specific project, the agent learns a project-specific detail (e.g. "this codebase uses Tailwind v4"). Open agent B on a different project and ask about CSS conventions → agent B does not assume Tailwind v4 — that detail stayed in agent A's per-agent memory, not user-level.
- Persistence across restart: after autonomous writes have occurred, fully quit Cherry Studio and relaunch → reopen any agent → status still recalls the previously-written entries.

## Related

#6388 (legacy Global Memory, removed in v2 via #14251)
#14393 (assistant-level memory)
#14214 (pluggable memory provider)

title: [Feature Request] Screen Reader Accessibility Support
body:
> [\!NOTE]
> This issue was translated by Claude.

## Feature Description

Cherry Studio currently lacks complete support for screen readers (such as NVDA, JAWS, VoiceOver), preventing visually impaired users from using the application properly. It is recommended to systematically adapt for accessibility (Accessibility / a11y).

## Current Issues

1. **Missing ARIA Labels**: Many interactive elements (buttons, input fields, dropdown menus) do not have `aria-label` or `aria-describedby`, making it impossible for screen readers to identify their purpose.
2. **Lack of Focus Management**: When modal dialogs open/close, focus is not properly transferred, causing keyboard users to become lost in the page.
3. **Dynamic Content Not Announced**: AI responses are streamed without using `aria-live` regions to notify screen readers.
4. **Icon Buttons Lack Accessible Names**: Many icon-only buttons (such as send, clear, copy, etc.) lack accessible text.
5. **Insufficient Semantic Structure in Conversation Lists**: Chat message lists do not use appropriate ARIA roles (such as `role="log"` or `role="feed"`).

## Proposed Improvements

- [ ] Add semantic ARIA attributes (`aria-label`, `aria-expanded`, `aria-haspopup`, etc.) to all interactive elements
- [ ] Implement proper focus management, especially for popups like modals and sidebars (focus trap)
- [ ] Add `aria-live="polite"` to AI response areas for dynamic content announcements
- [ ] Add `aria-label` or visually hidden text (`sr-only` class) to icon-only buttons
- [ ] Use `role="log"` semantic markup for chat message areas
- [ ] Integrate axe-core or Lighthouse for automated accessibility testing to prevent regressions

## Who Benefits

- Visually impaired users (relying on NVDA, JAWS, VoiceOver, and other screen readers)
- Users with motor impairments (relying on keyboard navigation instead of mouse)
- Helps comply with WCAG 2.1 AA accessibility standards

## References

- [WCAG 2.1 Guidelines](https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG21/)
- [WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices Guide](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/)
- [Electron Accessibility Docs](https://www.electronjs.org/docs/latest/tutorial/accessibility)
- [axe-core](https://github.com/dequelabs/axe-core)

## 问题现状 / Current Issues

1. **缺少 ARIA 标签**：大量交互元素（按钮、输入框、下拉菜单）未设置 `aria-label` 或 `aria-describedby`，屏幕阅读器无法识别其用途。
2. **焦点管理缺失**：模态框打开/关闭时焦点未正确转移，键盘用户可能迷失在页面中。
3. **动态内容未通知**：AI 回复流式输出时未使用 `aria-live` 区域通知屏幕阅读器。
4. **图标按钮无可访问名称**：大量仅含图标的按钮（如发送、清空、复制等）缺少可访问文本。
5. **对话列表语义化不足**：聊天消息列表未使用恰当的 ARIA 角色（如 `role="log"` 或 `role="feed"`）。

## 期望改进 / Proposed Improvements

title: [Bug]: Custom Agent bound to Feishu channel not loading Agent prompt, response uses default assistant role
body:
### [\!NOTE]
> This issue was translated by Claude.

### Platform
macOS

### Version
v1.9.3

### Bug Description
After adding a Feishu bot through the Cherry Studio "Channel" feature and binding a custom Agent, when conversing on the Feishu end, although messages are correctly routed to the bound Agent (the Agent's topic list shows message records from Feishu), the model's reply uses the default assistant's (Cherry Claw) role settings instead of loading the custom Agent's prompt.

When conversing directly with this Agent within the Cherry Studio app, replies are completely normal and correctly follow the prompt settings. This indicates that the Agent's prompt configuration is correct, and the issue only appears in the Feishu channel integration scenario.

### Steps To Reproduce
1. Create a custom Agent (e.g., "Obsidian Manager"), write the system prompt
2. Go to Cherry Studio "Channel" feature, add Feishu bot
3. In the channel settings, select and bind the above custom Agent, and save
4. Send a message to the bot in Feishu (e.g., "Hello")
5. Observe the reply content: the bot introduces itself as Cherry Claw (default assistant), not the Obsidian Manager
6. Return to Cherry Studio, open the "Obsidian Manager" Agent's topic list, and you can see the message records from Feishu, but they are not in Cherry Claw's topic list

### Expected Behavior
The Agent bound to the Feishu channel should correctly load that Agent's system prompt during conversation, and replies should conform to the Agent's custom role settings.

### Actual Behavior
Message routing is correct (messages appear in the bound Agent's topic), but the reply uses the default assistant's role settings.

### Additional Context
- Direct conversation with the Agent within the app works normally, only the Feishu channel is abnormal
- Channel settings confirmed to be saved successfully

body: ### Issue Checklist - [x] I understand that issues are for reporting problems and requesting features, not for off-topic comments, and I will provide as much detail as possible to help resolve the issue. - [x] I have checked the pinned issues and searched through the existing [open issues](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/issues), [closed issues](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20state%3Aclosed), and [discussions](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/discussions) and did not find a similar suggestion. - [x] I have provided a short and descriptive title so that developers can quickly understand the issue when browsing the issue list, rather than vague titles like "A suggestion" or "Stuck." - [x] The latest version of Cherry Studio does not include the feature I am suggesting. ### Platform Windows ### Version 0.4.6 ### Is your feature request related to an existing issue? ### Desired Solution Hi RAG Assistant team, First of all, thank you for creating such a useful tool. RAG Assistant for Zotero has become one of my favorite ways to add semantic search to my Zotero library. I would like to kindly request two important features that would make the tool much more practical for users with large collections (especially 10,000+ PDFs): 1. Support for Online Embedding API Providers (during indexing) Please add the ability to use cloud embedding APIs (e.g. OpenAI text-embedding-3-small/large, Alibaba Cloud DashScope text-embedding-v3/v4, ByteDance Doubao-embedding, etc.) for the PDF chunking + embedding phase. Currently the app only uses local SentenceTransformers models. For libraries with thousands or tens of thousands of PDFs, the initial full indexing is extremely slow (days or even weeks). Online APIs are dramatically faster, have excellent batch support, and are very affordable for this one-time bulk task (often just a few dollars for 15k PDFs). 2. Support resuming a Full Index after interruption When indexing a large Zotero database, the process can easily take many hours or days. It is very important to be able to pause/stop the indexing and resume later (or automatically resume after a crash, computer sleep, power outage, etc.) without having to start the entire process from scratch. Incremental/resumable indexing is critical for real-world large-library use cases. These two features would make RAG Assistant the go-to solution for serious researchers and heavy Zotero users with big PDF collections. Thank you very much for considering these suggestions. However, during debugging, I noticed that this endpoint returns a response even without an API key. Despite receiving a valid response, Cherry Studio is still unable to display the data. I suggest upgrading the integration to use the following endpoint instead: https://ai-gateway.vercel.sh/v1/models (requires an API key). Advantages of using /v1/models: Provides additional metadata such as: Model release date Context window Maximum tokens This extra information would be especially useful for UI improvements. ### Platform

macOS

### Version

v1.9.4

### Is your feature request related to an existing issue?

目前在模型服务中，`API Key` 和 `API Base URL` 是分开配置的。
但在实际使用中，如果接入多个中转站或多个 OpenAI 兼容服务，通常每个服务都有自己
对应的 `API Base URL` 和 `API Key`，这两个配置实际上是一一绑定的。

现在如果想在不同中转站之间切换，通常只能：

1. 手动分别修改 `API Base URL` 和 `API Key`
2. 或者创建多个重复的 provider 配置

这两种方式都不够方便，也比较容易出错。

### Desired Solution

希望在模型服务中支持将 `API Key + API Base URL` 绑定为一个可切换的配置组 / Profile。

例如：

- Profile A: `Base URL A + API Key A`
- Profile B: `Base URL B + API Key B`

这样当用户需要切换到另一个中转站时，只需要切换 Profile，而不需要每次手动修改地址和密钥。

一个可能的实现方式：

  - 在同一个模型服务 / provider 下支持多个配置组
  - 每个配置组包含：
    - 配置组名称
    - API Base URL
    - API Key
  - 支持在 UI 中快速切换当前启用的配置组

  如果后续支持的话，也可以考虑把这个能力扩展到更多 OpenAI 兼容服务场景中。

### Alternative Solutions

当前的替代方案主要有两个，但都不理想：

  1. 为每个中转站单独创建一个 provider
  会产生较多重复配置，管理起来比较乱。

  2. 每次手动修改 API Base URL 和 API Key
  切换成本高，而且容易填错。

### Additional Information

这个需求主要出现在以下场景：

  - 同时使用多个 OpenAI 兼容中转站
  - 不同中转站有不同的 API 域名和 API Key
  - 需要频繁切换不同服务进行测试或日常使用

如果能支持这种“成组绑定并快速切换”的方式，模型服务的配置体验会方便很多。

title: [Bug]: MemoryService TypeError at startup when no embedding model configured
body:
### Issue Checklist

- [x] I understand that issues are for feedback and problem solving, not for complaining in the comment section, and will provide as much information as possible to help solve the problem.
- [x] My issue is not listed in the [FAQ](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/issues/3881).
- [x] I've looked at pinned issues and searched for existing Open/Closed Issues and Discussions, no similar issue or discussion was found.
- [x] I've filled in short, clear headings so that developers can quickly identify a rough idea of what to expect when flipping through the list of issues.
- [x] I've confirmed that I am using the latest version of Cherry Studio.

### Platform

macOS

### Version

v1.9.3

### Bug Description

On every app startup (and on any `MemoryService.updateConfig()` call), the renderer logs a `TypeError`:

```
[MemoryService] Failed to update memory config: Cannot use 'in' operator to search for 'provider' in undefined
```

with a stack trace through `AiProvider.isModel` → `new AiProvider` → `getKnowledgeBaseParams` → `MemoryService.updateConfig`. The warning fires 3 times at startup (once per relevant store subscription tick) and does not affect functionality in practice, but it pollutes the error log and swallows a real bug.

**Root cause** (both `main` and `v1.9.3`):

- `MemoryService.updateConfig()` (`src/renderer/src/services/MemoryService.ts:210-223`) reads `memoryConfig.embeddingModel` which is `undefined` when the user has never configured a memory embedding model.
- It then calls `getKnowledgeBaseParams({ model: getModel(embeddingModel?.id, embeddingModel?.provider), ... })` → `base.model` becomes `undefined`.
- `getKnowledgeBaseParams()` (`src/renderer/src/services/KnowledgeService.ts:38`) calls `new AiProvider(base.model)` unconditionally.
- `AiProvider` constructor calls `this.isModel(modelOrProvider)` (`src/renderer/src/aiCore/AiProvider.ts:79,98`):
  ```ts
  private isModel(obj: Model | Provider): obj is Model {
    return 'provider' in obj && typeof obj.provider === 'string'
  }
  ```
  When `obj` is `undefined`, `'provider' in undefined` throws `TypeError`.

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Fresh install of Cherry Studio (no memory embedding model ever configured), or use any existing profile where Settings → Memory has no embedding model selected.
2. Launch the app.
3. Open DevTools → Console, or inspect `app-error.log` under `~/Library/Application Support/CherryStudio/logs/`.
4. Observe three `[MemoryService] Failed to update memory config: Cannot use 'in' operator to search for 'provider' in undefined` warnings at startup.

### Expected Behavior

- No `TypeError` when the user hasn't configured a memory embedding model.
- Either `MemoryService.updateConfig()` should early-return when `embeddingModel` is not set, or `AiProvider.isModel` should handle `null`/`undefined` defensively, or `getKnowledgeBaseParams` should short-circuit when `base.model` is missing.

### Relevant Log Output

```shell
{"level":"warn","message":"Failed to update memory config: Cannot use 'in' operator to search for 'provider' in undefined","stack":"Error: Cannot use 'in' operator to search for 'provider' in undefined","timestamp":"2026-05-01 20:46:16"}
```

Browser console stack (abbreviated):
```
at AiProvider.isModel (store-...js:352220:21)
at new AiProvider   (store-...js:352209:12)
at getKnowledgeBaseParams (store-...js:348690:21)
at MemoryService.updateConfig (store-...js:156780:51)
at MemoryService.init (store-...js:156697:14)
at new MemoryService (store-...js:156694:8)
at MemoryService.getInstance (store-...js:156701:29)
```

### Additional Context

Suggested minimal fixes (not mutually exclusive):

1. `MemoryService.updateConfig()` — early-return when `memoryConfig.embeddingModel` is falsy.
2. `AiProvider.isModel()` — guard against nullish input: `return !!obj && 'provider' in obj && typeof obj.provider === 'string'`.

Either fix silences the log spam. (1) is also semantically correct (no point building knowledge-base params with no embedding model). (2) is defence in depth.

### Platform

macOS

### Version

v1.9.3

### Bug Description

On every startup, the renderer DevTools console shows a red `[LoggerService]` error as the very first log line:

```
[LoggerService] window source not initialized, please initialize window source first
```

This is emitted by `LoggerService.processLog()` (`src/renderer/src/services/LoggerService.ts:118-121`) when some code path calls `logger.<level>(...)` before `loggerService.initWindowSource('mainWindow')` runs in `src/renderer/src/init.ts:10`. Net effect is that the first log of every session has its window source recorded as `UNKNOWN` instead of `mainWindow`, and produces a console-level error.

**Root cause**: module-load ordering. Some module imported early in the renderer entrypoint graph is executing top-level code that logs before `init.ts` has a chance to set the window source.

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Launch Cherry Studio on any platform.
2. Open DevTools → Console.
3. The first message shown is a red `[LoggerService] window source not initialized, please initialize window source first` error.

### Expected Behavior

No `window source not initialized` error on normal startup. Either:

- Call `loggerService.initWindowSource('mainWindow')` synchronously at the top of the entrypoint file, before any other imports that might log during module evaluation; or
- Buffer early log calls internally and replay them once `initWindowSource` is called; or
- Downgrade the missing-window case from `console.error` to `console.warn` (lowest-effort, but masks future regressions).

### Relevant Log Output

```shell
# DevTools Console (first line on startup)
[LoggerService] window source not initialized, please initialize window source first
```

### Platform & Version

- **Platform**: Windows
- **Version**: v1.9.4

### Bug Description

When using the **DeepSeek Official API** (api.deepseek.com) provider with the `deepseek-v4` model, typing `/context` shows the context length as **200K**. However, DeepSeek officially announced that V4 supports up to **1M** context length (1,000,000 tokens).

This discrepancy means users may not be aware that they can leverage the full 1M context window that DeepSeek V4 actually supports.

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Open Cherry Studio v1.9.4 on Windows 11
2. Add DeepSeek Official API provider (api.deepseek.com)
3. Select the `deepseek-v4` model and start a conversation
4. Type `/context` in the chat input
5. The displayed context length is **200K** instead of the expected **1M**

### Expected Behavior

The `deepseek-v4` model should show **1M (1,000,000 tokens)** as its context length when queried via `/context`, matching DeepSeek's official specification.

### Additional Context

Looking at the Cherry Studio model definitions, `deepseek-chat` and `deepseek-reasoner` are pre-configured with 64K context length. The `deepseek-v4` model may be inheriting a default value of 200K from the backend model list (api.cherry-ai.com) rather than its actual 1M cap. The model metadata for `deepseek-v4` needs to be updated to reflect the correct context length.

body:

- [x] I've confirmed that I am using the latest version of Cherry Studio.

### Platform

Windows

### Version

1.9.4

### Bug Description

v1.9.4（最新版），Windows 11

Agent 模式下使用 Skill 系统，只有 DeepSeek 能稳定完成多步 tool calling。
GLM 和 Kimi 均无法正常执行 skill：

■ GLM 4.6
  错误：400 (code:1210) "API 调用参数有误"
  表现：调用 skill 后立即报错，请求停止

■ Kimi K2.6
  错误：500 (no body)
  表现：调用 skill 后客户端卡死，长时间等待无响应

■ DeepSeek（唯一正常）
  Skill 完整执行，多步 tool calling 正常

两个问题的根因相同：
Claude Agent SDK 使用 Anthropic 原生 tool_use 格式，
CherryStudio 在转换到 OpenAI 兼容格式时存在缺陷。

具体有两个缺陷：
1. 未设置的可选参数被序列化为字符串 "[undefined]" 而非省略
   （例如 "user":"[undefined]", "tools":"[undefined]"）
   GLM API 校验严格，直接拒绝
2. Skill→ToolSearch→工具调用的嵌套链在转换时产生 Kimi API 无法解析的格式

关联已有 Issue：
- #11314 GLM 1210（标记 completed 但核心 [undefined] 问题未修复）
- #12219 [undefined] 参数被认定为"设计如此"
- #13511 Kimi K2.5 Agent 模式错误
- #13625 Agent 模式下自动切换协议端点

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Agent 模式选择 GLM 4.6 或 Kimi K2.6
2. 启用 Skill 系统，安装 project-brain skill
3. 对话中输入"查看项目"触发 skill
4. GLM → 立即返回 400 错误 "API 调用参数有误"
5. Kimi → 客户端卡死，Network 显示 500 no body

抓包数据（GLM Request Body）：
{"model":"glm-4.6","user":"[undefined]","max_tokens":"[undefined]","tools":"[undefined]","tool_choice":"[undefined]","frequency_penalty":"[undefined]","temperature":1.1,...}

响应：{"error":{"code":"1210","message":"API 调用参数有误，请检查文档。"}}

### Expected Behavior

Agent 模式下所有支持 function calling 的模型都能正常运行 Skill，包括 GLM 和 Kimi 系列。参数中的 [undefined] 占位符应在发送前被过滤掉，嵌套 tool call 链应正确转换为目标模型支持的格式。

### Relevant Log Output

```shell
GLM:
Error Cause: "[undefined]"
Status Code: 400
Request Path: https://open.bigmodel.cn/api/paas/v4/chat/completions
Response: {"error":{"code":"1210","message":"API 调用参数有误，请检查文档。"}}

Kimi:
API Error: 500 status code (no body)
ToolSearch → Skill tool reference → invoke → 500
```

### Additional Context

建议修复方向：

短期（参数清洗）：在 buildStreamTextParams 返回前递归过滤值为 "[undefined]" 的字段。
核心代码不到 20 行：
function stripUndefined(obj) {
  if (obj === '[undefined]') return undefined;
  if (Array.isArray(obj)) return obj.map(stripUndefined);
  if (obj && typeof obj === 'object') {
    const c = {};
    for (const [k,v] of Object.entries(obj)) {
      const val = stripUndefined(v);
      if (val !== undefined && val !== '[undefined]') c[k] = val;
    }
    return c;
  }
  return obj;
}
调用点：src/renderer/src/aiCore/prepareParams/parameterBuilder.ts → buildStreamTextParams 返回前，
或 src/renderer/src/services/ApiService.ts 发送请求前。

中期：增强 messageConverter.ts 对嵌套 tool_use 链的格式验证。
长期：参考 #13625 自动选择协议端点。

title: Bug: API Service /v1/messages sends requests to /v1/v1/messages (double path)
body:
### Description

The API Service's Anthropic Messages endpoint (`POST /v1/messages`) produces a double `/v1` path when forwarding requests to upstream providers. This causes all Anthropic-format requests through the API Service to fail with 404.

**Expected:** `https://upstream.example.com/v1/messages`  
**Actual:** `https://upstream.example.com/v1/v1/messages`

### Root Cause

In `packages/shared/anthropic/index.ts`, `getSdkClient()` passes `provider.apiHost` directly as the Anthropic SDK's `baseURL`:

```typescript
const baseURL =
  provider.type === 'anthropic'
    ? provider.apiHost
    : (provider.anthropicApiHost && provider.anthropicApiHost.trim()) || provider.apiHost
```

However, `provider.apiHost` has already been processed by `formatProviderApiHost()` → `formatApiHost()`, which appends `/v1` to the URL. The Anthropic SDK then **also** appends `/v1/messages` to the `baseURL`, resulting in `/v1/v1/messages`.

The same bug was already fixed for the Claude Code integration (which correctly uses `withoutTrailingApiVersion()`):

```typescript
// src/main/services/agents/ClaudeCodeService.ts (or similar)
const resolveAnthropicBaseUrl = () => {
  if (isAzureOpenAI) return `${withoutTrailingApiVersion(provider.apiHost).replace(/\/openai$/, '')}/anthropic`
  return withoutTrailingApiVersion(provider.anthropicApiHost?.trim() || provider.apiHost)
}
```

But this fix was not applied to the API Service's `getSdkClient()`.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Enable the API Service in Cherry Studio settings
2. Configure a provider with type `new-api` or `openai` (e.g., any OpenAI-compatible gateway that also supports Anthropic models)
3. Send a request to `http://127.0.0.1:{port}/v1/messages` with an Anthropic Messages format payload
4. Observe the upstream request goes to `/v1/v1/messages` and returns 404

### Suggested Fix

In `packages/shared/anthropic/index.ts`, wrap the `baseURL` with `withoutTrailingApiVersion()`:

```diff
+ import { withoutTrailingApiVersion } from '@shared/utils/api'
  
  // Inside getSdkClient():
- const baseURL =
-   provider.type === 'anthropic'
-     ? provider.apiHost
-     : (provider.anthropicApiHost && provider.anthropicApiHost.trim()) || provider.apiHost
+ const rawBaseURL =
+   provider.type === 'anthropic'
+     ? provider.apiHost
+     : (provider.anthropicApiHost && provider.anthropicApiHost.trim()) || provider.apiHost
+ const baseURL = withoutTrailingApiVersion(rawBaseURL)
```

This is consistent with the existing fix in the Claude Code integration.

### Why OpenAI chat completions are not affected

The `/v1/chat/completions` handler uses `new OpenAI({ baseURL: provider.apiHost })`. OpenAI SDK treats `baseURL` as a prefix and appends `/chat/completions` (without adding another `/v1`), so `/v1` in `apiHost` is correct for that path.

### Environment

- Cherry Studio version: 1.9.4
- OS: macOS
- Upstream provider: new-api v0.13.2 gateway

### Platform

Windows

### Version

1.9.4

### Bug Description

When sending PDF files to an OpenAI-compatible API server through Cherry Studio, the base64 encoding of the binary file content is incorrect, causing the server to receive a corrupted file after decoding that AI models cannot process.

**Comparison Data:**

| Stage | Size | SHA256 |
|---|---|---|
| Original PDF file | 174,551 bytes | `de766d8b...` |
| After Cherry Studio encoding (base64 received by API) | b64_len=232,764 | — |
| After server-side base64 decoding | 174,570 bytes | `664c5157...` (differs from original) |
| Correctly encoded with Python `base64.b64encode()` | b64_len=232,736 ✅ | — |

The base64 encoded by Cherry Studio has **28 extra characters** compared to the correct value (232,764 vs 232,736), and the decoded file has 19 extra bytes with completely corrupted content.

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Configure an OpenAI-compatible API endpoint in Cherry Studio
2. Select a PDF file (any binary PDF)
3. Send via `messages.content` using `type: "file"` + `file_data` (base64) method
4. Server receives the base64 data, but finds the file corrupted after decoding
5. Use `curl` / Python script to send the same file to the same API with correct `base64.b64encode()` encoding, file is intact and usable

### Expected Behavior

Cherry Studio should read files in binary mode (like `readAsArrayBuffer`), use standard base64 encoding (RFC 4648), and ensure that the encoded data has the correct length, and the file decoded by the server is completely identical to the original file.

### Relevant Log Output

```shell
Suspected problem is in the file reading/encoding stage. Binary files like PDFs may have been read in text mode (such as `readAsText`), causing non-printable bytes to be incorrectly converted. It is recommended to check the following logic:
- Whether files are read in binary mode
- Whether base64 encoding uses standard library's `btoa` / `Buffer.toString('base64')`
- Whether there is additional string processing when building the `file_data` field (such as newline conversion, etc.)
```

### Additional Context

- This is not a server-side issue: after correctly encoding with Python `base64.b64encode()` and sending to the same server, AI processes PDFs completely normally
- The same issue was reproduced on multiple PDF files
- Whether image upload has the same problem remains to be verified (may only affect binary files)
- Reference: In the OpenAI protocol, `file_data` should be a pure base64 string of the file (without `data:` prefix)
- Other: This issue was submitted by claude desktop

## Description

When using SiliconFlow's `BAAI/bge-m3` as the embedding model, the knowledge base shows green checkmarks (✓) indicating embedding is complete, but:

1. Searching within the knowledge base returns no results
2. When mounting the knowledge base in a conversation, the AI responds saying it cannot read/access the knowledge base content

Switching to `BAAI/bge-large-zh-v1.5` (also on SiliconFlow) and rebuilding the exact same knowledge base resolves the issue completely.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Add SiliconFlow as model provider with valid API key
2. Add `BAAI/bge-m3` as embedding model
3. Create a knowledge base with `BAAI/bge-m3` selected
4. Add text notes (or files) to the knowledge base
5. Wait for green ✓ marks indicating completion
6. Search within the knowledge base → **no results returned**
7. Mount knowledge base in a conversation and ask related questions → AI says it has no access to the knowledge base

## Expected Behavior

Knowledge base search should return relevant results, and conversations with mounted knowledge base should reference the stored content.

## Actual Behavior

- Embedding appears to succeed (green ✓) but vector data is not actually stored or retrievable
- Knowledge base internal search returns nothing
- AI in conversation cannot access knowledge base content

## Workaround

Switch embedding model to `BAAI/bge-large-zh-v1.5` on SiliconFlow and rebuild the knowledge base. Everything works correctly with this model.

## Environment

- Cherry Studio: latest version (as of 2026-05-03)
- OS: Windows 11
- Embedding provider: SiliconFlow
- Working model: `BAAI/bge-large-zh-v1.5`
- Non-working model: `BAAI/bge-m3`
- Content type: text notes (not file uploads)

## Additional Context

The SiliconFlow account has sufficient quota. The issue is specific to `BAAI/bge-m3` — it's possible the model API returns a successful response but with empty/invalid vectors, causing Cherry Studio to mark embedding as complete without actually storing usable data.

title: [Feature] Unified API Protocol Translation Layer (OpenAI ↔ Anthropic ↔ Google)
body:
## Problem

Currently, Cherry Studio requires each provider to be defined with a specific `provider_type` (`openai`, `anthropic`, `new-api`, etc.), and models under certain provider types cannot be accessed via other API protocols.

For example:
- Claude models under `new-api` providers fail when accessed via `/v1/chat/completions` (OpenAI format) with error: _"Provider of type 'new-api' is not supported for OpenAI chat completions"_
- Models under `anthropic` providers fail with the same error
- PR #14818 fixed the `/v1/v1/messages` double-path issue, but the fundamental limitation remains: **each provider type only supports its native protocol**

This forces users to:
1. Maintain separate provider configurations for the same upstream service
2. Be unable to use certain models through tools that only speak one protocol (e.g., Hermes Agent only speaks OpenAI format)
3. Manually figure out which `provider_type` + API endpoint combination works for each model

## Proposal

Add a **built-in protocol translation layer** that automatically converts between the three major AI API protocols:

| From \ To | OpenAI Chat | Anthropic Messages | Google Gemini |
|-----------|------------|-------------------|---------------|
| OpenAI Chat | — | ✅ | ✅ |
| Anthropic Messages | ✅ | — | ✅ |
| Google Gemini | ✅ | ✅ | — |

### How it would work

1. **Any model accessible via any endpoint**: A Claude model registered under a `new-api` provider could be called via `/v1/chat/completions` — Cherry Studio would detect the model type and translate the request to Anthropic Messages format before forwarding upstream, then translate the response back.

2. **Automatic protocol detection**: Based on the upstream provider type, Cherry Studio determines the native protocol and handles translation transparently.

3. **Unified streaming support**: SSE stream format differences between protocols are handled internally.

### Key translations needed

- **OpenAI → Anthropic**: `messages` format conversion, `system` → top-level `system` param, `max_tokens` handling, tool/function calling format, streaming `data:` format
- **Anthropic → OpenAI**: Reverse of above, `content_block` events → `choices[].delta`
- **Gemini ↔ Others**: `contents` / `parts` format conversion, `generationConfig` mapping

## Prior Art

- [LiteLLM](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm) — Python library providing unified interface across 100+ LLMs with protocol translation
- [OneAPI](https://github.com/songquanpeng/one-api) — OpenAI-compatible gateway with multi-provider support
- [AI Gateway (Portkey)](https://github.com/Portkey-ai/gateway) — Universal API gateway with protocol normalization

## Expected Benefit

- **Users**: Any model works through any API endpoint, no more provider-type restrictions
- **Tool ecosystem**: Tools like Hermes, Continue.dev, Cursor etc. that speak only OpenAI format can access all models seamlessly
- **Simplicity**: No need to configure multiple providers for the same upstream just to support different protocols

## Additional Context

Discovered while using Cherry Studio as a unified gateway for Hermes Agent. Out of 100 registered models, ~20 were inaccessible because their provider types didn't support the OpenAI chat completions protocol that Hermes uses exclusively.

3. The model receives duplicate-looking links even though the original search results are different pages.
4. Search quality can be degraded, especially for sites like Sina where many different articles share the same domain.

This is not the same as repeated web search calls. The one-search-per-response budget appears to work. The issue is that distinct result URLs are collapsed to the same origin before being passed to the model.

Important nuance: the final UI citations may still preserve the full original URLs and clicking the citation numbers can open the correct pages. The issue reported here is specifically about the tool message content sent to the model, where the `url` fields are shortened to origins.

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Enable built-in web search with Tavily.
2. Use a model such as `deepseek-v4-pro`.
3. Ask a query likely to return multiple results from the same domain, for example:
   `请详细搜索并总结“2026年欧冠决赛结果”，包括比分、进球者和关键事件。请确保信息完整。`
4. Open DevTools / Network and inspect the search provider response and the subsequent model request.
5. Compare original Tavily result URLs with the tool result content sent to the model.

Observed result:

Tavily returns distinct URLs, for example:

```text
https://k.sina.com.cn/article_7857201856_1d45362c0019052914.html
https://k.sina.com.cn/article_7857201856_1d45362c0019051st4.html
https://k.sina.com.cn/article_7857201856_1d45362c0019051vg8.html
```

But the tool result passed to the model contains:

```text
https://k.sina.com.cn
https://k.sina.com.cn
https://k.sina.com.cn
```

Another example:

```text
https://finance.sina.com.cn/roll/2026-04-27/doc-inhvwwms7950112.shtml
https://finance.sina.com.cn/tech/roll/2026-04-03/doc-inhtfkwz8796402.shtml
```

becomes:

```text
https://finance.sina.com.cn
https://finance.sina.com.cn
```


### Expected Behavior

Distinct search results should remain distinguishable in the tool result payload sent to the model, even if the UI separately keeps full citation URLs.

Possible approaches:

- Keep full URLs in the model-facing source payload.
- Or keep compact but unique URLs, e.g. origin + pathname without query/hash.
- Or add a separate compact display URL while preserving the canonical full URL for citation identity.
- Deduplicate only by canonical full URL, not by origin.

### Relevant Log Output

```shell
No API error. This is visible by comparing:

1. `api.tavily.com` response URLs
2. Subsequent model request tool message content
3. Final rendered citations, which may still contain the full original URLs
```

### Additional Context

This may be related to #14466, which intentionally shortened returned source URLs to origin to reduce token overhead. That optimization saves tokens, but collapsing all same-domain articles to the same origin loses source identity in the model-facing context and can make different results look duplicated to the model.

title: Support Quick Emoji Response in Feishu Agent Channel
body:
## Feature Request

When interacting with agents via the Feishu channel, users currently lack immediate feedback that the agent has received and is processing their message.

### Proposed Solution
- Add support for quick emoji reactions (e.g., 👀, ⏳, or 🤖) to user messages in the Feishu channel.
- The agent should automatically react with an emoji as soon as it starts processing, giving clear visual feedback that it's working.
- Remove or update the reaction once the response is sent.

This small UX improvement would significantly reduce user uncertainty during longer agent processing times.

Thanks!

title: [Feature]: OpenAI / Anthropic API Format Interoperability
body:
## Background

Cherry Studio's Agent mode currently only works with models exposed through an Anthropic-format endpoint. Frontier non-Anthropic models — for example GPT-5.5, even when accessed through aggregator providers like CherryIN that already proxy them — cannot be used in Agent mode at all. Users who want to drive Agent with a non-Claude model end up running an external proxy (cc-switch / cc-nim) on the side just to translate request formats, which is fragile and hard to discover. The same friction shows up in Chat mode for aggregator providers that expose multiple endpoint types per model: users have to guess which endpoint to pick, and frequently hit "endpoint mismatch" errors.

## Goal

Any supported model — including non-Anthropic models like GPT-5.5 — can be used in both Agent and Chat modes, with format conversion handled transparently inside Cherry Studio so users no longer need external proxies like cc-switch.

## Spec

- Agent mode accepts any model the user has configured, regardless of the model's native API format.
- When the user's selected model exposes an Anthropic-format endpoint (e.g. via an aggregator), Agent uses that endpoint directly without conversion.
- When the model has no Anthropic-format endpoint available, Cherry Studio translates between the model's native format (OpenAI, Gemini) and the Anthropic format expected by Agent, transparently in both request and response paths.
- Format translation preserves streaming, tool-use, and structured-output behaviors — the user does not see degraded capabilities when running a non-Anthropic model in Agent.
- The same translation layer also applies in Chat mode for aggregator providers, so users do not have to manually pick an endpoint that matches the requesting mode.
- When a request genuinely cannot be honored (the model truly does not support a feature being asked for), the UI surfaces a clear, actionable message instead of leaking a raw upstream API error.

## Verification

- Configure CherryIN provider, select GPT-5.5, switch to Agent mode → Agent runs end-to-end with tool calls and streaming working, no external cc-switch / cc-nim required.
- Configure CherryIN provider, select Claude Sonnet through the OpenAI-compatible endpoint, use in Chat mode → conversation works end-to-end with no "endpoint mismatch" error.
- Streaming a long Agent response from GPT-5.5 produces incremental chunks at the same cadence as a native Claude model in Agent (no perceived full-response buffering).
- Use Agent's tool-use with GPT-5.5 → tool calls and tool results both round-trip correctly; assistant final answer references the tool output.
- Add a Gemini provider and use a Gemini model in Agent mode → works end-to-end through translation.
- Disconnect upstream while a translated request is in-flight → user sees a clear "request failed, please retry" message, not an unhandled exception or stuck UI.

title: [Feature]: Keep Agent Tool Set in Sync with the Latest Claude Code
body:
## Background

Claude Code's terminal experience now ships sub-agent and task-orchestration tools — TeamCreate, TeamDelete, TaskCreate, TaskList, TaskGet, TaskUpdate, TaskStop, SendMessage and similar — that let the model spawn, coordinate, and message child agents. Cherry Studio's bundled Agent only recognizes an older subset, so when the model attempts to call any of these tools the user sees "tool not available" and loses the multi-agent workflows that Claude Code already supports natively.

## Goal

Cherry Studio's Agent supports the same tool set as the latest Claude Code, including sub-agent orchestration tools, with their execution surfaced in the conversation UI.

## Spec

- When the model calls any orchestration tool exposed by the latest Claude Code (TeamCreate / TeamDelete / TaskCreate / TaskList / TaskGet / TaskUpdate / TaskStop / SendMessage and the rest of this family), the call succeeds end-to-end without "tool not available" errors.
- These orchestration tools appear in the Agent's tool listing (e.g. Agent Settings / Tools) alongside existing tools, with names and descriptions that match Claude Code.
- Each orchestration tool call is visibly identified in the conversation — the user can see which tool ran, with what input, and what it returned, just as they do for existing tool calls.
- When an orchestration tool spawns or affects child agents/tasks, the resulting work is observable to the user (e.g. the user can tell that a sub-agent is running and see its outcome rolled back into the conversation).
- Permission/approval behavior (auto-allow vs prompt) extends to the new tools consistently with the rules already applied to existing tools.

## Verification

- In an Agent session, ask the model to "spawn a sub-agent to research X and report back." The conversation should show TaskCreate (or equivalent) executing, the sub-agent's progress, and a final consolidated reply — no "tool not available" error.
- Open Agent Settings → Tools. The list contains entries for TeamCreate, TeamDelete, TaskCreate, TaskList, TaskGet, TaskUpdate, TaskStop, SendMessage, with descriptions matching what Claude Code documents.
- Trigger SendMessage from the model to an existing sub-agent. The conversation visibly indicates a message was sent to the sub-agent and shows the response.
- Repeat the user-reported scenario from #12944: in the same workflow that previously failed in Cherry Studio but worked in terminal Claude Code, all referenced tools now run successfully inside Cherry Studio.
- Negative check: after the upgrade, none of the previously working tools (Bash, Edit, Read, Write, Grep, Glob, WebSearch, WebFetch, Task, TodoWrite, NotebookRead, NotebookEdit, MultiEdit) regress in availability or approval behavior.

title: [Feature]: Cherry Studio Skills — CherryIN Integration, Save-as-Skill, Public Submission, and Team Sharing
body:
## Background

Inside Cherry Studio, skills are increasingly the differentiator that delivers real productivity to non-technical users — the May 2026 enterprise workshop showed PPT-generation skills produce the strongest "wow" moment, and attendees immediately asked four things: how to install, how to find what's installed, how to **create their own**, and how to **share them publicly or with teammates**. Today the Skills page only supports keyword search across foreign registries with English-only descriptions, no curated landing, no in-place update, no path to create user-authored skills, no way to publish them, and no surface to tell users where an installed skill is actually mounted. The CherryIN marketplace backend (tracked separately) provides the supply side with a two-tier catalog (Official + Community); Cherry Studio is the consumer surface that makes these skills end-to-end usable, creatable, and publishable.

## Goal

Cherry Studio users discover, install, find, create, update, publish, and share skills entirely inside the app — backed by CherryIN's two-tier catalog (Official + Community) — without ever touching GitHub, zip files, or any external tool.

## Spec

- The Skills page integrates **CherryIN as the default skill source**, pinned at the top. Existing third-party sources (claude-plugins.dev, skills.sh, clawhub.ai) remain available alongside it.
- The Skills page presents four top-level entries: **Featured** (curated CherryIN Official highlights), **Community** (user-published skills, browseable by category/popularity/recency), **Installed** (user's installed skills with update status and where each skill is mounted), and **Categories** (browse the CherryIN catalog by category).
- **One-click install / update**: any CherryIN skill (Official or Community) installs / updates with a single click — no GitHub, no zip, no manual paths. No background auto-updates by default.
- **Day-one launch experience**: when Cherry Studio first ships this Skills page, Featured prominently surfaces a PPT / slide-deck generation skill (the highest-impact seed skill from workshop observations), followed by Feishu CLI, document processing, and data analysis seed skills.
- **Localized rendering**: skill name, description, and README render in the user's app language with English fallback. Skill triggers stay canonical (not localized).
- **Installed discoverability**: each Installed entry shows which Agents have this skill enabled, with a one-click jump to the Agent's settings. After install, the UI surfaces "Now available in [Agent name(s)]" so users are never left wondering where the skill went.
- **Save-as-Skill flow inside Agent conversations**: after the user completes a task, an inline "Save this as a Skill" affordance lets them package that workflow into a personal skill — the Agent guides naming, description, and trigger.
- **Publish to public marketplace — two paths**: every user-authored installed skill has a "Publish to CherryIN" action offering two choices:
  - **Submit for Official Review**: skill is sent to CherryIN's review queue; on approval it appears under Featured / Categories with the **Official** badge.
  - **Publish to Community**: skill is auto-published to the Community zone immediately, no upfront review. Subject to community rating and report-based moderation.
- **Community-zone trust signals**: every Community skill card shows install count, average rating (1–5 stars from users who installed it), and report flag count. Skills below a quality threshold (low rating / many valid reports) are auto-removed from Community listing by CherryIN.
- **Rate and report**: users can rate any installed skill (1–5 stars) and report violations (e.g. malicious behavior, broken, spam) directly from the Skills page or the skill's detail panel.
- **Share installed skill via Cherry Mail**: every installed skill exposes a "Share via Cherry Mail" action — one-click peer sharing without going through the public marketplace (see #15036 for full sharing semantics).

## Verification

- User opens Skills page for the first time → Featured tab opens by default, PPT / slide skill in the first row. Tab bar shows Featured / Community / Installed / Categories.
- User in zh-CN clicks install on the PPT skill from Featured → installs in under 5 seconds, no GitHub / zip prompts → toast: "Now available in Cherry Assistant". Clicking the toast jumps to Cherry Assistant's skills list with the new entry highlighted.
- In an Agent conversation, user asks "research topic X, summarize, send via email" → after completion, inline "Save this as a Skill" button appears → click → Agent prompts for name → user confirms → new skill appears in Installed.
- User opens the newly-saved skill's detail → clicks "Publish to CherryIN" → modal offers two choices. User picks "Submit for Official Review" → confirmation: "Submitted. You'll be notified when reviewed." User picks "Publish to Community" instead → confirmation: "Published to Community now."
- Same skill chosen "Publish to Community" → next time any user opens the Community tab in Cherry Studio, the new skill is visible with 0 installs / no rating yet. After several users install and rate it 4–5 stars, the average rating shown matches.
- A Community-zone skill receives multiple valid reports → CherryIN removes it; users browsing Community no longer see it; users who already installed it retain functionality but see a "removed from Community" notice on the Installed entry.
- User rates an installed skill 3 stars and writes a short reason → rating + review count visible on that skill's Community listing.
- User submits a skill for Official Review → CherryIN approves it via admin → next time the user opens Skills, that skill now appears in Featured / Categories with the Official badge; the Community-zone entry is replaced by the Official one.
- User opens an installed skill's detail → clicks "Share via Cherry Mail" → recipient gets one-click install (peer share); the skill is NOT published to Community or Official as a side effect.
- Existing third-party install paths (claude-plugins.dev, manual zip, directory copy) continue to work; previously installed third-party skills remain enabled and listed under Installed.

title: [Feature]: Allow Audio and Video Uploads When the Model Supports Them
body:
## Background

Frontier multimodal models now natively understand audio and video — Gemini 2.x supports both, and OpenAI's GPT-4o family supports audio. Cherry Studio's chat input still blocks audio and video file uploads regardless of which model is selected, so users on capable models have to transcribe or screenshot their files in another tool before sending. The v2 aiCore tracker calls this out as a P0 gap (#14018), and several open user reports (#11906, #13770, #13699, #12019) have stacked behind it.

## Goal

Users can upload audio and video files to the chat when the active model supports them, and are told clearly when it does not.

## Spec

- The upload control allows audio and video files when the active model declares support for that modality, and disallows them otherwise.
- Capability gating is per-modality: a model that supports audio but not video enables audio uploads only, and vice versa.
- When upload is disallowed, the user sees a clear, model-specific reason (not a generic "unsupported file" error).
- When the user switches the active model mid-conversation to one that no longer supports already-attached audio or video, the user is warned before the next send.
- Uploaded audio and video are sent to the model as multimodal input the model can consume natively, without client-side transcription or framegrabbing.
- Existing image upload behavior is unchanged; turning this on does not loosen file-size or format limits for images.

## Verification

- With Gemini 2.x selected, attach a `.mp4` and ask "what's happening in this video?" → the model answers based on the video content; repeat with `.mp3` and a content question → the model answers based on the audio.
- With GPT-4o selected (audio support, no native video), attaching `.mp3` succeeds and the model answers based on the audio; attempting to attach `.mp4` is rejected with a message that names the model and says it does not support video.
- With an image-only vision model selected (e.g., Claude Sonnet), both audio and video attachments are rejected; image upload still works as before.
- Attach a `.mp4` while on Gemini, then switch to a text-only model and try to send → the user sees a warning that the attachment will be ignored or that the message cannot be sent as-is.
- Attach a corrupted or unsupported-codec file → user sees a specific failure reason; no silent send with an empty payload.
- Repeat the existing image-upload regression scenarios (single image, multiple images, drag-and-drop, paste from clipboard) → behavior identical to current release.

title: [Feature]: Right-click quote correctly preserves KaTeX/MathJax math formulas
body:
## Background

When a message contains math formulas, right-click → Quote produces broken output. KaTeX-rendered formulas turn into multi-line Unicode glyph soup (e.g. `iℏ\n∂\n∂t\nΨ = ...`) inside the blockquote, which is not valid Markdown and re-renders incorrectly. MathJax-rendered formulas can't be quoted at all (the quoted content comes out empty). Users have to manually retype the LaTeX source every time.

## Goal

Right-clicking Quote on a message with math formulas inserts the original LaTeX source into the input box, so the quoted content is valid Markdown and re-renders identically.

## Spec

- Right-click Quote on a message preserves math formulas as their original LaTeX source (`$...$` for inline, `$$...$$` for display), regardless of whether the message was rendered with KaTeX or MathJax.
- The quoted text remains valid Markdown — sending it produces a message whose math renders the same as the original.

## Verification

- Message contains a KaTeX-rendered display formula `$$i\hbar \frac{\partial}{\partial t} \Psi = \hat{H} \Psi$$` → right-click Quote → input box shows `> $$i\hbar \frac{\partial}{\partial t} \Psi = \hat{H} \Psi$$` (single line, valid LaTeX). Sending this message renders the formula correctly.
