title: [Feature]: Allow Uploading and Analyzing ZIP Archives
body:
## Background

Users frequently want to share bundles of files with the assistant — small code repos, document packages, dataset folders — but Cherry Studio rejects ZIP files at upload time. The workaround is to extract locally and paste files one by one, which loses folder structure and forces the user to babysit the conversation. The original report (#13432) is closed but the pain is still live, especially in Agent mode where the assistant has tools to inspect arbitrary files but never gets the chance because the upload is blocked client-side.

## Goal

Users can attach a ZIP file to a conversation and have the assistant inspect and answer questions about its contents.

## Spec

- Users can attach a `.zip` file to a chat or agent conversation through the same upload entry points used for other file types.
- The assistant can answer questions about the archive's contents — folder structure, file names, and the content of text-readable files inside.
- A per-archive size limit applies. Archives exceeding the limit are rejected with the limit named in the error message.
- Password-protected (encrypted) ZIP archives are out of scope; uploading one is rejected with a message that names the reason.
- Behavior for other archive formats (tar, tar.gz, 7z, rar) is unchanged in this release; they remain blocked as today.
- Existing non-archive file upload behavior is unchanged.

## Verification

- Upload a ZIP containing `.md` and `.py` files arranged in nested folders, ask "what's in this archive?" → the assistant lists the structure and can answer follow-up questions about specific file contents.
- Upload a ZIP that contains a `.png` and a text file → the assistant can reference the image by filename and discuss the text file's contents.
- In Agent mode, upload a ZIP and ask the agent to extract it and run a script from inside → the agent completes the task using its filesystem/shell tools.
- Upload a ZIP larger than the configured size limit → upload is rejected with a message that names the limit.
- Upload a password-protected ZIP → upload is rejected with a message saying password-protected archives are not supported.
- Upload a `.tar.gz` or `.7z` → behavior is identical to the current release (still rejected with the current error).
- Re-run existing single-file upload regression scenarios (single file, multiple files, drag-and-drop, paste from clipboard) → behavior identical to the current release.

## Related

This is part of the ongoing v2 UI migration away from legacy antd and styled-components usage. The current shared renderer component area still carries many legacy UI dependencies even though the target UI stack is `@cherrystudio/ui` + Tailwind CSS.

Inventory was taken from `src/renderer/src/components` only on 2026-05-07:

- #14331 v2 UI Boundary and Theme Contract Consolidation Refactoring
- #14297 generic Drawer / Code Tool v2 design work
- #14535 shared selector composite work
- #14339 / #14351 translate-page UI work

Replace the remaining antd and styled-components usage under `src/renderer/src/components` with repo-standard primitives and styling:

- Prefer existing `@cherrystudio/ui` primitives/composites before adding new local wrappers.
- Use Tailwind CSS and Cherry Studio design tokens instead of `styled-components` for presentation styles.
- Replace antd components such as `Modal`, `Input`, `Select`, `Dropdown`, `Popover`, `Table`, `Upload`, `Typography`, `Form`, `Spin`, `Alert`, `Progress`, `Skeleton`, `Tabs`, and `Tag` with local v2-compatible equivalents.
- Replace `@ant-design/icons` usages with lucide icons or existing Cherry Studio icon components where appropriate.
- Keep business behavior unchanged; this issue is about shared renderer component UI dependency migration, not feature redesign.
- Split implementation into focused PRs by component bucket instead of one broad mechanical rewrite.

High-signal buckets from the scan:

- `Popups`: 25 antd files, 16 styled-components files
- `RichEditor`: 7 antd files, 4 styled-components files
- `CodeBlockView`: 2 antd files, 4 styled-components files, 31 styled declarations
- `MinApp`: 2 antd files, 3 styled-components files
- `app`: 1 antd file, 2 styled-components files

- `rg "from ['\"]antd|from ['\"]antd/|from ['\"]@ant-design|@ant-design" src/renderer/src/components` returns no component implementation imports, except for explicitly approved temporary compatibility shims.
- `rg "from ['\"]styled-components|styled-components" src/renderer/src/components` returns no component implementation imports, except for explicitly approved temporary compatibility shims.
- Replacements follow `DESIGN.md` and `packages/ui` public contracts.
- User-visible text remains i18n-backed.
- Existing tests are updated or preserved for migrated components.

- Leave the current mixed implementation in place and only migrate individual components when touched. This lowers short-term risk but keeps renderer shared components tied to legacy UI dependencies.
- Move selected reusable components into `packages/ui` first, then update renderer consumers. This is useful for truly reusable primitives/composites but should not be forced for business-coupled components.

- `packages/ui/docs/styles-reference.md`
- `packages/ui/docs/migration-plan.md`

title: [Feature]: Cross-Model Usage Dashboard with Opt-In Public Leaderboard
body:
## Background

Cherry Studio surfaces token counts on individual messages but offers no view of how much a user has spent across all conversations and all models. Power users have no way to gauge their own monthly cost without exporting and totaling by hand, and there's no community visibility to anchor "what does heavy use look like?" Tools like [vibecafe.ai/usage/rank](https://vibecafe.ai/usage/rank) and [ccusage.cherry-ai.com](https://ccusage.cherry-ai.com/) demonstrate the pattern works for AI coding tools, with leaderboards driving both engagement and natural identification of high-value users for community outreach.

## Goal

Users can see their own cumulative Cherry Studio usage across all conversations, and optionally publish their numbers to a public leaderboard that compares them with other Cherry Studio users.

## Spec

- A dedicated usage dashboard aggregates the user's token consumption and estimated cost across every conversation and every model used in Cherry Studio, with time tabs for 1 day, 7 days, and 30 days.
- The dashboard breaks down usage two ways: by individual model and by provider/model family, so users can see where their spend goes.
- Estimated cost uses the same per-model pricing already configured for the per-message cost display; models without configured pricing contribute to the token total but not the cost total.
- A public leaderboard tab is visible to all users in read-only mode by default, listing rank, handle, total tokens, and estimated cost, filterable by 1D / 7D / 30D and by model family.
- Joining the leaderboard is opt-in: clicking **"I want to be on the leaderboard"** publishes the user's aggregated numbers under a handle. The handle is the user's passport account name when signed in, and the existing user nickname from Cherry Studio settings otherwise.
- Only aggregated counts (tokens, estimated cost, model name, provider name) and the chosen handle leave the device. Conversation content, prompts, message text, and per-message detail never leave the device.
- Users on the leaderboard can opt out at any time, which removes their entry from the public ranking; the local dashboard is unaffected.
- Enterprise users (signed in to a Cherry Studio Enterprise account) see an additional **internal leaderboard** scoped to their own organization, shown alongside the public leaderboard. The internal leaderboard is visible only to members of the same organization; entries are identified by the enterprise account name.
- When a user's all-time estimated cost crosses a configurable threshold (default $999 USD), the dashboard surfaces a community group entry — labeled to match the threshold (e.g. "$999 Club") — that links to a designated Cherry Studio community group on WeChat. The threshold value, the entry label, and the destination link are configured by Cherry Studio operations. Users under the threshold do not see the entry.

## Verification

- Open the dashboard → see total tokens and estimated cost aggregated across all conversations and models; switch the 1D / 7D / 30D tabs → totals re-aggregate to the selected window.
- Use models from at least two providers in different conversations → the by-model breakdown lists every model used; the by-provider breakdown groups them correctly with summed totals.
- Use a model with no pricing configured → its token usage shows in the token total; the cost total excludes it without displaying a confusing zero or null.
- Click "I want to be on the leaderboard" while signed in to passport → the handle field is pre-filled with the passport account name; submit → user appears in the public leaderboard within a defined latency.
- Same flow without passport → the handle field uses the user nickname from settings; if the nickname is empty, the action is blocked with a prompt asking the user to set a nickname first.
- From the leaderboard, opt out → the user's entry is removed from the public ranking; the local dashboard still shows the same numbers.
- Inspect the network payload sent on opt-in → contains only aggregated counts, model/provider names, and the handle; no message content, no per-message records.
- Sign in as an enterprise user → an internal leaderboard tab appears alongside the public leaderboard, listing only members of the same organization; sign in as a different organization's user → the previous organization's internal entries are not visible.
- Sign in as a non-enterprise user → no internal leaderboard tab is shown; only the public leaderboard remains accessible.
- With the threshold configured at $999, simulate cumulative cost above and below it → entry appears and disappears at the boundary; clicking the entry opens the configured WeChat group.
- Change the configured threshold (e.g. to $500) → the boundary moves accordingly; the entry label updates to match the new threshold without a release.
- Existing per-message token and cost displays remain unchanged from the current release.

title: [Feature]: Bundle Portable Runtimes (uv, Git, Node) into Installer to Eliminate Environment Dependencies
body:
## Background

Cherry Studio depends on three external runtimes — uv, Git, and Node.js — but none of them ship with the installer. Users must download or install them separately, and each one has its own failure mode:

- **uv**: Downloaded at runtime via `install-uv.js` from a gitcode.com mirror with a hardcoded version. Frequently fails behind corporate firewalls, on weak networks, or offline — users see repeated "please install uv" prompts and MCP servers that depend on `uvx` simply don't work.
- **Git**: On macOS, `/usr/bin/git` is an Xcode CLT shim that passes the app's availability check but fails on actual `git clone`. On Windows, users must manually install Git for Windows and configure `CLAUDE_CODE_GIT_BASH_PATH`; those using fnm/nvm/mise find their PATH ignored by Git Bash.
- **Node.js**: Required for `npx`-based MCP servers. Non-developer users rarely have it installed. The current fallback to bundled `bun` has compatibility gaps (`.cmd` shims rejected on Windows, argument translation issues).

The combined effect: a non-developer user who installs Cherry Studio and tries to use Agent mode or MCP servers hits a wall of cryptic errors about missing tools they've never heard of.

## Goal

After installing Cherry Studio, all runtime-dependent features (MCP servers, Agent mode, skills, OpenClaw) work out of the box — the installer bundles portable uv, Git, and Node.js binaries so users never need to install developer tools or configure PATH manually.

## Spec

- The installer includes platform-specific portable binaries for uv, Git, and Node.js for each supported platform (macOS arm64/x64, Windows x64, Linux x64/arm64).
- On first launch, bundled binaries are extracted to the app's local binary directory and added to the app's internal PATH — no user action required.
- System-first priority: if the user already has a working system-installed version (meeting minimum version requirements), the system version takes priority over the bundled one.
- The runtime download scripts (`install-uv.js`, `install-bun.js`) and their associated UI prompts ("please install uv/bun") are removed; required tools are always present after install.
- Bundled binary versions are updated as part of the regular release process, not hardcoded in download scripts.
- On macOS, the bundled Git replaces reliance on the Xcode CLT shim — the app no longer assumes `/usr/bin/git` works.
- On Windows, the bundled Git includes git-bash, eliminating the need for users to install Git for Windows or set `CLAUDE_CODE_GIT_BASH_PATH`.
- The bundled Node.js provides `npx` directly, removing the bun-based npx fallback and its compatibility issues.
- All bundled binaries run in an isolated environment scoped to Cherry Studio — they do not modify the user's global PATH, shell profile, or system-level configuration.
- Phased delivery: uv ships first (P0, smaller binary ~12 MB, lower complexity); Git and Node.js follow in a subsequent release (larger binaries, platform-specific packaging complexity).

## Verification

- **[uv] Fresh install, offline**: macOS arm64, disconnect network before first launch, activate an MCP server requiring `uvx` — it should start successfully using bundled uv, no "install uv" dialog appears.
- **[uv] System uv present**: User has system uv 1.2.0 installed — Cherry Studio detects and uses the system version, not the bundled one (verify via version in logs).
- **[uv] Upgrade path**: Upgrade from a version that used `install-uv.js` to this version — no download prompt appears; previously downloaded uv in `~/.cherrystudio/bin` still works if newer than bundled.
- **[Git] macOS without Xcode CLT**: Fresh macOS with no Xcode CLT installed, use Agent mode that calls `git clone` — should succeed using bundled Git, no Xcode installation popup.
- **[Git] Windows without Git for Windows**: Fresh Windows install with no Git, enter Agent mode — should work without "Git Bash not found" error, no need to set `CLAUDE_CODE_GIT_BASH_PATH`.
- **[Node] No system Node**: Fresh install with no system Node.js, activate an MCP server specified with `npx` command — should start successfully using bundled Node/npx, not fall back to bun.
- **[Node] Windows .cmd shim**: Windows user with Node installed via fnm — MCP servers using `npx` should work regardless of `.cmd` shim issues, since bundled Node provides a real `npx` binary.
- **[Isolation] No global pollution**: After install and use, user's global PATH, `~/.bashrc`, `~/.zshrc`, and Windows system PATH remain unmodified by Cherry Studio's bundled binaries.
- **[Size] Installer growth**: Per-platform installer size increase stays within reasonable bounds (uv phase: <15 MB; full bundle phase: <150 MB).
- **[Priority override] System version wins**: User with Node 22 installed globally, Cherry Studio bundles Node 20 — app uses the system Node 22, not the older bundled one.

title: [Feature]: Pluggable Capability System — Expose Built-in Product Features as Agent-Callable Tools
body:
## Background

Cherry Studio ships several powerful built-in capabilities — OCR, Web Search, Knowledge Base (RAG), and image generation — but each is wired into a fixed UI workflow. Agents today can only call file/shell/web tools; they cannot invoke OCR to read a scanned receipt, query the Knowledge Base for context, generate an image, or (once shipped) transcribe audio or synthesize speech. Meanwhile, non-developer users frequently fail to set up the runtime prerequisites (git, node, Python, uv) that these capabilities depend on, and there is no way to browse, install, or manage the small local models (embedding models, OCR inference models, TTS voice models) that power offline capabilities — users must manually download binaries, configure paths, and troubleshoot version conflicts. The result is a monolithic app where capabilities cannot be composed by Agents, local models cannot be managed like apps in an app store, and the whole system cannot be easily toggled or extended by users.

> **Note:** Agent Knowledge Base (RAG) tool support has been split into a standalone deliverable: #14905. That issue can ship independently as a v2.1 milestone item.

## Goal

Restructure Cherry Studio's built-in capabilities (OCR, ASR, Web Search, Knowledge Base, Painting, TTS) into a pluggable system with a unified settings layout organized into three tiers — Environment & Dependencies (runtime prerequisites with one-click install), Local Models (an Ollama-like hub for browsing and installing small models), and Capability Tools (six toggleable modules) — where each enabled capability automatically becomes an Agent-callable tool.

## Spec

**I. Settings Layout — Three-Tier Structure**

The settings page is reorganized into three sections, replacing the current scattered layout (DocProcessSettings, WebSearchSettings, etc.) with a unified "Plugins" settings area:

- **Tier 1 — Environment & Dependencies**: Shows the installation status of each runtime (git, node, Python/uv) with a one-click install button for any that are missing. Status indicators (installed / not installed / version outdated) are visible at a glance without requiring the user to open a terminal. This tier builds on the bundled-runtimes foundation (#14893) — when runtimes are already bundled with the installer, this section confirms their status; when they are not yet bundled (e.g., early releases), this section provides the guided installation.

- **Tier 2 — Local Models**: An Ollama-like model hub where users browse a curated catalog of small local models, one-click install them, and manage their lifecycle. Four model categories:
  - **Embedding models** (for Knowledge Base): e.g., bge-small-zh (68MB), bge-m3 (1.2GB), nomic-embed-text (274MB)
  - **Inference models** (for OCR/document processing): e.g., PaddleOCR-v4 (12MB), surya-ocr (150MB)
  - **Speech models** (for TTS/ASR): e.g., Piper voices (15–45MB each), whisper-tiny (75MB)
  - **Multimodal models** (for image-aware Knowledge Base): models that let a Knowledge Base ingest and retrieve across images, scanned pages, charts, and tables — not just plain text. Two roles:
    - **Multimodal embedding** — embed images and text into one shared space so a text query can retrieve a diagram, screenshot, or scanned page: e.g., jina-clip-v2 (~0.9GB), nomic-embed-vision (pairs with nomic-embed-text in the same space), BGE-VL.
    - **Document-parsing vision models** — turn visually complex PDFs (multi-column layout, formulas, tables, figures) into structured text before embedding: e.g., the MinerU layout/table/formula pipeline, GOT-OCR2, a small Qwen-VL (e.g., 3B) for chart/figure understanding.

  When a Knowledge Base is created with a multimodal embedding backend, the embedding selector surfaces the installed multimodal models; document-parsing vision models feed the same ingest preprocessing path used by manual upload, so image-heavy documents are not silently reduced to "no extractable text".

  Each model card shows: name, size, description, status (not installed / downloading / ready), and action button (Install / Start / Stop / Delete). Inference engines start automatically when a capability tool needs them and stop after an idle timeout — users do not manually manage processes. When a capability tool is configured to use a local model backend, it draws from what is installed here.

- **Tier 3 — Capability Tools**: Lists six capability modules (OCR, ASR, Web Search, Knowledge Base, Painting, TTS), each with:
  - A master enable/disable toggle
  - A backend selector: choose between local engine (uses models from Tier 2) or cloud API (uses provider API key)
  - Provider-specific configuration (API keys, endpoint URLs, engine-specific settings)

  When a capability is disabled, it is completely unloaded — no memory footprint, no sidebar entry, no Agent tool registration.

**II. Agent Tool Integration**

- Each enabled capability automatically registers itself as an Agent-callable tool. Agents discover available capability tools at conversation start — the tool list reflects only what the user has enabled and configured.
- When an Agent calls a capability tool (e.g., "ocr_recognize", "knowledge_search", "generate_image", "web_search", "text_to_speech", "speech_to_text"), the request is routed through the same underlying service that the manual UI uses — one implementation, two entry points (UI and Agent).
- Each capability tool has a defined input/output contract visible to the Agent: what parameters it accepts, what it returns, and what errors it may surface. Agents can chain capability tools (e.g., OCR a document → search Knowledge Base with extracted text → summarize).
- Per-agent tool permissions remain in effect — administrators can restrict which agents may use which capability tools via the existing allowed_tools mechanism.
- **Knowledge Base (RAG) as Agent tool**: detailed spec and verification in #14905 (split out as v2.1 deliverable).

**III. Dependency-Aware Orchestration**

- If an Agent attempts to call a capability tool that depends on a missing runtime or uninstalled local model, the user sees a guided prompt to install the dependency — not a raw error. After installation, the Agent can retry without restarting the conversation.
- Capability tools that require no local dependencies (e.g., cloud-backed OCR, Web Search via API) work immediately after enabling — no runtime or model installation step needed.
- The Local Models tier shows dependency relationships: e.g., enabling "Knowledge Base" with local backend highlights that an embedding model is required and recommends one if none is installed.

## Verification

**Environment & Dependencies**
- Fresh install, no git/node/Python on the system. Open Settings → Environment & Dependencies — all three show "Not installed" with orange indicator and "Install" button. Click "Install" on node — progress bar appears, completes within 2 minutes, status changes to green "v22.x installed". No terminal interaction required.
- System already has node 22 installed. Environment & Dependencies shows green "v22.x (system)" — no install button, no override.

**Local Models**
- Open Settings → Local Models with nothing installed. Browse the catalog — models are grouped into Embedding, Inference, Speech, and Multimodal categories. Click "Install" on bge-small-zh (68MB) — download progress shows percentage, speed, and ETA. After completion, model card shows green "Ready" badge.
- User installs bge-small-zh, then navigates to Knowledge Base and creates a new base — the just-installed embedding model appears in the embedding model selector without any manual path configuration.
- User installs PaddleOCR-v4 model. No process is running yet. User then enables OCR capability with local backend and triggers OCR on a document — the PaddleOCR inference engine starts automatically, processes the document, and stops after 5 minutes of idle. No manual start/stop required.
- User clicks "Delete" on an installed model that is currently in use by a capability tool — a confirmation dialog warns "This model is used by OCR. Deleting it will disable local OCR. Continue?" After deletion, the OCR capability's backend selector shows "No local model — install one or switch to cloud API".
- Install a multimodal embedding model and create a Knowledge Base with it. Add a PDF that is mostly scanned pages and diagrams — a text query about content shown only inside a diagram retrieves the right page, and a manual upload of the same file and an Agent `knowledge_search` return the same result (one ingest path).

**Capability Tools**
- In Settings → Capability Tools, user disables "Painting". The Painting sidebar entry disappears. Start an Agent conversation and ask "generate an image of a cat" — Agent responds that image generation is not available (the tool is not in its tool list), rather than throwing an error.
- User enables OCR with local backend (PaddleOCR model installed). In an Agent conversation, user uploads a scanned PDF and says "extract the text from this document". Agent calls `ocr_recognize`, receives extracted text, and uses it in the response — same OCR quality as using the manual OCR button in the Knowledge Base upload flow.
- User enables Web Search (Tavily API). Agent is asked "what happened in tech news today" — Agent calls `web_search`, receives results, and answers with cited sources. The same Tavily API key from Capability Tools → Web Search config is used.
- Knowledge Base Agent tool verification: see #14905.

**Agent Chaining & Permissions**
- Agent chains two tools: user uploads a photo of a business card and says "find this person's company in my knowledge base". Agent calls `ocr_recognize` on the image, extracts the company name, then calls `knowledge_search` with that name — no manual intervention between steps.
- Admin creates Agent "Sales Bot" with allowed_tools excluding `knowledge_search`. Sales Bot cannot search the knowledge base even though the capability is enabled globally — the tool does not appear in its tool list.

**Dependency-Aware Orchestration**
- Agent calls `text_to_speech` but TTS requires a local Piper model that is not installed. Instead of a cryptic error, the user sees a notification: "TTS requires the Piper-zh voice model (45MB). Install now?" with an install button. After installation, user resends the message and Agent successfully generates audio.
- User enables Knowledge Base with local backend but has no embedding model installed. The Capability Tools panel shows an inline warning: "Requires an embedding model" with a link to the Local Models catalog, pre-filtered to the Embedding category.

**Unload Behavior**
- User disables all six capability tools. Agent conversations only have the base tools (Bash, Read, Write, etc.) — no capability tools appear. App memory usage is measurably lower than with all capabilities enabled.

## Related

title: [Feature]: Agent-Native Knowledge Library & File Manager
body:
## Background

Cherry Studio's knowledge base today is fully human-configured: users manually create knowledge bases, upload files, choose embedding models, and attach them to assistants. Agents cannot access knowledge bases at all, and there is no unified place to browse, filter, or organize the files that have been fed into the system. As agents become the primary way users interact with Cherry Studio, this human-only workflow creates friction — users must context-switch from an agent conversation to a separate settings page every time they want the agent to work with stored knowledge or uploaded documents.

## Goal

Users and agents share a unified Knowledge Library where agents can autonomously discover, retrieve, organize, and contribute knowledge and files — while users retain full visibility and control through an agent-native file manager that surfaces files by relevance to conversations and tasks rather than by manual folder hierarchy.

## Spec

- A new top-level **Knowledge Library** page aggregates all knowledge bases and their constituent files in one view, independent of the Resource Library (Assistants/Agents/Skills).
- Users can create, rename, and delete knowledge bases from this page; each knowledge base contains files with embedding status, source metadata, and tags.
- Agents can **retrieve** from any knowledge base they are granted access to during a conversation, without the user having to pre-attach it — the agent decides which knowledge bases are relevant based on the query.
- Agents can **write** to knowledge bases: when an agent determines that conversation content is durable and reusable (e.g., a user-provided specification, a research summary), it can autonomously add it as a new entry, with an inline notification shown to the user.
- Agents can **create and configure** new knowledge bases autonomously when a task warrants it (e.g., "research topic X and build me a knowledge base") — the user sees a confirmation prompt before the knowledge base is created.
- The file manager displays files primarily organized by **relevance to the current conversation or task context**, with secondary manual organization via tags and search. Manual folder hierarchy is not the default view.
- Users can filter files by: source type (uploaded document, web page, agent-generated), embedding status, tags, associated knowledge base, and date range.
- All agent actions on knowledge and files (create, write, delete) produce a visible audit trail in the conversation, so the user always knows what the agent did and can undo it.

## Verification

- User opens the Knowledge Library page → sees all existing knowledge bases listed with file counts and embedding progress; can search by name and filter by tag.
- In an agent conversation, user asks "what do our design guidelines say about button spacing?" without pre-attaching any knowledge base → agent autonomously searches across accessible knowledge bases, returns an answer citing the source document, and shows which knowledge base was queried.
- During a research task, agent finds a key technical specification in the conversation. Agent writes it to an existing knowledge base → user sees an inline notification: "Added 'WebSocket API spec' to knowledge base 'Backend Docs'". User clicks the notification to preview the entry and has an option to remove it.
- User tells agent: "Create a knowledge base from these 5 PDF files about regulatory compliance." Agent creates a new knowledge base, uploads the files, triggers embedding → user sees a confirmation dialog before creation proceeds, then sees embedding progress in the Knowledge Library.
- User opens file manager in the sidebar while in a conversation about "Q2 marketing plan" → files most relevant to marketing content surface at the top, ahead of unrelated technical documents, without the user manually navigating folders.
- User filters files by "agent-generated" source type → only entries that agents autonomously added appear; user selects three and bulk-deletes them → entries are removed from their respective knowledge bases.
- Agent autonomously deletes an outdated file from a knowledge base → conversation shows: "Removed 'v1-api-spec.md' from 'API Docs' (superseded by v2 spec)". User can undo via a button in the notification within 30 seconds.
- User revokes an agent's access to a specific knowledge base in settings → agent can no longer retrieve from or write to that knowledge base; attempts show a graceful message explaining the restriction.

title: [Feature]: Web Search — Auto Mode, Native Provider Coverage, and Default Plugin Cleanup
body:
## Background

Cherry Studio's web search has three problems today. (1) Multiple modern providers' native web search either isn't supported or is broken: Moonshot Kimi (#12861, #11253), Baidu ERNIE (#11958), Xiaomi MiMo (#14786), Qwen native DashScope mode (#10628), and Gemini's grounding stops working when the model is reached through an OpenAI-compatible channel (#10283). (2) The search-source dropdown forces users to pick a specific plugin per assistant — there's no "auto" mode where the model decides whether and how to search, and no convenient way to surface the model's own native search. (3) The bundled Google and Baidu webview plugins return uncurated, ad-heavy results that aren't useful, but still occupy slots in the dropdown.

## Goal

The model's own native web search is used by default whenever available, with a single search-button + dropdown control on the input box that exposes both the current model's native search and a curated set of external plugins.

## Spec

- The existing web search button in the input box continues to open a dropdown for selecting a source. The button's appearance is driven by what's selected in the dropdown:
  - **Nothing selected** → button in default (inactive) state. No search runs.
  - **Auto selected** → button shows the standard search icon in active/selected state.
  - **A specific source selected** (a provider's native or an external plugin) → button's icon changes to that source's icon, also in active state.
- Behavior driven by the same selection:
  - **Nothing selected** → no web search regardless of the prompt.
  - **Auto** → if the assistant's current model has a native web search capability, the request uses native search and lets the model decide whether to actually search. Otherwise the request uses Exa as the default external plugin in "model decides" mode where the plugin supports it.
  - **Specific source selected** → that source is forced on every turn. If it's the model's native option, the provider is asked to search every turn (e.g. Grok `search_parameters.mode = on`, DashScope `forced_search = true`). If it's an external plugin, that plugin runs unconditionally.
- The dropdown lists, in order: "Auto" (top, default for new assistants), the current model's single native search entry (only when the model supports native), then external plugins — Exa (default), Tavily, Bocha, Zhipu, Searxng, Bing, Querit. Google and Baidu webview-based plugins are removed.
- Native search is supported for these provider/model families with consistent citation rendering: Google Gemini, OpenAI, Anthropic Claude, xAI Grok, Moonshot Kimi, Alibaba DashScope (Qwen, native mode), Baidu Qianfan (ERNIE), Zhipu GLM, Xiaomi MiMo, Perplexity Sonar.
- Zhipu's dual role: when the assistant's model is GLM, Zhipu appears as the native entry in the dropdown; for other models Zhipu remains selectable as an external plugin.

## Verification

- Assistant model = **Gemini 2.x**, dropdown = Auto → button shows standard search icon in active state. Ask "What's the latest stable Cherry Studio version?" → response uses Gemini grounding with citations.
- Switch to **Kimi K2**, dropdown = "Kimi Search" (native) → button shows Kimi's icon, active. Even a non-search-shaped prompt triggers `$web_search`.
- Same **Kimi K2**, dropdown = Auto → button shows standard search icon. Ask "Explain quicksort" → Kimi does NOT trigger a search call (model decides).
- Click the active search button to deselect → button returns to default state; subsequent messages run no search.
- **Grok 4**, dropdown = Auto → maps to `search_parameters.mode = auto`; switch to "Grok Search" (native) → `mode = on`; deselect → `mode = off`.
- **Qwen3 in native DashScope mode**, dropdown = Auto → `enable_search: true, forced_search: false`; switch to "Qwen Search" (native) → `forced_search: true`; deselect → `enable_search: false`. Citations render in DashScope native mode (fixes #10628).
- **Baidu ERNIE**, dropdown = Auto → native search engages with citations (fixes #11958).
- **Xiaomi MiMo**, dropdown = Auto → native search works (fixes #14786).
- Gemini behind an OpenAI-compatible custom endpoint, dropdown = Auto → Gemini grounding still triggers and cites (fixes #10283).
- Model with no native (e.g. a small local model), dropdown = Auto → Exa is invoked.
- Model = **GLM-4** → dropdown shows: Auto, "Zhipu GLM Search" (native), Exa, Tavily, Bocha, Searxng, Bing, Querit. No Google or Baidu entries.
- Model = **OpenAI gpt-4o** → dropdown native entry shows "OpenAI Search"; Zhipu now appears in the external plugin section instead.
- Dropdown = Tavily, casual non-search prompt → Tavily runs unconditionally.

title: [Feature]: Cherry Studio Account System and Cross-Device Data Sync
body:
## Background

Cherry Studio currently has no first-party account system. Users who work across multiple devices (e.g. office Windows + home Mac) rely on WebDAV or S3 full-backup-and-restore to move data between machines. This approach suffers from frequent data overwrites when multiple clients back up to the same path (#1793), restoration failures when backup files exceed 512 MB (#12072), inability to merge changes from different devices (#10835), and the general friction of manually triggering backup/restore cycles. Users have repeatedly asked for account-based sync that "just works" (#12663 #10982 #12483 #12493), but no solution exists today. Meanwhile, Cherry Studio needs an account foundation to support upcoming value-added services — cloud storage, cloud VM, model services, and a credits system.

## Goal

Users can register a Cherry Studio account, log in across devices, and keep all their data — conversations, assistants, settings, API keys, and knowledge base — automatically synchronized, with an open-source sync server that can be self-hosted.

## Spec

- **Account system (Passport)**: Users can register and log in to a Cherry Studio account via the client. The Passport service first launches as a standalone web service (Express), then integrates into the desktop and mobile clients.
- **Credits and value-added services**: Each account has a credits balance. Credits unlock value-added services: cloud storage quota, cloud VM access, model API services, and model tools.
- **Full-scope sync**: After login, the following data categories sync across devices: conversations (topics + messages), assistant configurations, model provider and API key settings, app settings (general, display, data), and knowledge base entries.
- **Opt-in conversation cloud sync**: Conversation content upload to Cherry Studio's cloud is off by default. Users explicitly enable it in settings. When disabled, only configuration and metadata sync; conversations stay local.
- **Open-source sync server**: The multi-device sync server is released as an open-source project. Users who prefer to control their own data can deploy it on their own VPS and point their clients to it.
- **Incremental sync with conflict resolution**: Sync operates incrementally — only changed records are transmitted. When the same record is modified on two devices before syncing, the system resolves the conflict automatically (last-write-wins by timestamp, or per-field merge where feasible) without silently discarding either side's changes.
- **Offline resilience**: Changes made while offline queue locally and sync automatically when connectivity resumes. No data is lost due to temporary network unavailability.

## Verification

- User registers a Cherry Studio account on Device A (Mac), logs in, creates an assistant named "Code Reviewer" with custom prompt, and adds a CherryIN provider with API key. User logs into the same account on Device B (Windows) — "Code Reviewer" assistant and CherryIN provider with API key appear automatically without manual import.
- User has conversation cloud sync disabled (default). User chats with "Code Reviewer" on Device A. On Device B, the assistant config is visible but the conversation history is empty. User enables conversation cloud sync on both devices — the conversation from Device A appears on Device B.
- User modifies the same assistant's system prompt on Device A (offline) and Device B simultaneously. When Device A reconnects, sync completes and the assistant retains one coherent version — no data silently disappears, and no duplicate assistants are created.
- User deploys the open-source sync server on their own VPS and configures the client to use `https://my-sync.example.com`. All sync features work identically to the official cloud — account login, incremental sync, conversation opt-in.
- User disables conversation cloud sync after previously enabling it. Existing cloud-stored conversations are retained (not deleted), but no new conversation data is uploaded. A separate "delete cloud conversations" action is available if the user wants to purge.
- User's network drops mid-sync. After reconnection, queued changes sync without user intervention and without duplicating or corrupting records.
- On the Passport web portal, user tops up credits and subscribes to cloud storage. The client reflects the updated quota immediately after next sync.
- User with 50,000+ messages across 200+ topics enables conversation cloud sync for the first time. Initial sync completes progressively (not blocking the UI) and the user can continue chatting during sync.

## Related

title: [Feature]: Unified Notification Center
body:
## Background

Cherry Studio currently has no centralized place for users to see what happened while they were away. Reply-complete events, Agent task finishes, backup results, and token usage milestones all vanish silently — the user must keep watching the screen or miss them entirely. Version updates show a one-time dialog that is easy to dismiss and forget, and there is no channel for official announcements or community events to reach users inside the app. The existing notification infrastructure (NotificationService, toast, Ant Design alerts) handles transient pop-ups only — nothing is persisted, nothing is browsable, and nothing ties these disparate signals into a unified experience.

## Goal

Users have a single notification center that collects system events (reply complete, task finish, usage alerts), and official announcements (releases, events) into a persistent, browsable timeline with unread badges — so nothing important is missed even when the app is in the background.

## Spec

- A bell icon with an unread-count badge appears in the top navigation bar. Clicking it opens the notification center panel.
- The notification center shows a scrollable, chronological list of all notifications. Each entry displays a category icon, title, summary, timestamp, and read/unread state.
- Notifications are grouped into three categories, each with its own tab or filter:
  - **System**: reply complete, Agent task finish, message queue complete, backup success/failure, knowledge base embedding complete.
  - **Usage**: token consumption reaching user-defined thresholds (e.g., 80% of a daily budget), prompt cache about to expire, context window approaching model limit.
  - **Official**: new version available (pulled from GitHub Releases), official announcements and community events (pulled from a designated GitHub Discussions category or Releases notes).
- Each notification category can be independently enabled or disabled in Settings. System notifications are enabled by default; Usage and Official are enabled by default but individually toggleable.
- System and Usage notifications can optionally trigger an OS-level notification (sound + system toast) when the app is in the background. This is controlled by a per-category toggle in Settings, disabled by default.
- Official announcements support email notification as a future delivery channel — the notification center is designed as the in-app destination regardless of delivery method.
- Notifications persist locally and survive app restarts. A "Mark all as read" action and per-item dismiss are available. Notifications older than 30 days are automatically cleaned up.
- Clicking a notification navigates to the relevant context: a reply-complete notification opens that conversation, a usage alert opens the usage dashboard, an official announcement expands its full content inline.

## Verification

- Start a long Claude Sonnet response, switch to another app. After the reply finishes, the OS shows a system toast "Cherry Studio — Reply complete in [topic name]". Return to Cherry Studio → bell icon shows "1" badge. Open notification center → entry reads "Reply complete" with the topic name and timestamp. Click it → navigates to that conversation.
- Configure a daily token budget of 100k tokens in Settings. Send messages until cumulative usage reaches 80k → a "Usage" notification appears: "You've used 80% of your daily token budget (80k/100k)". Bell badge increments.
- A new GitHub Release is published for Cherry Studio. Next time the app checks for updates, an "Official" notification appears: "Cherry Studio vX.Y.Z is available" with release highlights pulled from the release notes. Click it → shows the full release notes inline, with an "Update Now" button.
- Open notification center with 15 unread notifications. Click "Mark all as read" → all entries show as read, bell badge disappears.
- Disable "System notifications" in Settings → no new system notifications appear in the notification center. Re-enable → new system events start appearing again (old ones from the disabled period are not retroactively generated).
- An Agent finishes a batch of 5 sequential tasks via the message queue → a single "Agent batch complete" notification appears (not 5 separate ones), summarizing "5 tasks completed in [topic name]".
- Leave the app untouched for 31 days, then open notification center → notifications older than 30 days are no longer visible.
- With "OS notification" toggle enabled for System category, minimize Cherry Studio and let a knowledge base embedding finish → OS notification appears with sound. With the toggle disabled → no OS notification, but the entry still appears in the notification center.
- Two conversations finish replies at the same time → two separate notifications appear in the center, each linking to its own conversation.
- Dismiss a single notification by clicking its close button → it disappears from the list and does not return.

title: [Feature]: Make File Paths and URLs in Assistant Output Clickable
body:
## Background

When the assistant tells a user where it just put a file ("PPT generated, saved to /Users/x/Desktop/DeepSeek_V4.pptx"), the path renders as inert plain text. To actually open the file, the user has to select the path, copy it, switch to a file manager, and paste — every single time. Web URLs in plain-text form behave the same way: visible but not actionable.

## Goal

File paths, folder paths, and web URLs in assistant output are clickable and open in the right app.

## Spec

- Absolute file and folder paths in assistant output (chat and agent) render as clickable elements. Clicking a folder path opens it in the OS file manager; clicking a file path reveals it in the file manager (selected) or opens it in the OS default app, with both options accessible.
- Web URLs in assistant output render as clickable links that open in the user's default browser, regardless of whether the URL is wrapped in markdown link syntax.
- Auto-detection covers common path shapes across macOS (`/Users/...`), Windows (`C:\...`), and Linux (`/home/...`), as well as `~`-prefixed home paths.
- Clicking a path that no longer exists shows a clear, named error stating that the file or folder is missing; no silent failure and no crash.
- Existing markdown link rendering, syntax highlighting, and code-block display are preserved; the new clickability does not introduce false positives inside code blocks.

## Verification

- Ask an agent to generate a file at a fixed path → the path in the response is clickable; on macOS, clicking reveals the file in Finder; on Windows, it opens File Explorer with the file selected; on Linux, the equivalent file manager action runs.
- Ask the assistant "where did you put it?" and have it answer with a folder path → clicking the folder opens it in the file manager.
- Paste an assistant message containing a plain-text URL (no markdown brackets) → the URL is clickable; click it → opens in the default browser.
- Manually delete a file referenced by a path in the chat, then click the path → user sees an error saying the file no longer exists; the app remains responsive.
- Open a code block that contains a path like `/Users/x/foo` → the path inside the code block is not auto-linked; copy-paste behavior is unchanged.
- Existing markdown links (`[label](url)`) → render and behave exactly as before.

title: [Feature]: MCP 2025-06-18 Compliance — Elicitation Support and Compatibility Fixes
body:
## Background

Cherry Studio's MCP integration has accumulated several reported gaps: server connections that complete the SSE handshake but never receive POST messages so the MCP session never opens (#13401); add/delete operations that leave the client and database out of sync (#14123); tool calls that ignore the auto-call setting and pop up confirmations anyway, hide which server is being called, and surface raw error codes instead of readable messages (#14095); conversations that stall on the "thinking" state even after the MCP tool returns successfully (#14077); and tool-call output rendered as `call:mcp__...` text that can't be collapsed (#14056). On top of these regressions, the MCP 2025-06-18 specification introduces Elicitation, which lets a server pause a workflow to ask the user for structured input — an absent capability that blocks safe interactive workflows on Cherry Studio (#9145). V2 is the moment to bring the integration end-to-end onto the current spec.

## Goal

Cherry Studio's MCP integration is compliant with the 2025-06-18 specification — including Elicitation — and free of the regressions tracked in the linked bug reports.

## Spec

- The MCP transport completes the spec-compliant handshake (initialize → notifications/initialized → tools/list) for any 2025-06-18-conformant server, including SSE-based servers that require POSTs after `endpoint`.
- Adding or removing an MCP server is atomic from the user's perspective: either the client connection and the persistent record both succeed, or neither does; partial state is not left behind on failure.
- Cherry Studio handles MCP elicitation requests per the 2025-06-18 spec; the user can respond with accept (submit data), decline, or cancel, and submitted data is validated against the server-provided schema before being returned.
- Servers that do not advertise elicitation behave exactly as today; no regression for existing MCP integrations.
- When auto-call is enabled for MCP tools, the user is not shown a manual confirmation dialog for each invocation; auto-call setting is honored consistently.
- The chat displays which MCP server and which tool a tool call is using, in the same place tool calls are surfaced for non-MCP tools.
- MCP tool errors are surfaced as readable, named messages explaining the cause, not as raw error codes or stack traces; the user can act on the message.
- The conversation continues normally after an MCP tool call returns successfully; the assistant does not stall on a "thinking" state once the tool result is delivered.
- MCP tool call rendering follows the same collapse / expand and visual style used by non-MCP tool calls; users can collapse MCP tool blocks the same way they collapse other tools.

## Verification

- Connect a 2025-06-18-conformant SSE-based MCP server; observe the handshake → initialize, notifications/initialized, and tools/list complete; the server reports an open session (#13401).
- Add an MCP server with the network momentarily unreachable so the client connection fails → no orphan database record is left behind; retry succeeds with a clean state. Repeat with the database write failing instead → no orphan client connection (#14123).
- Connect to a server that issues an elicitation request to confirm a destructive action; trigger the action → user responds accept → action proceeds; repeat with decline → server receives a refusal and the workflow halts visibly. Submit elicitation form with a required field empty → submission is rejected, request stays open until the user corrects it or cancels.
- Connect to an MCP server that does not use elicitation and run a representative tool call → behavior identical to current release.
- Enable auto-call for an MCP tool, have the assistant call it twice in a turn → no manual confirmation dialogs appear (#14095).
- During an MCP tool call, the chat shows the MCP server name and tool name in the same surface used by other tools (#14095).
- Force an MCP tool to return an error → the chat shows a readable explanation, not a raw code dump; the user can scroll back without UI breakage (#14095).
- Run a multi-step MCP workflow that invokes two different tools and finishes → the conversation does not get stuck in a "thinking" state after the last tool returns (#14077).
- Compare the rendering of an MCP tool call to a non-MCP tool call → both use the same collapse/expand affordance and visual style; the explicit `call:mcp__...` text representation does not appear (#14056).

title: [Feature]: Provider Gateway & CLI Config Sync
body:
## Background

Cherry Studio's Code module can launch 8 CLI coding tools with the right provider credentials injected at startup. But this only works when launching from Cherry Studio — users who open their own terminal must manually configure each tool. Each CLI tool uses a different config format (JSON, TOML, environment variables) with different field names, making multi-tool setup tedious and error-prone. When a provider goes down, every CLI tool fails independently with no recovery.

## Goal

Users configure providers once in Cherry Studio, and every CLI tool works correctly regardless of how it is launched — through persistent config sync and an optional intelligent gateway with failover.

## Spec

- Users can **sync** a provider to any CLI tool with one click. Cherry Studio writes the provider's credentials and endpoint into that tool's native config file, respecting its format. Managed entries use a namespace prefix so user-authored config is not overwritten.
- Before writing, a **diff preview** shows what will change. Users can confirm or cancel.
- **"Sync All"** updates every managed CLI tool at once. When a provider's API key or endpoint changes, one click propagates the change everywhere.
- Each CLI tool can be assigned a **different provider** — e.g., Claude Code uses CherryIN while Codex uses OpenAI direct.
- Users can optionally point CLI tools to Cherry Studio's **local gateway** instead of syncing credentials directly. The gateway provides:
  - **Protocol translation** — a tool sending OpenAI-format requests can be routed to an Anthropic-format provider transparently.
  - **Automatic failover** — when the active provider errors or times out, requests reroute to the next healthy provider without CLI tool restart.
  - **Circuit breaker** — after repeated failures a provider is temporarily skipped; health status is shown in the UI as green / yellow / red indicators.
- A **dashboard** in the Code Tools page shows each CLI tool's current provider, sync status, and gateway health at a glance.
- Users can **export** a provider config as YAML for tools or workflows not natively supported.

## Verification

- User selects CherryIN for Claude Code, clicks "Sync" → diff preview shows the config changes. User confirms → opens a fresh terminal, runs `claude` → Claude Code uses CherryIN without being launched from Cherry Studio.
- User selects OpenAI for Codex, clicks "Sync" → Codex's config file is updated. Existing non-Cherry entries (MCP servers, custom settings) remain untouched.
- User changes CherryIN's API key in Cherry Studio, clicks "Sync All" → all CLI tools reflect the new key immediately.
- User enables gateway mode for Claude Code. CherryIN goes down → gateway auto-routes to the backup provider with protocol translation. Claude Code continues working without interruption. Dashboard shows CherryIN in red, backup in green.
- CherryIN recovers → health indicator turns green; subsequent requests resume routing to CherryIN.
- User assigns Claude Code → CherryIN and Codex → OpenAI. Both tools send requests through the gateway simultaneously → each routes to its own provider with correct protocol.
- User exports provider config as YAML → file contains provider name, endpoint, and model list. Importable into a custom CI pipeline.
- All configured providers go down → gateway returns a clear error to the CLI tool; dashboard shows all providers in red with last-failure timestamps.

title: [Feature]: Agent Knowledge Base Tool — Enable Agents to Search RAG Knowledge Bases
body:
## Background

Cherry Studio has a fully functional Knowledge Base (RAG) system — users can create knowledge bases, index documents, and retrieve relevant chunks during conversations. However, this capability is only available through the Assistant workflow: an Assistant is manually assigned one or more knowledge bases in its settings, and retrieval happens implicitly during chat. Agents — which are far more capable at multi-step reasoning and tool orchestration — have no way to access the Knowledge Base at all. An Agent cannot search a user's indexed documents, cannot retrieve context from a knowledge base to answer questions, and cannot combine RAG results with other tool calls (e.g., OCR a document then search the knowledge base with the extracted text). Users who want RAG-powered answers must leave Agent mode entirely and use a manually configured Assistant instead.

## Goal

Agents can call the Knowledge Base as a first-class tool (`knowledge_search`) to query any of the user's knowledge bases and receive relevant document chunks with source citations — using the same retrieval pipeline that the Assistant workflow uses today.

## Spec

- A new Agent-callable tool `knowledge_search` is registered when the user has at least one knowledge base with indexed content. If no knowledge base exists or all are empty, the tool is not registered — Agents do not see it.
- The tool accepts a natural-language query and an optional knowledge base name/ID filter. When no filter is specified, the search runs across all knowledge bases the user has created.
- The tool returns ranked document chunks with: the matched text, a relevance score, the source document name, and the knowledge base name. The Agent uses these chunks as context to synthesize its response.
- The retrieval pipeline is identical to what the Assistant workflow uses — same embedding model, same vector search, same reranker (if configured). There is no separate retrieval path for Agents.
- Per-agent permissions apply: administrators can exclude `knowledge_search` from a specific Agent's allowed_tools, preventing that Agent from accessing the Knowledge Base even though the tool is globally available.
- The tool respects the user's existing Knowledge Base configuration (embedding model, chunk size, reranker settings) — no additional configuration is required to enable Agent access.

## Verification

- User has a knowledge base "Company Policies" with 20 indexed PDF documents. In an Agent conversation, user asks "what is our refund policy?" — Agent calls `knowledge_search` with the query, receives 3–5 relevant chunks from the policy documents, and synthesizes an answer citing the source document names.
- User has two knowledge bases: "Engineering Docs" and "HR Handbook". User asks the Agent "search HR Handbook for the parental leave policy" — Agent calls `knowledge_search` with the knowledge base filter set to "HR Handbook", and results come exclusively from that knowledge base.
- User asks the Agent "search my knowledge base for deployment procedures" but has no knowledge bases created — Agent does not attempt to call `knowledge_search` (the tool is not in its tool list) and responds that no knowledge base is available.
- Agent chains tools: user uploads a scanned contract image and says "find related clauses in my legal knowledge base". Agent calls `ocr_recognize` to extract text from the image, then calls `knowledge_search` with the extracted text as query — two tool calls in sequence, no manual intervention.
- Admin creates Agent "Public Bot" with allowed_tools excluding `knowledge_search`. Public Bot cannot search any knowledge base — the tool does not appear in its available tools, even though the user has knowledge bases with content.
- User changes the embedding model in Knowledge Base settings and re-indexes. The next Agent `knowledge_search` call uses the updated embeddings — no separate configuration needed for the Agent path.

title: [Feature]: Redesign Data Migration Progress UI with Real Progress Feedback
body:
## Background

When users change Cherry Studio's data storage path or upgrade from v1 to v2, the app copies all user data to the new location. During this process, users see a progress bar that shows fabricated percentages — the numbers increment randomly and have no relationship to actual bytes copied. For users with large data directories (multiple GB of knowledge bases, chat history, and attachments), this means staring at a fake progress bar with no ETA, no file count, no indication of what is being copied, and no way to know if the process is stuck or progressing. The confirmation flow before copying is also disjointed — up to three separate dialogs appear in sequence with no visual continuity, and the progress screen uses inline-styled components that look out of place with the rest of the v2 interface.

## Goal

Users see a polished, trustworthy data migration experience with real-time progress feedback (bytes copied, file count, current file, ETA), a unified confirmation-to-completion flow, and visual styling consistent with the v2 design system.

## Spec

- The migration progress screen shows **real** progress: percentage based on actual bytes copied vs. total bytes, number of files copied vs. total files, the name of the file currently being processed, and an estimated time remaining.
- The confirmation and progress steps are presented as a **single unified flow** (e.g., a multi-step panel or full-screen view) rather than a chain of separate pop-up dialogs. The user sees a clear progression: review source/destination → confirm → progress → done.
- During migration, the progress view is **non-dismissable** — users cannot accidentally close it or navigate away. A cancel button is available but requires explicit confirmation ("Canceling will leave your data in the original location. Cancel migration?").
- When migration completes successfully, the view transitions to a **completion state** showing a summary: total data size copied, number of files, time elapsed, and a single "Restart Now" button to apply the new data path.
- If migration fails mid-way, users see a clear **error state** with the specific failure reason (e.g., "Disk full — 2.1 GB required, 800 MB available"), the option to retry, and reassurance that the original data is untouched.
- The migration UI uses the v2 design system's visual language — consistent with the rest of the app's typography, colors, spacing, and component style. No inline-styled or visually inconsistent elements.

## Verification

- User has a 3 GB data directory with ~2,000 files. Initiates data path migration — progress bar shows percentage increasing in proportion to actual bytes (not random jumps), "1,247 / 2,003 files" counter updates in real time, the current filename scrolls as files are processed, and ETA counts down from an initial estimate (e.g., "~2 min remaining").
- User initiates migration on a 50 MB data directory — the entire flow (confirm → progress → done) stays within a single unified view. At no point do multiple overlapping modals appear.
- During a long migration (~5 min), user tries to close the app window — the window close is blocked and a warning appears: "Data migration in progress. Please wait for it to complete."
- Migration completes — completion screen shows "3.1 GB copied, 2,003 files, 2 min 34 sec elapsed" with a "Restart Now" button. No other action is required.
- User's target drive runs out of space at 60% progress — the progress view transitions to an error state: "Migration failed: insufficient disk space (need 1.2 GB more). Your original data is safe at [original path]." A "Retry" and "Cancel" button are shown.
- User clicks "Cancel" during an active migration — a confirmation prompt appears: "Canceling will stop the copy. Your original data remains at [original path]. Cancel migration?" On confirm, migration stops and the view returns to Settings with the original path still active.
- On first launch after v1→v2 upgrade, the migration flow appears as a full-screen welcome/upgrade view — not a small modal floating over a half-loaded app.
- The migration view's typography, button styles, and color palette are visually indistinguishable from other v2 settings pages — no elements look like they belong to a different design era.

title: [Feature]: PII Redaction via Local Models — Anonymize Sensitive User Data Before Sending to LLMs
body:
## Background

When users chat with cloud-hosted LLMs, their messages are sent verbatim to external servers — including any personal identifiable information (PII) they may have typed or pasted: national ID numbers, full names, phone numbers, home addresses, bank card numbers, email addresses, and more. Users working with contracts, medical records, HR documents, or financial data routinely paste content containing such information without realizing it will leave their device. Cherry Studio currently has no mechanism to detect or redact PII before transmission. Users who care about privacy must manually sanitize every message, which is error-prone and impractical for long documents.

## Goal

Users can enable a PII redaction capability — powered by a local model from the plugin system's Local Models tier — that automatically detects and masks sensitive personal information (ID numbers, names, phone numbers, addresses, etc.) in outgoing messages before they reach the cloud LLM, with no sensitive data ever leaving the device.

## Spec

- A new "PII Redaction" capability is available in Settings → Capability Tools (as part of the pluggable capability system, #14895). It has a master enable/disable toggle and runs entirely on-device using a local NER/PII model from the Local Models tier.
- When enabled, every outgoing user message is passed through the local PII detection model **before** being sent to the cloud LLM. Detected PII entities are replaced with type-tagged placeholders (e.g., "张三" → `[NAME_1]`, "310101199001011234" → `[ID_NUMBER_1]`, "13812345678" → `[PHONE_1]`, "北京市朝阳区XX路XX号" → `[ADDRESS_1]`).
- Supported PII categories at minimum: person names, national ID numbers, phone numbers, home/office addresses, email addresses, bank card numbers. Additional categories (passport numbers, license plates, medical record numbers) can be extended via the local model's capabilities.
- The LLM receives only the redacted message. When the LLM's response references a placeholder (e.g., "The holder of [ID_NUMBER_1] should..."), the placeholder is **restored** to the original value in the displayed response — so the user sees the real data in the conversation UI, but it was never transmitted.
- Users can preview the redacted version before sending: a visual indicator (e.g., a shield icon on the input bar) shows that PII redaction is active, and clicking it reveals which entities were detected and masked, allowing the user to override specific detections.
- PII redaction applies to user-typed messages, pasted text, and text extracted from uploaded documents. File attachments (images, PDFs) sent directly to multimodal models are **not** redacted by this feature (that would require OCR + redaction, tracked separately).
- All PII detection and placeholder mapping runs locally — the mapping table (placeholder ↔ original value) is held only in memory for the duration of the conversation and is never persisted to disk or transmitted externally.

## Verification

- User enables PII Redaction and has installed a local NER model (e.g., PII-detector-zh, 80MB). User types: "帮我写一封信给张三，身份证号310101199001011234，电话13812345678，住在北京市朝阳区建国路88号。" — the message sent to the LLM contains: "帮我写一封信给[NAME_1]，身份证号[ID_NUMBER_1]，电话[PHONE_1]，住在[ADDRESS_1]。" The user's conversation UI shows the original text with a small shield badge indicating redaction was applied.
- LLM responds: "Dear [NAME_1], regarding your ID [ID_NUMBER_1]..." — the displayed response in the conversation shows: "Dear 张三, regarding your ID 310101199001011234..." with placeholders seamlessly restored.
- User clicks the shield icon on the input bar before sending — a dropdown shows: "Detected: 张三 (Name), 310101199001011234 (ID Number), 13812345678 (Phone), 北京市朝阳区建国路88号 (Address)" with toggles to exclude specific items from redaction. User untogles "张三" — the name is sent in cleartext while other PII remains masked.
- User pastes a 2-page employment contract containing 5 names, 3 ID numbers, and 4 phone numbers — all are detected and masked within 1–2 seconds (local model inference). The shield icon shows "12 PII entities detected".
- User sends a message with no PII (e.g., "explain quantum computing") — the message is sent unmodified, no redaction applied, shield icon shows "No PII detected".
- PII Redaction is enabled but the required local model is not installed — the capability shows an inline warning: "Requires PII detection model (80MB). Install now?" Sending messages proceeds without redaction until the model is installed.
- User starts a new conversation — the placeholder mapping from the previous conversation is gone. Previous conversation's placeholders cannot be reverse-mapped, ensuring no cross-conversation PII leakage.
- User disables PII Redaction in settings — messages are sent verbatim to the LLM, no detection or masking occurs, shield icon disappears from the input bar.

title: [Bug]: OpenCode fails when provider name contains non-ASCII characters
body:
### Issue Checklist

- [x] I understand that issues are for feedback and problem solving, not for complaining in the comment section, and will provide as much information as possible to help solve the problem.
- [x] My issue is not listed in the [FAQ](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/issues/3881).

- [x] I've filled in short, clear headings so that developers can quickly identify a rough idea of what to expect when flipping through the list of issues.
- [x] I've confirmed that I am using the latest version of Cherry Studio.

### Platform

Linux

### Version

v1.9.4

### Bug Description

When a provider is named with non-ASCII characters (e.g. Chinese, Japanese, Korean, emoji, etc.), Cherry Studio generates an invalid environment variable name for OpenCode, causing a bash error:

```
bash: line 1: export: `OPENCODE_API_KEY_测试=sk-xxxx': not a valid identifier
```

Bash environment variable names only allow `[a-zA-Z0-9_]`. The `sanitizeProviderName` function in `src/renderer/src/utils/naming.ts` only handles spaces and some special characters, but does not strip non-ASCII characters.

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Go to Settings → Model Provider
2. Add a new provider with a non-ASCII name, e.g. "测试"
3. Configure an API key for this provider
4. Open a code tool (OpenCode) that uses this provider
5. See the bash export error

### Expected Behavior

Cherry Studio should sanitize the provider name to produce a valid bash environment variable identifier. Non-ASCII characters should be removed, and if the result is empty (pure non-ASCII name), a deterministic hash-based fallback should be used (e.g. `p_xxxxx` → `OPENCODE_API_KEY_P_XXXXX`).

### Relevant Log Output

```shell
bash: line 1: export: `OPENCODE_API_KEY_测试=sk-xxxx': not a valid identifier
```

### Additional Context

The fix is in `sanitizeProviderName()` at `src/renderer/src/utils/naming.ts`. The function needs to strip non-ASCII characters before constructing the env var name. A hash fallback ensures pure non-ASCII names still produce a valid identifier.

> [\!NOTE] > This issue was translated by Claude. ### Issue Checklist - [x] I understand that issues are for reporting problems and requesting features, not for off-topic comments, and I will provide as much detail as possible to help resolve the issue. - [x] I have checked the pinned issues and searched through the existing [open issues](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/issues), [closed issues](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20state%3Aclosed), and [discussions](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/discussions) and did not find a similar suggestion. - [x] I have provided a short and descriptive title so that developers can quickly understand the issue when browsing the issue list, rather than vague titles like "A suggestion" or "Stuck." - [x] The latest version of Cherry Studio does not include the feature I am suggesting. ### Platform Windows ### Version v1.9.4 ### Is your feature request related to an existing issue? When configuring DeepSeek V4 from the OpenCode Go package in Agent mode (regardless of whether the model ID is written as `deepseek-v4-flash` or `opencode-go/deepseek-v4-flash`), an error occurs when starting the agent: `Process failed after 0 turns` The underlying error shows: `Claude Code returned an error result: There's an issue with the selected model` **Root cause:** The Agent system uses the Claude Code agent loop underneath, and Claude Code only recognizes Anthropic protocol models. The same DeepSeek V4 (OpenAI compatible protocol) works completely fine in normal chat mode and can conduct conversations normally. **Conclusion:** Cherry Studio's Agent functionality is hard-coded to bind with the Claude Code agent engine, which only supports tool calling (function calling/tool use) for Anthropic protocol models. Any OpenAI compatible protocol models (including DeepSeek, Qwen, GLM, etc.) cannot be used in Agent mode, even though they work perfectly in chat mode. ### Desired Solution I hope to remove the Agent's restriction on model protocols, or make the upper-layer AI SDK compatible with OpenAI format tool calling protocols, so that non-Anthropic models can also use the full Agent functionality (web search, file operations, code execution, etc.). ### Alternative Solutions _No response_ ### Additional Information _No response_ ---

### Platform

Windows

### Version

v1.9.4

### Bug Description

When using Jina AI as the reranking provider in the Knowledge Base feature, Cherry Studio sends the model name as `jina-ai/jina-reranker-v3` instead of `jina-reranker-v3`. The Jina Rerank API (`https://api.jina.ai/v1/rerank`) does not accept the `jina-ai/` prefix and returns an HTTP 422 Unprocessable Entity error.

The API response explicitly states:
> Input tag 'jina-ai/jina-reranker-v3' found using 'model' does not match any of the expected tags: 'jina-reranker-v2-base-multilingual', 'jina-reranker-v1-tiny-en', 'jina-reranker-v1-turbo-en', 'jina-reranker-v1-base-en', 'jina-colbert-v1-en', 'jina-colbert-v2', 'jina-reranker-m0', 'jina-reranker-v3'

The model name field is not editable in the UI, so there is no workaround available to the user.

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Go to Settings → Model Provider → Jina and add your Jina API key.
2. Create a new Knowledge Base.
3. Select an embedding model (e.g., Mistral) and select `jina-reranker-v3` as the reranking model from Jina.
4. Add documents to the Knowledge Base and let them be indexed.
5. Open a chat, attach the Knowledge Base, and send any message.
6. The reranking step fails with the following error:

```
Error: Error invoking remote method 'knowledge-base:rerank': Error: Rerank request failed: HTTP 422: Unprocessable Entity
```

### Expected Behavior

Cherry Studio should send the model name as `jina-reranker-v3` (without the `jina-ai/` prefix) in the request body to the Jina Rerank API, matching the format that the API expects. The reranking step should complete successfully and return ranked results.

title: [Bug]: OpenCode built-in auto-update conflicts with Cherry Studio's update mechanism
body:

- [x] My issue is not listed in the [FAQ](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/issues/3881).

- [x] I've filled in short, clear headings so that developers can quickly identify a rough idea of what to expect when flipping through the list of issues. And not "a suggestion", "stuck", etc.
- [x] I've confirmed that I am using the latest version of Cherry Studio.

### Platform

Windows, macOS, Linux

### Version

v1.9.4

### Bug Description

OpenCode has a built-in auto-update check (`checkUpgrade()`) that runs 1 second after TUI startup. Cherry Studio installs OpenCode via `bun install -g` to `~/.cherrystudio/`, but the OpenCode process does not have `BUN_INSTALL` pointing to that path at runtime. As a result, OpenCode detects its install method as `"unknown"`.

When a **minor or major** update is available, OpenCode shows an "Update Available" dialog. If the user confirms the upgrade, it will always fail because the `"unknown"` install method has no upgrade strategy.

This conflicts with Cherry Studio's own `autoUpdateToLatest` update mechanism, which already handles OpenCode updates correctly via `bun install -g`.

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Install OpenCode via Cherry Studio's Code Tools page
2. Wait for OpenCode to release a new minor/major version
3. Launch OpenCode from Cherry Studio
4. After ~1 second, OpenCode shows an "Update Available" dialog
5. Confirm the upgrade → upgrade fails

### Expected Behavior

OpenCode should not show its built-in update dialog when launched from Cherry Studio, since Cherry Studio manages updates through its own `autoUpdateToLatest` mechanism.

### Relevant Log Output

```shell
N/A
```

### Additional Context

OpenCode supports the `OPENCODE_DISABLE_AUTOUPDATE=true` environment variable to disable its built-in update check. The fix is to set this env var in `generateToolEnvironment()` when launching OpenCode.
