title: [Bug] Claude Code Agent: cwd not set to accessible_paths – project folder not being used
body:
> [\!NOTE]
> This issue was translated by Claude.

## Description

When a Claude Code agent is started with a configured `accessible_paths` project folder, the working directory (`cwd`) of the Claude Code process is **not** set to this path. Instead, `cwd` remains in the agent's own directory under `Data/Agents/<agent-id>/`.

As a result, Claude Code cannot find the actual project and cannot work on it.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Cherry Studio → Create agent with type **Claude Code**
2. Configure path e.g. `F:\Codex\RSS_Reader_Android` as project folder
3. Start the agent
4. Check the `cwd` of the Claude Code process

## Expected Behavior

`cwd` = `F:\Codex\RSS_Reader_Android` (the path configured in `accessible_paths`)

## Actual Behavior

`cwd` = `C:\Users\<User>\AppData\Roaming\CherryStudio\Data\Agents\<agent-id>` (agent's own directory)

## Database Evidence

In `agents.db`, the path is correctly stored:
```
SELECT id, name, accessible_paths FROM agents WHERE id = 'agent_<id>'
→ RSS_Reader_Android | ["F:\\Codex\\RSS_Reader_Android"]
```

## Impact

- Claude Code cannot find the project in the `cwd`
- File operations (Read, Glob, Grep) fail or search in the wrong directory
- Project Git remote is not recognized
- The agent works essentially blind

## Environment

- **OS:** Windows 11
- **Cherry Studio Version:** (current, Claude Code Bridge 2.1.70)
- **Agent Type:** Claude Code

## Suspected Cause

`accessible_paths` is likely only treated as access permission, but not passed as a `--cwd` parameter when starting the Claude Code process.

---
<details>
<summary>Original Content</summary>

## Beschreibung

Wenn ein Claude-Code-Agent mit einem konfigurierten `accessible_paths`-Projektordner gestartet wird, wird das Arbeitsverzeichnis (`cwd`) des Claude-Code-Prozesses **nicht** auf diesen Pfad gesetzt. Stattdessen bleibt `cwd` im Agent-eigenen Verzeichnis unter `Data/Agents/<agent-id>/`.

Dadurch findet Claude Code das eigentliche Projekt nicht und kann nicht darauf arbeiten.

## Reproduktion

1. Cherry Studio → Agent mit Typ **Claude Code** anlegen
2. Pfad z. B. `F:\Codex\RSS_Reader_Android` als Projektordner konfigurieren
3. Agent starten
4. `cwd` des Claude-Code-Prozesses prüfen

## Erwartetes Verhalten

`cwd` = `F:\Codex\RSS_Reader_Android` (der in `accessible_paths` konfigurierte Pfad)

## Tatsächliches Verhalten

`cwd` = `C:\Users\<User>\AppData\Roaming\CherryStudio\Data\Agents\<agent-id>` (Agent-Eigenes-Verzeichnis)

## Datenbank-Beleg

In `agents.db` ist der Pfad korrekt gespeichert:
```
SELECT id, name, accessible_paths FROM agents WHERE id = 'agent_<id>'
→ RSS_Reader_Android | ["F:\\Codex\\RSS_Reader_Android"]
```

## Auswirkung

- Claude Code kann das Projekt nicht im `cwd` finden
- Dateioperationen (Read, Glob, Grep) scheitern oder suchen im falschen Verzeichnis
- Projekt-Git-Remote wird nicht erkannt
- Der Agent arbeitet quasi blind

## Umgebung

- **OS:** Windows 11
- **Cherry Studio Version:** (aktuelle, Claude Code Bridge 2.1.70)
- **Agent-Typ:** Claude Code

## Vermutete Ursache

`accessible_paths` wird vermutlich nur als Zugriffsberechtigung behandelt, aber beim Start des Claude-Code-Prozesses nicht als `--cwd`-Parameter übergeben.

</details>

title: [Bug] Task list in UI does not sync with actual progress of Claude Code Agent
body:
> [\!NOTE]
> This issue was translated by Claude.

## Description

The task list above the input field in the CherryStudio UI shows an outdated status and does not synchronize with the actual progress of the Claude Code Agent.

Specifically: The Agent reports "all tasks completed", but the UI continues to show open tasks (2/4 instead of 5/5).

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Start Claude Code Agent
2. Define multiple tasks (e.g. via `TodoWrite` tool)
3. Agent works through all tasks and marks them as `completed`
4. After completion: UI continues to show incomplete list

## Expected Behavior

CherryStudio UI recognizes `TodoWrite` status changes from the Agent and updates the task list in real time.

## Actual Behavior

The UI task list remains at an earlier status (e.g. 2/4) and does not show the final status (5/5).

## Additional: Counting Discrepancy

The Agent manages 5 task steps internally (Build + 3 Lint fixes + Check), but communicates 3 logical tasks to the user. The UI should display the same number of tasks that the Agent actually manages.

## Environment

- **OS:** Windows 11
- **Cherry Studio Version:** latest (Claude Code Bridge 2.1.70)
- **Agent Type:** Claude Code

## Impact

- User sees incorrect task status
- Confusion about actual project progress
- Loss of trust in the UI display

---
<details>
<summary>Original Content</summary>

## Beschreibung

Die Aufgabenliste oberhalb des Eingabefelds in der CherryStudio-UI zeigt einen veralteten Stand an und synchronisiert nicht mit dem tatsächlichen Fortschritt des Claude-Code-Agenten.

Konkret: Der Agent meldet „alle Aufgaben abgeschlossen", die UI zeigt aber weiterhin offene Tasks an (2/4 statt 5/5).

## Reproduktion

1. Claude-Code-Agent starten
2. Mehrere Aufgaben definieren lassen (z. B. via `TodoWrite`-Tool)
3. Agent arbeitet alle Aufgaben ab und markiert sie als `completed`
4. Nach Abschluss: UI zeigt weiterhin inkomplette Liste

## Erwartetes Verhalten

CherryStudio-UI erkennt `TodoWrite`-Statusänderungen des Agenten und aktualisiert die Aufgabenliste in Echtzeit.

## Tatsächliches Verhalten

Die UI-Aufgabenliste bleibt auf einem früheren Stand stehen (z. B. 2/4) und zeigt nicht den finalen Status (5/5) an.

## Zusätzlich: Zählungs-Differenz

Der Agent verwaltet intern 5 Aufgaben-Schritte (Build + 3 Lint-Fixes + Prüfung), kommuniziert an den Nutzer aber 3 logische Aufgaben. Die UI müsste dieselbe Anzahl an Aufgaben anzeigen, die der Agent auch tatsächlich verwaltet.

## Umgebung

- **OS:** Windows 11
- **Cherry Studio Version:** aktuell (Claude Code Bridge 2.1.70)
- **Agent-Typ:** Claude Code

## Auswirkung

- Nutzer sieht falschen Aufgabenstatus
- Verwirrung über tatsächlichen Projektfortschritt
- Vertrauensverlust in die UI-Anzeige

</details>

### Platform

v1.9.4

## Feature Description

Cherry Studio is a leading free software for leveraging AI technologies. However, as the number of responses within a single Cherry Studio session grows, it becomes increasingly difficult to locate specific pieces of information. To facilitate the precise retrieval of information, I propose a new feature enabled by developers that allows referencing conversations, prompts, and responses as linked entities.

**Concept: What are "Links"?**  
Just as PDF viewers like *evince* allow opening a specific page by index, or how Firefox can open specific URLs, I propose adding a command-line option to Cherry Studio to open specific conversations, prompts, or responses.

**Implementation Proposal**  
To implement this, developers should introduce the following capabilities:

*   **Right-click "Copy Conversation ID":** Add this option to the context menu in the conversation list (typically located on the left sidebar).
*   **Right-click "Copy Entry ID":** Add this option to the context menu for individual prompts or responses.
*   **Unique UUIDs:** Each generated ID should be a unique UUID to ensure accurate referencing.

**User Workflow**  
When a user wishes to open Cherry Studio to a specific prompt, conversation, or response, they can invoke the application via the shell using:

```bash
CherryStudio --entry-uuid <UUID>
```

Upon execution, Cherry Studio should:
1.  Bring itself to the foreground of the screen.
2.  Focus on the specific entry identified by the UUID.

**Benefits**  
This feature enables users to create new URIs that can be opened directly from other applications, effectively creating full hyperlinks. This integration extends beyond Cherry Studio to other applications such as web browsers, spreadsheets, Emacs, command-line interfaces, and other knowledge bases.

### Desired Solution

**Proposed Behavior**

1.  **ID Generation & Copying:**
    *   Developers should ensure that every Conversation, Prompt, and Response is assigned a unique, stable UUID.
    *   The UI should expose a "Copy ID" option via right-click context menus:
        *   **Conversation List:** Right-clicking a conversation name offers "Copy Conversation ID".
        *   **Content Area:** Right-clicking a specific prompt bubble or response area offers "Copy Prompt/Response ID".

2.  **Command Line Invocation:**
    *   The application must accept the `--entry-uuid <UUID>` argument.
    *   **Behavior:** When invoked with this flag:
        *   If Cherry Studio is closed, it launches.
        *   If Cherry Studio is running but hidden/backgrounded, it moves to the foreground.
        *   The UI automatically navigates to the specific entry identified by the UUID.
        *   If the ID corresponds to a conversation, that conversation is selected. If it is a specific prompt/response, the UI should scroll to and highlight that specific entry within the conversation.

3.  **URI Scheme Integration (Optional but Recommended):**
    *   Ideally, map the UUID to a custom URI scheme (e.g., `cherrystudio://open?uuid=<UUID>`) so that browsers and other apps can trigger this command natively.

**Visual Mockup Idea**
*   **Context Menu:** A standard right-click menu with a new divider and the option "Copy Entry UUID".
*   **Navigation:** When the command executes, the left sidebar highlights the correct conversation, and the main chat view scrolls to the specific message, potentially with a subtle highlight effect to indicate the jump location.

**用户工作流**
当用户希望打开 Cherry Studio 并定位到特定的提示词、对话或回复时，可以通过 Shell 调用应用程序：

```bash
CherryStudio --entry-uuid <UUID>
```

执行后，Cherry Studio 应：
1.  将自身置于屏幕最前端。
2.  聚焦并显示由 UUID 标识的特定条目。

**收益**
此功能使用户能够创建可以从其他应用程序直接打开的新 URI，从而实现完整的超链接功能。这种集成不仅限于 Cherry Studio 内部，还可以扩展到其他应用程序，如 Web 浏览器、电子表格、Emacs、命令行界面以及其他知识库。

### Desired Solution

**Proposed Behavior**

1.  **ID Generation & Copying:**
    *   Developers should ensure that every Conversation, Prompt, and Response is assigned a unique, stable UUID.
    *   The UI should expose a "Copy ID" option via right-click context menus:
        *   **Conversation List:** Right-clicking a conversation name offers "Copy Conversation ID".
        *   **Content Area:** Right-clicking a specific prompt bubble or response area offers "Copy Prompt/Response ID".

2.  **Command Line Invocation:**
    *   The application must accept the `--entry-uuid <UUID>` argument.
    *   **Behavior:** When invoked with this flag:
        *   If Cherry Studio is closed, it launches.
        *   If Cherry Studio is running but hidden/backgrounded, it moves to the foreground.
        *   The UI automatically navigates to the specific entry identified by the UUID.
        *   If the ID corresponds to a conversation, that conversation is selected. If it is a specific prompt/response, the UI should scroll to and highlight that specific entry within the conversation.

3.  **URI Scheme Integration (Optional but Recommended):**
    *   Ideally, map the UUID to a custom URI scheme (e.g., `cherrystudio://open?uuid=<UUID>`) so that browsers and other apps can trigger this command natively.

**Visual Mockup Idea**
*   **Context Menu:** A standard right-click menu with a new divider and the option "Copy Entry UUID".
*   **Navigation:** When the command executes, the left sidebar highlights the correct conversation, and the main chat view scrolls to the specific message, potentially with a subtle highlight effect to indicate the jump location.

***

**预期行为**

1.  **ID 生成与复制：**
    *   开发者应为每个对话、提示词和回复分配唯一且稳定的 UUID。
    *   UI 应通过右键上下文菜单暴露"复制 ID"选项：
        *   **对话列表：** 右键点击对话名称时，提供"复制对话 ID"选项。
        *   **内容区域：** 右键点击特定的提示词气泡或回复区域时，提供"复制提示词/回复 ID"选项。

2.  **命令行调用：**
    *   应用程序必须接受 `--entry-uuid <UUID>` 参数。
    *   **行为逻辑：** 当带有此参数调用时：
        *   如果 Cherry Studio 已关闭，则启动应用。
        *   如果 Cherry Studio 正在运行但处于后台/隐藏状态，则将其移至前台。
        *   UI 自动导航至由 UUID 标识的特定条目。
        *   如果 ID 对应的是对话，则选中该对话；如果是对特定的提示词/回复，UI 应滚动至该条目并高亮显示，以指示跳转位置。

3.  **URI 协议集成（可选但推荐）：**
    *   理想情况下，将 UUID 映射到自定义 URI 方案（例如 `cherrystudio://open?uuid=<UUID>`），以便浏览器和其他应用程序能够原生触发此命令。

- [x] I've confirmed that I am using the latest version of Cherry Studio.

### Platform

Windows

### Version

v1.9.4

### Bug Description

On Windows, country flag emojis (🇨🇳, 🇺🇸, 🇬🇧, etc.) display with visible white or black borders around each flag glyph. This affects all UI locations where flag emojis are shown, including the language selector in General Settings, translate language dropdowns, spell check language options, OCR language displays, and message menubar translate options.

**Root Cause:**

Chromium/Electron on Windows uses Segoe UI Emoji to render Regional Indicator characters. This system font renders flag codepoints (U+1F1E6–1F1FF) with inherent black/white borders. System-level color emoji rendering takes priority over CSS `font-family` declarations, so pure font replacement approaches (e.g., Twemoji Country Flags woff2 with `unicode-range`) cannot fully override the system font rendering.

**Attempted fix that didn't work:**

Applying `className="country-flag-font"` with `font-family: 'Twemoji Country Flags'` to all flag emoji spans. The Twemoji font does load and renders colored flags, but the underlying Segoe UI Emoji border artifact persists through the COLR/CPAL rendering pipeline. CSS-based workarounds like `clip-path: inset()` are DPI-dependent and not generalizable across display scaling configurations.

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Run Cherry Studio on Windows 10/11
2. Go to Settings → General → Language dropdown
3. Observe the country flag emojis — each flag has a visible white or black border around it
4. The same issue appears in any dropdown or UI element displaying country flag emojis (translate settings, OCR language settings, message translate menu, etc.)

### Expected Behavior

Country flag emojis should render cleanly without any visible border or outline, matching how they appear on macOS/Linux.

### Relevant Log Output

_No response_

### Additional Context

A fix is available that replaces font-based rendering with SVG images from the `flag-icons` package on Windows only, while keeping native emoji rendering on other platforms.

This seems to be a Windows command resolution issue when launching MCP servers. ### Context - OS: Windows 11 - Node.js: 24.15.0 - npm/npx: installed and available in PATH - Shell tests pass in both Command Prompt and PowerShell cmd: ``` C:\Users\xiaoy>node -v v24.15.0 C:\Users\xiaoy>npx -v 11.12.1 C:\Users\xiaoy>where npx D:\nodejs\npx D:\nodejs\npx.cmd ``` pwsh: ``` Get-Command npx -All CommandType Name Version Source ----------- ---- ------- ------ ExternalScript npx.ps1 D:\nodejs\npx.ps1 Application npx.cmd 0.0.0.0 D:\nodejs\npx.cmd Application npx 0.0.0.0 D:\nodejs\npx ``` So npx is clearly installed and available in PATH. title: [Feature]: Support Global System Prompt Configuration for Agents
body:
> [\!NOTE]
> This issue was translated by Claude.

### Issue Checklist

- [x] I understand that issues are for reporting problems and requesting features.
- [x] I have searched existing / closed issues and discussions, and did not find a similar suggestion.
- [x] I have provided a short and descriptive title.
- [x] The latest version of Cherry Studio does not include the feature I am suggesting.

### Platform

Linux

### Version

v1.9.4

### Is your feature request related to an existing issue?

Currently, each Agent's System Prompt in Cherry Studio is configured independently, with no way to inherit a unified "base prompt". When users have multiple Agents that share similar base rules (e.g., consistent language style, reply format, safety guidelines, output standards, etc.), they need to repeat the same content in each Agent, leading to the following pain points:

1. **Repetitive work**: Every time a new Agent is created, the common parts must be copied and pasted
2. **Maintenance difficulty**: When common rules need adjustment, each Agent must be modified individually
3. **Easy to miss**: When creating a new Agent, some common instructions may be forgotten
4. **Inconsistency risk**: Manual copying can easily lead to version inconsistencies

### Desired Solution

It is recommended to provide a "Global Common System Prompt" mechanism, primarily promoting the following combination of solutions:

**Solution A: Global Default Agent Prompt**
- Add a "Global Default System Prompt" configuration option in "Settings → Agent"
- Automatically inject as a prefix when creating a new Agent
- Individual Agents can choose to enable/override this global prompt

**Solution B: Prompt Snippet Reference / Include Mechanism**
- Support referencing external prompt snippets in Agent System Prompt via syntax like `@common-rules.md`
- After modifying a snippet, all Agents referencing that snippet automatically take effect
- Support combining multiple snippets

Both solutions can coexist: Solution A addresses "global unification", Solution B addresses "reuse modularity".

### Alternative Solutions

**Solution C: Agent Grouping + Group-level Common Prompts**
- Support Agent grouping (similar to folders)
- Each group can set "group-level common prompts"
- All Agents in the group automatically inherit

**Solution D: Prompt Snippet Library**
- Provide an independent "Prompt Snippet Management" page
- Users maintain reusable snippets
- When creating a new Agent, multiple snippets can be selected and combined

**Current Workaround (poor user experience)**:
- Copy existing Agent and modify the differences (high maintenance cost)
- Store common prompts in "Quick Phrases" and manually insert them (requires manual operation each time)

### Additional Information

**Reference Implementations**:
- Claude Code's `CLAUDE.md` (project-level global instructions, automatically injected)
- Cursor's `.cursorrules` (project root directory rule file)
- ChatGPT's Custom Instructions (account-level global instructions)
- Common "system prompt layering" pattern in Anthropic Claude API

**Typical Use Cases**:
- Users create separate Agents for different roles (programmer / product manager / copywriter), but all need common rules like "always reply in Chinese", "do not output sensitive information", "confirm requirements before answering"
- When sharing Agents within a team, want a unified "company messaging standards" prefix
- All Agents follow a unified output format (e.g., list key points first, then expand)

**Priority Recommendation**: Medium-High — A common need for multi-Agent users. Similar mechanisms have been provided in other AI products (Claude Code / Cursor / ChatGPT).

目前 Cherry Studio 中每个 Agent 的 System Prompt 都是独立配置的，无法继承一个统一的「基础提示词」。当用户拥有多个 Agent 且这些 Agent 共享部分相似的基础规则时（例如：统一的语言风格、回复格式、安全准则、输出规范等），需要在每个 Agent 中重复编写相同内容，存在以下痛点：

1. **重复劳动**：每次新建 Agent 都要复制粘贴公共部分
2. **维护困难**：当公共规则需要调整时，需要逐个 Agent 修改
3. **容易遗漏**：新建 Agent 时可能忘记加上某些公共指令
4. **不一致风险**：手动复制容易出现版本不一致

### Desired Solution

建议提供「全局公共 System Prompt」机制，主推以下两种方案的组合：

**方案 A：全局默认 Agent 提示词**
- 在「设置 → Agent」中增加「全局默认 System Prompt」配置项
- 新建 Agent 时自动作为前缀注入
- 单个 Agent 可选择是否启用 / 覆盖该全局提示词

**方案 B：提示词片段引用 / Include 机制**
- 支持在 Agent System Prompt 中通过类似 `@common-rules.md` 的语法引用外部提示词片段
- 修改片段后，所有引用该片段的 Agent 自动生效
- 支持组合多个片段

两种方案可以并存：方案 A 解决「全局统一」，方案 B 解决「复用模块化」。

### Alternative Solutions

**方案 C：Agent 分组 + 组级公共提示词**
- 支持 Agent 分组（类似文件夹）
- 每个组可设置「组级公共提示词」
- 组内所有 Agent 自动继承

**方案 D：提示词片段库（Prompt Snippet Library）**
- 提供独立的「提示词片段管理」页面
- 用户维护可复用的片段
- 新建 Agent 时可勾选多个片段组合

**当前变通方案（用户体验不佳）**：
- 复制现有 Agent 后修改差异部分（维护成本高）
- 用「快捷短语」存公共提示词后手动插入（每次都要手动操作）

- ChatGPT 的 Custom Instructions（账号级全局指令）
- Anthropic Claude API 中常用的「系统提示词分层」模式

**典型使用场景**：
- 用户为不同角色（程序员 / 产品经理 / 文案）各建了一个 Agent，但都需要「始终用中文回答」「不输出敏感信息」「回答前先确认需求」等公共规则

- 所有 Agent 都遵循统一输出格式（如先列要点再展开）

title: Tabs/AssistantItem: factor click + context menus from a single descriptor
body:
## Background

After PR #12060 (context-menu migration), `src/renderer/src/pages/home/Tabs/components/AssistantItem.tsx` maintains **two parallel menu trees**:

- A click-triggered \"more actions\" Dropdown still uses `antd Dropdown` (lines ~110–326).
- A right-click ContextMenu uses `@cherrystudio/ui` `ContextMenu` (lines ~353–555).

Both menus expose the same actions (edit, copy, clear, save-to-agent, icon-type submenu, tag management, sort, delete) but the menu construction is duplicated ~90 lines apart. Adding or tweaking an item requires editing both branches; tag operations could silently diverge between left-click and right-click.

PR #12060 took this as an acceptable follow-up because `@cherrystudio/ui` does not yet ship a click-driven dropdown menu primitive (only `ContextMenu` and `SelectDropdown`). Once a click-driven dropdown menu lands in `@cherrystudio/ui`, AssistantItem (and similar files: `AgentItem.tsx`, `AssistantPresetCard.tsx`, `YamlFrontMatterNodeView.tsx`) should drop the antd Dropdown.

## Proposed

1. Add a `DropdownMenu` primitive in `packages/ui/src/components/primitives/` (Radix `react-dropdown-menu` based, mirroring the structure of the new `ContextMenu`).
2. Factor a single \"menu descriptor\" array in `AssistantItem` (e.g. `{ key, label, icon, onSelect, danger?, children? }[]`) and render it twice — once from the click button, once from the right-click wrapper.
3. Do the same in `AgentItem.tsx`, `AssistantPresetCard.tsx`, and `YamlFrontMatterNodeView.tsx`.

## Why this matters

- Removes ~90 LOC of duplicated menu construction per file.
- Eliminates the silent-drift risk between click and right-click menus.
- Continues the v2 push to remove antd from the renderer surface.

## Out of scope for this issue

The legacy renderer CSS vars flagged by `comment-legacy-css-vars` in #12060's diff — tracked separately by the bot's reminder.

title: Hardcoded ~/mcp path causes unwanted directory creation on every startup
body:
> [\!NOTE]
> This issue was translated by Claude.

## Problem Description

Cherry Studio hardcodes the use of `~/mcp` as the MCP configuration directory. Every time it starts, it checks whether this directory exists and automatically creates it if not. Users cannot prevent this behavior even if they never use the MCP feature.

## Specific Behavior

- After deleting the `~/mcp` directory, Cherry Studio recreates it on the next startup
- The directory is empty (only containing an mcp-registry.json cache file), but is still created
- On macOS, `~/mcp` appears in the home directory, which is very conspicuous
- No configuration option is provided for users to customize or disable this path

## Expected Behavior

Provide any of the following solutions:
1. Allow users to customize the MCP configuration directory path
2. If the user has not configured any MCP servers, the `~/mcp` directory should not be created
3. Move the default directory to the application data directory (such as `~/Library/Application Support/CherryStudio/mcp`) to avoid polluting the user's home directory

## Temporary Workaround

Lock the directory with `chflags uchg ~/mcp`, but this affects normal functionality and is not a long-term solution.

---
<details>
<summary>Original Content</summary>

## 问题描述

Cherry Studio 硬编码使用 `~/mcp` 作为 MCP 配置目录，每次启动都会检查该目录是否存在，如果不存在则自动创建。用户即使从不使用 MCP 功能，也无法禁止这个行为。

## 具体表现

- 删除 `~/mcp` 目录后，Cherry Studio 下次启动会重新创建
- 目录为空（只有一个 mcp-registry.json 缓存文件），但仍会被创建
- macOS 上 `~/mcp` 出现在 home 目录，非常碍眼
- 没有提供任何配置项让用户自定义或禁用这个路径

## 期望行为

提供以下任一解决方案：
1. 允许用户自定义 MCP 配置目录路径
2. 如果用户没有配置任何 MCP 服务器，不应该创建 `~/mcp` 目录
3. 将默认目录移到应用数据目录下（如 `~/Library/Application Support/CherryStudio/mcp`），不污染用户 home 目录

## 临时 workaround

通过 `chflags uchg ~/mcp` 锁住目录，但这会影响正常功能，不是长久之计。

</details>

title: [Feature]: Display user-friendly names for MCP server tools instead of random hash IDs
body:
> [\!NOTE]
> This issue was translated by Claude.

### Feature Description

In the conversation interface, the MCP tool call card currently displays in the format `[server hash ID]:[tool name]`, for example:

`wkF7riFsi9EYy39jK7r8B:read`

The server ID is a randomly generated hash of characters that is completely unreadable to users and cannot intuitively indicate which MCP server the tool belongs to.

### Problem

- Users cannot quickly identify which MCP server provides the tool through the tool call card
- When multiple MCP servers are configured, troubleshooting or reviewing tool call chains becomes very difficult
- The display effect is not user-friendly, reducing the overall user experience

### Proposed Solution

1. **Use server name instead of hash ID**: Display the user-set name for the server in the tool call card (e.g., `filesystem:read`, `github:search`), rather than the internal hash ID
2. **Support custom aliases**: Add a "display name" field in the MCP server configuration to allow users to customize a readable alias
3. **Fallback strategy**: If no name is set, try to read the `name` field from the server's `package.json`, and finally fall back to the hash ID

### Expected Display

Current: `wkF7riFsi9EYy39jK7r8B:read`
Expected: `filesystem:read` or `本地文件系统:read`

### Additional Context

This is a UX improvement suggestion that does not affect functional logic but can significantly improve the readability and debugging experience when using MCP tools.

### Problem / 问题

- 用户无法通过工具调用卡片快速识别是哪个 MCP 服务器提供的工具
- 当配置了多个 MCP 服务器时，排查问题或审查工具调用链变得非常困难
- 显示效果不够友好，降低了整体使用体验

### Proposed Solution / 建议方案

1. **使用服务器名称替代哈希 ID**：在工具调用卡片中显示用户为服务器设定的名称（如 `filesystem:read`、`github:search`），而非内部哈希 ID
2. **支持自定义别名**：在 MCP 服务器配置中增加"显示名称"字段，允许用户自定义一个易读的别名
3. **降级策略**：若未设置名称，则尝试读取服务器 `package.json` 中的 `name` 字段，最后才 fallback 到哈希 ID

### Expected Display / 期望的显示效果

当前：`wkF7riFsi9EYy39jK7r8B:read`
期望：`filesystem:read` 或 `本地文件系统:read`

### Additional Context / 补充信息

这是一个 UX 改进建议，不影响功能逻辑，但能显著提升 MCP 工具使用时的可读性和调试体验。

title: [Feature]: Multi-Model Parallel Image Generation in Painting
body:
## Background

Cherry Studio's Painting module currently supports only one model per generation request — users pick a single provider and model, send a prompt, and get one image. To compare how different image models (e.g. FLUX.1-Kontext-pro, gpt-image-1, imagen-4.0-ultra, Nano Banana Pro) handle the same prompt, users must manually re-enter the prompt, switch provider, regenerate, and visually compare results across separate screens or pages. Meanwhile, Cherry Studio's chat side already supports multi-model parallel responses via `@` mention. Image generation has the same comparison need but no comparable workflow.

## Goal

Users can select multiple image models in one painting session and trigger them all from a single prompt, viewing all results side-by-side for direct comparison.

## Spec

- The painting prompt input supports **multi-model selection** via a multi-select dropdown and/or `@` mention, consistent with the chat side's interaction pattern.
- When multiple models are selected, a single submission **fans out into parallel generation requests** — one per selected model. Each model's request is independent and runs concurrently.
- **Prompt is shared** across all selected models. Other parameters (size, seed, style, negative prompt, etc.) default to each model's own settings, but users can optionally override per-model parameters before submission.
- Results are displayed in a **side-by-side grid**, one column per model. Each column shows the model name, image(s), generation status (pending / generating / done / failed), and per-model parameters used.
- Each result column retains its own action menu: save, edit/remix, copy prompt, regenerate (this model only), delete.
- Generation history records the entire batch as a **single group**, preserving the multi-model context. Reopening a batch from history shows the same side-by-side layout.
- Per-model failures do not block other models — a failing model shows an error in its column while successful models continue to display their results.
- The feature is available once the v2 Painting Refactor (#14207) lands, since it requires the unified data layer and provider registry to support cross-provider parallel dispatch.

## Verification

- User opens Painting page, types `a serene mountain lake at sunset` and selects FLUX.1-Kontext-pro + gpt-image-1 + imagen-4.0-ultra → clicks send. Three columns appear, each generating concurrently. As each finishes, its column updates from "generating" to showing the image.
- User selects Nano Banana Pro and FLUX.1-Kontext-pro, sets size to 1024×1024 for Nano Banana but leaves FLUX on its default → both generate with the user-specified size for Nano Banana and FLUX's default size respectively.
- During a multi-model generation, gpt-image-1 errors out with rate limit → its column shows the error message with a retry button, while the other two columns continue to completion.
- User opens generation history → batches with multiple models appear as a single grouped entry showing all model thumbnails. Clicking the group restores the side-by-side view with all original results.
- User selects 4 models and submits → all 4 columns display side-by-side without horizontal scrolling on a standard desktop window; if the user shrinks the window, columns become horizontally scrollable rather than wrapping.
- User selects a single model only → behavior is identical to today's single-model flow (no empty columns or extra UI overhead).
- User clicks "Regenerate" on one column → only that model regenerates; other columns remain unchanged.
- User selects FLUX (image-to-image capable) and gpt-image-1 (text-to-image only) and attaches a reference image → FLUX uses the reference, gpt-image-1 generates from prompt only with a small notice in its column ("reference image not supported by this model").

title: [Bug]: macOS Install Blocked on Fresh Devices Despite "Allow Any Source"
body:
## Background

On fresh MacBook devices (observed on 2026 Q1 "Neo" purchases), users who have already enabled "Allow apps from any source" in System Settings still see the macOS Gatekeeper warning when launching Cherry Studio from Launchpad or the Applications folder — the app refuses to open. The only workaround is to double-click the icon from the mounted DMG window itself, which is an unintuitive path. This was reported by multiple non-technical users during a May 2026 enterprise workshop and is a hard stop for first-time onboarding — once they hit this, they cannot proceed without facilitator help.

## Goal

First-time launch on any supported macOS version (including fresh Neo devices) succeeds from the standard install flow — drag DMG to Applications, click icon, app opens — with no Gatekeeper warning when the binary is properly signed and notarized.

## Spec

- The published macOS build is signed with a valid Developer ID and notarized by Apple before each release.
- First launch from Launchpad, Spotlight, or the Applications folder opens the app on the first attempt without any "cannot be opened" dialog.
- The Gatekeeper quarantine attribute is properly cleared on the binary after standard DMG-to-Applications drag.
- If a signing or notarization step fails in the release pipeline, the build is not published; CI surfaces a clear failure.

## Verification

- Fresh MacBook (no prior Cherry Studio install): download DMG from official site → drag to Applications → click icon from Launchpad → app opens immediately. No warning dialog.
- Same fresh machine, click icon from `/Applications` Finder view → app opens immediately.
- After install, run `spctl -a -vv "/Applications/Cherry Studio.app"` → returns `accepted, source=Developer ID` (or App Store) — not `rejected`.
- Run `codesign -dvv "/Applications/Cherry Studio.app"` → shows valid Apple-issued Developer ID signature with hardened runtime.
- Run `xattr -p com.apple.quarantine "/Applications/Cherry Studio.app"` after the standard DMG install → either no attribute or value indicating the app passed Gatekeeper check.
- On clean machine with default System Settings (no "any source" toggle changed), app opens without requiring user to change security settings.

title: [Feature]: Publish Cherry Studio v2 to Mac App Store
body:
## Background

Cherry Studio is currently distributed only via DMG download from the official website. For non-technical users — observed during the May 2026 enterprise workshop — installation is a recurring friction point: Gatekeeper warnings, signing concerns, manual DMG-to-Applications drag, and lack of a familiar "App Store" trust signal. Publishing to the Mac App Store eliminates all of these for the segment that already uses macOS naturally; the team confirmed in the 5/11 sync that the Apple developer account is already in place.

## Goal

Cherry Studio v2 is available on the Mac App Store, so users can install with one click from a trusted source without DMG download, Gatekeeper warnings, or manual security settings.

## Spec

- Cherry Studio v2 is published as a free app on the Mac App Store at the same time as (or shortly after) the v2 public release.
- The App Store build provides the same core feature set as the DMG build, with platform-required adjustments (sandboxing, entitlements) handled transparently to users.
- App Store listing includes accurate description, screenshots, privacy disclosure, and version history.
- Updates flow through App Store automatic update channel; users do not need to track DMG releases manually.
- DMG download from the official site continues to be available for users who prefer it or need features incompatible with App Store sandboxing.

## Verification

- Search "Cherry Studio" in Mac App Store on macOS → Cherry Studio v2 appears as a result with official publisher info.
- One-click "Get" → app installs without DMG download, security prompts, or Gatekeeper warnings.
- Launch from Launchpad after install → app opens immediately.
- App Store version number matches the latest stable v2 release within one release cycle.
- When a new v2 build ships, users with auto-update enabled receive it through App Store without manual action.
- Users who have App Store version and DMG version side-by-side can run either (or choose one) — App Store version's sandbox behavior is documented in the listing.

## Related

title: [Bug]: Safari Silently Blocks Stripe Payment Popup on CherryIN Recharge
body:
## Background

When users recharge CherryIN credits through Cherry Studio, the flow opens a browser tab to the CherryIN site, where clicking the Stripe payment button is supposed to open a payment popup. On macOS + Safari (the default browser for many non-technical users observed during the May 2026 enterprise workshop), Safari's default popup blocker silently prevents the payment window from appearing — no notification, no progress indicator. Users see nothing happen after clicking pay and assume the product is broken. Multiple users hit this in the same session, and even the facilitator did not immediately realize the cause was a Safari popup block.

## Goal

Stripe payment flow on CherryIN succeeds on Safari without users needing to know about or change popup-blocking settings.

## Spec

- The payment trigger on CherryIN does not rely on programmatically opening a popup window from JavaScript; it uses a user-initiated link click or in-page embed that Safari does not block.
- If a popup-based flow must remain as a fallback, Cherry Studio's recharge UI shows a clear inline message before the user clicks pay: "If the payment window doesn't appear, check your browser's popup blocker."
- After payment completion via any path, the user is returned to a clear next-step screen (back to Cherry Studio or a CherryIN confirmation page with explicit instructions).

## Verification

- Fresh macOS user with default Safari settings (popup blocker on) → opens Cherry Studio recharge flow → clicks pay → Stripe payment surface appears successfully in the same tab or as a permitted overlay.
- Same user without changing any Safari preferences completes a recharge end-to-end and sees the credit reflected.
- On Chrome / Edge / Firefox with their default popup blockers → same flow works.
- When a popup is unavoidable and gets blocked, an inline notice is visible to the user before they click pay, not buried in a debug log.

title: [Feature]: Recharge Flow in Electron In-App Window (Eliminate External Browser Hop)
body:
## Background

The May 2026 workshop confirmed that Cherry Studio's external-browser CherryIN recharge flow has multiple cascading failure modes — Safari popup blockers killing Stripe (#15018), users stranded on the CherryIN page after payment with no path back to the app, brittle credit-balance refresh, and no signal to the app that a recharge attempt is even in progress.

An earlier proposal to host the entire recharge flow inside an Electron in-app window was rejected because it would break Stripe's stored cards, OS-saved passwords, GitHub OAuth single-sign-on, and other browser-session-dependent flows that recurring users rely on. The agreed direction is to keep payments in the user's real system browser (same pattern as Claude Desktop / Anycall) but make the round-trip seamless: tag the outbound URL so the CherryIN page can deep-link back into Cherry Studio on completion, and have the app refresh affected state automatically when the callback arrives.

Revisiting the in-app-window approach is deferred until Cherry Studio has its own first-party account and credits system, at which point the entire payment surface can be re-implemented natively instead of wrapping a third-party page.

## Goal

When a user initiates CherryIN recharge from Cherry Studio, payment completes in their real system browser (preserving saved cards, passwords, OAuth), and they are deep-linked back into Cherry Studio with credit balance and model list already refreshed — no manual reload, no orphaned browser tab, no lost context.

## Spec

- **Launch tagging**: when Cherry Studio opens the CherryIN recharge URL externally, it appends a callback marker (e.g. `?source=cherry-studio&intent=recharge&return_uri=cherrystudio://recharge-callback&nonce=<uuid>`). The nonce is persisted locally so the app can correlate the return.
- **Custom protocol registration**: Cherry Studio registers a `cherrystudio://` URL scheme with the OS on macOS, Windows, and Linux. The CherryIN success and cancel pages deep-link to `cherrystudio://recharge-callback?status=success|cancel&nonce=<uuid>` when they detect a Cherry Studio origin via the launch tag.
- **Inbound handling**: when the OS dispatches the callback URL to Cherry Studio, the app validates the nonce, brings the window to the foreground, and routes the user back to the screen they triggered recharge from.
- **State refresh on success**: on a `status=success` callback, Cherry Studio re-fetches the CherryIN balance and pulls the model list automatically. This is the shared root-cause fix for #15022 and #15023.
- **In-progress UI**: while the external browser is open, Cherry Studio shows a non-blocking "Waiting for payment to complete in your browser…" indicator with a manual "I've finished / Cancel" override, so the user always has a way out even if the deep-link never fires (Safari content blocker, user closed the tab, etc.).
- **Failure / timeout fallback**: if no callback arrives within a reasonable timeout, show a recovery dialog ("Did your payment succeed? — Refresh balance / Try again / Contact support") and trigger a manual balance + model-list refresh.
- **No in-app browser hosting**: the recharge page is NOT loaded inside a `BrowserView` / `BrowserWindow`. The user always pays in their real system browser to keep Stripe / Apple Pay / OS-saved credentials / GitHub OAuth working.

## Verification

- User clicks "Recharge" inside Cherry Studio → their default system browser opens to the CherryIN recharge page; the URL includes the callback marker and nonce.
- Cherry Studio's main window shows a "payment in progress" indicator with a manual override.
- User completes Stripe payment in the system browser → CherryIN success page deep-links to `cherrystudio://recharge-callback?status=success&nonce=…` → Cherry Studio is brought to the foreground.
- Credit balance updates immediately and the model list is auto-fetched; no manual refresh required.
- If the user cancels in the browser → deep-link with `status=cancel` returns them to Cherry Studio with a non-alarming "Payment canceled" notice.
- If the deep-link never fires (browser content blocker, user closed the tab) → after the timeout, Cherry Studio shows a recovery dialog and the manual "Refresh balance" button restores correct state.
- Recharge works identically with Safari, Chrome, Edge, and Firefox as the system browser because no in-app browser is involved.
- The OS deep-link registration survives app updates on macOS, Windows, and Linux.

## Related

- #15018 — Safari Stripe popup block becomes irrelevant once the flow no longer depends on a popup window
- #15022 — balance auto-refresh is implemented by the inbound-callback handler
- #15023 — model-list auto-fetch is triggered by the same callback

title: [Bug]: CherryIN Balance Shows $0.00 After Successful Recharge Until Manual Refresh
body:
## Background

After completing a CherryIN recharge, when the user returns to Cherry Studio the account balance still displays `$0.00` until the user manually clicks refresh. During the May 2026 enterprise workshop, multiple non-technical users assumed their payment had failed and either tried to pay again or asked the facilitator for help. This bug was not caught earlier because the team never went through the actual recharge flow — only fetched balances on accounts that already had credit.

## Goal

After a CherryIN recharge succeeds, Cherry Studio displays the updated balance automatically without any user action.

## Spec

- On returning from a successful recharge (in-app window close or external return-to-app callback), Cherry Studio automatically fetches and displays the latest balance.
- During the brief refresh window, the balance area shows a clear loading state — not a stale `$0.00`.
- If the balance fetch fails after a successful payment, the UI shows an explicit "balance fetch failed, retry" message rather than silently leaving stale data.

## Verification

- Fresh user with $0 balance: completes a $10 recharge → returns to Cherry Studio → sees `$10.00` (or equivalent) immediately, no manual refresh needed.
- Same flow with simulated balance-API failure → sees an explicit error and retry button rather than persistent `$0.00`.
- Recharge from a paid plan to top up: existing balance `$5.00`, recharge `$10` → returns to see `$15.00` automatically.

## Related

#15016 #15019

title: [Feature]: Auto-Fetch Model List After CherryIN Recharge / OAuth Completion
body:
## Background

After completing CherryIN recharge, when the user returns to Cherry Studio and opens the model picker, the list is empty — users must manually click "Fetch Models" to populate it. Most non-technical users have no concept of "fetching models" and assume the product is broken or their payment did not work. This was a known requirement that has not yet been implemented, called out during the May 2026 workshop debrief.

## Goal

After OAuth login or recharge completion, the user's available model list is populated automatically without requiring a separate manual action.

## Spec

- When the OAuth / recharge flow returns successfully, Cherry Studio automatically triggers a model-list fetch in the background.
- The model picker is populated with the resulting list as soon as it loads; users do not need to click "Fetch Models".
- During the fetch window, the picker shows a brief loading indicator — not an empty list.
- If the fetch fails, the picker shows a clear retry option with an explanation, not a silent empty state.

## Verification

- New user completes OAuth + recharge → opens model picker → sees the full available model list without clicking any button.
- Existing user adds credit via recharge → model picker continues to show models without re-fetch action.
- Network-induced fetch failure → picker shows retry button with clear error, not an empty placeholder.

## Related

#15016 #15019

title: [Feature]: Surface Tool/Retry Errors in Neutral Color, Not Alarming Red
body:
## Background

Cherry Studio currently shows all backend errors and tool-call failures in bright red, including transient errors that the agent will automatically retry and recover from. Non-technical users in the May 2026 workshop interpreted red as "task failed" and gave up, even when the agent went on to recover and succeed. In comparison, tools like Cowork use neutral gray for in-flight errors and reserve red for terminal user-actionable failures.

## Goal

Transient errors that agents recover from are shown in a neutral color, so users don't panic at normal retry behavior. Red is reserved for failures the user actually needs to act on.

## Spec

- Tool-call failures that the agent will retry are rendered in a neutral / muted color (e.g. gray) with no alarming icon.
- Errors that have been recovered from (subsequent retry succeeded) collapse into a small inline notice or are hidden from the main thread.
- Red is reserved for terminal failures requiring user action (auth expired, no remaining credit, manual intervention needed).
- The change applies consistently across agent traces, tool calls, and message streams.

## Verification

- Agent makes a tool call that fails with a transient network error and succeeds on retry → first attempt shows in gray, retry succeeds, final UI shows the successful result with at most a small "retried" indicator — no red.
- Agent hits a hard auth failure that requires user action → red error with clear next-step instruction.
- Multiple transient failures in sequence → all shown in gray; no escalating red panic.
- User reviewing trace history → can still see all failures (gray) and successes; no information is lost, just visually de-escalated.

## Related

#15016

title: [Feature]: Improve AI Error Diagnosis with More Context and Hidden Raw Stack
body:
## Background

Cherry Studio already runs an AI diagnosis layer on errors, but the current implementation has two problems observed in the May 2026 workshop: (1) the diagnosis doesn't have enough context to be useful — it's running on a 4B model with thin prompts, so its conclusions are vague; (2) the raw English error code/stack trace is shown alongside the diagnosis on the main UI, which terrifies non-technical users. The 4B model is cheap enough that more context tokens are affordable; the raw error should be collapsed by default.

## Goal

AI error diagnosis produces actionable, localized explanations of failures with enough context to be useful, while raw error stacks stay collapsed by default behind a "view technical details" affordance.

## Spec

- The AI diagnosis call receives a richer context window: recent conversation, the tool/operation being attempted, and the full error metadata — taking advantage of the 4B model's low cost.
- The diagnosis prompt is tuned to produce concrete, user-friendly explanations in the user's UI language (i18n), not generic phrases.
- On the main error surface, only the AI's diagnosis text is shown by default; raw error code, stack trace, and English exception text are hidden behind an expandable "Technical details" section.
- Expanding "Technical details" reveals the original raw error for users who want to inspect it.

## Verification

- Cherry Studio set to Chinese: an upstream model timeout occurs → main error area shows Chinese diagnosis text like "模型暂时无响应，系统已自动重试" — no English stack trace visible by default.
- Same error: clicking "Technical details" → expands to show the raw English error message and stack.
- Diagnosis includes context: error caused by missing Python → diagnosis says "需要 Python 环境，可在设置 → 插件中安装" — not just "command failed".
- Cherry Studio set to English / Japanese: same flow produces diagnosis text in the matching language.

## Related

#15016

title: [Feature]: Auto-Select Most Stable Cherry Domain for Model Service
body:
## Background

Cherry Studio's model service currently runs across three domains (e.g. `.ai`, `.net`, `.cc`). Users today must manually switch between them when one becomes slow or unreachable due to ISP DNS pollution, regional throttling, or carrier-specific routing. Workshop users hit "very slow loading, eventually error" on Claude calls and had no way to recover except being told by the facilitator which domain to switch to. The team has CDN acceleration rolling out this week, but a layered approach is needed: auto-pick the healthiest domain at launch and recover from runtime failures.

## Goal

Cherry Studio automatically selects and uses the most stable Cherry domain for model service, transparently failing over without requiring users to switch endpoints by hand.

## Spec

- On Cherry Studio startup (and at runtime when failures occur), the client pings each configured Cherry domain and measures latency / reachability.
- The most stable / lowest-latency domain is selected automatically; the user does not need to choose.
- During a session, if the active domain begins failing or exceeds a latency threshold, Cherry Studio transparently switches to the next-best domain and retries the in-flight request.
- The currently active domain and its health status are visible to advanced users (e.g. in a settings or diagnostics panel), but normal users never need to look at this.
- The set of candidate domains can be reduced (e.g. converged from 3 to 2) without changing user behavior — the auto-selection adapts.

## Verification

- User launches Cherry Studio in an environment where `.ai` is slow but `.net` is fast → client picks `.net` automatically; user makes Claude calls successfully without any manual domain switching.
- During an active session on `.net`, the network changes so `.net` becomes unreachable but `.cc` is fine → next model call succeeds via `.cc`; the user sees no error message, only a brief retry indicator if anything.
- All three domains are down → user sees a clear "all model service endpoints unreachable" message with a retry option, not a confusing low-level error.
- User checks the diagnostics view → sees current active domain, last health-check latency for each, and recent failover history.

title: [Feature]: Onboarding Lands Users Directly in Agent Chat with Welcome and Task Cards
body:
## Background

After completing login and recharge in Cherry Studio, today users land on a configuration screen and must create an Agent before they can do anything — picking a model, deciding "autonomous mode vs classic mode", writing a system prompt, etc. Non-technical users observed during the May 2026 enterprise workshop were overwhelmed by this configuration step and either gave up or asked the facilitator what to fill in. Cowork-style tools simply drop the user into a conversation, and the team confirmed that creating-an-agent should not be a precondition for first use.

## Goal

First-time users go from completing recharge directly into an Agent conversation with a friendly welcome and one-click task starters — no Agent creation form required.

## Spec

- Immediately after first-time login + recharge completes, the user lands in an active conversation with a default Agent — not in a creation form or empty list.
- The Agent sends a proactive welcome message introducing itself, what it can do, and inviting the user to try a first task.
- Above the input box, a row of **task starter cards** is displayed (e.g. "Write me a weekly summary", "Make a slide deck from this doc", "Research topic X"). Clicking a card auto-fills the input box and submits immediately, so the user sees the Agent actually executing.
- The default Agent runs in **autonomous mode** by default; the autonomous vs. classic toggle is removed from the user-facing surface (autonomy is the only mode going forward).
- If users still want to create custom Agents, the existing creation flow is moved behind a clear "Create Custom Agent" entry point and is redesigned as a **step-by-step wizard** instead of a single form: step 1 picks model (with guidance — "Complex tasks: pick Claude; daily tasks: pick GLM / DeepSeek"); subsequent steps explain each option in plain language with previous/next navigation.
- The custom-creation wizard's permissions panel is simplified to the minimum required guardrails (e.g. file deletion is reversible / sandboxed); the explicit Plan vs Full-Auto choice is removed.

## Verification

- Brand new user installs Cherry Studio → completes login → completes recharge → instantly sees a conversation view with a welcome message from the default Agent and a row of starter cards above the input box. No "Create Agent" prompt anywhere on the path.
- User clicks the "Make a slide deck" starter card → the input is auto-populated and submitted → Agent immediately starts producing the deck. User sees a full successful task without typing anything.
- User opens the Agent list → sees the default Agent already there; there is no required first step to create one.
- User clicks "Create Custom Agent" → enters a step-by-step wizard. First step shows model picker with plain-language guidance text below it.
- Existing "autonomous vs classic" toggle is no longer visible anywhere in the default user flow; existing Agents continue to function (they all behave as autonomous).
- User tries to make the Agent delete a file in a sensitive folder → operation goes through a safe / reversible path (e.g. trash / undo within a window) rather than being blocked behind a manual permission prompt.

## Related

title: [Feature]: Built-In Skill Marketplace with One-Click Install and "Save As Skill" Guidance
body:
## Background

During the May 2026 enterprise workshop, the largest "wow" moment came from skills — the PPT-generation skill produced a dramatically better deck than the default output, and the entire room wanted to install it. But the only path was a GitHub repo, which non-technical users could not navigate. Several workshop attendees explicitly asked how to install a skill, where installed skills live, how to create their own, and how to share with colleagues. Beyond installation, users had no way to discover the "you can wrap a completed task into a reusable skill" capability — the facilitator had to tell them verbally.

## Goal

Users can browse a curated in-app marketplace, install skills with one click, and turn any completed task into a reusable skill via a built-in guidance flow — without ever touching GitHub or any external tool.

## Spec

- Cherry Studio includes a **built-in skill marketplace** entry, browsable from the main UI. Listings include skill name, screenshot/preview, description, tags, install button, and version.
- The marketplace ships with **curated featured skills**, prioritizing the most-asked categories: **PPT / slide generation**, **Feishu CLI**, and document / data analysis (mirroring the Office trio).
- Installing a skill is a **single click** — no GitHub, no zip, no manual file paths. The skill becomes immediately available in the user's Agents.
- Each skill listing shows where the installed skill lives (the Agent it attaches to) so users don't get lost after install.
- In any Agent conversation, after the user completes a task, an inline affordance prompts: "**Save this as a Skill?**" One click triggers an Agent-led flow that names, describes, and packages the task as a reusable skill in the user's library.
- The marketplace inspirational reference for layout and curation is the Notion / Defy template marketplace pattern: clean cards, categorized, curated by the team.

## Verification

- User opens marketplace → sees a featured row including a PPT skill, a Feishu CLI skill, and at least one data-analysis skill. Each card shows preview and one-click install.
- User clicks "Install" on the PPT skill → skill installs in under 5 seconds → user returns to their Agent → the PPT skill is now available without any restart or manual configuration.
- User asks the Agent to make slides → the just-installed PPT skill is automatically used; output quality matches the marketplace listing's preview.
- In a new conversation, user asks the Agent to "research X, summarize as a report, and email it to me" → after completion, an inline button appears: "Save this workflow as a Skill". User clicks → wizard captures name and description → new skill appears in the user's library and is immediately usable in future conversations.
- User opens the marketplace search → searches "Feishu" → finds the Feishu CLI skill and installs in one click.
- At no point in any of the above flows does the user open a browser, download a zip, or interact with GitHub.

title: [Feature]: Cherry Assistant — Always-Capable Default Agent with Active Version Push
body:
## Background

Cherry Assistant (小樱桃助理) is currently positioned as one Agent among many, but workshop observations show non-technical users naturally treat it as "the default Agent" — they expect it to handle anything they throw at it. Today it refuses tasks with "I can't do that", carries too many tools/skills by default (bloating token usage), and has restrictive permissions that block useful actions. Beyond that, Cherry Assistant is also the right surface for proactively telling users about new releases — today users have no idea when new capabilities ship, but the Assistant is the one Agent guaranteed to be in front of every user.

## Goal

Cherry Assistant always attempts any task the user asks, runs lean on tokens by default, and proactively notifies users of new capabilities each time the app updates.

## Spec

- Cherry Assistant accepts any user request and attempts execution — no upfront "I can't do that" refusals.
- Default tool/skill set is **minimal** (only the most universally useful), keeping per-turn token usage low. Cherry Assistant can autonomously add tools and skills as it determines they are needed for the current task.
- Default permission scope is **wide / autonomous** (consistent with the merged autonomous-mode default), with only the minimum safety guardrails (e.g. reversible file deletion).
- After every successful app update, on next launch Cherry Assistant **proactively sends an inline message** in its conversation: a short, plain-language summary of "what's new this version, what you can now do with me". Format is friendly and non-modal — it does not interrupt the user's current task.
- The version push reuses the same surface as the welcome message from the onboarding redesign (#15028) — same Agent, same conversation.

## Verification

- User opens Cherry Assistant and asks "make me a PPT" → Assistant attempts the task and produces output (or runs an applicable skill), instead of replying "I can't do that".
- Inspecting an unmodified Cherry Assistant's tool list shows a minimal set; once the user asks for something that needs an extra tool, the Assistant adds and uses it transparently.
- User performs a file-delete action via the Assistant → action proceeds without a manual permission prompt (delete is reversible).
- User has Cherry Studio installed, version v2.x ships an update → on next launch, opening Cherry Assistant shows a fresh inline message at the top of its conversation describing what's new, with friendly language and no blocking modal.
- User dismisses the version-update message → it does not re-appear until the next version update.

## Related

#15028 #15029

title: [Feature]: Preconfigure Default Models for Assistants and Agents After OOBE
body:
## Background

After completing OAuth / recharge, users today see assistants and agents with empty model selectors — they must pick a model themselves. Non-technical users in the May 2026 workshop had no idea what to pick: they had heard of DeepSeek and Doubao only, did not know Claude, and could not assess quality. Forcing this choice on a fresh user often led to poor model selection, which then made the entire Agent output look bad and broke trust in the product. The agreed direction is to ship sensible defaults.

## Goal

Right after OOBE, every assistant and agent in the user's library already has a sensible default model preselected — the user can start using them immediately without making a model choice.

## Spec

- After OOBE completes (OAuth + first recharge), Cherry Studio populates each built-in assistant and agent with a preselected default model from a curated list.
- The default-model choice **balances quality and cost** — Claude is too expensive to set as the default for every user (risk of burning through their balance); cost-effective high-quality models (e.g. latest GLM, latest Kimi, latest MiniMax, latest DeepSeek) are preferred for most defaults. Claude / GPT can be the default only for assistants and agents whose use case clearly justifies the cost.
- The default-model assignment is part of a product spec — defaults can be updated centrally as the model landscape shifts, without forcing existing users to reconfigure.
- Users retain full control to change the model for any assistant or agent; the default is just a starting point.
- If a preset model becomes unavailable to the user (account / region), Cherry Studio falls back to the next-best available model from the curated list and shows a small notice.

## Verification

- Fresh user completes OOBE → opens the assistants list → every built-in assistant card shows a preselected model name (e.g. `GLM-5.1` or `DeepSeek V4`); no card shows "select a model".
- Same user opens the agents list → same — each agent has a preselected default.
- User clicks a default-equipped assistant → immediately able to send a message; response arrives without picking a model.
- User has only DeepSeek configured (Claude unavailable for their account) → assistants that would have defaulted to Claude fall back to DeepSeek and show a small "fell back to DeepSeek" notice in settings.
- Product team updates the central default list to swap GLM 5.1 for GLM 5.2 → next time a user runs OOBE, GLM 5.2 is the default; existing users who already configured assistants are not changed.

## Related

#15023 #15028

title: [Feature]: Share Installed Skills With Teammates via Cherry Mail
body:
## Background

Workshop attendees consistently asked "how do I share this skill with my team?" once they realized skills are powerful and reusable. The Skill Marketplace (#15029) covers the team-curated install path, but the more common case in enterprise use is peer-to-peer: I built or installed a skill, my colleague wants the same one — today there is no in-app path. Cherry Mail is the channel teammates already use within Cherry Studio, making it the natural distribution mechanism for skill sharing.

## Goal

Users can share an installed skill with a colleague through Cherry Mail in one click, and the recipient can install it back into their own Cherry Studio with one click — without leaving the app.

## Spec

- Every installed skill has a "Share via Cherry Mail" action.
- Clicking it composes a Cherry Mail message addressed to one or more colleagues, containing the skill reference (not the raw files — Cherry Studio handles resolution on the receiving end).
- The recipient opens the Cherry Mail message and sees an inline "Install this skill" button that installs the skill into their own Cherry Studio with one click — same flow as marketplace install.
- Permissions / authorship metadata is preserved so the recipient can see who shared it.
- Sharing respects skill privacy / org boundaries: skills marked as private or org-internal cannot be shared outside their boundary.

## Verification

- User A installs a PPT skill. Opens its detail panel → clicks "Share via Cherry Mail" → composes mail addressed to User B with the skill reference attached. Sends.
- User B receives the mail in Cherry Mail → sees an inline "Install this skill" button → clicks → skill is installed in User B's Cherry Studio in under 5 seconds → immediately usable in B's Agents.
- User B sees in the mail that User A is the source / sharer.
- A skill marked private at organization boundary cannot be shared via Cherry Mail to an external address — the share action is disabled with a clear reason.

## Related

#15029

title: [Feature]: Curated Information-Source Subscription via Stella
body:
## Background

Non-technical users who just got into AI feel overwhelmed by self-media channels — too many opinions, too much hype, no way to distinguish signal from noise. Workshop attendees explicitly asked: "Where do I keep learning after this session without getting lost in self-media?" The Stella recording / subscription capability already exists in skeleton form; what's missing is a curated information-source layer for users who don't know which sources to follow themselves. Cherry Studio is already a trusted touchpoint with them; the team can curate sources and the user just clicks subscribe.

## Goal

Users can subscribe to a curated set of trusted AI / industry information sources from inside Cherry Studio, and receive distilled, non-overwhelming updates pushed to them by their assistant.

## Spec

- Cherry Studio includes a **curated information-source library** in the subscription section — sources chosen and maintained by the Cherry team (e.g. official Cherry channels, vetted industry analyses).
- Users can subscribe to any source with a single click; no need to find or evaluate sources themselves.
- Subscribed content is delivered through the user's default assistant (Cherry Assistant) as concise, distilled inline messages — not raw feeds — so the user sees only what matters.
- The delivery pace and depth (daily summary vs weekly digest) is user-configurable, with sane defaults.
- Users can unsubscribe from any source at any time.

## Verification

- User opens subscription section → sees curated list of trusted sources with one-click subscribe buttons.
- User subscribes to "Cherry official updates" → at the next configured cadence (default daily), Cherry Assistant sends an inline distilled summary in the user's conversation — not a raw RSS dump.
- User changes cadence from daily to weekly → next push respects the new cadence.
- User unsubscribes → no further pushes from that source.
- User subscribes to multiple sources → digest combines them coherently without duplicating identical news items.

## Related

title: [Bug]: MCP/Agent tool approval card defaults to collapsed, leaving users waiting indefinitely without knowing they need to click to expand
body:
> [!NOTE] > This issue was translated by Claude. ### Issue Checklist - [x] I understand that issues are for feedback and problem solving, not for complaining in the comment section, and will provide as much information as possible to help solve the problem. - [x] My issue is not listed in the [FAQ](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/issues/3881). - [x] I've looked at **pinned issues** and searched for existing Open Issues, Closed Issues, and Discussions, no similar issue or discussion was found. - [x] I've filled in short, clear headings so that developers can quickly identify a rough idea of what to expect when flipping through the list of issues. - [x] I've confirmed that I am using the latest version of Cherry Studio. ### Platform macOS ### Version v1.9.5 ### Bug Description When a built-in Agent (e.g. `Agent` / `Cherry Assistant`) calls an MCP tool that requires user authorization, the authorization card appears in the chat **in collapsed state**, showing only the tool-name summary line (e.g. `mcp__exa_web_search_exa gold price ...`). The user has to **actively click** the card to expand it before the `需要授权 / Cancel / Run` buttons become visible. There is no obvious visual cue in the collapsed state to tell the user "I'm waiting for you". As a result the conversation simply stalls — the user assumes the Agent is still thinking and keeps waiting. PR #13281 already removed the auto-execution countdown and added a system notification, but the system notification is only useful when the window is **out of focus**. When the user is staring at the chat window, the collapsed card alone is not discoverable enough. ### Steps To Reproduce 1. Open Cherry Studio v1.9.5 → **智能体 / Agents** → pick a built-in Agent (e.g. `Agent`) 2. Pick a model that can drive tool use (e.g. `anthropic/claude-opus-4`) 3. Send a message that requires an MCP tool call, e.g. `搜索黄金价格，分析涨跌原因，写一份报告，再做成 ppt` 4. The model decides to call an MCP tool (e.g. `exa:web_search_exa`); an approval card appears **collapsed** in the message stream 5. Do nothing — the card stays collapsed indefinitely with no visible "click me" affordance 6. Click the card → it expands and reveals `需要授权 / Cancel / Run`; clicking `Run` lets the conversation continue ### Expected Behavior Either: - (Preferred) The approval card is **expanded by default** the first time it appears in a conversation, so the `Run / Cancel` buttons are immediately visible; OR - The collapsed state carries a strong visual affordance ("Action required", pulsing highlight, badge, or an inline status banner above the input box like `Waiting for your approval`) so the user knows they need to interact. ### Relevant Log Output ```shell N/A ``` ### Additional Context - Reproducible 100% on macOS + Cherry Studio v1.9.5 - Related prior fix: PR #13281 (removed auto-execution countdown, added system notification) - Related open discussion: #13320 (dual-switch UI for tool permission) - Impact: discoverability problem that effectively blocks the MCP main path for users who don't realize the card is clickable. Encountered first-hand during 1.9.5 system testing by the PM. ---
Original Content (中文) ### 平台 macOS ### 版本 v1.9.5 ### Bug 描述 在内置智能体 (`Agent` / `Cherry Assistant`) 与模型对话过程中，当模型调用 MCP 工具且该工具需要用户授权时，授权卡片在聊天里以**折叠状态**出现，只显示工具名摘要 (如 `mcp__exa_web_search_exa gold price ...`)。用户必须**主动点击**该卡片才能展开看到「需要授权 / 取消 / 运行」按钮。 折叠状态下没有任何明显视觉提示告诉用户「需要你授权」，导致对话直接停滞——用户会以为 Agent 还在思考，一直等下去。 PR #13281 已经移除了倒计时自动执行 + 加了系统通知，但系统通知只在窗口失焦时才能起作用。窗口在焦点时，聊天里只有一张折叠卡片，发现成本很高。 ### 复现步骤 1. 打开 Cherry Studio v1.9.5 → 智能体 → 选择内置 Agent (如 `Agent`) 2. 选一个支持 tool use 的模型 (如 `anthropic/claude-opus-4`) 3. 发一条需要调用 MCP 工具的指令，例如：`搜索黄金价格，分析涨跌原因，写一份报告，再做成 ppt` 4. 模型触发 MCP 工具调用 (如 `exa:web_search_exa`)，聊天里出现一张**折叠**的授权卡片 5. 不操作 → 卡片一直折叠，对话停滞，没有视觉提示 6. 点击卡片 → 展开后看到「需要授权 / 取消 / 运行」按钮，点运行后对话才继续 ### 期望行为 二选一： - (推荐) 第一次出现时**默认展开**授权卡片，让「运行 / 取消」按钮立即可见 - 折叠态增加显性视觉提示 (「需要操作」、pulsing 高亮、红点徽标、或输入框上方一条 inline 状态条「等待你授权」) ### 补充信息 - macOS + Cherry Studio v1.9.5 100% 复现 - 相关已合并 PR：#13281 (移除倒计时 + 加系统通知) - 相关 open 讨论：#13320 (工具权限 dual-switch UI) - 影响：发现成本高的体验问题，等价于阻塞 MCP 主路径。1.9.5 系统测试中 PM 本人中招。

title: [Bug]: Switching from ask to fully-automatic mode mid-session still prompts for tool approval (regression of #14197)
body:
> [!NOTE] > This issue was translated by Claude. **This is a regression of #14197** (fixed via PR #14205, merged 2026-04-12) — the same symptom has reappeared in v1.9.5, possibly via a different code path. ### Issue Checklist - [x] I understand that issues are for feedback and problem solving, not for complaining in the comment section, and will provide as much information as possible to help solve the problem. - [x] My issue is not listed in the [FAQ](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/issues/3881). - [x] I've looked at **pinned issues** and searched for existing Open Issues, Closed Issues, and Discussions, no similar issue or discussion was found (#14197 was found, this issue is filed because it is a regression). - [x] I've filled in short, clear headings so that developers can quickly identify a rough idea of what to expect when flipping through the list of issues. - [x] I've confirmed that I am using the latest version of Cherry Studio. ### Platform macOS ### Version v1.9.5 ### Bug Description In an active Agent conversation, switching the permission mode from `ask` to `fully automatic` via the **mode toggle control at the bottom of the chat input bar** does not take effect for the next tool call in the same session. The next tool invocation (e.g. an `mkdir` to create a PPT output directory) still shows the `需要授权 / Cancel / Run` approval card. The user has to manually approve, or create a new session for the mode change to apply. Reference behavior: Claude's official app applies the mode switch immediately — subsequent tool calls in the same session run automatically without prompting. This is the same symptom as #14197 (originally found in v1.9.1, fixed via PR #14205). The earlier fix synced agent-level settings changes (via the Agent Settings popup) to the active session. Either: - (a) the same regression has reappeared in v1.9.5 (PR #14205 no longer effective), or - (b) the **in-conversation mode toggle** is a different code path that doesn't reuse the `AgentService.updateAgent` → session sync logic. ### Steps To Reproduce 1. Open Cherry Studio v1.9.5 → **智能体 / Agents** → pick the built-in `Agent` 2. Pick a tool-capable model (e.g. `anthropic/claude-opus-4`) 3. Send a multi-step task that triggers a chain of tool calls, e.g. `做一份黄金价格 PPT` 4. On the **first** tool-approval card, click the **mode toggle at the bottom-left of the input bar** and switch from `ask` to `fully automatic` 5. Wait for the next tool call (e.g. `mkdir -p "..../images"`) 6. **Expected**: It auto-executes — no approval card 7. **Actual**: The approval card still appears with `需要授权 / 取消 / 运行`; user must click `运行` manually ### Expected Behavior Switching permission mode in the active session should take effect immediately for the next tool call — matching Claude app behavior and matching the contract established by PR #14205. ### Relevant Log Output ```shell N/A ``` ### Additional Context - **This is a regression of #14197** (closed by PR #14205, merged 2026-04-12) - Reproducible 100% on macOS + Cherry Studio v1.9.5 - Impact: breaks the "run a long-chain task, decide mid-task to trust the Agent and let it run freely" flow. Users either have to discard the session and start over (losing context), or keep clicking approve, which defeats the purpose of fully automatic mode. - Suggested investigation: - Verify PR #14205's session-sync logic still runs in v1.9.5 - Check whether the in-conversation mode toggle goes through `AgentService.updateAgent` or a separate code path - If separate, unify the two entry points' session-sync behavior - Fallback: on permission-mode change, immediately re-evaluate auto-approve for the next pending/upcoming tool call in the active session ---

title: fix(agents): cron task sessions should use task name instead of agent name
body:
## Bug Description

When a CherryClaw agent runs scheduled cron tasks, all sessions created are named after the agent (e.g. MyBot) rather than the individual task name (e.g. Daily Report). Users cannot tell which session belongs to which task.

## Root Cause

In SchedulerService.ts, runTask() calls createSession with an empty object, so the session inherits the agent name.

## Proposed Fix

Pass the task name to createSession. One-line change:
  - createSession(agentId, {})
  + createSession(agentId, { name: task.name })

task.name is already populated from ScheduledTaskEntity.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Create a CherryClaw agent named MyBot
2. Add multiple scheduled tasks (Daily Report, Weather Alert)
3. Wait for tasks to execute
4. All sessions show as MyBot, indistinguishable

## Expected Behavior

Each session should be named after its task (e.g. Daily Report).

title: [Bug]: V8 SIGTRAP crash in main thread — app quits unexpectedly multiple times per day on macOS (Apple Silicon)
body:
### Issue Checklist

- [x] I understand that issues are for feedback and problem solving, not for complaining in the comment section, and will provide as much information as possible to help solve the problem.
- [x] My issue is not listed in the [FAQ](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/issues/3881).
- [x] I've looked at **pinned issues** and searched for existing [Open Issues](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/issues) and [Closed Issues](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20state%3Aclosed), and while #13578 is similar, my crash has a different root cause (V8 engine assertion failure, not memory/OOM).
- [x] I've filled in a short, clear title.
- [x] I've confirmed that I am using the latest version of Cherry Studio.

### Platform

macOS

### Version

v1.9.5

### Bug Description

Cherry Studio crashes unexpectedly multiple times per day. The app runs normally for hours, then quits without any warning or error dialog. This has been happening consistently for at least several weeks across multiple versions.

After analyzing the macOS crash report, the crash is:
- **Exception type**: `EXC_BREAKPOINT` / `SIGTRAP`
- **Faulting thread**: Thread 0 (main thread)
- **Root cause**: V8 engine internal assertion failure (CHECK/DCHECK), **not** an out-of-memory or null pointer dereference

The crash happens during the Cocoa RunLoop idle callback on the main thread. V8's garbage collector (`cppgc`) and JIT compilation optimizer are running in the background when a Rust native addon (via `cxxbridge`) appears to corrupt V8's internal object state, causing V8 to deliberately abort the process.

This is distinct from other reported crashes (#13578 which is OOM from large images, #7805 which is selection-hook null pointer).

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Launch Cherry Studio and use it normally throughout the day (Agent conversations, MCP tools, etc.)
2. The app typically runs 10–15 hours before crashing
3. Crash occurs during idle moments — not triggered by a specific user action
4. No error dialog appears; the app simply disappears from the Dock

The crash is not consistently reproducible with a short series of steps. It appears to be a cumulative issue (GC pressure or memory fragmentation building up over hours of runtime).

### Expected Behavior

The app should not crash during normal use, even after extended runtime.

### Relevant Log Output

Key frames from the faulting thread (Thread 0) call stack:

```
Exception Type:  EXC_BREAKPOINT (SIGTRAP)
Termination:     Trace/BPT trap: 5

Thread 0 Crashed (main thread):
  cxxbridge1$rust_vec$bool$capacity
  node::inspector::protocol::Target::Metainfo::version
  v8::Name::GetIdentityHash()
  node::PrincipalRealm::tick_callback_function() const
  cppgc::subtle::DisallowGarbageCollectionScope::~DisallowGarbageCollectionScope()
  v8::internal::OptimizingCompileInputQueue::Prioritize(...)
  v8::Exception::TypeError(...)
  __CFRUNLOOP_IS_CALLING_OUT_TO_A_SOURCE0_PERFORM_FUNCTION__
  __CFRunLoopDoSource0
  __CFRunLoopDoSources0
  __CFRunLoopRun
  _CFRunLoopRunSpecificWithOptions
  NSApplication run
```

**Analysis summary**:
- V8 engine modules: 206 symbol references
- Node.js modules: 69 symbol references
- Total threads at crash: ~70 (high, with extensive mach_msg / IPC activity)
- The crash occurs when V8's cppgc garbage collector finds inconsistent state during a Rust cxxbridge interaction in the inspector/debugger protocol context

Full crash report (`.ips` JSON) can be provided privately if needed — it has been withheld from public posting to avoid exposing device identifiers.

### Additional Context

- macOS version: 26.4.1 (25E253)
- Device: Apple Silicon (ARM-64)
- This crash pattern has persisted across multiple Cherry Studio versions
- Restarting the app daily (~every 12 hours) works as a temporary workaround, which further supports the "cumulative GC pressure" hypothesis

title: [Feature]: Add in-app local embedding for Knowledge Base without a separate embedding service
body:
