- [x] I have provided a short and descriptive title so that developers can quickly understand the issue when browsing the issue list, rather than vague titles like "A suggestion" or "Stuck."
- [x] The latest version of Cherry Studio does not include the feature I am suggesting.

### Platform

Windows

### Version

v1.9.5

### Is your feature request related to an existing issue?

This is somewhat adjacent to #14895, but the key point here is different: Knowledge Base embeddings could run directly inside Cherry Studio, with the app handling model download, caching, and inference, instead of requiring a separate embedding service.

### Desired Solution

I would like to suggest adding an in-app local embedding option for the Knowledge Base feature.

For example: Knowledge Base -> Embedding Model -> Built-in Local Embedding

The idea is that Cherry Studio could handle the embedding model download, local caching, and local inference inside the app itself, instead of requiring users to run a separate embedding service just for embeddings.

For many beginners, embedding configuration is one of the easiest places to get stuck when setting up a local Knowledge Base. Users may already know how to configure a chat model, but embeddings introduce another layer of concepts and setup:
- Which provider or model should I choose?
- Why can't I see any embedding models in the Knowledge Base selector?
- Why does this model not work even though I marked it as an embedding model?

A good reference is the Obsidian plugin Smart Connections. It provides local embedding inside the app environment. By default, it uses TaylorAI/bge-micro-v2. Smart Connections downloads and caches the model through Transformers.js, then runs embedding inference locally inside the app environment. From my own testing, this kind of setup works smoothly on a normal PC and does not require an advanced GPU. For ordinary note/document embedding, the resource usage feels quite reasonable.

This seems practical to implement because much of the hard work, such as model loading, caching, and local inference, is already handled by libraries like Transformers.js. Cherry Studio could start with a small default embedding model and keep the existing provider-based embedding options available for users who need more control.

The main goal is to provide a beginner-friendly path:
- Create a Knowledge Base
- Select Built-in Local Embedding
- Let Cherry Studio handle the embedding model locally
- No separate embedding service required

### Alternative Solutions

The current approach is to use external embedding providers or local model services such as Ollama, LM Studio, or cloud embedding APIs.

These options are useful for advanced users, but they still require extra setup. For beginners, having to install, configure, and keep another service running just for embeddings can make the Knowledge Base feature feel much harder than necessary.

Improving documentation for external embedding providers would help, but it would not fully solve the setup barrier. A lightweight in-app local embedding option would make the first-time Knowledge Base experience much smoother.

### Additional Information

Reference implementation:

https://github.com/brianpetro/jsbrains/blob/main/smart-embed-model/adapters/transformers.js

The Smart Connections implementation is useful as a reference because it shows a simple in-app local embedding path:

- Load Transformers.js inside the app environment
- Download a small embedding model
- Cache the model locally
- Run feature extraction locally
- Use the generated embeddings for local semantic search

The important part is not the exact model or exact backend, but the user experience:
- The app manages and runs the embedding model itself.
- The user does not need to start a separate embedding server.

Because this approach can run on top of the Chromium runtime using WebGPU when available and WASM when needed, it can be efficient on ordinary PCs and relatively easy to deploy across platforms.

The feature request is mainly about reducing the Knowledge Base setup barrier by adding an app-managed local embedding option. This could be introduced as a lightweight default option while keeping the existing provider-based embedding configuration for advanced users.

title: [Other]: [v2-refactor] REST violations in providers DataApi schema (rotated-key GET, registry-models POST)
body:
### Pre-submission Checklist

- [x] I understand that Issues are for feedback and problem-solving, not for complaints, and I will provide as much information as possible to help resolve the issue.
- [x] I have checked the pinned Issues and searched through existing open and closed Issues and didn't find similar questions.
- [x] I have written a short and clear title that helps developers quickly understand the nature of my question, rather than vague titles like "A question" or "Help needed".
- [x] My question doesn't fall under bug reports or feature requests categories.

### Platform

macOS (development environment — issue is code-level, platform-independent)

### Version

v2 branch (current dev)

### Question Description

This issue is filed for archival during the **v2 refactoring**. While reviewing `packages/shared/data/api/schemas/providers.ts` against [`docs/references/data/api-design-guidelines.md`](../blob/v2/docs/references/data/api-design-guidelines.md), two endpoints were found to violate the documented RESTful conventions, and three minor inconsistencies were noted for triage.

The findings have been cross-checked against the handler in `src/main/data/api/handlers/providers.ts` and the underlying service in `src/main/data/services/ProviderService.ts`.

### Relevant Context

#### Blocking issue 1 — `GET /providers/:providerId/rotated-key` is not idempotent

**Rule violated** (`api-design-guidelines.md` § HTTP Method Semantics):

> | Method | Purpose | Idempotent |
> |--------|---------|------------|
> | GET    | Retrieve resource(s) | **Yes** |

**Evidence** — `src/main/data/services/ProviderService.ts:188-223` mutates `CacheService` on every call:

```ts
// ProviderService.ts:188
async getRotatedApiKey(providerId: string): Promise<string> {
  // ...
  const currentIndex = enabledKeys.findIndex((k) => k.id === lastUsedKeyId)
  const nextIndex = (currentIndex + 1) % enabledKeys.length
  const nextKey = enabledKeys[nextIndex]
  cache.set(cacheKey, nextKey.id)   // ← state mutation on every GET
  return nextKey.key
}
```

Each call advances the round-robin cursor and returns a different key. This is a state-changing action, not a read. The same document's § Non-CRUD Operations explicitly models state changes as POST (e.g. `POST /topics/:id/archive`).

DataApi automatically retries idempotent failures — under the current GET method, a transient failure could cause the cursor to skip an extra slot. This is a latent correctness hazard, not just a stylistic issue.

**Proposed fix** — change method to POST in schema and handler:

```ts
'/providers/:providerId/rotated-key': {
  POST: {
    params: { providerId: string }
    response: { apiKey: string }
  }
}
```

Renderer call sites currently using `useQuery` for this path must migrate to `useMutation`.

#### Blocking issue 2 — `POST /providers/:providerId/registry-models` overloads the collection path

**Rule violated** (`api-design-guidelines.md` § Standard Endpoint Patterns + § Non-CRUD Operations):

> `POST` on a collection path means *create new resource in the collection*. Non-CRUD operations should use verb-based sub-resource paths (e.g. `/topics/:id/archive`, `/topics/search`).

**Evidence** — `src/main/data/api/handlers/providers.ts:68-79`:

```ts
'/providers/:providerId/registry-models': {
  GET: async ({ params }) => {
    return providerRegistryService.getRegistryModelsByProvider(params.providerId)  // read preset list
  },

  POST: async ({ params, body }) => {
    return await providerRegistryService.resolveModels(                              // resolve/enrich, NOT create
      params.providerId,
      body.models.map((m) => m.modelId)
    )
  }
}
```

The POST does not create a new `registry-model`; it takes raw model IDs and returns them enriched against registry presets. Sharing a path with the GET that lists presets makes the route table actively misleading — a reader naturally expects `POST /registry-models` to create one.

**Proposed fix** — split into a dedicated verb sub-resource:

```ts
'/providers/:providerId/registry-models': {
  GET: { params: { providerId: string }; response: Model[] }   // keep — reads presets
}

'/providers/:providerId/registry-models/resolve': {            // or /enrich
  POST: {
    params: { providerId: string }
    body: EnrichModelsDto
    response: Model[]
  }
}
```

#### Non-blocking inconsistencies (triage)

**3. `POST /providers/:providerId/api-keys` and `DELETE /providers/:providerId/api-keys/:keyId` return parent `Provider`**

`api-design-guidelines.md` § Handler Status Code Behavior establishes `POST → 201 + created entity`, `DELETE → 204 + undefined`. Both endpoints return the parent `Provider` instead — a one-roundtrip-refresh shortcut. Acceptable if intentional; either return the child entity (`ApiKeyEntry`) / `undefined` and let the renderer use `refresh: ['/providers/:providerId', '/providers/:providerId/api-keys']`, or add a schema comment explaining the trade-off.

**4. `defaultChatEndpoint` loses runtime enum validation via type cast**

```ts
defaultChatEndpoint: z.string().optional() as z.ZodOptional<z.ZodType<EndpointType>>
```

The cast narrows the TS type but Zod still accepts any string at runtime — weakening the IPC trust-boundary guarantee that Rule D in § Zod Schema & DTO Conventions exists to protect. Expose an `EndpointTypeValues` array from `provider-registry` and switch to `z.enum(EndpointTypeValues).optional()`.

**5. `ListProvidersQuerySchema` has no pagination / sort params**

```ts
export const ListProvidersQuerySchema = z.strictObject({
  enabled: z.boolean().optional()
})
```

Provider counts are small today, so this is fine. Track for future extension with `OffsetPaginationParams & SortParams` (matches `topics.ts` pattern) if the resource ever grows.

### Attempted Solutions

This is a tracking issue for archival — no code changes have been made yet. Fixes for blocking issues 1 and 2 will require coordinated changes across schema, handler, and renderer call sites, and should likely land in separate PRs to keep diff size manageable. Issue 1 (rotated-key) is user-facing behaviorally (`useQuery` → `useMutation` in renderer) and should be recorded under `v2-refactor-temp/docs/breaking-changes/`.

### Additional Information

**Affected files**

- `packages/shared/data/api/schemas/providers.ts` — schema definitions
- `src/main/data/api/handlers/providers.ts` — handler routing
- `src/renderer/**` — any call sites of `/providers/:providerId/rotated-key` and `/providers/:providerId/registry-models` (POST)

**Suggested test plan for the eventual fix PR**

- [ ] Unit tests for `providerService.getRotatedApiKey` assert it is invoked via POST (issue 1)
- [ ] Unit / integration tests for `providerRegistryService.resolveModels` switch to the new `/resolve` sub-path (issue 2)
- [ ] Grep and migrate renderer call sites: `rg "'/providers/:providerId/rotated-key'|/registry-models'" src/renderer`
- [ ] `pnpm lint && pnpm test` clean before opening the follow-up PR

**References**

- [`docs/references/data/api-design-guidelines.md`](../blob/v2/docs/references/data/api-design-guidelines.md)
- Related v2 refactor issues: #14209 (Provider DataApi migration), #14207 (v2 Painting refactor)

title: [Bug]: endpoint_type='image-generation' is ignored — chat send routes to /v1/chat/completions instead of /v1/images/generations
body:
### Issue Checklist

- [x] I understand that issues are for feedback and problem solving, not for complaining in the comment section, and will provide as much information as possible to help solve the problem.
- [x] My issue is not listed in the [FAQ](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/issues/3881).
- [x] I've looked at **pinned issues** and searched for existing [Open Issues](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/issues), [Closed Issues](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20state%3Aclosed), and [Discussions](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/discussions), no similar issue or discussion was found.
- [x] I've filled in short, clear headings so that developers can quickly identify a rough idea of what to expect when flipping through the list of issues. And not "a suggestion", "stuck", etc.
- [x] I've confirmed that I am using the latest version of Cherry Studio.

### Platform

macOS

### Version

v1.9.5

### Bug Description

When a NewAPI / CherryIN provider has a model whose endpoint type is explicitly set to **Image Generation (OpenAI)** (`endpoint_type: 'image-generation'`) in the Edit Model dialog, Cherry Studio still POSTs the chat request to `/v1/chat/completions` instead of `/v1/images/generations`. The upstream gateway rejects this with:

```
this channel only supports image generation, please use POST /v1/images/generations instead of /v1/chat/completions
```

surfaced in the renderer as `AI_RetryError: Failed after 3 attempts`.

The root cause is in `src/renderer/src/services/ApiService.ts` (`transformMessagesAndFetch`). The routing decision for whether to call the image endpoint relies **only** on `isDedicatedImageGenerationModel(model)`, which tests `model.id` against the static `DEDICATED_IMAGE_MODEL_REGEX` in `src/renderer/src/config/models/vision.ts`. The user's explicit `endpoint_type` tag is never consulted, so:

- Any model whose id does not match the built-in image regex always goes down the chat path even when the user picked the image endpoint type.
- For ids that *should* match the regex (e.g. `gpt-image-2`), there are cases where the chat path is still taken in the production build (see reproduction below) — the explicit endpoint tag would have been the safe override but is ignored.

Source code references back this up:

- `src/renderer/src/aiCore/utils/options.ts:564-587` explicitly maps `endpoint_type: 'image-generation'` to `OpenAICompatibleChatLanguageModel` (i.e. a chat model).
- `src/renderer/src/aiCore/provider/custom/newapi-provider.ts:121-123` falls `case 'image-generation':` through to `createCompatibleModel(modelId)` (a chat model).

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Add a NewAPI-type provider (any upstream gateway that exposes both chat and image endpoints — e.g. AIFAST, DeerAPI, etc.).
2. Add a model with id `gpt-image-2` (group name is irrelevant; can be the gateway's group key).
3. Open the Edit Model dialog, set **Endpoint Type = Image Generation (OpenAI)**, save.
4. Open a chat with that model and send any prompt (e.g. `hi`).
5. Open DevTools → Network, observe the request:
   - URL: `https://<host>/v1/chat/completions` (should be `/v1/images/generations`)
   - Request body contains `"model": "gpt-image-2"`, `"messages": [...]`, `"stream": true`, `"tools"`, etc.
   - Response: `500` with body
     ```json
     {
       "error": {
         "message": "this channel only supports image generation, please use POST /v1/images/generations instead of /v1/chat/completions",
         "type": "new_api_error",
         "code": "convert_request_failed"
       }
     }
     ```
6. Error surfaces in the UI as `AI_RetryError: Failed after 3 attempts. Last error: this channel only supports image generation, ...`.

### Expected Behavior

When `endpoint_type === 'image-generation'` is set on a model, sending a chat message to that model should route through `fetchImageGeneration → aiProvider.generateImage → provider.imageModel(...)` and POST to `/v1/images/generations`, regardless of whether the model id matches the hardcoded `DEDICATED_IMAGE_MODEL_REGEX`. The user's explicit endpoint-type selection should be the authoritative routing signal.

### Relevant Log Output

```shell
Error name: AI_RetryError
Error message: Failed after 3 attempts. Last error: this channel only supports image generation, please use POST /v1/images/generations instead of /v1/chat/completions (request id: 20260513163245418437509egtRAwft)
Stack:
  at _retryWithExponentialBackoff (.../store-Dlok2ptH.js:100920:37)
  at async streamStep                (.../store-Dlok2ptH.js:104421:109)
  at async fn                        (.../store-Dlok2ptH.js:104738:5)
  at async                           (.../store-Dlok2ptH.js:100723:19)
Error cause: "[undefined]"
```

Network panel (DevTools, 4 retries observed):

```
POST https://<gateway>/v1/chat/completions   →   500
POST https://<gateway>/v1/chat/completions   →   500
POST https://<gateway>/v1/chat/completions   →   500
POST https://<gateway>/v1/chat/completions   →   500
```

Request body (each attempt):

```json
{
  "model": "gpt-image-2",
  "messages": [
    { "role": "system", "content": "test" },
    { "role": "user",   "content": "hi"  }
  ],
  "stream": true,
  ...
}
```

### Additional Context

This is purely a routing-layer bug. Once the request reaches `fetchImageGeneration → aiProvider.generateImage`, the existing hotfix for `gpt-image-2` (#14578) already handles the image-generation specifics (multipart content-type, `response_format` handling, etc.) — so honoring `endpoint_type` at the routing layer is sufficient to fix this case.

A fix PR is on the way that adds `isImageGenerationEndpoint(model)` returning `true` for either `isDedicatedImageModel(model)` or `model.endpoint_type === 'image-generation'`, and uses it in `transformMessagesAndFetch`.

title: [Feature] Collapsible sidebar for tool call display
body:
## Problem Description

In the conversation interface, when an Agent calls MCP tools, the tool call details (tool name, parameters, return results, etc.) are displayed inline within the conversation flow. This can make the conversation visually cluttered, especially when multiple tools are called in sequence.

## Proposed Solution

Add a **collapsible sidebar panel** to display tool call information separately from the main conversation area.

## Expected Behavior

| Feature | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| **Sidebar Display** | Tool call information is shown in a separate sidebar panel (left or right), isolated from the main conversation |
| **Expand/Collapse** | Users can toggle the sidebar to show details or hide it for a cleaner interface |
| **Real-time Updates** | When the Agent executes tools, the sidebar shows real-time status (in-progress/success/failed) |
| **History View** | Users can view all tool call history within the current session |
| **Click to Details** | Clicking on a tool call expands to show parameters and return values |

## Use Cases

1. **Clean Reading Experience**: Users who only want to see the Agent's final response can collapse the sidebar
2. **Debugging**: Developers can inspect tool parameters and return values to troubleshoot Agent behavior
3. **Learning**: Users can understand how the Agent solves problems step-by-step through tool calls

## UI Mockup

\`\`\`
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ OpenClaw                                            [─][□][×]│
├─────────────────────────────────┬───────────────────────────┤
│                                 │ 📋 Tool Calls    [▼]     │
│   User: Help me check today's   │                           │
│         weather                 │ ├─ web_search  ✓ 0.8s    │
│                                 │ ├─ read_page   ✓ 1.2s    │
│   Agent: Sure, let me check...  │ └─ format_ans  ✓ 0.1s    │
│                                 │                           │
│   Based on the results...       │ [Click for details]       │
│                                 ├───────────────────────────┤
│   ─────────────────────────     │ 💡 When expanded:         │
│                                 │ • Tool name & parameters  │
│   Agent: Any other questions?   │ • Return results          │
│                                 │ • Execution time          │
│                                 │                           │
└─────────────────────────────────┴───────────────────────────┘
\`\`\`

## Optional Configuration Settings

- Default expand/collapse state
- Sidebar position (left/right)
- Auto-expand on new tool calls
- Max height for tool call list

## Additional Context

This feature would improve the user experience by:
- Reducing visual noise in the main conversation
- Providing better visibility into Agent tool usage
- Making it easier to debug and understand Agent behavior

title: [Bug]: Chinese IME candidate list not displayed when Quick Assistant is in fullscreen on macOS
body:
### Issue Checklist

- [x] I understand that issues are for feedback and problem solving, not for complaining in the comment section, and will provide as much information as possible to help solve the problem.
- [x] My issue is not listed in the FAQ.
- [x] I've looked at pinned issues and searched for existing Open Issues, Closed Issues, and Discussions, no similar issue or discussion was found.
- [x] I've filled in short, clear headings so that developers can quickly identify a rough idea of what to expect when flipping through the list of issues. And not "a suggestion", "stuck", etc.
- [x] I've confirmed that I am using the latest version of Cherry Studio.

### Platform

macOS

### Version

v1.9.5

### Bug Description

在 macOS 上，当某个应用窗口处于「全屏」（fullscreen）模式（即被推入独立 Space）时，唤起 Cherry Studio 的快捷助手（Quick Assistant），使用 **macOS 系统自带中文输入法**（如系统「拼音」）输入时，**IME 候选词列表无法显示**。

输入的拼音字符虽然已经被快捷助手输入框接收，但候选词面板完全不可见，导致用户无法选择正确的汉字、无法看到当前编辑状态，几乎无法在全屏环境中通过系统自带中文输入法使用快捷助手。

**仅观察到 macOS 系统自带 IME 触发该问题，第三方输入法（如微信输入法）在相同场景下表现正常，候选词可正常显示。** 这一差异提示问题可能与快捷助手窗口在全屏 Space 中的 window level / key window 协作机制相关，而非通用 IME 兼容问题。

如果切换回非全屏的桌面 Space，再唤起快捷助手输入中文，系统 IME 候选词面板可以正常显示。

### Steps To Reproduce

1. macOS 系统中将任意应用（如 Safari、VSCode）切换到全屏模式（绿色按钮 / `Control+Command+F`），系统将其推入独立 Space。
2. 在「系统设置 → 键盘 → 输入法」中确认启用并切换到 macOS **系统自带「拼音」输入法**。
3. 在该全屏 Space 中通过快捷键唤起 Cherry Studio 的快捷助手浮窗。
4. 在快捷助手输入框中输入任意拼音，例如 `nihao`。
5. 观察：输入框接收到了字符（如拼音串），但 macOS 系统 IME 的候选词面板没有出现在快捷助手输入框附近，也没有出现在屏幕其他位置。
6. 对比：在相同环境下切换为第三方输入法（如微信输入法），重复步骤 3–4，候选词面板可正常显示。

### Expected Behavior

在全屏 Space 中唤起快捷助手输入中文时，无论使用系统自带 IME 还是第三方 IME，候选词列表都应当与非全屏桌面环境一致，正常显示在输入框附近，用户可以正常选词、上屏。

### Relevant Log Output

```shell

```

### Additional Context

**关键差异线索：** 系统自带 IME 在全屏 Space 中失效，但第三方输入法（微信输入法）正常。

可能的原因方向：
- 系统自带 IME（基于 `InputMethodKit`）的候选窗由 macOS WindowServer 根据当前 **key window 所在 Space** 渲染；第三方输入法通常自管理候选窗的窗口层级（如 `NSWindowLevelPopUpMenu`），可以绕过 Space 限制。
- 这强烈提示快捷助手浮窗在全屏 Space 中：
  - 没能成为 key window（或 key window 状态与 Space 不一致），导致系统 IME 找不到正确的 anchor；
  - 或者 `collectionBehavior` 未设置 `NSWindowCollectionBehaviorCanJoinAllSpaces` / `NSWindowCollectionBehaviorFullScreenAuxiliary`，使 macOS 认为该窗口不属于当前全屏 Space。

建议从快捷助手 BrowserWindow 的 macOS 平台相关配置（`setVisibleOnAllWorkspaces({ visibleOnFullScreen: true })`、`type: 'panel'`、`focusable`、`alwaysOnTop` level 等）以及全屏 Space 下的 key window 接管时机方向排查。

title: [Bug]: MCP tool response silently drops content when structuredContent is present
body: ### Issue Checklist - [x] I understand that issues are for feedback and problem solving, not for complaining in the comment section, and will provide as much information as possible to help solve the problem. - [x] My issue is not listed in the [FAQ](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/issues/3881). - [x] I've looked at **pinned issues** and searched for existing [Open Issues](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/issues), [Closed Issues](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20state%3Aclosed), and [Discussions](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/discussions), no similar issue or discussion was found. - [x] I've filled in short, clear headings so that developers can quickly identify a rough idea of what to expect when flipping through the list of issues. And not "a suggestion", "stuck", etc. - [x] I've confirmed that I am using the latest version of Cherry Studio. ### Platform Windows ### Version 1.9.5 ### Bug Description ## MCP tool `read_file` response silently drops `content` array when `structuredContent` is present **Client:** Cherry Studio 1.9.5 **MCP Server:** `@wonderwhy-er/desktop-commander` (Desktop Commander) **Environment:** Windows 10, agent running as AI model via Cherry Studio ### Problem When calling the `read_file` tool from Desktop Commander, neither the AI model nor the user receives the actual file content. The AI only sees a tiny metadata object, and the user sees nothing in the chat UI. ### Steps To Reproduce 1. Configure Cherry Studio with Desktop Commander MCP server (`@wonderwhy-er/desktop-commander`) 2. Call the `read_file` tool with a path to any plain text file (e.g. `read_file({ path: "/tmp/test.txt" })`) 3. Observe the tool result — the AI receives only: ```json {"fileName":"test.txt","filePath":"/tmp/test.txt","fileType":"text"} ``` 4. The actual file content is not visible to the AI, nor displayed to the user in the chat ### Expected Behavior The AI should receive the file content as a `type: "text"` item in the `content` array, and/or the user should see the file text rendered in the chat UI. At minimum, the data should not be silently lost. ### Relevant Log Output ```shell ``` ### Additional Context ### Investigation We traced the issue by examining the Desktop Commander source code on GitHub (`src/handlers/filesystem-handlers.ts`). **`handleReadFile` returns BOTH fields** (lines 122-138): ```typescript // For all other files, return as text. return { content: [{ type: "text", text: textContent }], // file content here structuredContent: { // metadata here fileName: path.basename(resolvedFilePath), filePath: resolvedFilePath, fileType, }, }; ``` **`handleReadMultipleFiles` returns ONLY `content`** (no `structuredContent`): ```typescript return { content: contentItems }; ``` When we called the sibling tool `read_multiple_files` on the same file, the AI received the full content correctly — confirming the server works fine. The only difference is the presence of `structuredContent` in the response. ### Root Cause The MCP `CallToolResult` has two fields: - **`content`** (array of `ContentItem`) — the primary response payload, intended for the model/AI - **`structuredContent`** (optional JSON object) — an extension field designed for client-side UI widgets (file previews, interactive tables, etc.) When Desktop Commander's `read_file` returns both `content` (with the actual file text) and `structuredContent` (with file metadata), Cherry Studio appears to either: 1. **Give precedence to `structuredContent`**, using it as the sole tool result for the AI and discarding the `content` array entirely, OR 2. **Fail to render `content` items to the user** when `structuredContent` is present, treating them as mutually exclusive The file data is present in the server's response but never reaches either the AI's context or the user's view — it is silently lost. ### Evidence That the Server Response Is Correct Other MCP clients handle this pattern correctly: - **VS Code GitHub Copilot**: shows both `content` and `structuredContent` in the tool output view ([vscode issue #297669](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/297669): "When tools return both content and structuredContent, output shows both") - **Google ADK**: passes the entire response (both fields) to the LLM context ([adk-python discussion #3893](https://github.com/google/adk-python/discussions/3893)) - **Claude Desktop**: renders `content` in the chat UI and uses `structuredContent` for the Desktop Commander file preview widget The MCP specification requires `content` to always be present. The `structuredContent` field is additive — it should not replace or suppress `content`. ### Workaround For Desktop-commander `read_multiple_files` (even for single files) instead of `read_file`, since it returns only `content` without `structuredContent` and works correctly in Cherry Studio. _Examined with AI assistance_

### Platform

Windows

### Version

v1.9.5

### Is your feature request related to an existing issue?

This feature request is not directly related to a bug.

I searched existing issues and found some related discussions about plugin systems, CLI plugins, and pluggable capability systems, but I did not find an issue specifically about one-click model provider installation / authorization-based model service setup / provider configuration update.

Cherry Studio already supports custom model services, but users still need to manually enter the API key, Base URL, model IDs, and enable the provider. This flow works, but it can still be difficult for non-technical users and may easily lead to configuration mistakes. It also creates friction for third-party model service providers that want to offer a smoother onboarding experience.

### Desired Solution

I would like Cherry Studio to provide a model provider installation/update mechanism. This could be implemented through a plugin mechanism, provider install link, deep link, configuration import, or another suitable approach.

Expected flow:

The user clicks “Connect to Cherry Studio” either inside Cherry Studio or on a third-party provider website.
The user is redirected to the provider website to log in, authorize, activate the service, or create credentials.
After authorization is completed, the provider returns to Cherry Studio through a deep link, callback, or configuration import flow.
Cherry Studio shows a confirmation page before applying the change, including information such as the provider name, Base URL, model list, and permission scope.
After the user confirms, Cherry Studio automatically creates or updates the model provider configuration, adds or updates the model list, and enables the provider.
Cherry Studio optionally runs a connectivity check.

This mechanism does not need Cherry Studio to implement complex token lifecycle management. If the credential expires, becomes invalid, or needs to be reissued by the provider, the user can start the authorization flow again from the provider website. Cherry Studio only needs to support safely overwriting or updating the same provider configuration after user confirmation.

This feature would lower the barrier for users to configure model services and allow third-party providers to offer a more stable, secure, and maintainable onboarding experience. It would also avoid the need for third-party tools to modify local configuration files or IndexedDB directly, which is unstable and version-dependent.

title: v2 refactor: file module — overall migration tracking
body:
Tracking issue for the multi-phase File module v2 refactor. Single entry point for status and cross-batch coordination. Per-batch detail (scope, design decisions, and any follow-ups internal to that batch) lives in each batch's PR description.

**Owner:** @EurFelux

## Background

v1 file module: a single flat `FileMetadata` stored in renderer-side Dexie `db.files`, with a `FileStorage` main-side path-translation singleton.

v2 design:

- `FileEntry` — persistent DB row (UUID v4/v7, origin internal/external, ext, size, externalPath, trashedAt, timestamps)
- `FileInfo` — live descriptor produced from `fs.stat`
- `FileHandle` — tagged union (`FileEntryHandle` / `FilePathHandle`) for routing at IPC
- SQLite tables `file_entry` + `file_ref`, main-side `FileManager` lifecycle service
- Renderer reaches FileManager exclusively through IPC; Dexie `db.files` frozen, then deleted at end of refactor

Architecture: `docs/references/file/architecture.md`, `file-manager-architecture.md`. Plan: `v2-refactor-temp/docs/file-manager/rfc-file-manager.md` §9.7 + `phase2-consumer-migration.md`.

title: [Bug]: CherryIN open.cherryin.cc intermittently returns empty model list and later 401 invalid API key
body:
### Issue Checklist

- [x] I understand that issues are for feedback and problem solving, not for complaining in the comment section, and will provide as much information as possible to help solve the problem.
- [x] My issue is not listed in the FAQ.
- [x] I've searched for similar Open Issues, Closed Issues, and Discussions.
- [x] I've confirmed that I am using the latest test version.

### Platform

macOS

### Version

v1.9.6 draft

### Bug Description

When CherryIN is configured with `https://open.cherryin.cc`, the model list was empty for a period of time. After waiting for a while, fetching the model list started working again without any client-side configuration change.

In the same test window, the provider later showed available models, but Agent / knowledge-base calls still failed with:

```text
API Key 无效，请检查并重新配置
Error invoking remote method 'knowledge-base:search': Error: 401 Invalid API key
MODEL_AUTHENTICATION
```

This makes the failure look like an API key problem, but the intermittent behavior suggests it may also involve the `open.cherryin.cc` route, DNS/region routing, gateway cache, or a transient upstream issue. The tester also asked whether this could be related to CherryIN's server being in Singapore.

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Open Cherry Studio v1.9.6 draft.
2. Configure CherryIN provider with API host `https://open.cherryin.cc`.
3. Click `获取模型列表`.
4. Observe that the model list is empty for a period of time.
5. Try again later without changing the local config.
6. The model list becomes available again.
7. In Agent mode, use a CherryIN model such as `agent/glm-5.1 | CherryIN`.
8. Trigger an Agent / knowledge-base call.
9. The message can fail with `401 Invalid API key / MODEL_AUTHENTICATION`.

### Expected Behavior

- `/v1/models` should return a stable model list for a valid CherryIN key and host.
- If the backend is temporarily unavailable or region routing fails, the client should show a network/server error instead of making the user think the API key is invalid.
- The model-list endpoint and chat / knowledge-base request path should use consistent authentication and routing behavior.

### Actual Behavior

- Model list can be empty for a while, then recover later without local config changes.
- Agent / knowledge-base call can still show `401 Invalid API key / MODEL_AUTHENTICATION`.

### Additional Context

Observed during v1.9.6 system testing. Suggested backend checks:

- Compare `/v1/models` and chat / knowledge-base request logs in the same time window.
- Check request id, region, gateway status, upstream status, and authentication decision path.
- Check whether `open.cherryin.cc` DNS / routing to the Singapore service can intermittently fail or route to a different auth/cache state.

Original tester note:

> 有一段时间，他在这个 cc 域名之下，拉取模型为空。过了一阵子，突然又好了，不知道是否跟 cherryin 的服务器在新加坡有关。

title: [Bug]: Tool approval buttons are hidden behind collapsed or long tool cards, making authorization hard to discover
body:
### Issue Checklist

- [x] I understand that issues are for feedback and problem solving, not for complaining in the comment section, and will provide as much information as possible to help solve the problem.
- [x] My issue is not listed in the FAQ.
- [x] I've searched for similar Open Issues, Closed Issues, and Discussions.
- [x] I've confirmed that I am using the latest test version.

### Platform

macOS

### Version

v1.9.6 draft

### Bug Description

When an Agent tool call requires user authorization, the approval action is not discoverable enough:

1. In collapsed state, the user does not know that they need to click and expand the tool card before they can approve it.
2. After expanding, if the tool-call content is long, the `Run / Cancel` approval buttons can be pushed to the bottom of the card. The user may need to scroll inside a long content area and still may not notice the approval buttons.

This makes the Agent appear stuck even though it is actually waiting for user approval.

This is related to the closed issue #15038, but v1.9.6 still exposes a blocking approval UX problem in the long-content tool card scenario. The screenshot shows a file-write tool call waiting for approval. The generated file preview is long, and the approval controls are only visible at the bottom after scrolling.

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Open Cherry Studio v1.9.6 draft.
2. Enter Agent mode.
3. Ask the Agent to perform a multi-step task that writes or modifies a file, for example:

   ```text
   搜索黄金价格，分析涨跌原因，写一份报告，再做成 ppt
   ```

4. Wait until the Agent triggers a tool call that requires approval.
5. Observe the tool card in the message stream.
6. In collapsed state, the card does not make it obvious that approval is required.
7. Expand the tool card when the tool-call content is long.
8. The approval buttons can be hidden at the bottom of the card, requiring extra scrolling and still being easy to miss.

### Expected Behavior

Approval should be obvious and reachable whenever the task is blocked by user authorization.

Recommended behavior:

- Approval cards should default to expanded when they are waiting for user action; or
- The collapsed state should show a clear `Waiting for approval` status and primary action; and
- `Run / Cancel` should be sticky in the visible area of the tool card when the content is long.

### Actual Behavior

- The user has to know that they should click to expand before seeing authorization controls.
- Long tool-call content can push `Run / Cancel` out of view.
- The task appears to be running or stuck, while it is actually waiting for user approval.

### Additional Context

Original tester note:

> 当需要授权的时候，我并不知道需要点击展开才可以点击授权。而且有的时候因为里面的内容太长了，有时候你下滑都不一定看得到授权按钮。

Related:

- #15038 was closed for the collapsed approval card discoverability issue.
- This v1.9.6 test case adds the long-content / hidden approval button scenario and should be verified across all Agent tool approval cards, not only MCP cards.

title: [Bug]: Knowledge base embedding auth failure is reported as generic chat model API key error
body:
### Issue Checklist

- [x] I understand that issues are for feedback and problem solving, not for complaining in the comment section, and will provide as much information as possible to help solve the problem.
- [x] My issue is not listed in the FAQ.
- [x] I've searched for similar Open Issues, Closed Issues, and Discussions.
- [x] I've confirmed that I am using the latest test version.

### Platform

macOS

### Version

v1.9.6 draft

### Bug Description

Direct chat with the CherryIN chat model works, but the same conversation fails after selecting a knowledge base. The error card says the API key is invalid and asks the user to go to the model provider settings.

After troubleshooting, the tester found that the failing key/path is not the current chat model key. The failure comes from the knowledge base embedding model, shown as `qwen/qwen3-embedding-8b` with provider `CherryIN`.

This is confusing because:

- The current chat model (`agent/glm-5.1 | CherryIN`) works.
- The user did not intentionally change the key and has always used CherryIN.
- The error message directs the user to the generic model-provider settings instead of pointing to the knowledge base embedding model/provider.
- There is no clear way to inspect which provider/key/model the knowledge-base search path actually used.

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Open Cherry Studio v1.9.6 draft.
2. Use a CherryIN chat model such as `agent/glm-5.1 | CherryIN`.
3. Send a normal direct chat message.
4. Confirm direct chat works.
5. Select a knowledge base.
6. Send a message that triggers knowledge-base search.
7. Observe the error:

   ```text
   API Key 无效，请检查并重新配置
   Error invoking remote method 'knowledge-base:search': Error: 401 Invalid API key
   MODEL_AUTHENTICATION
   ```

8. Open the knowledge base page.
9. The embedding model is `qwen/qwen3-embedding-8b` with provider `CherryIN`.

### Expected Behavior

When knowledge-base retrieval fails due to embedding-model authentication, the error should clearly identify the failing stage and configuration:

- Stage: knowledge-base search / embedding / rerank / chat completion.
- Actual model used: e.g. `qwen/qwen3-embedding-8b`.
- Actual provider used: e.g. `CherryIN`.
- The action button should jump to the knowledge base embedding-model settings, not only the current chat model provider settings.

The user should be able to distinguish:

- Chat model key works, but embedding model key fails.
- Knowledge-base search fails before chat completion.
- Provider config may be stale, cached, or independently stored for knowledge base.

### Actual Behavior

The error is generic:

- It says `API Key 无效`.
- It points the user to model provider settings.
- It does not explain that the failure came from the knowledge base embedding model.

The user initially checks the chat model provider key, which is working, and does not know how to continue troubleshooting.

### Additional Context

Original tester note:

> 我直接对话是没问题的，但是当我选择知识库的时候，却有报错提示我去跳转到模型服务商那边，但我的 Key 是没有问题的。排查之后才发现，我的知识库选择的嵌入向量对应的 Key 失效。但实际上我并没有换过 Key，一直是 CherryIN。但目前不知道怎么排查这个问题。

Suggested things to investigate:

- Whether knowledge bases store a separate provider config/key snapshot.
- Whether embedding provider config can become stale after CherryIN model/key changes.
- Whether the embedding model still maps to the same CherryIN provider/account.
- Whether the error card can include a structured chain such as `knowledge-base.search -> embedding(qwen/qwen3-embedding-8b, CherryIN) -> 401`.

title: [Feature]: Make generated Markdown and HTML artifact paths clickable in Agent responses
body:
### Issue Checklist

- [x] I understand that issues are for feedback and problem solving, not for complaining in the comment section, and will provide as much information as possible to help solve the problem.
- [x] My issue is not listed in the FAQ.
- [x] I've searched for similar Open Issues, Closed Issues, and Discussions.
- [x] I've confirmed that I am using the latest test version.

### Platform

macOS

### Version

v1.9.6 draft

### Feature / UX Problem

After an Agent task generates local artifacts, the final answer shows Markdown / HTML output paths as plain text or code-styled text. They are not clickable, so the user has to manually locate the output directory and open the files.

Example output shown in the message:

```text
报告: output/黄金价格分析报告.md
PPT: output/gold_ppt.html
```

The files are already generated, but the handoff is inconvenient because the user cannot directly click the path to open or preview the artifact.

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Open Cherry Studio v1.9.6 draft.
2. Run an Agent task that generates local artifacts, for example:

   ```text
   Search for gold prices, analyze the reasons for price changes, write a report, and create a PPT
   ```

3. Wait until the Agent completes and reports generated files.
4. The final message includes local relative paths such as `output/xxx.md` and `output/xxx.html`.
5. Try to click those paths.
6. Nothing opens; the user must manually find the directory and open the file.

### Expected Behavior

Generated local artifacts should be actionable from the Agent response.

Recommended behavior:

- Render generated file paths as clickable file links.
- Support actions such as `Open`, `Reveal in Finder`, or `Preview`.
- Resolve relative paths against the Agent task workspace/output directory.
- For HTML artifacts, provide a direct preview/open action.
- If direct file opening is restricted for security reasons, show an explicit file card/button instead of plain text.

### Actual Behavior

The Agent shows the generated file paths, but they are not clickable. The user has to manually locate the files.

### Additional Context

Original tester note:

> The HTML and Markdown produced by the Agent are displayed as non-clickable, requiring users to find the corresponding file directory themselves, which is very inconvenient.

This is especially painful for final deliverables like reports, HTML slide decks, and Markdown files, where the expected next step is to inspect the generated artifact immediately.

## Bug Description

**Version:** v1.9.5  
**OS:** macOS 26.4.1

### Issue 1: Topic generation runs even with auto-generate disabled
The topic generation feature is executed even when the user has explicitly unchecked the "auto-generate" option.

### Issue 2: Topic generation fails/times out with local models
When auto-generate is enabled but a **local model** is selected, topic generation frequently fails or times out — even with models that achieve ~1000 tokens/s prefilling speed at low token counts (e.g., 10 tokens). The same operation works without issues when using the official default model.

**Steps to reproduce:**
1. Enable auto-generate for topic generation
2. Select a local model (e.g., Ollama or LM Studio)
3. Trigger topic generation
4. Result: Failure or timeout, even for very short prompts

**Expected behavior:** Topic generation should work reliably with local models, or at minimum not fail silently when the model is capable of fast responses.

### Bug Description

Every execute_code tool response from a custom API provider (Hermes Agent) triggers three consecutive AI_TypeValidationError popups. This error does NOT occur with other tool types (web_search, terminal, etc.) – only execute_code.

The error is caused by a Zod union validation: Cherry Studio expects either a "choices" array (standard OpenAI ChatCompletion) or an "error" object, but receives raw execute_code metadata fields instead.

Two variants of the error occur per call:

1. During execution (status: "running"): The API response contains non-standard fields like "emoji", "label", "tool", "toolCallId", "status" that are not part of the OpenAI schema.

2. After completion (status: "completed"): Same invalid_union – Zod can't parse the response as either a "choices" array or an "error" object.

Screenshot attached

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Set up a custom API provider (e.g. Hermes Agent) that returns execute_code tool calls with non-standard fields
2. Send any message that triggers code execution
3. Three TypeValidationError popups appear per execute_code call

Non-standard fields in the response:
- "emoji": "🐍"
- "label": "from hermes_tools import ..."
- "toolCallId": "call_..."
- "status": "running" or "completed"

Zod union validation:
- 1st attempt: expects "choices" as array → fails
- 2nd attempt: expects "error" as object → fails
→ invalid_union error

### Expected Behavior

Cherry Studio should tolerate extra execute_code-specific fields in the API response (use .passthrough() or .strip() in the Zod schema definition), or provide a fallback mechanism when the response contains neither "choices" nor "error".

The execute_code tool type appears to use a different internal format than standard OpenAI tools – the Zod validation should be adjusted for the custom provider use case.

Identical error, Value: {"tool":"execute_code","toolCallId":"call_1e07fbc0b046450eaf9b7","status":"completed"}.

body:

### Platform

macOS

### Version

v1.9.6

### Is your feature request related to an existing issue?

Cherry Claw / the intelligent agent page currently runs through the `claude-code` agent path and invokes `@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk`. When a user configures a NewAPI model such as `gpt-5.5` that uses the OpenAI-compatible standard format, the agent path still expects an Anthropic-compatible backend and can fall back to requests against `https://api.anthropic.com` instead of the configured NewAPI endpoint.

This prevents OpenAI-compatible NewAPI models from being used reliably in Cherry Claw, even though the same provider/model may work in the normal chat provider path.

### Desired Solution

Add OpenAI-compatible standard format support to the Cherry Claw / `claude-code` intelligent agent path.

Expected behavior:

- Users can select a configured NewAPI/OpenAI-compatible model such as `gpt-5.5` for Cherry Claw.
- The agent runtime should not request `https://api.anthropic.com` for that model.
- The runtime should route Claude Agent SDK Anthropic Messages traffic through a local Cherry Studio compatibility layer when the selected provider is OpenAI-compatible.
- The compatibility layer should forward requests to the configured provider `apiHost` using OpenAI Chat Completions or Responses format as appropriate.
- Existing Anthropic-compatible providers should keep their current behavior.

### Alternative Solutions

- Require every provider used by Cherry Claw to expose an Anthropic-compatible `anthropicApiHost`. This works for some gateways but excludes standard OpenAI-compatible models.
- Rewrite the agent runtime to bypass Claude Agent SDK for OpenAI-compatible models. This is more invasive and risks losing Claude Code tool orchestration behavior.

### Additional Information

Relevant current code path:

- Renderer agent message stream: `src/renderer/src/store/thunk/messageThunk.ts`
- Agent API route: `src/main/apiServer/routes/agents/handlers/messages.ts`
- Session stream service: `src/main/services/agents/services/SessionMessageService.ts`
- Claude Code runtime env setup: `src/main/services/agents/services/claudecode/index.ts`
- Existing OpenAI-compatible chat API service: `src/main/apiServer/services/chat-completion.ts`

Implementation should update API documentation and include tests for request translation and streaming behavior.

title: [Feature]: Add WeCom and DingTalk Channel Adapters
body:
## Background

Cherry Studio's CherryClaw agents support IM channel integration through a pluggable adapter system (#13359). Telegram, WeChat (personal), and Feishu have shipped. But the two dominant Chinese enterprise IM platforms — **WeCom (企业微信)** and **DingTalk (钉钉)** — are still missing. For most enterprise teams in China, who overwhelmingly standardize on one of these two, this gap blocks adopting CherryClaw as a work-integrated AI agent. Personal WeChat does not satisfy enterprise needs (no work/personal separation, no group bot semantics, no administrative install path).

## Goal

CherryClaw users can configure WeCom and DingTalk channels so the agent receives and responds to messages in those platforms' groups and 1-on-1 chats, with feature parity to the existing Telegram / WeChat / Feishu adapters.

## Spec

- WeCom and DingTalk both appear in the CherryClaw channel catalog alongside Telegram / WeChat / Feishu.
- Configuration UI accepts each platform's standard bot credentials (the credential shape mirrors what the platform officially documents — e.g., webhook URL + signing secret, or app key + secret).
- Inbound: when a user sends a message to the configured bot (group or 1-on-1), CherryClaw receives it and processes it as a session message.
- Outbound: agent responses are delivered back to the same chat, with streaming / typing indicators consistent with existing adapters.
- Attachments: file and image attachments work both directions (consistent with #14489).
- Configuration errors (invalid credentials, network unreachable) surface clear, specific error messages and do not enable the channel.
- Multiple channels coexist on one agent: a single CherryClaw can have WeCom + DingTalk + Feishu enabled simultaneously, each with isolated chat history.

## Verification

- User opens a CherryClaw agent → Channel settings → catalog lists Telegram, WeChat, Feishu, **WeCom**, **DingTalk**.
- User configures WeCom with valid bot credentials → in a WeCom group with the bot, user sends "总结今天 OpenAI 的发布会"; bot replies with the summary in the same group within ~5 seconds, typing indicator visible during generation.
- Same flow on DingTalk: user adds the bot to a DingTalk group, sends a message, agent responds in the same group.
- User sends an image in a DingTalk group → CherryClaw receives it and uses it as context in the response (no "image not supported" fallback).
- User configures WeCom with an invalid webhook → settings UI shows a specific error like "WeCom credential verification failed: webhook returned 401" and the channel stays disabled.
- A single CherryClaw agent with both WeCom and DingTalk enabled receives messages from both platforms independently; chat history in WeCom does not leak into DingTalk's context.

## Related

#13359 #14005 #14489

PRs: #13714 #14421

title: [Feature]: Aggregated Third-Party Web Search (Brave / Perplexity / ...) — Cherry-Hosted Paid Service
body:
## Background

Top-tier web search providers like **Brave Search** and **Perplexity** require accounts and API keys that users in mainland China cannot easily obtain (no overseas billing, no overseas phone, etc.). At the May 2026 food-expo, a researcher explicitly said he and his school would happily **pay extra** if Cherry Studio aggregated these APIs as a built-in service. This is a clear monetization signal on a real friction point — users want premium search and are willing to pay, but the access barrier (not the cost) is what's blocking them today.

## Goal

Cherry Studio users access top-tier third-party web search engines through a single Cherry-aggregated entry point — no individual overseas accounts, no manual API key management, no provider-specific config — for a transparent Cherry-managed fee.

## Spec

- Web Search settings expose a "**Cherry-Aggregated Search**" provider option, alongside the existing per-provider options (Tavily, Exa, etc.).
- Cherry-Aggregated Search supports at least **Brave Search** and **Perplexity Search** at launch; the provider list is curated and grows.
- Users access the service via a single Cherry account credential / subscription — they do not manage per-provider keys.
- Pricing is transparent in the settings UI: query rate, subscription tier, remaining balance (whichever model ships).
- The service is exposed as a backend for the unified `web_search` capability tool (per #14895) — Agents calling `web_search` can use Cherry-Aggregated Search transparently.
- Per-query results indicate which underlying provider produced them, for transparency.

## Verification

- User opens Settings → Web Search → sees "Cherry-Aggregated Search" alongside Tavily / Exa, with clear pricing display.
- User subscribes / tops up → immediately queries Brave-quality results without entering any Brave API key.
- Same user can query Perplexity-style answers without a Perplexity account.
- Agent (per #14895) calls `web_search` with Cherry-Aggregated backend → receives results from underlying provider, response cites which provider.
- User in mainland China without VPN can use the service end-to-end — Cherry's aggregation endpoint is reachable from China.
- When the user's balance is exhausted or subscription expires, settings UI shows a clear renewal CTA and `web_search` calls return a specific "service quota exceeded" error rather than a raw HTTP failure.

## Related

#14895 (Pluggable Capability System) — `web_search` is one of the capability tools listed there.

每个技能描述几百 token，每回合浪费上千 token，且随轮次线性累积。使用 API Key 的用户直接承担经济损失。

### Desired Solution

复用 CLI 子进程，让 zN6 技能去重机制跨回合生效：

维护 CLI 进程池，同一 topic 的连续消息复用同一个进程
或在 Cherry Studio 桥接层自行维护技能列表的发送状态，避免 SDK 重复注入
这样技能描述仅在会话开始时注入一次，后续回合不再重复。

### Alternative Solutions

提供一个环境变量或配置开关，让用户自行选择是否在每回合注入技能 system-reminder。

title: PRD: Mise-based tool manager for Cherry Studio
body:
## Problem Statement

Cherry Studio currently manages external CLI binaries (uv, bun, ovms, openclaw) through ad-hoc per-tool install scripts (`resources/scripts/install-*.js`). Each new tool requires a bespoke download script, a dedicated IPC channel, and custom extraction/placement logic. This approach doesn't scale — adding a new tool means touching 4+ files and duplicating error-prone download/extract/chmod boilerplate.

Users and developers need a unified, declarative way to manage CLI tools that Cherry Studio depends on — similar to how the [stella project](https://github.com/CherryHQ/stella) uses mise as an embedded tool installer with a YAML manifest.

## Solution

Embed [mise](https://mise.jdx.dev/) (a polyglot tool version manager) into Cherry Studio as a bundled binary. Expose a single `MiseService` lifecycle service that:

1. **Reads a tool list from the Preference system** (`feature.mise.tools`) — each entry is a `{ name, tool, version? }` tuple using mise-native tool keys (e.g., `github:sharkdp/fd`, `uv`, `bun`).
2. **Reconciles on startup** — compares the desired tool list against a local state file, installs missing or outdated tools via mise, and copies resulting binaries to `~/.cherrystudio/bin/`.
3. **Runs mise in an isolated environment** — dedicated `MISE_DATA_DIR`, `MISE_CONFIG_DIR`, etc. under `~/.cherrystudio/mise/` so it never interferes with the user's own mise setup.
4. **Exposes IPC** for the renderer to trigger installs, removals, reconciliation, and state queries.

**Scope decision:** OAuth-based tool authentication (as in anna) is explicitly out of scope. This is tool download only.

## User Stories

1. As a user, I want Cherry Studio to automatically install CLI tools it depends on at startup, so that features like MCP servers, code execution, and web search work without manual setup.
2. As a user, I want to see which tools are installed and their versions, so that I can troubleshoot issues.
3. As a user, I want to add custom tools to be managed by Cherry Studio (e.g., `fd`, `ripgrep`), so that agents and MCP servers can use them.
4. As a user, I want to remove a managed tool, so that I can free disk space or resolve conflicts.
5. As a user, I want tool installations to not interfere with my system-wide mise or other tool managers, so that my development environment stays clean.
6. As a developer, I want a single service to manage all CLI tool downloads instead of writing per-tool install scripts, so that adding new tools is a one-line config change.
7. As a developer, I want the mise binary to be bundled at build time (not downloaded at runtime), so that first-run UX is fast and doesn't depend on network availability for the bootstrapper itself.
8. As a developer, I want tool install state to be persisted and cache-checked, so that startup reconciliation is fast when tools are already at the correct version.
9. As a user, I want to trigger a manual re-install/update of a specific tool from the UI, so that I can recover from corrupted installs.
10. As a user, I want to configure tool versions (or pin to "latest"), so that I have control over what gets installed.
11. As a developer, I want the tool manager to work on macOS (arm64/x64), Linux (x64/arm64), and Windows (x64), since Cherry Studio ships on all these platforms.
12. As a user, I want a settings UI to manage the tool list (add/remove/edit tools), so that I don't have to manually edit config files.

## Implementation Decisions

- **Mise binary bundled at build time** in `resources/binaries/{platform}-{arch}/mise` (same pattern as RTK). Downloaded via `scripts/download-mise-binary.js`, hooked into `scripts/before-pack.js`.
- **Isolated mise environment**: All mise dirs (`MISE_DATA_DIR`, `MISE_CONFIG_DIR`, `MISE_CACHE_DIR`, `MISE_STATE_DIR`, `MISE_SHIMS_DIR`) plus `HOME` and `XDG_*` are redirected to `~/.cherrystudio/mise/`. Only whitelisted env vars (PATH, proxy, TLS, GitHub tokens) pass through.
- **Tool config in Preference system**: `feature.mise.tools` key of type `MiseTool[]` where `MiseTool = { name: string; tool: string; version?: string }`. The `tool` field uses mise-native tool keys (`github:owner/repo`, `uv`, `bun`, `npm:pkg`, etc.).
- **Install flow per tool**: Write a temporary `mise.toml` → `mise trust` → `mise install <tool>` → `mise which <name>` to locate binary → copy to `~/.cherrystudio/bin/`.
- **State tracking**: JSON file at `~/.cherrystudio/mise/state.json` recording installed tool name, mise tool key, version, and install timestamp. Cache hit = skip reinstall (unless version is "latest" or empty).
- **Path registry additions**: `feature.mise.data` and `feature.mise.state_file`.
- **IPC channels**: `mise:reconcile`, `mise:install-tool`, `mise:remove-tool`, `mise:get-state`.
- **Service lifecycle**: `MiseService` at `Phase.Background` — registers IPC handlers in `onInit`, then reconciles if the tool list is non-empty.

## Testing Decisions

- MiseService unit tests should mock `execFileAsync` and filesystem operations to verify:
  - Reconcile logic (skip cached, install missing, handle failures)
  - State load/save correctness
  - Isolated env construction
- Integration test with real mise binary is desirable but can be a follow-up (requires mise on CI).
- Use the project's existing mock system (see `tests/__mocks__/README.md`).

## Out of Scope

- OAuth/authentication for tools (anna's `oauth_provider`, `session_env`)
- Prompt injection or skill bundling from tool plugins
- Migration of existing install scripts (uv, bun, ovms) to use mise — that's a separate effort once this foundation is proven
- Renderer UI for managing tools (separate issue, depends on this backend)
- Auto-update of tools on a schedule (can be added later via `registerInterval`)

title: [Feature]: Bundle claude-code-setup as a Featured One-Click Plugin for Cherry Studio Agents
body:
## Background

Anthropic recently released the `claude-code-setup` plugin (installable via `/plugin install claude-code-setup@claude-plugins-official` in Claude Code). Once active, it scans the current context and walks the user step-by-step through installing recommended skills, MCP servers, and sub-agents. Claude Code users widely report it dramatically improves the out-of-the-box experience. Cherry Studio's agents are built on the Claude Code SDK and read the same `.claude/plugins/` plugin format, so this plugin is structurally compatible with any Cherry agent. However, Cherry Studio currently strips the `/plugin` slash command and does not surface `claude-code-setup` anywhere in its UI — agent users have no path to discover or install it. The result: a high-value plugin sits behind a wall, and most Cherry agent users continue to run on bare defaults.

## Goal

Cherry Studio features `claude-code-setup` as a one-click installable plugin available to all Cherry agents, so any agent user can adopt it without knowing its name, marketplace, or installation syntax — and once installed, can invoke it normally inside any agent.

## Spec

- `claude-code-setup` appears as a featured / recommended entry in the unified plugin/skill management surface that Cherry Studio agents share, with a clear name, one-line description, and an "Install" button.
- The description tells the user what the plugin does in plain language — "scans your context and walks you through installing recommended skills, MCP servers, and sub-agents for your agent" — not a generic "an Anthropic plugin".
- Clicking Install performs the full installation (fetching from the upstream registry, writing into the plugin directory Cherry agents read) without requiring any slash command or terminal input from the user.
- The install progresses with visible feedback (downloading / installing / installed); failures (network, registry, invalid manifest) show a clear error message and keep the entry installable for retry.
- After install, the entry shows an "Installed" badge and an "Uninstall" action, consistent with how other installed plugins/skills are presented.
- Once installed, the plugin is available to any Cherry agent the user opens or creates — built-in or user-created — through that agent's normal plugin/skill invocation path; the user does not need to install per-agent and does not need to type `/plugin` or any Claude Code-native command Cherry Studio doesn't expose.
- The featured entry is visible on the plugin/skill surface without requiring the user to type a search term or navigate to a hidden submenu — discoverability is the point.

## Verification

- A new Cherry Studio user, who has never heard of `claude-code-setup`, opens any Cherry agent and sees the plugin featured with its description and an Install button — without searching, without typing a command.
- User clicks Install → plugin is installed end-to-end in one action; UI shows progress, ends with an "Installed" badge.
- User then invokes the plugin in Cherry Claw → the plugin's own step-by-step setup behavior runs; Cherry Studio does NOT reimplement the scanning or recommendation logic.
- Same user opens Cherry Assistant (a different agent) → the same installed plugin is invokable there too, without a second install.
- User creates a brand-new custom agent → the same installed plugin is immediately available in that new agent.
- User clicks Uninstall → plugin is removed from the shared install location; subsequent invocations in any agent no longer find it; the featured entry returns to its installable state.
- Network is offline → Install action surfaces "Couldn't reach the plugin registry, retry later"; clicking install again after network restores succeeds.
- User has already installed `claude-code-setup` through some other route (e.g. manually copied into `.claude/plugins/`) → Cherry Studio detects this and shows the entry as "Installed" rather than offering to install again.
- Featured entry is visible on a clean install of Cherry Studio without any specific agent context, opened project, or search query.

title: feat: Mise-based tool manager — build bundling, service, IPC, preferences, UI, tests
body:
## Parent

#15181

## What to build

A complete mise-based tool management system for Cherry Studio. Mise is bundled at build time and used at runtime to download/install CLI tools into `~/.cherrystudio/bin/`. The tool list is stored in the Preference system (`feature.mise.tools`). A `MiseService` lifecycle service reconciles on startup, and IPC channels allow the renderer to install/remove/query tools. A settings UI lets users manage their tool list.

### End-to-end behavior

1. **Build time**: `download-mise-binary.js` fetches the mise binary for the target platform and places it in `resources/binaries/{platform}-{arch}/mise`. `before-pack.js` invokes this and filters out non-target binaries.

2. **App startup**: `MiseService` (Phase.Background) locates the bundled mise binary, reads `feature.mise.tools` from preferences, and reconciles — installing any tools not already at the target version. Mise runs in an isolated environment under `~/.cherrystudio/mise/` to avoid conflicts with the user's own mise.

3. **Runtime IPC**: Renderer can call `mise:reconcile`, `mise:install-tool`, `mise:remove-tool`, `mise:get-state` to manage tools dynamically.

4. **Settings UI**: A tool manager page in settings where users can view installed tools and their versions, add new tools (name + mise tool key + optional version), remove tools, and trigger reinstalls.

5. **Preload**: Expose mise IPC channels through the preload bridge so the renderer can access them.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Mise binary is downloaded at build time for all supported platforms (darwin-arm64, darwin-x64, linux-x64, linux-arm64, win32-x64)
- [ ] `MiseService` starts in Background phase, finds bundled mise, reconciles tool list from preferences
- [ ] Mise runs in isolated env (`~/.cherrystudio/mise/`) — does not read/write user's own mise config
- [ ] Tools are installed to `~/.cherrystudio/bin/` and tracked in `~/.cherrystudio/mise/state.json`
- [ ] Cache hit: tools at correct version are skipped during reconcile
- [ ] IPC channels work: reconcile, install single tool, remove tool, get state
- [ ] `feature.mise.tools` preference (type `MiseTool[]`) is defined and accessible via `usePreference`
- [ ] Preload bridge exposes mise IPC channels to renderer
- [ ] Settings UI page for managing tools (list, add, remove, version display)
- [ ] Unit tests for MiseService (reconcile logic, state management, env isolation)
- [ ] Works on macOS, Linux, and Windows

## Blocked by

None — can start immediately

- [x] My issue is not listed in the [FAQ](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/issues/3881).

### Platform

Windows

### Version

latest

### Bug Description

When using Cherry Studio’s Claude Code mode with an MCP server enabled, Claude requests fail with an Anthropic API 400 error.

The MCP server config itself is very simple and does not contain defer_loading or cache_control:
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "avalonia_devtools": {
      "command": "avdt",
      "args": ["mcp"],
      "env": {
        "AVALONIA_TOOLS_LICENSE_KEY": "your-license-key"
      }
    }
  }
}

However, Cherry Studio’s Claude Code integration appears to generate tool definitions where the same MCP tool contains both:{
  "defer_loading": true,
  "cache_control": {}
}

This causes Anthropic API to reject the request:
Tool 'modify_mcp14' cannot have both defer_loading=true and cache_control set.
Tools with defer_loading cannot use prompt caching.

A similar error also occurs with another generated tool name:
Tool 'monitor_mcp13' cannot have both defer_loading=true and cache_control set.
Tools with defer_loading cannot use prompt caching.


The same MCP server works correctly in:

Official Claude CLI / Claude Code
Kiro
Normal Claude chat mode in Cherry Studio

So the MCP server itself and the license/environment configuration are valid. The issue seems specific to Cherry Studio’s Claude Code MCP adapter.

Expected behavior: Cherry Studio should not apply cache_control to tools that have defer_loading=true, or it should disable prompt caching for deferred MCP tools.

In summary, Cherry Studio appears to be sending invalid Anthropic tool definitions when Claude Code mode, MCP tools, prompt caching, and tool defer loading are used together.

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Install and open Cherry Studio on Windows.

2. Configure an MCP server in Cherry Studio with the following config:

   ```json
   {
     "mcpServers": {
       "avalonia_devtools": {
         "command": "avdt",
         "args": ["mcp"],
         "env": {
           "AVALONIA_TOOLS_LICENSE_KEY": "your-license-key"
         }
       }
     }
   }
Enable the MCP server in Cherry Studio.
Open Cherry Studio's Claude Code mode.

Send any prompt that causes Claude Code to load or use MCP tools, for example:

Use the avalonia_devtools MCP to inspect the current Avalonia application.
The request fails with an Anthropic API 400 error.

Observed error:

AI_ProviderSpecificError: Claude Code returned an error result: API Error: 400 {
  "error": {
    "type": "<nil>",
    "message": "Tool 'modify_mcp14' cannot have both defer_loading=true and cache_control set. Tools with defer_loading cannot use prompt caching."
  },
  "type": "error"
}

Sometimes the generated tool name is different, for example:

Tool 'monitor_mcp13' cannot have both defer_loading=true and cache_control set. Tools with defer_loading cannot use prompt caching.
Disable the MCP server or avoid Claude Code mode, and the error no longer occurs.

The same MCP server works correctly in the official Claude CLI:

claude mcp add avalonia_devtools -t stdio -e AVALONIA_TOOLS_LICENSE_KEY=xxx -- avdt mcp
claude
/mcp
The same MCP server also works in Kiro and normal Claude chat mode in Cherry Studio.

Expected result:

Claude Code mode should load and use the MCP server normally.

Actual result:

Cherry Studio Claude Code mode appears to send MCP tool definitions that contain both defer_loading=true and cache_control, which Anthropic API rejects.

title: [Bug] API Server crashes after switching model — port conflict between API Server and local inference service
body:
> ⚠️ 本报告由 AI 协助整理。

### Bug Description

当 API Server 端口（默认 23333）与本地模型推理服务端口相同时，切换模型会触发 API Server 重启，导致端口冲突并崩溃。

### Steps To Reproduce

1. 启动 Cherry Studio，开启 API Server（默认端口 23333）
2. 添加并运行本地模型服务，也配置在同一端口（23333）上
3. 在对话中切换模型（例如切换到 V4-PRO）
4. API Server 尝试重启，发现端口 23333 已被模型推理服务占用
5. API Server 绑定失败，直接崩溃

### Expected Behavior

- API Server 在重启时应自动检测端口冲突，或使用 `SO_REUSEADDR` 优雅处理
- 或者在启动时校验端口，提示用户端口已被占用

### Additional Context

- 将 API Server 端口改为其他端口（如 1000）后问题消失，确认是端口冲突导致
- `netstat` 确认 Cherry Studio 进程（PID 4664）同时监听两个端口时，两者各不冲突；但共用同一端口时后者无法绑定
- Windows 11 Pro，Cherry Studio 最新版本

### Workaround

手动将 API Server 端口改为未被占用的端口。

### Platform

Windows

### Version

1.9.6

### Is your feature request related to an existing issue?

Cherry Studio IndexedDB Contamination: Problem, Root Cause & MCP Guardian Solution

    1. The Problem

    In Cherry Studio v0.9.21, MCP server configurations are stored in Electron's IndexedDB (backed by LevelDB at
    %APPDATA%\Roaming\CherryStudio\IndexedDB\file__0.indexeddb.leveldb\). When a user pastes MCP JSON configuration
    containing Linux-style paths (e.g., "cwd": "/" or "cwd": "/root/project") directly from an AI response into the
    Cherry Studio config UI, these invalid fields get written into IndexedDB and persisted. Subsequently, when Cherry
    Studio calls child_process.spawn() with this invalid cwd parameter, the Linux-format path cannot be resolved on
    Windows, causing all MCP server processes to fail at startup. The UI only checks whether a record exists to
    display a "Connected" status, so everything appears normal while all MCP tools are actually dead. Restarting
    Cherry Studio does not help (IndexedDB is persistent storage). The only recovery option is to delete the entire
    IndexedDB directory and let Cherry Studio regenerate the default state — but this wipes all custom MCP
    configurations.

    2. Root Cause

    The issue stems from three missing layers of protection: ① No field whitelist at storage layer — Cherry Studio
    does not filter incoming JSON fields before writing to IndexedDB, allowing undeclared fields like cwd to be
    persisted; ② No parameter validation before spawn — the cwd value is passed directly to spawn() without checking
    whether it's a valid Windows path; ③ No diagnostic tools for users — once contaminated, there is no way to detect
    or repair without full deletion.

### Desired Solution

3. MCP Guardian — A Fundamental Solution

    MCP Guardian is an external defense, detection, and repair tool system that requires no modification to Cherry
    Studio's source code. It eliminates the impact of IndexedDB contamination at its root through a wrapper layer.

    Architecture: Instead of launching MCP servers directly, Cherry Studio goes through mcp-launcher.bat →
    mcp-guardian.js as an intermediary. The wrapper intercepts all parameters before spawn(), validates the cwd field
    (detecting Linux paths like / or /root/), and automatically falls back to a user-configured safe working directory
     when an invalid value is found — all while logging audit trails. This ensures that no matter what dirty cwd value
     is stored in IndexedDB, the actual MCP process always runs in the correct directory, effectively neutralizing the
     contamination.

    Three Components:
     - 🛡️ Guardian Core (mcp-guardian.js + mcp-launcher.bat): Runtime defense layer — parameter validation, safe
       fallback, stdio bridging. Serves as the unified entry point for all MCP servers.
     - 🔍 Health Scanner (mcp-scanner.js --scan): Offline IndexedDB LevelDB scanner that outputs a contamination report,
        pinpointing which servers are affected and what invalid cwd values were written.
     - 🔧 Repair Tool (mcp-scanner.js --fix): One-click repair that removes or replaces invalid cwd fields without
       deleting IndexedDB — all healthy configurations are preserved.

- [x] I have provided a short and descriptive title so that developers can quickly understand the issue when browsing the issue list, rather than vague titles like "A suggestion" or "Stuck."
- [x] The latest version of Cherry Studio does not include the feature I am suggesting.

### Platform

macOS

### Version

v1.9.6

### Is your feature request related to an existing issue?

会话窗口太多

### Desired Solution

## Problem

The `mcp__claw__cron` tool currently supports three actions:

- `add` — create a new job
- `list` — list all jobs
- `remove` — delete a job

There is no `update` action. To modify a job (e.g., optimize the prompt, adjust the cron schedule, change timeout), the only workflow is:

1. `remove` the old job
2. `add` a new job

## Pain Points

1. **Session explosion** — Each new job gets a new `task_id`, which CherryStudio treats as a fresh task. After every optimization, new execution sessions appear on the right sidebar. The old sessions become orphaned and must be manually closed.
2. **Channel IDs lost** — The `channel_ids` array must be re-specified on every re-add. If forgotten, notifications silently fail (empty channel list).
3. **Loss of execution history** — `last_run` / `last_result` are reset to null, making it impossible to track a job's performance over time.
4. **Unnecessary agent cognitive overhead** — The agent must explain to the user why windows are multiplying and manually clean up.

## Proposed API

Add an `update` action:

### Alternative Solutions

mcp__claw__cron action="update"
id: "task_xxx"              # required — existing job ID
name: "new name"            # optional
cron: "0 8 * * 1-5"        # optional
message: "new prompt"       # optional
timeout_minutes: 10         # optional
channel_ids: ["xxx"]        # optional


Only the `id` field is required. All other fields are optional and only override when provided. The `task_id` remains unchanged, so:

- Existing execution sessions on the sidebar continue to be reused
- `last_run` / `last_result` history is preserved
- Channel bindings persist unless explicitly changed

## Alternatives Considered

- Using `remove` + `add` (current workaround) — causes all pain points listed above
- Direct file manipulation of cron storage — fragile and not supported by the MCP protocol

## Use Case

Daily maintenance of scheduled tasks (market monitoring, security audits, etc.) requires frequent prompt tuning and schedule adjustments. An `update` action would make this a single atomic operation.

---

**Priority:** Medium — not blocking, but causes daily friction for active users.

title: MCP 文件服务器 read_text_file 返回过期缓存内容，导致文件被旧版本覆盖
body:
## 问题描述

MCP 文件服务器（Filesystem MCP Server）的 `read_text_file` 方法存在**读缓存 Bug**，返回的文件内容是过期/缓存的旧版本，与磁盘实际内容不一致。

## 复现步骤

1. 通过 MCP `write_file` 或 `edit_file` 写入一个 Kotlin 源文件（如 PlayerScreen.kt，276 行）
2. 稍后通过 MCP `read_text_file` 读取同一文件
3. 返回的内容只有 196 行（旧版本），而不是磁盘上的 276 行

## 实际结果

- `read_text_file` 返回 196 行旧内容
- Bash `wc -l` / `cat` 读取磁盘看到 276 行当前内容
- 两个结果**不一致**

## 影响

这是一个**数据丢失级别**的 Bug。因为 Agent 基于 `read_text_file` 返回的旧内容做出编辑决策，然后通过 `edit_file` 写回，导致：
- 新代码被旧内容覆盖
- 源码遭到破坏
- Kotlin 编译报错（`Unresolved reference`、`Unsupported literal prefixes` 等）

## 验证数据

| 读取方式 | PlayerScreen.kt 行数 |
|---------|---------------------|
| MCP `read_text_file` | 196 行 |
| Bash `wc -l` | 276 行 |

两个版本内容完全不同（196 行版本缺少长按快进、全屏切换等功能）。

## 环境信息

- OS: Windows 11 Home China 10.0.26200
- MCP Server: Filesystem MCP (mcp__fSOoVaOg1slC8LUzjlcxp__)
- 文件路径包含中文字符: `C:\Users\刘双灵\AndroidProjects\CleanPlayer\...`
- 文件编码: UTF-8

## 临时绕过方案

使用 Bash `cat`/`head`/`tail` 代替 MCP `read_text_file` 读取文件。MCP `write_file` 和 `edit_file` 写入功能正常。
