title: [Feature]: Add a unified global search and quick app launcher
body:
### Issue Checklist

- [x] I understand that issues are for reporting problems and requesting features, not for off-topic comments, and I will provide as much detail as possible to help resolve the issue.
- [x] I have checked the pinned issues and searched through the existing [open issues](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/issues), [closed issues](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20state%3Aclosed), and [discussions](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/discussions) and did not find a similar suggestion.
- [x] I have provided a short and descriptive title so that developers can quickly understand the issue when browsing the issue list, rather than vague titles like "A suggestion" or "Stuck."
- [x] The latest version of Cherry Studio does not include the feature I am suggesting.

### Platform

macOS

### Version

v2 development branch (`feat/global-search`)

### Is your feature request related to an existing issue?

Cherry Studio currently has separate navigation and search surfaces for chat topics, agent sessions, assistants, agents, and knowledge bases. Users need to know where an item lives before they can find it, then manually switch modules to open the result.

Related issues exist around broader global search behavior, such as #14520, #10510, and #11898. This issue scopes the v2 entity-level global search and launcher experience: unified discovery, recent navigation, and quick access across core app areas. It does not cover full historical message-content search or message-level jump behavior.

### Desired Solution

Add a unified global search panel that works as an app-level command/search surface:

- Add a DataApi `GET /global-search` endpoint that aggregates assistants, agents, chat topics, agent sessions, and knowledge bases.
- Support result type filters, per-type limits, and updated-time filters such as today, last 7 days, last month, and last 3 months.
- Return lightweight search results with title, subtitle, emoji, updated time, and minimal navigation targets instead of leaking full domain entities across boundaries.
- Add a global search panel opened from the shell/tab bar and existing search entry points.
- Show grouped results, recent route/topic/session entries, keyboard navigation, loading/empty/error states, and result highlighting.
- Open results directly into the right destination: chat topic, agent session, assistant/agent edit page, or selected knowledge base.
- Add quick app shortcuts in the panel for visible sidebar entries.
- Add a quick app manager for sidebar shortcut visibility, ordering, and reset behavior.
- Persist recent global-search entries and sidebar shortcut preferences through the v2 Cache/Preference layer.
- Cover the schema, handler, service aggregation, grouping logic, panel behavior, and shell trigger with focused tests.

Acceptance criteria:

- Searching from the global panel returns grouped results across the supported entity types.
- Type and time filters affect the DataApi request and the rendered groups.
- Empty query shows recent entries where applicable.
- Selecting each supported result type navigates to the correct app state.
- Quick app shortcuts open the correct routes.
- Quick app visibility and ordering changes persist.
- The implementation does not reintroduce v1 Redux/Dexie/ElectronStore dependencies.

### Alternative Solutions

- Keep search inside each module only. This avoids new app-level UI, but keeps discovery fragmented and does not solve cross-module navigation.
- Implement only message-content global search. That is useful, but it does not address finding assistants, agents, sessions, knowledge bases, or app routes.
- Add static sidebar shortcuts only. That improves navigation, but does not provide search, recents, filters, or entity-level open behavior.

### Additional Information

Current branch summary:

- Branch: `feat/global-search`
- Target branch: `v2`
- Scope: DataApi schema/handler/service, renderer global search panel, shell/tab bar trigger, sidebar shortcut preferences, recent-entry cache, i18n, and focused tests.

The current implementation searches entity metadata and navigation targets. Message body search and deep message jump reliability should remain tracked separately.

title: [Feature]: Auto-position to the most recently updated conversation after restart
body:

### Issue Checklist

### Platform

Windows

### Version

Latest

### Is your feature request related to an existing issue?

After restarting CherryStudio, the left sidebar conversation list remains at the position of the conversation being viewed when last closed.

However, external messages integrated through Feishu channels update in real-time (based on WebSocket long connections). After restart, the latest messages from Feishu channels are saved in the corresponding conversations, but the UI still displays the old conversation from before closing by default.

Users need to manually search through the left sidebar list to find recently updated conversations to see the latest messages, which involves a longer operation path and a less smooth experience.

### Desired Solution

After restarting CherryStudio, the left sidebar conversation list automatically positions to the conversation with the most recent message update (sorted by `updated_at`). This way, users can see the latest messages immediately upon opening, without manual searching.

Or a more elegant solution: add a "Sort by Recent Update" option to the left sidebar conversation list, along with unread markers, allowing users to quickly locate which conversations have new messages.

### Alternative Solutions

1. Add a "Recent Update" sort toggle at the top of the conversation list
2. Bold unread conversations or mark them with a red dot
3. Show a notification on startup indicating there are unread conversations

### Additional Information

Use case: Users conduct real-time conversations with CherryStudio Agents (such as Xiaozhi, Xiaomei, Xiaoxia, etc.) through Feishu bot. These messages are sent and received in real-time through WebSocket channels, but after restarting CherryStudio UI, the UI cannot automatically jump to the latest conversation.

body:
### Issue Checklist

- [x] I have checked the pinned issues and searched through the existing [open issues](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/issues), [closed issues](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20state%3Aclosed), and [discussions](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/discussions) and did not find a similar suggestion.
- [x] I have provided a short and descriptive title so that developers can quickly understand the issue when browsing the issue list, rather than vague titles like "A suggestion" or "Stuck."
- [x] The latest version of Cherry Studio does not include the feature I am suggesting.

### Platform

macOS

### Version

v.1.9.6

### Is your feature request related to an existing issue?

No. This is a request to enhance the newly discovered "Service Tier" feature.

Currently, Cherry Studio has a "Service Tier" setting under **OpenAI Settings** with the options: `Ignore`, `Off`, `auto`, `default`, and `priority`. 

However, the **`flex`** tier is missing from this list. 

This is a major pain point because the `flex` tier is the most important setting for saving API costs on platforms like **OpenRouter** and **Google Gemini** (which offers up to 50% cost reduction on models like Gemini Flash when using the `flex` tier). 

Currently, trying to pass `service_tier: flex` via Custom Headers results in the parameter being sent as an HTTP Header (`Service_tier: flex`) instead of the JSON Request Body, which is ignored by the APIs.

### Desired Solution

Please add the **`flex`** option to the existing "Service Tier" dropdown menu under OpenAI Settings.

When `flex` is selected, it should be appended to the JSON Request Body like this:

```json
{
  "model": "google/gemini-3.5-flash",
  "service_tier": "flex",
  "messages": [...]
}
```

**Proposed UI Change:**
Under OpenAI Settings -> Service Tier, add **`flex`** to the dropdown options:

- Ignore
- Off
- auto
- default
- priority
- flex (<- New Option)

### Alternative Solutions

I tried setting Service_tier: flex in the Custom Headers. While Cherry Studio successfully sends this, it is sent as an HTTP Header, which both OpenRouter and Gemini APIs ignore (they expect it in the JSON request payload, not the header).

### Additional Information

Additional Information
OpenRouter Service Tiers Guide: https://openrouter.ai/docs/guides/features/service-tiers (Explains how flex works for routing and cost savings).

- [x] I've confirmed that I am using the latest version of Cherry Studio.

## Platform

macOS

## Version

1.9.6

## Bug Description

When switching between models with different thinking/reasoning-effort support, the assistant-level `reasoning_effort` value can be overwritten by fallback logic and the original model's preference is lost.

Example: Model A supports thinking control and the user selects `none` (no thinking). After switching to Model B, the app applies a fallback reasoning effort for Model B. When switching back to Model A, Model A's previous `none` preference is no longer restored because the single assistant-level value was overwritten by Model B's fallback.

This changes the user's thinking preference unexpectedly and can affect request parameters, latency, and cost.

## Steps To Reproduce

1. Use Cherry Studio 1.9.6 on macOS.
2. Select a model that supports configurable thinking/reasoning effort (Model A).
3. Set Model A's thinking option to `none` / no thinking.
4. Switch the assistant to another model with a different set of supported thinking options (Model B), so the app applies fallback reasoning effort for Model B.
5. Switch back to Model A.
6. Observe that Model A's previous `none` / no-thinking preference is not preserved.

## Expected Behavior

Each model should preserve its own reasoning-effort preference independently. Switching to another model and applying fallback for that model should not overwrite the original model's stored preference.

If per-model persistence is not implemented, fallback should at least avoid destroying the previous model's user-selected value.

## Relevant Log Output

```shell
N/A
```

## Additional Context

Root cause appears to be that `reasoning_effort` is stored as a single assistant-level value. Model-switch fallback updates that single value, so returning to the previous model uses the fallback value instead of the previous model-specific preference.

A local fix branch exists with a proposed implementation that stores reasoning effort per model: `jorkey/fix/model-reasoning-effort-reset`. This is only a local branch/reference and has not been confirmed as merged upstream.

title: [Feature]: Recycle Bin for Deleted Chat Topics and Agent Sessions
body:
## Background

Today, deleting a chat topic or an agent session in Cherry Studio is permanent and instant — there is no way to recover the data afterward. Users repeatedly report accidentally deleting items: a single misclick on the close icon erases an entire conversation thread; users running long multi-step branch edits in a chat lose hours of work to one wrong click; long-running agent sessions with substantial back-and-forth history can be wiped in a single click. This pain has been raised across more than ten issues since 2024-09 and was explicitly acknowledged as "planned" by the project owner in #76 and #1188, but the recovery flow has never shipped.

## Goal

Users can recover any chat topic or agent session they delete, via a Recycle Bin under Settings → App Settings → Archive Management. Items stay in the Recycle Bin until the user clears them explicitly.

## Spec

- Chat topic and agent session deletion both flow through a unified Delete action that opens a confirmation dialog: *"Delete `<name>`? It will be moved to the Recycle Bin, where you can restore it later."* with two buttons: **Cancel** and **Delete**. On Delete, the item is moved to the Recycle Bin instead of being erased.
- The Recycle Bin is reached via **Settings → App Settings → Archive Management → Recycle Bin**.
- The Recycle Bin shows all deleted items mixed in a single list, sorted by deletion time descending. Each row shows entity type (Topic / Session), entity icon, original title, the parent assistant or agent the item came from, and deletion timestamp.
- Each row supports two actions: **Restore** (returns the item to its original parent and position) and **Delete permanently** (removes from the Recycle Bin and frees underlying storage).
- The Recycle Bin offers a global **Empty Recycle Bin** action that permanently deletes everything in one step, behind a confirmation dialog because this action is unrecoverable.
- Items in the Recycle Bin are never auto-purged. They remain available indefinitely until the user clicks **Restore**, **Delete permanently**, or **Empty Recycle Bin**.
- If the user attempts to restore a topic or session whose parent assistant or agent no longer exists, the restore is blocked with a message explaining that the parent is required. The item stays in the Recycle Bin.
- Files on the user's local disk — including agent working directories chosen by the user, and any artifacts Claude Code or other agents wrote inside them — are never touched by delete, restore, or permanent deletion. Only Cherry's own metadata (topic records, session records, message records) and Cherry-managed chat attachments are moved with the entity.
- Chat topic attachments stored in Cherry's File Manager follow their parent topic into the Recycle Bin and back. Permanent deletion of the topic releases the file reference, and the file is physically removed once no other entity references it.

## Verification

- In a chat with assistant "Translator" that has 5 topics, click delete on topic #3 → a confirmation dialog appears with text including "Moved to the Recycle Bin"; click Delete → sidebar updates to 4 topics; the Recycle Bin shows topic #3 with parent "Translator" and a fresh timestamp.
- Restore the deleted topic from the Recycle Bin → topic #3 reappears in "Translator" in its original position; the row leaves the Recycle Bin.
- In an agent "CodeFixer" with 3 sessions, delete session #2 → after confirming, the session disappears from the agent's session list; the Recycle Bin shows the session with parent "CodeFixer".
- Create an agent session that produces a `summary.md` inside the agent's working directory at `/Users/foo/myproject`. Delete the session, then permanently delete it from the Recycle Bin. Verify `summary.md` and the rest of `/Users/foo/myproject` are untouched on disk; only the session's chat history disappears from Cherry.
- Delete a topic in "Translator", then delete the "Translator" assistant directly (assistant deletion is the existing flow, not via Recycle Bin). Open the Recycle Bin and attempt to restore the orphaned topic → restore is blocked with a clear message that the parent assistant no longer exists; the topic stays in the Recycle Bin.
- Place 20 deleted items in the Recycle Bin spanning 90 days of deletion timestamps. Restart Cherry → all 20 items remain (no auto purge).
- Click **Empty Recycle Bin** with 10 items present → a confirmation dialog appears; on confirm, the list becomes empty and previously stored chat attachments referenced only by those deleted topics are removed from disk.
- Permanently delete a chat topic that had 2 attached images and a PDF → the files no longer appear in the File Manager (unless still referenced by another topic).
- Navigate to **Settings → App Settings → Archive Management** → a "Recycle Bin" entry is visible and clickable.

## Related

#76 #1188 #5075 #9891 #10805 #1419 #2120 #1434 #428
PRs: #14669 #14159 #13851

title: [Feature]: Complete the Settings Infrastructure — Foundation for Agent Automation (V2)
body:
## Background

Cherry Studio has accumulated dozens of settings panels and hundreds of toggles. Manual configuration is the dominant onboarding pain — users routinely take minutes to locate options, abandon setup mid-way, or assume features are missing because they're buried. The natural way to lower this barrier is to let the in-app Cherry Assistant (and external automation, scripts, CI) handle configuration on the user's behalf. But the current settings layer cannot support that yet, and is itself the bottleneck. Concretely, the following gaps still need to be filled:

- **Language switching reverts to English** after the user picks another language (#13986).
- **Tray icon visibility** toggle persists but the icon doesn't actually hide or show until app restart.
- **Launch-to-tray** and **minimize-to-tray-on-close** only take effect after restart, with no UI warning.
- **Auto-update channel** changes silently fail to take effect until next launch.
- **Proxy settings** don't reliably persist — restarting the app sometimes loses the configuration.
- **Multi-window propagation** is missing: a change in one window doesn't reflect in others.
- **No programmable read/write surface** for settings — every change today flows through manual clicks, blocking any agent or automation from operating the app the same way a user can.

Completing this foundation is a prerequisite for Cherry Assistant going from "navigator that points to settings panels" to "agent that actually performs configuration on the user's behalf" — and also unblocks the upcoming Cherry CLI, account sync (#14898), and mobile-PC sync (#12934).

## Goal

Any setting change — whether through clicks, scripts, or programmatic callers — is reflected everywhere instantly, takes effect without app restart, and is available through a single authenticated local interface.

## Spec

- Every setting has exactly one canonical value at any moment. Every UI surface, sub-window, and external caller reads and writes through that single value.
- Any change to a setting immediately updates every UI surface displaying it, with no manual refresh and no waiting for the user to revisit the settings page.
- Every toggle exposed in the UI takes effect without app restart. Where an OS-level constraint genuinely requires a restart or system boot (e.g., launch-on-boot registration), the UI explicitly states that constraint next to the toggle, and any programmatic caller receives the constraint back in its response.
- Dependent subsystems — tray, application menu, theme, language, window behavior, update channel, shortcuts, proxy — re-read affected settings the moment they change.
- A single authenticated local interface exposes the full settings surface for read and write. Sensitive fields (API keys, OAuth tokens) are redacted under default scope; full values require an elevated scope explicitly granted by the user per session.
- Concurrent changes to the same setting (e.g., one window and one script writing simultaneously) converge to a single consistent final value with no duplicates and no half-applied states.

## Verification

- User switches language from English to 日本語 in settings → tray menu, application menu bar, settings page, and all other open windows switch to Japanese within 1 second. The change persists after restart. (#13986 must not recur.)
- User toggles "Show tray icon" off → tray icon disappears within 1 second; no "please restart" prompt.
- User toggles "Minimize to tray on close" = true → clicks the window close button → app keeps running in tray. Toggles it back → close button quits the app. No restart between toggles.
- User changes auto-update channel from Stable to Beta → next "Check for updates" run uses the Beta channel without restart.
- User configures a custom proxy → restarts the app → proxy settings are intact and active on first request.
- User opens settings in two windows. Window A changes theme to dark → Window B reflects dark theme within 1 second without manual refresh.
- External script calls the local interface with the user's credentials: `set theme = dark` → main window flips to dark immediately. `get theme` returns `dark`.
- External script calls `get settings` with default scope → returns all settings but API keys are redacted (e.g. `"openai_api_key": "sk-***"`). Calls again after the user explicitly grants elevated scope → returns full unredacted values.
- One window toggles dark, an external script writes light at the same instant → both surfaces converge to one value (whichever arrived last); no half-applied theme; no duplicate state.
- User attempts to set "launch on boot" via the local interface → setting persists, response includes "Effective at next OS boot — OS-level setting"; UI shows the same explanation next to the toggle.

## Related

#13986 #14898 #14904 #12934

title: [Feature]: Cherry CLI — Terminal Tool with Full GUI Feature Parity (V2)
body:
## Background

Cherry Studio is feature-rich — 60+ providers, agent creation, knowledge bases, MCP servers, painting, code tools, granular settings. Manual configuration through the GUI is the dominant onboarding cost: users routinely spend 15+ minutes setting up their first provider (API key + endpoint + model list + default selections), wiring up a working agent (model + instructions + MCP servers + accessible paths), or replicating a working setup onto a second machine. The current state has explicit gaps:

- **No batch or scripted setup**: every configuration step is a click sequence. There's no way to share a working setup as a config file, no way to re-apply it on a new machine, no way to automate it in CI.
- **No headless operation**: Cherry Studio always boots a GUI window. Servers, CI runners, and SSH sessions without a display can't drive the app at all.
- **No external automation path**: knowledge base ingestion, agent provisioning, backup/restore — anything multi-step — has to be performed by a human at the keyboard.
- **Limited discoverability for power features**: users who live in the chat UI commonly miss knowledge bases, MCP servers, code tools, and paintings because surface area is split across many panels.
- **No reusable surface for in-app intelligent assistants**: an in-app assistant that wants to actually perform actions (not just point to settings panels) has no consistent execution layer to call.

## Goal

A single command-line tool, installable from npm/Homebrew, exposes every GUI-accessible feature with full CRUD semantics — so users, scripts, CI, and in-app assistants share one consistent way to configure and drive Cherry Studio.

## Spec

- Every operation reachable by clicks in the GUI is reachable as a CLI command with create/list/get/update/delete semantics: agents, sessions, messages, knowledge bases, providers, MCP servers, paintings, backups, settings.
- Commands are organized by feature domain: `cherry agent`, `cherry session`, `cherry knowledge`, `cherry provider`, `cherry mcp`, `cherry painting`, `cherry backup`, `cherry config`.
- The CLI installs from npm and Homebrew as a single `cherry` binary, independent of whether Cherry Studio is running in the foreground.
- First-run auth: `cherry login` opens an in-app consent prompt and returns a scoped token. Users never paste long API keys by hand. The same consent mechanism allows callers to request elevated scope when an operation needs sensitive access.
- Output: human-readable by default, machine-readable with `--output json`. Streaming operations (session messages, painting progress, knowledge ingestion) stream incrementally to stdout.
- Headless launch: when Cherry Studio isn't running, CLI invocations start it headlessly (no visible window). Subsequent commands within the same shell session reuse the running instance.
- Same execution surface for all callers: when the CLI, an in-app assistant, or any other authenticated caller performs an operation, the result is identical and visible everywhere — e.g., a newly created agent appears in the GUI agent list immediately, indistinguishable from a user clicking "New Agent".
- Errors are actionable: missing install → download link; expired auth → run `cherry login`; port conflict → override flag hint.

## Verification

- Fresh install: `brew install cherry-studio-cli` → `cherry login` → Cherry Studio opens a consent prompt → user confirms → CLI prints "Logged in as <email>". No manual API key paste.
- User runs `cherry agent create --name "Code Reviewer" --model claude-sonnet-4 --instructions "Review Python for bugs"` → exits 0, prints new agent id; the GUI agent list immediately shows "Code Reviewer".
- User runs `cherry provider add --name MyProvider --api-key sk-xxx --set-default` → MyProvider appears in the GUI provider list with the key configured and is the default for new chats.
- User runs `cherry session send <id> "summarize this PR"` → assistant tokens stream to stdout incrementally; same content as the GUI would render.
- User runs `cherry knowledge search --base-id <id> "embedding"` → top-N matches with source file and score, table by default, JSON with `--output json`.
- User exports their working setup: `cherry backup export ~/my-cherry.tar.gz`; on a second machine after `cherry login`, runs `cherry backup import ~/my-cherry.tar.gz` → providers, agents, knowledge bases, and settings are restored as on the first machine.
- SSH into a headless server with no display: `cherry agent list --output json` → returns valid JSON; no Electron window is created.
- With Cherry Studio closed, user runs a CLI command → CLI prints "Starting Cherry Studio in headless mode..." on stderr, waits ≤5 s, completes the command. Next command in the same shell session completes immediately without re-launching.
- Token expires → next command exits non-zero with "Authentication expired. Run `cherry login` to renew."
- `cherry agent list --output json | jq '.[].name'` outputs the list of agent names cleanly; stderr is empty on the happy path.
- When an in-app intelligent assistant performs `cherry agent create` programmatically, the new agent appears in the GUI list immediately — indistinguishable from a user clicking through the New Agent flow.

## Related

#14898 #14904 #15181 #15183 #15029

---

## Appendix: Detailed Command Matrix (v2 planning)

This appendix is the detailed v2 spec derived from a survey of:
- Cherry Studio's existing API server (`src/main/apiServer/`, Express + OpenAPI, Swagger at `/api-docs`)
- The lark-cli design (https://github.com/larksuite/cli) — three-layer command architecture
- Related v2 issues (#14898 account system, #14904 Provider Gateway, #15181/#15183 mise tool manager, #15029 skill marketplace)

**Scope legend** — `[v2.0]` = first-batch CLI on existing endpoints • `[v2.x]` = requires new API server endpoints • `[v2.3+]` = depends on #14898 account/sync

### A.1 Design Principles

#### A.1.1 Three-layer command architecture

| Layer | Form | Purpose | Example |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Shortcuts** | `cherry <group> +<verb>` | High-frequency combos with smart defaults, table output, `--dry-run` preview. Friendly to humans and AI agents | `cherry agent +chat "Code Reviewer" "review this PR"` |
| **API commands** (generated) | `cherry <group> <resource> <action>` | Auto-generated from `openapi-spec.json`, covers every endpoint | `cherry agent list`, `cherry session create --agent-id ag_xxx` |
| **Generic call** | `cherry api <METHOD> <path>` | Fallback for any endpoint not yet wrapped | `cherry api GET /v1/agents --params '{"limit":50}'` |

#### A.1.2 Global options

```
--format json|pretty|table|ndjson|csv    Output format, default pretty
--output <file>                          Redirect to file
--dry-run                                Print the HTTP request, do not execute
--as user|agent|api-key                  Identity switch (active after #14898)
--profile <name>                         Multi-profile switch (home/work/CI)
--endpoint <url>                         Override Cherry Studio instance URL, default http://127.0.0.1:23333
--token <token>                          Override credential (also $CHERRY_TOKEN)
--timeout <ms>                           Request timeout
--no-color / --quiet / --verbose
```

#### A.1.3 Auth

| Phase | Mechanism |
|---|---|
| **Transitional (v2.0)** | `cherry auth login --token cs-sk-xxx` — reuse current single-key from API server (paste from Settings → API Server) |
| **From v2.3.0** | `cherry login` → browser-based consent via Passport (#14898) → scoped token returned |
| **Storage** | macOS Keychain / Windows Credential Manager / libsecret (never plaintext config file) |
| **Multi-identity** | `--as user` (default), `--as agent`, `--as api-key` — shared identity model with in-app agents |
| **Device-code mode** | `cherry login --device-code` for headless/remote machines (mirrors `lark-cli --device-code`) |
| **No-wait mode** | `cherry login --no-wait` returns auth URL immediately, token written asynchronously |

#### A.1.4 Output & streaming
- Default `pretty` (color + table); auto-downgrades to `ndjson` when piped
- Session messages, painting progress, knowledge ingestion stream via SSE → token/event-level to stdout
- `--format ndjson` for `jq` pipelines

#### A.1.5 Introspection
- `cherry schema <group> <action>` prints params, request body, response, required scopes (mirrors `lark-cli schema`)
- `cherry --help` / `cherry <group> --help` / `cherry <group> +<verb> --help` fully populated
- `cherry schema --openapi > spec.json` exports the raw spec

#### A.1.6 Headless startup
When Cherry Studio is not running:
- **Prefer**: connect to local `http://127.0.0.1:23333` if alive
- **Fallback**: spawn Electron main with `--headless` (no BrowserWindow), wait for API server ready, then issue request. Process auto-exits 5 min after last shell command.
- **Force**: `cherry --no-spawn` connects only, never spawns

#### A.1.7 Error handling
- Exit codes: `0` ok • `1` general • `2` invalid args • `3` auth failed • `4` connection/network • `5` resource not found • `6` permission denied
- stderr always structured JSON `{"code":..., "message":..., "hint":...}`; stdout carries data

---

### A.2 Top-level Command Groups (v2 complete = 44 groups)

For reference, lark-cli ships 18 service domains + 11 meta commands (`config`/`auth`/`api`/`schema`/`completion`/`doctor`/`service`/`profile`/`event`/`update`/`init`/`build`/`prune`). Cherry's domains differ, but the meta command surface should align.

| Category | Group | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| **Auth & CLI config** | `auth` | login/logout/identity/scopes/device-code |
| | `config` | CLI local config (endpoint, format, token store) |
| | `profile` | Multi-profile (home/work/CI) |
| **Chat & agents (V2 core)** | `chat` | Stateless one-shot chat (OpenAI/Anthropic compatible) |
| | `agent` | Agent CRUD + full configuration + invocation |
| | `session` | Sessions + message stream + branching/export |
| | `permission` | Per-agent tool/file permissions (V2 new) |
| **V2 plugins / extensions** | `skill` | Skill install/enable/manage (V2 plugin system) |
| | `plugin` | V2 plugin CRUD |
| | `mcp` | MCP servers, tools, resources, prompts |
| | `tool` | mise-based binary tool management (#15183) |
| **Models & providers** | `provider` | LLM provider configuration (deep fields) |
| | `model` | Model list, capability inspection |
| | `gateway` | Provider Gateway (#14904) |
| **Knowledge & memory** | `knowledge` | RAG knowledge bases (chunk/embedding/reranker) |
| | `memory` | Long-term memory |
| | `note` | Notes module |
| | `file` | Attachments / uploaded files |
| **Content generation** | `painting` | Image generation |
| | `translate` | Translation |
| | `websearch` | Web search |
| **Automation & integration** | `task` | Scheduled tasks |
| | `channel` | Telegram/WeChat/Feishu/Discord adapters |
| | `event` | Real-time event stream (agent messages, channel inbound, task triggers, MCP notifications) |
| **Backup & sync** | `backup` | WebDAV/S3/LAN/Nutstore backup |
| | `sync` | Cross-device sync (#14898) |
| **App configuration** | `setting` | App settings root (with sub-domains) |
| | `theme` | Theme, accent color |
| | `language` | UI language, i18n |
| | `proxy` | Proxy configuration |
| | `shortcut` | Keyboard shortcuts |
| | `quick-phrase` | Quick phrases |
| | `selection` | Selection toolbar |
| | `sidebar` | Sidebar modules |
| **Windows & runtime** | `service` | Cherry Studio main-process management (start/stop/restart/status, headless) |
| | `window` | Multi-window management |
| | `tab` | Multi-tab management |
| | `update` | App updates |
| | `log` | Log read/export |
| | `doctor` | High-level health check (one-shot diagnose + fix) |
| | `diag` | Low-level diagnostics (network/MCP/Dexie/SQLite breakdown) |
| **Meta commands** | `api` | Generic HTTP escape hatch |

| | `prune` | Local cache / orphan cleanup |

---

### A.3 Per-group command surface

#### A.3.1 `auth` — Authentication `[v2.0]`

```bash
cherry auth login [--token cs-sk-xxx] [--browser] [--no-wait] [--device-code <CODE>]
cherry auth logout [--profile <name>]

cherry event consume <event-key> [--max-events 100] [--timeout 60s]
                                                  # NDJSON streamed to stdout
                                                  # stderr emits ready-marker before consuming (AI agent subprocess contract)

cherry event types                                # list event keys
cherry event consume agent.message [--agent <id>]
cherry event consume channel.inbound [--type telegram]
cherry event consume task.triggered
cherry event consume mcp.notification [--server <id>]
cherry event consume sync.conflict
cherry event consume update.available
cherry event consume system.* --filter '...'

cherry event emit <event-key> --data '{...}'      # for testing
```

#### A.3.42 `completion` — Shell autocompletion `[v2.0]`

```bash
cherry completion bash > /etc/bash_completion.d/cherry
cherry completion zsh > "${fpath[1]}/_cherry"
cherry completion fish > ~/.config/fish/completions/cherry.fish
cherry completion powershell > $PROFILE
```

#### A.3.43 `init` — Scaffolding `[v2.x]`

```bash
cherry init skill <name>                          # generate skill dir from template
cherry init agent <name>                          # generate agent config YAML
cherry init plugin <name>
cherry init mcp-server <name>
cherry init config                                # generate cherry.yaml in cwd (project-level)
```

#### A.3.44 `build` — Package build `[v2.x]`

```bash
cherry build skill [path]                         # bundle skill dir → .cherry-skill
cherry build plugin [path]
cherry build mcp-server [path]
cherry build agent <id> --output <file>           # export portable agent (incl. mcp/skill refs)
cherry build --watch
```

#### A.3.45 `prune` — Local cleanup `[v2.x]`

```bash
cherry prune cache                                # HTTP/embedding/painting caches
cherry prune orphan-files                         # unreferenced attachments
cherry prune logs --older-than 30d
cherry prune sessions --before <date> --archived
cherry prune all --dry-run
```

#### A.3.46 `api` — Generic call `[v2.0]`

```bash
cherry api GET /v1/agents --params '{"limit":50}'
cherry api POST /v1/agents/{id}/sessions --data '{"name":"..."}'
cherry api DELETE /v1/agents/{id}
cherry api PATCH /v1/agents/{id} --data '{...}'
cherry api stream POST /v1/.../messages --data '{...}'
cherry api openapi
```

#### A.3.47 `schema` — Introspection `[v2.0]`

```bash
cherry schema list                                # full command tree
cherry schema agent create                        # single command schema
cherry schema --openapi > spec.json
cherry schema --json                              # command tree as JSON
cherry schema field provider type
```

---

### A.4 API Server Gap Analysis

Endpoints required on `src/main/apiServer/` for each CLI surface. Existing API server already covers a sizable subset; remaining items are gated on V2 backend work.

| Domain | API server today | CLI needs | Gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| Agents / Sessions / Messages | ✅ Complete (incl. SSE) | Use directly | 0 |
| MCP server / tools / resources / prompts | ✅ Complete | + field completeness | Small |
| Knowledge base + entry + search | ✅ Basic | + chunk/embedding/reranker config, batch, migration | Medium |
| Models | ✅ list | + alias/pricing/capability | Small |
| Channels | ✅ Complete | + route/webhook URL/rate-limit | Small |
| Tasks | ✅ Complete | + history/logs | Small |
| Chat (OpenAI/Anthropic) | ✅ Complete | Use directly | 0 |
| **Providers** | ❌ Redux + IPC only | `/v1/providers/*` incl. keys/models/pricing/rate-limit | **Large** |
| **Painting** | ❌ Redux + IPC only | `/v1/paintings/*` | **Large** |
| **Backup** | ❌ IPC only (`BackupManager`) | `/v1/backup/*` + WebDAV/S3/LAN/Nutstore | **Large** |
| **Settings** | ❌ Redux + IPC only | `/v1/settings/*` with schema introspection | **Large** |
| **Memory** | ❌ IPC only | `/v1/memory/*` | Medium |
| **Notes** | ❌ Dexie + IPC only | `/v1/notes/*` + Dexie→HTTP bridge | Medium |
| **Files/Attachments** | ❌ IPC only | `/v1/files/*` | Medium |
| **WebSearch** | ❌ Redux only | `/v1/websearch/*` | Medium |
| **Translate** | ❌ Redux + IPC only | `/v1/translate/*` | Small |
| **Skills (V2 plugin)** | ⏳ In V2 design | `/v1/skills/*` | **Large** |
| **Plugins** | ⏳ In V2 design | `/v1/plugins/*` | **Large** |
| **Permissions** | ⏳ In V2 design | `/v1/agents/{id}/permissions/*` | Medium |
| **Theme/Language/Proxy/Shortcut/QuickPhrase/Selection/Sidebar** | ❌ Redux only | Bundled under `/v1/settings/*` with sub-namespace | Medium |
| **Window/Tab** | ❌ IPC only | `/v1/windows/*` `/v1/tabs/*` (cross-process, handle with care) | Medium |
| **Update** | ❌ IPC only (`AppUpdater`) | `/v1/update/*` | Small |
| **Logs** | ❌ Filesystem | `/v1/logs/*` or local read | Small |
| **Diag** | ❌ Does not exist | `/v1/diag/*` aggregator | Medium |
| **Sync (#14898)** | ❌ Does not exist | `/v1/sync/*` + Passport | **Large** (gated on #14898) |
| **Gateway (#14904)** | ❌ Does not exist | `/v1/gateway/*` | **Large** |
| **Tool/mise (#15183)** | ⏳ In design | `/v1/tools/*` proxying mise IPC | Medium |

**Architectural note**: CLI **always** speaks HTTP to the API server; it does not talk to Electron IPC directly. For Renderer-side Dexie data (topics/messages/notes) to be CLI-visible, the main process must either (a) provide a Dexie→HTTP bridge or (b) wait for V2's data layer migration to SQLite (already underway).

---

### A.5 Implementation Phases

**Phase 1 — v2.0**: Thin client over existing endpoints
- Groups: `auth` / `config` / `profile` / `chat` / `agent` (basic fields) / `session` / `model` / `mcp` (basic) / `knowledge` (basic) / `channel` / `task` / `websearch` (basic) / `api` / `schema` / `completion`
- No main-process changes; single `cs-sk-*` token
- npm publish `@cherry-studio/cli`

**Phase 2 — v2.1–2.2**: Backend completion + V2 plugin system
- New endpoints: `providers/painting/backup/settings/memory/notes/files/skills/plugins/permissions/translate`
- Groups: `provider` (full) / `agent` (full fields) / `permission` / `skill` / `plugin` / `painting` / `translate` / `memory` / `note` / `file` / `setting` / `theme` / `language` / `proxy` / `shortcut` / `quick-phrase` / `selection` / `sidebar` / `backup` / `update` / `log` / `doctor` / `diag` / `service` / `event` / `window` / `tab` / `init` / `build` / `prune`
- Provider Gateway (#14904) + Tool/mise (#15183)

**Phase 3 — v2.3.0**: Account + full experience
- `cherry login` browser-OAuth (#14898)
- `sync` group online
- Headless mode (modify `src/main/index.ts`)
- Homebrew publish

---

### A.6 Open Questions

1. **CLI repo location**: `packages/cli/` in-tree vs separate repo (eases npm + Homebrew tap)
2. **Dexie data ownership**: topic/message/note live in Renderer IndexedDB; bridge to HTTP now or wait for SQLite migration?
3. **Shortcuts naming**: keep `+verb` prefix (matches lark-cli) or bare verb
4. **Multi-profile timing**: v2.0 or after #14898 lands
5. **`window` / `tab` CLI-ization**: is cross-process control of Renderer windows worth the complexity? (lark-cli has no analog)
6. **`session` as top-level vs `agent session` sub-group**: top-level recommended (high frequency)
7. **`setting` vs sub-groups (theme/language/...)**: keep both entries (sub-groups are syntactic sugar)
8. **TTS / Voice**: V3 only; reserve `voice` placeholder?
9. **`doctor` vs `diag` split**: keep both; Cherry's data layer is more complex than lark-cli's
10. **Sidecar OAuth process**: lark-cli isolates OAuth in `sidecar/`; Cherry can reuse Electron main, or spawn a separate sidecar?

---

### A.7 Lark-CLI Inspiration Notes

#### A.7.1 Lark-CLI surface (verified)

**18 service domains**: calendar, messenger (im), docs, drive, markdown, sheets, slides, base, tasks, wiki, contact, mail, meetings (vc), attendance, approval, okr, project, apps.

**11 meta commands**: `config init`, `auth (login/logout/status/check/scopes/list)`, `api (GET/POST)`, `schema`, `completion`, `doctor`, `service`, `profile`, `event (consume)`, `update`, `init`, `build`, `prune`.

**Repo top-level**:
- `cmd/` (api/auth/completion/config/doctor/event/profile/schema/service/update + root/bootstrap/build/init/prune)
- `shortcuts/` — **Shortcuts are centralized**, not split per service
- `sidecar/` — **OAuth callback as an isolated process**
- `events/`, `extension/`, `skills/`, `skill-template/`, `tests/cli_e2e/`

**26 skills (layered)**:
| Layer | Skills |
|---|---|
| Foundation | `lark-shared` |
| Service wrappers | `lark-calendar`, `lark-im`, `lark-doc`, `lark-drive`, `lark-markdown`, `lark-sheets`, `lark-slides`, `lark-base`, `lark-task`, `lark-mail`, `lark-contact`, `lark-wiki`, `lark-event`, `lark-vc`, `lark-whiteboard`, `lark-minutes`, `lark-attendance`, `lark-approval`, `lark-okr` |
| Meta | `lark-openapi-explorer`, `lark-skill-maker` |
| Workflow orchestration | `lark-workflow-meeting-summary`, `lark-workflow-standup-report` |

#### A.7.2 Patterns Cherry should adopt

| Pattern | Lark-cli approach | Cherry mapping |
|---|---|---|
| Three-layer commands | Shortcuts → generated API → generic `api` | Same. Shortcuts centralized in `shortcuts/` (important) |
| Sidecar OAuth | Separate process for OAuth callback | Reuse Electron main OR spawn `cherry-auth-sidecar` |
| Skill layering | foundation / service / meta / workflow | Same layout: `cherry-shared`, per-domain wrappers, `cherry-skill-maker`, `cherry-openapi-explorer`, `cherry-workflow-*` |
| Device-code mode | Headless/remote login | Mandatory for Cherry CI/SSH use |
| No-wait mode | Return URL, write token async | Same |
| Scopes commands | `auth scopes` / `auth check --scope` | Same; requires scoped tokens (depends on #14898) |
| Doctor / self-check | One command reports full state | Split into `doctor` (high-level) + `diag` (low-level) |
| Event consume | NDJSON to stdout + stderr ready-marker | Same. Cherry has more event sources |
| Schema introspection | `schema <method>` outputs params/req/resp/scope | Derive from openapi-spec.json |
| Prune | Top-level cleanup | Same; Cherry has more cache types |
| Service | Manage CLI/related processes | Map to Cherry Studio Electron main (start/stop/restart/headless) |
| Build | Bundle skill packages | Same: skill/plugin/mcp-server/agent-export |
| Init | Project scaffolding | Same: `cherry init skill/agent/plugin/mcp-server/config` |
| Completion | 4 shell completions | Same |
| Flat naming | `lark-cli calendar` not `lark-cli service calendar` | Cherry follows: top-level `agent`, `session`, `knowledge`, `mcp` |
| E2E tests | `tests/cli_e2e/` | Cherry CLI should have its own e2e suite, not mixed with the main app's Playwright |

#### A.7.3 Cherry-unique surface (lark-cli has no analog)

| Cherry-only | Reason |
|---|---|
| `agent` / `session` / `permission` | Cherry's core is the agent; lark-cli is purely API wrapping |
| `provider` / `model` / `gateway` | LLM concepts |
| `chat` | One-shot chat; lark-cli has no conversational concept |
| `knowledge` / `memory` | RAG + long-term memory |
| `mcp` | MCP protocol is Cherry-specific |
| `painting` | Image generation |
| `tool` (mise) | Binary tool management (#15183) |
| `skill` / `plugin` | V2 plugin system (Cherry is the host; lark-cli is itself a skill provider) |
| `selection` / `quick-phrase` / `sidebar` | Cherry GUI-specific interactions |

#### A.7.4 Lark-CLI domains Cherry won't mirror

| Lark-cli domain | Why not |
|---|---|
| `calendar`, `mail`, `attendance`, `approval`, `okr`, `project` | Outside Cherry's scope |
| `docs`/`sheets`/`slides`/`base`/`wiki` (Feishu cloud docs) | Cherry's `note` is positioned differently |
| `vc`/`minutes`/`whiteboard` | Meetings/minutes/whiteboard — not Cherry's domain |
| `apps` (HTML app dev) | Overlaps with Cherry's agent/plugin system |

#### A.7.5 Cherry skill ecosystem (mapped to lark-cli layering)

After full v2 buildout the skill catalog should look like:

| Layer | Cherry skills | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Foundation | `cherry-shared` (auth/config/scope) | New (v2) |
| Service wrappers | `cherry-agent`, `cherry-session`, `cherry-knowledge`, `cherry-mcp`, `cherry-provider`, `cherry-skill`, `cherry-task`, `cherry-channel`, `cherry-backup`, `cherry-painting`, `cherry-memory` | New (v2) |
| Meta | `cherry-openapi-explorer`, `cherry-skill-maker` | Skill Creator partially exists, explorer to be added |
| Workflow | `cherry-workflow-daily-digest`, `cherry-workflow-pr-review`, `cherry-workflow-knowledge-ingest`, `cherry-workflow-agent-bootstrap` | New (v2.x) |

title: [Feature]: Unified Recycle Bin for Deleted Items
body:
## Background

Cherry Studio users frequently report accidentally deleting chat topics, Agent sessions, paintings, and custom resources with no way to recover them (#76, #5075, #9891, #10805, #15240). The current 5-second undo toast (shipped via #1188) helps for immediate reverts but disappears too quickly — users who realize the mistake hours or days later have no recourse. Archive partially addresses long-term storage but is a separate intentional action; it doesn't catch accidental deletes. There is no unified safety net for delete operations across the full set of user assets.

## Goal

Every delete action a user can take in Cherry Studio — across chat topics, Agent sessions, paintings, and the six creatable resource kinds (Skill / Assistant / Agent / MCP / Prompt / Knowledge Base) — routes through a single Recycle Bin that gives a 30-day window to recover by default, while strictly leaving user-owned local files untouched.

## Spec

**Scope & layout**
- A "Recycle Bin" page lives under Settings → App Settings, next to Archive Management. It lists every item the user has deleted across 9 types, with a left sidebar organized into two groups:
  - **History records** (activity outputs): Chat topics, Agent sessions, Paintings
  - **Custom resources** (creatable resources): Skill, Assistant, Agent, MCP, Prompt, Knowledge Base
- The list shows one row per item with the item title, a type chip, an optional "Previously archived" chip, and a relative deletion time on the right (hover swaps the time for restore + permanent-delete actions). Items are independent peers — no parent-child grouping is rendered in the bin.
- Multi-select supports batch restore and batch permanent-delete.

**Move-to-bin confirmation**
- Every move-to-bin delete (from chat sidebar, Agent session list, Market manage dialog's custom resources, Library, painting gallery, or archive page) shows a small iOS-style confirm dialog: a centered trash icon, the title "Move to Recycle Bin?", and side-by-side [Cancel] [Move to Recycle Bin] buttons. No item-name display, no educational subtext, no "don't ask again" toggle.
- Installed-from-market resources bypass the bin and are uninstalled directly — the user can reinstall from the market at any time.
- After confirmation, the item moves to the bin and a 5-second undo toast appears at the bottom-right with the message "{item} moved to Recycle Bin · recoverable for 30 days at Settings → Recycle Bin [Undo]". Clicking Undo returns the item to its source state.

**Painting delete entry**
- The Creation page's gallery view exposes a hover Trash button on each image card (in the top-right overlay alongside the favorite heart). Clicking it routes the painting through the same move-to-bin confirm dialog.

**Permanent-delete & retention confirmations**
- Any permanent-delete action (single row, batch, empty-bin) and any retention-shortening that would expire items shows the same iOS-style confirm dialog (red trash icon for deletes; amber warning icon for the retention case). Titles are short and direct:
  - Single row: "Confirm permanent delete?"
  - Batch: "Confirm permanent delete of N items?"
  - Empty bin: "Empty Recycle Bin?" with subtitle "All N items will be permanently deleted"
  - Retention shortening: "Shorten retention?" with a subtitle that splits the affected items into two cohorts — "X items will be cleaned up immediately, Y items will expire within 7 days" if both buckets are non-empty, otherwise the single applicable bucket. The action button reads "Shorten anyway" (warning tone).
- Restore is immediate and does not require confirmation.

**Decoupled flat model in the bin**
- Items in the bin are independent peers. Deleting a parent (assistant or agent) moves only the parent itself — its topics or sessions stay where they are in the active world (or sit in the bin separately if the user deleted them independently). There is no parent-child cascade visualization in the bin.
- **Orphan recovery**: if a user restores a chat topic or Agent session whose original parent assistant/agent no longer exists, the row's Restore button gains a small dropdown chevron and opens an inline popover listing fallback parents (e.g. "Default Assistant", "Claude 4 Sonnet", "GPT-4o" for topics; "Default Agent", "Coding Agent", "Research Agent" for sessions). Selecting one immediately restores the item attached to that fallback. The success toast names the chosen parent: "{item} restored · assigned to Default Assistant". No Dialog overlay.
- Non-orphan items keep a plain single-click restore button.

**Archive integration**
- Deleting an archived item from the Archive Management page routes through the recycle bin with a "Previously archived" marker. Both the 5-second undo toast and the later Restore action inside the bin return the item back to the archive list (not to active state). The rationale: the user already made a conscious archive decision earlier, so restoring should respect that prior state. To return it to active use, the user can un-archive from the archive page afterwards.

**Retention**
- Items in the bin show their relative deletion time on the right side of the row ("Today / 3 days ago / 1 month ago"). Default retention is **30 days**; user-configurable via the Cleanup Settings popover at the top of the page to 7 / 30 / 60 / 90 / Never. Expired items are removed in a background sweep.

**Engineering boundaries — data ownership & relationships**
- **User-owned local files are never touched** by any recycle-bin action (delete, restore, permanent delete, auto-purge). This includes Agent working directories chosen by the user and any artifacts external tools (e.g. Claude Code) wrote inside them. Only Cherry's own metadata records and Cherry-managed file attachments are affected.
- **Cherry-managed chat attachments follow their parent topic** into and out of the recycle bin. While the parent is in the bin, its attachments remain referenced (not garbage-collected). Restoring the topic restores attachment access transparently.
- **Permanent delete is two-layered**: metadata records are removed immediately when the user confirms; managed file blobs are unlinked from the entity, and the underlying file is physically removed only when its reference count reaches zero. A file shared by multiple topics is not deleted until the last referencing topic is permanently removed.
- **Permanent delete is a true erasure (right-to-be-forgotten / GDPR compliance)**: physically erased, not soft-deleted; extends to search indexes, caches, content fingerprints, and any derived references. The data must not be recoverable through ordinary file-recovery or DB-undelete means.
- **Decoupled lifecycle**: deleting an assistant or agent moves only that entity into the bin. Its previously associated topics/sessions are independent — they remain in the active world (or, if separately deleted, sit in the bin as peers). On restore of a child whose original parent no longer exists, the orphan-recovery picker offers a fallback parent to re-attach.

**Operational behavior**
- **Batch operation atomicity**: large batch deletes (permanent delete, empty-bin) commit per-item. If interrupted (app crash, force-quit), completed items stay deleted; the rest remain in the bin. No partial/inconsistent metadata states.
- **Auto-purge timing**: a sweep runs (a) on app launch, (b) when the user opens the Recycle Bin page, and (c) periodically while the app is open.
- **Retention change recomputes expiresAt** for all existing items based on `deletedAt + new retention`. When shortening retention would expire items, the user is asked to confirm with an explicit split of "X items will be cleaned up immediately, Y will expire within 7 days".
- **Integrity sweep on app start**: a background reclaim removes orphan managed-attachment files whose owning entity no longer exists in any state (active / bin).

## Verification

**Move-to-bin happy path**
- Chat sidebar → right-click topic → Delete → small iOS-style dialog "Move to Recycle Bin?" appears → confirm → topic moved + 5-second undo toast at bottom-right "{title} moved to Recycle Bin". Click [Undo] within 5s → topic reappears.
- Same dialog shape for: Agent session delete, Library resource delete, Market manage → Custom tab → X.
- Market manage → Installed-from-market tab → X on an installed MCP → silent uninstall, NOT in Recycle Bin.
- Creation → Gallery → hover any image → Trash button → same dialog → confirm → image in Recycle Bin under History records → Paintings.
- Archive Management → trash icon on a row → same dialog → confirm → item in Recycle Bin with "Previously archived" tag. Click Restore inside the bin → item back in Archive Management list (NOT in active chat list).

**Permanent-delete confirmations**
- Recycle Bin → hover row → trash icon → dialog "Confirm permanent delete?" + Cancel / Permanent delete → confirm → item removed.
- Select 3 rows → batch Permanent delete → dialog "Confirm permanent delete of 3 items?".
- Empty Recycle Bin button → dialog "Empty Recycle Bin?" + "All N items will be permanently deleted".
- Cleanup Settings → 30 days → 7 days with mix of old/new items → dialog "Shorten retention?" + "X items will be cleaned up immediately, Y items will expire within 7 days" (or just one bucket if applicable). Confirm → all items' expiresAt recomputed.

**Orphan recovery (decoupled model)**
- Seed: a topic whose original assistant is gone. In the bin, hover its row → restore button shows "Restore ▾". Click → popover opens with 4 fallback assistants → pick "Default Assistant" → toast "{item} restored · assigned to Default Assistant".
- For a non-orphan row, hover → "Restore" (no chevron) → direct restore + toast "Restored".

**Engineering boundaries**
- Create an Agent session with working dir `/Users/foo/myproject` where the Agent wrote `summary.md`. Delete + permanent-delete the session → `summary.md` and the rest of the directory remain on disk; only Cherry's session record is gone.
- Topic with 2 images attached: in bin, attachments remain. Restore → attachments come back. Permanent-delete → attachments are removed from Cherry's File Manager (assuming no other reference).
- Same image uploaded to topics A and B → permanent-delete A → image still on disk, accessible from B → permanent-delete B → only now is the file physically removed.
- GDPR check: permanent-delete a topic with an attached image → (a) no topic record in any DB table; (b) image file is gone from disk (verified via file-recovery tool, no leftover blob); (c) full-text search of the topic's content returns zero hits; (d) restart app and re-verify (a)-(c) all still hold.

## Related

#76 #1188 #5075 #9891 #10805 #1419 #2120 #1434 #428 #15240
PRs: #14669 #14159 #13851

title: [Feature]: Add a Recycle Bin for all deletable content
body:
### Issue Checklist

- [x] I understand that issues are for reporting problems and requesting features, not for off-topic comments, and I will provide as much detail as possible to help resolve the issue.
- [x] I have checked the pinned issues and searched through the existing [open issues](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/issues), [closed issues](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20state%3Aclosed), and [discussions](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/discussions) and did not find a similar suggestion.
- [x] I have provided a short and descriptive title so that developers can quickly understand the issue when browsing the issue list, rather than vague titles like "A suggestion" or "Stuck."
- [x] The latest version of Cherry Studio does not include the feature I am suggesting.

### Platform

macOS

### Version

v1.9.4

### Is your feature request related to an existing issue?

Yes. There are related but narrower requests:

- #10805 requests a recycle bin for messages/chat replies only.
- #5075 requests a topic recycle bin for accidentally deleted topics.
- #14336 and #15121 highlight data loss scenarios where users overwrite or lose conversations with no built-in recovery mechanism.

Currently, Cherry Studio treats deletion as permanent across the board — conversations, agents, assistants, skills, knowledge bases, and other user-created content are gone immediately with no safety net. This leads to irreversible data loss from accidental clicks, mistaken identity (e.g., deleting the wrong conversation branch), or momentary lapses. There is no undo, no trash, no grace period. Given how many distinct deletable entity types exist in Cherry Studio, a unified solution is more maintainable and consistent than adding per-type undo features.

### Desired Solution

Introduce a **unified Recycle Bin** that applies to **all deletable user content**, including but not limited to:

- Conversations / chat topics
- Agents
- Assistants
- Skills
- Knowledge bases / files
- Any other user-created entities

**Behavior:**

1. **Soft delete by default.** When a user deletes any of the above items, instead of permanent removal, the item is moved to the Recycle Bin.
2. **Recycle Bin entry point.** Place the Recycle Bin access inside **Settings → Data Settings** (设置 → 数据设置), which is already the hub for backup, restore, and data management operations.
3. **30-day auto-purge.** Items in the Recycle Bin are automatically permanently deleted after 30 days. A countdown or timestamp should be visible per item so users know how much time remains.
4. **Manual purge.** Provide a "Clear Recycle Bin" (清空回收站) button that permanently deletes all items, with a confirmation dialog to prevent accidents.
5. **Restore.** Each item in the Recycle Bin has a "Restore" (恢复) action that returns it to its original location with its original state intact.
6. **Batch operations.** Allow selecting multiple items for batch restore or batch permanent delete.

**UI considerations:**

- The Recycle Bin view should show: item type (icon), name, deletion date, remaining days before auto-purge, and available actions (Restore / Delete Permanently).
- A badge or counter on the Recycle Bin entry showing the number of items inside would be a nice touch.

**Edge cases to consider:**

- If a restored conversation's parent topic/agent was also deleted and is still in the trash, restore should still work (the conversation belongs to the user, not strictly to the parent).
- Permanently deleting an agent/assistant that has associated conversations in the trash should either warn the user or handle the orphaned conversations gracefully.
- Empty Recycle Bin should confirm before executing, listing the total number of items that will be permanently lost.

### Alternative Solutions

1. **Undo toast only.** A simple "Undo" snackbar/toast after deletion (like Gmail's approach) would be a lighter-weight alternative, but it only covers the immediate moments after deletion and does not help if the user realizes the mistake minutes/hours later.
2. **Per-type trash bins.** Separate trash bins for conversations, agents, assistants, etc. This would work but leads to UI fragmentation and inconsistent UX.
3. **Backup-based recovery only.** Rely entirely on the existing backup/restore system, but this is heavy-handed (requires restoring a full snapshot) and does not address the most common case of "I just deleted the wrong thing."

The unified Recycle Bin approach is preferred because it provides consistent UX, covers all entity types, and serves as a natural safety net that aligns with user expectations from virtually every modern application (OS file managers, email clients, note-taking apps, etc.).

### Additional Information

Many popular applications implement this pattern effectively — macOS Finder Trash, Gmail Trash, Notion Trash, WeChat chat history recovery, etc. Users have come to expect this as a baseline safety feature, and its absence in a productivity tool where users invest significant time building conversations, agents, and assistants is a notable gap.

Related issues for context:
- #10805 — "add undo function or trash-bin to messages"
- #5075 — "建议新增-话题回收站"
- #14336 — data loss after backup restore
- #15121 — chat history file disappears

body:
