- [x] I've confirmed that I am using the latest version of Cherry Studio.

### Platform

Windows

### Version

1.9.6

### Bug Description

Reasoning effort config not working for AIHubMix

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Select any model that uses `OpenAICompatibleChatLanguageModel` backend and supports Reasoning Effort configuration, e.g. DeepSeek 4 series model, from AIHubMix
2. Select Reasoning Effort to "off"
3. Reasoning is still on in the response
4. The Reasoning Effort parameters are missing from the request, if inspected in DevTools

### Expected Behavior

The Reasoning Effort parameters are correctly set in the request, according to the configuration, and the reasoning content in the response is controlled.

### Relevant Log Output

```shell

```

### Additional Context

## The reason of the problem:

reasoning options is built in:
```
src\renderer\src\aiCore\utils\options.ts:
	buildProviderOptions():
	rawProviderId == 'aihubmix' =>
		providerSpecificOptions = buildAIGatewayOptions() => 
		buildGenericProviderOptions('openai-compatible')
```
The reasoning options is built with `providerId == 'openai-compatible'`

Request is done by `OpenAICompatibleChatLanguageModel`, which is constructed with
	`provider == '${AIHUBMIX_PROVIDER_NAME}.openai-compatible-chat' == 'aihubmix.openai-compatible-chat'`:
```
src\renderer\src\aiCore\provider\custom\aihubmix-provider.ts:
	createAihubmix():
		OpenAICompatibleChatLanguageModel(... provider: `openai-compatible.${AIHUBMIX_PROVIDER_NAME}`)
```

Initiating request, inside `OpenAICompatibleChatLanguageModel`
in `@ai-sdk+openai-compatible@2.0.41_zod@4.3.4\node_modules\@ai-sdk\openai-compatible\src\chat\openai-compatible-chat-language-model.ts`
```getArgs():
	calls parseProviderOptions() to get the options:
		calls providerOptionsName() =>
			split `aihubmix.openai-compatible-chat` by '.' and extract the 'aihubmix' part
			Look for the options with providerId = 'aihubmix' from the last step (or some variants)
```

So the problem is:
reasoning options is built with `providerId == 'openai-compatible'`
the openai sdk uses `providerId = 'aihubmix'` to get the options

The solution:
either: change the `providerId` in `buildProviderOptions` to `'aihubmix'`,
or: change the `providerId` in `OpenAICompatibleChatLanguageModel` to `'openai-compatible.aihubmix'` (note that the `'openai-compatible-chat'` part in the original form still doesn't match)

Since `buildProviderOptions` is shared among different providers, the latter solution may be better, which affects exlusively the `OpenAICompatibleChatLanguageModel` inside aihubmix

title: Architecture: main-process cache infrastructure gap (memory / persisted / LRU / TTL)
body:
**Owner:** to be assigned (architecture decision needed)

## Background

Discovered during review of #15067, but the scope extends well beyond that PR.

The v2 data layer ([`docs/references/data/`](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/tree/v2/docs/references/data)) defines four systems: BootConfig, Cache, Preference, DataApi. The **Cache** system has three tiers (memory / shared / persist), but the persist tier is **renderer-only** — `src/main/data/CacheService.ts:477-479` reserves the interface yet does not implement storage; Main only forwards `CacheSyncMessage { type: 'persist' }` to peers.

This gap matters because main-process services routinely need:

1. **Persistent state that must not enter the backup product** (e.g. machine-local markers, dev-mode trace data)
2. **In-memory caches with TTL / LRU** (e.g. fs.stat results, CLI version probes, external app detection)

Today every service that needs either pattern rolls its own. A codebase survey found **10 distinct ad-hoc implementations** in `src/main/`. The trigger for this issue is a 3rd persistent-marker site landing in #15067 — concrete symptom that the gap is no longer hypothetical.

## Survey Results

Categorized by what they need (persistence × eviction policy). Cluster D/E excluded from "needs unified infra" — listed for completeness only.

### Cluster A — Persisted, no eviction (needs main-side persistent KV)

| Service | Storage backend | Key | Value | Physical location |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `BootConfigService` | self-managed sync IO | fixed schema | scalar / object | `~/.cherrystudio/boot-config.json` |
| `SpanCacheService` | hand-rolled `fs.promises` | UUID / topicId | span trees (large objects) | `~/.cherrystudio/trace/` |
| **`file.lastProcessedMigrationCompletedAt`** *(#15067)* | borrows BootConfig | fixed schema | `number \| null` | (inside BootConfig file) |

**Common shape:**
- Must survive restart and **must not** enter the backup product
- All physically live under `~/.cherrystudio/<subdir>/` (each picked the location ad-hoc)
- No size cap, no TTL, no eviction
- DeJeune's review on #15067 flagged the BootConfig borrow as semantic drift — see [thread](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/pull/15067#discussion_r-bootconfig-thread) (BootConfig's documented inclusion criterion is "must load before lifecycle", but the marker's real criterion is "machine-local, not in backup product").

### Cluster B — In-memory with TTL (largest cluster)

| Service | TTL | Key | Value | Accelerates |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `danglingCache` | 30 min | `FileEntryId` | `{state, observedAt, source}` | `fs.stat` |
| `CodeCliService.versionCache` | 30 min | CLI tool name | version string | CLI version probe |
| `CodeCliService.terminalsCache` | 5 min | (single value) | `TerminalConfig[]` | terminal enumeration |
| `ExternalAppsService.cache` | 5 min | (single value) | `ExternalAppInfo[]` | OS app detection |
| `assistant.ts healthCache` | 30 sec | providerId | health result | network probe |

**Common shape:**
- Accelerate repeat expensive operations (fs / CLI / network)
- Each implementation hand-writes `{value, timestamp}` + explicit expiry check
- TTL spans 30 seconds to 30 minutes
- CacheService **does** expose a main-side memory tier (`cache-overview.md` L99-104, "Internal cache"), but the API uses absolute `expireAt` (Unix ms) rather than relative `ttlMs`; services preferred to hand-roll.

### Cluster C — In-memory LRU (single but core hot path)

| Service | Capacity | Key | Value |
|---|---|---|---|
| `src/main/services/file/versionCache.ts` | 2000 | `FileEntryId` | `FileVersion` (mtime+size) |

Textbook Map-rotation LRU. FileManager hot path is sensitive — bugs would degrade `writeIfUnchanged` and any read-modify-write flow.

**Note (already-available infrastructure):** the `lru-cache` npm package is already a root dependency:

| Location | Imports `lru-cache`? | Usage |
|---|---|---|
| **root `package.json:376`** | **yes (`^11.1.0`)** | available to any process |
| `packages/aiCore` (own workspace dep) | yes (`package.json:48`, `^11.2.4`) | `ProviderExtension.instances` (settings hash → provider) |
| `src/renderer/` | yes | `ShikiStreamService` (×3), `shikiStream.worker`, `AgentMessageDataSource`, `messageThunk` |
| **`src/main/`** | could (root dep), but doesn't | zero usage today — `versionCache.ts` hand-rolls a Map-rotation LRU |

So Cluster C is **not even a packaging gap** — the dep is already at root, main can `import { LRUCache } from 'lru-cache'` directly. `versionCache.ts` hand-rolls purely as a legacy artifact (author likely didn't realize the dep was reachable). Lowest design weight of all clusters; a ~5-minute mechanical replacement, not an architectural decision.

### Cluster D — Specialized structures (do **not** force into cache abstraction)

| Service | Structure |
|---|---|
| `ServerLogBuffer` | per-server 200-entry ring buffer |
| `danglingCache` reverse index | `Map<FilePath, Set<FileEntryId>>` |

These are intentionally domain-specific. Listed so they're not lumped into the design.

## What main-side CacheService lacks (root cause)

Comparing the three clusters against current CacheService capability:

| Capability | Renderer Cache | Main Cache (today) | Demanded by cluster |
|---|---|---|---|
| Memory tier (free-form key) | yes | yes | B, C |
| Memory tier — TTL with relative `ttlMs` | absolute `expireAt` only | absolute `expireAt` only | B |
| Memory tier — LRU eviction | not via CacheService; community `lru-cache` used directly | community `lru-cache` already at root, unused in main (legacy) | C |
| Shared tier (cross-window) | yes | yes (relay) | (none in survey) |
| Persist tier — storage authority | yes (localStorage) | **no** (relay only) | A |

Two gaps with different shapes:
- **Persist gap** (Cluster A): architecturally visible — Cluster A leaks into BootConfig today. The most consequential design choice.
- **Memory-tier TTL ergonomics gap** (Cluster B, 5 services hand-rolled): quantitatively largest. CacheService memory tier exists but `expireAt`-only TTL pushed services to hand-roll.
- **LRU gap** (Cluster C): not a design issue at all — `lru-cache` already at root, just unused in main (`versionCache.ts` legacy hand-roll). Lowest design weight.

## Key design questions (for architecture decision)

These intentionally do not have proposed answers. They're the forks that determine downstream API shape.

### Q1 — Architectural placement (most consequential)

How does main-side cache infra relate to the existing renderer `CacheService`?

- **(a) Extend CacheService**: implement persist tier in Main. Both A and B/C plug into the same surface.
  Pro: unified API. Con: CacheService was renderer-first — adding Main-authoritative persist has to answer: IPC sync between Main persist and renderer persist? Per-process? Conflict resolution?
- **(b) Independent `MainCacheService`**: separate service from renderer's CacheService.
  Pro: clean boundary. Con: two services with similar shape but different semantics — onboarding cost.
- **(c) Three services**: keep renderer `CacheService` as-is + new `MainMemoryCache` (handles B/C) + `MainPersistedCache` (handles A).
  Pro: each service has a narrow purpose. Con: service explosion; cross-tier patterns become awkward.

### Q2 — Persistence backend (for whichever option in Q1 carries Cluster A)

- **(a) JSON files** (BootConfig style) — simple, atomic write via tmpfile+rename; slow for large data
- **(b) SQLite table** (typed cache table, similar to `app_state` but with schema)
  Caveat: there's a separate TODO to include SQLite in the backup product (`BackupManager.ts:225`). If cache lives in the same DB, it'd need to be in a separate DB file (e.g. `cache.db`) to stay out of the backup. Adds DbService surface for a non-product DB.
- **(c) Per-namespace file directories** (SpanCache style) — suits large blobs, awkward for plain KV
- **(d) Hybrid**: small KV → JSON file, large blobs → file directory

### Q3 — API shape

- **(a) schema-driven typed** (Preference / BootConfig style) — compile-time safety, fewer free-form footguns
- **(b) free-form string keys** (current CacheService memory tier) — flexibility, no schema migration burden
- **(c) builder pattern** — services declare their own cache instance with `withTTL(30_000).withCapacity(2000).build()`

### Q4 — TTL ergonomics

(LRU is essentially handled by `lru-cache` — already at root, see Cluster C note. Open question is only about TTL.)

- **(a) inline options**: `cache.set(k, v, { ttl: 30_000 })`
- **(b) per-namespace defaults**: namespace declares default TTL, individual writes can override
- **(c) decorators / factory**: `withTTL(cache, 30_000)`
- **(d) defer to `lru-cache`**: TTL is already supported by the package (`ttl` option); same dep that covers Cluster C also covers Cluster B if every consumer is willing to instantiate `LRUCache` directly

### Q5 — Schema migration

For persisted caches whose value shape changes between app versions: do we expect schema migration support, or is "delete on mismatch" acceptable (consistent with "cache can be regenerated")?

## Out of scope

- Cluster D entries (specialized structures intentionally kept ad-hoc)
- Renderer-side cache (already works)
- Whether to delete the existing `app_state` schemaless-KV-commons pattern (separate concern — see DeJeune review thread on FileManager direct access)

## Related

- PR #15067 — trigger PR (file module Phase 2 Batch 0), where the BootConfig borrow surfaced
- Issue #15112 — file module v2 refactor tracking (parent context for #15067)
- `docs/references/data/cache-overview.md` — current Cache system docs
- `docs/references/data/boot-config-overview.md` / `boot-config-schema-guide.md` — current BootConfig docs

## Action requested

Architecture decision on Q1 first (placement); Q2-Q5 follow once Q1 is settled. Open to a design RFC or smaller series of decisions, whichever fits team conventions.

title: Architecture: AppStateService — encapsulate the app_state schemaless KV table
body:
**Owner:** to be assigned (architecture decision needed)

> **Update 2026-05-23:** the original triggering site (`FileManager.getMigrationCompletedAt`) was removed in `9f24df74a` along with the skip-once mechanism it served. The issue remains valid — `SeedRunner` and `MigrationEngine` continue to bypass any service boundary — but the urgency profile has shifted from "two consumers and a third just landed" to "two consumers, the third never landed".

## Background

Surfaced during review of #15067 (DeJeune comment on the now-removed `FileManager.getMigrationCompletedAt`). The `app_state` table is a SQLite schemaless KV commons that has accumulated direct-read/write sites across the codebase. The pattern works today but the invariants are entirely informal — there are no schema-level, type-level, or service-level guardrails.

This issue tracks the design of a dedicated `AppStateService` to encapsulate the table.

## Current state

### Schema

`src/main/data/db/schemas/appState.ts`:

```typescript
export const appStateTable = sqliteTable('app_state', {
  key: text().primaryKey(),
  value: text({ mode: 'json' }).notNull(),  // schemaless JSON
  description: text(),                       // optional, currently unused at every call site
  ...createUpdateTimestamps
})
```

### Direct consumers (2)

| Service | Key(s) | Access pattern | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `MigrationEngine` (`src/main/data/migration/v2/core/MigrationEngine.ts`) | `migration_v2_status` | read + write (preboot phase) | Sole writer of `migration_v2_status`. Value shape: `MigrationStatusValue` (`packages/shared/data/migration/v2/types.ts:101-108`). |
| `SeedRunner` (`src/main/data/db/seeding/SeedRunner.ts`) | `seed:*` prefix | read + write | Uses a `seed:` prefix convention to namespace, but the convention has no schema enforcement. |

> A third consumer (`FileManager.getMigrationCompletedAt`, the cross-domain reader that originally triggered this issue) was removed in `9f24df74a` along with the skip-once mechanism it served. The issue's structural concern still applies to the two remaining consumers.

No `AppStateService`, no helper functions, no repository layer between either of these and the schema.

### Why this is structurally fragile

1. **No write-ownership enforcement.** "Only MigrationEngine writes `migration_v2_status` during preboot" is an unwritten invariant. If a future lifecycle-phase service writes the same key (intentionally or by typo collision), conflicts surface only in production.
2. **No value-shape guarantee.** Every consumer casts `value` to its expected shape (`as { completedAt?: unknown }`, etc.). Value evolution between app versions has no migration story.
3. **No key-namespace enforcement.** `SeedRunner` uses `seed:` prefix as a soft convention. Nothing prevents another service from picking the same prefix.
4. **The `description` column has never been populated** at any call site — the only schema-level affordance for documenting a key's purpose is dead.
5. **Dead `status` lane.** `MigrationStatusValue.status` includes `'in_progress'` in the type union but `MigrationEngine` never writes it. Any future cross-domain reader of `migration_v2_status` will have to handle an unwritten state defensively without any schema or service-level guidance about whether `'in_progress'` is allowed to be observed.

## Triggering review comment

[DeJeune on #15067, `FileManager.ts:808`](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/pull/15067#discussion_r-app-state-thread) flagged a cross-domain bare read added in that PR and observed that it "continues to flatten the 'app_state is a schemaless KV commons' anti-pattern". That specific call site was removed in `9f24df74a` together with the skip-once mechanism it served, so the trigger is gone — but the underlying anti-pattern that the comment highlighted still applies to `SeedRunner` and `MigrationEngine`, and this issue captures the structural fix.

## Key design questions (for architecture decision)

These do not have proposed answers — they're the forks that determine downstream API shape.

### Q1 — Service shape

- **(a) Lifecycle service** (`@Injectable @ServicePhase(Phase.BeforeReady)` like `DbService` / `PreferenceService`). Pro: integrates with the rest of v2 data layer. Con: heavier than a pure data accessor needs to be.
- **(b) Direct-import singleton** (non-lifecycle, like `danglingCache`). Pro: lighter. Con: no `application.get()` discovery; less consistent with `DbService` / `PreferenceService`.
- **(c) Module-level helpers** (`readAppState(key)` / `writeAppState(key, value)` functions). Pro: smallest API surface. Con: still no service-level place to enforce ownership.

### Q2 — Type-level enforcement model

- **(a) Schema-driven typed** (Preference / BootConfig style — see `docs/references/data/preference-schema-guide.md`). Each key declared with its value shape; compile-time check on `get<K>()` / `set<K>()`. Drives migration tooling. Highest safety, biggest authoring overhead.
- **(b) Per-domain branded keys** (e.g. `MigrationStatusKey extends Brand<'app_state.migration_v2_status'>`). Lighter than (a), still type-safe at the call site. Doesn't drive migration.
- **(c) Free-form string keys with optional shape registration**. Smallest change from today. Lowest safety; not much better than now.

### Q3 — Write-ownership enforcement

- **(a) Compile-time**: writer service declared per key; consumers get read-only handles. Possible via Q2(a) typing.
- **(b) Runtime**: writer asserts itself via a token. Less strict but adds a guardrail.
- **(c) Documentation-only**: JSDoc invariants; no enforcement. Effectively today's state.

### Q4 — Migration story for value shape evolution

When `MigrationStatusValue` adds/removes a field across app versions, what's the upgrade path?

- **(a) Versioned values** (`{ version: number, ...payload }`). Each read site checks `version` and either uses-as-is or runs an in-place migrator. Explicit but verbose.
- **(b) Latest-shape only** with a one-time migration at app startup. Cleaner runtime code, but coupling with the data-classify toolchain (see `v2-refactor-temp/tools/data-classify/`).
- **(c) Reset on shape mismatch** — acceptable only for regenerable values. `migration_v2_status` is NOT regenerable, so this option doesn't apply uniformly; per-key policy may be needed.

### Q5 — Relationship with #15270 (main-process cache infra)

The cache-infra discussion in #15270 used the now-removed `file.lastProcessedMigrationCompletedAt` BootConfig marker as one of its case studies. With that marker also gone (`9f24df74a`), the two issues are still orthogonal but no longer share any current consumer:

- **#15270**: cache-shaped (regenerable, eviction-aware) main-side state
- **This issue**: durable, non-regenerable, schemaless KV that exists in SQLite

But the design decisions interact — e.g. whether AppStateService stores in SQLite or a separate store overlaps with #15270's Q2 (persistence backend). Worth keeping cross-references when deciding.

## Out of scope

- Migrating each consumer atomically. AppStateService rollout can be phased — first SeedRunner (smallest blast radius), then MigrationEngine.
- `description` column population — separate concern (probably belongs in the migration story Q4).
- Adding new app_state keys — this issue is about wrapping the existing 3 keys; new keys should wait until the service exists.

## Related

- PR #15067 — trigger PR, where the FileManager cross-domain read was originally introduced and subsequently removed in `9f24df74a`
- Issue #15270 — main-process cache infrastructure gap (related but distinct; see Q5 above)
- `docs/references/data/preference-overview.md` — closest existing comparable in the v2 data layer

## Action requested

Architecture decision on Q1 (service shape) and Q2 (typing model) first — they cascade to the rest.

title: [Feature] Pin agent-generated HTML apps to Launchpad
body:
## Background

When agents produce an HTML artifact — a visualization, a small tool, an illustrated report — users often want to reuse it later. Today these get buried in chat history. Cherry Studio can already render HTML artifacts inline in messages (with Preview / Open External / Download), and has a Launchpad that lists user-pinned mini-apps. This iteration adds two levels of persistent entry so a useful artifact doesn't get lost.

## Goal

Provide two levels of persistent entry for agent-generated HTML artifacts:
1. **Pin to chat** — quick re-access within the current chat.
2. **Save to Launchpad** — persistent access across all chats (the HTML becomes a custom mini-app).

Whether the HTML is purely static or pulls live data via an external API makes no difference to this feature — it's the same HTML either way.

## User experience

### Pin to chat (new)
- Add a "Pin" toggle on the inline HTML artifact in a message.
- When pinned, the artifact stays accessible in a quick-access area of the current chat, so users don't have to scroll back through history.
- Scope: current chat only.

### Save to Launchpad (new)
- Add a "Save to Launchpad" action on the inline HTML artifact, alongside the existing Preview / Open External / Download.
- On click, prompt for a name (default: the HTML's title; fallback `"HTML App {timestamp}"`).
- After saving, the HTML becomes a custom mini-app and appears automatically in Launchpad and the mini-apps list.
- Single click opens it inside Cherry Studio (no external browser).
- Rename / remove / pin / unpin behave the same as any other custom mini-app.

### Non-goals
- Editing the HTML after save (delete and re-save instead).
- Custom icon picker (v1 uses the default).
- Cross-device sync.
- Intercepting the HTML's own network behavior — external API calls are the HTML's own concern.

## Verification

- [ ] Both "Pin" and "Save to Launchpad" actions are visible on the inline HTML artifact.
- [ ] After pinning, the artifact stays quickly accessible within the current chat.
- [ ] After saving, the app appears in Launchpad and the mini-apps list, and opens inside Cherry Studio (not an external browser).
- [ ] If the HTML references an external data source (e.g. calling an external API for live data), the data loads and renders correctly.
- [ ] App restart preserves saved apps.
- [ ] Existing rename / remove / pin / unpin on custom mini-apps works on saved HTML apps.
- [ ] Removing a saved HTML app also cleans up its underlying local storage (no leftover files).
- [ ] No regression on the existing Preview / Open External / Download actions.

## Related

- #15120 — Agent-generated file paths should be clickable (same theme: make agent artifacts actionable beyond chat).
- #12565 — MinApp editing functionality (complements this — saved HTML apps will benefit from edit / icon / reorder).

title: [Feature]: Add 'Topic Auto-Rename' toggle to all assistant types and per-session name lock
body:
> [\!NOTE]
> This issue/comment/review was translated by Claude.

### Issue Checklist

- [x] I understand that issues are for reporting problems and requesting features, not for off-topic comments, and I will provide as much detail as possible to help resolve the issue.
- [x] I have checked the pinned issues and searched through the existing [open issues](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/issues), [closed issues](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20state%3Aclosed), and [discussions](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/discussions) and did not find a similar suggestion.
- [x] I have provided a short and descriptive title so that developers can quickly understand the issue when browsing the issue list, rather than vague titles like "A suggestion" or "Stuck."
- [x] The latest version of Cherry Studio does not include the feature I am suggesting.

### Platform

macOS

### Version

v1.2.3 (main branch; aware this may target v2)

### Is your feature request related to an existing issue?

Yes. This proposal extends two existing issues:
1. **#14824** ("Pin conversation name") — Users manually rename conversation tabs, but the next AI reply overwrites it. Auto-naming should respect manual modifications.
2. **#14459** ("Add topic auto-rename toggle for regular assistants and Agents") — Points out that **Quick Assistants** already have a "Topic Auto-Rename" toggle, but **default assistants and Agent settings don't have this toggle**. This creates inconsistent experience: some assistants can be toggled, others can't.

This proposal combines both: extend the toggle to all assistant types, and add a lightweight per-session "lock" feature for users who don't want to disable it globally but still want to pin specific session names.

### Problem Description

#### Real-world Scenario
1. You create a new session, defaulting to "New Session" or auto-named from the first message.
2. You manually rename it to something meaningful, like "Default Session", "Q3 Budget Planning", "Weekly Report Draft".
3. After the next AI reply, Cherry Studio **silently overwrites the name** to an AI-generated summary.
4. You rename it again → gets overwritten again → **infinite loop**.

#### Why It's Frustrating
- Users managing **dozens of conversation tabs** rely on fixed names for quick identification. Auto-renaming scrambles this mental map entirely.
- Some sessions are for **long-term reference** (project management, knowledge base, scheduled tasks), names should remain stable.
- Currently, the only workaround is to keep manually renaming it—essentially fighting against the software.

#### Code-level Basis
Quick Assistants already have a "Topic Auto-Rename" toggle, indicating the underlying logic supports it. But this option isn't shown in default assistant and Agent settings, causing auto-renaming to be force-enabled and impossible to disable.

### Desired Solution

#### Primary: Add "Topic Auto-Rename" toggle to all assistants
Extend the existing toggle to **all assistant types** (default assistants, Agents, custom assistants), not just Quick Assistants.

**Location:** In the assistant settings panel.

**Behavior:**
- **On (default):** Same as current behavior, auto-generates title based on conversation content.
- **Off:** Session retains its current name; manual renaming takes effect permanently and won't be overwritten.

**Rough effect:**


#### Secondary (Nice-to-have): "Lock Name" button for each session
Add a small lock icon on each conversation tab (or an option in the right-click menu) for users to **individually pin a session name** without disabling global auto-naming.

**Behavior:**
- 🔒 Locked: Name is frozen, never auto-overwritten.
- 🔓 Unlocked (default): Auto-renaming works normally.
- Locked sessions remain locked after manual renaming; new names won't be overwritten either.



This avoids the "all-or-nothing" dilemma—lock 2-3 reference sessions, let others auto-name.

### Alternative Solutions

1. **Manual rename auto-locks** (proposal from #14824): Lock after one rename. Simple enough, but unfriendly to users who "renamed but still want it to continue auto-updating."
2. **Right-click menu "Disable Renaming"**: Hidden in the menu, not as discoverable as a visible lock icon.
3. **Pure config file control**: Let users edit `config.json` to disable. Too high a barrier for most people.
4. **External script workaround**: Technically feasible (modify SQLite + reload page), but not something ordinary users should have to do.

### Additional Information

- This feature is suggested for implementation on the **v2 branch**, as the main branch is under code freeze.
- Related UX issue #14272 (breadcrumb topic name click opens Agent settings instead of rename interface) is planned for v2 resolution; this feature can be done together.
- Quick Assistants' existing "Topic Auto-Rename" toggle can serve as implementation reference—directly port it to other assistant types.

---
**Thank you Cherry Studio—it has become my primary tool, hoping to help make it even better\!**

---

### Is your feature request related to an existing issue?

## 这个功能跟已有 issue 有关吗？
有关。本提案延伸了两个已有 issue：
1. **#14824**（"固定会话名称"）——用户手动改了会话标签页的名字，但 AI 下一条回复就把它覆盖了。自动命名应该尊重用户的手动修改。
2. **#14459**（"为常规助手和 Agent 添加话题自动重命名开关"）——指出**快速助手**已经有「话题自动重命名」开关了，但**默认助手和 Agent 设置里没有这个开关**。这让体验不一致：有的助手能关，有的不能。
本提案把两者整合：让开关覆盖所有助手类型，同时加一个轻量的单会话「锁定」功能，让不想全局关闭的用户也能单独固定某个会话名。

## 问题描述

### 实际场景
1. 你新建一个会话，默认叫「新会话」或者从第一条消息自动取名。
2. 你手动把它改成有意义的名字，比如「默认会话」「Q3 预算规划」「周报草稿」。
3. AI 下一次回复后，Cherry Studio **悄悄把名字覆盖了**，变成了 AI 自动生成的摘要。
4. 你再改回来 → 又被覆盖 → **无限循环**。

### 为什么难受
- 维护**几十个会话标签页**的用户，靠固定名字快速识别。自动重命名把这张脑内地图全打乱了。
- 有些会话是**长期参考用的**（项目管理、知识库、定时任务），名字应该稳定不动。
- 目前的唯一办法是不停手动改回来，纯属跟软件较劲。

### 代码层面的依据
快速助手已经有「话题自动重命名」开关了，说明底层逻辑是支持的。但默认助手和 Agent 的设置界面里不显示这个选项，导致自动重命名强制开启、无法关闭。

### Desired Solution

### 主要：让所有助手都有「话题自动重命名」开关
把已有开关扩展到**所有助手类型**（默认助手、Agent、自定义助手），不只是快速助手。
**位置：** 助手设置面板中。
**行为：**
- **开（默认）：** 跟现在一样，根据对话内容自动生成标题。
- **关：** 会话保留当前名字不动，手动改名永久生效，不会被覆盖。
**大致效果：**
┌─ Agent 设置 ──────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                                                        │
│  ☑ 话题自动重命名                                       │
│     根据对话内容自动生成会话标题                          │
│                                                        │
│     关闭后，手动修改的会话名称将被保留                     │
│                                                        │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

Text
### 次要（锦上添花）：每个会话的「锁定名称」按钮
在每个会话标签页上加一个小锁图标（或右键菜单中的选项），让用户**单独固定某个会话名**，不用关掉全局自动命名。
**行为：**
- 🔒 锁定：名字冻结，永远不被自动覆盖。
- 🔓 未锁定（默认）：自动重命名正常工作。
- 锁定的会话手动改名后，仍保持锁定状态，新名字也不会被覆盖。
┌─ 会话标签页 ───────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                                                             │
│  🔒 默认会话    │  向日葵盐碱胁迫  │  美股板块监测 📈          │
│  （已锁定）     │  （自动命名）    │  （自动命名）            │
│                                                             │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

Text
这样避免「要么全关、要么全开」的尴尬——锁 2~3 个参考用的会话，其他让它们自动命名。


### Alternative Solutions

1. **手动改名自动锁定**（#14824 的提议）：改一次就锁住。够简单，但对「改了名但还是想让它继续自动更新」的用户不友好。
2. **右键菜单「禁用重命名」**：藏在菜单里，不如可见的锁图标好发现。
3. **纯配置文件控制**：让用户改  来关。对大多数人来说门槛太高。
4. **外部脚本绕过去**：技术上可行（改 SQLite + 重载页面），但这不是普通用户该干的事。

### Additional Information

- 该功能建议在 **v2 分支**实现，因为 main 分支处于代码冻结状态。
- 相关 UX issue #14272（面包屑中话题名点击打开了 Agent 设置而非重命名界面）已计划在 v2 解决，本功能可以一起做。
- 快速助手已有的「话题自动重命名」开关可作为实现参考，直接移植到其他助手类型即可。

---
**感谢 Cherry Studio——它已经成为我的主力工具，希望能一起让它变得更好！**

</details>

title: [Feature]: Recover Agent Workspace When Saved Directory Is Missing
body:
## Background

When a user migrates Cherry Studio from one computer to another through backup or sync, an Agent may keep a workspace path that only existed on the original computer. In that state, Agent skill loading can remain stuck without explaining that the saved workspace is missing, leaving users unable to understand the problem or recover by themselves.

## Goal

Users can recover an Agent whose saved workspace directory is missing by seeing a clear error state and selecting a new workspace path, instead of being trapped in indefinite loading.

## Spec

- When opening an Agent or loading its skills, Cherry Studio detects whether the saved Agent workspace path is missing or inaccessible before continuing normal skill loading.
- If the workspace cannot be reached, the Agent leaves the loading state and shows a clear, user-readable message that the current workspace directory is unavailable.
- The unavailable-workspace state provides an action for the user to choose a replacement workspace directory.
- After the user selects a valid replacement directory, Cherry Studio rebinds the Agent to the new workspace and retries skill loading.
- If the user cancels the directory selection, Cherry Studio keeps the Agent usable in a recoverable error state and does not continue showing an indefinite loading indicator.
- The same recovery behavior applies after device migration, backup restore, path rename, deleted folder, or disconnected external drive scenarios.

## Verification

- On computer A, configure an Agent with workspace path `/Users/alice/AgentWorkspace`. Restore or sync the same Cherry Studio data to computer B where that path does not exist. Open the Agent: the UI should stop loading and explain that the saved workspace directory is unavailable.
- From the unavailable-workspace state, choose an existing local folder as the new workspace. The Agent should save the new path and show its available skills after loading completes.
- From the unavailable-workspace state, cancel the directory picker. The Agent should remain on a clear recoverable error state with a retry or reselect action, not return to infinite loading.
- Delete or rename an Agent's workspace folder while Cherry Studio is closed, then reopen the Agent. The same missing-workspace recovery path should appear.
- Point the Agent workspace to an external drive, disconnect the drive, then open the Agent. Cherry Studio should explain that the workspace is inaccessible and allow the user to reselect a directory.
- After rebinding to a new workspace, reopening the same Agent should use the new path and should not show the missing-workspace message again.
- The target UI should show the missing workspace path, a short explanation of why skills cannot load, and a primary action to choose a new workspace directory.

## Related

No related GitHub issues or PRs were found in the searches for Agent workspace migration, missing workspace directory, skill loading, and backup/sync recovery.

body:

- [x] I understand that issues are for feedback and problem solving, not for complaining in the comment section, and will provide as much information as possible to help solve the problem.
- [x] My issue is not listed in the [FAQ](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/issues/3881).
- [x] I've looked at **pinned issues** and searched for existing [Open Issues](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/issues), [Closed Issues](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20state%3Aclosed), and [Discussions](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/discussions), no similar issue or discussion was found.
- [x] I've filled in short, clear headings so that developers can quickly identify a rough idea of what to expect when flipping through the list of issues. And not "a suggestion", "stuck", etc.
- [x] I've confirmed that I am using the latest version of Cherry Studio.

### Platform

Windows

### Version

1.9.6

### Bug Description

> **Severity / Priority**: data-integrity bug — `agents.db` content can be silently corrupted across machines. Recommend treating this as a **hotfix** candidate against the `main` branch.
>
> **Note on regression history**: this is **not a v1.9.6 regression**. The underlying race condition has been latent since **v1.7.18** (when `agents.db` was first moved into `Data/` and started being included in backups — PR #12830, 2026-02-12). Users only started reporting it widely around v1.9.x because the agents feature was significantly expanded (CherryClaw autonomous agent in #13359, per-agent skill workspaces with symlinks in #14247, etc.), causing far more frequent writes to `agents.db` and dramatically increasing the chance of collision with the auto-backup snapshot.

Users syncing Cherry Studio across two machines (home / office) via the built-in Nutstore (WebDAV) backup intermittently see two failure modes on the receiving machine after restoring from a Nutstore backup:

1. **Data loss**: Assistants and/or agent session history are partially or fully missing.
2. **Database error when creating a new conversation**:
   ```
   session_creation_failed
   failed to create session: failed query: update "sessions" set "sort_order" = "sessions"."sort_order" + 1 where "sessions"."agent_id" = ? params: agent_<id>
   ```

The only workaround that recovers usability is to **close Cherry Studio, manually delete `{userData}/Data/agents.db` (and the `-wal` / `-shm` sidecar files), restart Cherry, and re-create all agents + re-register MCP and skill files**.

### Root Cause (from reading `BackupManager.ts`)

The agents subsystem is backed by LibSQL/SQLite at `{userData}/Data/agents.db`, running in WAL mode (so `agents.db-wal` and `agents.db-shm` sidecar files exist alongside it). `agents.db` has been part of the backup payload since v1.7.18 (PR #12830 moved it from `{userData}/agents.db` into `{userData}/Data/`).

`BackupManager.backup()` (`src/main/services/BackupManager.ts:211–225`) copies the entire `Data/` directory using a raw `fs.copy()` call **while the application is still running and the database connection is open**:

```ts
// BackupManager.ts:211
if (!skipBackupFile) {
  const sourcePath = path.join(userDataPath, 'Data')
  const tempDataDir = path.join(this.tempDir, 'Data')
  if (await fs.pathExists(sourcePath)) {
    const totalSize = await this.getDirSize(sourcePath, { dereferenceSymlinks: true })
    await this.copyDirWithProgress(sourcePath, tempDataDir, ...)
  }
}
```

There is no:
- `PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE)` before the copy
- Use of LibSQL's online backup API / `VACUUM INTO`
- Closing or pausing the agents `DatabaseManager` connection
- Any coordination with the agents subsystem

The three files (`agents.db`, `agents.db-wal`, `agents.db-shm`) are copied one at a time. If a write transaction commits between two of those file copies, the snapshot inside the ZIP is **internally inconsistent**: the `-wal` references pages that are not present in the copied `.db`.

When this corrupt ZIP is later restored on another machine via `restoreDirect()` (the v6+ direct restore path that stages `Data.restore` and renames on next startup), Cherry boots with a half-consistent DB. The first write that touches `sessions.sort_order` (i.e. creating a new chat) fails with the error message above.

This is a **race condition**, which matches the user-reported "sometimes" pattern — it only happens when the auto-backup happens to fire during an active write to `agents.db`.

Note: on Windows the issue is arguably easier to hit because LibSQL is configured with `intMode: 'number'` for Windows compatibility (`DatabaseManager.ts:144`), and Windows file locking semantics differ from POSIX during the multi-file copy.

### Steps To Reproduce

1. On Machine A (Windows, Cherry Studio 1.9.6), set up the built-in **Nutstore backup** (Settings → Data → Nutstore), logged in, with **auto-backup enabled at 15 minutes** and **"Slim Backup" (skip file data) disabled**.
2. Use Cherry actively — create assistants, open agent sessions, send messages. Make sure the next auto-backup tick coincides with active usage (e.g. while waiting for a model response, or right after sending a message).
3. Wait for the scheduled auto-backup to complete.
4. On Machine B (also Windows, also 1.9.6, signed into the same Nutstore account), click **"从坚果云恢复" / "Restore from Nutstore"** and pick the latest backup.
5. After Cherry restarts and finishes restoration, open Cherry and try to **create a new conversation under any agent**.
6. Observe: either (a) some agents / sessions are missing, or (b) the new-conversation action fails with `session_creation_failed ... update "sessions" set "sort_order" = "sessions"."sort_order" + 1`.

Reproduction is probabilistic; with frequent active usage during auto-backup, several rounds of restore on the other machine will trigger it.

### Expected Behavior

The backup ZIP should contain a **consistent snapshot** of `agents.db`, so that restoring it on another machine yields a healthy, fully-usable database — no `session_creation_failed`, no missing agents/sessions.

Concretely: when `BackupManager` copies `Data/` while Cherry is running, it should produce a SQLite snapshot using one of the safe mechanisms:
- Use LibSQL's online backup API (preferred) to write a checkpoint-consistent `.db` into the temp directory, with no `-wal`/`-shm` sidecars.
- Or issue `PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE)` and pause writes through the agents subsystem during the file copy.
- Or use `VACUUM INTO 'path/to/temp/agents.db'`.

The IndexedDB and Local Storage portions of the backup are less impacted (Chromium handles concurrent reads more forgivingly), but the same general "live file copy" concern applies — fixing this for SQLite is the higher-impact change.

### Relevant Log Output

```shell
session_creation_failed
failed to create session: failed query: update "sessions" set "sort_order" = "sessions"."sort_order" + 1 where "sessions"."agent_id" = ? params: agent_<id>
```

### Additional Context

- **Why only reported now**: although the race has been latent since v1.7.18, several factors during the v1.8.x–v1.9.x cycle have raised the trigger rate to the point where end users now hit it repeatedly:
  - `sessions.sort_order` introduced in v1.8.0 (PR #13460) — every new chat now triggers an `UPDATE sessions SET sort_order = sort_order + 1` write transaction, widening the per-action write window.
  - CherryClaw autonomous agent type (PR #13359) and per-agent skill workspaces with symlinks (PR #14247) shipped during v1.9.x — these features drive substantially more frequent writes to `agents.db`.
  - Anecdotally, users only started broadly enabling cross-device sync (Nutstore / WebDAV) as the agents feature matured into something worth syncing.
- **Hotfix justification**: this is a silent data-integrity bug, not a UI/cosmetic regression. Users who rely on cross-machine sync via the built-in Nutstore/WebDAV backup can lose assistants and chat history with no obvious cause, and the only recovery path forces them to manually delete `agents.db` and re-create everything. Suggest a minimal `hotfix/*` PR to `main` adding a checkpoint+pause (or LibSQL backup API) wrapper around the `Data/` copy in `BackupManager.backup()`.
- The failing query is the one in `SessionService.createSession` (`src/main/services/agents/services/SessionService.ts:172`), executed inside a transaction — fully consistent with a WAL/main-db mismatch.
- **Important diagnostic note for reviewers**: please do **not** look only at the v1.9.5 → v1.9.6 diff. `BackupManager.ts` had zero changes in that window and there are no new migrations between v1.9.5 and v1.9.6 — the root fix must live in `BackupManager.backup()`'s `Data/` copy step regardless of release.
- User-level workaround until fixed: disable auto-backup; perform manual backup only while Cherry is idle (no in-flight writes); wait for backup completion before quitting / leaving the machine.

title: [Feature]: Agent session supports /clear command to reset context
body:
## Problem
When using Agent (claude-code type) in CherryStudio, there is no way to clear the conversation context within an existing session. The `/clear` command from Claude Code CLI is not exposed in the CherryStudio UI.

Currently, the only workaround is to create a new Topic/Session, which loses all session state and configuration.

## Proposed Solution
Add a "Clear Context" button or support the `/clear` slash command in the Agent session UI. This should:
- Clear the conversation history while keeping the same session
- Reset the context window without creating a new session
- Be accessible via a UI button and/or slash command input

## Additional Context
- CherryStudio's Agent system is built on `@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk`, which already supports `/clear` natively in the CLI
- The SDK's `SessionService` already merges slash commands from `.claude/commands/`, so exposing `/clear` in the UI should be feasible
- Related (but different): #12452 (clear chat window for Assistants, not Agent sessions)

## Environment
- Cherry Studio v1.x
- Agent type: claude-code
- OS: Windows 11

title: [Feature]: Marketplace Connectors — Third-Party Integrations via OAuth or MCP
body:
## Background

The v2 UI work at [`CherryHQ/cherry-studio-ui-design`](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio-ui-design) treats Connectors as a first-class kind inside the Marketplace, alongside Skills, MCP, Agents, Assistants, Prompts, Knowledge Base, and CLI. A dedicated Connectors view, a privacy-forward install dialog with paired Cherry/service logos, a custom-connector submission entry, and an initial set of seed services are being laid out there. What does not exist is the implementation. Today, users who want their Agent to act on Gmail, Notion, or similar services still hit a configuration wall — copy-pasting JSON MCP configs, installing runtimes, refreshing tokens by hand. Connectors close this gap by giving every supported service a single Marketplace card that connects in one click. A Connector's underlying form may be **OAuth** (Cherry runs the OAuth itself) or **MCP** (Cherry connects to the service's MCP server), and users can add their own custom Connectors in either form.

## Goal

Users browse, authorize, and manage third-party Connectors entirely from the in-app Marketplace — via OAuth or MCP, official or user-contributed — and any Agent in Cherry can then act on the connected services with no further configuration.

## Spec

- The Marketplace sidebar lists **Connectors** as a first-class kind alongside Skill, MCP, Agent, Assistant, Prompt, Knowledge Base, and CLI.
- Selecting Connectors renders a dedicated management view: section header with a short subtitle, a Submit Custom Connector button at the top-right, and a card grid of available Connectors. Each card carries a small badge indicating its connection form — **OAuth** or **MCP**.
- Clicking any Connector card opens an install dialog with paired Cherry/service logos, a title of the form "Connect Cherry with {service}", and three fixed privacy policy rows: (1) the user controls which data Cherry can access; (2) Cherry follows the service's existing permissions; (3) Cherry does not use the user's data to train models. The primary CTA "Continue" branches by form:
  - **OAuth** form: Continue launches OAuth in the system browser and returns to Cherry on success.
  - **MCP** form: Continue reveals MCP endpoint and auth inputs pre-filled with the publisher's defaults; on submit, Cherry establishes the MCP session, running the server's own OAuth if it requires one.
  - In either form the CTA flips to "Connected to {service}" once authorization completes and the card shows an installed-state indicator.
- Launch Official catalog ships six high-frequency services covering email / cloud storage / calendar / notes / code hosting / messaging — **OAuth: Gmail, Google Drive, Google Calendar, GitHub, Slack; MCP: Notion** — each matching the form the vendor officially recommends.
- **Custom Connectors**: the Submit Custom Connector entry lets users add their own. The user picks OAuth or MCP, supplies the required config (OAuth client/scopes, or MCP endpoint/transport/auth), and the entry appears in their grid; users can also publish a custom Connector to the public catalog via the standard Marketplace submission flow used by other kinds.
- Connected Connectors are available to all Agents by default, with per-Assistant toggles in Assistant settings — consistent with how Skills attach to Agents (#15029, #14876).
- Disconnect revokes credentials locally; where the provider supports remote revocation (e.g. Google), upstream tokens are also revoked; MCP sessions are torn down on disconnect.
- Token or session expiry surfaces an in-app Reconnect prompt through the Unified Notification Center (#14899) — never a silent failure or a raw error toast.

## Verification

- Open Marketplace → sidebar shows Connectors in the kind list. Click Connectors → the view renders the management header with a Submit Custom Connector button at the top-right and a grid of six seed cards (Gmail, Google Drive, Google Calendar, Notion, GitHub, Slack); each card shows a small OAuth or MCP badge matching the catalog above.
- **OAuth path**: click the Gmail card → install dialog opens centered with Cherry and Gmail logos at the top, title "Connect Cherry with Gmail", three policy rows in order: (1) you control which Gmail data Cherry can access; (2) Cherry follows Gmail's existing permissions; (3) Cherry does not use your Gmail data to train models. CTA reads "Continue". Click Continue → system browser opens Google OAuth → user authorizes → browser hands back to Cherry → CTA changes to "Connected to Gmail" and the Gmail card shows the installed-state indicator.
- **MCP path**: click the Notion card → the same dialog layout opens with Cherry and Notion logos and the three policy rows. Continue reveals MCP endpoint and auth inputs pre-filled with Notion's official MCP server values; submit triggers Notion's MCP OAuth → CTA changes to "Connected to Notion" with the installed-state indicator.
- In any Agent conversation immediately after, user says "list this week's emails from John and summarize" → Agent uses Gmail; separately, "create a Notion page summarizing today's meeting" → Agent creates the page via the Notion MCP connector. Neither flow requires additional configuration in between.
- **Custom Connector**: click Submit Custom Connector → modal lets the user pick OAuth or MCP. Choose OAuth, supply client ID/scopes → new card appears in the grid with the OAuth badge. Repeat with MCP, supply endpoint/auth → new card appears with the MCP badge. Both can be connected like Official entries.
- In Assistant A's settings, disable Notion → that Assistant cannot call Notion tools even though Notion remains connected globally; Assistant B with Notion enabled still works.
- Disconnect Gmail from the grid → repeating the earlier prompt returns "Gmail is not connected" or prompts the user to reconnect. Disconnect Notion → the MCP session is closed; subsequent Notion calls fail with the same Reconnect prompt.
- A long-idle Gmail connection (OAuth) and a long-idle Notion connection (MCP): the next Agent call to each surfaces a Unified Notification Center entry indicating that connector needs to be reconnected, with a one-click Reconnect button.
- Open Settings → there is no separate Connectors page; the only management entry point for Connectors is the Marketplace's Connectors view.

title: [Feature]: Cherry Skill Creator — Built-in Agent for Creating and Maintaining Skills
body:
## Background

Cherry Studio supports installing skills from external registries, ZIP archives, and local directories — but offers no in-product guidance for users who want to create a skill from scratch. Non-technical users who hit a workflow worth wrapping into a reusable skill have nowhere to turn inside the app; they must learn authoring conventions (frontmatter shape, description-as-trigger, references structure) on their own. Cherry Assistant can help, but it's a generalist — skill creation is one of dozens of things it handles, and once a skill is installed, no agent in the app proactively spots opportunities to fix or improve it.

## Goal

Users — from absolute beginners to experienced authors — can create high-quality Skills through conversation with a dedicated built-in Agent that also proactively flags opportunities to improve existing Skills.

## Spec

- A built-in Agent named **"Cherry Skill Creator"** (icon 🛠️) appears in the Agent list immediately after Cherry Assistant.
- On the first message of every new conversation, the Agent briefly introduces itself as Cherry Studio's built-in helper for creating and maintaining Skills.
- For users who don't know where to start, the Agent walks them through a guided flow — target use case, trigger phrases, expected input/output — and produces a minimal runnable Skill at the end.
- For experienced users, the Agent produces Skills that conform to authoring conventions: correct frontmatter, trigger-friendly description, conventional directory layout, proper use of references.
- When the user mentions an existing Skill misbehaving, asks why a Skill didn't trigger, or describes a new need that fits cleanly into an already-installed Skill, the Agent proactively offers to update or improve that Skill rather than waiting to be asked.
- When the user asks something outside Skill creation/maintenance, the Agent gives a brief one-line answer and then redirects them to Cherry Assistant for general help.

## Verification

- Opening Cherry Skill Creator for the first time shows a one-paragraph self-introduction naming it as the built-in Skill creation helper.
- User types "I want to make a skill but don't know where to start" → Agent responds by asking for the use case, expected trigger phrases, and what input/output the skill should produce, instead of asking the user to provide a spec.
- After the user describes a scenario (e.g. "summarize meeting notes from Feishu Minutes"), the Agent produces a skill folder containing a SKILL.md whose frontmatter description begins with a use-case + sample trigger phrases that Claude can match on.
- User says "my Feishu skill keeps responding to non-Feishu questions" → Agent offers to inspect the skill's description and propose a tightened version, without the user explicitly asking for an update.
- User asks "what's the weather today" → Agent gives a one-line answer ("I can't check live weather") and immediately suggests "for general questions, Cherry Assistant is a better fit — want me to hand off?"
- The Agent list shows agents in order: Cherry Claw → Cherry Assistant → Cherry Skill Creator.

## Related

#14538 #15029

title: [Feature]: Built-in Official Vendor Assistants (Claude / ChatGPT / Gemini / DeepSeek / Kimi / Doubao)
body:
## Background

When users pick a vendor's model in Cherry Studio (Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, DeepSeek, Kimi, Doubao), they get the raw model capability but lose the vendor's official chat experience — the identity framing, response style, formatting conventions, and current-date awareness that the vendor's own web app injects via system prompt. Users who want "the claude.ai feeling, but inside Cherry" today have to find and paste in the prompt themselves, which is fragile and undiscoverable. Cherry's existing preset assistant gallery contains many community-contributed roles (Product Manager, Translator, etc.), but no entries that mirror the third-party vendor experience users are most familiar with.

## Goal

Users can one-click add an official-vendor assistant (Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, DeepSeek, Kimi, Doubao) that comes pre-configured with that vendor's style and automatically routed to a model from that vendor in the user's own provider configuration, so chatting with it inside Cherry feels indistinguishable from chatting with that vendor's own web app.

## Spec

- In the assistant preset gallery, six new entries are surfaced: Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, DeepSeek, Kimi, Doubao. Names are kept as the vendor's brand (not localized). Each entry shows a vendor-branded icon.
- Each preset bundles a system prompt authored to evoke the vendor's official chat behavior, and is associated with a vendor (not with a specific model version).
- The bundled system prompt explicitly accounts for the runtime gap between Cherry Studio and the vendor's own web app — it sets identity / tone / formatting in the vendor's style, but does not promise tools (image gen, file creation, sandbox URLs, vendor-specific compute backends) that Cherry cannot deliver via that vendor's API.
- Predefined system prompts do not embed any date. The current date is injected by Cherry at conversation start, so the assistant's date awareness stays accurate over time without a content update.
- The assistant's responses, including self-introduction, follow the user's Cherry UI language by default. The predefined system prompt must not hardcode a specific output language (e.g. it cannot force "I'm Claude" in English regardless of UI). The model still mirrors the user's input language when the user writes in a different language mid-conversation.
- When a user adds a preset to My Assistants, Cherry resolves the actual model by first checking whether the user has set a default model for that vendor's provider (and using that if so), otherwise picking from the user's enabled list according to a vendor-specific preference order favoring the tier suited for general chat (e.g. Claude → Sonnet, ChatGPT → GPT-5 main line, Gemini → Pro, DeepSeek → chat, Kimi → K2 main, Doubao → the user's first available Doubao endpoint).
- Adding a preset to "My Assistants" creates a normal editable assistant. The original preset entry stays in the gallery for re-adding. Users can edit or delete the copy freely without affecting the gallery entry.
- If the user opens a preset assistant whose bound provider has not been configured or has no enabled models for that vendor, the user is shown an inline prompt to configure that provider. The assistant does not silently fall back to a different vendor's model — doing so would break the "feels like the official experience" promise.

## Verification

- Open the assistant preset gallery → see six new entries (Claude / ChatGPT / Gemini / DeepSeek / Kimi / Doubao), each with vendor-branded icon and the brand name in English (not translated).
- With Anthropic provider configured (Sonnet and Opus both enabled, no explicit default set) and Cherry UI set to English, add Claude → ask "who are you?" → assistant resolves to Sonnet (the preferred chat tier) and introduces itself in English ("I'm Claude, made by Anthropic"), demonstrating Claude's tone and formatting without claiming Cherry-unavailable tools (e.g. no offer to "create a downloadable file" via vendor sandbox).
- Same setup but Cherry UI set to Chinese → add Claude → ask "你是谁？" → assistant introduces itself in Chinese ("我是 Claude，由 Anthropic 开发"), not in English.
- User on Chinese UI types an English message → assistant replies in English, mirroring the user's current message language.
- User has explicitly set the Anthropic provider's default model to Opus → adds Claude assistant → assistant uses Opus, respecting the user's explicit choice.
- User has Anthropic provider configured but no Claude model enabled → clicks Claude preset → sees configure-provider guidance (same flow as the provider-not-configured case), not a silent swap to an OpenAI model.
- User configures Volcano Ark with multiple Doubao endpoints → adds Doubao assistant → assistant uses the user's first available Doubao endpoint without requiring extra setup.
- Ask each official assistant "what's today's date?" → assistant answers with today's actual date. Inspecting the predefined prompt content confirms no date string is hardcoded.
- Add Claude to My Assistants, edit its system prompt, delete it → "Claude" preset entry is still visible and re-addable from the gallery; My Assistants list no longer shows the deleted copy after restart.
- Add the same preset twice → user gets two independent assistant copies that can be edited separately.
- Switch the Cherry UI between Chinese and English → preset names stay in the vendor's brand spelling; preset descriptions show in the matching language.

## Related

#3922 #14021

title: feat(file-module): persist FileEntryId in FileUIPart, hydrate URL on read
body: ## Background v2 messages store file references as `FileUIPart.url` in `message.data.parts[]`. Currently these are absolute `file://` paths (e.g., `file:///Users/alice/.../Data/Files/{uuid}.ext`). This is fragile: - **`userData` path change** (cross-device sync, data directory migration, OS user rename) invalidates every persisted internal file URL. - Internal file physical paths are a runtime-resolved value (`application.getPath('feature.files.data') + filename`) — hardcoding them in persisted data breaks the "Main is SoT for path resolution" principle established in `architecture.md §4.1.1.1`. Design discussion: #14911 (comment https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/pull/14911#issuecomment-4551463414). ## Proposal Use a custom URL scheme for internal FileEntry references in persisted message parts. The app already registers `cherrystudio://` as a system-level deep-link protocol via `ProtocolService` (`app.setAsDefaultProtocolClient`); the file URL scheme should build on or coexist with this existing registration. **Example** (concrete scheme TBD — could be `cherrystudio://file/internal/{uuid}.ext`, `cherrystudio-file://internal/{uuid}.ext`, or similar): ``` cherrystudio://file/internal/{uuid}.ext ``` ### Properties - `{uuid}` in the filename **is** the `FileEntryId` — reverse lookup to entry is free (no DB query). - External files remain `file:///absolute/path` (user-owned paths, not affected by `userData` changes). - The scheme is an internal persistence format — resolved before reaching AI SDK or provider APIs. ## Scope ### File Module side 1. **`file.getCherryUrl(entryId): string`** — IPC method that returns the custom-scheme URL for a given FileEntryId. This is the canonical way for renderer code to obtain a persistable file reference when constructing `FileUIPart`. 2. **Electron `protocol.handle` registration** — register a handler for the custom URL scheme via Electron's `protocol.handle()` API so that **renderer-process HTML elements can consume these URLs directly** without an extra IPC round-trip. **Why this is needed:** `FileUIPart.url` values are rendered by the renderer in multiple contexts — ``, `

title: [Feature]: Auto-Adapt Context Length Based on Model Context Window
body:
> [\!NOTE]
> This issue was translated by Claude.

## Background

Cherry Studio's "Context Count" slider in assistant model settings limits history by message count (0–100, last tick = unlimited). Because message length varies wildly — a single code-paste can be larger than 30 chat turns combined — the same slider value behaves very differently across conversations and across models, with two symptoms visible in user feedback:

1. **Silent overflow on long chats** — history exceeds the model's context window, returning hard API errors like the one in #11688.
2. **Loss of conversational continuity after switching models** — when users switch to a model with a smaller context window mid-conversation, responses appear to no longer reference earlier turns, and the assistant's answers can feel inconsistent with what was discussed before. A real user observation:
   > "After switching the model, the responses feel disconnected from the earlier conversation — is it only referencing the most recent message?"

   The community workaround is to manually split a conversation into multiple topic windows, since "a single window's context length is limited; the longer the chat, the more likely the model loses earlier context." This forces users to memorize each model's context window (128K vs 200K vs 1M) and pre-plan topic splits themselves, which #12739 and #10883 both flagged as unintuitive.

## Goal

Make context length self-managing by default — automatically fit history within the selected model's context window — while letting power users fall back to manual message-count control.

## Spec

- The "Context Count" row in assistant model settings has a mode toggle with two states: **Auto** (default) and **Manual**.
- In **Auto** mode: the slider is hidden; the system automatically decides how much history to include each turn based on the currently selected model's context window, leaving headroom for the user's next prompt and the model's response.
- In **Manual** mode: the existing 0–100 (last tick = unlimited) message-count slider is shown and behaves exactly as today.
- Switching the assistant's model in Auto mode immediately re-adapts to the new model's context window — no user action required.
- Switching from Auto to Manual restores the user's last manual value (or the existing default if there is none); switching from Manual to Auto preserves the manual value so toggling back doesn't lose it.
- If the selected model's context window is unknown to Cherry Studio, Auto mode falls back to a safe default and tells the user (via the same row) that the value is an estimate.

## Verification

- Open assistant model settings on a fresh install: the "Context Count" row shows mode toggle = Auto by default, no slider visible.
- In Auto mode, select a 128K-window model and a 1M-window model in sequence and send a ~100K-token history to each: both turns succeed without the overflow error in #11688, and the second turn visibly retains more history than the first.
- In Auto mode with the slider hidden, switch to Manual: slider appears at the previous manual value (or default), and current behavior is unchanged from today's product.
- Toggle Auto → Manual → Auto → Manual repeatedly: the manual value last set by the user is preserved across all toggles.
- In Auto mode, select a model whose context window is unknown to Cherry Studio (e.g. a freshly added custom model): the row shows an "estimated" indicator and the conversation still succeeds without overflow.
- Reproduce the #11688 scenario (long Agent novel-writing turn against a 131K-token model) with Auto mode on: no `maximum context length exceeded` API error.
- Reproduce the user-reported scenario: start a long conversation on a 1M-window model, then switch to a 128K-window model mid-conversation. In Auto mode, responses should remain consistent with earlier turns up to what the new model's context window can fit, rather than appearing to reference only the most recent message.

## Related

#12739 #10883 #14985 #11688 #12786

title: refactor: unify all binary acquisition under BinaryManager
body:
## Summary

Rename `MiseService` → `BinaryManager` and consolidate all binary acquisition paths into a single mise-backed service. This addresses review feedback on #15184 — `mise` is an implementation detail that should not leak into persisted surfaces.

## Problem

Binary acquisition currently happens through 5+ uncoordinated mechanisms:

| Mechanism | Location | How it works |
|---|---|---|
| MiseService | `src/main/services/MiseService.ts` | Bundled mise + `mise use -g` for registry/npm/pipx tools |
| rtk extraction | `src/main/utils/rtk.ts` | Copies bundled binary to `~/.cherrystudio/bin/` |
| OpenClaw install | `resources/scripts/install-openclaw.js` | Downloads from GitHub/mirror |
| CodeCliService | `src/main/services/CodeCliService.ts` | `bun install -g` to `~/.cherrystudio/install/global/` |
| ripgrep | `node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk/vendor/` | Vendored, hardcoded path in FileStorage |

This fragmentation means: no unified install state, scattered on-disk paths, duplicated mirror logic, and `getBinaryPath()` can't find binaries from all sources.

## Design

### Single backend: mise handles everything

mise already supports registry, npm (`npm:X`), pipx (`pipx:X`), GitHub (`github:owner/repo`), and HTTP backends. No multi-backend interface needed — BinaryManager is a mise lifecycle wrapper with a backend-agnostic public surface.

### Persisted surface rename

| Current | Target |
|---|---|
| `feature.mise.tools` | `feature.binary.tools` |
| `mise:*` IPC (7 channels) | `binary:*` |
| `MiseTool` / `MiseState` | `ManagedBinary` / `BinaryState` |
| `MiseToolPreset` / `PREDEFINED_MISE_TOOLS` | `BinaryToolPreset` / `PREDEFINED_BINARY_TOOLS` |
| `feature.mise.data` / `feature.mise.state_file` | `feature.binary.data` / `feature.binary.state_file` |
| `MiseService` (`@Injectable`) | `BinaryManager` |

### Default core tools: uv, bun, rg

All three ship **bundled at build time** (added to `download-binaries.js`) for instant first-run availability. mise manages updates after extraction.

- **rg (ripgrep)**: replaces vendored SDK binary; `FileStorage.getRipgrepBinaryPath()` → `getBinaryPath('rg')`
- **before-pack.js** ripgrep vendor filtering deleted

### Migration per mechanism

| Mechanism | Action |
|---|---|
| **rtk** | Delete `extractRtkBinaries()` + AgentBootstrapService call. rtk is opt-in from Plugins page via mise registry. `rtkRewrite()` degrades gracefully when absent. |
| **OpenClaw** | Delete `install-openclaw.js`. Use `npm:openclaw` via BinaryManager. Keep runtime orchestration in OpenClawService. |
| **CodeCliService** | Replace `bun install -g` with mise npm/pipx backends. Remove `BUN_INSTALL` env var + `~/.cherrystudio/install/global/`. |
| **ripgrep** | Bundle rg at build time. Replace hardcoded vendor path with `getBinaryPath('rg')`. |
| **OVMS** | **Not included** — server provisioning (hardware detection, multi-zip, patching, config generation), not binary acquisition. |

### npm/pip mirror support

Add `NPM_CONFIG_REGISTRY` and `PIP_INDEX_URL` to `MISE_PASSTHROUGH_ENV`. Auto-detect China users (via existing `isUserInChina()`) and set mirror URLs in `buildIsolatedEnv()`:
- npm: `https://registry.npmmirror.com`
- pip: `https://pypi.tuna.tsinghua.edu.cn/simple`

## Implementation phases (single PR, logical commits)

1. **Rename + lock persisted surface** — IPC, types, prefs, pathRegistry, service file rename
2. **rtk cleanup + rg as default** — delete extraction, add rg to build bundling + BinaryManager
3. **Mirror support** — env passthrough + China auto-detection
4. **OpenClaw → mise** — delete install script, delegate to BinaryManager
5. **CodeCliService → mise** — replace bun global install with mise npm/pipx

## Open questions

- [ ] **claude-code shim**: After `mise use -g claude`, does the shim work as a drop-in replacement for `bun cli-wrapper.cjs`?
- [ ] **China mirror timing**: `isUserInChina()` is async; `buildIsolatedEnv()` is sync. Need to handle the async gap.
- [ ] **rg build assets**: Need exact GitHub release asset names + sha256 for all 6 platform-arch combos.

## Related

- PR: #15184 (original MiseService implementation)
- Review: https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/pull/15184#pullrequestreview-4372085509
- Parent issue: #15183

title: [Bug]: MCP OAuth callback accepts first code without state validation
body:
### Issue Checklist

- [x] I understand that issues are for feedback and problem solving, not for complaining in the comment section, and will provide as much information as possible to help solve the problem.
- [x] My issue is not listed in the [FAQ](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/issues/3881).
- [x] I've looked at **pinned issues** and searched for existing [Open Issues](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/issues), [Closed Issues](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20state%3Aclosed), and [Discussions](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/discussions), no similar issue or discussion was found.
- [x] I've filled in short, clear headings so that developers can quickly identify a rough idea of what to expect when flipping through the list of issues. And not "a suggestion", "stuck", etc.
- [x] I've confirmed that I am using the latest version of Cherry Studio.

### Platform

Linux

### Version

Cherry Studio `1.9.6`, commit `3ccf6d34cae5409a02a573533373441ec95f612c`

### Bug Description

The MCP OAuth local callback server accepts any request whose URL starts with the configured callback path and contains a `code` query parameter. It does not bind the callback to the OAuth transaction with a `state` value, and it does not propagate or validate the callback `state` before calling `transport.finishAuth(authCode)`.

As a result, during the five-minute OAuth window, a request to `http://127.0.0.1:12346/oauth/callback?code=<attacker_code>` can win the race and cause Cherry Studio to complete the OAuth flow with the attacker's authorization code instead of the code from the user's current login flow.

Relevant code:

- `src/main/services/mcp/oauth/callback.ts`: `req.url?.startsWith(path)` is accepted, only `code` is extracted, and only `code` is emitted.
- `src/main/services/MCPService.ts`: `waitForAuthCode()` returns the first emitted code and passes it directly to `transport.finishAuth(authCode)`.
- `src/main/services/mcp/oauth/provider.ts`: `McpOAuthClientProvider` does not implement the SDK's optional `state()` method, so the SDK does not add a transaction-bound `state` parameter for this provider.

Observed impact:

- OAuth callback injection / first-code-wins behavior.
- Login CSRF / authorization binding confusion during a pending MCP OAuth flow.
- Potential account or service binding confusion, depending on the MCP OAuth provider's authorization-code handling.
- Potential sensitive data exposure if the misbound MCP service can receive user prompts, files, tool arguments, or other user-provided data.

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Start an MCP OAuth flow in Cherry Studio for an HTTP/SSE MCP server that requires OAuth.
2. While Cherry Studio is waiting for the OAuth callback, send a request to the local callback endpoint before the legitimate OAuth provider redirects back:

   ```text
   http://127.0.0.1:12346/oauth/callback?code=MalloryCode&state=attacker_state
   ```

3. Allow the legitimate provider callback to arrive later:

   ```text
   http://127.0.0.1:12346/oauth/callback?code=AliceCode&state=victim_state
   ```

4. Observe that the first code is accepted and passed to `finishAuth()`.

A minimal local reproduction, without modifying project files, produced:

```json
{
  "chosen_by_handleAuth": "MalloryCode",
  "finishAuth_received": "MalloryCode",
  "vulnerable": true
}
```

The same reproduction also showed that `/oauth/callback.extra?code=PrefixCode` is accepted because the callback path check uses `startsWith(path)`.

### Expected Behavior

Cherry Studio should bind each OAuth callback to the exact OAuth transaction that initiated it. The callback handler should reject callbacks with missing or mismatched `state`, should use exact path matching, and should only pass an authorization code to `finishAuth()` after validating that the callback belongs to the pending OAuth flow.

### Relevant Log Output

```shell
No application log is required. The issue is visible from source behavior and was reproduced with a local callback simulation matching the current callback flow.
```

### Additional Context

The callback server listens on `127.0.0.1`, which limits remote network reachability, but browser-based attacks can still target loopback URLs while the victim has an OAuth flow pending.

The strongest confirmed impact is OAuth callback injection / login CSRF. Broader provider mix-up or data exposure depends on the specific MCP OAuth server and the capabilities exposed by the misbound MCP service.

### Is your feature request related to an existing issue?

Image-edit models like nano-banana / gpt-image-2 / seedream support multi-round editing where a previous output is reused as the next round's reference image. Today there is no in-product path to feed an AI-generated image back as a reference — users have to right-click → save the image to disk, then drag-drop or pick it back into the inputbar manually. This friction breaks the iteration loop that makes these image-edit models genuinely useful for creative work.

Related community feedback: a user pointed out that nano-banana-style image editing is becoming a core workflow, and the current copy/save/reupload cycle blocks fast iteration.

### Desired Solution

Add a **"Use as Reference"** action button under every AI-generated image in the assistant reply. Clicking it injects the image into the inputbar's reference-image slot — same data path as drag-drop upload — ready for the next prompt.

**Spec:**

1. Below each generated image in `MessageContent → ImageBlock`, render an action bar alongside existing Download / Copy buttons.
2. Add a **"Use as Reference"** action (suggested icon: 🖼️↩️ or similar reference-loop glyph).
3. On click, push the image (as a `FileBlock` with `type: image`) into the current chat's pending input attachments — same behavior as drag-drop / file-picker upload.
4. The button is visible only when the current assistant's selected model has image-input capability (e.g. nano-banana, gpt-image-2, seedream); for text-only models, do not render it.

- Send a prompt that generates an image.
- Click "Use as Reference" under the result → image appears in inputbar reference slot.
- Next prompt edits the image as expected.

### Alternative Solutions

- **Right-click → "Use as Reference"** context menu instead of a visible button. Hides clutter for text-only models automatically, but discoverability is much lower than a button.

body:

- [x] I have checked the pinned issues and searched through the existing [open issues](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/issues), [closed issues](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20state%3Aclosed), and [discussions](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/discussions) and did not find a similar suggestion.
