title: [Feature]: Optimize global memory: per-model GPU pinning + idle delay + use conversation model for summarization
body:
> [\!NOTE]
> This issue was translated by Claude.

### Issue Checklist

- [x] I understand that issues are for reporting problems and requesting features, not for off-topic comments, and I will provide as much detail as possible to help resolve the issue.
- [x] I have checked the pinned issues and searched through the existing [open issues](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/issues), [closed issues](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20state%3Aclosed), and [discussions](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/discussions) and did not find a similar suggestion.
- [x] I have provided a short and descriptive title so that developers can quickly understand the issue when browsing the issue list, rather than vague titles like "A suggestion" or "Stuck."
- [x] The latest version of Cherry Studio does not include the feature I am suggesting.

### Platform

Windows

### Version

v1.9.8

### Is your feature request related to an existing issue?

I am using two models running through Ollama in Cherry Studio:

Conversation model: qwen3.6:27b-q8_0 (approximately 26.6 GiB)

Global memory model: qwen3-embedding:8b (approximately 4.4 GiB, used for automatically organizing conversation history)

Hardware:

GPU 0: 48 GB (suitable for running large models)

GPU 1: 16 GB (sufficient for running embedding)

Core pain point: Both models compete for GPU 0 memory, causing frequent eviction, performance degradation, and even crashes.

### Desired Solution

Problem 1: Cannot specify GPU for different models

Phenomenon

Ollama by default schedules all models to GPU 0, causing memory conflicts, frequent eviction, performance degradation, and even crashes. Users cannot make the embedding model fixed to use GPU 1 (which it can run completely fine) through the Cherry Studio interface.

Suggestion

Add a "GPU allocation" option (Auto / GPU 0 / GPU 1 / CPU only) in the model configuration interface. If Ollama supports the gpu_ids API parameter in the future, Cherry Studio can pass it directly; before that, advanced user options can be provided (such as launching separate Ollama subprocesses for each model and setting different CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES).

Problem 2: Global memory trigger timing is not intelligent enough

Current status

The global memory feature seems to run in real-time or on a scheduled basis, without considering whether the conversation model is currently in use. When users are interacting intensively with the main model, the embedding model suddenly starts, competing for GPU resources, causing conversation response lag or even interruption.

Suggestion

Add a delay organization strategy based on main model idle time:

Allow users to set an "idle wait time" (e.g., 30 seconds, 1 minute, 5 minutes, etc.).

Only trigger the global memory organization operation when the main model (conversation model) has no new requests during that period.

If the user starts a new conversation during the organization process, it should be able to immediately interrupt the organization (or cancel the current embedding call) and prioritize responding to the user.

Requirement 3: Use the conversation model itself to organize memory (new idea, from community feedback #13011)

Problems with the existing solution

Even if the embedding model is pinned to GPU 1, two models still need to be loaded simultaneously, occupying double the memory (approximately 31 GB). Although GPU 1's 16 GB is sufficient, it still causes resource waste and potential bandwidth competition.

More elegant approach

Use the last conversation's model to generate memory/summaries instead of using a separate embedding model.

Specific approach

Record the model ID used for each conversation (e.g., qwen3.6:27b).

When organizing memory is needed (e.g., after the user has been idle for a while), directly call the same conversation model's summarization or embedding capability to let it summarize historical messages.

This way, Cherry Studio only needs to keep one model in the GPU at any given time—the one currently being used for the conversation.

When organizing memory, the model is already in memory, no additional loading needed, zero switching overhead.

Advantages

Completely avoid multi-model memory conflicts.

Fully utilize existing model capabilities (modern LLMs can already do good summarization).

Simplify GPU scheduling, no need to allocate GPU separately for each model.

For multi-conversation scenarios, each conversation independently uses its own model without interference.

Implementation suggestions

When organizing memory, send a special system prompt to the current model, such as:

"Please summarize the following conversation history into a short paragraph for long-term memory."

If the model itself does not support embedding (e.g., pure conversation model), use its generation summary function instead of vector storage; or allow users to configure a fallback strategy: when the model does not support it, fall back to a small embedding model (but the loading issue still needs to be resolved).

Provide options for users:

Use conversation model to organize (recommended, saves memory)

Use dedicated lightweight model to organize (more accurate but uses more memory)

User configuration example

yaml
Global memory settings:
  Organization timing: After main model idle for 1 minute
  Organization model: Use current conversation model (automatic)
  Fallback strategy: If model does not support, use qwen3-embedding:8b (only when memory is sufficient)

Expected summary

Through improvements in the above three directions (GPU allocation, idle delay, reuse conversation model), Cherry Studio can:

Completely avoid multi-model GPU conflicts.

Significantly reduce memory usage.

Improve smoothness in multi-task scenarios.

Thanks to community users for the "reuse conversation model" idea, which should be the most elegant solution in the current environment.

### Platform

Windows

### Version

v1.9.8

### Is your feature request related to an existing issue?

我在 Cherry Studio 中同时使用两个通过 Ollama 运行的模型：

对话模型：qwen3.6:27b-q8_0（约 26.6 GiB）

全局记忆模型：qwen3-embedding:8b（约 4.4 GiB，用于自动整理对话历史）

硬件：

GPU 0: 48 GB（适合跑大模型）

GPU 1: 16 GB（足够跑 embedding）

核心痛点：两个模型抢占 GPU 0 显存，导致频繁驱逐、性能下降甚至崩溃。

### Desired Solution

问题 1：无法为不同模型指定 GPU
现象
Ollama 默认将所有模型调度到 GPU 0，导致显存冲突、频繁驱逐、性能下降甚至崩溃。用户无法在 Cherry Studio 界面中让 embedding 模型固定使用 GPU 1（它完全跑得动）。

建议
在模型的配置界面增加"GPU 分配"选项（自动 / GPU 0 / GPU 1 / CPU only）。如果 Ollama 未来支持 gpu_ids API 参数，Cherry Studio 可以直接传递；在此之前，可提供高级用户选项（如为每个模型启动独立的 Ollama 子进程，并设置不同的 CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES）。

问题 2：全局记忆的触发时机不够智能
现状
全局记忆功能似乎是实时或定时执行，没有考虑对话模型当前是否正在使用。当用户与主模型密集交互时，embedding 模型突然启动，抢占 GPU 资源，导致对话响应卡顿甚至中断。

建议
增加一个基于主模型空闲时间的延迟整理策略：

允许用户设置一个"空闲等待时间"（例如 30 秒、1 分钟、5 分钟等）。

只有当主模型（对话模型）在该时间段内没有任何新请求时，才触发全局记忆的整理操作。

如果在整理过程中用户又发起新对话，应能立即中断整理（或取消当前 embedding 调用），优先响应用户。

需求 3：使用对话模型自身来整理记忆（新思路，来自社区反馈 #13011）
现有方案的问题
即使将 embedding 模型固定到 GPU 1，仍然需要同时加载两个模型，占用双倍显存（约 31 GB），且 GPU 1 的 16 GB 虽然够用，但依然造成资源浪费和潜在的带宽竞争。

更优雅的思路

用最后一次对话所使用的模型来生成记忆/摘要，而不是使用一个独立的 embedding 模型。

具体做法

每个对话记录最后使用的模型 ID（例如 qwen3.6:27b）。

当需要整理记忆时（例如用户空闲一段时间后），直接调用同一个对话模型的摘要或嵌入能力，让它对历史消息进行总结。

这样，整个 Cherry Studio 在任意时刻只需要保持一个模型在 GPU 中——就是当前对话正在使用的那个模型。

整理记忆时，模型已在显存中，无需额外加载，零切换开销。

优点

✅ 彻底避免多模型显存冲突。

✅ 充分利用已有模型的能力（现代 LLM 本身就能做很好的摘要）。

✅ 简化 GPU 调度，无需为每个模型单独分配 GPU。

✅ 对于多对话场景，每个对话独立使用其自己的模型，互不干扰。

实现建议

在整理记忆时，向当前模型发送一个特殊的系统提示，例如：

"请将以下对话历史总结为一小段文字，用于长期记忆。"

如果模型本身不支持 embedding（比如纯对话模型），可以使用其生成摘要功能代替向量存储；或者允许用户配置降级方案：当模型不支持时，回退到一个小型 embedding 模型（但此时仍需解决加载问题）。

提供选项给用户：

使用对话模型整理（推荐，省显存）

使用专用轻量模型整理（更精确但多占用显存）

用户配置示例

yaml
全局记忆设置:
  整理时机: 主模型空闲 1 分钟后
  整理模型: 使用当前对话模型（自动）
  降级策略: 若模型不支持，则使用 qwen3-embedding:8b（仅当显存充足时）
期望总结

通过以上三个方向的改进（GPU 分配、空闲延迟、复用对话模型），Cherry Studio 可以：

完全避免多模型 GPU 冲突。

极大降低显存占用。

提升多任务场景下的流畅度。

感谢社区用户提供的"复用对话模型"思路，这应该是当前环境下最优雅的解决方案。

title: [Bug]: New user startup in 2.0 - default assistant sentinel mapping and IPC import instance error prevents creating new conversations
body:
> [\!NOTE]
> This issue was translated by Claude.

### Issue Checklist

- [x] I understand that issues are for feedback and problem solving, not for complaining in the comment section, and will provide as much information as possible to help solve the problem.
- [x] My issue is not listed in the FAQ.
- [x] I've looked at pinned issues and searched for existing Open Issues, Closed Issues, and Discussions, no similar issue or discussion was found.
- [x] I've filled in short, clear headings so that developers can quickly identify a rough idea of what to expect when flipping through the list of issues. And not "a suggestion", "stuck", etc.
- [x] I've confirmed that I am using the latest version of Cherry Studio.

### Platform

Windows

### Version

v2.0.0

### Bug Description

When a new user installs v2.0.0 and launches the application for the first time, the default assistant in the Redux store uses the sentinel value `id: 'default'`. Due to the foreign key constraint introduced by the v2 database on `topic.assistant_id`, using this sentinel when creating a new conversation (POST /topics) triggers a database foreign key error.

Additionally, during the implementation of fixes and handling of the default assistant bootstrap process, the following issues exist in the code:
1. Import spelling error in `src/main/ipc.ts`: it imports `assistantService` which is not exported; the actual exported instance name is `assistantDataService`. This directly causes type compilation to fail, and at runtime causes a `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'getDefault')` error crash.
2. The `UUID_V4_PATTERN` regex in `assistantBootstrapThunk.ts` is too strict: it only supports UUID v4 format. If the database generates a UUID v7 format assistant ID, the `isUuid` check will fail, causing the bootstrap process to execute repeatedly.
3. `toV1Shape` does not properly extract the model provider: the transformation assigns an empty value `''` to `provider`, breaking the expected type contract.

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Fresh install Cherry Studio v2.0.0 (or clear existing data and launch).
2. The application launches and renders the main page.
3. Observe the type compilation status or click to create a new conversation and an error occurs, or during this process the application may not function normally due to an uncaught member-not-exist error within IPC.

### Expected Behavior

1. New users can normally load the bootstrap process; after application startup, the `default` sentinel is safely replaced within `BootstrapGate` with the real UUID of the default assistant initialized by Seeder.
2. IPC channels load normally, each module imports correctly and type validation passes.
3. Can identify and be compatible with compliant assistant IDs including UUID v7.

### Relevant Log Output

```shell
src/main/ipc.ts(7,10): error TS2724: '"@data/services/AssistantService"' has no exported member named 'assistantService'. Did you mean 'AssistantDataService'?
```

### Additional Context

This issue has been successfully reproduced and reviewed locally; modifications needed to `src/main/ipc.ts` for the export name and corrections to `assistantBootstrapThunk.ts` for related regex and mapping logic.

### Platform

Windows

### Version

v2.0.0

### Bug Description

当新用户全新安装 v2.0.0 启动应用时，Redux store 中的默认助手采用 sentinel 哨兵值 `id: 'default'`，而由于 v2 数据库对 `topic.assistant_id` 引入了外键约束，导致新建会话（POST /topics）时使用此 sentinel 会引发数据库外键错误。

此外，在实现修复和处理默认助手的引导流程中，代码中存在如下问题：
1. `src/main/ipc.ts` 导入拼写错误：导入了未导出的 `assistantService`，实际上导出的实例名为 `assistantDataService`。这会直接导致类型编译挂掉，且在运行时会引起 `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'getDefault')` 报错崩溃。
2. `assistantBootstrapThunk.ts` 中的 `UUID_V4_PATTERN` 匹配正则过于严格：只支持 UUID v4 版本。若数据库生成了 UUID v7 格式的助手 ID，则 `isUuid` 判断会失败，这导致 bootstrap 引导过程将重复执行。
3. `toV1Shape` 未正常提取 model provider：转换过程中将 `provider` 赋空值 `''`，破坏了类型期待。

### Steps To Reproduce

1. 全新安装 Cherry Studio v2.0.0（或清空已有数据启动）。
2. 在应用启动渲染主页面。

title: [Feature]: Guided Creation Flow for Chat Assistants and Agents
body:
## Background

Creating a new Chat Assistant in Cherry Studio is a one-shot modal (emoji, name, free-form system prompt, optional knowledge base) — and creating a new Agent is another one-shot modal (~8 fields including instructions, model, allowed tools, MCPs, scheduler config). Users who don't already know "what kind of assistant they want" or "which Skills / MCPs / Prompts fit their use case" stare at a blank form and either copy-paste from somewhere external or leave the fields empty and hope for the best. The Prompts library and the (growing) Skills library both exist, but neither is surfaced at the moment a user actually needs them — at creation time. The result is that the long tail of users either give up before their first useful Assistant/Agent, or ship under-configured ones that don't reach their potential.

## Goal

Users describe in one or two sentences what they want a new Assistant or Agent to do, and Cherry Studio produces a fully pre-populated draft — name, prompt, relevant Skills, relevant MCPs, suggested model — that they review and confirm in one click.

## Spec

- Both "Create Assistant" and "Create Agent" entry points offer a **Guided** path alongside the existing single-form modal (relabeled "Manual"); Guided is the default for first-time users, Manual is the default for users who have created at least one before.
- Guided starts with a single free-text "What should this do?" input plus optional structured hints (use-case category, target audience, language); the user can submit with only the free-text filled in.
- On submit, the flow proposes a complete draft on one review screen: name + emoji (Assistant) / name + description (Agent), system prompt, suggested model — and for Agent additionally a set of relevant Skills toggled on by default, suggested MCPs, and any obviously inferable configuration (e.g. scheduler cron if the user said "every morning").
- When the user's description matches existing entries in the Prompts library (by title / tags / content similarity), the proposed system prompt is **drawn from the library** with a visible "From your Prompts library: <name>" badge, instead of silently generating a new one; the user can toggle "Generate new instead".
- Every field in the review screen is inline-editable; nothing in the draft is locked. Confirming creates the Assistant/Agent exactly as previewed.
- When no matching Skills / MCPs / Prompt are found, the flow degrades gracefully: the draft still shows with empty Skills / MCPs sections labelled "No matches — add manually later" and a freshly generated prompt.
- Cancelling the Guided flow at any point saves the user's free-text description as a resumable draft; reopening "Create Assistant" / "Create Agent" surfaces a "Resume draft" banner.

## Verification

title: [Feature]: "Chat Now" Button in Assistant Preset Preview for Instant Trial
body:
## Background

When a user browses the Assistant preset gallery, clicking a card opens a preview modal showing the preset's name, description, and system prompt as markdown. The only action button is "Add to my assistants" — so to *try* a preset, the user must first commit to adding it to their library, then go find it in their assistant list, then start a chat. This turns preset browsing into a high-friction "shop-then-commit" experience: users either over-add (their assistant list fills with unevaluated presets they end up cleaning later) or under-explore (they skim the prompt, guess at fit, and skip presets they'd actually have liked once tried). There's no "try before commit" mechanism anywhere in the app today.

## Goal

From the preset preview modal, the user can start an immediate trial conversation with the preset's exact configuration without permanently adding the preset to their assistant list — and from inside the trial chat, can either keep the assistant in one click or discard it by closing.

## Spec

- The preset preview modal exposes two primary actions: **"Add to my assistants"** (existing) and **"Chat now"** (new). "Chat now" is the suggested default for users with an empty assistant list, while "Add" remains the default for users who already have at least one assistant.
- Clicking "Chat now" closes the modal and opens a chat using the preset's name, emoji, system prompt, default model, knowledge bases, and settings — the exact same configuration "Add" would have persisted.
- The trial chat is visibly marked as a trial: a banner above the input reads "Trying preset: <name> — not yet added to your assistants", with two inline actions: **"Keep this assistant"** and **"Discard"**.
- "Keep this assistant" persists the assistant to the user's library and converts the trial chat's topic into a normal topic under that assistant; the conversation history is preserved.
- "Discard" or closing the trial wipes the trial chat and its messages. A confirmation appears only if the trial has at least one user message.
- The trial persists across navigation: switching to another conversation in the sidebar does not discard the trial; it stays listed in a dedicated "Trial" section of the sidebar until kept or discarded.
- At most one trial chat exists at a time. Starting a new "Chat now" while another trial is unsaved prompts the user to keep or discard the existing trial before the new one opens.
- If the preset has no default model, "Chat now" uses the user's global default model — same convention as a normal new chat — and the banner notes "Using default model: <name>".

## Verification

- User opens the Assistant preset gallery, picks "Code Reviewer", clicks "Chat now" → modal closes, a new chat opens with name "Code Reviewer", emoji, system prompt loaded; banner reads "Trying preset: Code Reviewer — not yet added".
- In the trial, user sends "Review this snippet" with code → assistant responds using the preset's prompt; "Code Reviewer" does NOT appear in the regular assistant list during the trial; it is listed under a "Trial" section in the sidebar.
- User clicks "Keep this assistant" → toast "Code Reviewer added"; banner disappears; "Code Reviewer" now appears in the regular assistant list with the trial chat preserved as its current topic.
- User opens "Translator" preset and clicks "Chat now" while the "Code Reviewer" trial is still unsaved → prompt "Keep or discard 'Code Reviewer' trial?" appears before the Translator trial opens.
- User sends 2 messages in a trial, clicks "Discard" → confirmation "Discard trial chat? This will delete 2 messages"; on confirm, both the trial assistant and its messages are gone; on cancel, the trial stays open.
- User starts a trial, sends no messages, navigates to another conversation, returns the next day → trial still listed under the "Trial" section with all original configuration intact.
- Preset with no default model → "Chat now" still works; banner additionally shows "Using default model: <user's global default>".

title: [Feature]: Fix Scheduled Task Message Perspective — Frame Trigger as Task Execution, Not User Reminder
body:
## Background

Today, when a user creates a scheduled task on an Agent (e.g. "remind me to drink water every 2 hours"), they fill in a single `prompt` field. When the task fires, the scheduler injects that prompt verbatim into the conversation as a user-side message, with no framing telling the Agent this is a scheduled trigger. The Agent reads the firing message as a fresh user request and replies in kind — so the user's "drink water" reminder reads as the user telling the Agent to drink water, and the Agent answers "thanks for the reminder, I'll drink some water" — perspective inverted. The same code path already wraps "heartbeat"-type messages with a `[Heartbeat]` framing prefix, but regular scheduled tasks don't get that treatment. The result is every scheduled reminder feels visibly broken: cold, off-perspective, and clearly unfinished to anyone trying to actually use the feature.

## Goal

When a scheduled task fires, the Agent's response is the actual reminder or action the user originally asked for — framed from the Agent to the user — instead of a reply to an imaginary user message.

## Spec

- The task creation UI replaces the single ambiguous "prompt" field with two clearly labeled fields: **"What should the Agent do when this fires?"** (the instruction the Agent executes) and an optional **"Task name"** (used in lists and notifications, never sent to the Agent).
- When a scheduled task fires, the scheduler wraps the task's instruction in a system-level framing before handing it to the Agent — the Agent receives clear context that this is a scheduled task firing, who it's for, and what the user originally asked the task to do.
- The Agent's resulting message is what the user sees as their reminder — addressed from Agent to user (e.g. "It's been two hours — time to drink some water"), not a reply to a fabricated user turn.
- Scheduled-task messages render in the conversation timeline with a visible "Scheduled task" marker (icon or label), so the user can distinguish them at a glance from their own typed messages.
- Tasks created under the old single-prompt UI are migrated by treating their existing prompt text as the new "instruction" field; no data is lost and old tasks fire with the new framing without manual edits.
- The heartbeat task path's existing `[Heartbeat]` framing is unified with this new scheduled task framing — they share one implementation, not two parallel ones.
- The same framing convention applies to every entry point that injects scheduled messages (cron MCP tool, Cherry Claw scheduled tasks, regular scheduled tasks), so the perspective is consistent across all surfaces.
- The task creation UI shows a one-line **preview** of how the Agent's reminder will read when the task fires, computed from the user's instruction, so users catch perspective mistakes before saving.

## Verification

- User creates a scheduled task on a Chat Assistant with instruction `"Remind me to drink water"`, schedule = every 2 hours. Two hours later → the conversation shows a "Scheduled task" marker, and the Agent's message reads e.g. `"Hey — it's been two hours, time to drink some water!"` — NOT `"Got it, I'll drink some water!"`.
- User creates `"Run a check on yesterday's open PRs and post a summary"` on a Cherry Claw agent, schedule = daily 9am. At 9am → Agent actually performs the check and posts the summary; does NOT respond as if the user just asked.
- User who created tasks under the old single-prompt UI sees their existing tasks intact after upgrade — the old prompt text appears in the new "What should the Agent do" field; tasks fire with the new framing without manual edits.
- Heartbeat tasks continue to work — heartbeat messages produce the same kind of Agent response as before the change, with no perspective regression.
- A task fires while the Agent is mid-conversation on an unrelated topic — the scheduled-task message appears in the timeline visibly marked as scheduled, not silently as a normal user turn.
- In the task creation UI, a user types instruction `"喝水"` (ambiguous one-word) → the preview shows what the Agent will say (e.g. "Reminder: drink water") so the user can refine the instruction or accept; preview updates as the user edits.
- A scheduled task triggered via the cron MCP tool produces a reminder framed exactly the same way as one triggered via the Tasks UI — no inconsistency across surfaces.

title: [Feature]: Temporary Chat — Disposable Conversations That Don't Persist to Topics or Sessions
body:
## Background

Today, every conversation in Cherry Studio is persisted from the moment the user sends the first message — the topic appears in the sidebar, all messages go to SQLite, and the only way to discard a chat later is to manually delete it from the topic list. There is no path for "I just want to ask a quick question and have it leave no trace": every casual lookup, every experimental prompt, every sensitive ad-hoc question pollutes the topic list, and the user either accumulates disposable topics they later sweep up or goes to a separate tool altogether. The in-memory infrastructure for non-persisted conversations actually already exists in the backend (a dedicated service with create/delete/messages/promote endpoints) — but no UI surface wires through to it. The capability is dormant.

## Goal

Users can start a chat that does not persist to the topic list, sidebar history, or any database — it lives only as long as it's open — with the option to promote any temporary chat to a permanent topic if they decide to keep it.

## Spec

- A clearly labeled **"Temporary Chat"** entry point appears next to the existing "New chat" / "New topic" button, with an unambiguous icon (e.g. incognito / eye-with-slash).
- Clicking it opens a chat surface visually distinguished from normal chats — a persistent banner reading **"Temporary chat — nothing will be saved"** and an accent color or subtle background tint — so the user cannot mistake it for a normal chat.
- The chat uses the user's current default Assistant + model, same as a normal new chat; the difference is purely in persistence — all data flows through the in-memory path, no DB writes.
- A temporary chat does not appear in the main topic list. It lives in a dedicated **"Temporary"** strip at the top of the sidebar (or in a popover above the topic list), visible only while a temporary chat is active.
- Closing the temporary chat — clicking close, navigating to a different chat without saving, quitting the app, or system crash — **wipes the chat and all its messages from memory**. No DB record, no log line referencing message content, nothing recoverable.
- A single **"Save as topic"** action in the temporary chat header promotes the chat to a normal persisted topic: all messages are persisted in one transaction, the temporary chat disappears from the "Temporary" strip, and the new topic appears in the regular sidebar with the conversation intact.
- At most one temporary chat is alive at a time. Starting a new "Temporary Chat" while another is open closes the previous one — with a confirm prompt only if the previous has at least one user message.
- Temporary chats are also available with V2 Agents — same entry point in the Agent surface, same in-memory backend, same banner, same Save-as-topic affordance for the Agent's session.
- A keyboard shortcut (configurable, default e.g. `Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+N`) opens a temporary chat instantly from anywhere in the app.

## Verification

- User clicks "Temporary Chat" → a new chat opens with the persistent banner "Temporary chat — nothing will be saved"; the regular topic list shows no new entry; a "Temporary" strip appears above it with this chat.
- User sends 3 messages → the assistant replies normally; conversation flows the same as any regular chat surface.
- User closes the temporary chat → confirmation "Discard temporary chat? 3 messages will be deleted"; on confirm, the chat vanishes from sidebar and memory.
- User starts a temp chat, sends 2 messages, clicks "Save as topic" → toast "Saved as 'Quick question about X'"; the "Temporary" strip disappears; a new topic appears in the regular topic list with both messages intact.
- User starts a temp chat, opens a different normal topic without saving, navigates back to the temp chat → it is still there, banner still visible, conversation intact (only explicit close or app exit ends it).
- User quits the app entirely while a temp chat with 5 messages is open → on next launch, no trace of the temp chat exists; the DB has no row for it; no log line records its message bodies.
- User has an active temp chat A with 2 messages, clicks "Temporary Chat" again → confirm "Close current temporary chat? It will be discarded"; on confirm, A is wiped and a fresh B opens; the "Temporary" strip never shows two entries at once.
- User in a V2 Agent context clicks "Temporary Chat" → a temp session opens for that Agent (in-memory only); Save-as-topic, close, and DB-no-trace behavior match the Assistant-side path exactly.
- User presses `Cmd+Shift+N` from any screen → a temp chat opens immediately with the user's current default Assistant; banner visible.

## Related

#12664 (Draft feature — adjacent but distinct: pre-send drafts vs. post-send disposable chats)
#14898 (Account system & sync — adjacent privacy angle once cross-device sync is in scope)
#15571 ("Chat Now" preset trial — sibling ephemeral-conversation pattern, scoped to preset trial)

title: [Feature]: Realtime Conversation Mode — Voice, Video, and Screen Share with Realtime Models
body:
## Background

Cherry Studio has already catalogued realtime-capable models in its provider registry (Gemini 2.5 Flash Live, GPT-4o Realtime, and related), and has even declared `AUDIO_START / AUDIO_DELTA / AUDIO_COMPLETE` chunk types in the message stream pipeline. The half-finished plumbing is sitting there. But none of the infrastructure needed to *actually* use those models exists: no microphone capture, no audio playback, no camera input, no screen capture, no realtime streaming transport, no OS-level permission handling, no audio rendering block. Users who pay for realtime APIs cannot reach those capabilities through Cherry Studio — they go to the provider's first-party app (Google AI Studio, OpenAI Playground) or build their own UI. Cherry Studio's signature value — unified configurable provider access — evaporates the moment a user wants the conversational mode the rest of the AI ecosystem is rapidly moving toward.

## Goal

Users can have a real-time spoken conversation with a Realtime model inside Cherry Studio — with optional camera and screen sharing as additional input — using whichever realtime-capable provider they already have configured.

## Spec

- A **"Realtime"** mode toggle is visible at the chat input area when the active Assistant uses a realtime-capable model; the toggle is hidden when no realtime model is configured for the current assistant.
- Clicking the toggle opens a dedicated realtime conversation surface (full-pane or panel) with three input controls: **microphone**, **camera**, and **screen share**. Mic is on by default. Camera and screen share are off until enabled.
- The assistant streams audio output through the user's default output device with a visible waveform; a live text transcript of both user and assistant turns is shown alongside for noisy environments and accessibility.
- All three input modes route through the realtime provider's native API — Cherry does not run a separate STT or TTS pipeline; the model handles modality conversion natively.
- A persistent **"End conversation"** affordance terminates the provider connection, closes mic/camera/screen capture, and returns the user to the regular chat surface; the realtime turn is summarized into the parent topic as a collapsible block so the conversation thread is preserved.
- First use of mic / camera / screen share on each platform explicitly triggers an OS permission request (macOS / Windows / Linux), with an in-app explanation of why each is needed before the OS prompt fires; if denied, the in-app message gives a one-click path to the platform's settings panel.
- When a non-realtime context receives an audio chunk (e.g. a chat assistant configured with an audio-output model but not in realtime mode), the audio chunk renders as a play-button audio block in the message stream — reusing the existing audio chunk types.
- The model picker UI labels realtime-capable models with a clear "Supports realtime conversation" indicator; un-declared modalities on already-listed realtime models (currently the GPT-4o Realtime family) are filled in so the indicator works uniformly.
- Settings expose audio input/output device, output volume, and noise suppression (if the provider supports it); mic-mute / camera-off / screen-share-off keyboard shortcuts work from the realtime surface.
- When the provider connection drops mid-session, the surface shows "Reconnecting…" and restores mic / camera / screen state on reconnect without re-prompting permissions or re-selecting devices.

## Verification

- User configures Gemini API key, selects `gemini-2.5-flash-live` for an Assistant. Opens a new chat → "Realtime" toggle is visible at the top of the input area; click → realtime surface opens with mic indicator pulsing.
- User speaks "What's on my screen?" while screen share is off → assistant responds in audio (audible) and live text transcript (visible); response is grounded in mic input only.
- User enables screen share → OS-level screen/window picker appears; user picks a window; asks "Read me the error message in the dialog" → assistant identifies and reads the error.
- User enables camera, holds up a printed document → assistant describes its content; transcript shows both sides.
- User ends the realtime session → connection closes; the parent topic now shows a collapsible block "3-minute realtime conversation about screen content — view transcript"; clicking expands the transcript.
- User with no realtime-capable model configured → the "Realtime" toggle does not appear in the chat input area; model picker shows realtime-capable models marked with "Supports realtime conversation".
- First-ever realtime click on macOS → in-app primer ("Cherry needs microphone access to enable realtime conversation") → OS mic permission prompt; user denies → in-app message with one-click "Open System Settings > Privacy & Security > Microphone" link; clicking opens the OS panel.
- User in realtime mode mutes mic mid-conversation → mic icon shows muted; assistant pauses listening; un-mute → assistant resumes; no incoming audio is dropped during the mute window itself.
- User on a non-realtime chat with an audio-output model receives an audio reply → message stream renders a play-button audio block; clicking plays through default output with a progress indicator.
- Provider connection drops mid-session → surface shows "Reconnecting…"; on reconnect, the mic stays on (no re-permission prompt), camera/screen share resume on the previously chosen sources.

## Related

#41 (closed — original voice I/O ask, long inactive)
#13204 (closed — TTS for Selection Assistant; subset of audio output, superseded by realtime native audio)
#12928 (Grok Image Generation — sibling multimodal-output request)
#15359 (Video generation results not viewable — sibling video-output surface gap)

## Bug: Agent module suffers severe lag due to zombie MCP references in agents.db

### Environment
- CherryStudio: 19.9
- OS: Windows 11 (Dell G15 5520, 16GB RAM)
- Number of Agents: 3

### Problem Description
After opening the Agent module, severe lag/unresponsive spinning occurs, while other functions (model chat, knowledge base) work normally.
In today's logs:
- "Server not found" warnings: 3,446 times
- "Server not found while fetching info": 3,441 times
- "Failed to list MCP tools": 2,141 times
- Total approximately 9,000+ exceptions today

### Root Cause Analysis
**The `mcps` column of each Agent in agents.db stores independent MCP reference lists, which are not synchronized with the global config.json.**

Even after users delete MCP servers from "Settings → MCP", the `mcps` column in the Agent table still retains old references.
When opening the Agent module, CherryStudio enumerates all Agents and initiates connections to all `mcps`—
including long-defunct ones like `@bailian/WebSearch`, `@modelscope/firecrawl-mcp-server`, etc.,
causing a continuous retry storm that blocks the UI thread.

### Steps To Reproduce
1. Add several MCP servers in global settings
2. Assign these MCPs to Agents
3. Delete these MCPs in global settings
4. Open Agent module → observe lag
5. Check agents.db → the mcps column in the agents table still contains deleted MCPs

### Log Evidence (2026-06-02)

### Steps To Reproduce

Error types:

Error activating server 联网搜索 Streamable HTTP error (405): current mcp not support streamableHttp
Error activating server rednote-mcp MCP error -32000: Connection closed

Warning statistics:

Server not found: 3,446 times/day

Failed to list MCP tools: 2,141 times/day

### Expected Behavior


### Temporary Fix
After manually editing the agents table in agents.db and deleting invalid MCP references from the mcps column, normal operation is restored.

### Suggested Fix Direction
1. When deleting global MCPs, synchronously clean up mcps lists for all Agents
2. Do not initiate connections for MCPs marked as isActive:false
3. Add exponential backoff retry after MCP connection failure (instead of fixed-interval retry)

### Related Issues

title: Bug: When agent session list has many items, bottom sessions show rendering anomalies like disappearance, overlap, duplication
body:
> [\!NOTE]
> This issue was translated by Claude.

Environment Information
Cherry Studio Version: v1.9.9 (macOS arm64)
Platform: macOS
Version Source: version.log shows 1.9.9|mac|prod|packaged|install|2026-06-02T08:22:50.543Z

Bug Description
When the conversation list in the Agent sidebar accumulates to a certain number (visually estimated 20+), scrolling to the bottom of the list causes three types of rendering anomalies in the bottom few sessions:

- Disappearance: Session entries are completely invisible in the list and cannot be selected even when clicked
- Overlap: Two session entries render in the same position with text overlapping each other
- Duplication: The same session appears as two entries in the list (content is completely identical)

These anomalies may self-recover after switching sessions or scrolling the list, but they repeatedly appear and seriously affect the multi-session management experience.

Steps to Reproduce
1. Create 20+ sessions in Agent mode (conversing with any agent)
2. Scroll to the bottom of the session list
3. Observe the rendering state of the last 3-5 sessions
4. Try clicking bottom sessions to switch, observe if the list shows jumping/misalignment

Expected Behavior
All session entries render stably, without interference, with correct positions, and can be selected/switched normally by clicking.

Actual Behavior
Session entries near the bottom of the list render unstably, showing disappearance, overlap, or duplication, with inconsistent state after scrolling/switching.

Analysis and Speculation
From the release notes, there have been related fixes before:

- #14954 hotfix(agents): show all sessions and agents in sidebar (v1.9.5) — Fixed the issue of incomplete session display in sidebar
- #13995 hotfix(agents): paginate session messages to reduce initial paint time (v1.9.0-rc.0) — Paginated rendering of session list

But the problem still exists in v1.9.9, speculating that in the session list virtual scrolling implementation:

- Dynamic row height calculation cache is inaccurate, causing virtual window offset
- There are boundary bugs in DOM node recycling/reuse logic when list items update
- The session list key may not be a unique stable value, causing rendering confusion

Additional Information
- After turning off "topic auto-rename", the session list still has this problem (excluding the impact of renaming triggering re-rendering)
- Restarting the client can briefly relieve it, but as the number of sessions used increases, it will appear again
- The session list in non-Agent mode (normal conversation) does not seem to have this problem, only the Agent sidebar is affected

Suggested Fix Direction
- Check the overscanCount and itemCount calculation logic for Agent session list virtual scrolling
- Ensure each session entry's key uses a stable unique identifier (like session.id), not index
- Consider forcing a reset of the virtual scrolling cache when list data changes

---
<details>
<summary>Original Content</summary>

环境信息
Cherry Studio 版本：v1.9.9（macOS arm64）
平台：macOS
版本号来源：version.log 显示 1.9.9|mac|prod|packaged|install|2026-06-02T08:22:50.543Z

Bug 描述
当智能体（Agent）侧边栏的会话列表积累到一定数量后（目测 20+），滚动到列表底部时，最下面的几个会话会出现三种渲染异常：

消失：会话条目在列表中完全不可见，点击也无法选中
重叠：两个会话条目渲染在同一个位置，文字相互覆盖
复制：同一个会话在列表中显示为两条（内容完全一致）
这些异常在切换会话或滚动列表后可能自行恢复，但会反复出现，严重影响多会话管理体验。

复现步骤
在 Agent 模式下创建 20+ 个会话（与任意智能体对话即可）

尝试点击底部会话切换，观察列表是否出现跳动/错位
预期行为
所有会话条目稳定渲染，互不干扰，位置正确，点击可正常选中切换。

实际行为
靠近列表底部的会话条目渲染不稳定，出现消失、重叠或复制，滚动/切换后状态不一致。

分析与推测
从 release notes 来看，此前已有相关修复：

#14954 hotfix(agents): show all sessions and agents in sidebar（v1.9.5）— 修复了侧边栏会话显示不全的问题
#13995 hotfix(agents): paginate session messages to reduce initial paint time（v1.9.0-rc.0）— 会话列表分页渲染
但问题在 v1.9.9 上仍然存在，推测是会话列表虚拟滚动（virtual list）实现中：

动态行高（variable row height）计算缓存不准确，导致虚拟窗口偏移
列表项更新时 DOM 节点回收/复用逻辑存在边界 bug
会话列表 key 可能不是唯一稳定值，导致渲染混乱
额外信息

重启客户端可短暂缓解，但随着使用会话数量增加会再次出现
非 Agent 模式（普通对话）的会话列表似乎没有此问题，仅 Agent 侧边栏受影响
建议修复方向
检查 Agent 会话列表虚拟滚动的 overscanCount 和 itemCount 计算逻辑
确保每个会话条目的 key 使用稳定的唯一标识（如 session.id），而非索引
考虑在列表数据变更时强制重置虚拟滚动的缓存

title: [Feature]: Multi-User Identity Awareness in External IM Channel Adapters
body:
## Background

Cherry Studio's external IM channel adapters (Feishu, WeChat, Slack, Telegram, Discord, QQ) let one Cherry Agent serve many users inside an external group chat. The infrastructure for identifying speakers actually already exists — every inbound message is wrapped in a `[SECURITY NOTICE]` system block that's supposed to include the sender's name and platform ID. But the practical experience breaks down in three concrete ways:

1. The Feishu adapter ships the sender's display name as an empty string — every other adapter resolves the name via the platform's user-info API, the Feishu adapter alone does not — so the LLM sees `user "" (ID: oc_xxxx)` for every Feishu message.
2. Sessions are scoped per external chat, not per external user — when multiple users in the same Feishu group `@` the Agent, all their messages share one session with shared memory and shared context, so the Agent confuses one user's facts with another's.
3. The rapid-fire message-merging step combines messages from different senders in the same batch window and silently drops the second sender's identity.

Users reporting this describe it as "the Agent calls me by my colleague's name" and "the Agent doesn't seem to know we're different people". The bot in a Feishu group becomes unusable for any team workflow because no two people can use it without contaminating each other's experience.

## Goal

When multiple external users in an IM group chat with the same Cherry Agent, the Agent correctly knows who is speaking each turn, addresses each user individually (including `@`-mention in replies where the platform supports it), and keeps each user's memory and context isolated from others in the same group.

## Spec

- All channel adapters (Feishu, WeChat, Slack, Telegram, Discord, QQ) resolve the sender's display name from the external IM's user-info API with per-adapter caching; the resolved name flows into the existing `[SECURITY NOTICE]` system block instead of being left empty.
- The Agent session model is extended so that group-chat messages are scoped per `(external-chat, external-user)` pair instead of per `external-chat`. Each user in an external group gets their own conversational thread with the Agent, with separate context history.
- The Agent's memory (current `FACT.md` and any future memory features) is also scoped per external user inside a group — facts the Agent learns about user A never leak into responses for user B in the same group.
- The message batching / merge step that combines rapid-fire messages does so **only within the same sender's stream** — messages from different senders in the same batch window remain separate turns, each carrying the correct sender identity.
- When replying in a group chat, the Agent's response addresses the asking user explicitly: `@`-mention on platforms that support it (Slack, Discord, Telegram, Feishu, QQ guild) and a name prefix on platforms that don't (WeChat C2P).
- The system prompt sent to the Agent for each turn always includes the current speaker's name and platform-side ID in a structured, parseable section distinguishable from message content.
- Direct-message (1:1 with the bot) behavior is unchanged — no regression for the single-user case, since the per-user scoping naturally collapses to today's behavior in 1:1.
- Existing channel sessions are migrated by treating the first observed sender in the existing session as that session's legacy owner; subsequent new users from the same external chat get fresh per-user sessions.
- When the same external user is later promoted from a 1:1 DM into a group (or vice versa), prior memory does not silently follow them across that boundary — group-user memory and DM memory are separate scopes.

## Verification

- In a Feishu group with users A, B, and C all `@`-mentioning the same Cherry Agent: each receives replies addressed to them by their actual Feishu display name, each reply `@`-mentions the asker. (Today: replies have no `@`, address everyone as generic "you" with empty sender name in the system prompt.)
- User A tells the Agent "remember that I'm a data scientist". A week later in the same group, user B asks "what do you remember about me?" → the Agent responds with B's known facts only (which may be none), not A's. (Today: B sees A's profile leaked into B's reply.)
- Three users in a Feishu group post messages within a 5-second window → each becomes its own turn in the Agent's context with the correct user identity attached, not merged into one. (Today: the second/third users' identities are silently dropped during merge.)
- The same Agent in a 1:1 Feishu DM with user A behaves identically to today's 1:1 — same response style, same memory recall, no regression.
- A new user X joins a Feishu group where the Agent has been running for months → user X's first message starts a fresh per-user session with no contamination from prior users' histories or memory.
- The system prompt for any turn in a group chat contains a clearly structured speaker section like `Current speaker: Alice Wang (ID: ou_abc123, platform: feishu)` — the LLM can quote it verbatim in tracing or debug output.
- Slack, Telegram, Discord, QQ, WeChat all produce the same correctness as Feishu when run through the same multi-user scenarios — the fix lifts the floor for every channel, not just Feishu.
- A user moves the bot from a 1:1 DM into a group (Feishu allows this) → the group-session memory is fresh; the prior 1:1 memory does not silently follow them into the group.

## Related

#15169 (WeCom + DingTalk Channel Adapters — sibling channel work)
#15376 (Agent IM Collaboration — Cherry-native collab via SMTP, parallel surface, different transport)
#14910 (PII Redaction via Local Models — adjacent "channel metadata into Agent" surface)

title: [Feature]: Merge Mode for Backup/Restore Independent of Account Sync
body:
## Background

Cherry Studio's current backup/restore mechanism (Local zip / WebDAV / S3) wipes the target before writing — restoring on Device B replaces everything on Device B with the contents of the backup. Users who work across multiple devices and use WebDAV or S3 to keep them in sync see non-trivial work on one device vaporized whenever the other device's auto-backup arrives. This has been raised twice (#1793, #10835) and closed both times without implementation. The recent `BackupManager` → `LegacyBackupManager` rename signals that this code path is being replaced in V2 — the right moment to bake merge semantics into the replacement rather than carry overwrite-only behavior forward. Account-based sync (#14898) addresses merge for users who adopt Cherry's account, but a large segment — self-hosted, privacy-first, offline-first, "I just want a zip I control" — will continue to rely on backup/restore and deserves the same data-loss protection.

## Goal

Backup/restore offers an opt-in **Merge mode** that reconciles a backup's contents with the target device's existing data instead of overwriting it — driven by per-record timestamps where available, with explicit, user-visible strategies for record types that lack timestamps.

## Spec

- Restore (Local zip / WebDAV / S3) exposes a new top-level mode selector: **Overwrite (current default)** and **Merge (new, opt-in per restore action)**.
- In Merge mode, restore is per-record, not per-directory: each record from the backup is reconciled with the corresponding record on the target device by ID.
- **For record types with `updatedAt`** (Topic, Message, MessageBlock, KnowledgeNote): same-ID records on both sides resolve to the side with the more recent `updatedAt`; one-sided records (present only in backup or only on target) are kept.
- **For record types without timestamps** (Settings, QuickPhrase, provider config / API keys), a per-type default strategy applies, surfaced in the preview screen:
  - Settings: **target wins** by default (don't let an older backup overwrite the user's current settings)
  - QuickPhrase: **union** by default (keep both sides' entries)
  - Provider config / API keys: **target wins** by default (don't restore stale credentials)
- A pre-restore preview shows the planned outcome: net-new records to add, conflicting records and which side currently wins, records on target not in backup, records on backup not on target — counts per category with examples viewable. The user can override per-category strategy before confirming.
- Merge runs are transactional via the existing `*.restore` atomic-swap staging mechanism — either all reconciled changes apply or none; on failure the target's pre-restore state is preserved byte-for-byte.
- The same merge logic is exposed to WebDAV / S3 auto-backup cycles as an opt-in: when enabled, auto-restore cycles merge instead of overwriting, letting two devices sharing a WebDAV/S3 path converge to the union of their data over time.
- The existing Overwrite mode is unchanged — selecting Overwrite restores byte-for-byte equivalence with the backup, no preview UI, no behavioral regression.
- The conflict resolution algorithm (per-record timestamp comparison + per-type strategy) is **shared** with #14898's account-sync conflict resolution so the two paths converge on identical semantics.
- This work targets the V2 backup replacement (the code superseding `LegacyBackupManager`), not the legacy implementation. Any backporting to v1.9.x for hotfix relief is explicitly out of scope.

## Verification

- Device A has 50 topics, Device B has 30 topics, with 20 shared by ID. User restores Device A's backup to Device B in Merge mode → Device B ends with 60 unique topics (30 own kept + 30 new from A; the 20 shared are reconciled per `updatedAt`).
- A specific shared topic was edited on Device B after Device A's backup was taken. Merge restore → Device B keeps its newer version (target wins by `updatedAt`).
- A specific shared topic was edited on Device A after Device B's last sync and not touched on B. Merge restore → Device B receives A's newer version.
- Pre-restore preview shows e.g. "47 new topics to add, 3 conflicting topics (2 backup wins, 1 target wins), 5 differing settings keys (target wins — override?), 0 records will be deleted". User confirms → restore proceeds with exactly that outcome.
- User changes the settings strategy in the preview from "target wins" to "backup wins", confirms → settings come from the backup; topics still follow timestamp resolution.
- Restore fails midway (e.g. WebDAV connection drops at 60% progress) → target's pre-restore state is intact byte-for-byte; no partial merge applied.
- User selects Overwrite mode for the same restore → no preview UI appears; behavior is exactly today's overwrite restore.
- WebDAV auto-backup mode with "auto-merge on auto-restore" enabled: Devices A and B both auto-back-up to the same WebDAV path; over a week of normal use across both devices, neither device experiences silent data loss; both converge to the union of their data with timestamp-based reconciliation on conflicts.
- QuickPhrase reconciliation: Device A has 5 phrases, Device B has 4 different phrases. Merge → Device B ends with 9 phrases (union); the preview's QuickPhrase row showed "5 phrases will be added (union)".
- Provider config reconciliation: target device has API key X for provider P; backup has older API key Y for provider P. Merge with default strategy → target keeps X; preview clearly showed "API key for provider P: target wins".

## Related

- #14898 (Account System — merge for account-sync path; this issue provides parallel merge for backup/restore; both should share the conflict resolution algorithm)
- #10835 (closed 2025-11 — earlier WebDAV merge ask, never implemented; this issue's V2-aware redesign supersedes it)
- #1793 (closed — multi-device WebDAV overwriting; same root pain)
- #15476 (open — backup omits `.claude/projects/`; adjacent backup-completeness gap)
- #15423 (open CRITICAL — IndexedDB wipe; adjacent data-loss class)
- #15112 (open — v2 file module refactor; this issue's V2 backup replacement likely interacts)

title: [Feature]: Starter Cards Carousel on Empty Chat & Agent Sessions (Click to Pre-fill Prompt)
body:
## Background

Users hit a cold-start wall every time they open a new empty session in Cherry Studio: they know it's powerful but don't know what to ask first, and don't know how to phrase a high-quality prompt. Workshop observation showed users staring at the empty input box, typing one-liners that produce weak output, and concluding "I don't know what this tool is for". The pain is general — it applies to both the regular Chat surface and the Agent surface, on every new session, not just first launch.

## Goal

On any empty Chat or Agent session, the user can pick from a small set of example task cards; clicking one pre-fills a complete, well-structured prompt into the input box, which the user can review, lightly edit, and send in one click.

## Spec

- Whenever a Chat or Agent session is empty (zero messages sent), a **starter-card carousel** is shown below the input box on both surfaces.
- The carousel shows **3 cards at a time across 3 pages (9 cards total)**, with **3 page-indicator dots** centered below the cards. Cards advance via (a) automatic rotation at a steady cadence, (b) clicking a dot to jump to that page, or (c) swiping / dragging horizontally.
- **Auto-rotation pauses while the cursor is hovering anywhere over the carousel**, and resumes when the cursor leaves.
- Each card shows an icon, a short title (one task name), and a one-line description of what the task produces.
- Clicking a card **pre-fills** the input box with a complete, multi-line structured prompt — it does NOT auto-send. The user reviews the prompt, may edit it, then sends manually.
- A **"Shuffle" button** sits next to the carousel; clicking it refreshes the 9 visible cards to a different curated set from the underlying catalog and resets the carousel to page 1.
- The default 9 cards per surface appear in a **fixed, curated order** (deterministic — the same fresh session shows the same 9 in the same order) until the user clicks Shuffle.
- Once the session has at least one user message, the carousel is hidden for that session (it does not flash back when the user clears input mid-conversation).
- The Chat and Agent surfaces each have **their own catalog** of starter cards, curated separately — Chat cards lean toward quick Q&A / writing / lookup tasks, Agent cards lean toward multi-step tool-using tasks. Catalogs ship with the app and are fully localized for every supported UI language.
- Each card represents a task that produces a **concrete artifact** (a summary, a document, a slide deck, a script, a comparison table — not an open-ended Q&A like "what is X?"). The pre-filled prompt is **self-contained and structured**: it states the objective, the inputs, the constraints, and the desired output format, so the user can send it as-is and get a useful result on the first try.

## Verification

- Open a brand-new Chat session → input box is empty; below it the carousel shows 3 cards with 3 dots centered underneath; first dot is active.
- Wait a few seconds without touching anything → cards auto-advance to page 2, second dot becomes active. Hover the mouse over any of the visible cards → auto-rotation stops; move the mouse away → it resumes.
- Click the third dot → cards jump to page 3 (the last 3 cards of the 9). Swipe / drag the cards horizontally → flips to the adjacent page.
- Click the "GitHub AI Trending Roundup" card on Chat → the input box is populated with a full multi-line prompt (e.g. lines for "fetch time window", "fields to extract", "output format"). No message has been sent yet.
- User edits one line of the pre-filled prompt and clicks send → the *edited* prompt is sent (not the original card prompt).
- Click "Shuffle" → the 9 cards refresh to a different set, the carousel resets to page 1, and the first dot becomes active again.
- Open the same fresh session twice without clicking Shuffle → both times show the same 9 cards in the same order on page 1 (deterministic default).
- After the first user message goes out, the carousel disappears and stays hidden; deleting all input text mid-conversation does NOT bring it back.
- Open a brand-new Agent session → same carousel layout (3 cards / 3 dots / Shuffle button / auto-rotate / hover-pause / click-to-fill), but the **9 cards are a different catalog** than Chat — visibly tilted toward multi-step / tool-using tasks. Sending dispatches to the current Agent, not the Chat assistant.
- Switch app language from Chinese to English → card titles, descriptions, the pre-filled prompt text, and the Shuffle button label are all in English.
- On a session that already has messages, navigate away and back → carousel remains hidden (state is per-session, not per-app-launch).

## Related

title: [Feature]: Interactive In-Message Annotations on Agent HTML & Markdown Artifacts
body:
## Background

When an Agent produces an HTML report or a long Markdown document in a session, today the only way for a user to refine it is to type free-form feedback into the next message ("the third paragraph is wrong, and the chart on the right uses the wrong color"). The Agent has to guess which paragraph, which chart. Users either give up, or re-prompt from scratch and lose a v1 they were 90% happy with.

## Goal

In the current session, users can annotate specific regions of the most recent HTML or Markdown artifact in an Agent reply, then send those annotations to the Agent as one precisely-anchored revision request that produces a new reply.

## Spec

- Markdown artifacts in an Agent message support text-selection annotations: the user highlights a span of rendered text, opens a comment, and the comment is anchored to that span.
- HTML artifacts in an Agent message support both text-selection annotations and element-pointer annotations: the user can highlight rendered text, or click a discrete visual element (e.g. a chart bar, a card, an image) to pin a comment to that element.
- Each annotation is a single comment attached to one anchor; the artifact view shows all pending annotations as highlights/markers on the artifact with a side panel listing them.
- Submission is user-driven with two modes: a default batch mode (multiple annotations accumulate; the user clicks "Send to Agent" to dispatch the whole batch as one revision request) and a per-annotation "Send now" action that immediately dispatches just that annotation.
- Sending a batch posts a structured user message to the session that carries each annotation as (anchor description + anchored excerpt + user comment); pending annotations are cleared from the artifact on send.
- The Agent's response is a normal next message in the session; if it contains a new HTML or MD artifact, that new artifact becomes annotatable in the same way. Prior artifacts in scrollback are read-only — no new annotations can be added to a superseded artifact.
- Annotations are session-local and ephemeral: they live only until sent (or discarded), are not persisted across app restarts, and are not visible to anyone else.

## Verification

- In an Agent reply containing a Markdown weekly report, highlight the phrase "Q3 revenue grew 12%", add comment "should be 15%", click "Send to Agent" → a new user message appears in the session carrying the annotation; the Agent's next reply produces a corrected report.
- In an Agent reply containing an HTML dashboard, click a specific chart bar, add comment "this bar should use brand primary, not gray" → the annotation marker stays pinned to that bar while the user scrolls within the artifact view or resizes the side panel.
- On the same Markdown artifact, add three annotations on three different paragraphs, click "Send to Agent" once → all three are bundled into a single user message; the Agent's resulting reply addresses all three.
- On a single annotation, click "Send now" → only that annotation is dispatched; any other pending annotations remain visible on the artifact for later sending.
- After a successful send, the just-sent annotations are cleared from the artifact view (markers gone, side panel empty for that batch).
- Scroll up to a prior Agent reply (now superseded): the older artifact is read-only — selecting text or clicking elements does not offer the annotation affordance.
- Attempt to click "Send to Agent" with zero pending annotations → the action is disabled with a tooltip explaining why.
- Attempt to save a comment with empty text → the save action is disabled until text is entered.
- Discard a pending annotation → the marker disappears from the artifact and from the side panel; no message is sent.
- Close and reopen the app while annotations are pending → the pending annotations are gone (ephemeral, as specified); the underlying Agent reply is unchanged.
- An HTML artifact that fetches live data from an external API still accepts element-pointer annotations on rendered elements; the dispatched message describes the element by a stable descriptor (e.g. tag + text/index path) so the Agent can identify it unambiguously in source.

## Related

#15279 #15398

title: [Feature]: Sanitize Identifiers and Names for AWS Bedrock-Backed Providers
body:
## Background

When using AWS Bedrock-backed Claude models — directly or routed through an aggregator like CherryIN — requests fail with a hard `400 aws_invoke_error` mid-stream because Cherry Studio sends identifiers and names that violate Bedrock's strict validation rules. Tool calls break when a `tool_use.id` contains characters outside `^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+$` (e.g. `.` or `:`); file uploads break when a `document.name` contains dots or consecutive spaces. The same requests succeed against Anthropic's direct API, so the failure is provider-specific, and the response stream is cut off with a raw error users cannot act on.

User-reported evidence (tool call via a Bedrock-backed Claude model failing on `content.3.tool_use.id`):

![Bedrock tool_use.id 400 validation error](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kennyzheng-builds/cherry-issue-assets/main/bedrock-tooluse-id-400.jpg)

## Goal

Users can use tool calls, file uploads, and other Bedrock-backed provider features without hitting 400 validation errors caused by characters Cherry Studio places in identifiers or names.

## Spec

- When sending requests to any Bedrock-backed provider, Cherry Studio normalizes all identifiers and names subject to Bedrock's character constraints so the request is accepted.
- Tool calls succeed regardless of the characters in the originally generated `tool_use.id`.
- File uploads succeed regardless of dots, consecutive spaces, or other invalid characters in the file name.
- Normalization affects only the value sent over the wire; the user-facing original (e.g. displayed filename) is preserved unchanged.
- The behavior covers both direct AWS Bedrock providers and aggregators that route to Bedrock (e.g. CherryIN).
- If a value genuinely cannot be made valid, the user sees a clear, actionable message instead of a raw `aws_invoke_error`.

## Verification

- Select a Bedrock-backed Claude model (e.g. `anthropic/claude-opus-4.x` via CherryIN) and trigger a tool call → conversation completes, no `content.N.tool_use.id: String should match pattern '^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+$'` error, stream not interrupted.
- Upload a PDF named `my.report.v2.pdf` (dots) or `11.pdf` to a Bedrock Claude model → upload succeeds, and the chat still displays the original filename `my.report.v2.pdf` to the user.
- Upload a file named `final  draft.pdf` (consecutive spaces) → succeeds.
- A single turn with 3+ tool_use blocks → none of them trigger the id-pattern 400.
- The same tool call against an Anthropic-direct provider behaves unchanged (no regression).
- The previously failing flows in #14845 (part 3) and #13022 both succeed after the change.

## Related

#14845 #13022 #14021

title: [Feature]: Make Agents Aware of Cherry Studio Capabilities — Including How to Connect IM Channels
body:
## Background

Agents created in Cherry Studio have no knowledge of the Cherry Studio client they run inside. When a user asks their agent to help with something Cherry Studio actually supports — e.g. "I want to talk to you on WeChat, how do I bind it?" — the agent doesn't know Cherry Studio offers channel binding (WeChat, Feishu, Telegram, QQ, Discord, Slack) and gives a generic or wrong answer. In one real case the agent told the user to look at Claude's own desktop app / web / CLI instead. Users can't get their agent to help them operate the very app it lives in.

## Goal

An agent running in Cherry Studio can answer "how do I do X in Cherry Studio?" and guide the user to the right place to configure it.

## Spec

- Agents have access to current knowledge of Cherry Studio's user-facing capabilities and where to configure them (channel binding such as WeChat/Feishu, model providers, knowledge base, settings), enabling them to answer "how do I …" questions about the app.
- When a user's question maps to an existing Cherry Studio feature, the agent explains the steps within Cherry Studio rather than describing unrelated or other-vendor products.
- This applies to user-created custom agents, not only the built-in assistant.
- The knowledge reflects the installed version's actual features — it does not invent steps for capabilities Cherry Studio lacks, nor reference removed ones.
- The guidance surfaces only when relevant, without injecting app-configuration text into normal task responses.

## Verification

- In an agent chat, ask "我想在微信上跟你交流，怎么绑定" → the agent explains Cherry Studio's WeChat channel-binding flow and where to find it, and does not point the user to Claude's own products.
- Ask "how do I add a new model provider?" → the agent directs the user to provider settings inside Cherry Studio.
- Ask about a capability Cherry Studio does not have → the agent states it's unavailable in Cherry Studio instead of inventing steps.
- A user-created custom agent (e.g. one running glm-5.1, not the built-in CherryClaw) answers the WeChat-binding question correctly.
- A normal task request unrelated to app config (e.g. "summarize this file") gets no injected Cherry Studio configuration text.

## Related

None (sourced from internal user feedback).

title: [Feature]: Quick Assistant Web Search Toggle
body:
## Background

Many users rely on Quick Assistant for fast, contextual queries without leaving their current workflow. However, Quick Assistant currently lacks web search capability, which means time-sensitive questions (e.g., latest news, real-time data, current events) cannot be answered accurately. Users must switch to the main chat window just to toggle web search on, breaking the lightweight, quick-access experience.

## Goal

Enable web search directly within the Quick Assistant interface so users can get up-to-date answers without switching to the main chat window.

## Spec

- Add a web search toggle button to the Quick Assistant input area, visually consistent with the existing toggle in the main chat window.
- When web search is enabled, display a search engine selector menu allowing users to choose from the same engines available in the main chat.
- The selected search engine preference should persist across Quick Assistant sessions.
- Web search state in Quick Assistant should be independent of the main chat window's web search state.
- Search results should be cited inline in the assistant's response, matching the main chat behavior.

## Verification

- Enable web search in Quick Assistant, ask a time-sensitive question (e.g., "What happened in tech news today?"), and verify the response includes recent, cited web results.
- Change the search engine in Quick Assistant, perform a search, and confirm the selected engine is used.
- Close and reopen Quick Assistant; verify the previously selected search engine persists.
- Confirm that toggling web search in Quick Assistant does not affect the main chat window's web search state, and vice versa.

title: [Feature]: Quick Assistant Inline Assistant Picker

## Background

Currently, users can only assign an assistant to Quick Assistant through the Settings page. This means every time a user wants to switch to a different assistant for a different type of query, they must navigate away from their current context into Settings, find the Quick Assistant option, change it, and return. This friction discourages users from leveraging multiple assistants and undermines the "quick" promise of the feature.

## Goal

Allow users to pick or switch assistants directly from the Quick Assistant interface without navigating to Settings.

## Spec

- Add an assistant indicator/selector in the Quick Assistant header or input area showing the currently active assistant.
- Clicking the indicator opens an inline picker listing available assistants, with search/filter support.
- Selecting a new assistant switches the Quick Assistant's active assistant immediately; the current conversation context resets.
- The last-used assistant should be remembered and restored the next time Quick Assistant is opened.

- The existing Settings path for choosing a Quick Assistant default remains available as a fallback.

## Verification

- Click the assistant indicator and verify a picker appears with the list of available assistants.

title: [Feature]: Quick Assistant and Word Lookup Zoom Support

While the main application window supports zoom/scaling, these auxiliary panels do not respond to zoom adjustments, forcing users to squint at small text. This is especially painful for the Word Lookup Assistant, where users are trying to quickly parse definitions and translations.

## Goal

Make the Quick Assistant and Word Lookup Assistant response panels respect the application's zoom level, so text scales consistently across all interfaces.
