title: [Feature]: Non-Interruptive Interaction During Agent Runtime
body:
## Background

When an Agent is running in Cherry Studio, the input box is locked — users can only wait or abort the entire task. There is no way to ask a quick side question, queue a follow-up, or inject context into the current run. This forces users to interrupt expensive long-running tasks just to ask something small, or lose their thought while waiting. Claude Code's `/btw` and Codex's Steer demonstrate that lightweight mid-run interaction is both feasible and highly valued.

## Goal

Enable three non-interruptive interaction modes so users can communicate with the assistant during Agent execution without aborting the current task.

## Spec

- **/btw Side Query**: While an Agent task is running, the user can type `/btw <question>` to fork the current context into a single-turn side query. The response displays inline (e.g., a collapsible card) and is **not** written into the main conversation history.
- **Ctrl+S Queue Injection**: The user can press Ctrl+S to compose a follow-up message that is queued and automatically sent once the current Agent task completes, preserving task ordering without manual timing.
- **Ctrl+Shift+S Immediate Injection**: The user can press Ctrl+Shift+S to inject a message directly into the current turn's context, making it visible to the Agent on its next tool-call cycle within the same run.
- The input box must remain accessible (unlocked or with a secondary input area) whenever an Agent task is in progress.
- Each interaction mode should have a clear visual indicator showing its type (side query, queued, injected) so the user can distinguish them from normal messages.
- This feature complements the existing message-level side-query capability in PR #13975; the two should coexist without conflict.

## Verification

- Start a long-running Agent task, type `/btw What is 2+2?`, and confirm the answer appears inline without interrupting the running task or appearing in main history.
- During an Agent run, press Ctrl+S and compose a message; verify it is held until the current task finishes, then automatically sent.
- During an Agent run, press Ctrl+Shift+S and inject context (e.g., "also check file X"); verify the Agent references that injected context in its very next tool call.
- Confirm that after using all three modes during a single Agent run, the main conversation history only contains the original task and the queued follow-up — not the `/btw` side query or the injected context.
- Verify keyboard shortcuts do not conflict with existing shortcuts and work on both macOS and Windows.

## Related

- #15452
- #13975

title: [Feature]: Intel GPU Detection for OVMS
body:
## Background

Cherry Studio currently determines OVMS (OpenVINO Model Server) compatibility by checking whether the CPU name contains "Intel." This means users with an AMD CPU paired with an Intel discrete GPU (e.g., Intel Arc B580) are incorrectly blocked from using OVMS, even though their Intel GPU is fully capable of running OpenVINO workloads. As Intel Arc GPUs become more popular as affordable AI accelerators, this false negative increasingly frustrates users who have the right hardware but are told they cannot use it.

## Goal

Expand OVMS support detection on Windows to recognize Intel GPUs in addition to Intel CPUs, enabling OVMS for any system that has at least one qualifying Intel component.

## Spec

- On Windows, the OVMS compatibility check should pass if **either** an Intel CPU **or** an Intel GPU is detected in the system.
- Intel GPU detection should query the OS-level GPU/display adapter information (e.g., via system APIs or standard utilities) rather than relying solely on the CPU brand string.
- On macOS and Linux, retain existing behavior (Intel CPU check only) unless OpenVINO officially supports Intel discrete GPUs on those platforms.
- When OVMS is enabled via GPU detection (but the CPU is non-Intel), surface a brief note in the UI indicating that OVMS is running on the Intel GPU.
- If neither an Intel CPU nor an Intel GPU is found, the existing "not compatible" message should remain unchanged.

## Verification

- On a system with an AMD CPU + Intel Arc GPU (e.g., Arc B580), confirm OVMS is offered and functional.
- On a system with an Intel CPU + non-Intel GPU, confirm OVMS detection still works as before.
- On a system with an AMD CPU + AMD/NVIDIA GPU (no Intel components), confirm OVMS remains unavailable with the existing incompatibility message.
- Verify the UI note about GPU-based OVMS appears only when OVMS eligibility comes from the GPU (not the CPU).

## Related

- #15415

title: [Feature]: Batch Delete Multiple Messages
body:
## Background

Users engaged in long-running emotional or roleplay conversations accumulate context exceeding 1M tokens, causing per-turn costs to climb continuously. When they want to trim old history to reduce costs, they face a dilemma: starting a new conversation loses character continuity and relationship context, relying on global memory alone cannot preserve nuanced persona state, and the current UI only allows deleting one message at a time — making it impractical to remove hundreds of old messages. Users need a fast way to bulk-remove historical messages while keeping recent context intact.

## Goal

Allow users to select and delete multiple messages at once so they can efficiently prune conversation history without losing recent context or character continuity.

## Spec

- Add a "Select" or "Manage" mode to the conversation view that lets users check multiple messages via checkboxes or a range selection (e.g., shift-click for contiguous ranges).
- Provide a "Delete Selected" action that removes all checked messages in a single operation with a confirmation prompt showing the count.
- Support a "Delete messages before this point" shortcut: right-click a message and choose "Delete all above" to quickly remove everything older than a chosen boundary.
- After bulk deletion, the remaining messages should retain their original order, timestamps, and role attributions; the conversation should continue to function normally.
- Display the updated token count (if shown in the UI) immediately after deletion so users can confirm the cost reduction.
- Optionally offer an "Archive" alternative that moves deleted messages to a read-only archive rather than permanently destroying them, giving users a safety net.

## Verification

- In a conversation with 200+ messages, enter Select mode, check 50 non-contiguous messages, press "Delete Selected," confirm the prompt, and verify all 50 are removed while the rest remain intact.
- Right-click a message in the middle of a long conversation, choose "Delete all above," confirm, and verify all preceding messages are removed.
- After bulk-deleting old messages, send a new message and confirm the conversation continues normally with correct context.
- Verify that the token/context counter updates to reflect the reduced history after deletion.
- Attempt bulk deletion with zero messages selected and confirm the action is disabled or shows an appropriate warning.

## Related

- #15590

title: [Feature]: DeepSeek Native Web Search Support
body:
## Background

DeepSeek's API natively supports web search — when the model determines a query benefits from real-time information, it can invoke DeepSeek's built-in retrieval endpoint. However, Cherry Studio does not yet surface this capability in its native search provider list, forcing users who rely on DeepSeek to fall back on third-party search integrations or lose access to grounded, up-to-date answers entirely.

## Goal

Enable DeepSeek's native web search as a first-class search provider in Cherry Studio so that users on DeepSeek models get real-time, grounded answers without extra configuration.

## Spec

- Add "DeepSeek Web Search" to the native search provider list alongside existing providers (e.g., Google, Tavily).
- When a user selects DeepSeek Web Search, the search request is routed through DeepSeek's own retrieval API rather than a third-party service.
- The feature should be available in both Agent mode and standard Chat mode.
- Search results (citations / source links) returned by DeepSeek should be rendered inline in the assistant's response, consistent with how other native search providers display sources.
- If the user's configured DeepSeek API key does not support web search (e.g., incompatible plan), show a clear, actionable error message.
- The provider should respect the existing "enable/disable web search" toggle — no new UI surfaces required beyond the provider picker.

## Verification

- Configure a DeepSeek API key, select "DeepSeek Web Search" as the search provider, and ask a question about today's news — the response should contain up-to-date information with source citations.
- In Agent mode, trigger a task that requires real-time data (e.g., "What is the current weather in Tokyo?") — the agent should invoke DeepSeek web search and return grounded results.
- Switch the search provider away from DeepSeek and confirm that DeepSeek's web search is no longer invoked.
- Use a DeepSeek API key that does not support web search — verify the error message is clear and tells the user what to do.
- Toggle web search off globally — confirm DeepSeek web search is not triggered even when selected as the provider.

## Related

- #15579

title: [Feature]: Cross-Session Goal Tracking for Agents
body:
## Background

Today, when a user assigns a multi-step or long-running objective to a Cherry Studio Agent, there is no persistent record of what the goal was, how far it progressed, or what remains. If the session ends — whether intentionally or due to a crash — all context is lost and the user must re-explain the objective from scratch. Competing tools (e.g., Codex CLI's Goals feature) already offer cross-session goal tracking with independent storage and progress visibility, setting a new baseline expectation for agentic workflows.

## Goal

Introduce a Goal tracking system that lets users define explicit objectives for Agents, persist progress across sessions, and provide visibility into goal status at any time.

## Spec

- Users can create a Goal from within an Agent conversation — a Goal has a title, optional description, and a status (e.g., Not Started, In Progress, Completed, Paused).
- Goals persist independently of chat sessions; reopening Cherry Studio or starting a new conversation with the same Agent shows existing Goals and their current status.
- The Agent can update Goal progress automatically as it completes sub-tasks, and users can also manually update status or add notes.
- A dedicated Goal panel (sidebar or tab) lists all Goals across Agents, filterable by status and Agent.
- When resuming a conversation, the Agent is aware of outstanding Goals and can proactively continue work or ask for direction.
- Deleting or archiving a Goal does not delete the associated conversation history.

## Verification

- Create a Goal "Refactor auth module" for an Agent, close Cherry Studio, reopen it, and confirm the Goal appears with its original status.
- Start a new session with the same Agent — verify the Agent references the outstanding Goal and offers to continue.
- Manually update a Goal's status from "In Progress" to "Paused" — confirm the change is reflected in the Goal panel and the Agent acknowledges the pause in the next interaction.
- Open the Goal panel and filter by "Completed" — only completed Goals should appear.
- Delete a Goal and verify the related conversation history is still accessible.

## Related

- Competitive reference: Codex CLI v0.133.0 Goals feature

title: [Feature]: Unified @ Mentions Search Picker
body:
## Background

Cherry Studio's input box currently lacks a unified way to reference contextual resources while composing a message. Users who want to attach a file, pull from a knowledge base, invoke a plugin, or select a skill must navigate separate menus or remember different workflows for each resource type. Competing tools (e.g., Codex CLI) offer a single `@` mention picker that searches across files, directories, plugins, and skills in one unified interface, significantly reducing friction.

## Goal

Provide a single `@` mention picker in the chat input that lets users search and select files, knowledge bases, plugins, skills, and other contextual resources from one unified interface.

## Spec

- Typing `@` in the chat input opens a search picker overlay that indexes all available resource types: files/directories, knowledge bases, plugins, skills, and Agents.
- The picker supports fuzzy search — results are ranked by relevance and grouped by resource type with clear visual labels.
- Selecting a resource inserts a styled mention token into the input; the token is resolved at send time to attach the appropriate context to the message.
- The picker is keyboard-navigable (arrow keys to browse, Enter to select, Escape to dismiss) and also supports mouse/touch interaction.
- Resource types displayed in the picker are contextual — e.g., if no knowledge bases are configured, that category is hidden rather than showing an empty group.
- Multiple `@` mentions can be chained in a single message (e.g., `@report.pdf @summarizer-skill please summarize this`).

## Verification

- Type `@` in the chat input — confirm the picker appears and shows resources from at least two different categories (e.g., files and skills).
- Search for a file name using partial/fuzzy text — confirm the file appears in results and can be selected.
- Select a knowledge base via the picker, send a question, and verify the knowledge base context is included in the request.
- Use keyboard only (no mouse) to open the picker, navigate to a skill, select it, and send the message — confirm the entire flow works.
- Type two `@` mentions in one message — confirm both resources are correctly attached when the message is sent.

## Related

- Competitive reference: Codex CLI unified `@` search picker

title: [Feature]: Goal Mode — Long-Running Autonomous Agent Execution
body:
## Background

Current Cherry Studio agents operate in a single-turn, single-task paradigm — the user sends a prompt, the agent responds, and the interaction ends. For complex, multi-step objectives (e.g., "research competitors and produce a weekly summary," "monitor a data pipeline and fix issues as they arise"), users must manually break goals into sub-tasks and re-prompt repeatedly. Codex shipped Goal Mode (graduated May 2026) covering app/IDE/CLI, enabling agents to autonomously pursue a goal over hours or days with pause/resume/clear lifecycle controls. Cherry Studio lacks this long-running, goal-driven execution model.

## Goal

Enable users to assign a high-level goal to an agent that autonomously plans, executes, and iterates over an extended period — with full lifecycle control and persistent state across restarts.

## Spec

- Users can create a **Goal** by providing a natural-language objective; the agent decomposes it into a plan and begins autonomous execution.
- Goals support **pause / resume / clear** actions from the UI at any time; pausing preserves all intermediate state.
- Goal state is **persisted locally** so that goals survive app restarts and can be resumed without loss of progress.
- The agent surfaces a **live progress timeline** showing completed steps, current step, and remaining plan — updated in real time.
- Users receive **configurable notifications** (in-app or system) when a goal completes, encounters a blocker, or requires human input.
- A **goal history** view lists past and active goals with status, duration, and outcome summary.

## Verification

1. Create a goal "Summarize the top 5 Hacker News stories every 2 hours for 12 hours." Confirm the agent begins execution, produces at least 6 summaries, and the progress timeline updates after each cycle.
2. Pause an in-progress goal, quit and relaunch Cherry Studio, then resume. Verify the agent continues from where it left off without repeating completed steps.
3. Clear an active goal and confirm all intermediate artifacts are archived and the agent stops execution immediately.
4. Assign a goal that requires human clarification mid-way. Verify the agent pauses, sends a notification requesting input, and resumes after the user responds.
5. Open the goal history view and confirm it accurately shows status, elapsed time, and outcome for at least 3 completed/cleared goals.

## Related

- Community interest in autonomous agent capabilities and multi-step task execution.

title: [Feature]: AppShots — Global Hotkey to Capture Foreground App as Context
body:
## Background

When users want to ask the AI about something on their screen — an error dialog, a chart, a UI layout — they must manually screenshot, switch to Cherry Studio, paste the image, and describe the context. This multi-step friction discourages spontaneous "what am I looking at?" interactions and breaks flow. Codex shipped Appshots (macOS, May 2026) with a single global hotkey that captures the foreground app's window screenshot plus any readable text, sending it directly to the AI as context. This is a high-impact, low-effort UX improvement for a desktop client.

## Goal

Let users press a single global hotkey to capture the foreground application's window (screenshot + extracted text) and send it to the AI as conversation context — zero manual copy/paste required.

## Spec

- A **configurable global hotkey** (default: `⌘ + Shift + S` on macOS, `Ctrl + Shift + S` on Windows) captures the currently focused application window.
- The capture includes both a **screenshot image** and **extracted readable text** (via OS accessibility/OCR) bundled as a single context attachment.
- The captured context is **inserted into the active conversation** (or starts a new one if none is active) with a system label indicating the source app name and timestamp.
- Users can **preview and optionally discard** the capture via a brief toast/overlay before it is sent, to avoid accidental captures of sensitive content.
- A **privacy safelist/blocklist** in settings lets users exclude specific apps (e.g., password managers, banking apps) from ever being captured.
- The feature works when Cherry Studio is **running in the background** (minimized or in the system tray); the hotkey activates globally.

## Verification

1. With Cherry Studio minimized, open a browser showing an error page. Press the global hotkey. Verify Cherry Studio activates, a new message appears containing both the screenshot and the extracted error text.
2. Configure a blocklisted app (e.g., 1Password). Focus 1Password and press the hotkey. Verify the capture is blocked and a brief notification explains why.
3. Press the hotkey, see the preview toast, and click "Discard." Confirm nothing is sent to the conversation.
4. Change the hotkey in settings to a custom combination. Verify the old hotkey stops working and the new one captures correctly.
5. Capture a window containing both images and text (e.g., a Figma design with labels). Confirm the extracted text includes the visible labels and the screenshot is legible.

## Related

- Community requests for faster image/context input workflows.

title: [Feature]: Computer Use — Desktop Application Automation via Agent
body:
## Background

Users frequently need AI assistance with tasks that span multiple desktop applications — filling forms, testing workflows across apps, extracting data from legacy software with no API. Today, Cherry Studio can only interact via text and files; it cannot see, click, or type into other applications. Users must manually perform every step and relay results back to the AI. Codex shipped Computer Use (Mac/Windows, May–June 2026) with full desktop automation, screen-locked remote operation, short-lived authorization, screen masking, and instant revocation via local input. This is a medium-term, high-investment capability that would unlock a new class of agent-driven workflows.

## Goal

Enable the agent to observe and control desktop applications — viewing the screen, clicking, scrolling, and typing — so it can autonomously perform multi-app tasks on the user's behalf, within clear security boundaries.

## Spec

- The agent can **capture the current screen state** (screenshot + UI element tree where available) and **perform mouse and keyboard actions** (click, double-click, scroll, type, key combos) on any visible application.
- Each Computer Use session requires **explicit user authorization** with a configurable time limit (default: 15 minutes); the session auto-terminates when the timer expires.
- A **persistent on-screen indicator** (overlay badge) is visible whenever the agent has active control, showing remaining session time.
- The user can **instantly revoke control** at any time by pressing any key or moving the mouse; the agent immediately stops all actions and logs the interruption.
- A **screen masking** option lets users designate sensitive screen regions (e.g., password fields) that the agent cannot read or interact with during the session.
- All agent actions are recorded in a **session audit log** with timestamps, screenshots, and action descriptions — reviewable after the session ends.

## Verification

1. Start a Computer Use session, authorize for 5 minutes. Ask the agent to open System Preferences and toggle Dark Mode. Verify the agent completes the task and the on-screen indicator counts down correctly.
2. During an active session, move the mouse. Confirm the agent immediately stops, the session is revoked, and the audit log records the interruption event.
3. Mask a screen region covering a password field. Ask the agent to fill a login form. Verify the agent fills the username but skips or requests help for the masked password region.
4. Let a session timer expire without manual revocation. Confirm the agent stops, the overlay disappears, and a summary notification is shown.
5. Review the session audit log after a completed task. Verify it contains timestamped screenshots and action descriptions for every step the agent performed.

## Related

- Community interest in desktop automation and agent-driven workflows.

title: [Feature]: Chrome Extension — Reuse Browser Login State for Agent Tasks
body:
## Background

Cherry Studio currently operates as a standalone chat client with no ability to interact with users' authenticated browser sessions. When agents need to perform web-based tasks (e.g., filling forms, extracting data from logged-in dashboards, or automating workflows on SaaS platforms), users must manually copy-paste content or provide credentials separately. Competitors like Codex have shipped Chrome Extensions (2026-05) that let agents reuse existing browser login state, turning their clients into real browser automation platforms.

## Goal

Enable Cherry Studio agents to perform web tasks by reusing the user's authenticated browser sessions through a companion Chrome Extension, with fine-grained permission controls.

## Spec

- Provide a companion Chrome Extension that bridges Cherry Studio agents with the user's active browser sessions, allowing agents to read page content, click elements, fill forms, and navigate — all within already-authenticated contexts.
- Implement per-site authorization: users explicitly grant or deny agent access to specific domains via a whitelist/blacklist mechanism managed from both the extension popup and Cherry Studio settings.
- Support multi-tab parallel execution so agents can work on multiple web tasks concurrently in background tabs without blocking the user's active browsing.
- Display a persistent visual indicator (badge/icon state) on the extension whenever an agent is actively operating in the browser, so users always know when automation is running.
- Log all agent browser actions in a reviewable activity timeline accessible from Cherry Studio, enabling users to audit what the agent did and on which sites.
- Allow users to interrupt or pause any ongoing browser task from either the extension popup or the Cherry Studio conversation interface.

## Verification

- Grant agent access to a specific site (e.g., GitHub), send a prompt asking the agent to read the user's notification page, and confirm the agent returns accurate content without requiring the user to re-authenticate.
- Add a domain to the blacklist, then ask the agent to perform a task on that domain — verify the agent is blocked and returns an appropriate permission-denied message.
- Trigger two simultaneous web tasks targeting different sites, confirm both execute in parallel background tabs and complete independently.
- While an agent task is running, verify the extension badge shows an active-automation indicator, and confirm it clears once the task completes.
- Interrupt a running browser task mid-execution from the Cherry Studio chat, verify the agent stops and the affected tab is left in a stable state.

## Related

- Community interest in browser automation and agent tool use capabilities

title: [Feature]: Sites — Built-in Web App Hosting and Deployment
body:
## Background

Users who build small web apps, dashboards, internal tools, or interactive demos with AI assistance currently have no way to host and share them directly from Cherry Studio. They must manually export generated code, set up separate hosting, and manage deployments themselves. Codex has previewed a "Sites" feature (2026-06) that lets users create, save, deploy, and view web applications within the client. This capability could extend Cherry Studio beyond a chat interface into a lightweight app creation and hosting platform — though it represents a notable expansion of the product's current scope and requires careful boundary evaluation.

## Goal

Allow users to create, preview, deploy, and share simple web applications (dashboards, tools, demos, mini-games) directly from within Cherry Studio, with platform-managed hosting.

## Spec

- Provide an in-app web editor/preview pane where users can create or refine HTML/CSS/JS projects through conversation with the AI, with live preview updating as changes are made.
- Support one-click deployment that publishes the project to a Cherry Studio-hosted URL, giving users a shareable public link without any external hosting setup.
- Allow users to manage deployed sites (list, update, unpublish, delete) from a dedicated "Sites" section in the Cherry Studio sidebar or settings.
- Assign each deployed site a stable, human-readable subdomain (e.g., `<project-name>.cherry.site`) that persists across updates.
- Enforce per-user resource limits (number of sites, storage quota, bandwidth) with clear usage indicators, to keep hosting costs sustainable.
- Support static-site projects only in the initial version (HTML/CSS/JS with no server-side execution), with a clear upgrade path for future server-side capabilities.

## Verification

- Through conversation, ask the AI to build a simple dashboard page, verify it renders correctly in the in-app preview pane.
- Deploy the dashboard, confirm a public URL is generated and the page is accessible from an external browser without authentication.
- Update the deployed site via a follow-up conversation edit, re-deploy, and verify the public URL now reflects the changes.
- Unpublish a site from the management panel, then visit the URL and confirm it returns a 404 or appropriate "site removed" page.
- Create sites up to the per-user limit, attempt to create one more, and verify the system shows a clear quota-exceeded message.

## Related

- Potential synergy with Cherry Studio's existing artifact/preview capabilities

title: [Feature]: Incremental/Differential App Updates
body:
## Background

Cherry Studio's desktop app currently requires users to download the full installation package for every update. As the app grows in size, this means large downloads (often 100MB+) even for minor patches, leading to slow updates, wasted bandwidth, and a frustrating experience — especially for users on limited or slow network connections. Frequent release cycles compound the problem. Competitors like Codex have adopted differential/incremental update mechanisms where only the changed portions are downloaded (e.g., ~46MB diff packages), significantly reducing update time and data usage.

## Goal

Introduce incremental/differential updates so that Cherry Studio desktop users only download the binary diff between their current version and the new version, making updates faster and more bandwidth-efficient.

## Spec

- When a new version is available, the updater calculates and downloads only the binary difference between the user's current version and the target version, instead of the full installation package.
- Fall back gracefully to a full download if the differential patch cannot be applied (e.g., corrupted local installation, version too old for a diff path, or patch verification failure).
- Display download size and estimated time for the differential update in the update dialog, so users can see the benefit compared to a full download.
- Verify the integrity of the patched application after applying the diff (e.g., checksum/signature validation) before completing the update, to prevent corrupted installations.
- Support differential updates across all desktop platforms (Windows, macOS, Linux) that Cherry Studio ships on.
- Maintain the existing "download full installer" option as a manual fallback accessible from settings, for users who prefer or need a clean install.

## Verification

- Upgrade from version N to N+1 using the differential updater, confirm the downloaded patch is significantly smaller than the full installer and the app launches correctly after update.
- Simulate a corrupted local installation, trigger an update, and verify the system detects the diff cannot be applied and falls back to a full download automatically.
- Check the update dialog displays accurate differential download size and that it is noticeably smaller than the full package size shown in release notes.
- Apply a differential update on each supported platform (Windows, macOS, Linux), verify the post-update integrity check passes and the app runs without issues.
- After a successful differential update, verify the app's version string, settings, and user data are all intact and unchanged.

## Related

- Frequently reported community feedback about large download sizes during updates

title: [Feature]: Default Agent Max Rounds to Unlimited
body:
## Background

When using Agents for complex, multi-step tasks (e.g., deep research, multi-tool workflows), the current "max rounds" setting often cuts execution short before the task completes. Users are forced to guess an appropriate round limit upfront or manually increase it after hitting the cap. This leads to frustration and wasted context, especially for long-running agentic workflows that involve many sequential tool calls.

## Goal

Default the Agent max rounds setting to unlimited so that tasks run to natural completion, only applying a round cap when the user explicitly sets one.

## Spec

- Change the default value of the Agent "max rounds" (max turns) setting to unlimited (no cap).
- When the setting is at its default (unlimited), the Agent continues executing until the task completes, the user manually stops it, or another limit (e.g., token budget) is reached.
- If a user explicitly sets a numeric value for max rounds, that value is respected as a hard stop.
- Existing Agents that already have a user-configured max rounds value retain that value after the change.
- The setting UI should clearly indicate when the value is "Unlimited" vs. a user-defined number.
- Ensure the token-level limits (`#14985`) and context compression (`#14552`) remain independent controls that are unaffected by this change.

## Verification

- Create a new Agent without touching the max rounds setting; run a 20+ step tool-calling task and confirm it completes without being truncated.
- Set max rounds to 5 on an Agent; confirm execution stops after exactly 5 rounds.
- Upgrade from a previous version where an Agent had max rounds = 10; confirm the value is preserved at 10 after upgrade.
- Confirm the settings UI shows "Unlimited" as the default and allows switching to a numeric value.

## Related

- #14985 - Configurable max context tokens for Agent mode
- #14552 - Auto-compress context

title: [Feature]: Auto OCR Fallback for Non-Vision Models
body:
## Background

When a user sends an image to a non-vision model (e.g., GLM 5.1), the model simply cannot process it and the image is effectively ignored. Users expect "reading an image" to just work regardless of which model they've selected — competing products like Workbody already handle this transparently. Cherry Studio already has OCR infrastructure in its document processing pipeline, but this capability is not leveraged for chat-time image inputs.

## Goal

Automatically extract text from images via OCR and pass the extracted content to the LLM whenever the selected model lacks native vision capabilities, so users can "read images" with any model.

## Spec

- Detect at send-time whether the active model supports vision/multimodal input.
- If the model lacks vision support and the user's message contains one or more images, automatically run OCR on each image before sending the message.
- Inject the OCR-extracted text into the prompt context (e.g., as a clearly labeled text block) so the LLM can reason over the image content.
- Reuse the existing OCR configuration from the document processing module — no separate OCR setup required.
- Show a brief, non-blocking indicator (e.g., "Extracting text from image...") so the user understands why there is a short delay.
- If OCR extraction fails or returns empty, send the message anyway and inform the user that the image could not be read.

## Verification

- Select a non-vision model (e.g., GLM 5.1), send an image containing clearly readable text, and confirm the model responds with accurate references to the text in the image.
- Select a vision-capable model, send the same image, and confirm the image is sent natively without OCR fallback.
- Send an image with no readable text (e.g., a photo of a landscape) to a non-vision model and confirm the system handles the empty OCR result gracefully.
- Verify the OCR fallback respects the user's existing OCR provider configuration from document processing settings.
- Send multiple images in one message to a non-vision model and confirm all are OCR-processed.

## Related

- #14976 - Use document processing OCR for image recognition
- #10399 - Use vision model to recognize images (closed)
- #8394 - Vision model proxy recognition (closed)

title: [Feature]: Add Auto Mode to Agent Permission Levels
body:
## Background

Cherry Studio's Agent permission system currently offers several modes (ask, fully-automatic, accept-edits, plan) but lacks an "Auto mode" tier that sits between supervised and fully autonomous. Users familiar with Claude Code's permission model (Ask / Accept Edits / Plan / Auto / Bypass) expect a similar graduated scale. Without Auto mode, users must choose between stopping to approve every action or granting full autonomy with no guardrails, leaving no middle ground for trusted-but-monitored execution.

## Goal

Add an "Auto mode" permission level to the Agent permission menu, providing a balanced tier where the Agent executes most actions autonomously but still asks for confirmation on high-risk operations.

## Spec

- Add "Auto mode" as a new option in the Agent permission level selector, positioned between "Accept Edits" (or equivalent) and "Fully Automatic / Bypass."
- In Auto mode, the Agent executes read operations, searches, and standard tool calls without prompting, but requests user confirmation for destructive or irreversible actions (e.g., file deletion, external API writes, system-level changes).
- The set of actions considered "high-risk" should be predefined and documented; advanced users may customize this list in the future.
- The permission menu order should align with the Claude Code model: Ask > Accept Edits > Plan > Auto > Fully Automatic (Bypass).
- Switching between permission levels mid-conversation takes effect immediately for subsequent actions.
- The default permission level for new Agents remains unchanged (Ask mode).

## Verification

- Open an Agent's permission settings and confirm "Auto mode" appears as a selectable option in the correct position.
- In Auto mode, trigger a read-only tool call (e.g., web search) and confirm it executes without prompting.
- In Auto mode, trigger a destructive action (e.g., deleting a file) and confirm the user is prompted for approval.
- Switch from Auto mode to Ask mode mid-conversation and confirm subsequent actions require approval.
- Confirm existing Agents retain their previously selected permission level and are not affected by the addition.

## Related

- #15039 - Permission mode enhancements
- #14197 - Agent permission controls
- #11017 - Permission level configuration

title: [Feature]: Wire Up Missing Claude Agent SDK Capabilities — auto / dontAsk Permission Modes, Budget Controls, Sandbox, File Checkpointing, Thinking-Effort UI
body:
## Background

Cherry Studio's Agent runtime is built on `@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk@0.3.145`, which exposes a much wider capability surface than Cherry currently wires up. Concrete gaps verified in code:

- The SDK's `PermissionMode` enum has **6 values** (`default`, `acceptEdits`, `bypassPermissions`, `plan`, `dontAsk`, `auto`); Cherry's schema enumerates only **4** — `dontAsk` and `auto` are dropped on the floor. `auto` is the SDK's model-classified permission flow (the model itself decides per tool call whether to prompt) — exactly what users approximate today by clicking approve repeatedly. `dontAsk` is "deny by default, no prompts" — useful for high-trust automation.
- The SDK exposes **per-session budget caps** (`taskBudget` for tokens, `maxBudgetUsd` for spend); Cherry has **zero** code references to either, so long autonomous runs burn through unbounded.
- The SDK exposes **sandboxed command execution** (`sandbox: { enabled, network }` with `bubblewrap` / `sandbox-exec` etc. underneath); Cherry has **zero** sandbox code references, so every shell tool call runs unrestricted in the user's main environment.
- The SDK provides **file checkpointing** (`enableFileCheckpointing` + `Query.rewindFiles()` to roll files back to any prior user message); Cherry has **zero** references — users who want to undo an agent's recent file edits must `git stash` manually.
- The SDK provides **external session mirroring** (`sessionStore` interface to export transcripts to user-controlled storage); Cherry has **zero** references in the agent runtime.
- `thinking` and `effort` are actually wired in the agent runtime but **not exposed in the Agent settings UI** — they only work programmatically. The chat-side Assistant has a `ThinkingButton`, but Agent users have no way to set them.

Closing these gaps is mostly *exposing* and *passing through* what the SDK already implements — not new model logic.

## Goal

Cherry exposes the SDK capabilities currently dropped or hidden — two missing permission modes, budget caps, sandbox isolation, file rewind, optional session mirroring, and the Thinking/Effort UI gap on the Agent side — through coherent agent settings and inline controls, with no regression for existing agents on existing modes.

## Spec

- **Extend `AgentPermissionModeSchema`** from 4 to 6 values, adding **`dontAsk`** (no prompts, deny if not pre-approved) and **`auto`** (model classifier decides per tool call). Both appear in the same agent settings permission-mode picker as today's modes, with one-line tooltips explaining the trade-offs.
- **Add agent-settings budget fields**: optional `Max tokens per task` (mapped to SDK `taskBudget.total`) and `Max spend per task (USD)` (mapped to SDK `maxBudgetUsd`). Both can be left empty (no cap — current behavior). When hit, the agent stops cleanly with `"Budget cap reached at <value> — extend to continue?"` and a one-click extend button.
- **Add `Run shell commands in a sandbox` toggle** in agent settings, mapped to SDK `sandbox: { enabled, network }`. Default off (no regression). When enabled, commands run inside the platform's sandbox primitive (macOS `sandbox-exec`, Linux `bubblewrap`) with optional network isolation. If SDK reports sandbox dependencies missing, the agent surfaces a clear "Sandbox unavailable on this platform — install bubblewrap?" message rather than silently running unrestricted.
- **Enable file checkpointing** (`enableFileCheckpointing: true`) by default for new agents; expose a small **"Rewind files to here"** action on each user message in the agent conversation, calling SDK `Query.rewindFiles(messageId)`. Confirmation dialog lists which files will revert before applying. The rewind is recorded as a distinct event in the conversation, not silently mixed with agent edits.
- **Surface Thinking and Effort controls in the Agent settings form** — two dropdowns mirroring the SDK's enums: `Thinking: adaptive / enabled / disabled` and `Effort: low / medium / high / xhigh` (xhigh tooltip notes "Opus 4.7 only, others fall back to high"). The runtime path is already wired; this is purely UI exposure. Mirrors the chat-side `ThinkingButton` for consistency.
- **(Optional) Session mirroring** as an advanced agent setting: user-supplied SQLite path or HTTP endpoint, mapped to SDK `sessionStore`. Default off. When enabled, each agent run's transcript is mirrored to the user-controlled destination; turning off stops new writes but does not delete existing rows.
- Existing agents on the existing 4 modes are unchanged on upgrade. All new fields default to empty/off.

## Verification

- In agent settings, user picks `auto` permission mode → agent runs; the model decides per tool call: reading a file passes silently, but a `rm -rf` candidate triggers a prompt that includes the model's risk reasoning. The 4 existing modes behave identically to before.
- User picks `dontAsk` mode and tries a tool not in the pre-approved list → agent denies the call inline with `"Tool '<name>' not pre-approved under dontAsk mode"` without prompting.
- User sets `Max spend per task: $2.00` and runs an agent task. At $2.05 the agent stops with `"Budget cap reached at $2.05 — extend to continue?"` inline. Clicking extends. Without the cap set, the agent runs to completion.
- User enables `Sandbox` + `Network isolation`, then sends `"fetch https://example.com"` → agent's shell tool reports network access denied. Same agent with sandbox off completes the fetch.
- On a Linux system without `bubblewrap`, user enables sandbox → agent settings surfaces `"Sandbox unavailable — install bubblewrap to use this"` link before save; saving leaves sandbox off rather than silently mis-configuring.
- User has file checkpointing on, agent edits 5 files across 3 turns. User clicks **"Rewind files to here"** on the second-to-last user message → confirmation dialog lists 2 files; confirm → those 2 revert, the 3 from earlier turns stay. The agent context records the rewind as a distinct event.
- In Agent settings, user changes `Effort: xhigh` and picks Opus 4.7 model → next tool-use turn visibly uses higher reasoning budget. Switching the model to Sonnet → Effort silently falls back to `high` (per SDK behavior); UI tooltip explains why.
- User enables session mirroring to `~/cherry-transcripts.db` → after each agent run, the run's full transcript appears in that DB; disabling mirroring stops new writes without deleting existing rows.
- On upgrade, an existing agent configured with `default` mode runs identically — no permission flow changes, no new prompts, no budget caps.

## Related

- #14552 (closed — auto-compact context, adjacent SDK capability surfacing)
- #15182 (open — Bundle claude-code-setup as featured plugin, adjacent SDK ecosystem)
- #15043 (open — Optimize Claude Agent startup speed, adjacent SDK perf)
- #15323 (open — `/clear` command, adjacent SDK session-control surface)

title: [Feature]: Inline Provider Configuration Prompt in Chat — Configure API Key Without Leaving the Conversation
body:
## Background

Today when a Cherry Studio user picks a model in chat whose provider isn't configured, the model selector shows it just fine, the send button works, and the user only discovers the problem **after** sending — when a bare 401 error toast appears. To fix it the user must navigate **Settings → Providers → find the right provider → paste the key → save → close Settings → return to chat → re-send the message**. That's 4-6 clicks, no inline affordance anywhere, and the typed message is often lost in the context-switching. The settings-gear icon next to models in the picker only navigates away from chat. This is exactly the friction Cline, OpenCode, and similar tools solve by letting users paste credentials inline at the point of need — zero navigation cost, the original message survives, and the user stays in their conversation.

## Goal

When a user picks or attempts to send with a model whose provider isn't configured, an inline popover lets them paste the API key (and the minimum provider-specific fields) without leaving the conversation; on successful save the original message sends automatically.

## Spec

- The chat model picker shows a **"Not configured"** tag (subtle ⚠️ + label) on every model whose provider has no enabled API key — no longer treated as equally usable.
- Clicking a "Not configured" model in the picker opens an **inline popover** (not a navigation away) titled `Configure <Provider>`, anchored to the model entry. The popover contains an API key field (paste-friendly), the minimum provider-required fields (e.g. base URL for Azure, deployment name where applicable), and a primary `Save and continue` CTA.
- Sending a message to a "Not configured" model **also** opens the same popover — the typed message is **not lost**; the popover surfaces above the composer with the original text retained in the input.
- On successful save, the popover closes, the picker shows the model as **Configured**, and if the user had a pending send queued, it auto-fires. The user does not re-click send.
- The popover offers a small `Open full provider settings` link for users who need the full multi-field config page — the inline path is for the common case (paste key, go).
- Provider-specific minimum field sets are surfaced inline: Anthropic shows API key only; Azure OpenAI shows key + base URL + deployment name; an OpenAI-compatible provider shows key + base URL. The popover adapts per provider, no field bloat.
- On invalid key (4xx auth response on the next request), the popover stays open and shows `Authentication failed — check the key` inline, without losing the typed message.
- After successful save, the existing Smart Model Auto-Discovery (#13418) flow fires automatically — newly available models from this provider appear in the picker without manual refresh.
- The `Not configured` badge persists until the provider is verified end-to-end (one successful chat completion). A configured provider whose key is later revoked re-acquires the badge on the next failed request.

## Verification

- User opens chat model picker with no OpenAI key set → `gpt-5` shows a "Not configured" tag. Clicking it opens a `Configure OpenAI` popover overlay; the chat input retains any typed text.
- User pastes a valid OpenAI API key + clicks `Save and continue` → popover closes; the picker shows `gpt-5` as configured; if user had typed a message, it auto-sends without a re-click.
- User saves an invalid key → popover surfaces `Authentication failed — check the key` inline, doesn't close, doesn't lose the typed message; user pastes a corrected key and saves again.
- User picks Azure OpenAI → popover shows API key + base URL + deployment name (three Azure-required fields). User picks Anthropic → popover shows API key only.
- User picks an unconfigured model with no message typed → popover opens; on save, popover closes; user types and sends normally afterward.
- User clicks `Open full provider settings` in the popover → navigates to existing settings page; chat input preserves the typed text and sends on return to chat.
- After successful save, the existing Smart Model Auto-Discovery (#13418) silently fetches the provider's full model list → picker updates without a manual refresh.
- User's previously-configured Anthropic key is revoked upstream → next chat request fails 401 → the model entry re-acquires the "Not configured" badge and tapping it surfaces the same inline popover with a "Re-authenticate" framing.
- On upgrade, providers already configured stay configured — no popover surfaces, no behavior change for existing keys.

## Related

title: [Feature]: Remove the Agent "Max Conversation Turns" Setting
body:
## Background

Agent advanced settings expose a "Max conversation turns" option (default 100) meant to cap how long an agent runs autonomously. With agents now relying on the SDK's built-in context compaction (auto-compact / `/compact`) to keep long conversations within the model's context window, this manual cap is redundant configuration that most users don't understand and that can cut an agent off mid-task when set too low.

## Goal

Users no longer see or manage a max-turns cap when configuring an agent; long-running agents are kept healthy by automatic context compaction instead.

## Spec

- The "Max conversation turns" field is removed from the Agent advanced settings UI.
- Existing agents that previously had a custom max-turns value continue to work without error after the field is removed (the stored value is ignored or migrated, not surfaced).
- With no user-facing cap, an agent runs until it naturally completes the task; long conversations stay within context limits via automatic compaction rather than a turn count.
- Removing the setting does not change any other agent advanced setting (environment variables, permissions, tools, skills remain as-is).

## Verification

- Open an agent's advanced settings → there is no "Max conversation turns" field; the panel shows only the remaining options (e.g. environment variables).
- An agent created before this change (with max turns set to e.g. 20) still runs normally; it is not stopped at 20 turns.
- Run a long agent task that previously would exceed 100 turns → it continues to completion, and a compaction boundary is observed in the conversation instead of an abrupt turn-limit stop.
- Other advanced settings (environment variables, permission mode, tools, skills) are unchanged and still save correctly.

None (sourced from internal product feedback).

title: [Feature]: Apply Existing Error Classification to Toasts — Typed Errors with Actionable Affordances
body:
## Background

Cherry Studio already has a comprehensive error classification utility (`errorClassifier.ts`) that maps thrown errors into 16 distinct categories (auth, model, quota, context_length, payload, network, proxy, stream, content, server, deprecated, knowledge, ocr, mcp, parse, unknown) — but it's only used **downstream** in the chat message `ErrorBlock` component. The 432 `window.toast.error(...)` call sites across the renderer all pass either a raw `error.message` or a generic i18n string, so users see the same flat "something went wrong" treatment regardless of whether the underlying problem is a missing API key, a quota cap, a network blip, or a corrupt MCP response. There are no inline action buttons on any toast today — users can't click "Configure" / "Retry" / "Open settings" from the toast itself, even when the natural next step is obvious. #15024 and #15025 (both v1.9.8) tackle adjacent symptoms (neutralizing alarm colors on retryable errors; hiding raw stacks), but neither applies the existing classifier as a system-wide toast layer or adds the actionable affordances that would close the loop.

## Goal

Every toast error is routed through the existing classifier, rendered with type-appropriate visual + copy, and (where the next step is unambiguous) carries one inline action button that closes the loop without forcing the user to navigate elsewhere.

## Spec

- A single helper — `window.toast.errorFromException(error, context?)` — wraps the existing classifier and replaces direct `window.toast.error(error.message)` calls. The existing 5-variant `window.toast` API stays for explicit-type calls; the new helper is for "I have an Error / thrown value, route it correctly".
- The classifier output maps to **toast presentation**:
  - `auth` → "Configure" inline button → opens `<ProviderQuickConfigPopover>` (#15646) for the relevant provider
  - `quota` → "Open billing" inline button + the provider's billing/usage page
  - `network` / `proxy` → "Retry" inline button → re-runs the originating action; tooltip explains the difference
  - `context_length` → "Trim history" inline button → opens the `/clear` or auto-compact flow (#15323)
  - `model` (deprecated / unavailable model) → "Switch model" inline button → opens model picker scoped to the same provider
  - `mcp` → "View MCP server" inline button → opens the offending MCP's status panel
  - `payload` / `parse` / `content` → no action button; humanized copy explaining the underlying constraint
  - `unknown` → fallback to current generic toast behavior (no regression)
- Toast **copy** for each category is humanized through new i18n keys (e.g. `toast.error.auth.missing_key` rather than echoing the raw provider error string). Raw `error.message` is moved to a hover tooltip / expand affordance, not removed.
- A toast with an inline action carries a distinct visual treatment (action button right-aligned, toast width slightly wider, dismiss icon still present). Actions are clickable directly from the toast — no need to navigate.
- The classifier and its mappings are exposed as data, so call sites can pass a `category` override when they have more context than the classifier infers from the exception alone.
- All existing `window.toast.error(string)` calls keep working unchanged (no regression); the new helper is opt-in at call sites. Migration is gradual — the highest-traffic call sites switch first.
- Errors classified as `quota` or `auth` while in a chat send-path also trigger the existing path for marking the provider as "Not configured" (per #15646), so the picker badge stays in sync.

## Verification

- User sends to Claude with no Anthropic key → toast appears with type `auth`, copy `Configure Anthropic to use Claude`, inline `Configure` button → click → `<ProviderQuickConfigPopover>` opens for Anthropic. (Today: raw 401 error message in plain text.)
- User hits OpenAI rate limit → toast appears with type `quota`, copy `OpenAI rate limit reached — try again in N seconds, or upgrade your plan`, inline `Open billing` button → click → opens billing URL. (Today: raw `rate_limit_exceeded` JSON snippet.)
- User loses WiFi mid-stream → toast type `network`, copy `Network unreachable — retry?`, inline `Retry` button → click → re-runs the same chat request. (Today: raw `fetch failed` message.)
- User sends with a context that exceeds model window → toast type `context_length`, copy `Conversation too long for <model> — trim history?`, inline `Trim history` button → opens `/clear` flow (#15323).
- User invokes a tool from an offline MCP server → toast type `mcp`, copy `MCP server '<name>' not responding`, inline `View MCP server` button → opens MCP status panel.
- User hovers a typed toast → tooltip shows the underlying raw `error.message` (preserved, not hidden) for debugging.
- User clicks `Retry` on a `network` toast and the retry succeeds → success toast (`window.toast.success`) replaces; if retry fails, the error toast re-appears (no infinite stacking).
- Existing call sites using `window.toast.error('Something failed')` (literal string) keep behaving exactly as today — no migration regression.
- User passes an opaque `Error` object the classifier maps to `unknown` → fallback to current generic-error toast with no action button; underlying raw message visible inline.
- For an `auth` error during chat send-path, the provider's model picker badge updates to "Not configured" per #15646 — the two issues stay in sync.

## Related

- #15024 (open, v1.9.8 — Surface Tool/Retry Errors in Neutral Color; addresses visual treatment for retryable errors, complementary to this issue's type-based visual scheme)
- #15025 (open, v1.9.8 — Improve AI Error Diagnosis with hidden raw stack; addresses stack handling, complementary to this issue's tooltip-preserved-raw-message pattern)
- #15323 (open — `/clear` command in Agent session; this issue's `context_length` toast action invokes that flow)
- #15646 (this session — Inline Provider Configuration Prompt in Chat; this issue's `auth` toast action triggers #15646's popover)

title: [Feature]: Folder-Based Knowledge Vault (Agent-Friendly Knowledge Base)
body:
## Background

Cherry Studio's knowledge base today is effectively a RAG/SQLite store: users import files, URLs, notes, and directories, which get loaded, chunked, embedded, and written to a vector DB. Even an imported directory is only a *source* — not the knowledge base itself — so users can't see, browse, or manage the real folder, and agents have no stable, readable/writable knowledge workspace. Users with messy real-world material (local files, folders, web pages, notes, third-party docs) want to manage it all in one visible place and hand it to an agent to organize.

## Goal

Users can create a folder-based knowledge "vault" where a Cherry-managed local folder *is* the knowledge base — browsable as a file manager, optionally embedded for Chat RAG, and handed to an agent to organize.

## Spec

- Two knowledge-base modes coexist: the existing RAG knowledge base and a new folder-type "vault". Existing knowledge bases keep working unchanged; no migration.
- Creating a vault asks for a name, a template (Blank / LLM Wiki), and an *optional* embedding model. Cherry creates and owns the folder; the storage location is hidden from the user.
- Adding content (local file, local folder, web link → Markdown, note, new folder) **copies/converts it into the managed folder** rather than referencing external paths; original sources are left untouched.
- The vault detail page is a single-directory file manager (columns: name / type / size / updated time / index status) showing the real imported structure — "what you import is what you see" — not source-type tabs and not a fixed Raw / Agent-organized layout. Internal `.cherry`-style data is always hidden.
- Embedding is optional: without it the vault is still browsable and agent-usable, just not answerable in normal Chat RAG. Users can enable an embedding model later in settings and (re)build the index from the current folder.
- "Use with Agent" lets the user pick an agent, then jumps to the agent chat with the vault folder passed as an accessible path and the input prefilled with "help me organize this knowledge base".
- An agent may read the folder freely, but must present a plan/diff (create / move / rewrite / delete list) and get user confirmation before modifying; deletes go to an archive/recycle area, not permanent removal.

## Verification

- Create a Blank vault with embedding disabled → it appears in the list; detail page shows an empty directory + a top-right Add menu; no forced embedding-model selection; no Raw/Agent tabs.
- Import a real local folder (e.g. an Obsidian vault with nested dirs, Markdown, hidden config) → content is copied into the managed folder; the original folder on disk is not moved or modified; detail page shows the original structure; `.DS_Store` / `.obsidian` / `.cherry` are not listed, not searched, not embedded.
- Click a Markdown file → preview opens on the right; click an unsupported file (e.g. `.canvas`) → no crash, clear "cannot preview" state, file still listed.
- Enable an embedding model in a previously embedding-disabled vault → indexable files enter the queue with visible progress; afterwards Chat can answer from the vault. Trying RAG before enabling shows a clear "embedding not enabled" message, not an empty-model error.
- Add a new Markdown file and reindex → it becomes searchable; delete a file → it stops being retrieved; hidden `.cherry` never enters the index.
- Click "Use with Agent" → agent picker opens defaulting to the most recently used agent; after confirming, jumps to chat with the vault folder accessible and input prefilled "help me organize this knowledge base".
- Ask the agent to organize the imported vault → it first returns a plan (dirs/files to create, what to archive, classification) and does **not** silently modify the folder; after the user confirms, it writes and the detail page refreshes with the new content.
- Keyword-search "AI产品" / "理财" inside the vault → matches both file names and Markdown body text, locating the right files.
- Delete the vault → second confirmation; Cherry's managed copy and derived index are removed, but the original external folder on disk is not deleted.

## Related

#14896 #10685 #11720 #4405 #11119

title: [Feature]: Complete Toast Coverage for Silent User Operations — Success, Loading, and Info Notifications
body:
## Background

Cherry Studio's renderer has 681 toast call sites today, but the distribution is heavily skewed: **432 error**, **158 success**, **65 warning**, **17 info**, and only **9 loading**. The ratio means errors are nearly 3× the success count, and `loading` is essentially absent. The product implication is concrete: a large set of user operations succeed silently, with no visible confirmation. A user who clicks "Save", "Delete", "Export", "Copy link", "Sync now", "Install Skill", "Apply preset", or hundreds of other actions today often sees *nothing* on success — leaving them unsure whether the click was actually registered. The same applies to long-running operations that should surface progress: backup, restore, knowledge-base indexing, MCP server install, model auto-discovery, agent skill activation — most run silently and only surface a toast on terminal failure. Power users guess at completion by waiting and re-clicking; new users either re-click and trigger duplicates, or quietly give up. This isn't a deep technical gap — the toast system supports `success` / `loading` / `info` variants fully — it's a coverage gap from call sites not opting in.

## Goal

Every user-initiated operation that has a discrete completion event — save, delete, export, copy, install, sync, apply, activate — provides clear visible feedback through the toast system, with `loading` toasts for long-running operations and `success` toasts for completions, so users never have to guess whether their action took effect.

## Spec

- Conduct an audit across the renderer codebase of every user-initiated mutation operation (save / delete / export / copy / install / sync / apply / activate / toggle / publish / share) and document which have toast coverage today and which don't.
- Add `window.toast.success(...)` calls for every audit-identified silent success path. The toast message uses the action verb in past tense (e.g. `Saved`, `Deleted '<name>'`, `Skill '<name>' installed`), and includes the object name when one exists.
- Add `window.toast.loading(...)` for operations that typically take >2 seconds end-to-end (backup, restore, KB indexing, model auto-discovery, MCP install, large file ingestion); the loading toast updates in place to a `success` or `error` toast on completion (toast system already supports this via toast ID).
- Add `window.toast.info(...)` for state changes the user should know about but didn't directly initiate (e.g. "Auto-saved draft", "Background sync complete", "Heartbeat task fired", "Model `X` deprecated — switching to `Y`").
- Toast text is humanized through i18n keys with the action verb baked in — `toast.success.saved`, `toast.success.deleted_with_name`, `toast.loading.indexing_kb` — not a single generic "Done".
- For mutation operations that already show success in a downstream UI surface (e.g. saving a record that immediately appears in the list), a toast is **still** shown but with a shorter dismiss timeout (default 2s vs 4s) and a smaller visual weight, so the user gets the confirmation signal without being saturated.
- Bulk operations show a single aggregated toast (e.g. `Deleted 5 topics` not 5 separate toasts), with the count and an optional `Undo` action where the operation supports it.
- The audit document becomes a tracked checklist in the issue body — each line items either gets a coverage commit or an explicit "intentionally silent" justification.
- Existing `error` toasts are unchanged — this work is purely additive on the success / loading / info side. (Error coverage / classification is tracked separately in #15651.)

## Verification

- User clicks `Save` on an assistant edit → `Saved` success toast appears (current behavior: in many cases, no toast).
- User deletes a topic → `Deleted '<topic title>'` success toast with `Undo` action; clicking `Undo` within 5s restores the topic.
- User initiates a knowledge base re-index → a `Indexing knowledge base '<name>'…` loading toast appears immediately; when indexing completes the same toast updates in place to `Indexed knowledge base '<name>' (N items)` success; on failure it updates to a typed error toast (per #15651).
- User installs a Skill from the marketplace → `Installing Skill '<name>'…` loading toast → on completion updates in place to `Skill '<name>' installed`.
- User selects 5 topics and bulk-deletes → single aggregated success toast `Deleted 5 topics` with `Undo` action (not 5 separate toasts).
- User triggers a background sync via WebDAV → loading toast `Syncing to WebDAV…` → completes in place to `WebDAV sync complete (N items uploaded)` success.
- Auto-save fires on a draft message → subtle info toast `Draft auto-saved` with shorter dismiss timeout (≤2s).
- Scheduled task fires → info toast `Scheduled task '<name>' fired` (also visible inline in conversation per #15574).
- User copies a chat link to clipboard → quick `Link copied` success toast (today: silent in many cases).
- Audit checklist in the issue body shows every covered call site marked complete, and every intentionally-silent path explicitly justified — no silent successes remaining without a documented reason.

## Related

- #15651 (related — Apply Existing Error Classification to Toasts; this issue is the success/loading/info coverage parallel — both close the loop on toast UX from opposite sides)
- #15574 (related — Scheduled Task Message Perspective; this issue's info-toast on scheduled-task fire aligns with #15574's timeline marker)
- #14899 (open, v2.4.0 — Unified Notification Center; this issue covers ephemeral toast feedback while #14899 covers persistent notification history)
- #15024 (open, v1.9.8 — Surface Tool/Retry Errors in Neutral Color; aligns visual treatment philosophy)

title: [Feature]: Highlight Current Position in the Conversation Navigation Bar
body:
## Background

Long conversations in Cherry Studio have a message navigation bar on the right edge (one marker per turn) that lets users jump between messages. But it gives no visual indication of which marker corresponds to the message currently on screen, so while scrolling a long chat users repeatedly click the wrong marker and lose their place.

## Goal

The conversation navigation bar visually highlights the marker for the message currently in view, so users can always tell where they are and jump accurately.

## Spec

- The navigation bar marks the message currently in the viewport with a distinct visual state (e.g. a highlight color) clearly different from the other markers.
- The highlight updates live while scrolling — it always reflects the message currently visible in the chat area, with no perceptible lag leaving two markers highlighted.
- Clicking a marker still jumps to that message; after the jump, the highlighted marker matches the new position.

## Verification

- Open a long conversation and scroll to the middle → the marker for the visible message is highlighted in a distinct color; the others are not.
- Scroll up/down continuously → the highlight moves in sync with the visible message, never leaving a stale second marker highlighted.
- Click a marker far from the current position → the view jumps there and the highlight moves to the clicked marker.
- Short conversation that fits on one screen → the active marker is still highlighted correctly (no missing or stuck highlight).
- Switch to another topic and back → the highlight reflects the restored scroll position, not a stale one.

title: [Feature]: Preprocess Multimodal Inputs to Text for Non-Vision Models — Reuse Knowledge Base Preprocess Pipeline in Chat
body:
## Background

Cherry Studio's chat composer treats vision capability as a UI gate: when the active model has no `image` in its `inputModalities`, the file picker hides image options and the attachment button tooltip says "documents only". But the gate is only at the picker — if the user drags-drops an image, pastes a screenshot, or attaches an Excel / PPT / PDF / ZIP, the file lands in the message parts as a raw base64 `data:` URL and is sent straight to the LLM. Text-only models then either error out or silently ignore the binary, and the user is left wondering why their question about a screenshot didn't get answered. Meanwhile, **Cherry already has a complete multimodal-to-text preprocessing pipeline** in `src/main/knowledge/preprocess/` — 5 providers (Mistral OCR, Mineru, Doc2x, PaddleOCR, OpenMineru) that already convert PDFs, images, and Office documents into clean markdown — **wired only to knowledge base ingestion**. The chat path doesn't reuse any of it. Closing this gap costs nothing in new infrastructure: it's wiring + a model-modality check + a `loading` toast for progress. The result is that any text-only model becomes effectively multimodal for the user's everyday "read this file and tell me what it says" use case.

## Goal

When a user attaches an image, PDF, Office document, or ZIP to a chat with a model that doesn't natively support that modality, Cherry transparently runs the file through its existing preprocessing pipeline to produce text, and sends the text to the model — so any text-only model can answer questions about visual or binary content the user uploaded.

## Spec

- When a user attaches a file in chat and the active model's `inputModalities` doesn't include the file's modality (image / pdf / office / archive), Cherry routes the file through the existing preprocessing pipeline before send, instead of inlining as base64.
- The composer no longer hides incompatible file types from the picker — all picker types become available to all models. Compatibility is handled by the preprocessor, not by hiding.
- Each modality maps to an existing preprocess provider:
  - **Images (PNG/JPG/WebP/screenshot)** → OCR provider (default: Mistral OCR, fallback PaddleOCR if user has it configured)
  - **PDF** → text extraction provider (Mineru / Doc2x / Mistral)
  - **DOCX / XLSX / PPTX** → markdown conversion (existing Office preprocess path; tables flattened to markdown tables; sheets concatenated with `## Sheet: <name>` headers)
  - **ZIP** → unpack, recursively run preprocessing per file, concatenate with file-path headers
- During preprocessing, a `loading` toast (per #15653) shows the current file + progress. Multi-file uploads show aggregated progress.
- When preprocessing completes, the model receives a structured user message containing the original filename(s) and the extracted text, with a clear header noting "Extracted from `<filename>` (via OCR / via PDF extract / etc.)" so the model knows the content is preprocessed rather than authored by the user.
- The original file is **still attached** to the user's message in the UI (so the user can re-download it), but only the extracted text is sent to the LLM.
- For models that natively support the modality (e.g. image to GPT-5), Cherry sends the original directly — no preprocessing, no regression.
- User can override per-attachment: a small "Send as-is (skip preprocessing)" toggle on each attachment chip, default off. Useful for power users testing what a model can natively handle.
- When no preprocess provider is configured for a needed modality, Cherry surfaces a typed `auth` toast (per #15651) with `Configure OCR provider` inline action → opens the existing knowledge-base preprocess provider settings.
- Preprocessing happens in main (not renderer) to reuse the existing pipeline; renderer dispatches an IPC and receives the extracted text + progress events.

## Verification

- User selects GPT-3.5 (text-only) and drags a screenshot into chat → `loading` toast `Extracting text from screenshot.png…` appears; on completion, a user message lands in the conversation showing the screenshot thumbnail and below it `Extracted from screenshot.png (via Mistral OCR): <text>`. User asks "what does the error say?" — GPT-3.5 answers from the extracted text. (Today: GPT-3.5 receives raw base64 and either errors or ignores it.)
- Same user with GPT-5 (vision-capable) drags the same screenshot → no preprocessing toast; GPT-5 receives the image natively. (Today: identical behavior, no regression.)
- User attaches a 30-page PDF to a text-only model → `loading` toast `Extracting text from doc.pdf (1/1)…` → completes to message body with extracted markdown; user asks "summarize section 3" — model answers from extracted text.
- User attaches an Excel with 4 sheets → preprocessing produces a markdown body with `## Sheet: Revenue`, `## Sheet: Expenses`, etc. headers; model can query individual sheets ("what's the total in Revenue row 12?").
- User attaches a ZIP containing 3 PDFs + 2 PNGs → loading toast shows aggregated progress; on completion, the message contains preprocessing output for each file, each prefixed by its filename header.
- User toggles `Send as-is` on an attachment in a text-only-model chat → preprocessing is skipped; current behavior preserved.
- User attaches an image but has no OCR provider configured → typed `auth` toast appears with `Configure OCR provider` inline action; clicking opens the existing knowledge-base preprocess provider settings (same UI Cherry already has).
- Multi-file upload: 5 PDFs at once → single aggregated loading toast `Extracting text from 5 files (2/5)…` updates as each completes; on done, all extractions land in one combined user message.
- Preprocessing error on one file in a batch → that file's section in the message reads `Extraction failed: <reason>`; other files succeed; user can choose to re-attach the failed file or proceed.

## Related

- #14878 (open, v2.2.0 — Allow Audio and Video Uploads When the Model Supports Them; this issue is the inverse direction — allow uploads when the model **doesn't** support them by preprocessing first)
- #15381 (open, v2.4.0 — Knowledge Base Image Ingestion and Multimodal Retrieval; complementary on the KB side, this issue brings the same capability to chat)
- #15470 (open — knowledge file processing integration; adjacent KB pipeline expansion)

- #15653 (related — Complete Toast Coverage; this issue's `loading` toast for preprocessing aligns with the in-place loading→success pattern)
