title: [Feature]: Market Page — Skills, Assistant Library, and MCP
body:
## Background

Discovery is split across separate surfaces: assistant presets are browsed in an Assistant Library dialog, Skills have their own marketplace dialog, and Settings → MCP → Marketplaces mainly lists external sites. A user looking for reusable capabilities has no single place to browse and install all three kinds of resource.

This issue defines the first unified **Market** page for **Skills, Assistant Templates, and MCP servers**. “Assistant Library” here means a catalog of templates users can add to their local collection, not the management view for assistants they already own.

## Goal

Users can find a Skill, assistant template, or MCP server from one in-app Market page, inspect it, install or configure it through the appropriate existing flow, and then find the resulting local resource where they use or manage it.

## Desired Solution

### Market entry and catalog

- Add a top-level **Market** entry with three first-class sections: **Skills**, **Assistant Library**, and **MCP**. All three sections show real catalog results rather than placeholder cards.
- Each section supports browsing, keyword search, and a detail view. Cards show at least the resource name, description, source/publisher, and installation state; show category/tags and an update state when that information exists in the source.
- Make the current section and search state clear when moving between sections. Empty, loading, and fetch-error states must tell the user what happened and offer a useful next action.
- Provide a clear path from an installed item to its existing local management or usage surface. Adding Market must not depend on #14408 being complete or remove an existing local management entry.

### Skills

- Reuse the supported Skill sources and installation flow. A user can inspect a Skill and install it from Market without manually copying a GitHub URL or downloading a zip.
- Installed Skills show their actual state and offer a path to the installed Skill and its Agent usage/settings. Source-specific expansion, CherryIN publication, community ratings, and sharing remain tracked by #14876.

### Assistant Library

- Browse the existing assistant preset catalog as installable templates. A user can inspect a template and add it as a local Assistant through the existing creation flow.
- An added Assistant is available in the Home assistant picker. The Market reflects that it has already been added and avoids creating an accidental duplicate from a repeated click.

### MCP

- Browse and search MCP server entries inside Market. A list of links to external marketplace websites alone does not fulfill this section.
- An MCP entry opens an in-app detail and install/configuration flow. Prefill catalog-provided settings, request only the values the user must supply, and use the existing MCP server creation and connection flow. Do not report “Installed” until the local server record has actually been created; show connection errors with a way to repair its configuration.
- An installed MCP entry opens its local server settings. OAuth/MCP **Connectors** that represent third-party account integrations are tracked separately by #15340.

## Verification

- Open Market from the main navigation. Skills, Assistant Library, and MCP are all visible and each loads actual entries. Search within each section returns matching entries and a useful no-results state.
- Open a Skill, inspect its details, install it, revisit Market, and confirm the item is shown as installed and is available in the relevant Agent/Skill management flow.
- Open an Assistant template, add it, and confirm the new Assistant appears in the Home picker. Revisit the template and confirm its added state prevents an accidental second copy.
- Open an MCP entry, complete any required configuration, and confirm the new server appears in local MCP settings. If connection fails, the entry remains repairable and does not falsely claim a working connection.
- Reopen Market after a restart and confirm installation states come from the actual local resources, rather than a temporary UI flag.
- Catalog loading failures and installation failures are visible, and retrying does not create duplicate local resources.

## Scope and related issues

- #14408 covers **management of local resources**. This issue covers **discovery and installation**; it does not assume the proposed unified local Library has shipped.
- #15029 records the core Skill marketplace and Save-as-Skill request. #14876 covers the broader CherryIN Skill lifecycle; this issue owns the shared Market entry and integration of Skill discovery into it.
- #6392 requested an MCP marketplace. This issue makes MCP a first-class section of the unified Market. #15340's OAuth/MCP Connectors remain a separate resource type and workflow.
- The previous version of this issue also proposed Use Cases, and a comment proposed prompt packs. Those remain valuable follow-ups, but the first Market page described here has the three sections above. This rewrite does not resolve those historical requests.

## Alternative Solutions

Keeping three unrelated discovery dialogs/pages leaves users to discover each resource type through a different navigation path. A single Market entry gives them a consistent starting point while each resource keeps its existing installation and local management rules.

## Additional Information

This issue describes the user-facing contract. Reuse current catalog and installer capabilities where possible; choose any additional catalog source needed for the in-app MCP experience during implementation.

title: [Bug]: Builtin skills sync creates garbage directories with backslash paths in ~/Downloads
body:
## Bug Description

When Cherry Studio starts up and syncs builtin skills, if the `accessible_paths` column in the agents table contains Windows-style backslash paths (e.g., from a cross-platform backup restore), the skills service creates garbage directories with literal backslashes in the filename under the working directory.

### Symptom

A directory tree like this appears in `~/Downloads/`:

```
~/Downloads/\home\bubu12\.config\CherryStudio\Data\Agents\t-default\
```

This happens because the backslash path is not recognized as an absolute path on Linux, so `mkdir({ recursive: true })` creates it relative to the process CWD (which is often `~/Downloads/` when the AppImage is launched from there).

### Root Cause

`SkillService.parseFirstAccessiblePath()` reads `accessiblePaths` from the database without calling `normalizePaths()`, unlike `AgentService` and `AgentSessionService` which were already fixed in PR #15480.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Have an agent database where `accessible_paths` contains Windows-style paths (e.g., from restoring a Windows backup on Linux)
2. Install a new builtin skill (or trigger `syncBuiltinSkill` on startup)
3. Observe garbage directories created in the process CWD (often `~/Downloads/`)

### Expected Behavior

Backslash paths should be normalized to forward slashes before any filesystem operations, so the correct absolute path is used.

### Platform

Linux (non-Windows)

### Additional Context

- Related PR: #15480 (fixes the same issue in AgentService and AgentSessionService)
- The `normalizePaths()` function already exists and just needs to be called in `SkillService.parseFirstAccessiblePath()`

title: [Feature]: Automatically restore latest S3 backup on startup across devices
body:
### Issue Checklist

- [x] I understand that issues are for reporting problems and requesting features, not for off-topic comments, and I will provide as much detail as possible to help resolve the issue.
- [x] I have checked the pinned issues and searched through the existing [open issues](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/issues), [closed issues](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20state%3Aclosed), and [discussions](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/discussions) and did not find a similar suggestion.
- [x] I have provided a short and descriptive title so that developers can quickly understand the issue when browsing the issue list, rather than vague titles like "A suggestion" or "Stuck."
- [x] The latest version of Cherry Studio does not include the feature I am suggesting.

### Platform

Windows

### Version

v1.9.9

### Is your feature request related to an existing issue?

Cherry Studio currently supports S3-compatible backup and automatic backup upload. However, the current “auto sync” behavior appears to only upload backups periodically. It does not automatically check and restore the latest remote backup when Cherry Studio starts on another computer.

This makes cross-device usage inconvenient. For example:

1. Computer A uploads a new S3 backup automatically.
2. Computer B starts Cherry Studio later.
3. Computer B still uses its local data unless the user manually opens the S3 backup manager and restores the latest backup.

For users who use Cherry Studio on multiple computers with the same S3-compatible storage, this feels more like “automatic backup” than “automatic sync”.

### Desired Solution

Add an option to automatically synchronize from S3-compatible backup storage when Cherry Studio starts.

Suggested behavior:

- Add a setting such as “Auto restore latest backup on startup” or “Sync from remote on startup”.
- On startup, Cherry Studio checks the configured S3 backup location for the latest backup file.
- If the latest remote backup is newer than the current local backup/sync timestamp, prompt the user to restore it, or optionally restore automatically depending on a setting.
- The restore flow should clearly show which device created the backup, the backup time, and the file name before applying it.
- To avoid accidental data loss, automatic restore should be opt-in and should not silently overwrite local data by default.
- If local data has changed after the latest remote backup, Cherry Studio should warn about a possible conflict instead of blindly restoring.

This would make S3-compatible backup useful for cross-device startup synchronization, while still keeping users safe from unexpected overwrites.

### Alternative Solutions

A simpler first step could be:

- On startup, only check whether a newer S3 backup exists.
- Show a notification/banner: “A newer backup from another device is available. Restore now?”
- Let the user manually confirm the restore.

A more advanced future solution could support real multi-device merge/sync, but startup detection plus guided restore would already solve the main pain point.

### Additional Information

Current behavior appears to be:

- S3 auto sync periodically calls backup upload.
- Backups are named with timestamp, hostname, and device type.
- Restore from S3 is available, but it is manual.
- Backup retention is per current device because cleanup filters by hostname and device type.

This feature request is specifically about different computers using the same S3-compatible backup configuration and automatically detecting/restoring the latest remote backup when the app starts.

title: [Feature]: In-Conversation File Downloads for Agent-Generated Artifacts
body:
## Background

Modern AI products increasingly produce **specific, sandbox-generated files** as outputs — a Python sandbox builds a multi-sheet Excel with real SUM formulas, a chart tool emits a PNG, a slide library produces a PPTX with real layouts. These artifacts **cannot be expressed in chat markdown** — they only exist because the agent ran code in a sandbox and wrote actual binary files. ChatGPT pioneered exposing these as inline download links from `/mnt/data/`, and the pattern is now a baseline expectation for AI products.

Cherry Studio cannot match this experience today. Cherry Claw can write files via Write/Edit tools, but the chat shows only a plain text line — "Created file: /path/foo.docx" — forcing users to leave the app and dig through the workspace; even when users find the file, conversation context is lost. Cherry Assistant cannot write files at all. And critically, **even ChatGPT's own download cards have no inline preview** — users download blind, open the file, discover it's the wrong layout / missing data / wrong style, then re-prompt — a frustrating round-trip. The opportunity is to ship the sandbox-download UX *and* fix its biggest weakness: **let users see the artifact's quality before they download**, so iteration happens inside the conversation, not across filesystem and apps.

## Goal

Whenever an Agent generates a file during a conversation, the user sees a downloadable card inline in the chat — with filename, type, size, an inline preview of the actual content, and a one-click download / "Save to…" action — so users can judge quality, iterate, and save artifacts without ever leaving the conversation.

## Spec

- When an Agent generates a file in its current session sandbox or workspace, a **download card** renders inline in the message stream at the point of generation. Card shows: filename, file-type icon (Word / Excel / PDF / image / code / generic), size, and primary action **Download** (with secondary **Open in Finder/Explorer**).
- The download card **renders an inline preview of the file content before any download action**, wherever feasible: images render as full thumbnails; PDFs show the first page; Excel and Word render a faithful first-page preview with formatting (sheet structure, formulas, fonts); CSV/JSON show a top-N rows snippet; code files show syntax-highlighted first lines. This is a deliberate differentiator from ChatGPT's "blind download" cards — users judge quality and decide whether to download or re-prompt without leaving the conversation.
- Download triggers a native Save dialog defaulting to the user's Downloads folder; cancelling does nothing destructive.
- Download cards **persist in the conversation history**. Reopening a past conversation still shows the card and the file remains downloadable for as long as the source file exists in its sandbox/workspace.
- If the source file has since been deleted (e.g. user wiped the workspace), the card renders in a disabled "no longer available" state with the original filename still shown — it does not silently disappear.
- The Cherry Assistant per-session sandbox is session-scoped — when the session is deleted, its sandbox directory is removed. Before deletion the user is warned that any generated files inside will be lost. (Cherry Claw files in user-chosen workspaces are unaffected.)
- The cards work uniformly for both Cherry Assistant and Cherry Claw — same component, same UX, regardless of which agent produced the file.
- Files generated under a per-session sandbox (Cherry Assistant) are owned and cleaned up by Cherry; files written under a user-chosen workspace (Cherry Claw) are never auto-deleted by this feature.
- **Mechanism note**: Cherry detects generated files through **tool-call observation** (the agent uses an explicit Write tool, Cherry emits a `generated-file` data part), not by parsing a special URI like `sandbox:/...` from model output. This is more robust than relying on the model to emit precise link syntax, and works across providers without prompt engineering.

### Pre-dependencies

- **A — Cherry Assistant sandbox**: Cherry Assistant today has no file-write capability or working directory. This feature requires Cherry Assistant to gain a per-session auto-provisioned sandbox directory and a minimal file-write tool, so its generated files have somewhere to live. Cherry Claw already has a workspace and the Write tool; no new infrastructure needed on that side beyond the rendering.
- **B — Generated-file data model**: a new `CherryDataPartTypes` entry (e.g. `generated-file`) is added to the message schema so that file-generation events become first-class parts of the message stream, decoupled from the raw tool-output text. The rendering layer reads from this part type, not from regex-parsing tool text.
- **C — File-generation detection**: a layer that observes Agent tool calls (Cherry Claw Write/Edit, future Cherry Assistant file-write tool, and any MCP tool whose output declares a generated file) and emits the `generated-file` data part with the absolute path + metadata. Without this, no card renders.
- **D — Sandbox security**: file-write tools must reject paths escaping the sandbox / workspace root (path traversal protection), enforce a per-file size cap (default 100 MB, configurable), reject disallowed extensions (executable binaries, system files), and surface clear errors when limits are hit instead of failing silently.
- **E — Inline preview rendering**: a per-file-type preview renderer that can faithfully display the first page / first rows / first frame of the most common formats (Office docs, PDF, images, CSV/JSON, code). Falls back gracefully to the type icon when a renderer is not available.

## Verification

- Ask Cherry Assistant: "Generate an Excel summary of the top 10 programming languages in 2026" → an Excel download card appears inline in the response with filename, size, an inline preview of the sheet (visible columns, data, even formula cell hints), and a Download button → clicking Download opens native Save dialog → user saves and opens it locally → file is a valid .xlsx with formatting matching the inline preview.
- Generate a PPT with Cherry Assistant → card shows first-slide preview inline with layout, fonts, and images visible.
- Generate a layout that's clearly wrong (e.g. ask for "5-column table", agent produces 3-column) → user spots the error from the inline preview, replies "make it 5 columns", new file generates → all without ever downloading the original wrong file.
- Ask Cherry Claw to refactor a project and write a new README → the new README.md appears as a download card inline at the moment of write, with the markdown content syntax-highlighted in the preview → the file also exists in the user's workspace as today.
- In Cherry Claw, ask it to write 5 files in one turn → 5 download cards render in the message in the order of writes; each downloads its own file correctly; each shows its own inline preview.
- Generate a chart image with Cherry Assistant → card shows an actual image thumbnail (not just a generic icon).
- Close and reopen a past conversation that produced a download card → card still renders with inline preview → Download still works (source file still in sandbox/workspace).
- Manually delete the source file from disk, reopen the conversation → card renders in "no longer available" disabled state with the original filename still shown → no download attempt, no crash.
- For Cherry Assistant, the file lives under an auto-provisioned per-session sandbox directory (not in the user's chosen workspace); confirming this on disk shows a Cherry-managed location separate from user workspaces.
- For Cherry Claw, no Cherry-managed sandbox is created; files land in the workspace the user chose, identical to current behavior.
- Delete a Cherry Assistant session that has generated files → warning prompt clearly states files will be lost → on confirm, the session sandbox directory is removed; on cancel, nothing happens.
- Attempt to write a file via the Cherry Assistant file-write tool to a path outside the sandbox (e.g. `../../etc/passwd`) → the tool rejects with a clear error and no card renders.
- Attempt to write a file larger than the configured size cap → tool rejects with a clear "exceeds size limit" error.
- When the generation detection layer emits a `generated-file` data part, the card renders; when it does not (e.g. a tool that wrote a temp file but isn't wired through the detection layer), no card renders. The behavior is data-part driven, not text-parsed.

### Platform

Windows

### Version

1.9.9

### Bug Description

When using MCP tools, the model can successfully call the tool, receive the tool result, and generate a response based on that result within the current turn.

However, in subsequent turns, the original MCP tool call and tool result do not appear to be included in the conversation context sent back to the model. Only the assistant's final natural-language response seems to remain.

As a result, the model loses access to the original structured data returned by the MCP tool and can only rely on the assistant's previous summary.

For example:

User asks the model to query data through an MCP tool.
MCP returns structured data (JSON, file contents, search results, etc.).
The model generates a correct response using that data.
In the next turn, the model can no longer reference the original MCP output because it is no longer present in the conversation context.

This is especially noticeable when using MCP servers that return large amounts of structured information, such as database queries, filesystem operations, or knowledge-base retrieval.

I am not sure whether this is intentional behavior or not, but it significantly affects multi-turn MCP workflows.

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Configure an MCP server that returns structured data (database, filesystem, search, etc.).
2. Start a new conversation.
3. Ask the model to retrieve information through the MCP tool.
4. Verify that:

   * The MCP tool is called successfully.
   * The tool returns data successfully.
   * The model generates a correct answer based on the tool output.
5. Ask a follow-up question that depends on details contained in the original MCP tool result.
6. Observe that the model appears to have access only to the assistant's previous response and not the original MCP output.

Example:

Turn 1:

User:
"List all projects."

Tool returns:

```json
[
  {"id":1,"name":"Project A"},
  {"id":2,"name":"Project B"}
]
```

Assistant:
"Projects are Project A and Project B."

Turn 2:

User:
"What is the ID of Project A?"

Expected behavior:
The model should still have access to the original MCP tool result.

Actual behavior:
The model appears to have lost access to the original tool output and can only rely on the previous assistant response.

### Expected Behavior

The conversation context should preserve MCP tool call messages and tool result messages across turns, or provide an option to do so.

This would allow the model to continue reasoning over previously retrieved MCP data instead of relying only on the assistant's summarized response.

If the current behavior is intentional for context-length optimization, it would be helpful to have a configurable option to retain MCP tool messages for agent-style workflows.

Based on the debug logs, this appears to be a frontend request deduplication issue caused by a missing dependency in the Cache Key (e.g., React Query/SWR queryKey). The frontend state manager likely caches the first search request using only the messageId or topicId, causing subsequent tool calls in the same message to be intercepted and served with the cached result of the first search. title: [Bug]: FileManager init crash on startup — ZodError "Name must not contain path separators" from cross-platform v1→v2 file migration
body:
### Issue Checklist

- [x] I understand that issues are for feedback and problem solving, not for complaining in the comment section, and will provide as much information as possible to help solve the problem.
- [x] My issue is not listed in the FAQ.
- [x] I've looked at pinned issues and searched existing Open/Closed Issues and Discussions, no similar issue was found.
- [x] I've filled in short, clear headings.
- [x] I've confirmed that I am using the latest version of Cherry Studio.

### Platform

macOS (the crash; the source data originated on Windows — see below)

### Version

2.0.0-dev (v2 branch / current `main`)

### Bug Description

On startup, the `FileManager` lifecycle service (`Phase.WhenReady`) fails to initialize with a `ZodError`. The lifecycle container logs `Continuing despite error in 'FileManager'`, so the app window still comes up, but **`FileManager` is dead for the whole session**: none of its `File_*` IPC handlers get registered (they are registered inside `onInit`), so every renderer-side file operation fails.

The trigger is a single `file_entry` row whose `name` column contains path separators. This happens when **v1 data created on Windows is synced/restored onto a macOS machine and then migrated to v2 there**.

Root cause is in `FileMigrator` (`src/main/data/migration/v2/migrators/FileMigrator.ts`). It derives the v2 `name` with Node's platform-default `path` module:

```ts
// toFileEntry()
name: path.basename(row.path, path.extname(row.path)) || row.name
```

On macOS, `node:path` is the POSIX variant and only treats `/` as a separator. Given a Windows path like `C:\Users\<USER>\AppData\Roaming\CherryStudio\Data\Files\<uuid>.png`:

- `path.extname(...)` returns `.png` (correct, it keys off the last dot)
- `path.basename(..., '.png')` finds no `/`, so it treats the **entire string** as the basename and only strips the `.png` suffix → the persisted `name` becomes `C:\Users\<USER>\...\Files\<uuid>` (directory never stripped, backslashes intact)

The same separator mismatch also breaks origin discrimination: `row.path.startsWith(path.join(userData, 'Data', 'Files'))` is `false` for the Windows path on macOS, so a file that was **internal** on Windows is mis-classified as **external** in v2.

`FileMigrator` bulk-inserts rows directly (`tx.insert(fileEntryTable).values(batch)`) and only validates `ext` via `SafeExtSchema` — it never validates `name`. So the malformed `name` lands in SQLite unchecked. The runtime read path is strict: `FileEntryService.rowToFileEntry()` runs `FileEntrySchema.parse()` (where `name: SafeNameSchema`), which rejects any `/` or `\`. Because `findMany()` does `rows.map(rowToFileEntry)`, a single un-parseable row throws and aborts the entire result set — which is what takes `FileManager.onInit` down.

The offending DB row (de-sensitized):

```json
{
  "id": "<uuid>",
  "origin": "external",
  "name": "C:\\Users\\<USER>\\AppData\\Roaming\\CherryStudio\\Data\\Files\\<uuid>",
  "ext": "png",
  "external_path": "C:\\Users\\<USER>\\AppData\\Roaming\\CherryStudio\\Data\\Files\\<uuid>.png",
  "deleted_at": null
}
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Have a v1 install on Windows that holds file metadata with Windows-style absolute paths (e.g. `C:\Users\<USER>\AppData\Roaming\CherryStudio\Data\Files\<uuid>.png`).
2. Sync / restore that v1 data onto a macOS machine.
3. Launch the v2 build on macOS and let the v1→v2 migration run.
4. `FileMigrator` persists a `file_entry` row whose `name` is the full Windows path (backslashes not stripped).
5. Restart the app. During `WhenReady`, `FileManager.onInit` → `danglingCache.initFromDb()` → `FileEntryService.findMany({ origin: 'external' })` → `rowToFileEntry` → `FileEntrySchema.parse` throws.
6. Observe `FileManager` initialization failure in the logs and broken file features for the rest of the session.

### Expected Behavior

- The v1→v2 file migration should derive `name` correctly regardless of the separator style of the source path (handle `\` even when migrating on a POSIX host), and should validate `name` before persisting (skip + warn on malformed rows, the same way it already handles malformed `ext`).
- A single un-parseable legacy row should not crash `FileManager` at boot. Bulk reads (`findMany` etc.) should skip + warn on rows that fail schema validation rather than aborting the whole result set and taking the service down. Point reads (`findById` / `getById`) may keep throwing for the specific requested id.

### Relevant Log Output

```shell
[error] Service 'FileManager' initialization failed: [
  {
    "code": "custom",
    "path": [ "name" ],
    "message": "Name must not contain path separators"
  }
]
ZodError: [
  {
    "code": "custom",
    "path": [ "name" ],
    "message": "Name must not contain path separators"
  }
]
    at rowToFileEntry (.../out/main/index.js)
    at Array.map (<anonymous>)
    at FileEntryServiceImpl.findMany (.../out/main/index.js)
    at async DanglingCacheImpl.initFromDb (.../out/main/index.js)
    at async FileManager.onInit (.../out/main/index.js)
    at async FileManager._doInit (.../out/main/index.js)
    at async LifecycleManager.initializeService (.../out/main/index.js)
    at async Promise.allSettled (index 5)
    at async LifecycleManager.startPhase (.../out/main/index.js)
    at async Application.bootstrap (.../out/main/index.js)
[warn] Continuing despite error in 'FileManager'
```

### Additional Context

Affected code:

- `src/main/data/migration/v2/migrators/FileMigrator.ts` — `toFileEntry()` derives `name` via POSIX `path.basename`/`path.extname` and does origin discrimination via `startsWith(path.join(...))`; both break on foreign-separator paths. Bulk insert validates `ext` only, not `name`.
- `src/main/data/services/FileEntryService.ts` — `rowToFileEntry()` / `findMany()` hard-fail the whole batch on one un-parseable row. (Note: `update()` and `setExternalPathAndName()` already `SafeNameSchema.parse` before writing, with a comment explaining that skipping it would "leave the row permanently un-parseable" — `FileMigrator` and `create()` lack the equivalent guard.)
- `src/shared/data/types/file/essential.ts` — `SafeNameSchema` (rejects path separators), the validator that fires.
- `src/main/services/file/danglingCache.ts` — `initFromDb()` is the startup caller that surfaces the crash.

For reference, the v2 runtime create path already parses separator-agnostically: `src/main/services/file/internal/entry/create.ts` uses `split(/[\\/]/)` in `defaultNameFromPath` / `extWithoutDot`, so it never produces this malformed `name`. The migrator is the only producer.

title: [Feature]: Gracefully Handle Cloud-Synced (iCloud) Backup Files That Need Downloading Before Restore
body:
## Background

Users who store backup files in iCloud Drive folders encounter two problems during restore: (1) They select the backup zip through the file picker, but the file is an iCloud placeholder that hasn't been downloaded locally. The app fails to read the file and silently re-shows the "Data Restore" dialog, asking the user to re-select — creating an infinite loop with no feedback. (2) When the iCloud download eventually completes in the background, the app attempts to extract the zip, but the extraction is incomplete (likely due to residual temp state from earlier failed attempts or reading the file before iCloud has fully flushed it). This triggers a misleading "Backup file format error" (ENOENT on a temp-extracted path), even though the backup file itself is valid — a subsequent manual restore succeeds.

## Goal

When a user selects a cloud-synced backup file that hasn't been downloaded locally, the app detects this state, triggers the download, shows progress, and automatically proceeds with restore once the file is fully ready — without requiring re-selection and without producing false "format error" messages.

## Spec

- After the user selects a backup file, the app checks whether the file is fully available locally before attempting to read or extract it.
- If the file is a cloud placeholder (e.g., iCloud, OneDrive, Google Drive file stream), the restore dialog transitions to a "Downloading backup file…" state with a progress indicator and a cancel button.
- Once the file is fully downloaded, restore proceeds automatically using the already-selected file path — the user is not asked to re-select.
- Before extracting, the app cleans up any residual temp extraction directories from prior attempts to avoid partial-state conflicts.
- If the download fails or the user cancels, the app shows a clear error message explaining that the file could not be downloaded, and returns to the file selection state.
- Error messages distinguish between actual format errors (invalid/corrupted zip) and file-access failures (incomplete download, ENOENT during extraction).

## Verification

- Place a backup zip in an iCloud Drive folder, ensure it shows the cloud download icon (not yet local). Select it for restore → app shows "Downloading…" with progress, then automatically starts the restore after download completes.
- During the download wait state, click Cancel → app returns to the restore dialog with the "Select Backup File" button, no error flash.
- Select a backup file that is already local (not cloud-synced) → restore starts immediately with no download step.
- Disconnect network while a cloud file is downloading for restore → app shows an error like "Download failed — check your network and try again" instead of silently looping or showing "Backup file format error".
- Trigger a failed restore attempt, then immediately retry with the same (now-downloaded) file → restore succeeds without "format error", confirming temp directory cleanup works.
- Feed a genuinely corrupted zip file → error message says "Backup file format error" (not "Download failed"), confirming error classification is correct.

title: [Feature]: Typing-Triggered Plan Mode Hint — plan / 计划 Surfaces a One-Click Enter
body:
## Background

Cherry Claw fully supports Claude Code's Plan Mode (`permission_mode: 'plan'` — agent plans the work without executing tools, asking the user to confirm the plan before any side effects). The capability is wired end-to-end: schema, settings builder, mid-session runtime toggle, and a composer launcher icon for selecting permission modes. But the entry point is **buried** — users have to discover the permission-mode submenu, recognize the Route icon, and read the description. In practice no one finds it. Meanwhile users frequently type things like "make a plan for…", "plan this refactor", "帮我规划一下", "先做个计划" without realizing Plan Mode exists. Codex shipped a typing-triggered floating hint — when the user types "plan", a small affordance offers "Use Plan Mode" with a Shift+Tab shortcut, and users now expect Cherry to nudge them the same way.

## Goal

When a user types planning-intent keywords in the Agent composer, Cherry surfaces a non-intrusive floating hint that one-click switches the current session into Plan Mode, so the capability is discovered at the moment of intent.

## Spec

- When the user types one of the trigger keywords as a standalone word in the composer (case-insensitive, word-boundary aware), a **floating hint** appears anchored above the composer input. Initial keyword set: English `plan`, `planning`, `make a plan`; Chinese `计划`, `规划`, `做个计划`, `先规划`. The set is centralized so it can be extended via locale files.
- The hint shows: a plan-icon, the label **Create plan**, a **Shift+Tab** shortcut chip, a primary button **Use Plan Mode**, and a dismiss **X**.
- Clicking **Use Plan Mode** switches the current Agent session's `permission_mode` to `plan` immediately (uses the existing runtime toggle), reflects the change in the composer's permission-mode launcher, and dismisses the hint. The user can continue typing without losing input.
- Pressing **Shift+Tab** while the hint is visible has the same effect as clicking the button. When the hint is **not** visible, Shift+Tab retains its current Composer behavior (prompt variable token navigation). The hint takes precedence only when actually shown.
- Clicking **X** dismisses the hint for the **current message draft only** — typing a fresh trigger in a future message re-shows it. Dismissed state does not persist across sessions; this is a transient discovery hint, not a permanent setting.
- The hint never appears when the session is **already in Plan Mode** — no redundant nudging.
- The hint appears at most **once per message draft**, even if the user types the trigger word multiple times or deletes-and-retypes. Once shown and either acted on or dismissed, it stays gone for the rest of that draft.
- The hint never appears for Cherry Assistant (which is not coding-oriented and has no Plan Mode semantics) — only for Cherry Claw and other Claude Code based agents.
- Visual styling matches the existing composer toast / popover language (`@cherrystudio/ui` primitives), positioned to never obscure the input the user is typing.

## Verification

- Open a Cherry Claw session in default permission mode, type "make a plan for refactoring the auth module" → as the word "plan" is completed, the floating hint appears above the composer with the four elements: plan icon, "Create plan" label, "Shift+Tab" chip, "Use Plan Mode" button, and X.
- Click "Use Plan Mode" → hint disappears → composer's permission-mode launcher now shows Plan Mode → send the message → agent behaves in plan mode (proposes a plan instead of executing).
- Type the same message again in a new draft → hint reappears (dismissal is per-draft, not per-session).
- Type "计划一下未来一周的工作" in Chinese → hint appears (Chinese trigger words work).
- With the hint visible, press Shift+Tab → equivalent to clicking the button (mode switches, hint dismisses, input not lost).
- Without the hint visible (no trigger word typed), press Shift+Tab → existing prompt variable token navigation behavior unchanged.
- Already in Plan Mode → typing "plan" → no hint appears.
- Type "plan" then delete it then retype it within the same draft → hint appears once total, not twice.
- Click X → hint dismisses → keep typing other words including "plan" again → hint stays dismissed for this draft → send and start a new draft → hint can reappear.
- In a Cherry Assistant session, type "make a plan" → no hint appears (Cherry Assistant has no Plan Mode).
- Hint positioning never covers the cursor position or the current line being typed; on a small window, hint repositions to stay visible without obscuring input.

title: Standardize pre-insert BO-schema validation across migrators and data services
body:
## Background

#15733 (fixed by #15737) exposed a systemic gap, not a one-off bug: **SQLite rows can be written without ever passing the validation that the read path will later apply.** Three independent incidents share this single root cause:

| Incident | Write path that let it in | Read path that detonated |
|---|---|---|
| #15733 — `name` with path separators | `FileMigrator` bulk insert (validated `ext` only) | `FileEntrySchema.parse` → killed `FileManager.onInit` |
| Whitespace-only knowledge base name | `KnowledgeMigrator` guard checked `name !== ''` | `KnowledgeBaseSchema` `name: trim().min(1)` → poisoned the whole list query |
| Note item with blank `source` | `transformKnowledgeItem` note branch had no source guard | `KnowledgeItemSchema` `source: trim().min(1)` → broke the item list for the base |

#15737 fixed these instances and added a pre-insert probe to `FileMigrator`, but the *mechanism* is still missing everywhere else.

## Current state (audited 2026-06)

**Migrators** — 14 migrator files, ~28 `tx.insert(...)` call sites, all bare inserts. Validation is hand-written per migrator (field guards, ad-hoc checks) and has historically drifted from the read schemas — that drift *is* the three incidents above. The only pre-insert BO-schema probe is the one #15737 added to `FileMigrator`.

**Data services (`src/main/data/services/`)** — write-side validation is inconsistent:

- `FileEntryService.update()` / `setExternalPathAndName()` parse `SafeNameSchema` **before** the SQL UPDATE, with a comment explaining why: otherwise the value "commits to SQLite first and only fails at `rowToFileEntry`'s schema parse — leaving the row permanently un-parseable".
- `FileEntryService.create()` has **no equivalent guard** (also noted in #15733). The post-insert read-back `parse` does throw, but by then the corrupted row is already persisted.
- Other services need an audit; most appear to rely on caller discipline plus read-time `parse`.

A "throwing read-back" is not a substitute for write-side validation: it fails fast for the caller but leaves the bad row in the database, where every later bulk read must skip it (post-#15737) or every point read throws.

## Why not a DB-row schema (e.g. drizzle-zod)

`createInsertSchema(table)` only expresses column types / nullability — exactly the layer already covered at compile time by `$inferInsert` assignability. Checked against the three real incidents above, a derived row schema blocks **none of them**: separator rules, `trim().min(1)`, and JSON-payload fields are all **BO-schema knowledge**. Hand-adding `.refine()` to a row schema would duplicate the BO rules and recreate the drift problem this issue exists to eliminate.

The single source of truth for "what is a valid row" already exists: the BO schemas (`FileEntrySchema`, `KnowledgeBaseSchema`, `KnowledgeItemSchema`, ...).

## Proposal: standardize the pre-insert probe

Enforce the invariant **write-side validation ≥ read-side validation** mechanically, at both write surfaces:

1. **Migrators**: provide a single insert-with-probe affordance on `BaseMigrator` (or an enforced convention at the end of `prepare()`): every prepared row is projected to BO shape and `BoSchema.safeParse`d before insert; failures degrade per-row (skip / sanitize + warning), never crash the migration. `FileMigrator` in #15737 is the reference implementation.
2. **Data services**: `create()` (and any remaining unguarded mutation) validates the would-be row against the BO schema (or the relevant field schemas) **before** the SQL statement, mirroring what `FileEntryService.update()` already does.

Supporting work:

- The `rowToXxx` projections are currently module-private per service; the probe needs them shared (or an equivalent BO-shape constructor) so migration and service layers validate against the same truth, not a copy.
- Knowledge schemas contain `.transform`s and a multi-state discriminated union — projection shapes need case-by-case verification.
- Audit every service in `src/main/data/services/` for unguarded write paths (a sweep similar to the one done for bulk-read crash surfaces in #15733 review).

## Known costs / risks

- Per-row `safeParse` on bulk migration batches: one-shot cost at migration time, acceptable; service writes are single-row and unnoticeable.
- Strict BO schemas (`z.strictObject`) make the probe double-sided: schema gaining a required field *and* row gaining an unknown field both fail loudly — desirable, but means schema evolutions surface in migration tests immediately.
- Scope is wide (14 migrators + service audit); should land incrementally, entity by entity, after the mechanism lands in `BaseMigrator`.

## References

- #15733 (incident), #15737 (instance fixes + reference probe implementation)
- `src/main/data/services/FileEntryService.ts` — `update()` pre-SQL validation comment; `create()` lacking the same
- `src/main/data/migration/v2/migrators/FileMigrator.ts` — reference pre-insert probe


---

## Pre-v2-release audit checklist

This is architectural design debt. **Before the v2 release, run every item below against each data module** (entity table + its service + its migrator). An item is checked when it holds for *all* modules — partial progress is tracked in the implementing PRs, not here.

- [ ] **1. Field rules are named atoms.** No single-field validation rule (`trim().min(1)`, regex, length caps, separator bans, ...) lives only inline inside an object schema.
  *Verify:* every inline rule in the entity's BO schema references a shared named schema (the `essential.ts` / `SafeNameSchema` pattern) that write sites can import.

- [ ] **2. BO schema composes atoms and owns cross-field invariants.** Object-level rules (e.g. `origin ⟺ externalPath ⟺ size`) are expressed in the BO schema (`strictObject`), not re-derived by callers.
  *Verify:* no migrator/service hand-copies a rule the BO schema already expresses.

- [ ] **3. Service write methods validate DO-level before SQL.** `create` validates the whole object (or all field atoms); `update` validates each provided field with its atom; correctness does not depend on any entry layer (DataApi DTO parse is protocol courtesy only).
  *Verify:* for each mutation method, a value rejected by the read path cannot reach the SQL statement.

- [ ] **4. Migrators probe before insert.** Every prepared row passes the read schema (projection + `safeParse`) before bulk insert; failures degrade per-row (skip / sanitize + warning), never crash the migration.
  *Verify:* no bare `tx.insert` on a path that skips the probe; a malformed-row fixture is skipped with a warning in tests.

- [ ] **5. CHECK-expressible rules are sunk into DDL.** The subset of domain rules SQLite CHECK can express (separator bans, non-blank, non-negative) exists as table constraints.
  *Verify:* inserting a violating row via raw SQL fails at the SQLite layer. Deadline: the pre-release `migrations/sqlite-drizzle` wipe-and-regenerate — CHECKs must be in the final initial migration.

- [ ] **6. Write/read symmetry is tested.** A test per entity asserts: data accepted by the write path parses on the read path.
  *Verify:* the test fails if a write guard is loosened below the read schema (this is the regression that caused all three #15733-class incidents).

- [ ] **7. Bulk reads isolate corrupted rows** *(applies only to services whose read path strict-parses — currently FileEntryService, FileRefService, KnowledgeBaseService, KnowledgeItemService)*. Collection queries exclude un-parseable rows with a warning carrying the row id; point reads and write-read-backs keep throwing.
  *Verify:* a raw-SQL-injected bad row does not break list queries or service init.

**Scope:** all entities under `src/main/data/db/schemas/` with their services (`src/main/data/services/`) and migrators (`src/main/data/migration/v2/`). Audit the four strict-parse services first — there a corrupted row breaks queries or whole services; elsewhere it currently only pollutes fields. Preference/BootConfig have their own generated validation pipeline: verify, don't rebuild.

### Release gate

This checklist is a **v2 release blocker**: every item must hold for every module, or carry an explicit per-module waiver recorded in this issue.

title: [Feature Request] Preserve scroll position when switching conversations
body:
> [\!NOTE]
> This issue was translated by Claude.

## Problem Description

In Cherry Studio, when users switch between multiple conversations, each switch forces a jump to the **top** of the target conversation. This is very inconvenient in long conversations—users often need to look back at context (such as previous code, tables, reference materials), and after switching away and back, they must scroll back to their original position.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open any long conversation (with many messages)
2. Scroll to the middle or bottom of the conversation
3. Switch to another conversation in the left conversation list
4. Switch back to the original conversation
5. **Expected**: Return to the original scroll position
6. **Actual**: Scroll position is reset to the top

## Expected Behavior

When switching conversations, **preserve the original conversation's scroll position** (similar to VSCode, WeChat, web browser tab behavior), or at least provide an option to toggle "preserve scroll position when switching conversations".

## Suggested Solution

- Record each conversation's `scrollTop` in the `ConversationList` / `Chat` component
- Read and restore the value when switching conversations
- Add a toggle in Settings → General: `Preserve scroll position when switching conversations` (enabled by default)

## Environment Information

- Operating System: Windows 11
- Cherry Studio Version: Latest stable version
- Trigger Scenario: All long conversations (especially noticeable with > 20 messages)

## Temporary Workarounds

- Use `Ctrl + End` to quickly jump to the end of the current conversation
- Minimize unnecessary conversation switching

## Impact Scope

Affects all users who frequently switch between multiple long conversations; this is a high-frequency UX issue.

The above content was generated using MiniMax 3 in Cherry Studio.

---

<summary>Original Content</summary>

## 问题描述
在 Cherry Studio 中，当用户在多个会话之间切换时，每次切换都会强制跳到目标会话的**顶部**。这在长对话中非常不便——用户经常需要回头查看上下文（如之前的代码、表格、参考资料），切走再切回后必须重新滚动到原来的位置。

## 复现步骤
1. 打开任意一个长对话（消息数较多）
2. 滚动到对话中段或底部
3. 在左侧会话列表切换到另一个会话
4. 再切回原会话
5. **预期**：回到原滚动位置
6. **实际**：滚动位置被重置到顶部

## 期望行为
切换会话时**保留原会话的滚动位置**（类似 VSCode、微信、网页浏览器的标签页行为），或至少提供"是否保留滚动位置"的开关选项。

## 建议方案
- 在 `ConversationList` / `Chat` 组件中记录每个会话的 `scrollTop`
- 切换会话时读取并恢复该值
- 可在「设置 → 通用」中添加开关：`切换会话时保持滚动位置`（默认开）

## 环境信息
- 操作系统：Windows 11
- Cherry Studio 版本：最新稳定版
- 触发场景：所有长对话（> 20 条消息尤其明显）

## 临时缓解
- 使用 `Ctrl + End` 快速跳到当前对话末尾
- 减少不必要的会话切换

## 影响范围
影响所有频繁在多个长对话间切换的用户，属于高频 UX 问题。

The Problem:
Currently, AI models often suffer from "temporal misalignment" due to their training data cutoffs. Many models still perceive the current date as 2024 or 2025. Without a consistent real-time reference point, the AI cannot accurately process time-sensitive information.

Key Benefits:

Resolving Temporal Conflicts: By injecting a system-level timestamp into the context, the AI can immediately recognize the current date/time, overriding outdated internal knowledge.
Enhanced Contextual Awareness: This allows the AI to track durations and intervals.
Example: For healthcare or habit tracking, the AI could say: "Today is the 10th day of your medication cycle. How are you feeling today?" instead of just treating each prompt as a static event.
Improved Longitudinal Tracking: It helps the AI understand the "time span" between different user queries in the same session.

title: [Bug]: Jina AI embeddings fail with ZodError (missing usage.prompt_tokens in OpenAI Compatible provider)
body:
### Issue Checklist

- [x] I understand that issues are for feedback and problem solving, not for complaining in the comment section, and will provide as much information as possible to help solve the problem.
- [x] My issue is not listed in the [FAQ](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/issues/3881).
- [x] I've looked at **pinned issues** and searched for existing [Open Issues](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/issues), [Closed Issues](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20state%3Aclosed), and [Discussions](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/discussions), no similar issue or discussion was found.
- [x] I've filled in short, clear headings so that developers can quickly identify a rough idea of what to expect when flipping through the list of issues. And not "a suggestion", "stuck", etc.
- [x] I've confirmed that I am using the latest version of Cherry Studio.

### Platform

Windows

### Version

v1.9.11

### Bug Description

When configuring Jina AI as an "OpenAI Compatible" custom provider for embeddings, the health check and the embedding generation fail with an `AI_TypeValidationError` (ZodError).
The Jina AI API correctly processes the request and returns the embedding array. However, Jina's API response omits the `prompt_tokens` field inside the `usage` object, returning only `total_tokens`. 
Cherry Studio strictly expects `prompt_tokens` to be a number. Because it is missing, Zod throws a validation error and the app discards the perfectly valid embedding data, showing an "Invalid JSON response" error.

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Go to Settings > Model Provider
2. Choose JinaAi and set the api key.
3. Add an embedding model like `jina-embeddings-v5-omni-nano` or `jina-embeddings-v5-text-small` (NOT 
jina-ai/jina-embeddings-v5-omni-small)
4. Click on the "Health Check" button for the model (or try to embed a document in the Knowledge Base).
5. See the error "Invalid JSON response".

### Expected Behavior

Cherry Studio should tolerate the absence of `prompt_tokens` in the `usage` object for embedding responses, or default it to the value of `total_tokens`. Making `prompt_tokens` optional in the Zod schema for `OpenAICompatibleEmbeddingModel` would instantly fix compatibility with Jina AI and other alternative providers.

### Relevant Log Output

```shell
Error cause: {
  "name": "AI_TypeValidationError",
  "cause": {
    "name": "ZodError",
    "message": "[\n  {\n    \"expected\": \"number\",\n    \"code\": \"invalid_type\",\n    \"path\": [\n      \"usage\",\n      \"prompt_tokens\"\n    ],\n    \"message\": \"Invalid input\"\n  }\n]"
  },
  "value": {
    "model": "jina-embeddings-v5-text-small",
    "object": "list",
    "usage": {
      "total_tokens": 3
    },
    "data": [
      {
        "object": "embedding",
        "index": 0,
        "embedding": [ 0.00550978, -0.09516474, ... ]
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

### Additional Context

According to the official Jina AI schema, their embedding endpoints can return a `BaseUsage` object which only requires `total_tokens`:
https://api.jina.ai/openapi.json
This is a very quick fix (likely just adding `.optional()` to the Zod schema for the usage object) but it entirely blocks the use of Jina's embedding models.

title: [Feature]: Agent–MCP Reference Integrity — Cascade Cleanup, Connection Backoff, and Schema Parity with Assistants
body:
## Background

In v2, agents store MCP references as a JSON array on the agent row (`agent.mcps`), with no foreign-key constraint to the `mcp_server` table. Assistants in v2 already use the correct relational pattern — a junction table `assistant_mcp_server` with `ON DELETE CASCADE` — but agents were not refactored alongside. The consequence: when a user globally deletes an MCP server, every agent that referenced it keeps a zombie ID. On the next agent session start, settings builder logs errors for the missing MCP but continues; the MCP runtime then attempts ping/reconnect without exponential backoff. A real user (張冠湘 via support, 1.9.9) reported 9,000+ retry exceptions in a single day and severe agent-module lag — the same architectural gap exists unchanged in current v2 code.

## Goal

Agents and Assistants share the same MCP relational model; deleting an MCP globally automatically cleans up all references; connection failures use exponential backoff so a single broken MCP never produces thousands of retries.

## Spec

- Migrate `agent.mcps` from a JSON array column to a junction table (e.g. `agent_mcp_server`) with `ON DELETE CASCADE`, mirroring `assistant_mcp_server`.
- Deleting an MCP server globally atomically removes all agent AND assistant references via the join tables.
- MCPs marked `isActive: false` are skipped at session start — no connection attempt, no log noise.
- MCP connection attempts use exponential backoff: 1s, 2s, 4s, 8s, 16s, then give up for that session. After give-up, no further connection attempts until user manual retry or session restart.
- On agent open, any reference to a non-existent MCP ID is silently cleaned from the join table (defensive heal for legacy / migrated data).
- The agent's MCP status panel shows per-MCP state: **Connected / Connecting / Backing off (with next retry time) / Failed (with reason and manual retry button) / Disabled**.

## Verification

- Create an agent with 3 MCP servers attached → all 3 connect → status panel shows green.
- Delete one MCP globally → that MCP disappears from the agent's MCP list immediately (cascade) → other 2 stay connected.
- Mark an MCP `isActive: false` → no connection attempt in logs → status panel shows Disabled.
- Kill a running MCP's process → retry at 1s, 2s, 4s, 8s, 16s in logs → after 5 attempts stop → status panel shows Failed with reason and manual retry button → no further connection attempts in logs.
- Plant a zombie MCP ID in legacy join-table data, open the agent → agent opens cleanly with no retry storm; the zombie reference is gone from the join table.
- With 10 agents × 5 MCPs, opening the agent module completes within 2s; no retry storm visible in logs.

title: [Feature]: Prompt Cache Hit-Rate for MCP-Heavy Conversations — Stable Breakpoints, Tool Schema Stability, and Cache Observability
body:
## Background

Cherry implements Anthropic prompt caching via `cache_control: ephemeral` markers, but the feature is **off by default** — users must manually enable `cacheControl.enabled: true` and set a `tokenThreshold` in provider settings. When MCP tools are added to a conversation, three forces work against the cache: (1) MCP tool schemas are re-fetched from live servers on every request (`syncMcpToolsToRegistry`), so any schema drift busts the cache prefix; (2) the system prompt's deferred-tool namespace listing regenerates each turn — the code itself carries a `// FIXME： maybe break cache` comment acknowledging this; (3) cache hit/write tokens are tracked internally but folded into `promptTokens` for display, so users have no visibility — a code comment explicitly states "users can't see cache hit-rate or audit premium-rate cache writes." A real user (Refraction Hikari via support) reports a 30-40% hit rate with MCP enabled — and the current code behavior matches that number exactly. For heavy MCP users, this means paying full prompt cost every turn while believing cache is working.

## Goal

Prompt cache works correctly out-of-the-box for users with MCP tools enabled; cache hit rate is visible in the UI; users can identify which MCPs are cache-hostile and act on the information.

## Spec

- Anthropic prompt caching is **on by default** with sensible thresholds — system prompt always cached when above N tokens; last 2 user/assistant messages cached. User can adjust or disable, but should not need to enable it manually.
- MCP tool schemas are **cached per-session** rather than re-fetched per-request. A schema fetch happens once at session start and on explicit MCP config change events; not on every model call.
- The system prompt's deferred-tool namespace section is **byte-stable for a given tool set** — same tools enabled → identical bytes across turns. Changes only when tools are actually added or removed (not when message stream grows).
- Cache hit/write tokens are **first-class fields** in `MessageStats` (separate from `promptTokens`). Per-message indicator shows `cache_read / cache_write / no_cache` breakdown; per-conversation header shows aggregate hit rate; per-session stats panel shows cumulative input tokens saved via cache.
- MCP settings page surfaces a per-MCP "cache impact" indicator (e.g. "stable" / "occasionally invalidates" / "rebuilds every turn") so users can identify cache-hostile servers.
- The existing `// FIXME： maybe break cache` and `// TODO: use context manager replace middleware` markers in the codebase are resolved as part of this work.

## Verification

- Fresh install, no manual cache config → start a Claude Sonnet conversation, run 5+ turns of normal chat → `cache_read_tokens` grows turn-over-turn; UI shows hit rate ≥ 70%.
- Add an MCP tool to the same conversation, run 5+ more turns → cache hit rate stays ≥ 60% (small overhead from tool definitions, but nothing like 30-40%).
- Compare a conversation with caching enabled vs disabled → stats panel shows a clear input-token savings number.
- Change an MCP server's configuration mid-conversation → next request invalidates only that MCP's cache; subsequent requests re-stabilize.
- Inspect Anthropic API responses in a debug view → both `cache_read_input_tokens` and `cache_creation_input_tokens` are surfaced as separate UI fields, not collapsed into `promptTokens`.
- In MCP settings, identify a known cache-hostile MCP (e.g. one with dynamically generated tool descriptions) → its row shows the "rebuilds every turn" indicator; switch to a stable MCP and the indicator changes to "stable".

title: [Feature]: Per-Channel Message Policy — Sender / Mention / Chat-Type Gating Before Agent Invocation
body:
## Background

Cherry's IM channel adapters (Feishu, WeChat, Slack, Discord, Telegram, QQ) currently forward **every** received message to the agent as a user-message event — there is no policy layer between adapter and agent. The only "filter" available to users is to write rules into the agent's SOUL.md / system prompt (e.g. "only reply to person X in this group"), but prompt-based rules are soft constraints: the LLM follows them probabilistically and routinely violates them, especially under long context or after multiple turns. Code confirms the gap: `FeishuAdapter.ts` defines `chat_type`, `mentions`, and `sender` in the event type but uses none of them for filtering — `sender.open_id` is only read for downstream routing. Real users report that detailed SOUL.md rules with concrete open_ids ("never auto-post to groups", "only reply when person X @-mentions me") still fail to stop the agent from replying. Workarounds today require putting a custom event proxy in front of Cherry (e.g. piping `lark-cli event consume` through a Python filter), which most users can't do.

## Goal

Channel adapters apply a user-configured filter policy **before** invoking the agent. Messages that don't pass the policy are silently dropped — they never reach the LLM. Filtering becomes a hard guarantee, not LLM hope.

## Spec

- `AgentChannel.config` gains an optional `filter` section with these fields:
  - `allowedSenders` / `deniedSenders` — sender open_id (or platform-equivalent ID) whitelist / blacklist
  - `requireMention` — boolean; when true, only messages that @-mention the bot pass through
  - `allowedChatTypes` — subset of `["p2p", "group", "channel"]`; empty = all allowed
  - `allowedChatIds` / `deniedChatIds` — specific chat whitelist / blacklist by platform chat ID
- Policy is evaluated **before** the adapter wraps the message as an agent user-event. Failed-policy messages produce no LLM call, no agent state change, no message record.
- All six channel adapters (Feishu, WeChat, Slack, Discord, Telegram, QQ) implement the same policy schema consistently — same field semantics across platforms (with per-platform ID mapping handled inside the adapter).
- Cherry Settings shows a "Message Policy" section under each channel config. Empty filter = allow all (backwards compatible — no behavior change for existing channels).
- Allowlist values can be entered as user-friendly identifiers (name search) and resolve to platform IDs at save time, so users don't have to copy-paste open_ids manually.
- A counter "messages dropped by policy" is exposed per channel for observability, without spamming logs by default.
- Policy edits take effect on the next incoming message; no channel restart required.

## Verification

- Configure a Feishu channel with `allowedSenders=[Alice]`, `requireMention=true`, `allowedChatTypes=["group"]`. Test:
  - Alice @ bot in target group → agent invoked, replies normally
  - Alice in target group without @ → silent drop, no agent invocation, no token cost
  - Alice DMs bot → silent drop (chat_type mismatch)
  - Bob @ bot in target group → silent drop (sender mismatch)
  - Anyone posts in group without @ → silent drop
- Empty filter (default) → all messages pass through; behavior identical to today.
- Configure WeChat channel with `deniedSenders=[spam-bot-id]` → spam-bot messages silent drop; all other users pass through.
- Edit policy in UI (e.g. add a new allowed sender) → next message from that sender immediately passes; no channel restart needed.
- The channel stats panel shows "N messages dropped by policy this hour" growing as drops happen.
- Verify via debug log / token usage that dropped messages produce zero LLM calls and zero stored message records.
- Same set of scenarios reproduced on Slack and Telegram → identical behavior to Feishu.

## Related

title: [Bug]: DeepSeek V4 reasoning_effort is dropped for custom OpenAI-compatible providers
body:
### Issue Checklist

- [x] I understand that issues are for feedback and problem solving, not for complaining in the comment section, and will provide as much information as possible to help solve the problem.
- [x] My issue is not listed in the FAQ.
- [x] I've looked at pinned issues and searched existing issues/discussions; I did not find this exact custom API / openai-compatible DeepSeek V4 reasoning_effort case.
- [x] I've filled in a short, clear heading.
- [x] I've confirmed that I am using the latest version of Cherry Studio.

### Platform

Linux amd64

### Version

v1.9.11

### Bug Description

When using a custom API / OpenAI-compatible provider with a DeepSeek V4+ model such as `deepseek-v4-pro`, Cherry Studio shows the reasoning effort selector correctly. However, selecting `high` or `xhigh` does not send the corresponding reasoning effort parameter to the backend.

Observed request body on the backend:

```json
{
  "model": "deepseek-v4-pro",
  "max_tokens": 32000,
  "thinking": { "type": "enabled" },
  "has_tools": true,
  "tool_choice": "auto",
  "stream": true,
  "stream_options": { "include_usage": true }
}
```

The selected reasoning effort is missing from the payload.

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Add a custom API provider that uses the OpenAI-compatible endpoint type.
2. Add/select a DeepSeek V4+ model, for example `deepseek-v4-pro`.
3. Select a reasoning effort such as `high` or `xhigh` in the chat UI.
4. Send a message and inspect the backend request body.

### Expected Behavior

For DeepSeek V4+ models used through custom OpenAI-compatible providers:

- `high` should be forwarded as a reasoning effort value.
- `xhigh` should map to DeepSeek's max effort value.
- The generated request should not silently drop the effort parameter.

For example, the request should include a DeepSeek V4 reasoning effort control such as `reasoning_effort: "high"` or `reasoning_effort: "max"`, depending on the selected UI effort and provider adapter behavior.

### Relevant Log Output

```shell
No application error log is emitted. The issue is visible from the backend request payload: `thinking` is sent, but the selected reasoning effort parameter is missing.
```

### Additional Context

v1.9.11 already includes the DeepSeek provider patch that forwards `reasoning_effort` for `@ai-sdk/deepseek@2.0.30`.

The issue seems specific to the custom API / `openai-compatible` path. In `getReasoningEffort()`, the DeepSeek V4+ branch returns snake_case `reasoning_effort`:

```ts
return {
  thinking: { type: 'enabled' as const },
  reasoning_effort: reasoningEffort === 'xhigh' ? 'max' : 'high'
}
```

But `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible` drops/overwrites snake_case `reasoning_effort`; Cherry already has logic in `buildProviderOptions()` to convert user custom parameters from `reasoning_effort` to `reasoningEffort` for openai-compatible providers. That conversion appears to only apply to user custom parameters, not to the automatically generated reasoning params from `getReasoningEffort()`.

A possible fix would be to convert the generated DeepSeek V4+ `reasoning_effort` to `reasoningEffort` when the actual AI SDK provider key is `openai-compatible`, or make the DeepSeek V4+ openai-compatible branch emit `reasoningEffort` directly.

Related context:

- #14551 added DeepSeek V4+ model support and reasoning effort UI.
- #14572 fixed forwarding for the official DeepSeek/Claude-compatible paths.
- This report is about the remaining custom API / OpenAI-compatible path in v1.9.11.

title: @cherrystudio/ai-core CJS/type exports point to missing dist files

## Summary

`@cherrystudio/ai-core@2.0.1` publishes CommonJS/default/react-native/type entrypoints that point to `.js` and `.d.ts` files missing from the npm package.

ESM imports work because the `.mjs` files are present, but CommonJS consumers and TypeScript declaration resolution through the advertised `types` targets are broken.

## Reproduction

```sh
tmp="$(mktemp -d)"
cd "$tmp"
npm init -y >/dev/null
npm install --ignore-scripts @cherrystudio/ai-core@2.0.1

node - <<'NODE'
const fs = require('node:fs');
const path = require('node:path');
const root = path.join(process.cwd(), 'node_modules/@cherrystudio/ai-core');
const pkg = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(path.join(root, 'package.json'), 'utf8'));

console.log(pkg.exports);
for (const file of [
  'dist/index.js',
  'dist/index.mjs',
  'dist/index.d.ts',
  'dist/provider/index.js',
  'dist/provider/index.mjs',
  'dist/built-in/plugins/index.js',
  'dist/built-in/plugins/index.mjs',
]) {
  console.log(file, fs.existsSync(path.join(root, file)));
}
NODE

node -e "require('@cherrystudio/ai-core')"
```

## Actual behavior

The package includes `.mjs` files, but not the `.js` or `.d.ts` files referenced by `main`, `types`, `react-native`, `require`, and `default`.

For the root entrypoint, `require('@cherrystudio/ai-core')` fails with:

```text
MODULE_NOT_FOUND
Cannot find module '.../node_modules/@cherrystudio/ai-core/dist/index.js'
```

## Expected behavior

All exported conditions should point to files included in the package. Either emit the `.js`/`.d.ts` artifacts, or update package metadata to match the `.mjs`-only output.

## Notes

The current `packages/aiCore/package.json` on `main` still points CJS/default/react-native/types targets at `dist/*.js` and `dist/*.d.ts`, while the published package contains the corresponding `.mjs` files only.

Environment used to reproduce: macOS, Node v24.10.0, npm 11.6.0.

title: Inject model identity into default system prompt for assistant chat
body:
## Background

When users ask a model "what model are you?" in the regular assistant chat mode, the model often responds with incorrect information (e.g., a GPT-5 model claiming to be GPT-4). This leads users to suspect the model is being misrepresented.

The root cause: **Agent mode** (via Claude Agent SDK preset) automatically includes model/environment identity in its system prompt, so the model can correctly self-identify. However, **regular assistant chat mode** does not inject model identity into the system prompt by default.

The codebase already supports a `{{model_name}}` template variable in `prompt.ts`, but the default assistant prompt does not use it — so models have no way to know their own identity unless the user manually configures the template.

## Goal

Ensure all assistant chat conversations automatically include model identity information, so models can correctly self-identify when asked — without requiring users to manually configure template variables.

## Proposed Solution

In `parameterBuilder.ts` (around line 281), when assembling the system prompt, always append a model identity line regardless of whether the user's prompt template includes `{{model_name}}`:

```
You are powered by ${model.name}.
```

This is a minimal, non-intrusive change that:
- Fixes the self-identification issue for all users by default
- Doesn't break existing custom prompts
- Aligns assistant chat behavior with Agent mode
- Prevents user confusion about model authenticity

## Verification

1. Create a new default assistant chat with any model (e.g., GPT-5, Claude Sonnet)
2. Ask "What model are you?"
3. The model should correctly identify itself based on the configured model name
