title: Upgrade eslint-plugin-react-hooks (5.2.0 → 7.x): recognize useEffectEvent and adopt React Compiler rules
body:
## Summary

`eslint-plugin-react-hooks` is pinned at `^5.2.0`, whose `exhaustive-deps` rule does not recognize `useEffectEvent`. As a result, any Effect Event — which by React's contract MUST be excluded from a `useEffect` dependency array — is reported as a "missing dependency" false positive.

Observed in #15831, where `ResourceSelectorShell.tsx` uses `useEffectEvent` to fire `onOpen` without making the effect reactive:

```
261:6  warning  React Hook useEffect has a missing dependency: 'handleOpen'. Either include it or remove the dependency array  react-hooks/exhaustive-deps
```

## Root cause

In `eslint-plugin-react-hooks@5.2.0`, the `exhaustive-deps` rule's Effect Event detector is hard-stubbed to disable the feature:

```js
// node_modules/eslint-plugin-react-hooks/cjs/eslint-plugin-react-hooks.development.js
function isUseEffectEventIdentifier(node) {
    return false;
}
```

So the rule never registers `useEffectEvent(...)` return values as Effect Events, treats them as ordinary reactive values, and demands they be added to deps. Effect Event awareness only ships from the v6 line onward.

## Current workaround

A line-local suppression, matching the existing precedent at `src/renderer/pages/home/Inputbar/Inputbar.tsx:213`:

```ts
useEffect(() => {
  if (open) handleOpen()
  // eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps
}, [open])
```

This is a band-aid, not a fix.

## Breaking changes on the upgrade path

Upgrading to a version that recognizes `useEffectEvent` (6.x / 7.x) is NOT a drop-in bump. Spiking `7.1.1` (current latest) surfaced a chain of issues, each with a known fix:

1. **Load failure** — 7.x pulls in `zod-validation-error` and imports its `./v4` subpath; the version resolved in this workspace (`3.5.4`) only exports `./v3`, so ESLint crashes with `ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED`. Fix: a `pnpm.overrides` bump of `zod-validation-error` to `^4`.
2. **Config format change** — `reactHooks.configs['recommended-latest']` becomes a legacy eslintrc-style object (`plugins: ["react-hooks"]`), which flat config rejects. Fix: switch to `reactHooks.configs.flat['recommended-latest']`.

## Full-repo impact (measured)

Full-repo `eslint` run, 5.2.0 baseline vs 7.1.1 with `recommended-latest`:

| | 5.2.0 (baseline) | 7.1.1 (`recommended-latest`) |
|---|---|---|
| `react-hooks/*` errors | 0 | **347** |
| `react-hooks/*` warnings | 14 | 25 |
| files affected | 13 | **198** |

The 347 new errors come from the React Compiler rule set that `recommended-latest` enables:

| rule | errors |
|---|---|
| `set-state-in-effect` | 150 |
| `refs` | 127 |
| `immutability` | 26 |
| `preserve-manual-memoization` | 18 |
| `globals` | 9 |
| `static-components` | 7 |
| `set-state-in-render` | 6 |
| `use-memo` / `purity` | 2 each |

**These are signal, not noise.** The compiler rules are not false positives — they flag genuine latent issues (effects that trigger cascading re-renders, mutations of props/state, components recreated on every render, ...) that have accumulated unnoticed because no rule was watching for them. The 347 count is as much a map of unreviewed tech debt worth surfacing as it is a migration cost.

**The `useEffectEvent` false positive itself is trivially resolved by the upgrade:** `exhaustive-deps` goes 14 → 13, and the single removed entry is exactly `ResourceSelectorShell.tsx:261` (the `handleOpen` warning). Zero `exhaustive-deps` regressions were introduced.

## Two resolution paths

- **Path A — wholesale React Compiler onboarding.** Adopt `recommended-latest`. Resolves the false positive *and* surfaces the 347 latent issues across 198 files for review and fixing (`set-state-in-effect`, `immutability`, `purity`, ... each warrant case-by-case attention). A standalone, large — and arguably valuable — migration project; it should not be bundled with feature work.
- **Path B — minimal upgrade.** Upgrade to 6.x / 7.x but enable only `rules-of-hooks` + `exhaustive-deps`, leaving the compiler rules off (for now). Resolves the false positive at **code-fix effort ≈ 0** (`exhaustive-deps` nets −1, `rules-of-hooks` stays 0). Cost is config-only: dependency bump + `zod-validation-error` override + flat config entry switch. The compiler rules can then be enabled incrementally, one at a time, each as its own cleanup PR.

## Proposed next steps

- [ ] Decide between Path A (adopt everything now) and Path B (minimal upgrade now, enable compiler rules incrementally).
- [ ] Either path retires every `useEffectEvent` `eslint-disable` workaround (Inputbar + ResourceSelectorShell).
- [ ] For the compiler rules, triage per rule (`set-state-in-effect`, `refs`, ... ) and land fixes as dedicated PRs — these are real issues, not lint noise.
- [ ] Until the upgrade lands, use line-local `eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps` for `useEffectEvent` false positives (see the Inputbar precedent above).

Related: #15831

title: [Bug]: DeepSeek V4+ reasoning_effort dropped for OpenAI-compatible providers on main (forward-port of #15824)
body:
### Issue Checklist

- [x] I understand that issues are for feedback and problem solving, not for complaining in the comment section, and will provide as much information as possible to help solve the problem.
- [x] My issue is not listed in the FAQ.
- [x] I've looked at pinned issues and searched existing Open/Closed Issues and Discussions; no similar issue was found.
- [x] I've filled in a short, clear heading.
- [x] I've confirmed that I am reporting against the latest `main`.

### Platform

Linux

### Version

`main` (post-v2 merge, active development branch)

### Bug Description

Forward-port of #15824 to `main`. The same defect exists on `main`: for a custom OpenAI-compatible provider hosting a DeepSeek V4+ model (e.g. `deepseek-v4-pro`), selecting reasoning effort `high` or `xhigh` does not reach the backend — the effort is silently dropped from the request body.

Root cause on `main` (reasoning logic moved to the main process during the v2 refactor):

- `getReasoningEffort` in `src/main/ai/utils/reasoning.ts` is the **generic (openai-compatible) builder** (per its own header comment "only for generic provider"). Its `isDeepSeekV4PlusModel` branch still returns **snake_case-only** `reasoning_effort`.
- `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible` overwrites snake_case `reasoning_effort` to `undefined` (it only honors camelCase `reasoningEffort`, which it re-serializes back to `reasoning_effort` in the body), so the effort is dropped.
- The official `deepseek` provider uses the dedicated `@ai-sdk/deepseek` serializer (snake_case only), but in `src/main/ai/utils/options.ts` its dispatch (`case 'deepseek'`) falls through to `openai-compatible`/`default` → `buildGenericProviderOptions` → `getReasoningEffort`. So a provider with a special SDK reuses the generic builder.

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Build/run `main`.
2. Add a custom provider using the OpenAI-compatible endpoint type.
3. Add/select a DeepSeek V4+ model, e.g. `deepseek-v4-pro`.
4. Select reasoning effort `high` or `xhigh` in the chat UI.
5. Send a message and inspect the outgoing request body — `thinking: { type: "enabled" }` is present, but `reasoning_effort` is missing.

### Expected Behavior

- `high` is forwarded as `reasoning_effort: "high"`; `xhigh` maps to `reasoning_effort: "max"`.
- The effort is sent on both the official `deepseek` provider path and the custom OpenAI-compatible path.
- The effort parameter is never silently dropped.

### Relevant Log Output

```shell
No application error log is emitted. The issue is visible only from the outgoing request body: `thinking` is sent, but `reasoning_effort` is missing.
```

### Additional Context

This issue tracks doing the fix **more thoroughly on `main`** than the v1 stopgap.

**v1 stopgap (PR #15834):** the `deepseek_v4` branch emits BOTH `reasoning_effort` (snake, for `@ai-sdk/deepseek`) and `reasoningEffort` (camel, for `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible`). It works because the two keys never conflict, but it is a workaround — minimal/regression-safe was the goal on the frozen v1 line.

**Proposed thorough fix on `main`:** `main` already has per-provider reasoning builders — `getOpenAIReasoningParams` / `getAnthropicReasoningParams` / `getGeminiReasoningParams` / `getXAIReasoningParams` / `getBedrockReasoningParams` / `getOllamaReasoningParams` — but **no `getDeepSeekReasoningParams`**. The official `deepseek` provider should not reuse the generic builder.

1. Add `getDeepSeekReasoningParams(assistant, model)` in `src/main/ai/utils/reasoning.ts`, returning snake_case `reasoning_effort` (`high` | `max`) + `thinking` for the official `@ai-sdk/deepseek` serializer.
2. Give `deepseek` its own dispatch in `src/main/ai/utils/options.ts` (e.g. `buildDeepSeekProviderOptions`) instead of falling through to `buildGenericProviderOptions`.
3. Collapse the `deepseek_v4` branch inside `getReasoningEffort` to **camelCase `reasoningEffort` only**, since that function is the generic/openai-compatible builder. This removes the dual-emit.
4. Port the regression tests from PR #15834 and add coverage for the new `getDeepSeekReasoningParams`.

Note: on `main`, `getReasoningEffort` already receives `provider` as a third argument (`getReasoningEffort(assistant, model, provider)`), which makes the dispatch split cleaner.

Related: #15824 (original report), #15834 (v1 stopgap), #14551 (DeepSeek V4+ support), #14572 (official DeepSeek/Claude-compatible forwarding).

## Security Risk

CherryClaw's channel credentials (Telegram bot_token, QQ app_id/client_secret, etc.) are stored in **plaintext** in the `channels` table of `agents.db`.

Any process that can access `%AppData%\\CherryStudio\\Data\\agents.db` (malware, third-party scripts, MCP services) can obtain all channel credentials.

title: [Feature] Native PPTX/DOCX Parsing Support
body:
## Background

Users frequently need to upload PPTX and DOCX files for AI-assisted analysis, but the current document processing pipeline only handles PDF and plain text formats. This forces users to manually convert their Office files to PDF before uploading, adding unnecessary friction — especially for slide decks where conversion can lose formatting and speaker notes.

## Goal

Support native parsing of binary Microsoft Office formats (PPTX, DOCX) in the document upload pipeline, so users can directly upload these files without manual conversion.

## Specification

- Add PPTX and DOCX to the accepted file type list in the upload dialog
- Implement server-side parsing for:
  - **DOCX**: Extract text content, headings, tables, and embedded images
  - **PPTX**: Extract slide text, speaker notes, tables, and embedded images (per-slide)
- Integrate parsing output into the existing document chunk pipeline used by Agent and knowledge base (OpenClaw)
- Maintain the same chunking and indexing behavior as PDF documents
- Display a preview or structured outline of the parsed content in the UI

## Verification

- [ ] Upload a multi-slide PPTX file → content is correctly extracted and available for AI Q&A
- [ ] Upload a DOCX file with headings, tables, and images → text and structure are preserved
- [ ] Verify parsed content appears correctly in Agent context and OpenClaw knowledge base
- [ ] Confirm no regression in existing PDF/TXT upload flows

title: [Feature] Optional Web Search Links in Export
body:
## Background

When users export chat conversations to PDF or DOCX, web search reference links are included inline, cluttering the exported document. For users who share exported chats as reports or documentation, these reference URLs add visual noise and make the output less professional.

## Goal

Provide a toggle during chat export that lets users choose whether to include or exclude web search reference links in the exported file.

## Specification

- Add a checkbox option in the export dialog: **"Include web search references"** (default: checked, preserving current behavior)
- When unchecked:
  - Strip all web search citation markers (e.g., `[1]`, `[2]`) from the exported text
  - Remove the "References" / "Sources" footer section containing the URLs
- Apply to all export formats: PDF, DOCX, and Markdown
- The toggle should only appear when the conversation actually contains web search results
- The in-app chat view is not affected — links remain visible in the UI regardless of the export setting

## Verification

- [ ] Export a conversation with web search results with the toggle ON → links and citations are present
- [ ] Export the same conversation with the toggle OFF → no citation markers or reference URLs in output
- [ ] Verify the toggle does not appear for conversations without web search content
- [ ] Test across PDF, DOCX, and Markdown export formats

title: [Feature] Agent Skill Delete and Disable
body:
## Background

Currently, Agent Skills can only be added but not removed or temporarily disabled. As users iterate on their agent configurations, they accumulate skills that are no longer needed or that interfere with each other. Without a way to disable or delete skills, users must recreate their agents from scratch to clean up the skill list.

## Goal

Allow users to delete or temporarily disable individual skills on an Agent, giving full lifecycle control over the skill configuration.

## Specification

- **Delete**: Add a delete action (trash icon or context menu) on each skill entry in the Agent skill list
  - Show a confirmation dialog before deletion
  - Deleting a skill removes it from the agent's configuration permanently
- **Disable/Enable**: Add a toggle switch on each skill entry
  - Disabled skills remain in the list (visually dimmed) but are not included in the agent's active toolset
  - Disabled skills are skipped during agent execution — the model does not see them in its tool list
- Skill ordering should be preserved when toggling enable/disable
- Both actions should be available in the Agent edit panel's Skills section

## Verification

- [ ] Add 3 skills to an agent → disable one → agent execution only uses the 2 active skills
- [ ] Re-enable the disabled skill → agent can use all 3 again
- [ ] Delete a skill → it is permanently removed from the agent's skill list
- [ ] Confirm deletion dialog appears before permanent deletion
- [ ] Verify no orphaned skill references remain after deletion

title: [Feature] Per-Model Web Search and Reasoning Effort Persistence
body:
## Background

When users switch between models in a chat session, the web search toggle and reasoning effort settings reset to defaults. This is frustrating for users who maintain different preferences per model — for example, enabling web search for a general-purpose model but disabling it for a coding model, or setting high reasoning effort for complex tasks but low effort for quick Q&A models.

## Goal

Persist web search and reasoning effort settings on a per-model basis, so switching models automatically restores that model's last-used configuration.

## Specification

- Store the following settings per model (keyed by model ID):
  - **Web search**: on/off
  - **Reasoning effort**: low / medium / high (for models that support it)
- When the user changes either setting while a model is selected, save it to that model's stored preferences
- When the user switches to a different model, restore that model's saved preferences (or use sensible defaults if no preference has been saved yet)
- Default behavior for models without saved preferences:
  - Web search: off
  - Reasoning effort: medium (or the model's default if specified)
- Settings are persisted locally and included in the data backup/restore flow
- The UI controls for web search and reasoning effort should visually update when switching models

## Verification

- [ ] Set web search ON for Model A, switch to Model B and set it OFF → switching back to Model A shows web search ON
- [ ] Set reasoning effort to High for Model A → switch away and back → reasoning effort is still High
- [ ] A model with no saved preferences uses sensible defaults
- [ ] Settings persist across app restart
- [ ] Settings are included in backup and correctly restored

title: [Bug] @ Symbol in Paste Freezes Agent UI on Windows
body:
## Background

On Windows 11, pasting text that contains the `@` symbol into an Agent chat input causes the UI to freeze. The `@` character triggers the tool/skill mention popup, and when pasted content contains `@` in non-mention contexts (e.g., email addresses, code decorators like `@Override`, or social media handles), the popup searches for a match it cannot find and locks up the input.

## Goal

Prevent the `@` mention popup from causing UI freezes when `@` appears as part of pasted content rather than a deliberate user-typed mention trigger.

## Specification

- **Do not trigger** the `@` mention popup when text is pasted (as opposed to typed character-by-character)
  - Detect paste events and suppress the mention popup for `@` symbols introduced via paste
- If the popup is triggered and finds no matches, it should:
  - Dismiss itself automatically after a short timeout (e.g., 500ms with no match)
  - Never block the input field or cause the UI to become unresponsive
- The popup should still work correctly when the user manually types `@` to invoke a tool mention
- Test specifically on Windows 11 where the issue is reported, but ensure fix does not regress on macOS/Linux

## Verification

- [ ] Paste code containing `@` (e.g., `@decorator\ndef foo():`) into Agent chat on Windows 11 → no UI freeze
- [ ] Paste an email address (e.g., `user@example.com`) → no freeze, no mention popup
- [ ] Manually type `@` in Agent chat → mention popup appears normally
- [ ] Verify the fix works on Windows 11, macOS, and Linux
- [ ] No regression in normal `@` mention selection flow

title: [Feature] Granular Model Settings Backup
body:
## Background

The current backup system is all-or-nothing: users can only export and import their entire configuration at once. Users who work across multiple machines often want to sync just their model and provider settings (API keys, endpoint URLs, model lists) without overwriting other local preferences like chat history, agents, or UI settings.

## Goal

Allow users to selectively export and import model/provider settings independently from the rest of their configuration.

## Specification

- Add a **"Export Model Settings"** option in the backup/data management section
  - Exports a standalone JSON file containing:
    - Provider configurations (API keys, base URLs, custom headers)
    - Model list and per-model settings (display name, context length overrides, enabled/disabled status)
    - Per-model preferences (if per-model persistence is implemented)
  - File should be clearly named (e.g., `cherry-studio-models-YYYYMMDD.json`)
- Add a corresponding **"Import Model Settings"** option
  - Merges imported model settings with existing configuration
  - For conflicts (same provider/model already exists), prompt the user: **Replace**, **Skip**, or **Replace All**
  - Does not touch non-model settings (agents, chat history, UI preferences, etc.)
- The existing full backup/restore flow remains unchanged
- Sensitive data (API keys) should have the same handling as the current full backup (no additional encryption required, but warn the user the export contains API keys)

## Verification

- [ ] Export model settings → file contains provider configs and model list, no chat history or agent data
- [ ] Import model settings on a fresh install → providers and models are configured correctly
- [ ] Import on a machine with existing config → conflict resolution dialog works (Replace/Skip)
- [ ] Full backup/restore still works as before
- [ ] API key warning is shown during export

title: [Feature]: Make Scheduled Task Channel Binding Optional (Default to In-App Conversation)
body:
## Background

When creating a scheduled task, the "Send to channel" field is mandatory — users must bind an IM channel (Telegram / QQ / Feishu / WeChat) before they can save. Users who just want a task to run and review its output inside Cherry are forced to set up and pick an IM channel they don't need.

## Goal

Users can save and run a scheduled task without binding any IM channel; when no channel is bound, the task's output appears in its conversation inside Cherry, the same way Codex and Cowork results do.

## Spec

- The "Send to channel" field is optional. A task can be saved and run with no channel selected.
- The channel selector offers an explicit "no channel / in-app only" state (e.g. leaving it empty), distinct from the IM options.
- When no channel is bound, each task run writes its output to the task's own conversation inside Cherry, where the user can open and read it — same behavior as Codex / Cowork.
- When a channel IS bound, current behavior is unchanged: output is pushed to that IM channel (and still also viewable in the in-app conversation).
- Users can change the binding later — adding a channel to a previously channel-less task, or clearing the channel from a bound task.

## Verification

- Create a task, leave "Send to channel" empty, click Save → save succeeds with no validation error blocking on the channel field.
- Run the channel-less task → its output is visible in that task's conversation inside Cherry, with no message sent to any IM platform.
- Create a task bound to WeChat → output is pushed to WeChat as before (no regression to existing channel behavior).
- Edit a channel-less task, add Feishu, save, run → output now goes to Feishu; then clear the channel, save, run → output again only appears in the in-app conversation, nothing sent to Feishu.
- With zero IM channels configured in the app at all, a scheduled task can still be created, saved, and run end-to-end.

title: [Feature]: Create Scheduled Tasks via Chat
body:
## Background

Today, creating a scheduled task (Automation) means filling out a structured form — name, trigger, cron/interval, prompt template. New users often don't know what a good automation looks like or how to phrase the task, so the form is a cold start. Tools like Codex offer a conversational alternative: describe what you want in plain language and the agent figures out the schedule and the prompt with you.

## Goal

Users can create a scheduled task conversationally — from the Automations page they enter an agent chat that is pre-seeded with a guiding prompt, and the agent walks them through what to automate and when, then creates the task for them.

## Spec

- The Automations (Scheduled Tasks) page exposes a "Create via chat" entry point alongside the existing form-based creation.
- Selecting "Create via chat" opens an agent conversation with an editable starter prompt already filled into the input box (not auto-sent), instructing the agent to briefly explain how automations work and then ask the user a few questions to determine what to automate and when it should run.
- The user can edit or send the pre-filled prompt as-is; the conversation then proceeds normally.
- Through the conversation, the agent gathers the task intent and schedule and creates the scheduled task on the user's behalf, surfacing a confirmation of what was created (name, schedule, prompt).
- The conversational flow uses an autonomous-capable agent, consistent with the existing requirement that scheduled tasks need Soul Mode / Bypass Permissions.

## Verification

- On the Automations page, a "Create via chat" control is visible near the top of the page (mirroring the existing form entry). Clicking it lands the user in an agent chat with the starter prompt already in the input box.
- The starter prompt is in the input box but not yet sent — the user can edit it before sending, and nothing is created until they do.
- Send the pre-filled prompt unchanged → the agent responds by briefly explaining automations and asking clarifying questions (e.g. "what should I do, and when?"), rather than immediately creating a task.
- Complete the conversation (e.g. "remind me of gold price every day at 9pm") → a new scheduled task appears in the Automations list with a matching name and daily 9:00 PM schedule.
- The pre-filled prompt text is localized to the user's UI language (Chinese UI shows a Chinese starter prompt).
- Negative: opening "Create via chat" and then navigating away without sending does NOT create any scheduled task.

## Related

#14286

title: [Feature]: Notification Permission Priming Banner & System Notifications for Agent Events
body:
## Background

Cherry Studio already has the infrastructure to fire OS notifications, but it is off by default, buried in Settings, and Cherry never proactively asks for the macOS system-level notification permission. As a result, users running Agent tasks, waiting on a confirmation prompt in non-auto mode (#15152), or relying on scheduled tasks must keep watching the window or miss the event entirely. There is no discoverable, in-context prompt that nudges users to turn notifications on at the moment they'd benefit.

## Goal

Users are proactively prompted to enable system notifications via a dismissible banner above the input box, and once enabled they receive OS notifications when an Agent task completes, when the agent needs their confirmation to proceed, and when a scheduled task starts.

## Spec

- A dismissible banner appears above the input box prompting the user to turn on notifications, with an "Allow" action and a close (X) — modeled on the ChatGPT "Turn on notifications" banner.
- Clicking "Allow" triggers the OS-level notification permission request; on grant, system notifications are enabled for Cherry.
- The banner only shows while notifications are not yet enabled/granted; after the user enables them or dismisses it, it does not keep nagging.
- Once enabled, the user receives a system notification when: (a) an Agent task completes, (b) the agent is waiting for the user's confirmation/approval to proceed, (c) a scheduled task starts running.
- Clicking a notification brings Cherry Studio to the foreground and navigates to the relevant conversation/task.
- Notifications fire only when the Cherry window is not focused, so the user is never notified about what they are already watching.
- Each of the three scenarios remains individually toggleable in Settings; the banner is the priming entry point, not the only control.

## Verification

- Fresh install, notifications never granted → banner shows above the input box with "Allow" + X. Click "Allow" → the macOS system notification permission dialog appears.
- After granting, switch to another app and run an Agent task to completion → a system notification fires; clicking it focuses Cherry and opens that conversation.
- Run an agent in non-auto mode; when it reaches a step needing approval while Cherry is in the background → a notification fires prompting the user to return and confirm (the #15152 pain).
- A scheduled task fires while Cherry is backgrounded → a system notification announces it has started.
- Dismiss the banner with X → it does not reappear; after notifications are enabled it never shows again.
- Negative: with the Cherry window focused on the active conversation, completing an Agent task does NOT fire a system notification.
- OS permission denied → the banner stops prompting and Settings indicates notifications are unavailable / links out to system settings.

## Related

#14899 #15152 #15387 #15634
PRs: #14802 #13955

title: [Feature]: Automations Entry Point Above Agent Sessions + Task Template Gallery
body:
## Background

Scheduled tasks (Automations) already exist in Cherry Studio, but they're reachable only through a buried, per-agent Settings tab. Most users never discover the feature, and the ones who do face a cold-start: creating a task means filling a structured form (name, trigger, cron/interval, prompt) with no examples of what a useful automation looks like. As a result a powerful capability stays underused.

## Goal

A prominent "Automations" entry sits above the session list in the Agent area; opening it shows all the user's scheduled tasks and their recent run history in one place, and a template gallery lets users spin up a common automation in one click.

## Spec

- The Agent area shows a persistent "Automations" entry pinned above the conversation/session list, visually distinct so it reads as a primary destination rather than one more session.
- Opening Automations lands on a management page split into **Created** (active task definitions, each showing its schedule in plain language — e.g. "Once · 4/23 1:25 PM", "Daily · 12:30") and **Recent runs** (run history with per-run status and relative time).
- The page offers two creation paths: **Add** (the existing structured form) and **Add from template**.
- "Add from template" opens a gallery of ready-made automations grouped for everyday use (e.g. daily AI news digest, daily English words, weekly work report, on-this-day-in-history, meeting-prep reminder, pet wallpaper), each with a title and one-line description.
- Selecting a template pre-fills a new task with that template's schedule and prompt; the user can edit any field before saving, and saving creates a normal task that then appears under Created.
- Each run in the history is traceable — the user can open the conversation/output a given run produced.

## Verification

- With zero scheduled tasks, the Automations entry is still visible above the session list, and opening it shows an empty Created section plus the template gallery as the primary call to action.
- Pick the "Weekly work report" template → a new task opens pre-filled with a weekly schedule and a report prompt; save without editing → it appears under Created showing "Weekly · <day/time>".
- Edit a template's time before saving (e.g. change 12:30 to 09:00) → the saved task reflects 09:00, not the template default.
- A task that has run several times shows multiple entries under Recent runs with distinct statuses (e.g. success vs failed); clicking a successful run opens its conversation/output, and that view is not empty.
- Creating a task from a template and creating one via the structured form produce indistinguishable entries under Created (no second-class "template task").
- The entry label and template card titles/descriptions are localized (Chinese UI shows Chinese strings, not raw keys).

## Related

#14286 #15952 #15570

title: [Feature]: Open Skill Folder from Skills Management
body:
## Background

Skills in Cherry Studio live as folders on disk (SKILL.md plus scripts/assets). When a user wants to share a skill with someone — send it to a colleague, back it up, or zip it — they currently have no way to get from the Skills management UI to the skill's folder on disk. They have to hunt for the install location manually.

## Goal

Users can open a skill's folder in the OS file manager directly from the Skills management page, making it easy to locate, share, or back up the skill.

## Spec

- Each skill in the Skills management page offers an "Open folder" action that reveals the skill's folder in the OS file manager (Finder / File Explorer).
- The action opens the folder for that specific skill, with the skill's directory selected/highlighted.
- The action is available for user-managed skills that exist on disk; it is not offered (or is disabled) for skills that have no resolvable local folder.

## Verification

- On the Skills management page, trigger "Open folder" on the `skill-creator` skill → the OS file manager opens with that skill's folder revealed, containing its SKILL.md.
- The folder that opens belongs to the skill acted on (open folder on skill A vs skill B reveals two different directories).
- From the opened folder, the user can copy/zip the directory to share it — confirming the folder is the real, complete skill directory, not a temp copy.
- On Windows and macOS, the action opens File Explorer / Finder respectively.
- Negative: a built-in or non-local skill with no resolvable folder does not show a broken/erroring "Open folder" action.

title: [Feature]: Surface IM Channel Binding from the Agent List and Agent Settings
body:
## Background

IM channel binding currently lives only under global Settings ("Channels"), buried several levels deep and disconnected from any specific Agent. Users who want to talk to a given Agent over WeChat / Feishu can't find where to bind it — the entry is so hidden that a prior fix (#15624) had to teach Agents to verbally guide users to it.

## Goal

Users can reach IM channel binding for an Agent directly from the Agent list and from inside that Agent's settings dialog, without digging through global Settings.

## Spec

- In the Agent list, each Agent's menu includes an item for connecting to IM (e.g. "Connect to WeChat / Feishu…").
- Selecting that menu item opens the Agent's settings dialog with the "Channels" tab already active.
- The Agent settings dialog itself contains a "Channels" tab (reachable directly, not only via the list menu) where the user binds/unbinds IM channels for that Agent.
- The Channels tab lets the user pick among the supported IM channels (WeChat, Feishu, Telegram, QQ, Discord, Slack) and bind one or more to the Agent.
- Bindings made here are scoped to that Agent.
- The existing global Settings "Channels" entry remains; this adds shallower entry points rather than replacing it.

## Verification

- Open an Agent's menu in the Agent list → an "Connect to IM" item is visible.
- Click that item → the Agent settings dialog opens with the Channels tab already selected (not the default tab).
- In the Channels tab, bind WeChat → that Agent is now reachable over WeChat; a WeChat message routed to it reaches this Agent.
- Open the same Agent's settings dialog directly (not via the list menu) → the Channels tab is present and shows the current bindings.
- Unbind Feishu from an Agent that had it → the Agent no longer receives messages from that Feishu channel.
- An Agent with no channel bound still works normally in the in-app conversation (no binding is forced).

title: [Feature]: Reusable Guidance Banner Component Above the Input Box
body:
## Background

Cherry Studio has no shared way to surface in-context guidance right where the user is working. Each onboarding or nudge need (grant a permission, connect an IM channel, top up API credit, etc.) would otherwise be built one-off, leading to inconsistent UI and scattered effort. Claude Code and ChatGPT solve this with a small dismissible banner directly above the input box — icon, copy, an action, and a close — and reuse it across many prompts. A first concrete need for exactly this banner already exists (#15953, notification-permission priming), with more guidance cases coming.

## Goal

A single reusable banner component renders above the input box and can be driven by any guidance trigger (authorization, new session, scheduled tasks, IM connect, skill creation, API top-up, …), so new guidance can be added by declaring a trigger rather than building bespoke UI.

## Spec

- The banner renders directly above the input box and has a consistent anatomy: a leading icon, copy text (supporting inline links/commands, e.g. `/model`), one or more action buttons, and a close (X).
- Multiple banners can stack above the input box; when several apply, they show in a defined priority order, with a cap on how many are shown at once (the rest queue).
- Each banner is individually dismissible via X; once dismissed, that banner type does not nag again (dismissal persists across restarts).
- A banner auto-clears when its triggering condition no longer holds (e.g. after the user completes the guided action).
- Banners are defined through a registry of guidance triggers; each trigger declares its show condition, icon, copy, action(s), priority, and dismissal behavior — no per-banner custom UI.
- Initial guidance triggers covered by this component: enable authorization / permissions, start a new session, enable scheduled tasks, connect WeChat / Feishu, create a skill, top up API credit.
- Clicking a banner's action runs that trigger's handler (e.g. open the channel-binding tab, open the recharge page) and, where the action resolves the condition, the banner clears.

## Verification

- A banner renders above the input box with icon + copy + action + close; clicking the action runs its handler; clicking X dismisses it and it does not reappear after restart.
- Two conditions hold at once (e.g. authorization needed + API balance low) → both banners stack above the input box in priority order.
- API credit runs low → a "top up" banner appears with a Recharge action that opens the billing/recharge flow; after the user tops up, the banner auto-clears.
- An agent that could use an IM channel has none connected → a "connect WeChat / Feishu" banner appears; clicking its action opens the Agent's channel-binding tab (#15956).
- The notification-permission case (#15953) is implemented as one trigger on this component, not a separate one-off banner.
- Dismiss a banner, restart the app → that banner type stays dismissed.
- Negative: when no trigger condition is met, no banner shows and the input box sits flush as today.

title: [Feature]: Encrypt Agent Channel Credentials at Rest
body:
## Background

Every agent channel persists its connection config — Telegram bot token, QQ app id + secret, Feishu app id + app secret, Discord bot token, Slack token — as plaintext JSON in the local agent database, written verbatim at creation and kept there until the channel is deleted. Anyone or anything with read access to that file (malware, third-party scripts, an installed MCP server, a synced backup, a shared machine) obtains every channel's live credentials with no decryption step. Users have flagged this as a real exposure (#15841).

## Goal

Channel credentials are unreadable from the database file, backups, exports, or logs — recoverable only by the app at runtime on the machine that created them.

## Spec

- Sensitive credential fields for every channel type (Telegram / QQ / Feishu / Discord / Slack / WeChat) are encrypted before being written and decrypted only in-memory at the moment a channel connects.
- Encryption is bound to the current machine + OS-account secure storage / keychain, so the ciphertext is useless if copied to another machine or user.
- Non-sensitive config (name, type, active state, chat bindings, permission mode) stays in clear so listing, search, and management keep working.
- In settings, saved secrets are masked (never echoed back in full); the user can replace but not read an existing secret.
- Credentials are never written to logs, traces, error reports, or crash dumps.
- On upgrade, existing plaintext credentials are transparently re-encrypted in place — no user re-entry.
- Backup, agent export, and config sync never carry recoverable plaintext secrets; restoring on a new machine prompts the user to re-enter rather than silently shipping a credential or connecting with a stale one.
- If OS secure storage is unavailable (e.g. Linux without a keyring), the app warns and blocks plaintext persistence rather than silently falling back.

## Verification

- Add channels of each type, open the DB with an external SQLite tool → no token/secret appears as plaintext for any of them.
- After encryption, each channel still connects and exchanges messages (runtime decryption works).
- Settings shows a saved Telegram token masked; there is no way to reveal the full original value back.
- Grep the full log/trace output after a channel connects → the secret string never appears.
- Copy the DB (and a backup file) to another machine/account → secrets can't be decrypted; the user is prompted to re-enter rather than the bot silently connecting.
- Export an agent that has channels → the export file contains no recoverable plaintext secret.
- Upgrade from a plaintext build → channels keep working with zero re-typing, and the stored values are no longer plaintext afterward.
- Negative: a third-party MCP server or script reading the DB obtains nothing usable.

## Related

#15841 #15734

title: [Feature]: Reliable Delivery of Long-Running Agent Task Results to IM Channels
body:
## Background

When a user triggers an Agent task from WeChat or QQ that runs many rounds (~100 tool turns over 5+ minutes), the Agent finishes and produces a reply, but the channel never receives it — the result is silently lost. The current channel pipeline throttles streaming edits but has no guarantee that a final result lands after a long, possibly connection-interrupted run, leaving the user staring at silence (#15721).

## Goal

An Agent's final result reliably reaches the originating IM channel for tasks of any length or round count, exactly once, with progress visible while it runs.

## Spec

- The final reply is delivered to the originating channel regardless of task duration or number of tool rounds.
- Long tasks emit periodic progress / "still working" signals so the user knows the task is alive, not stalled.
- Replies that exceed the platform's per-message length limit are split into ordered chunks; nothing is truncated or dropped.
- If the channel connection drops or times out mid-task, the result is re-delivered after reconnection, with idempotency so the user never receives a duplicate final message.
- Transient send failures are retried with bounded backoff before being declared failed.
- On unrecoverable failure, an explicit error notice is delivered to the channel and logged — never a silent no-op.
- When multiple tasks run on the same channel, their results stay correctly attributed and ordered, not interleaved or mixed up.

## Verification

- From WeChat, trigger ~100 tool rounds over 5+ minutes → the final reply arrives after completion.
- Same from QQ → final reply arrives.
- During the long task, the user sees at least one progress/heartbeat message before the result.
- Produce a reply longer than the platform message limit → it arrives as multiple in-order chunks with nothing missing.
- Disconnect the channel mid-task, then reconnect → the final result is delivered exactly once (no duplicate, no loss).
- Run two long tasks on the same channel concurrently → both results arrive, each attributed to the right request.
- Negative: after a long task completes, the channel is never left with no message and never receives two copies of the same final reply.

## Related

#15721

title: [Feature]: Selectable System Variables (Time, Location, Model) for Conversation Context
body:
## Background

Assistant chat sends the model no notion of "now", "where", or "which model is answering" — it defaults to its training cutoff (often believing it's 2024/2025), has no timezone or regional awareness, and cannot reliably state which model is replying. Time-sensitive, locale-aware, and "which model are you" answers are wrong unless the user restates the facts every conversation. Agent sessions inject a date but assistant chat does not, so behavior is inconsistent across the two (#15768).

## Goal

Users pick which system variables — current time, coarse region, and the current conversation model — to attach to a conversation; the selected values plus a preset declaration are appended to each turn so the model answers with accurate temporal, regional, and model self-awareness, consistently across assistant chat and agent sessions, without degrading prompt-cache efficiency.

## Spec

- A settings panel lists the available system variables as checkboxes: Current Time (with timezone), Region/Locale, and Current Model. The user selects any combination; selecting none injects nothing.
- When one or more variables are selected, each turn carries the selected values together with a preset declaration prompt that names and explains them to the model (e.g., that the time is the real current time and the model field is which model is answering).
- Region is coarse (locale + timezone) sourced from system settings — never precise coordinates or active geolocation.
- The Current Model variable carries the active model's name; in a multi-model conversation (one turn answered by several models) it is automatically omitted and shown as unavailable in the selector, since there is no single current model.
- Injected values reflect the real state of each turn — time updates over a long conversation, and the model value reflects a mid-conversation model switch — rather than freezing at session start.
- Assistant chat and agent sessions use the same selection and injection behavior.
- Injection is positioned so it does not churn the cacheable prompt prefix — enabling variables must not collapse prompt-cache hit-rate for MCP-heavy conversations (#15798).
- The user can inspect exactly which variables, values, and declaration text were attached to a given turn.

## Verification

- Select only Current Time → ask "what's today's date?" → the model answers the actual current date; region and model are absent from the attached context.
- Select Current Model in a single-model chat → ask "which model are you?" → the answer matches the selected model name.
- Switch the model mid-conversation with Current Model selected → the next turn's injected model value reflects the new model, not the old one.
- Start a multi-model conversation → the Current Model checkbox is shown unavailable and no model variable is injected for any of the models.
- Select Time + Region → "what time is it for me?" matches the system timezone; deselect Region → region disappears from the next turn.
- Inspect a turn → the user sees the exact variables, their values, and the preset declaration text appended.
- In an MCP-heavy conversation, enabling variables does not measurably drop the prompt-cache hit-rate versus none selected (#15798).
- Negative: precise GPS coordinates are never injected; in a multi-model turn no model variable leaks into any model's context.

## Related

#15768 #15798

title: [Feature]: Knowledge Base — Connect External Knowledge Bases (Feishu Wiki) as a Synced Source
body:
## Background

A Cherry knowledge base today only ingests local files, URLs, notes, sitemaps, and directories. Teams keep their living documentation in Feishu Wiki, so to use it in Cherry they must manually export each doc and re-upload — and the copy goes stale the moment Feishu changes. Users have asked for native Feishu data integration (#13032).

## Goal

Users connect a Feishu Wiki space as a knowledge base source whose documents are imported and kept in sync, so Agents and Assistants retrieve up-to-date Feishu content with no manual export.

## Spec

- A new knowledge base source type — **External Knowledge Base** — lets the user authorize and pick a Feishu Wiki space (or a specific node / subtree) as a source.
- Authorization goes through the connector/OAuth path (reuse #15340) with least-privilege read scope — no manual token pasting.
- Selected Feishu docs and their nested wiki tree are imported, parsed, chunked, and embedded into the chosen base like any other source.
- The source stays in sync: new / edited / deleted docs in Feishu are reflected on refresh, re-embedding only what changed rather than the whole base (builds on #15958 / #15417).
- The user controls sync scope and cadence (manual refresh and/or scheduled) and can disconnect — which stops syncing and optionally removes the imported items.
- Import respects Feishu permissions: only docs the authorizing account can read are imported; docs that become inaccessible are dropped on the next sync.
- The design generalizes to other external knowledge bases (Notion, Confluence) — Feishu is the first provider, not a one-off.

## Verification

- Connect a Feishu Wiki space and pick a 20-doc subtree → those docs appear as items in the chosen base and are retrievable in chat.
- Edit one doc in Feishu, trigger refresh → the updated content is retrievable, and only the edited doc is re-embedded (the other 19 are not).
- Delete a doc in Feishu, refresh → it disappears from the base and is no longer retrievable.
- A doc the authorizing account cannot read is never imported.
- Disconnect with "remove imported items" → those items are gone; disconnect with "keep" → they remain as static items.
- Schedule a daily sync → a Feishu doc added after connection shows up after the scheduled run with no manual action.
- Negative: connecting Feishu does NOT pull in docs outside the selected space/subtree.

## Related

#13032 #15340 #15417 #15958 #14905 #15840

title: [Feature]: Group the Agent List by Inherited Tags
body:
## Background

Once Agent and Assistant surfaces are merged, a user can accumulate dozens of agents in one flat, scrolling list with no way to organize them. Assistants already support tags, but agents do not — so the list stays an unstructured pile and finding the right agent means scrolling the whole thing.

## Goal

The Agent list groups agents by the tags they inherit from the unified assistant/agent tag system, and each tag group can be collapsed or expanded so users navigate a large agent set by category instead of one long scroll.

## Spec

- After the Agent/Assistant merge, agents become taggable through the same tag system assistants already use — an agent carries whatever tags it inherited, and the list renders one collapsible group per tag.
- Each tag group header shows the tag name, its color, and the count of agents under it; collapsing a group hides its agents while keeping the header visible.
- An agent with multiple tags appears under each of its tag groups; an agent with no tags falls into a default "Untagged" group.
- Collapsed/expanded state per group persists across app restarts.
- Users can add or remove an agent's tags inline from the list, and the grouping updates immediately to reflect the change.
- Existing pin and ordering behavior is preserved: pinned agents stay surfaced, and ordering applies within each group.

## Verification

- Tag three agents "Coding" and two "Research"; the list shows a "Coding (3)" group and a "Research (2)" group, each with its agents nested.
- Collapse "Coding" → its three agents hide, the header stays; restart the app → "Coding" is still collapsed.
- Give one agent both "Coding" and "Research" tags → it appears under both groups simultaneously.
- Create an agent with no tags → it appears under "Untagged".
- Remove the "Research" tag from an agent inline → it immediately leaves the "Research" group with no manual refresh.
- Negative: an agent never disappears from the list just because all its groups are collapsed — collapsing hides the rows under a header, it does not drop the agent.

## Related

#15396

title: [Feature]: "Use Cases" Gallery in the Marketplace — Click to Prefill a Prompt into the Agent
body:
## Background

New Cherry Studio users often don't know what the product can actually do or how to phrase a first request, so they stall at an empty input box. There's no in-app gallery that demonstrates concrete ways to use Cherry Studio and lets users start one in a single click. Codex's "Use Cases" page is the reference: a browsable gallery of cards (image, title, description, category) where picking one drops a ready example prompt straight into the composer.

## Goal

Users can browse a "Use Cases" gallery inside the Marketplace and, with one click, have that use case's example prompt prefilled into the Agent input box ready to review and send.

## Spec

- The Marketplace gains a "Use Cases" module: a gallery of use-case cards, each with an image/icon, title, short description, and category tags.
- Use cases can be filtered by category and searched, mirroring the Codex "All use cases" layout (category list + card grid).
- Clicking a use case prefills its example prompt into the Agent input box, focused and editable — it does NOT auto-send; the user reviews and sends.
- A use case may target a specific Agent; clicking it routes to that Agent with the prompt prefilled. If none is specified, it uses the current/default Agent.
- The use-case catalog is curated and configured by official staff in this iteration; the model is designed so community-contributed use cases can be added later (ties into Marketplace #15029).
- Each use case entry carries: title, description, category/tags, image, the example prompt text, and optional target Agent.

## Verification

- Open the Marketplace → a "Use Cases" module is present, showing cards with image, title, description, and tags.
- Click a use case (e.g. "Proactive teammate") → its example prompt appears in the Agent input box, focused and editable, with nothing sent yet.
- Filter by a category (e.g. "Automation") → only use cases in that category are shown; clearing the filter restores the full gallery.
- A use case that targets a specific Agent → clicking it opens that Agent with the prompt prefilled.
- In this iteration there is no end-user authoring UI — the catalog reflects what official staff configured.
- Negative: clicking a use case never auto-sends the message; the user must press send.

## Related

#15957 #15029 #15398

title: [Feature]: Installable CLIs in the Skill Marketplace — One Click, Installed by the Agent
body:
## Background

Many of Cherry Studio's most useful skills are backed by an external CLI (the Feishu/Lark unified CLI, a Notion CLI, a 企查查 business-lookup CLI, an Obsidian CLI, …). Today there's no place in the Skill Marketplace to discover and install these CLIs, and getting one onto the machine means manual download, PATH setup, and auth — work most users can't or won't do. Cherry already has an Agent that can run commands; it should do the install for the user.

## Goal

Users can browse CLIs in the Skill Marketplace and install one with a single click, with the Agent carrying out the install (download/build, PATH, and any auth) and reporting progress and result.

## Spec

- The Skill Marketplace lists CLIs as an installable item kind, each with a name, description, icon, and category (initial set: Feishu CLI, Notion CLI, 企查查 CLI, Obsidian CLI).
- Clicking Install on a CLI hands the installation to the Agent: it runs the install steps in a session, streams progress, and ends in an explicit success or failure state.
- When a CLI requires authentication (e.g. Notion login / OAuth), the Agent walks the user through it as part of the install.
- On failure (e.g. a missing runtime, a network error), the Agent surfaces the reason instead of leaving a silent half-install.
- After a successful install, the CLI is available for skills and Agents to call as a tool.
- An already-installed CLI shows an "Installed" state rather than reinstalling on click, and offers update / uninstall.
- The CLI catalog is curated and configured by official staff in this iteration, designed to extend to more CLIs (and community contributions) later.

## Verification

- Open the Skill Marketplace → a CLI section lists Feishu CLI, Notion CLI, 企查查 CLI, and Obsidian CLI with name, description, and icon.
- Click Install on "Feishu CLI" → an Agent session runs the install, streams progress, and ends in a success state; the CLI is then callable by skills/Agents.
- Install a CLI that needs auth (e.g. Notion) → the Agent guides the user through login/OAuth before reporting success.
- Trigger a failing install (e.g. missing runtime) → the Agent reports the specific failure reason; the item does not show as installed.
- Reopen the Marketplace after a successful install → that CLI shows "Installed" and clicking it offers update/uninstall, not a blind reinstall.
- Negative: clicking a CLI never installs silently — the Agent session always shows what it is doing.

## Related

#15672 #15029 #15545 #15181 #15370

title: Insert current model name into chat system prompt via template variable
body:
## Background

In chat, an assistant's system prompt is static. Users who want the model to be "self-aware" of which model is currently answering (e.g. for differentiated behavior, debugging, or role framing) have to hardcode the model name, which breaks when they switch models mid-conversation.

## Goal

Let the system prompt reference the current model via a template variable so it is auto-filled with the model actually used for each request.

## Spec

- Support a `{{model_name}}` (and/or `{{model_id}}`) placeholder inside an assistant's system prompt.
- At send time, substitute it with the name/identifier of the model selected for that message.
- If the user switches model mid-conversation, the substituted value follows the current model.
- Leave the placeholder untouched if no model is resolved (graceful fallback).

## Verification

- Put `{{model_name}}` in a system prompt → ask the model "what model are you" → it answers with the correct current model name.
- Switch model in the same conversation → next message reflects the new model name.

## Related

- Variable/template substitution in system prompt (if any existing prompt-variable mechanism exists, extend it).

title: [Bug]: Deleting MCP server does not cascade clean agent's mcps list, causing massive connection error logs
body:
> [\!NOTE]
> This issue was translated by Claude.

### Issue Checklist
- [x] I understand that issues are for feedback and problem solving
- [x] My issue is not listed in the FAQ
- [x] I have looked at pinned issues and searched for existing open/closed issues and discussions, no similar issue found
- [x] I have filled in short, clear headings
- [x] I am using the latest version of Cherry Studio

### Platform
Windows

### Version
v1.9.11

### Bug Description
After deleting an MCP in Cherry Studio Settings → MCP Servers, the MCP remains in the `agents.mcps` column in `agents.db` (each agent stores an independent JSON array). The agent continues to attempt connecting to the deleted MCP, generating massive `connection refused` / `404` errors.

**Test Data:**
- 5 agents had 20 deleted MCP references remaining
- Generated 77,550 error logs in 4 days
- Affected MCP IDs (all from ModelScope public marketplace): `bilibili-mcp`, `arxiv-mcp-server`, `hyperbrowserai/mcp`, `bing-cn-mcp-server`, `Retrieve-Douyin-video-data`, `xiaohongshu-mcp`

### Steps To Reproduce
1. Add a streamableHttp MCP (e.g., any MCP from ModelScope marketplace)
2. Check this MCP for that agent in agent settings
3. Go to Settings → MCP Servers → Delete that MCP
4. Check agents.db → agents table → `mcps` column → that MCP ID is still in the JSON array
5. Check error log → the agent continuously retries connecting to the deleted MCP

### Expected Behavior
When deleting a global MCP, should cascade cleanup all references to that MCP in every agent's `mcps` column.

### Relevant Log Output
After deleting MCP, logs continuously show `connection refused` / `404` errors, approximately 19,000+ per day.

title: Agent Modes: Standard (AI SDK) vs Enhanced (Claude Agent SDK) with subtle in-conversation switching
body:
## Background

Chat and Agent stay as two separate top-level entries (no merge). Today the Agent runs only on the Claude Agent SDK runtime, which is heavy and slow. We want a lighter, faster agent option while keeping a full agent (loop, file writes, tool use).

## Goal

Give an Agent two runtime "modes":
- **Standard** = an AI SDK–based agent (lighter & faster; full loop + file writes; reference opencode's AI-SDK agent).
- **Enhanced** = the Claude Agent SDK runtime.

## Spec

- **Create flow**: when creating an Agent, choose mode **Standard (AI SDK)** or **Enhanced (Claude Agent SDK)**, with a tooltip explaining the difference. Editable later.
- **Conversation**: follows the Agent's configured runtime by default; allow **manual switching** in-conversation. The switch control lives **inside the input box and is de-emphasized** — NOT a heavy "Chat mode / Task mode" style toggle.
- **Auto-prompt to upgrade**: if the user appears unsatisfied with Standard mode's results, show a small popover **above the input box** suggesting they switch to Enhanced.
- **Status indicator**: a subtle quick/power icon near the input box so the user can tell at a glance whether they're on Standard or Enhanced (no strong/intrusive prompt).

## Verification

- Create an Agent in Standard → runs a multi-step task (loop + writes a file) correctly and noticeably faster than Enhanced.
- Switch to Enhanced in the same conversation → uses Claude Agent SDK; switch control is subtle.
- When Standard underperforms, the "switch to Enhanced" popover appears above the input box.

## Related

- #15685 (Work Mode), #15397 (AI SDK / Pi as alternative agent runtime)

title: [Feature]: CherryAI 默认服务商、默认模型与默认助手初始化方案设计
body:
## Issue Checklist

- [x] I understand that issues are for reporting problems and requesting features, not for off-topic comments, and I will provide as much detail as possible to help resolve the issue.
- [x] I have checked the pinned issues and searched through the existing open issues, closed issues, and discussions and did not find a similar suggestion.

## Platform

macOS

## Version

2.0.0-dev (`codex/main-5-assistant-library-data`). This is a v2 data migration / initialization design issue and should be treated as cross-platform data-layer behavior.

## Design Topic

This issue tracks the v2 design for CherryAI default provider, default model, default assistant, and the related Settings visibility policy.

The goal is to make migration and fresh database initialization deterministic, with clear ownership boundaries instead of scattered runtime fallback logic.

## Scope

The design should cover:

1. Old-user v2 migration.
2. Fresh-user database seed.
3. Default provider initialization.
4. Default model initialization.
5. Default model preferences for chat, quick assistant, and translate.
6. Default assistant seed behavior.
7. Settings visibility and deletion policy for default data.

## Proposed Behavior

### Old-user migration

1. Migration should ensure the built-in CherryAI provider (`cherryai`) exists.
2. Migration should ensure the seeded default model (`cherryai::qwen`) exists.
3. Migrated model preferences should keep valid user-selected model ids.
4. Missing, empty, null, invalid, or old CherryAI preference values should be backfilled to `cherryai::qwen`.
5. Assistant migration should only migrate real legacy assistants; it should not synthesize a new default assistant for old users.

### Fresh-user seed

1. Seed should create the built-in CherryAI provider.
2. Seed should create `cherryai::qwen`.
3. Seed should initialize these preferences to `cherryai::qwen`:
   - `chat.default_model_id`
   - `feature.quick_assistant.model_id`
   - `feature.translate.model_id`
4. Default assistant seed should point to `cherryai::qwen`, but it should not own model preference writes.

### Settings visibility and deletion policy

1. The built-in CherryAI provider is protected default data and should be hidden from the Settings provider list.
2. The seeded default model (`cherryai::qwen`) is protected default data and should be hidden from the Settings model list.
3. Settings UI should filter out the protected default provider and protected default model, so users do not see delete, edit, or other normal custom-data operations for them.
4. The default assistant is user-facing seed data and should remain visible and deletable by the user.
5. Deleting the default assistant should not cause migration or seed fallback code to recreate it for existing users; chat behavior should rely on the default model preference when no assistant is available.

## Proposed Ownership Contract

1. `ProviderModelMigrator` owns CherryAI provider and default model backfill for old-user migration.
2. LLM preference migration owns default model, quick assistant model, and translate model preference fallback for old users.
3. `CherryAIDefaultModelSeeder` owns CherryAI provider, default model, and default model preferences for fresh database seed.
4. `DefaultAssistantSeeder` owns only the fresh-user default assistant row and relies on the default model seed for provider/model/preference setup.
5. Runtime code should not carry fallback logic for data that migration or seed can persist deterministically.

## Related files

- `src/main/data/db/defaults/cherryaiDefaultModel.ts`
- `src/main/data/db/seeding/seeders/cherryaiDefaultModelSeeder.ts`
- `src/main/data/db/seeding/seeders/defaultAssistantSeeder.ts`
- `src/main/data/migration/v2/migrators/ProviderModelMigrator.ts`
- `src/main/data/migration/v2/migrators/mappings/LlmModelTransforms.ts`

Reading long AI responses on screen for a long time causes severe eye strain. Cherry Studio currently has no native TTS text-to-speech feature. I have to copy text to external tools for audio reading, which breaks the workflow and creates extra steps.
Many text-only LLMs do not support image vision capabilities. When uploading images in chat, the model cannot extract text inside the picture. I have to rely on third-party OCR tools to grab text and manually paste it into the input box, which is inefficient.

Auto Text-to-Speech (TTS)
Add a global toggle to automatically read aloud Assistant replies once generation finishes. Include manual controls for playback, speech speed and voice tone. Allow users to only read assistant outputs while skipping System/User messages. Support built-in OS voice engines.

All-in-one workflow
OCR extract text from images → send query to LLM → auto TTS read model replies. Users won’t need external third-party tools for image or audio functions.


### Alternative Solutions

Right now I have to use separate third-party apps as workarounds:
Copy chat text to web pages or note-taking apps to get TTS audio;
Use standalone OCR software to extract image text then paste back into Cherry Studio;

title: [Bug] Custom system prompts are not mapped to the instructions field in Responses API mode
body: ## Bug Description 在 Responses API 类型的供应商配置中，即使设置了「系统提示词」，实际发出的请求里 `instructions` 字段仍未被正确填充，导致部分服务端自动注入默认系统提示词（Codex CLI 指令集），用户无法通过 Cherry Studio 自带的系统提示词设置覆盖。 **复现步骤**： 1. 添加一个 Responses API 格式的自定义供应商 2. 在该供应商的「系统提示词」字段写入自定义内容 3. 发起对话，观察模型回复的行为/身份 4. 模型的自我介绍和行文风格仍遵循服务端默认提示词，而非用户设置,且显示有固定的5000tokens输入内容,实测各种不同供应商均能复现这个问题 **原因分析**： - Responses API 的系统提示词字段是 `instructions`，不同于 Chat Completions 的 `messages[role=system]` - 通过抓包可以看到请求发出时 `instructions` 字段未被正确设置 - 手动在「自定义参数」中添加 `instructions`，值为文本类型，可以正常覆盖服务端默认提示词，说明问题在客户端未将系统提示词映射到 `instructions` **临时解决办法**： 在供应商配置的「自定义参数」中添加参数名 `instructions`，类型选择文本，值填入内容即可。 ### Platform Windows ### Version v1.9.11 ### 关联 已有 issue #12962 反馈过 Responses API 下未设置系统提示词时会发送 `"instructions": "[undefined]"`，侧面印证 `instructions` 字段映射存在问题。

title: [Bug]: Agent fails with ECONNREFUSED when a stale system proxy is set (Claude Code subprocess blindly inherits system HTTP_PROXY)
body:
## Summary

The **Agent** (Claude Code runtime) fails with `API Error: Unable to connect to API (ECONNREFUSED)` for *any* prompt — even ones that trigger no tools (e.g. "你是谁?") — whenever the OS has a **configured-but-dead system proxy** (common after a proxy/VPN client such as Clash is closed without clearing the macOS network proxy entry). Regular chat to the same provider works fine in the same state; **only the Agent fails**.

## Environment
- Cherry Studio v1.9.11 (production)
- Proxy mode: **System** (default)
- macOS with a stale *enabled* proxy entry (e.g. `127.0.0.1:7890`) left behind by a closed proxy client

## Steps to reproduce
1. In macOS Network settings, have a system proxy entry **enabled** (e.g. left by Clash) but the proxy process **not running**.
2. Cherry Studio proxy mode = **System** (default).
3. Open an Agent, send `你是谁?` (no tool/web-search triggered).
4. → `API Error: Unable to connect to API (ECONNREFUSED)`. Regular chat to the same CherryIN/provider endpoint succeeds.

## Root cause

The Agent forks a Claude Code subprocess. The subprocess inherits the main-process proxy env via `getProxyEnvironment(process.env)`, then a bootstrap injected with `--require` forcibly routes **all** subprocess requests (including the model API) through that proxy, with **no fallback**.

In `proxyMode=system`, `ProxyManager.configureProxy` uses `os-proxy-config` (1.1.2), which reads the macOS proxy **enable flag only** and returns the configured address (e.g. `http://127.0.0.1:7890`) **even when nothing is listening** on it. That address is written into `process.env.HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY` and inherited by the subprocess → every model-API request is forced through a dead local port → **ECONNREFUSED**.

Regular chat instead goes through Electron/Chromium `session.setProxy`, which falls back / direct-connects when the proxy is unavailable — so chat works while the Agent fails.

Signature: the error is **`ECONNREFUSED`** (connection refused to a local port), **not a timeout** — which distinguishes it from network/GFW blocking. The model endpoint itself is reachable (successful billing records confirm it).

**Code references (v1.9.11):**
- `src/main/services/agents/services/claudecode/index.ts` — env assembly (~206-235), proxy bootstrap inject (~497-509)
- `src/main/services/proxy/nodeProxy.ts` — env extract/apply (~259-293, 517-544), global request hijack (546-658)
- `src/main/services/proxy/bootstrap.ts` — subprocess proxy entry
- `src/main/services/ProxyManager.ts` — system proxy detection (~56-67)
- `src/renderer/src/store/settings.ts:263` — default `proxyMode: 'system'`

## Suggested fix
1. **Bypass proxy for the model endpoint**: add the active provider/model host to the subprocess `NO_PROXY` by default (domestic endpoints don't need a proxy). The bypass mechanism already exists in `nodeProxy.ts`; it just needs the model host added.
2. **Availability-check the system proxy**: before injecting a `proxyMode=system` address into the child env, TCP-probe the port; if dead, skip it so the subprocess direct-connects.
3. **Don't blindly inherit `process.env` proxy** into the Claude Code subprocess.

## Workaround (for users now)
- Cherry Studio → Settings → Proxy mode → **No proxy** (direct), or
- macOS → Network → (active interface) → Details → Proxies → disable all proxy toggles.

## Notes
- Reported via community user group; multiple users affected (agent hangs / ECONNREFUSED without VPN, works with VPN).
- A separate, secondary issue exists where Agent web search repeats the same query many times — that one stems from the Agent forcing an overseas Exa MCP (`mcp.exa.ai`, `claudecode/index.ts:585-588`) with no timeout/fallback; tracked separately.

body:

- [x] I understand that issues are for feedback and problem solving, not for complaining in the comment section, and will provide as much information as possible to help solve the problem.
- [x] My issue is not listed in the [FAQ](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/issues/3881).

- [x] I've filled in short, clear headings so that developers can quickly identify a rough idea of what to expect when flipping through the list of issues. And not "a suggestion", "stuck", etc.
- [x] I've confirmed that I am using the latest version of Cherry Studio.

### Platform

Windows

### Version

1.9.11, Also affects: `main` branch (v2.0.0-alpha)

### Bug Description

Custom parameters defined in assistant settings (string, number, boolean, JSON types) never appear in the HTTP request body for most providers. 
The feature UI suggests users can add arbitrary key-value pairs that will be sent to the LLM API, but the underlying Vercel AI SDK provider adapters silently drop unrecognized fields from `providerOptions`.

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Open Cherry Studio, go to an assistant's settings.
2. Add a custom parameter: name = `store`, type = boolean, value = `false`.
3. Send a chat message using Anthropic type provider.
4. Inspect the outgoing HTTP request.
5. Observe that `store: false` does **not** appear in the request body.

Same result for JSON type:

1. Add a custom parameter: name = `cache_control`, type = JSON, value = `{"type":"ephemeral"}`.
2. Send a chat message.
3. Observe that `cache_control` does **not** appear in the request body.

### Expected Behavior

Custom parameters added via assistant settings should appear as top-level fields in the HTTP request body, regardless of which provider adapter is used.

### Relevant Log Output

```shell

```

### Additional Context

## Current Behavior

1. User adds a custom parameter in assistant settings (e.g., `store` = boolean `false`, or `cache_control` = JSON `{"type":"ephemeral"}`).
2. Cherry Studio's internal pipeline correctly extracts and merges these into `providerOptions[providerId]`.
3. The AI SDK provider adapter's `getArgs()` method only reads **whitelisted** fields from `providerOptions` and ignores everything else.
4. The custom parameter is silently dropped and never reaches the HTTP request body.

**Affected providers (all except OpenRouter):**

| Provider Adapter | Whitelisted Fields Only |
|---|---|
| `@ai-sdk/anthropic` | `thinking`, `effort`, `taskBudget`, `cacheControl`, `sendReasoning`, `anthropicBeta`, `output_config` |
| `@ai-sdk/openai` | `reasoningEffort`, `reasoningSummary`, `forceReasoning`, `serviceTier`, `textVerbosity`, `store` |
| `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible` | `reasoningEffort` |
| `@ai-sdk/google` | `safetySettings`, `thinkingConfig`, `cachedContent`, `responseModalities`, `speechConfig`, `imageGenerationConfig` |
| `@ai-sdk/xai` | `reasoningEffort`, `logprobs`, `topLogprobs`, `serviceTier` |
| `@ai-sdk/deepseek` | `thinking`, `reasoning_effort` |
| `ollama-ai-provider-v2` | `think`, `options` |

`@openrouter/ai-sdk-provider` is the **only** adapter with a rest-spread passthrough that forwards unrecognized fields.

## Suspected Cause

> **Note**: Code paths below were traced on the `main` branch (v2). The v1.9.11 codebase uses different file paths (`src/renderer/src/aiCore/` instead of `src/main/ai/`) but the same fundamental logic and the same AI SDK adapter limitation.

The custom parameters pipeline works correctly inside Cherry Studio:

1. `getCustomParameters()` converts UI entries to a flat `Record<string, any>`.
2. `extractAiSdkStandardParams()` splits into standard params (e.g., `temperature`, `topK`) vs provider-specific params.
3. Provider-specific params are merged into `providerOptions[providerId]`.

The break occurs at the **AI SDK provider adapter layer**: each adapter's `getArgs()` method only destructures known fields from `providerOptions[providerId]` and discards the rest. There is no generic passthrough or `extraBody` mechanism in these adapters.

Cherry Studio correctly assembles `providerOptions` and passes them through to the adapter's `doGenerate()`/`doStream()`, where unrecognized keys are dropped.

## Proposed Fix

Inject custom parameters at the **fetch level** by wrapping the provider's `fetch` function. The wrapper intercepts POST requests, parses the JSON body, merges custom parameters (with low precedence so SDK-set fields win), and re-serializes.

This approach:
- Works for **all** providers (operates on raw HTTP, not provider-specific options)
- Requires no AI SDK patches or upstream changes
- Is a small, additive change (one new file + a few lines of wiring)

**Why not other approaches?**
- `transformParams` (plugin hook): can modify `providerOptions`, but the adapter's `getArgs()` still drops unrecognized fields downstream
- `extra_body`: only `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible` supports this passthrough; other adapters (`@ai-sdk/anthropic`, `@ai-sdk/google`, `@ai-sdk/openai`, etc.) do not

**v2 integration note**: On the `main` branch (v2), this fetch wrapper can be implemented as an aiCore plugin via `configureContext`, consistent with existing features like `applyHttpTrace` and `CherryAI signature fetch` that already wrap the provider's fetch function.

## Historical Fix Pattern

The history shows a recurring pattern: each time a user reports custom params not working for a specific provider, a targeted fix is merged for that provider alone (Gemini → [#11456](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/pull/11456), reasoning_effort → [#12831](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/pull/12831), Bedrock → [#9172](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/pull/9172), Gateway → [#11605](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/pull/11605)). But the fundamental problem — **AI SDK adapters dropping all unrecognized fields** — remains, and new providers or new parameter names will hit the same issue.

### Why a New Issue Is Warranted

1. **No existing issue captures the full cross-provider scope** — each prior report covers only one provider or one parameter
2. **Prior fixes are narrow patches**, not a systemic solution — the core adapter filtering is untouched
3. **Arbitrary custom parameters still don't work** — only specifically known fields (like `reasoning_effort`) have been patched
4. **Would serve as the actionable implementation issue for Category Q** in #14021

# Disclaimer

The following is a trace code analysis and write-up that I had Claude help me with after encountering this issue, and I personally made some minor adjustments; the content may contain errors

### Is your feature request related to an existing issue?

Picking models one by one in the chat input every single time is a real daily annoyance when you keep cycling through the same set of models. There's still no way to save a group of models and pull them all in at once.

To be honest, this has been a frustrating road, and I think it's fair to lay out why. This feature was already built twice — #10006, then a complete rewrite in #10949 — and neither one got merged:

- #10006 missed its merge window because the team overlooked the related discussion. That wasn't on me — EurFelux acknowledged it directly in #10949 and apologised for it.
- I was then explicitly told to hold off until the v2 data architecture was ready. So I did exactly that, and waited.
- #10949 was later closed as "stale" for having "no new commits since the start of 2026" — in other words, penalised for following the maintainers' own instruction to wait. 

What makes the closure especially odd: in that same thread, EurFelux noted this feature has already been incorporated into the v2 architectural design. So the need clearly hasn't gone away — the contribution just got dropped on the floor.

### Desired Solution

Model groups:

- Create named groups of models in Settings (full CRUD).
- @mention a group in the chat input to pull in every model in it at once, alongside the existing single-model @mention.
- Groups persist across sessions.
