(Real data-at-rest encryption to be tracked as a separate requirement.)

title: [Feature]: Deleting Agent/Assistant messages should also clear the SDK conversation context
body:
## Background

In V2's Agent and Assistant modes, what the user sees in the conversation is not the same as the context the model actually has. The model's working context lives inside the Claude Agent SDK session — the SDK keeps its own running transcript of the conversation. When a user deletes a message from the visible conversation, Cherry removes it from the UI, but the SDK session is untouched, so the model still "remembers" the deleted content and keeps referencing it in later turns.

This breaks the user's mental model and has concrete consequences:

- **Corrections don't stick** — a user deletes a wrong instruction or a bad tool result to steer the agent away from it, but the agent keeps acting on the deleted content.
- **Privacy / leakage** — a user deletes a message with sensitive content, assuming it's gone, yet it stays in the model's context and can resurface.
- **Wasted budget** — deleted-but-retained messages keep consuming context window and cost on every subsequent call.

Scenario: a user pastes an API key by mistake, deletes the message, and continues — but several turns later the agent echoes the key, because it was never removed from the SDK context.

## Goal

When a user deletes one or more messages in an Agent / Assistant conversation, those messages are removed from **both** the UI and the model's working context, so the model no longer sees or references the deleted content in any subsequent turn.

## Spec

- **Two-way delete.** Deleting a message (single or multi-select) removes it from the rendered conversation and from the runtime context used for the next model call.
- **Covers all message kinds.** User messages, assistant messages, and tool-call / tool-result pairs can each be removed; deleting an assistant turn also drops its associated tool calls and results, so no orphaned context remains.
- **Session re-sync.** Because the Claude Agent SDK owns the session transcript, a delete reconciles the SDK session to match the surviving on-screen messages (editing the session in place where supported, otherwise re-establishing it from the remaining messages).
- **Immediate effect.** The next user turn after a delete is sent with the trimmed context — no app restart or manually started new session.
- **Persists across reload.** After delete + reload, the restored context matches what's on screen; the deletion is durable, not just visual.
- **Graceful when unsupported.** If a provider / runtime cannot edit an in-flight session, fall back to rebuilding the session from the remaining messages, and show a brief notice when a hard reset was required.

## Verification

- Delete a message containing a unique codeword (e.g. `BANANA-42`), then ask "what was the codeword?" → the agent has no record of it.
- Send a wrong instruction, delete it, then tell the agent to continue → it acts only on the surviving instructions.
- Delete an assistant turn that called a tool → the tool call and its result are both gone from context; a follow-up shows no memory of that tool output.
- Delete a message, fully reload the conversation, then ask something that would reveal the deleted content → still absent.
- Multi-select three messages and delete → all three leave the context in one operation, and the next turn reflects it.
- On a runtime that can't edit a live session, the delete still yields a trimmed context (via rebuild), with a one-line "context updated" notice.

title: [Feature]: Usage dashboard — view daily / weekly / total token usage
body:
## Background

Users have no in-app way to see how much they're spending. Token usage and cost accrue silently across chats and agent runs, and checking means logging into each provider's own console — if it offers one at all. As models get pricier and agents run autonomously, "how much did I use today / this week" is a basic question Cherry can't answer. Competitors such as OpenAI Codex (`/usage`) already surface daily / weekly / cumulative usage in-tool.

Reality to scope around: **usage-data availability varies by provider.** CherryIn and providers that return usage in their API responses can be aggregated accurately; many third-party / OpenAI-compatible providers don't return reliable per-request token counts, so full cross-provider coverage isn't possible.

Scenario: a user runs agents all week, then wonders why their CherryIn balance dropped — with no in-app breakdown they can't tell which day or which model spent it.

## Goal

The user can see their token usage over time — daily, weekly, and cumulative — broken down by provider and model where the data exists, without leaving Cherry Studio.

## Spec

- **Time rollups.** Daily, weekly, and cumulative token totals (and cost where available), shown as a simple chart plus table.
- **Breakdown.** Split usage by provider and model; where available, separate input / output / cache tokens.
- **Source-aware.** For providers that report usage (e.g. CherryIn) show real numbers; for those that don't, clearly mark "usage not available" rather than guessing or showing zero.
- **Chat + agent.** Usage from both normal chat and agent runs is counted in the same totals.
- **Local only.** Usage is computed and stored on-device; nothing goes to Cherry-controlled telemetry.
- **Drill-in.** Selecting a day or a model shows the underlying breakdown for that slice.

## Verification

- After a day of use, the dashboard shows today's total tokens and cost, split by model.
- Switch to weekly → the last 7 days aggregate correctly; cumulative shows the all-time total.
- A provider that doesn't report usage shows "usage not available", not zero or a fabricated number.
- An agent run's tokens appear in the same totals as chat usage.
- Drill into one model → input/output (and cache, where reported) token split is shown.
- Reference parity: daily / weekly / cumulative views mirror what OpenAI Codex `/usage` offers.

title: [Feature]: Improve knowledge base retrieval recall (hybrid search / reranking / metadata filtering / chunk tagging)
body:
## Background

Knowledge base retrieval today relies on embedding (vector) similarity alone. That misses relevant chunks whenever the query wording differs from the source text, when exact keywords matter (names, codes, IDs), or in domain corpora where semantic similarity is weak. The result is low recall: the right passage exists in the KB but never reaches the model's context, so answers are incomplete or wrong and users lose trust in the knowledge base.

This is a parent / umbrella requirement to raise KB recall, tracking candidate approaches rather than committing to one mechanism. (Reframed from an original "tag chunks to improve recall" request — manual tagging is just one, weak, option.)

Scenario: a user asks about error code "E-4012"; the chunk that explains it exists but uses different surrounding wording, so pure vector search ranks it below the cutoff and the model answers "no information found".

## Goal

The user gets noticeably higher retrieval recall from their knowledge bases — relevant chunks reliably reach the model's context — through retrieval improvements that need no manual per-chunk effort.

## Spec

- **Hybrid search.** Combine lexical (BM25 / keyword) retrieval with vector search and fuse the results (e.g. RRF), so exact-keyword matches aren't lost by embeddings alone.
- **Reranking.** An optional second-stage cross-encoder / rerank model reorders a larger candidate set and lifts truly relevant chunks above the cutoff.
- **Metadata filtering.** Index chunk metadata (source, section, type, date) and allow filtering / boosting by it at query time.
- **Chunking quality.** Tune chunk size / overlap and use structure-aware splitting to reduce fragmentation of relevant content.
- **Chunk tagging (one option).** Optionally attach tags to chunks (manual and/or rule-based) and use them in retrieval — explicitly the lowest-priority approach, since manual tagging rarely scales.
- **Measurable.** A way to compare recall before/after on the user's own KB (e.g. a small eval set), so gains are verified rather than assumed.

## Verification

- A query whose answer uses different wording than the source still retrieves the correct chunk (hybrid + rerank) where pure vector search missed it.
- An exact-keyword query (a code / ID) returns the chunk containing that token even when its embedding similarity is low.
- Enabling reranking measurably raises the rank of the correct chunk on a sample query set.
- A metadata filter ("only this source / section") narrows retrieval correctly.
- On a user-provided eval set, recall@k after the changes beats the vector-only baseline.

title: [Feature]: Knowledge base — add an option to hide inline reference/citation markers
body:
## Background

When a knowledge base answers a question, Cherry inserts inline reference / citation markers into the response text (the small superscript / bracketed source markers). They help trace sources, but some users find them visually noisy — they clutter the prose, break reading flow, and are unwanted when the user just wants a clean answer or is copying the text elsewhere. There's currently no way to turn them off.

Scenario: a user builds a KB to draft documents; every generated paragraph is peppered with citation markers they then have to manually strip before pasting into their doc.

## Goal

The user can choose to hide the inline reference / citation markers in knowledge-base answers, getting clean prose, while still being able to reach the underlying sources when they want them.

## Spec

- **Toggle.** A setting hides / shows inline reference markers in KB-grounded answers; default preserves current behavior (markers shown).
- **Sources still reachable.** Hiding the inline markers does not remove the citations — sources stay accessible (e.g. a sources list under the message, or on hover), so traceability isn't lost.
- **Clean copy.** With markers hidden, copying the answer yields clean text with no marker artifacts.
- **Consistent.** Applies across chat and agent answers that use knowledge bases, and to both streaming and final rendered text.

## Verification

- Toggle off → a KB-grounded answer renders with no inline markers; toggle on → markers return.
- With markers hidden, the sources are still available via the sources list / hover.
- Copy a marker-hidden answer → the clipboard text contains no citation-marker characters.
- Default (fresh install / existing users) keeps markers visible — no behavior change unless opted in.

## Related

#11646

title: [Feature]: New Model Launch Notification with One-Click Try
body:
## Background

When a new flagship model launches (e.g. Kimi K2.7), users searching for it in the conversation model picker can't find it — the list is stale until they manually go into provider settings and refresh. Most users don't know to do this, so they miss newly available models and a smoother path to trying them.

## Goal

Proactively let users know when a notable new model becomes available and let them start using it in one click, without hunting through provider settings.

## Spec

- When a notable/flagship model becomes available, the app surfaces a non-intrusive in-app banner announcing it (server-driven announcement, not client-side polling of provider lists).
- The banner offers a primary "Try it now" action that fetches the latest model list for the relevant provider and switches the active conversation to the new model in one step.
- If the user is not registered with CherryIN, the "Try it now" flow instead guides them through CherryIN registration before enabling the model.
- The banner is dismissible/ignorable, and the same announcement is not shown again after the user dismisses or acts on it.
- Announcements are targeted (one announcement = one model/promotion) and do not stack or repeatedly interrupt the user.

## Verification

- A new flagship model is announced; the user sees a non-intrusive banner without having opened provider settings.
- Clicking "Try it now" pulls the updated model list and the current conversation is switched to the announced model without extra manual steps.
- A user who is not registered with CherryIN clicking "Try it now" is routed into the CherryIN registration flow.
- After the user dismisses an announcement, that same announcement does not reappear on later launches.
- Two different announcements do not pile up on screen at the same time.

## Related

title: [Feature]: Custom Image Icon for Assistants
body:
## Background

When creating or editing an assistant, users can only pick from the built-in emoji/icon set. Several users have asked for a more personal feel — role-play and persona setups in particular feel impersonal when every assistant uses the same generic AI-style glyphs. They want to set a real picture (their own avatar, a character image, a logo) as the assistant's icon.

## Goal

Users can set a custom local image as an assistant's icon, in addition to the existing built-in emoji/icon options.

## Spec

- When choosing an assistant icon, users see an additional option to upload an image from their local machine alongside the existing emoji/icon picker.
- After selecting an image, users can perform a simple crop to frame the icon before confirming.
- The custom image icon is shown wherever the assistant's icon appears (assistant list, topic header, message avatar).
- Removing the custom image reverts the assistant to a built-in icon.
- A custom image set on one assistant applies only to that assistant and does not affect others.

## Verification

- Open an assistant's edit panel, choose "upload image", pick a local PNG → the icon picker now shows that image; after saving, the assistant list and chat header display the cropped image instead of an emoji.
- Upload a non-square image and crop it to a square frame → the saved icon shows only the cropped region, not the full original image.
- Set a custom image on assistant A but not on assistant B → B keeps its built-in icon; only A shows the custom image.
- Remove the custom image from assistant A → it falls back to a built-in icon and no longer shows the uploaded picture.
- Custom image icons persist after restarting the app.

title: [Feature]: Add Anysearch as a Web Search Provider
body:
## Background

Users who rely on web search for in-depth research find that the currently available search providers do not give results deep enough for their needs. One concrete request is to add Anysearch (https://www.anysearch.com) as a web search provider, which the requester believes better fits deep-search scenarios.

## Goal

Users can select Anysearch as a web search provider and use it to power web search in conversations.

## Spec

- Anysearch appears as a selectable option in the web search provider list.
- Users can configure their Anysearch API credentials in settings, the same way other web search providers are configured.
- Once configured and selected, web searches triggered in a conversation are served by Anysearch and its results are used to ground the model's answer.
- If the Anysearch credentials are missing or invalid, the user gets a clear error and search falls back to its normal not-configured state rather than failing silently.

## Verification

- In web search settings, the provider list includes Anysearch; selecting it reveals a field to enter the API key.
- With a valid Anysearch key configured and selected as the active provider, ask a question that requires fresh information → the answer cites results retrieved via Anysearch.
- Enter an invalid Anysearch key and trigger a search → a clear error is shown indicating the credential problem; the app does not crash.
- Switch the active provider from Anysearch to another configured provider → subsequent searches use the newly selected provider, not Anysearch.

title: [Feature]: Migrate Feishu/Lark Integration to Official Channel SDK
body:
## Background

Cherry Studio's Feishu/Lark channel integration was built by hand on top of the low-level Lark SDK, covering message parsing, streaming card updates, app registration, and group authorization as bespoke code. This hand-written layer is large to maintain and lacks several robustness behaviors (deduplication, per-chat message queuing, stale-message filtering, connection keepalive) that the team would otherwise have to build and maintain itself. An official higher-level Lark channel library (@larksuite/channel) now packages exactly these patterns.

## Goal

Move the Feishu/Lark integration onto the official higher-level channel library so that the same user-facing capabilities are retained with less custom code and added robustness, with no regression for existing Feishu/Lark users.

## Spec

- All current Feishu/Lark channel capabilities remain available after the migration: receiving text, image, and file messages; streaming reply cards; QR-code app registration; and group/DM authorization.
- Streaming replies continue to update incrementally and handle long responses without breaking the card.
- The integration gains resilience behaviors: duplicate incoming messages are ignored, messages within a single chat are handled in order, stale/expired messages are dropped, and the connection auto-recovers after a drop.
- Existing Feishu/Lark channel configurations continue to work after upgrade without the user needing to re-set them up.

## Verification

- After migrating, in a configured Lark group send text, an image, and a file to the bot → each is received and handled correctly, matching pre-migration behavior.
- Trigger a long streaming reply that exceeds the single-card size limit → the reply continues across the rollover without truncation or a broken card.
- Send the same message twice in quick succession (or simulate a redelivered event) → the bot responds only once.
- Drop and restore the network connection while the bot is idle → it reconnects automatically and resumes handling new messages without a manual restart.
- Upgrade from a build with an existing Feishu/Lark configuration → the bot keeps working with the previously saved settings, no reconfiguration required.

title: [Feature]: Instrument Official Website With PostHog Analytics
body:
## Background

The Cherry Studio official website currently has no structured product analytics. Without behavioral data — which pages visitors land on, where they drop off, which download/CTA buttons they click, how they move from landing to conversion — the team makes website and product decisions on guesswork rather than evidence.

## Goal

Instrument the official website with PostHog event tracking so the team can analyze visitor behavior and ground website/product decisions in real usage data.

## Spec

- Page views across the official website are captured automatically, including referrer, entry page, and device/locale context.
- Key conversion actions are tracked as named events — at minimum: download button clicks (per platform), primary navigation clicks, and outbound links to the repo/docs/community.
- Tracking respects user privacy expectations: it collects no personally identifying content and honors Do-Not-Track / cookie-consent where applicable.
- Captured events flow into the team's PostHog project so funnels (landing → download) and retention can be analyzed there.

## Verification

- Visiting any website page produces a `$pageview` event in PostHog within seconds, carrying the correct path and referrer.
- Clicking the macOS download button fires a distinct, identifiable event separate from the Windows/Linux download buttons.
- A funnel from website landing to download-button click can be built in PostHog and shows non-zero conversion.
- A visitor with Do-Not-Track enabled (or who declines consent, where a consent banner is shown) generates no tracked events.
- No event payload contains email addresses, full URLs with auth tokens, or other PII.

## Related

Internal infrastructure requirement — no external user issue.

title: [Feature]: Migrate Bundled Google Code CLI From Gemini CLI to Antigravity CLI
body:
## Background

Cherry Studio bundles the Gemini CLI so users can drive Google models through a built-in code agent. Google is retiring Gemini CLI access for Google One and unpaid tiers and is steering users to the new Antigravity CLI. Users on free/Google One tiers will find the bundled Gemini CLI stops serving requests, breaking that workflow inside Cherry Studio.

## Goal

Users can continue using Google's code CLI from within Cherry Studio after the Gemini CLI deprecation, by migrating the integration to Antigravity CLI.

## Spec

- The built-in Google code CLI integration uses Antigravity CLI as its backing tool instead of (or in addition to) the deprecated Gemini CLI.
- Authentication and account selection work with Antigravity CLI, including free/Google One tier accounts that Gemini CLI no longer serves.
- Existing users whose configuration referenced the Gemini CLI are transitioned without manual reinstallation or a broken state.
- If both CLIs remain available for a transition period, the user can see which backend is active and the default points to the supported one.

## Verification

- A user on a free/Google One Google account can authenticate and run a code task through the Google CLI integration and receive a successful response (where Gemini CLI would now refuse).
- After upgrading from a version that used Gemini CLI, the Google CLI integration is functional on first launch without the user reinstalling or reconfiguring it.
- Launching a code task shows the request being served by Antigravity CLI, not the deprecated Gemini CLI.
- A user with no Google account configured is prompted to authenticate rather than hitting a silent failure.

title: [Feature]: In-Conversation Context Outline and Message Navigation
body:
## Background

In a long single conversation, users have no fast way to jump back to an earlier message. Cherry Studio can summarize the content of one model turn, but offers no overview that lets users locate a specific earlier exchange across many turns — so scrolling through a long thread to find "the part where I asked about X" is slow and frustrating.

## Goal

Within a single conversation, users can browse an outline of the turns and jump directly to any earlier message.

## Spec

- A conversation outline lists the turns in the current conversation, each entry showing a short preview of the user's input (and/or the assistant's reply) so the user can recognize it.
- Clicking an outline entry scrolls the conversation to and highlights that turn.
- The outline updates as the conversation grows, staying in sync with new turns.
- Users can search/filter the outline by text to locate a turn by keyword rather than by scrolling.
- The outline can be opened and dismissed without disrupting the ongoing conversation.

## Verification

- In a conversation with 30+ turns, opening the outline shows an entry per turn with a recognizable preview snippet of each.
- Clicking an entry near the top of the outline scrolls the message list to that exact turn and visibly highlights it.
- Typing a keyword that appears in one earlier message filters the outline to the matching turn(s); clicking the result jumps to it.
- Sending a new message adds a corresponding entry at the end of the outline without requiring a manual refresh.
- Searching for a keyword that appears in no turn yields an empty outline state rather than an error.

## Related

#16116

title: [Feature]: Auto-Sync Local Folder to Knowledge Base With Incremental Re-Indexing
body:
## Background

Users who maintain a local RAG knowledge base by writing files to a folder (e.g. via the File System MCP tool) must manually re-index the knowledge base every time a file is added, changed, or removed before the new content becomes searchable. This manual refresh breaks the otherwise automatic "search → save → reuse" loop, is easy to forget, and prevents the knowledge base from growing hands-free as the user works.

## Goal

Users can bind a local folder to a knowledge base so that file additions, edits, and deletions in that folder are detected and incrementally re-indexed automatically, with optional review before new content enters the base.

## Spec

- A user can bind a knowledge base to a local folder; the app watches that folder for file additions, modifications, and deletions in the background.
- When a watched file is added or changed, the knowledge base is incrementally re-indexed for just that file — no full rebuild and no manual refresh.
- When a watched file is deleted, its content is removed from the knowledge base index.
- Users can optionally require a review step: newly detected files are presented as a list the user confirms before they are indexed, so unwanted or erroneous files can be excluded.
- Auto-sync can be enabled or disabled per bound folder.

## Verification

- After binding a folder, writing a new Markdown file into it makes that file's content retrievable in the knowledge base within a short delay, with no manual re-index.
- Editing an already-indexed file so it contains a new term makes a query for that term return the updated content; the stale version is no longer returned.
- Deleting a file from the watched folder makes its content no longer appear in retrieval results.
- With the review step enabled, a newly added file does NOT enter the index until the user confirms it in the pending-files list; declining it leaves it out.
- Disabling auto-sync on a bound folder stops further automatic indexing while leaving already-indexed content searchable.

## Related

#16114

title: [Feature]: Allow Users to Select MinerU Parsing Mode (Pipeline / VLM / Hybrid)
body:
## Background

When parsing documents with MinerU for knowledge bases or in-conversation file uploads, different document types and accuracy needs call for different parsing strategies. Today the parsing strategy is fixed, so users cannot trade off between speed and extraction quality, and scanned/image-heavy or complex-layout documents may be parsed sub-optimally.

## Goal

Let users choose the MinerU parsing mode (Pipeline / VLM / Hybrid) so document parsing can be matched to the document type and the desired accuracy.

## Spec

- In the MinerU document-parsing settings, expose a parsing-mode selector with at least: Pipeline, VLM, and Hybrid.
- Each mode shows a short, plain-language description of when to use it (e.g. fast/general vs. higher accuracy for complex or image-based documents).
- The selected mode is persisted and applied to subsequent MinerU parsing tasks (knowledge base preprocessing and in-conversation file parsing) until the user changes it.
- A sensible default mode is preselected so users who do not care still get reasonable results without configuration.
- The mode choice is respected for both single-file and directory/batch uploads.

## Verification

- Opening MinerU parsing settings shows a mode selector offering Pipeline, VLM, and Hybrid.
- Selecting a non-default mode and parsing a document causes that mode to be used; reopening the app preserves the selection.
- Parsing an image-based / scanned PDF in VLM (or Hybrid) yields better text extraction than Pipeline on the same file.
- Switching modes does not break existing knowledge bases already parsed under a previous mode.
- Default mode is applied when the user has never changed the setting.

title: [Feature]: Default Sidebar Leads with Agent for New Users
body:
## Background

The left sidebar lists top-level sections in a default order that new installs inherit and users can customize later. Today that default puts Chat (Assistants) ahead of the Agent section, so a brand-new user lands Chat-first and Agent — V2's flagship capability — isn't the first thing they see. We want newcomers to lead with Agent, without disturbing existing users who already have a settled sidebar and muscle memory.

## Goal

New users see the Agent section as the first sidebar entry — before Chat — while existing users keep their current sidebar order and customizations unchanged.

## Spec

- A new user's default sidebar places the Agent section before the Chat (Assistants) section, so Agent is the first entry they see.
- Existing users' sidebar order and customizations are preserved exactly; this change never reorders an existing user's sidebar.
- The new ordering is only the initial default — after first run a new user can freely reorder or hide entries, including moving Chat above Agent.
- New-vs-existing is decided once when this ships and does not flip afterward.

## Verification

- Fresh install → the sidebar's first entry is Agent, with Chat (Assistants) immediately after.
- An existing user updates to this version → their sidebar order is unchanged; nothing is reordered.
- A new user drags Chat above Agent and restarts → the customized order persists; the default does not re-apply.
- An existing user who had hidden or reordered icons keeps every one of those choices after the update.
- A new user hides the Agent entry → it stays hidden on next launch (not forcibly restored).

## Related

#16053

title: [Bug]: CherryIN gemini-3.1 AI_APICallError
[Feature]: Context-driven feature/plugin resolution to avoid per-fallback recompute in multi-model requests
body:
### Issue Checklist

- [x] I understand that issues are for reporting problems and requesting features, not for off-topic comments, and I will provide as much detail as possible to help resolve the issue.
- [x] I have checked the pinned issues and searched through the existing open issues, closed issues, and discussions and did not find a similar suggestion.
- [x] I have provided a short and descriptive title so that developers can quickly understand the issue when browsing the issue list.
- [x] The latest version of Cherry Studio does not include the feature I am suggesting.

### Platform

macOS (architecture change — affects all platforms)

### Version

2.0.0-dev (main)

### Is your feature request related to an existing issue?

Follow-up from the model retry/fallback work in #16057.

The request-feature/plugin system (`src/main/ai/runtime/aiSdk/params/`) is **model-specific by construction**: `collectFromFeatures(scope, features)` gates each feature with `feature.applies(scope)` against one specific model, and each plugin **closes over** values computed from that model (e.g. `createQwenThinkingPlugin(enableThinking)` bakes the decision into a middleware via closure; `configureContext` never reads `context.modelId` at resolve time).

Consequence: a model's plugin set + middleware/params can only be obtained by running `buildAgentParams` for *that* model. So any feature that resolves a **second** model in the same request — notably **cross-model retry/fallback** (#16057) — must re-run `buildAgentParams` per fallback to recompute its plugins and params. The fallback fix in #16057 does exactly this (`AiService.buildFallbackModels` → `resolveLanguageModel(..., plugins)`), which works but means the app layer recomputes per fallback and the retry registration cannot live purely in `@cherrystudio/ai-core` (aiCore is provider-agnostic and cannot derive a model's correct plugin set).

### Desired Solution

Refactor the feature/plugin layer to be **context-driven** instead of build-time/closure-driven:

- Each feature decides applicability and middleware/params from the **resolving model in `context`** at resolve time, rather than being gated by `applies(scope)` and closing over a model when the plugin is constructed.
- A single registered plugin set then **self-configures** for whatever model `pluginEngine.resolveModel(modelId)` is resolving — primary or fallback.

Payoff:
- Cross-model fallback (and any multi-model request feature) no longer needs a per-fallback `buildAgentParams` recompute.
- Retry/fallback registration can move into the `@cherrystudio/ai-core` executor/plugin pipeline (the natural layer), keeping `src/main/ai` thinner.
- One code path shapes every resolved model identically, reducing drift between primary and fallback behavior.

### Alternative Solutions

- **Status quo (shipped in #16057):** app-layer per-fallback `buildAgentParams` + `resolveLanguageModel(plugins)`. Correct, but recomputes per fallback and keeps retry registration in the app layer. Acceptable near-term; this issue tracks the cleaner architecture.

### Additional Information

This is a large, higher-risk rewrite touching every feature in `src/main/ai/runtime/aiSdk/params/features/` and the `collectFromFeatures` / `pluginEngine.resolveModel` contract. It should be scoped and designed separately (it is explicitly out of scope for #16057). No user-visible behavior change is intended — it is an internal refactor enabling cheaper, more uniform multi-model resolution.

title: 抽象 latest-wins 异步副作用收敛器供 Preference 驱动服务复用
body:
## 背景

在 review PR #16207 时，我们发现 `ProxyManager` 原先没有接上 `app.proxy.*` Preference/lifecycle，后续修复中又暴露出一个更通用的问题：Preference 变化经常触发异步副作用，但各服务目前各自手写 busy flag / `void async` / fire-and-forget，容易出现错误丢失或最终状态与用户最后选择不一致。

这不是“给所有订阅加消息队列”的需求。订阅层只应表达事实：某个 key changed。真实需求更窄：**对 Preference 驱动的异步副作用，提供 single-flight + latest-wins + error logging 的浅层复用模式**。

## 消费者考古 / 现有信号

### 强信号

- `ProxyManager`
  - 代理配置是异步副作用：`getSystemProxy()`、`session.setProxy()`、`app.setProxy()`、Node proxy apply。
  - 快速切换 `system → custom → none` 时，用户最后选择应胜出，中间状态不需要 FIFO 完整执行。
- `ApiGatewayService`
  - 已经手写了 `desiredEnabled + reconciling`，本质就是 latest-wins 收敛器。
  - 说明该模式已在代码中真实存在，而不是假想需求。

### 候选消费者

- `AnalyticsService`
  - Preference 回调中 `void this.activate()` / `void this.deactivate()`。
  - `onDeactivate()` 是 async，快速开关可能导致最终状态和最后 preference 不一致。
- `SelectionService`
  - Preference 回调中 `void this.activate()` / `void this.deactivate()`，并且启动阶段有 `setImmediate` warm-up。
  - 需要确认快速切换/延迟激活时是否可能重新激活已关闭功能。
- `QuickAssistantService` / `TrayService`
  - 当前 activate/deactivate 多数同步，需求较弱；主要风险是 `void` 错误处理，不一定需要迁移。

### 不应迁移的消费者

- `ThemeService`
- `AppMenuService`
- `ShortcutService`
- `SelectionService` 的普通 filter/trigger/zoom 配置更新

这些大多是同步、幂等、轻量更新，引入队列/收敛器会是过度抽象。

## 建议方向

抽象一个很浅的工具，而不是通用消息队列，例如：

- `LatestAsyncRunner`
- `AsyncConverger`
- `DesiredStateReconciler`

目标语义：

1. 同一时间只执行一个 `apply`；
2. 执行中收到新请求时只保留最新 snapshot；
3. 当前执行结束后，如果最新 snapshot 仍未收敛，再执行一次；
4. 异步错误集中 catch/log；
5. 支持 dispose，服务停止后不再继续运行；
6. 不改变 `PreferenceService.subscribeChange` 的基础语义。

伪代码：

```ts
const runner = createLatestAsyncRunner<ProxyConfig>({
  name: 'ProxyManager.applyProxy',
  getSnapshot: readProxyConfigFromPreferences,
  isSettled: (next) => isSameProxyConfig(currentConfig, next),
  apply: (next) => configureProxy(next),
  onError: (error, next) => logger.error('Failed to apply proxy', error)
})

preferenceService.subscribeMultipleChanges(proxyKeys, () => {
  runner.request()
})
```

## 非目标

- 不做持久化队列；
- 不做优先级队列；
- 不做 retry/backoff；
- 不把所有 Preference 订阅都迁移；
- 不把 policy 塞进 `PreferenceService`。

## 验收标准

- 明确选择 2–3 个真实消费者迁移，优先考虑 `ProxyManager` 和 `ApiGatewayService`；
- 保持工具 API 小而具体，避免泛化为通用 message queue；
- 每个迁移消费者都有测试覆盖快速连续触发时“最后状态胜出”；
- 同步、幂等的订阅消费者保持现状。

title: [Feature]: Graceful degradation when MCP server fails to initialize — prevent single MCP failure from blocking Agent startup
body:
## Issue Checklist

- [x] I understand that issues are for reporting problems and requesting features, not for off-topic comments, and I will provide as much detail as possible to help resolve the issue.
- [x] I have checked the pinned issues and searched through the existing open issues, closed issues, and discussions and did not find a similar suggestion.
- [x] I have provided a short and descriptive title so that developers can quickly understand the issue when browsing the issue list.
- [x] The latest version of Cherry Studio does not include the feature I am suggesting.

## Platform

macOS

## Version

v1.9.11

## Is your feature request related to an existing issue?

When Cherry Claw (Agent) starts up, it initializes all configured MCP servers simultaneously. If any single MCP server fails to connect — due to network issues, invalid API keys, or slow remote services (e.g., `consensus`, `scite`) — the entire Agent fails to start, leaving the user unable to use Cherry Claw at all.

The only workaround is to manually delete the problematic MCP servers from settings, which is not a good user experience.

## Desired Solution

Implement graceful degradation during Agent startup:

- If an individual MCP server fails to initialize (timeout / connection error / auth failure), **skip it and continue** the startup process.
- Mark the failed MCP as "unavailable" with a warning indicator (e.g., red badge) in the Agent's tool list.
- Allow the Agent to start and operate normally with the remaining available MCPs.
- Optionally, show a non-blocking notification like: *"2 MCP servers failed to connect. Agent started with limited tools."*

## Alternative Solutions

- Add a per-MCP "disable on startup failure" toggle so users can control which MCPs are critical vs. optional.
- Add a startup timeout setting per MCP server.

## Additional Information

Reproduced by: having `consensus` and `scite` MCP servers configured. Cherry Claw fails to launch. After removing these two servers, Cherry Claw starts normally. This suggests the failure is caused by blocking on unresponsive remote MCP endpoints during Agent initialization.

### Platform

Windows

### Version

v1.9.11

### Bug Description

When using MiniMax-M3 model via Cherry Studio, every chat request fails with a 400 Bad Request error. The root cause is that Cherry Studio sends "thinking": { "type": "enabled" } in the request body, but the MiniMax-M3 API does not accept "enabled" as a valid value for thinking.type.


### Steps To Reproduce

1.Add MiniMax-M3 as a model provider in Cherry Studio.
2. Set the Thinking Intensity / Reasoning option to any level other than "Off" (e.g., "Default", "Low", "Medium", "High" — all of them trigger the bug).
3. Send a message or let MiniMax-M3 generate any content.
4. The API call fails immediately with a 400 Bad Request error.

### Expected Behavior

Cherry Studio should send one of the following instead of "enabled":
• "thinking": { "type": "adaptive" } — to allow the model to decide
• "thinking": { "type": "disabled" } — to turn off thinking entirely
Or, the "Thinking Intensity" setting should map to "adaptive" (or simply omit the thinking field) when the user selects "Default".

### Relevant Log Output

```shell
"error": {
    "message": "invalid params, invalid ***.type: \"enabled\" (allowed: adaptive, disabled) (2013)",
    "type": "rix_api_error",
    "param": "",
    "code": null
  }
}
```

### Additional Context

I set the Thinking Intensity / Reasoning Effort option to "Default" in the model settings, but the error still occurs. It appears that "Default" maps to "type": "enabled" in the request, which is not a valid value for MiniMax.
According to the MiniMax API documentation, the only accepted values for thinking.type are:
"adaptive" — the model decides when to use thinking
"disabled" — thinking is turned off
This issue was reproduced using a third-party API proxy (dmxapi.cn), but the error originates from the MiniMax API itself, so it likely affects all endpoints that conform to MiniMax's official API spec.
A related but different error also occurs with older MiniMax models (e.g., MiniMax-01): "reasoning part reasoning-0 not found", which suggests a broader compatibility issue with Cherry Studio's MiniMax reasoning/thinking adapter.

title: [Bug]: Startup recovery re-dispatches a retry job already running in the current process
body:
### Issue Checklist

- [x] I understand that issues are for feedback and problem solving, not for complaining in the comment section, and will provide as much information as possible to help solve the problem.
- [x] My issue is not listed in the [FAQ](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/issues/3881).
- [x] I've looked at **pinned issues** and searched for existing Open/Closed Issues and Discussions, no similar issue or discussion was found.
- [x] I've filled in short, clear headings so that developers can quickly identify a rough idea of what to expect.
- [x] I've confirmed that I am using the latest version of Cherry Studio.

### Platform

macOS (the race is **platform-independent** — it lives in the cross-platform job runtime; it was first reproduced on macOS via the system OCR handler).

### Version

`2.0.0-dev` (`main` @ `d04d38063`)

### Bug Description

The startup-recovery sweep in the shared job subsystem can re-dispatch a job that is **still executing in the current process**, causing the same job to run twice.

For handlers declared with `recovery: 'retry'` (e.g. `file-processing.background`), `runStartupRecovery` (`src/main/core/job/runtime/recovery.ts`) runs ~60s after `onAllReady` and resets every non-terminal `running` row of that handler back to `pending`, then re-dispatches it. It does **not** check whether that row is owned by a job the current `JobManager` is still running. So a job that was enqueued and started inside the startup-recovery window gets reset `running → pending` and dispatched a second time. Both runs then race to finalize the same row.

This is a **pre-existing** defect in the core job runtime and affects **all** job types that use `recovery: 'retry'` (cron / knowledge / file-processing), not any single feature.

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Register a `recovery: 'retry'` job handler (any of cron / knowledge / file-processing; the system OCR `image_to_text` handler is the easiest trigger).
2. Enqueue a job for that handler within ~60s of app start, so it is still `running` when the startup-recovery sweep fires.
3. Observe the handler `execute` run **twice** for a single `enqueue`, with both runs competing to finalize the same job row.

### Expected Behavior

A job that the current process is already executing must be **left alone** by startup recovery — the handler runs exactly once per enqueue. Recovery should only reset/re-dispatch rows that are genuinely orphaned (not in-flight in this process).

### Relevant Log Output

```shell
14:48:55 [FileProcessingService] Enqueued file processing job { feature: 'image_to_text', ... }
14:48:55 [SystemImageToTextHandler] Running system OCR for image_to_text { ... }   # 1st run
14:49:25 [JobRecovery] Retry recovery { type: 'file-processing.background', reset: 1, ... }
14:49:25 [JobManager] Resurrected queues from non-terminal jobs { count: 1 }
14:49:25 [SystemImageToTextHandler] Running system OCR for image_to_text { ... }   # 2nd run (duplicate)
```

### Additional Context

- **Surfaced by** PR #16125 (route Translate image OCR through File Processing): it is the first feature that reliably enqueues a `retry` job inside the startup-recovery window, turning this latent race into a frequently reproducible one (independently reproduced during review — a single OCR ran the system handler twice).
- **Blast radius:** the fix is in `runStartupRecovery`, shared by every job type — it warrants job-subsystem owner review.
- **Proposed fix:** thread an `isJobInFlight(jobId)` predicate (backed by `JobManager.inFlightExecuted`) into `runStartupRecovery` and filter JobManager-owned in-flight rows out **before** any recovery strategy, so cancel/orphan paths are unaffected. Covered by a new `JobManager.integration.test.ts` regression case.

title: [Bug]: Deleting agent messages in Cherry Studio UI does not remove them from Claude Code SDK .jsonl transcript — deleted messages reappear in context on resume
body:
## Bug Description

When a user deletes a message from an **Agent mode** conversation in the Cherry Studio UI, the deletion only removes the record from Cherry Studio's internal database (`agents.db` → `session_messages` table). It does **not** propagate to the Claude Code SDK's `.jsonl` transcript file on disk.

As a result, when the session is resumed (`--resume <sessionId>`), the SDK reads the full `.jsonl` transcript and reconstructs the conversation history — **including the "deleted" messages**. The model (e.g. Opus 4.6) sees those messages in its context window as if they were never deleted.

## Reproduction Steps

1. Open an Agent mode conversation in Cherry Studio
2. Send several messages and get responses
3. Delete one or more messages via the Cherry Studio UI (right-click → delete, or equivalent)
4. Confirm the messages disappear from the Cherry Studio chat view
5. Send a new message in the same session (triggering `--resume`)
6. Observe that the model's response references or is influenced by the "deleted" messages — they are still in its context

## Root Cause — The Binding Chain

```
Cherry Studio DB (agents.db)
  └─ session_messages.agent_session_id = "<sessionId>"
       │  ← deletion happens HERE only
       ▼
Claude Code SDK (--resume <sessionId>)
  └─ reads transcript from:
       <CherryStudio appData>/.claude/projects/<encoded-cwd>/<sessionId>.jsonl
       │  ← NOT updated on deletion
       ▼
Model context window
  └─ receives the FULL .jsonl content, including "deleted" messages
```

The `.jsonl` transcript path on Windows is typically:
```
C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Roaming\CherryStudio\.claude\projects\<encoded-cwd>\<sessionId>.jsonl
```

## Expected Behavior

When a message is deleted from the Cherry Studio UI, the corresponding entry in the `.jsonl` transcript file should also be removed (or marked as deleted), so that subsequent `--resume` calls do not reload deleted messages into the model's context.

## Suggested Fix

When Cherry Studio's message deletion handler fires, it should **also**:

1. Locate the corresponding `.jsonl` file for that agent session
2. Either:
   - **Remove** the matching line(s) from the `.jsonl` file, or
   - **Write a tombstone/deletion marker** that the SDK can interpret to skip those entries during context reconstruction

Option (1) is simpler but requires rewriting the file. Option (2) is append-only friendly but requires SDK-side support.

An alternative interim workaround for users: manually edit the `.jsonl` file to remove the unwanted entries — but this is fragile and not user-friendly.

## Environment

- **Cherry Studio version**: latest (as of 2026-06-23)
- **OS**: Windows 10 Pro
- **Claude Code SDK model**: Opus 4.6
- **Agent mode**: Claude Code (native SDK integration)

这是 PR #13892（安全修复，移除 file:// 白名单）导致的功能回归。该 PR 修复了 RCE 漏洞（GHSA-p6vw-w3p8-4g72），但同时使 PR #9928/#10000（知识库引用打开功能）失效。

类似问题 #14433（vscode:// 被拦截，已修复）。

建议：不需要简单把 file:// 加回白名单，而是为知识库引用创建一个专门的受控 IPC 通道，或限制 file:// 仅能打开 Data/Files/ 目录下的文件，兼顾安全与功能。

title: [Feature]: Richer read-back for persisted tool outputs — fs_read byte-range + search/jq escape hatch
body:
### Issue Checklist

- [x] I understand that issues are for reporting problems and requesting features, not for off-topic comments, and I will provide as much detail as possible to help resolve the issue.
- [x] I have checked the pinned issues and searched through the existing open issues, closed issues, and discussions and did not find a similar suggestion.
- [x] I have provided a short and descriptive title so that developers can quickly understand the issue when browsing the issue list.
- [x] The latest version of Cherry Studio does not include the feature I am suggesting.

### Platform

macOS (platform-agnostic — main-process tool logic; macOS only because that is where it surfaced)

### Version

main @ `feat/context-build-truncation` (PR #15988), 2.0.0-dev

### Is your feature request related to an existing issue?

Follow-up from the maintainer review of #15988 (context-build). That feature persists oversized tool results to a VFS blob and the model reads them back through the `fs_read` builtin. In the aiSdk chat path `fs_read` is the **only** way to read those blobs, and it is purely line-sequential (`offset`/`limit` by line). Two capability gaps remain versus Claude Code's persisted-output read-back protocol:

1. **No byte/char-range (sub-line) read.** A single physical line larger than the per-call char cap — heavily minified JSON, one very long log line — cannot be paged: `fs_read` returns `output-too-large` and everything past the cap is unreachable. (After #15988 lines ≤ cap return in full; only this single-oversized-line case remains.)
2. **No search / structured-query escape hatch.** Claude Code's large-output instructions (`getLargeOutputInstructions`) point the model at **search (Grep)** and **`jq`** for structured queries over the saved file. Cherry's aiSdk chat path exposes only `fs_read` (no Bash/jq/Grep over the VFS blob), so the model can only sequentially page — it can never search or query a large persisted output.

### Desired Solution

Extend the persisted-output read-back surface (some subset):

- A **byte/char-range read mode** on `fs_read` (e.g. a `range` / `byteOffset`+`byteLimit` param) so a single oversized physical line can be retrieved in chunks.
- A **search-over-blob capability**: a Grep-style builtin scoped to the VFS root, or a structured-query (`jq`-style) tool, so the model can locate/extract within a large persisted output instead of only sequential line paging.
- Once these exist, mirror Claude Code's `getLargeOutputInstructions` guidance in the persisted-output system prompt (read 100% of the content / explicitly state if you did not / use search + structured queries).

### Alternative Solutions

- **Wrap/split long physical lines at persist time** so they stay line-pageable — cheaper, but mangles the original bytes and breaks the exact round-trip the truncate layer guarantees. Rejected for now.
- **Do nothing** — acceptable for the common case after #15988 (full-line return), but leaves >cap single-line blobs and structured queries unserved.

### Additional Information

- Surfaced by PR #15988 maintainer review: finding **W1** (single-long-line unrecoverable) + the "no Grep/jq escape hatch" observation.
- Reference (Claude Code read-back design): `mcpOutputStorage.getLargeOutputInstructions` (offset/limit + search + jq), `FileReadTool` / `readFileInRange` (whole-line return, token-budget gating, never chops mid-line).
- Scope: v2 / context-build follow-up — not a v1 issue.

title: [Feature]: 打通"助手 / 智能体 / CherryClaw"三通道，统一为单一智能体渐进式能力体系
body:
### Issue Checklist

- [x] I understand that issues are for reporting problems and requesting features, not for off-topic comments, and I will provide as much detail as possible to help resolve the issue.
- [x] I have checked the pinned issues and searched through the existing [open issues](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/issues), [closed issues](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20state%3Aclosed), and [discussions](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/discussions) and did not find a similar suggestion.
- [x] I have provided a short and descriptive title so that developers can quickly understand the issue when browsing the issue list, rather than vague titles like "A suggestion" or "Stuck."
- [x] The latest version of Cherry Studio does not include the feature I am suggesting.

### Platform

Windows

### Version

v1.9.11

### Is your feature request related to an existing issue?

当前 Cherry Studio 有三个互相独立的概念入口：助手（Assistant）、智能体（Agent）、CherryClaw。从用户视角看，这三者本质上是同一个东西的三种能力等级——"聊天 → 干活 → 自主干活"——却被拆分成了不同的类型、不同的创建入口、不同的能力边界。

具体痛点：
用户被迫做技术决策。 创建时就要在 claude-code / cherry-claw / cherry-assistant 之间选择，但普通用户根本不知道这些类型的区别，也不知道"选错了还能不能改"。
高级能力被锁死。 频道、定时任务、Soul 人格、心跳调度这些能力只有 cherry-claw 类型才有。如果我最初建了一个普通 Agent 做日常对话，后来想让它定时推送——对不起，得重建。
"助手"被排除在外。 用户如果想给一个聊天助手逐步加上执行能力，当前只能另起炉灶建 Agent，无法从"助手"平滑升级。
心智模型碎片化。 "助手"在左侧栏、"智能体"在顶部 Tab、CherryClaw 又在智能体列表里——用户会困惑：它们到底是什么关系？
这与 Cherry Studio 作为"智能体桌面交互平台"的核心定位相矛盾。用户真正需要的是一个统一的智能体，而不是三个分裂的入口。

### Desired Solution

核心思路：将"助手 / 智能体 / CherryClaw"三通道打通合并，统一为"智能体"一个概念，通过渐进式能力开关替代类型选择。

### Alternative Solutions

创建智能体
  │
  ├── 🟢 基础层（对应原"助手"）
  │   └── 设定人格、选模型、调参数
  │   └── 此时就能在对话界面聊天
  │
  ├── 🟡 工具层（对应原"智能体"）
  │   └── 开启开关 → 获得文件读写、命令执行、MCP 工具调用能力
  │
  └── 🔴 自主层（对应原"CherryClaw"）
      └── 开启开关 → 获得 Soul 人格、Cron 调度、IM 频道、心跳唤醒

用户界面变化：
去掉 Agent 类型选择器。 新建 Agent 只有一个入口，不再区分 claude-code / cherry-claw。
用能力开关代替类型。 在 Agent 设置里，工具执行、自主模式等作为可开启的功能，而非创建时的一次性选择。
"助手"并入智能体体系。 现有的"助手"本质上就是一个"仅开启基础层"的智能体，可以直接显示在智能体列表中，或提供一键升级路径。
能力可随时升级。 用户最初只开基础层聊天，后续随时可以打开工具层、自主层，不需要重建。
这与已有的 Issue [#13829](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/issues/13829)（统一 Agent 类型）方向一致，但更进一步——把"助手"也纳入统一体系，彻底消除三通道分裂。

### Additional Information

另外，还有两个反馈；
1）虽然可以通过告知api后让其另外调用模型实现复合组队任务，但目前无法直接实现1拖多的模型场景。
认为可以提升的方式→智体建设中，提供改编智体小队功能：设定主队长模型+辅角色模型。
2）目前cherrystudio仅能在我们在桌面端的时候与我们绑定，频道入口也是个较弱的场景，希望能推出结合“云中台”的同时提供“移动端”入口（提供）。让cherrystudio可以成为个人“贾维斯”。提供不开机也能干定时任务的可能，或者远程让电脑开启通过移动端输入命令让桌面端跑任务的可能。

title: [Feature]: 智能体支持"小队模式"：设定主队长模型 + 辅角色模型，实现 1 拖多协作
body:
### Issue Checklist

- [x] I understand that issues are for reporting problems and requesting features, not for off-topic comments, and I will provide as much detail as possible to help resolve the issue.
- [x] I have checked the pinned issues and searched through the existing [open issues](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/issues), [closed issues](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20state%3Aclosed), and [discussions](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/discussions) and did not find a similar suggestion.
- [x] I have provided a short and descriptive title so that developers can quickly understand the issue when browsing the issue list, rather than vague titles like "A suggestion" or "Stuck."
- [x] The latest version of Cherry Studio does not include the feature I am suggesting.

### Platform

Windows

### Version

1.9.11

### Is your feature request related to an existing issue?

当前 CherryClaw 虽然可以通过在对话中告知 API 地址、手动调度其他模型来完成任务，但这种"口头调度"方式存在明显局限：

无法固化配置。 每次都要在对话里描述"请用 GLM-5 做 A，用 Qwen-Max 做 B"，无法将模型分工保存为智能体的固有配置。
缺乏可视化。 用户看不到"小队"里有哪些角色、各自负责什么，调度全靠文字描述。
协作靠运气。 模型间的任务分配完全依赖 Agent 当场判断，没有预设的分工规则，稳定性差。
与行业趋势脱节。 当前 Codex + Claude Code 的"配对 Agent"模式已经证明跨模型协作的巨大价值，Cherry Studio 有天然的多模型优势（已配置几十个模型提供商），却缺少让它们在同一个 Agent 内组队协作的界面。

### Desired Solution

在智能体设置中新增"小队模式"配置面板：
智能体设置
  │
  ├── 基础配置（名称、头像、模型）
  │
  ├── 🆕 小队模式
  │   ├── 主队长模型：DeepSeek-V4Pro  ← 负责规划、调度、整合
  │   │
  │   ├── 辅角色 1：GLM-5
  │   │   ├── 角色标签：中文文案
  │   │   ├── 擅长的任务类型：[✓] 文案写作  [✓] 翻译  [ ] 代码
  │   │   └── 调用优先级：高
  │   │
  │   ├── 辅角色 2：MiniMax-M2.5
  │   │   ├── 角色标签：创意发散
  │   │   ├── 擅长的任务类型：[✓] 头脑风暴  [✓] 创意文案
  │   │   └── 调用优先级：中
  │   │
  │   ├── 辅角色 3：Kimi-K2.6
  │   │   ├── 角色标签：长文分析
  │   │   ├── 擅长的任务类型：[✓] 文档总结  [✓] 研究分析
  │   │   └── 调用优先级：中
  │   │
  │   └── [+ 添加辅角色]
  │
  └── 自主模式 / 频道 / 定时任务（不变）

工作逻辑：
主队长模型负责接收用户任务 → 拆解 → 根据辅角色的"擅长标签"分派子任务 → 整合结果交付
辅角色只被调用执行其擅长的子任务，不参与全局对话
用户可在对话中看到队长调度辅角色的过程（折叠卡片展示）
底层实现：利用 Cherry Studio 已有的多 Provider 配置，队长调用 OpenAI 兼容 API 向各辅角色模型发起请求即可。

### Alternative Solutions

如果完整的"小队模式"工作量太大，可以先做一个轻量版：
在 Agent 设置中增加"备用模型列表"，Agent 在执行任务时可自行判断是否切换到备用模型
为每个 MCP 工具指定"推荐执行模型"
在对话中增加 /delegate <角色名> <任务> 快捷指令

### Additional Information

Cherry Studio 相比所有竞品最大的优势就是已配置了几十个模型提供商。把这个优势从"用户可以手动切换模型聊天"升级到"Agent 自动调度多模型协作"，就是从一个多模型聊天客户端到一个真正的智能体指挥平台的质变。

- [x] The latest version of Cherry Studio does not include the feature I am suggesting.

### Platform

Windows

### Version

1.9.11

### Is your feature request related to an existing issue?

当前 CherryClaw 的自主能力受限于一个根本问题：电脑关了，它就死了。
定时任务依赖开机。 如果想每天早上 8 点推送简报，电脑必须开着。出差、周末关机、笔记本合盖——任务全部丢失。
IM 频道是弱绑定。 虽然能通过 Telegram/微信收到 CherryClaw 的消息，但 Agent 本体在本地桌面端，频道只是一个"消息转发管道"——手机端只能收消息，不能反向指挥 Agent 干活。
无法远程唤醒。 如果人在外面，想让 CherryClaw 在电脑上跑一个任务（比如处理一份本地文件），当前做不到。
不是真正的"贾维斯"。 真正的个人 AI 助理应该随时在线、随时可达，不论你是在电脑前还是走在路上。这是从"桌面工具"到"个人基础设施"的关键一跃。

### Desired Solution

分两层架构：云中台 + 移动端

一、Cherry Cloud（云中台）
一个轻量云服务，作为 Cherry Studio 桌面端的"影子代理"：
Cherry Cloud 云中台
  │
  ├── 当桌面端在线时：
  │   └── 纯中继，任务透传到本地执行（保留本地优先）
  │
  ├── 当桌面端离线时：
  │   ├── 接管定时任务 → 使用用户在云端配置的 API Key 执行
  │   ├── 接收移动端指令 → 暂存，待桌面端上线后同步执行
  │   └── 基础对话能力 → 用云端模型回复简单消息
  │
  └── 同步层：
      ├── Agent 配置同步（Soul、记忆、任务、频道）
      ├── 对话历史同步
      └── 任务结果回传

关键原则：
本地优先。 桌面端在线时，所有执行都在本地，云中台只做消息路由
云端降级。 桌面端离线时，云中台接管定时任务和基础对话（用用户自己的 API Key）
用户控制。 哪些数据同步到云端、哪些任务允许云端执行，全部由用户配置


二、Cherry Mobile（移动端入口）
一个轻量移动端 App（或小程序），作为 Cherry Studio 的随身入口：
Cherry Mobile
  │
  ├── 对话界面
  │   ├── 与 CherryClaw 聊天（通过云中台中继）
  │   ├── 支持语音输入
  │   └── 查看历史对话
  │
  ├── 任务面板
  │   ├── 查看 / 创建 / 暂停定时任务
  │   ├── 查看任务执行记录
  │   └── 触发一次性任务
  │
  ├── 远程桌面指令 🆕
  │   ├── 向桌面端发送指令（"帮我处理桌面的 report.xlsx"）
  │   ├── 查看桌面端在线状态
  │   ├── 接收桌面端执行结果通知
  │   └── 远程唤醒（WoL / Push Notification）
  │
  └── 通知
      └── 定时任务结果推送

典型场景
场景 | 体验
早上通勤 | 手机收到 CherryClaw 推送的今日简报（云中台执行的定时任务）
开会中 | 手机发消息让 CherryClaw "帮我把上周的销售数据整理成图表"
回到工位 | 电脑开机，任务已同步完成，图表在桌面上等着
周末出差 | 电脑关机，CherryClaw 照常执行定时任务（云端降级），手机可随时对话

### Alternative Solutions

分阶段实施：
Phase 1（最小可行）：先做云中台接管定时任务（桌面端离线时云端兜底），保持 IM 频道推送不中断
Phase 2：加上移动端对话界面（小程序或轻量 App）
Phase 3：实现远程桌面指令和唤醒
或者可以考虑与现有的开源方案（如 OpenClaw 的 Gateway）做桥接，不重复造轮子。

### Additional Information

这一步是从"桌面 AI 客户端"到"个人 AI 基础设施"的跨越。目前市场上没有哪个产品做到了"桌面端深度执行 + 云端兜底 + 移动端随身"三位一体。如果 Cherry Studio 率先打通，就是真正的"个人贾维斯"——不开机也能干活，手机就是遥控器。

title: [Feature]: 技能与记忆可视化：让用户看到 Agent"学会了什么"、能微调、能标记重点
body:
### Issue Checklist

- [x] I understand that issues are for reporting problems and requesting features, not for off-topic comments, and I will provide as much detail as possible to help resolve the issue.
- [x] I have checked the pinned issues and searched through the existing [open issues](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/issues), [closed issues](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20state%3Aclosed), and [discussions](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/discussions) and did not find a similar suggestion.
- [x] I have provided a short and descriptive title so that developers can quickly understand the issue when browsing the issue list, rather than vague titles like "A suggestion" or "Stuck."
- [x] The latest version of Cherry Studio does not include the feature I am suggesting.

### Platform

Windows

### Version

1.9.11

### Is your feature request related to an existing issue?

当前 CherryClaw 的技能系统和记忆系统对用户几乎完全不可见，导致三个核心痛点：

1. 技能是黑盒。 比如，我和 Agent 一起迭代了几十版打磨出的 PPT 构建技能，里面沉淀了大量专属规范——颜色体系、排版参数、KPI 卡片模式、图表防变形规则、副作用隔离模式。但这一切在 Cherry Studio 界面里完全看不到，用户只知道技能"存在"，不知道里面有什么。想微调一个参数？没入口。

2. 记忆不透明。 Agent 有 FACT.md（持久知识）和 JOURNAL（事件日志），但用户无法查看、无法编辑、无法确认"Agent 到底记住了什么"。用户告诉 Agent 一个重要偏好，下次对话 Agent 又忘了——用户不知道这是因为没记、还是记了但没触发。

3. 缺乏"重点标记"。 有些信息用户希望 Agent 永久铭记（如的用语三原则：数字先于态度"），但当前没有机制让用户对某条记忆标注优先级或"钉选"。Agent 对所有记忆一视同仁，导致关键信息可能在上下文中被稀释。

这三个痛点合在一起，让用户对 Agent 的"大脑"完全没有掌控感。

### Desired Solution

在智能体设置中新增两个面板："技能工坊" 和 "记忆库"。

一、技能工坊（Skill Workshop）
智能体设置 → 技能工坊
  │
  ├── 已安装/已创建技能列表（卡片式）
  │   ├──Skill的名称1
  │   │   ├── 📄 查看 SKILL.md 内容（可滚动预览）
  │   │   ├── ✏️ 编辑（内嵌 Markdown 编辑器，可直接微调）
  │   │   ├── 📊 统计：XX次迭代 · XXX行 · 最后修改日期
  │   │   ├── 🔄 更新（从市场拉取新版本）
  │   │   └── ⏸️ 暂停 / ❌ 卸载
  │   │
  │   ├── Skill的名称2
  │   ├── Skill的名称3
  │   └── ...
  │
  ├── 🔍 技能市场（ClawHub）
  │
  └── ➕ 新建技能（调用 skill-creator）

关键功能：
技能内容预览：不用打开文件管理器，在 Cherry Studio 内直接看到 SKILL.md 全文
内嵌编辑：能直接在界面里微调技能内容（比如改一个颜色值、加一条规则）
版本/迭代记录：看到技能被修改了多少次
启用/停用开关：临时关掉某个技能而不卸载

二、记忆库（Memory Vault）
智能体设置 → 记忆库
  │
  ├── 📌 钉选记忆（Pinned）⭐
  │   ├── 🔴 用户用语三原则：数字先于态度..."  [编辑] [取消钉选]
  │   ├── 🔴 "PPT 过程文件必须放 某个地址 [编辑] [取消钉选]
  │   └── [+ 手动添加钉选记忆]
  │
  ├── 📋 知识库（FACT.md）
  │   ├── API 配置
  │   ├── 模型调度原则
  │   └── ...  [可编辑]
  │
  ├── 📝 事件日志（JOURNAL）
  │   ├── 2026-06-24 · PPT 构建 · ...
  │   ├── 2026-06-09 · PPT 风格 · XXX标准
  │   └── ...  [可搜索] [可筛选]
  │
  └── 🗑️ 记忆管理
      ├── 清空短期记忆
      ├── 归档旧事件
      └── 导出记忆备份

关键功能：
钉选记忆：用户可以把某条记忆标记为"⭐ 永久记住"，Agent 每次会话都必须加载
可编辑：用户可以手动修改 FACT.md 中的任何内容（纠正 Agent 记错的东西）
可搜索：在 JOURNAL 中快速查找
透明化：用户终于知道 Agent "学会了什么"

三、对话中的"Highlight 记住"快捷操作
在对话界面中，用户可以选中 Agent 的一段回复（或自己的一段话），右键 → "🔴 让 Agent 记住这条"：
用户：记住，PXXXXXXXXX（一段要求）
      ↓ 右键 → "让 Agent 记住这条"
      ↓
Agent：已将这条规则写入 FACT.md 并标记为 ⭐ 钉选记忆。
       以后每次做 PPT 我都会检查路径。
这比现在需要用户自己去编辑 FACT.md 文件直观得多。

### Alternative Solutions

如果完整方案工作量太大，可以先做最小可用版：

Phase 1（最小可行）：
技能列表页增加"查看内容"按钮（弹窗预览 SKILL.md，只读）
记忆面板增加"钉选记忆"列表（可手动添加/编辑/删除）
对话中右键增加"加入钉选记忆"快捷操作

Phase 2（增强）：
技能内容内嵌编辑器
JOURNAL 搜索和筛选
记忆导入/导出

### Additional Information

这个改进的核心价值在于：把 Agent 从"你只能信任它"变成"你可以掌控它"。
当前 Cherry Studio 的用户体验是：你教会 Agent 很多东西，但你不确定它记住了没有、记住了多少。如果用户能看到技能内容、能管理记忆库、能标记重点——用户对 Agent 的信任感会大幅提升，也更愿意长期"养"一个专属 Agent。
对于非IT背景的用户，"智能体桌面交互平台"定位——一个真正的"平台"应该让用户能管理 Agent 的大脑，而不只是跟它聊天。

title: [Bug]: TranslateButton mirrors loading prop into local state
body:
### Issue Checklist

- [x] I understand that issues are for feedback and problem solving, not for complaining in the comment section, and will provide as much information as possible to help solve the problem.
- [x] My issue is not listed in the FAQ.
- [x] I've looked at pinned issues and searched existing open issues, closed issues, open PRs, and discussions; no similar issue or discussion was found.
- [x] I've filled in a short, clear heading.
- [x] I've confirmed that this was found against the latest fetched `origin/main` checkout.

### Platform

macOS; renderer code path appears platform-independent.

### Version

`origin/main` at `ca133e33b1` (`fix: correct minor bugs across image-preview, provider-config, mini-apps, painting, notes, and selector (#16343)`).

### Bug Description

`src/renderer/components/TranslateButton.tsx` stores the external `isLoading` prop in the same local `isTranslating` state used for the component's own async translation flow:

```tsx
const [isTranslating, setIsTranslating] = useState(false)

useEffect(() => {
  setIsTranslating(isLoading ?? false)
}, [isLoading])
```

This violates the Vercel React rule `rerender-derived-state-no-effect`: a value derived from current props should not be copied into state by an effect. It adds an avoidable render after `isLoading` changes and couples parent loading state to local in-flight translation state.

Risk: if parent loading and local translation overlap, the prop-sync effect can overwrite the local busy state instead of letting the button derive disabled/spinner state from both sources. The button should keep only local translation state and derive a render-time busy value from `isTranslating || (isLoading ?? false)`.

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Inspect `src/renderer/components/TranslateButton.tsx`.
2. Note that `isLoading` is copied into `isTranslating` through `useEffect`.
3. Render the button with `isLoading` changes; each prop change schedules a second render only to mirror the prop value into state.
4. Start a local translation while a parent-provided loading value can change; both sources write the same `isTranslating` flag.

### Expected Behavior

`TranslateButton` should not mirror `isLoading` into local state. It should keep local async translation state separate and compute a render-time busy flag, for example:

```tsx
const isBusy = isTranslating || (isLoading ?? false)
```

Then use `isBusy` for the disabled state and spinner.

### Relevant Log Output

```shell
No runtime logs; this is a React render/state-management issue found by static audit.
```

### Additional Context

Audit source: daily renderer React audit using `/Users/suyao/Devs/projects/web2/cherry-studio/.agents/skills/vercel-react-best-practices/SKILL.md`.

Violated rule: `rerender-derived-state-no-effect` (`Calculate Derived State During Rendering`).

Duplicate checks performed:

- `gh issue list --repo CherryHQ/cherry-studio --state all --search "TranslateButton"`
- `gh issue list --repo CherryHQ/cherry-studio --state all --search "TranslateButton isLoading isTranslating useEffect"`
- `gh pr list --repo CherryHQ/cherry-studio --state open --search "TranslateButton filename:src/renderer/components/TranslateButton.tsx"`

title: [Bug]: MiniMax-M3 cannot set or disable thinking mode in UI
body:
> This issue was translated automatically.

## Bug Description

In the current version (v1.9.11), the MiniMax-M3 model does not provide a thinking mode toggle in the assistant mode UI, preventing users from disabling or adjusting the thinking mode.

Since the code hardcodes `thinking.type = "enabled"` (introduced in PR #15513 / v1.9.8), and the MiniMax API only accepts `"adaptive"` or `"disabled"`, this causes:
1. Cannot disable thinking mode → every request includes `thinking.type = "enabled"` → API returns 400 error
2. Cannot switch to `"adaptive"` → even without errors, the model cannot be used correctly

## Reproduction Steps

1. Add MiniMax-M3 model (via OpenAI-compatible provider)
2. Select this model in assistant mode
3. View model parameters panel → **no thinking mode setting available**
4. Send a message → receive 400 error: `invalid thinking.type: "enabled" (allowed: adaptive, disabled)`

## Expected Behavior

The UI should provide a thinking mode toggle, allowing users to:
- Disable thinking mode (either omit the thinking field or send `"disabled"`)
- Select `"adaptive"` to let the model decide

## Root Cause

The `getReasoningEffort()` function in `src/renderer/src/aiCore/utils/reasoning.ts` hardcodes `thinking.type = "enabled"` for MiniMax models:

```js
if (isMiniMaxReasoningModel(model)) {
  if (assistant?.settings?.reasoning_effort === "none") return { thinking: { type: "disabled" } };
  return { thinking: { type: "enabled" } }   // ← hardcoded
}
```

The `reasoning_effort === "none"` escape hatch is not exposed in the OpenAI-compatible provider UI, so users cannot set it.

## Workaround

- Agent mode is not affected (does not go through the `getReasoningEffort` code path)
- Wait for PR #15991 to be merged and released

## Environment

- Platform: Windows
- Version: v1.9.11
- Model: MiniMax-M3 (via OpenAI-compatible provider, base_url: https://api.minimaxi.com/v1)

## Related Issues

- #16247 — thinking.type "enabled" returns 400
- #16201 — Hardcoded value cannot be modified
- #15782 — v1.9.11 MiniMax-M3 Error
- #15794 — Error when enabling deep thinking mode

---

<summary>Original Content</summary>

## Bug 描述

在当前版本 (v1.9.11) 中，MiniMax-M3 模型在助手模式的 UI 中没有提供思考模式的设置开关，用户无法关闭或调整思考模式。

由于代码硬编码了 `thinking.type = "enabled"`（自 PR #15513 / v1.9.8 引入），而 MiniMax API 只接受 `"adaptive"` 或 `"disabled"`，导致：
1. 无法关闭思考模式 → 每次请求都带上 `thinking.type = "enabled"` → API 返回 400 错误
2. 无法切换为 `"adaptive"` → 即使不报错也无法正确使用模型

## 复现步骤

1. 添加 MiniMax-M3 模型（通过 OpenAI 兼容 provider）
2. 在助手模式中选中该模型
3. 查看模型参数面板 → **没有思考模式的设置项**
4. 发送消息 → 收到 400 错误：`invalid thinking.type: "enabled" (allowed: adaptive, disabled)`

## 预期行为

UI 应提供思考模式开关，允许用户：
- 关闭思考模式（不发 thinking 字段或发 `"disabled"`）
- 选择 `"adaptive"` 让模型自行决定

## 根因

`src/renderer/src/aiCore/utils/reasoning.ts` 中的 `getReasoningEffort()` 函数对 MiniMax 模型硬编码了 `thinking.type = "enabled"`：

if (isMiniMaxReasoningModel(model)) {

}

## 临时方案

- Agent 模式不受影响（不走 `getReasoningEffort` 代码路径）

- #16201 — 硬编码无法修改
- #15782 — v1.9.11 MiniMax-M3 Error
- #15794 — 开启深度思考模式报错

title: [Feature]: Upgrade "Topics" to "Roles": Multiple identities in parallel for the same agent, with linkable information
body:
> This issue was translated automatically.

### Issue Checklist

- [x] I understand that issues are for reporting problems and requesting features, not for off-topic comments, and I will provide as much detail as possible to help resolve the issue.
- [x] I have checked the pinned issues and searched through the existing [open issues](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/issues), [closed issues](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20state%3Aclosed), and [discussions](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/discussions) and did not find a similar suggestion.
- [x] I have provided a short and descriptive title so that developers can quickly understand the issue when browsing the issue list, rather than vague titles like "A suggestion" or "Stuck."
- [x] The latest version of Cherry Studio does not include the feature I am suggesting.

### Platform

Windows

### Version

1.9.11

### Is your feature request related to an existing issue?

Currently, the interface is divided into "Agents"/"Assistants" + "Topics". The naming logic and meaning of "Topics" is unclear, and topics themselves are uncontrollable.

1. The concept of "Topic" has no meaning for users. A "Topic" is essentially a group of independent conversation threads under the same assistant, auto-named by LLM. Users cannot control the naming, nor do they understand the difference between "Topic" and "Project", "Task", or "Role". Related Issues: #3460 (custom topic naming), #3397 (topic naming language errors).

2. Topics are completely isolated, but real-world scenarios require information to be connected. An agent responsible for brand strategy discusses competitor dynamics in "Project A" topic, but in "Project B" topic, it knows nothing about it—even though it's the same Agent, and insights from both projects should be shared.

3. Naming logic is chaotic. Auto-naming is often inaccurate ("Refactor Plan v2" vs "Refactor Plan v3", or just gibberish), and users are forced to accept a name they don't understand.

Root cause: "Topic" is a product of engineer perspective—directly exposing technical "session isolation" to users. What users really need is a concept closer to human thinking: the same agent switching between different identities in different scenarios.

### Desired Solution

Change "Topic" to "Role", just like a "person" can be a father, a son, a husband, etc. For the same agent, it's the same—the same agent has different responsibilities and considerations under different identities, but it's still the same person, and information can be connected between them.

Upgrade "Topics" to "Roles", reshaping the mental model:

**Key Design**

1. **Role = Conversation Context + Lightweight Role Prompts**
A role is not creating a new Agent, but adding a layer of "role filter" on the same Agent:
- Each role has its own conversation history and context
- Roles can have lightweight supplementary prompts (e.g., "Data Analyst" role adds "You excel at Excel analysis")
- But it doesn't change the Agent's core personality and memory

2. **Information Can Be Connected**
This is the most essential difference from "Topics":

Current (Topic Isolation):
```
Topic A "AAA Project" 🚫 Topic B "BBB Project"
Agent is "amnesic" in both topics
```

After Upgrade (Role Connection):
```
Role A "Brand Strategist" ─── Competitor insights auto-linked ─── Role B "Data Analyst"
Agent knows "I discussed this in the strategist role before, the data analyst role can use it"
```
Technical implementation: Agent's workspace memory (FACT.md, JOURNAL) is shared by all roles, only conversation context is isolated by role.

3. **User-defined Naming, No More LLM Auto-generation**
Role names are manually entered by users at creation time, and can be modified anytime. AI-suggested naming can be optionally provided, but the user makes the final decision.

4. **Role Panel**
```
Agent Conversation Interface
  │
  ├── Top-left: Current role dropdown switch
  │   ├── 🎭 Brand Strategist [Current]
  │   ├── 🎭 Data Analyst
  │   ├── 🎭 Creative Copywriter
  │   ├── 🎭 Daily Assistant
  │   └── ➕ New Role
  │
  └── Conversation Area: Current role's context
```
One-click role switching, conversation history switches accordingly, but Agent's core memory (who you are, your preferences) remains consistent.

5. **Division of Labor Between "Role" and "New Agent"**

| | New Agent | New Role |
|---|---|---|
| Personality | Completely different | Same personality + Role filter |
| Memory | Independent | Shared |
| Model | Can be different | Usually same |
| Channel/Scheduled Tasks | Independent config | Inherited |
| Use Case | Work and life separated | Different responsibilities within work |

### Alternative Solutions

If the "Role" change is too big, it can be done in phases:

Phase 1: First solve the controllability of "Topics"—allow users to manually name/rename topics, merge topics, and add tags to topics.

Phase 2: Introduce the "Role" concept, allowing multiple topics of an Agent to be categorized under different roles.

Phase 3: Implement cross-role information linking, using FACT.md as the shared memory bridge.

### Additional Information

The core value of this improvement is: transforming AI assistants from "tools" to "partners". A true AI partner should be like a person: communicating with you in different identities in different scenarios, but always being the same "person", remembering all your interactions. The concept of "Role" is closer to human thinking than "Topic", and gives users a stronger sense of "I'm raising my own dedicated Agent".

---

### Issue Checklist

- [x] I have checked the pinned issues and searched through the existing [open issues](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/issues), [closed issues](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20state%3Aclosed), and [discussions](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/discussions) and did not find a similar suggestion.
- [x] I have provided a short and descriptive title so that developers can quickly understand the issue when browsing the issue list, rather than vague titles like "A suggestion" or "Stuck."
- [x] The latest version of Cherry Studio does not include the feature I am suggesting.

### Platform

Windows

### Version

1.9.11

### Is your feature request related to an existing issue?

目前界面分“智能体”/“助手”+“话题”，话题的命名逻辑与意义不明晰，话题本身不可控。

1. "话题"这一概念对用户没有意义。 "话题"本质上是同一助手下的一组独立对话线程，LLM 自动命名。用户既不能控制命名，也不理解"话题"和"项目""任务""角色"的区别。相关 Issue：#3460（自定义话题命名）、#3397（话题命名语言错误）。
2. 话题之间完全隔离，但现实场景需要信息串联。 一个负责品牌策略的智能体，在"A项目"话题中讨论了竞品动态，在"B项目"话题中却完全不知道这件事——明明是同一个 Agent，明明两个项目的洞察应该共享。
3. 命名逻辑混乱。 自动命名经常不准确（"重构方案 v2" vs "重构方案 v3"，或直接是乱码），用户被迫接受一个自己不理解的名字。
根本原因："话题"是工程师视角的产物——把技术上的"会话隔离"直接暴露给了用户。 用户真正需要的是一个更贴近人类思维的概念：同一个智能体，在不同场景下切换不同身份。

### Desired Solution

还不如话题改成”角色“，就像一个“人”可以是父亲、也是儿子、也是丈夫、等等，对于同一个智体还说也是一样的，同一个智体在不同身份下，考虑的事情和职责也不一样，但都还是同一个人，相互之间还是能信息串联的。

将"话题"升级为"角色"（Role），重塑心智模型：

关键设计
1. 角色 = 对话上下文 + 轻量角色提示词
角色不是新建一个 Agent，而是在同一个 Agent 上叠加一层"角色滤镜"：
每个角色有自己的对话历史和上下文
角色可以有轻量的补充提示词（如"数据分析师"角色追加"你擅长 Excel 分析"）
但不改变 Agent 的核心人格和记忆

2. 信息可串联
这是和"话题"最本质的区别：
当前（话题隔离）：
  话题 A "AAA项目" 🚫 话题 B "BBB项目"
  Agent 在两个话题里是"失忆"的
升级后（角色串联）：
  角色 A "品牌策略师" ─── 竞品洞察自动关联 ─── 角色 B "数据分析师"
  Agent 知道"我之前在策略角色里讨论过这个，数据分析角色可以用上"
技术实现：Agent 的工作区记忆（FACT.md、JOURNAL）是所有角色共享的，只有对话上下文按角色隔离。

3. 用户自命名，不再 LLM 自动生成
角色名称由用户在创建时手动输入，可随时修改。可选提供 AI 建议命名，但最终由用户决定。

4. 角色面板
5. 智能体对话界面
  │
  ├── 左上角：当前角色下拉切换
  │   ├── 🎭 品牌策略师 [当前]
  │   ├── 🎭 数据分析师
  │   ├── 🎭 创意文案
  │   ├── 🎭 日常助理
  │   └── ➕ 新建角色
  │
  └── 对话区：当前角色的上下文
一键切换角色，对话历史随之切换，但 Agent 的核心记忆（你是谁、你的偏好）保持一致。

5. "角色"和"新建智能体"的分工
        | 新建智能体 | 新建角色
人格 | 完全不同 | 同一人格 + 角色滤镜
记忆 | 独立 | 共享
模型 | 可不同 | 通常相同
频道/定时任务 | 独立配置 | 继承
使用场景 | 工作和生活分开 | 工作内不同职责

### Alternative Solutions

如果"角色"改动太大，可以分步走：
Phase 1： 先解决"话题"的可控性——允许用户手动命名/重命名话题、合并话题、给话题加标签。
Phase 2： 引入"角色"概念，允许将一个 Agent 的多个话题归属到不同角色下。
Phase 3： 实现跨角色信息串联，用 FACT.md 作为共享记忆桥梁。

### Additional Information

这个改进的核心价值在于：把 AI 助手从"工具"变成"伙伴"。让一个真正的 AI 伙伴应该像人一样：和你在不同场景下以不同身份交流，但始终是同一个"人"，记得你们的所有交集。"角色"这个概念——比"话题"更贴近人类的思维方式，也比"话题"更能让用户产生"我在养一个专属 Agent"的归属感。
</details>

title: [Feature]: Task Dashboard in Agent Sidebar — Running & Awaiting Review Sections
body:
## Background

Cherry Studio's scheduled tasks today live deep in `Settings → Tasks`, with no surface in the Agent sidebar. Users who set up Cherry Claw scheduled tasks (daily reports, periodic syncs) have no way to see at a glance whether a task is currently running or whether a recent run produced a result they haven't reviewed yet — they have to navigate to Settings, find the task, and open its run log. Long-running Agent sessions (multi-step goals, watch jobs) have the same invisibility problem: once the user closes the conversation tab, they lose track of whether the Agent is still working.

## Goal

Users see a compact task dashboard at the top of the Agent sidebar that always exposes two things: which tasks are running right now, and which recently finished tasks they haven't reviewed yet — clickable straight to the underlying session, with no settings detour.

## Spec

- The Agent sidebar gains a **Task Dashboard** section pinned above the existing scheduled-tasks list, with two labeled groups: `Running` and `Awaiting review`. Each group shows a numeric badge with its count and an entry list when expanded.
- The `Running` group lists tasks with at least one active run (either a scheduled-task run in progress or a long-running Agent session that hasn't returned). Each entry shows the task / session name, the Agent it belongs to, and elapsed time updated live.
- The `Awaiting review` group lists completed runs whose result session the user has not opened since completion. Failed and cancelled runs also surface here with a distinct status indicator.
- Clicking an entry navigates the user directly to the corresponding session. Opening a session under `Awaiting review` immediately removes that entry from the group; entries can also be dismissed manually via a hover action without opening.
- Each entry exposes one quick action on hover: `Stop` for `Running` (cancels the run, mirroring the existing per-task cancel), `Dismiss` for `Awaiting review` (marks the run as reviewed without opening).
- The dashboard state persists across app restarts: running tasks remain visible if they're still executing in the background, and awaiting-review entries survive restart until opened or dismissed.
- The dashboard is empty-state aware: when both groups are empty, the section collapses to a single thin row reading `No active tasks`, never blocking the scheduled-tasks list below it.

## Verification

- User creates a scheduled task `Daily PR triage` set to fire every weekday at 9:00. At 9:00 the next workday with Cherry running, the entry moves from the scheduled-tasks list into `Running` with an incrementing timer. Once the run finishes 4 minutes later, the entry moves to `Awaiting review` with `4m` duration shown; the user clicks it → the corresponding session opens, and the entry disappears from `Awaiting review`.
- User has 3 entries in `Awaiting review`. Closes Cherry, reopens it next morning — all 3 entries are still there. User hover-dismisses one without opening → that entry disappears, the other 2 remain.
- User starts a long-running Goal Mode session, then closes the conversation tab. The session remains in `Running` with a live elapsed timer; reopening the conversation does not remove it because the Agent is still working. When the Agent self-declares completion, the entry moves to `Awaiting review`.
- User hovers a `Running` entry and clicks `Stop` → the run is cancelled, the entry moves to `Awaiting review` with status `Cancelled`. User clicks it → session opens showing the cancellation point, entry disappears.
- A scheduled task fails with an error. The run lands in `Awaiting review` with a failure indicator. User dismisses without opening → entry disappears but the run record remains visible in the underlying task's run history.
- Both groups are empty → sidebar shows a single-line `No active tasks` strip above the scheduled-tasks list, taking minimal vertical space; the scheduled-tasks list below is fully visible and operable.

## Related

#15634 #15396 #15600 #15643 #15574

### Platform
