[Feature]: Old-view right-pane refactor follow-ups (agent Shell reuse + Topics/Sessions presentation decomposition)
body:
### Issue Checklist

- [x] I understand that issues are for reporting problems and requesting features, and I will provide as much detail as possible.
- [x] I have checked existing issues/discussions and did not find a similar one.
- [x] I have provided a short and descriptive title.
- [x] The latest version does not include the change I am proposing.

### Platform

All — internal refactor, not platform-specific.

### Version

`main` (follow-up to #16434, branch `jd/resource-list-config`).

### Is your feature request related to an existing issue?

Two internal architecture follow-ups surfaced during the #16434 multi-agent design review. Both are **accepted tech debt** in #16434 (deliberately deferred to keep that PR scoped), not regressions. They make the old-view right-pane area more compositional and remove an asymmetry between the assistant (conversation) and agent (work) surfaces.

Design reference: `v2-refactor-temp/docs/chat/chat-view-modes.md`.

### Desired Solution

#### Item 1 — Unify the agent right pane into a single reused Shell (drop per-branch remount)

**Problem.** `AgentChat` renders a fresh `AgentRightPane` (= a fresh `Shell`) per conversation branch (initializing / draft / missing-agent / persistent). `AgentRightPane` is a "fat" wrapper bound to per-session runtime data (`messages` / `partsByMessageId` / `traceId` / `sessionId` / `modelFallback` / …) that only exists inside the session-resolved inner frame. Sending the first message in a draft remounts the Shell, which would snap the work pane shut — worked around today by re-seeding `defaultOpen={workPaneOpen}`. Home, by contrast, keeps one page-level `Shell` (open state persists naturally). So the same "keep/open the right pane" behavior uses two different mechanisms, plus a minor edge: locating the **already-active** session does not open the pane (no remount to re-seed).

**Proposed approach.** Make `AgentRightPane` a *thin* shell (chrome + open-state + `resourcePane` + `revealRequest`) and inject its session-bound tab contents (files / status / flow / trace / info-card) via context from the inner `AgentChatSessionFrame` — extending the existing `ResourcePaneProvider` pattern. Hoist the single shell above the branch switch (mirroring Home's `renderWithRightPane`). Then delete the `defaultOpen` re-seed and reuse Home's live `openTab` bridge so both surfaces share one mechanism.

**Affected.** `pages/agents/AgentChat.tsx`, `pages/agents/components/AgentRightPane/AgentRightPane.tsx`, `pages/agents/AgentPage.tsx`.

**Risks.** ~10 session-bound props → context conversion; branches that currently render no right pane (locked / empty / loading) must render under the unified shell; regress files / status / flow / trace / info-card tabs and the draft→persistent handoff.

#### Item 2 — Replace the `presentation: 'sidebar' | 'right-panel'` boolean flag with composition

**Problem.** `Topics.tsx` (~1500 lines) and `Sessions.tsx` (~1600 lines) serve both the new-view classic sidebar and the old-view right panel through ~15 inline `isRightPanel` branches. This is the least compositional part of the design (the opposite of the entity rail's clean layering). Accepted in #16434 because the repo treats these two as parallel hand-written giants and the change is large.

**Proposed approach.** Extract a `<ResourceListRightPanel>` (or a right-panel descriptor) that composes the existing `ResourceList` primitives for the right panel's fixed behavior (time grouping, single-entity filter, search-only header, no drag), instead of threading `isRightPanel` through the giant list components. Leave the new-view sidebar path unchanged.

**Affected.** `pages/home/Tabs/components/Topics.tsx`, `pages/agents/components/Sessions.tsx`, and the right-panel wiring (`resourcePane.node`) in `HomePage.tsx` / `AgentPage.tsx`.

**Risks.** These components also drive the **new-view** sidebar → must not regress it; needs focused tests on both views.

### Alternative Solutions

- Keep both as-is (the current accepted tradeoff). Functionally correct; the cost is maintainer cognition (two right-pane mechanisms; `isRightPanel` sprinkled through two giant components).

### Additional Information

**Recommended sequencing:** do these as **two separate PRs** — they are independent (any order) and have different blast radius (Item 1 is agent-render-structure; Item 2 also affects the new-view sidebar). One PR with two isolated, separately-revertable commits is acceptable if fewer PRs are preferred.

title: [Bug]: Painting migrator leaves dangling model_id (no user_model row) → composer can't resolve model, send disabled
body:
### Issue Checklist

- [x] I understand that issues are for feedback and problem solving, not for complaining in the comment section, and will provide as much information as possible to help solve the problem.
- [x] My issue is not listed in the FAQ.
- [x] I've looked at pinned issues and searched existing Open/Closed Issues and Discussions, no similar issue was found.
- [x] I've filled in short, clear headings so that developers can quickly identify the issue.
- [x] I've confirmed that I am using the latest version of Cherry Studio.

### Platform

macOS

### Version

2.0.0-dev (`main`, v2 refactor)

### Bug Description

The v2 painting migrator scopes each legacy painting's model into a v2 unique id but **never verifies that model actually exists in the migrated `user_model` table**. As a result a migrated painting can end up pointing at a `provider::model` that has no `user_model` row, and that painting can no longer be generated.

In `src/main/data/migration/v2/migrators/mappings/PaintingMappings.ts`:

```ts
function createScopedModelId(providerId: string, rawModelId: string, warnings: string[]): string | null {
  try {
    return createUniqueModelId(providerId, rawModelId) // format-only; no existence check
  } catch (error) {
    warnings.push(`Dropped invalid legacy model id '${rawModelId}': ...`)
    ...
  }
}
```

It only validates the **format** (`isUniqueModelId`), not that the model is one the user actually has under that provider in v2.

Downstream, the v2 paintings composer resolves the model from the provider's own model list and disables sending when it can't be resolved (this is intentional — there is deliberately **no fallback**, per an earlier decision to surface bad model refs rather than hide them):

```ts
// PaintingComposer.tsx
const { models } = useModels({ providerId: draft.providerId })
const model = models.find(m => m.providerId === draft.providerId && m.apiModelId === draft.model)
// ...
sendDisabled = generating || (text empty && no files) || !model  // <- !model disables send
```

So a dangling `model_id` ⇒ `model === undefined` ⇒ **send button is permanently greyed out**. The model dropdown still shows the model name because the selector falls back to the raw id string (`selectedModel?.name ?? draft.model`), which makes it look like a valid selection — so the user sees a named model but cannot generate.

**Observed real data** (macOS dev DB):

```
painting.model_id = aihubmix::imagen-4.0-ultra-generate-preview-06-06
```
…but `user_model` has **zero** imagen rows under `aihubmix` (its image models are `gpt-image-1`, `gpt-image-2`, `gemini-3-pro-image-preview`; imagen only exists under the `gemini` provider). The composer cannot resolve it ⇒ send disabled.

Note: the same dangling-reference symptom is also reachable without migration (selecting an image model that exists in the registry/catalog but not in the provider's `user_model`), but the migrator is the systematic source — it can mint these references in bulk.

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Have a v1 painting whose model is no longer present in the user's models for that provider (e.g. the provider's model list changed, or the model was removed).
2. Run the v1 → v2 data migration.
3. Open Paintings (v2 canvas) and select that migrated card (or its model in the composer).
4. The composer shows the model name, but the send button stays disabled — the painting can't be regenerated.

(Also reproducible without migration: in v2, select an image model that is offered by the picker/catalog but has no `user_model` row for the chosen provider.)

### Expected Behavior

The migrator should not leave paintings pointing at models that don't exist in the migrated `user_model`. Suggested directions (open to discussion):

- Reconcile `modelId` against the migrated `user_model` for the same provider; if there's no match, **null the `modelId`** (the painting then falls back to model selection in the composer) instead of keeping a dangling reference.
- Emit/collect a migration warning so dangling model refs are visible during migration.
- Open design question: the painting migrator likely needs the migrated `user_model` set available at painting-migration time (an ordering dependency between the model migrator and the painting migrator) — worth confirming whether that lookup is feasible in the current pipeline.

### Relevant Log Output

```shell
# user_model has no imagen under aihubmix
sqlite> SELECT COUNT(*) FROM user_model
        WHERE provider_id='aihubmix' AND model_id='imagen-4.0-ultra-generate-preview-06-06';
0

# but a painting references it
sqlite> SELECT provider_id, model_id, status FROM painting WHERE model_id LIKE '%imagen%';
aihubmix|aihubmix::imagen-4.0-ultra-generate-preview-06-06|NULL
```

### Additional Context

Code pointers:
- Migrator: `src/main/data/migration/v2/migrators/mappings/PaintingMappings.ts` — `createScopedModelId`, `resolveLegacyPaintingModelId`, `normalizeLegacyModelId` (format-only validation).
- Renderer resolution: `src/renderer/pages/paintings/components/PaintingComposer.tsx` (`model` lookup + `sendDisabled` includes `!model`); selector fallback in `src/renderer/pages/paintings/components/PaintingModelSelector.tsx` (`selectedModel?.name ?? draft.model`).
- Related earlier symptom: a painting referencing `ppio::jimeng-txt2img-v3.1` with no `user_model` row produced the same "send button greyed out" behavior.

### Platform

macOS

### Version

`origin/main` at `0d87c5d9eb` (`fix(stream-manager): drop empty text/reasoning parts before persisting (#16455)`)

### Bug Description

The selection toolbar/action windows import `lucide-react/dynamic` on hot renderer entrypoints:

- `src/renderer/windows/selection/toolbar/SelectionToolbar.tsx:11-12`
- `src/renderer/windows/selection/toolbar/SelectionToolbar.tsx:140-150`
- `src/renderer/windows/selection/action/ActionWindow.tsx:10-12`
- `src/renderer/windows/selection/action/ActionWindow.tsx:230-232`

The default built-in selection actions have a fixed icon set in `src/shared/data/preference/preferenceSchemas.ts:658-684` (`languages`, `file-question`, `scan-text`, `search`, `clipboard-copy`, `wand-sparkles`, `quote`). Loading the dynamic Lucide icon resolver for those built-ins is unnecessary on these small, latency-sensitive overlay windows. User-defined actions still need dynamic icon names, but built-ins can be served by static imports.

This violates the Vercel React best-practice rule `bundle-dynamic-imports`: avoid broad dynamic import maps on critical paths when the runtime choices are known.

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Inspect `SelectionToolbar.tsx` and `ActionWindow.tsx` imports.
2. Open the default selection toolbar, where all enabled actions are built-ins by default.
3. The toolbar/action window code still imports the dynamic Lucide resolver even though the built-in icon names are a closed set.

### Expected Behavior

Built-in selection actions should render from a statically imported icon map. Dynamic Lucide icon resolution should be kept only for user-defined actions, ideally behind a lazily loaded custom-icon component so the default overlay path does not include the dynamic icon map.

### Relevant Log Output

```shell
N/A
```

### Additional Context

Skill rules used for this audit:

- `vercel-react-best-practices/rules/bundle-dynamic-imports.md`
- `vercel-react-best-practices/rules/bundle-conditional.md`

Minimal expected fix:

- Add a small shared selection-action icon renderer for the fixed built-in icon set.
- Replace direct `DynamicIcon` usage in selection toolbar/action windows for built-ins.
- Keep custom/user-defined icons working via a lazily loaded dynamic icon fallback.
- Add focused tests for built-in icon rendering and custom fallback behavior if an appropriate test surface exists.

title: [Bug]: Mini app keep-alive cache updates can overwrite newer state
body:
### Issue Checklist

- [x] I have searched for existing issues and open pull requests
- [x] I have verified this on the current `origin/main`
- [x] I have included exact files and a minimal expected fix

### Platform

macOS

### Version

`origin/main` at `0d87c5d9eb` (`fix(stream-manager): drop empty text/reasoning parts before persisting (#16455)`)

### Bug Description

The renderer cache hook exposes a setter that only accepts a concrete value:

- `src/renderer/data/hooks/useCache.ts:140-143`
- `src/renderer/data/hooks/useCache.ts:361-364` for the persist-cache equivalent

That makes cache-backed UI state look like React state but prevents React-style functional updates. Mini app keep-alive state already depends on the previous list and currently has to compute new arrays from captured snapshots:

- `src/renderer/components/MiniApp/MiniApp.tsx:92-96`
- `src/renderer/hooks/useMiniAppPopup.ts:175-194`
- `src/renderer/hooks/useMiniAppPopup.ts:232-237`
- `src/renderer/hooks/useMiniAppPopup.ts:284-290`

This violates the Vercel React best-practice rule `rerender-functional-setstate`: when new state is computed from previous state, use a functional updater so the update is based on the latest committed value. The current `handleHide` path is especially risky because it waits for `updateAppStatus(...).then(...)`; if another mini app is opened or closed while the mutation is in flight, the stale `openedKeepAliveMiniApps` array captured by the rendered card can overwrite the newer keep-alive list.

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Inspect `useCache('mini_app.opened_keep_alive')` in `src/renderer/hooks/useMiniApps.ts`.
2. Inspect `handleHide` in `src/renderer/components/MiniApp/MiniApp.tsx`.
3. Start hiding mini app A while the keep-alive list is `[A, B]`.
4. Before the async status mutation resolves, open mini app C so the current list becomes `[A, B, C]`.
5. When the hide mutation resolves, `handleHide` writes `openedKeepAliveMiniApps.filter(...)` from the stale `[A, B]` snapshot, dropping C.

### Expected Behavior

Cache-backed setters that model UI state should support functional updaters, and mini app keep-alive list updates should derive from the latest cache value at write time. Hiding A in the scenario above should result in `[B, C]`, not `[B]`.

### Relevant Log Output

```shell
N/A
```

### Additional Context

Skill rules used for this audit:

- `vercel-react-best-practices/rules/rerender-functional-setstate.md`
- `vercel-composition-patterns/references/state-decouple-implementation.md`

Minimal expected fix:

- Extend `useCache`, `useSharedCache`, and `usePersistCache` setters to accept `React.SetStateAction<T>` or an equivalent local type.
- Resolve function values against the latest cache value from `cacheService.get*()` before writing.
- Update mini app keep-alive mutations to use functional updaters where they derive from the previous list.
- Add focused tests for functional cache setter behavior and the mini app hide race.

Duplicate checks performed before filing:

- GitHub issues: `openedKeepAliveMiniApps stale state MiniApp keep alive`, `mini app hide overwrite keep alive stale`, `useCache functional updater stale closure`
- Open PRs: same query set

title: [Bug]: Code block toolbar derives tools through effect-driven state
body:
### Issue Checklist

- [x] I have searched for existing issues and open pull requests
- [x] I have verified this on the current `origin/main`
- [x] I have included exact files and a minimal expected fix

### Platform

macOS

### Version

`origin/main` at `0d87c5d9eb` (`fix(stream-manager): drop empty text/reasoning parts before persisting (#16455)`)

### Bug Description

`CodeBlockView` renders code-toolbar tools through effect-driven registration state:

- `src/renderer/components/CodeBlockView/view.tsx:109` initializes `tools` as local state.
- `src/renderer/components/CodeBlockView/view.tsx:209-264` calls toolbar hooks with `setTools`.
- `src/renderer/components/CodeToolbar/hooks/useCopyTool.tsx:43-77` registers/removes tools in `useEffect`; the other toolbar hooks follow the same pattern.
- `src/renderer/components/ActionTools/hooks/useToolManager.ts:7-20` updates `tools` via state setters.

Every code block first commits with `tools=[]`, then each mounted toolbar hook schedules effect updates to register the tools. Chat messages can contain many code blocks, so this multiplies post-render commits in the message list and makes toolbar contents arrive after the first paint even though the set of tools is derived from the current props/state.

This violates the Vercel React best-practice rule `rerender-derived-state-no-effect`: do not put derived render data in state and update it from an effect when it can be computed during render.

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Render a markdown message with several code blocks.
2. Inspect `CodeBlockView` render flow: `tools` starts as `[]`.
3. After the first commit, each `use*Tool` hook runs an effect and calls `registerTool`.
4. The component commits again with the derived toolbar list.

### Expected Behavior

The toolbar tool list should be built during render from the current hook state and props, so each code block can render its correct toolbar without an extra effect-driven registration pass.

### Relevant Log Output

```shell
N/A
```

### Additional Context

Skill rules used for this audit:

- `vercel-react-best-practices/rules/rerender-derived-state-no-effect.md`
- `vercel-react-best-practices/rules/rerender-no-inline-components.md` checked for nearby churn, but this issue is specifically about effect-driven derived state.

Minimal expected fix:

- Refactor code toolbar hooks to return `ActionTool`/`ActionTool[]` values (or small builder objects) instead of accepting `setTools` and registering in effects.
- Compose and sort the tools in `CodeBlockView` with `useMemo` during render.
- Preserve transient hook state such as copied/saved indicators.
- Update the existing `CodeToolbar` hook tests to assert returned tools instead of effect registration side effects.

Duplicate checks performed before filing:

- GitHub issues: `CodeBlockView useToolManager setTools toolbar effect`, `CodeBlock toolbar extra render effect derived state`
- Open PRs: same query set

title: [Bug]: Recent items in GlobalSearch panel do not update after renaming a topic or session
body:
## Bug Description

Renaming a topic (or agent session) does not immediately update its entry in the GlobalSearchPanel's "Recent" list. The stale title persists until either:

- The user re-opens that topic and `HomePage`'s `activeTopic` effect runs (`HomePage.tsx:258-270`, which prepends — it doesn't update the existing entry's title), **or**
- The mount-time refresh effect in `GlobalSearchPanel` runs again, which is throttled by a 60s cooldown per `kind:id` (`GlobalSearchPanel.tsx:84`, `RECENT_ITEMS_REFRESH_THROTTLE_MS`).

There is also a related symptom: when a newly created / freshly renamed topic has no server-side title yet, the recent row in the panel renders as **"Untitled Session"** / **"Untitled"** (or similar placeholder). Even after the server returns a real name on a subsequent visit, the panel keeps showing the placeholder until the 60s throttle expires.

Expected: renaming a topic (or session) anywhere in the app should propagate the new name to its existing recent-items entry instantly, no matter whether the panel is open or closed, no matter the throttle state.

## Steps To Reproduce (Windows)

1. Launch Cherry Studio on Windows.
2. In any assistant, create a topic named e.g. **"Q3 plan"**.
3. Open the Global Search panel via the shortcut **Ctrl+K** (default on Windows/Linux; macOS uses Cmd+K). The topic now appears in the "Recent" group.
4. Rename the topic:
   - Use the shortcut **F2** in the topic sidebar list, **or**
   - Right-click the topic in the sidebar → Rename, **or**
   - Trigger the `topic.rename` command (default Windows shortcut: configurable under Settings → Shortcuts).
5. Type the new name **"Q4 plan"** and confirm.
6. Immediately reopen the Global Search panel with **Ctrl+K**.
7. Observe: the entry still shows **"Q3 plan"**.

## Expected Behavior

After step 5, reopening Ctrl+K should show **"Q4 plan"** in the Recent list, with no delay.

The same applies to **agent sessions** renamed via the agents page (the existing mount-time refresh in `GlobalSearchPanel` was added to cover both topics and sessions, but neither write path actually triggers an upsert on rename).

## Relevant Log Output

No application errors are emitted. The mount-time refresh effect in `GlobalSearchPanel.tsx:374-436` will log `Failed to refresh recent title` only when the fetch itself fails; it never logs the staleness itself. Adding a `logger.warn` inside `updateTopic`'s post-success hook would help here, but is not the fix.

## Additional Context

### Root cause

The write path is complete; the propagation step is missing.

1. **Rename entry**: `Chat.tsx:84-97` `topic.rename` command handler calls `patchTopic(topic.id, { name, isNameManuallyEdited: true })`.
2. **Mutation**: `useTopicMutations().updateTopic` runs `useMutation('PATCH', '/topics/:id', { refresh: ['/topics', '/topics/:id'] })` (`useTopic.ts:276-278`). It invalidates the SWR caches for `/topics` and `/topics/:id` — **but it never touches `ui.global_search.recent_items`**.
3. **No reader notices**: 
   - `HomePage.tsx:258-270` upserts only when a topic becomes the `activeTopic` again, gated by a `signature = "${id}:${name}"` check. A rename where the user immediately switches away (or never visits) leaves the stale entry.
   - `AgentPage.tsx:184-200` is symmetric for sessions.
   - `GlobalSearchPanel.tsx:374-436` mount-time refresh is a fallback only, throttled to one fetch per `kind:id` per 60s, so users hit it on every panel open inside the cooldown window.
4. **Empty-title feedback loop**: when an entity has `name: ''` (e.g. a freshly created topic before the user types anything), the empty-title bypass (`GlobalSearchPanel.tsx:382`) refetches forever, but the throttle slot is only updated on success — so a server that legitimately returns `''` causes perpetual refetch and the "Untitled" placeholder sticks.

A repo-wide grep for `upsertGlobalSearchRecentEntry` shows it is only called from `HomePage.tsx:265`, `AgentPage.tsx:192`, `AppShell.tsx:37`, and the helper's own definition + tests. **No rename / update mutation path calls it.**

### Suggested fix

After a successful `updateTopic`, call:

```ts
upsertGlobalSearchRecentEntry(currentRecentItems, createRecentTopicEntryFromTopic(updatedTopic))
```

Both `upsertGlobalSearchRecentEntry` and `createRecentTopicEntryFromTopic` already exist in `src/renderer/components/GlobalSearch/globalSearchGroups.ts:141` and `:193`. The `updateTopic` (or a wrapper around `useTopicMutations`) needs access to the `ui.global_search.recent_items` persist-cache value + setter — a small dedicated hook (e.g. `useRecentItemsSync()`) can encapsulate this so both topic and session rename paths share one implementation.

Apply the same fix to the agent-session rename path (`useSessionMutations` analog).

### Files involved

- `src/renderer/hooks/useTopic.ts:302-309` — `updateTopic` lacks the recent-items sync side effect.
- `src/renderer/hooks/agents/useSession.ts` — analogous hook for agent sessions, same gap.
- `src/renderer/components/GlobalSearch/GlobalSearchPanel.tsx:374-436` — mount-time refresh is a partial mitigation; the 60s throttle + read-on-mount poll is the wrong layer.
- `src/renderer/components/GlobalSearch/globalSearchGroups.ts:128-139` — `areGlobalSearchRecentEntriesEqual` already exists and could be reused to short-circuit no-op writes inside `upsertGlobalSearchRecentEntry`.

### Priority

P2 — the app is functional and the user can still find the topic by clicking it (the navigation uses the live `/topics/:id` fetch, not the recent-entry title). The impact is purely cosmetic / UX freshness of the panel.

### Environment

- Platform: Windows
- Repro verified on the current `main` branch with the recent mount-time refresh effect present.

## Background

Currently, Cherry Studio relies on embedding and OCR capabilities in scenarios such as knowledge base / attachment processing / document parsing. We want to support **fully local** embedding and OCR, allowing users to choose local models for vectorization and text recognition, avoiding mandatory reliance on cloud services.

## Requirements

### 1. Local Embedding

Support using local embedding models to generate vectors, for example:

- Ollama local embedding models
- llama.cpp / GGUF embedding models
- ONNX / Transformers local embedding models
- Other extensible local embedding providers

Expected capabilities:

- Add a "Local Embedding" configuration entry in settings
- Knowledge base can select local embedding provider
- Support model path / service address / model name configuration
- Support basic parameters like dimensions, batch size, timeout, etc.
- Support testing if embedding is available
- Support offline use, no dependency on external APIs

### 2. Local OCR

Support using local OCR models to recognize text in images / PDFs / screenshots, for example:

- PaddleOCR
- Tesseract
- RapidOCR / ONNX OCR
- Other extensible local OCR providers

Expected capabilities:

- Add a "Local OCR" configuration entry in settings
- Local OCR can be selected during attachment / image / PDF parsing
- Support configuration of model path / language / recognition accuracy / orientation detection, etc.
- Support offline use, no uploading of user files
- OCR results can be indexed in knowledge base or used as conversation context

## Use Cases

- Users in privacy-sensitive scenarios who don't want documents, screenshots, PDFs uploaded to the cloud
- Using Cherry Studio in offline or intranet environments
- When building local knowledge bases, wanting embedding to go through local models entirely
- Images, scanned documents, PDFs need OCR before entering knowledge base retrieval

## Suggested Design

- Abstract both embedding and OCR as providers:
  - Cloud Provider
  - Local Provider
- Local Provider can first support Ollama embedding + one of PaddleOCR / Tesseract, then expand later

- Allow selecting OCR provider in attachment parsing / OCR configuration

First screen performance investigation (`pnpm analyze:renderer` output) found: main window **first screen static JS closure ≈ 20.8MB / 8399 modules**, of which **provider icons account for ~3.5MB**. Root cause: `packages/ui/src/components/icons/providers/catalog.ts` statically imports all 159 icon components and assembles them into `PROVIDER_ICON_CATALOG`, which is referenced by the first screen chain → every cold start pulls all icons into the first screen and parses them, even if only a few are rendered. Size is highly concentrated (80/20): 8 source SVGs >50KB = 1.9MB, top 3 = 1.6MB: - `icons/providers/light/aionlabs.svg` 744KB (4272 `` elements, extremely complex vector) - `icons/providers/light/dangbei.svg` 689KB (embedded base64 PNG bitmap) - `icons/providers/light/abacus.svg` 176KB (path + bitmap hybrid) `packages/ui/scripts/validate-svgs.ts` already has "<50KB / no embedded bitmap" checks, but only as warnings, not blocking. ### Desired Solution Convert heavy icons to "static WebP export": 1. Detection: Source SVG satisfies `isImageBased()` (already exists in `svg-utils.ts`) or `size > 50KB` → use WebP branch. 2. Rasterize: Use `sharp@0.34.5` (already in dependencies) to render SVG as WebP (covering max display size ~128–192px). 3. Generate `` leaf component: `generate-icons.ts` outputs `import url from './light.webp'` + ``, outer compound/`.Avatar`/`colorPrimary` unchanged → **zero public API changes, zero consumer code changes**. WebP is output by Vite as independent asset, `` loads on demand, **removed from first screen JS closure**. 4. Change `validate-svgs` size/bitmap checks from warn to error and integrate into CI to prevent regression. Expected first screen closure reduction: -1.9MB. Note: webp chunk is still bundled, saving is in first screen load/parse time, not install package size. ### Alternative Solutions - Use only SVGO aggressive path optimization: limited benefit, potential distortion, ineffective for embedded bitmaps. - Lazy icon registration (catalog dynamic loading): high risk — 13 synchronous consumers expect synchronous `CompoundIcon`, `ProviderLogoPicker` to iterate through full list at render time, codebase has no lazy precedent. body:
> This issue was translated automatically.

### Issue Checklist

- [x] I understand that issues are for reporting problems and requesting features, and I will provide as much detail as possible to help resolve the issue.
- [x] I have searched existing open/closed issues and discussions and did not find a similar suggestion.
- [x] I have provided a short and descriptive title.
- [x] The latest version of Cherry Studio does not include the feature I am suggesting.

### Platform

macOS (platform being analyzed; first screen issue is common across all three platforms)

### Version

2.0.0-dev

### Is your feature request related to an existing issue?

First screen performance investigation found: `src/renderer/i18n/index.ts` **statically imports all 12 language JSONs** when calling `i18n.init({ resources })`:
- `locales/` (human-written original) en-US/zh-CN/zh-TW ≈ 856KB
- `translate/` (machine-translated) de/el/es/fr/ja/pt/ro/ru/vi 9 languages ≈ 3.1MB
- Total **~3.9MB all loaded into first screen closure and parsed**, while users typically only use one language.

### Desired Solution

Only load the current language (+ fallback):
- Use i18next backend for on-demand dynamic import, `import.meta.glob('./{locales,translate}/*.json')` (lazy) to let Vite split each language into independent chunks, loading only `lng` + `fallbackLng` during init.
- Change `void i18n.init(...)` in `index.ts` to `await i18n.init(...)` (module already uses top-level await), keeping `t()` synchronous, zero changes at consumption points, no Suspense needed.

Expected: en-US users 3.9MB → ~290KB (save ~3.6MB); other languages → active+en fallback ~600–750KB (save ~3.2MB). Other languages become on-demand chunks, loaded when switching.

### Alternative Solutions

Zero-dependency approach: pure `import.meta.glob` + manual `addResourceBundle`, wrapping `changeLanguage` (dynamic load+add when switching languages). About 15 lines of custom code.

### Additional Information

- Recommended dependency `i18next-resources-to-backend` (~1KB, official mechanism).
- Does not affect i18n toolchain: `i18next.config.ts` and `scripts/sync-i18n.ts`/`check-i18n.ts` read disk files directly, independent of import method.
- **Important distinction**: Lazy loading saves **first screen load/parse time**, **does not reduce installation package size** (language chunks are still bundled). Reducing package size is a separate lever (delete/remote-ize machine-translated languages, align with `electronLanguages`), orthogonal to this issue.
- `dayjs` locale also currently uses full static import, can be lazified as well (secondary).

- **ChatMarkdown not lazy loaded**: Statically imported by 4 message block components (`MainTextBlock`/`CompactBlock`/`ThinkingBlock`/`MessageTranslate`), chain `HomePage → Chat → … → ChatMarkdown` is all static → even with 0 messages, markdown engine (remark/micromark pipeline ~436KB) is loaded with first screen.
- **Composer RichEditor not lazy loaded**: `ComposerSurface` statically imports editor core, `createExtensions` always adds `EnhancedMath` → `@tiptap/extension-mathematics` → **katex (~0.5–1MB)**.
- **mermaid (~500KB) loaded on mount**: `useMermaid` uses dynamic import, but `CodeStyleProvider` (first screen Provider) calls it **unconditionally** → loaded on every startup mount, regardless of whether there are charts.

> Methodology note: During investigation, `lucide-react` (3260 modules) and `@codemirror` (724KB) appeared to be in first screen static closure, but this is a **barrel illusion** (actual direct connections from real non-barrel components = 0, rollup will tree-shake), already excluded. Criterion: static direct connections from real components > 0 counts as true first screen.

### Desired Solution

Load on content render:
1. **ChatMarkdown lazy loading** (cleanest, independent): Add `ChatMarkdownLazy` (`lazy()` + `Suspense fallback=plain text`), change import paths in 4 block components → markdown engine removed from first screen.
2. **Composer editor lazy mount**: Lightweight placeholder (can focus/input immediately) → mount tiptap on first focus or idle, transfer draft → tiptap + math extension + katex removed from first screen.
3. **mermaid trigger point moved down**: `useMermaid` only triggers when mermaid code block actually appears in current message.

> Dependency: katex has two independent importers (ChatMarkdown and Composer), both 1+2 need to complete for complete removal.

### Alternative Solutions

- Extension-level lazy loading (only lazy tiptap math extension): Not feasible—tiptap extensions are fixed at editor initialization, math node view uses katex synchronously, clean path only exists with whole editor lazy mount.

### Additional Information

- Risk points: Under streaming render, ChatMarkdown first frame fallback is plain text (original text, acceptable experience); editor placeholder→tiptap focus/draft/IME/paste handoff needs separate refinement.
- Verification: `pnpm analyze:renderer` confirms markdown/katex becomes on-demand chunk; production boot timing comparison for first screen.

- **ChatMarkdown 未懒加载**：被 4 个消息块组件静态 import（`MainTextBlock`/`CompactBlock`/`ThinkingBlock`/`MessageTranslate`），链路 `HomePage → Chat → … → ChatMarkdown` 全静态 → 即使 0 条消息，markdown 引擎（remark/micromark 管线 ~436KB）也随首屏加载。
- **Composer RichEditor 未懒加载**：`ComposerSurface` 静态引编辑器内核，`createExtensions` 永远加入 `EnhancedMath` → `@tiptap/extension-mathematics` → **katex（~0.5–1MB）**。
- **mermaid（~500KB）挂载即加载**：`useMermaid` 用动态 import，但 `CodeStyleProvider`（首屏 Provider）**无条件**调用 → 每次启动挂载就拉，与有无图表无关。

> 方法论提醒：排查时 `lucide-react`（3260 模块）与 `@codemirror`（724KB）在静态闭包里看似首屏，实为 **barrel 假象**（被真实非 barrel 组件直连数为 0，rollup 实际会 tree-shake），已排除。判据：被真实组件静态直连 > 0 才算真首屏。

### Desired Solution

随内容渲染时再加载：
1. **ChatMarkdown 懒化**（最干净、独立）：新增 `ChatMarkdownLazy`（`lazy()` + `Suspense fallback=纯文本`），4 个块组件改 import 路径 → markdown 引擎移出首屏。
2. **Composer 编辑器懒挂载**：轻量占位（可立即聚焦/输入）→ 首次聚焦或空闲后挂载 tiptap，转移草稿 → tiptap + 数学扩展 + katex 移出首屏。
3. **mermaid 触发点下移**：`useMermaid` 仅在当前消息真正出现 mermaid 代码块时触发。

> 依赖：katex 有两个独立引入者（ChatMarkdown 与 Composer），需 1+2 都完成才彻底移出。

### Alternative Solutions

- 扩展级懒加载（只懒 tiptap 数学扩展）：不可行——tiptap 扩展在编辑器初始化时固定、math node view 同步用 katex，干净路径只有整编辑器懒挂载。

### Additional Information

- 风险点：流式渲染下 ChatMarkdown 首帧 fallback 为纯文本（即原文，体验可接受）；编辑器占位→tiptap 的焦点/草稿/IME/粘贴交接需单独细化。
- 验证：`pnpm analyze:renderer` 确认 markdown/katex 变按需 chunk；生产 boot 计时对比首屏。
- 属于「首屏砍闭包」系列之一。
</details>

title: [Feature]: Build optimization: lodash → lodash-es, reducing initial bundle by ~350–450KB
body:
> This issue was translated automatically.

### Issue Checklist

- [x] I understand that issues are for reporting problems and requesting features, and I will provide as much detail as possible to help resolve the issue.
- [x] I have searched existing open/closed issues and discussions and did not find a similar suggestion.
- [x] I have provided a short and descriptive title.
- [x] The latest version of Cherry Studio does not include the feature I am suggesting.

### Platform

macOS (analysis platform; initial load issue is common across all three platforms)

### Version

2.0.0-dev

### Is your feature request related to an existing issue?

Initial load performance investigation found that **`lodash` full package (single ~480KB CJS module) is bundled into the initial screen** and cannot be tree-shaken:

- 50 files use `from 'lodash'` (full import), 0 use `lodash-es`.
- `lodash` is a single large CJS module, `import { isEmpty } from 'lodash'` pulls in the entire package.
- Confirmed as true initial screen: statically linked by 43 real components, including core initial screen files `PreferenceService.ts`, `CacheService.ts`, `composites/scrollbar`, `ApiService.ts`, `ChatMarkdown.tsx`, `useModel.ts`, etc.
- Only 20 methods are actually used: `compact debounce findIndex first isEmpty isEqual isNil isUndefined last merge omit omitBy partial sortBy takeRight throttle toInteger toPairs trim uniq`.

### Desired Solution

Migrate `lodash` → `lodash-es` (tree-shakeable ESM):
1. Change 50 files from `from 'lodash'` to `from 'lodash-es'` (all are named imports, no `import _ from`/`import * as`/`from 'lodash/xxx'`/`_.chain()` edge cases → mechanical replacement possible).
2. Dependencies: add `lodash-es` + `@types/lodash-es`, remove `lodash` + `@types/lodash`.

Result: Only ~20 used methods are bundled (tree-shaken, ~tens of KB), **initial bundle reduced by ~350–450KB**. The change is mechanical, API-consistent, low-risk, and **requires no lazy loading/Suspense**.

### Alternative Solutions

Further replacing `isEmpty/isNil/isUndefined/first/last/uniq/trim/compact` etc. with native JS could completely remove the lodash dependency. This can be done as a follow-up; the main benefit is already achieved without it.

### Additional Information

Two small confirmations before implementation:
- Whether tests have `vi.mock('lodash')` / `@test-mocks` mocking lodash (need to sync change to lodash-es).
- Whether vitest can properly transform lodash-es (generally no issue with Vite stack).

This is part of the "initial screen closure reduction" series; this is the most mechanical and lowest-risk item.

title: feat: optimize tools auto mode
body:
> This issue was translated automatically.

## Background

Current tools usage patterns need further optimization, especially for Auto Mode. When using Agent / Chat tool calls, users expect the system to more intelligently determine whether tools need to be called, which tools to call, and how to continuously call tools to complete tasks.

## Requirements

Optimize Tools' Auto Mode to make it closer to "automatically completing tasks" rather than simply "automatically choosing whether to call tools."

## Expected Capabilities

### 1. Smarter Tool Selection

- Automatically determine whether tools need to be called based on user intent
- When multiple tools are available, prioritize the most relevant tool
- Avoid meaningless or repetitive tool calls
- Confirm or downgrade high-risk tool calls

### 2. Support for Continuous Tool Calls

- In Auto Mode, support decision-making for next steps based on previous tool results
- Support multi-step task chains, e.g., search → read → summarize → write/generate result
- When tool calls fail, automatically attempt alternative paths or provide clear errors

### 3. Better User Control

- Users can configure the aggressiveness of Auto Mode, for example:
  - Conservative: only call tools when clearly needed
  - Balanced: automatically call low-risk tools by default
  - Aggressive: automatically advance multi-step tasks as much as possible
- Support per-tool settings for whether Auto Mode can automatically call them
- High-risk actions like write, delete, payment, publish must be confirmed

### 4. Clearer Process Feedback

- Show in UI why Auto Mode calls a certain tool
- Display current tool call chain and next step plan
- Provide readable reasons when tool calls fail, instead of just exposing raw errors
- Users can abort Auto Mode's continuous calls

## Use Cases

- User asks Agent to query materials and organize a report
- User asks Agent to read files, analyze content, and generate results
- User asks Chat to automatically use search, document, and code tools to assist in answering
- User doesn't want to manually approve each low-risk tool call, but still wants high-risk operations controlled

## Suggested Design

- Add risk level / permission metadata for tools
- Auto Mode decides to auto-execute or request confirmation based on risk level
- Introduce tool planning / tool execution loop
- Add trace to tool call process for easier UI display and debugging
- Support user-level / assistant-level / session-level Auto Mode configuration

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Auto Mode can automatically select appropriate tools based on user intent
- [ ] Auto Mode supports continuous multi-step tool calls
- [ ] Low-risk tools can be auto-executed, high-risk tools will request confirmation
- [ ] Users can configure Auto Mode strategy and the scope of tools allowed for auto-calling
- [ ] UI can display tool call reasons, process, and results
- [ ] Users can abort ongoing Auto Mode tool call chains

title: feat: support pi (pi.dev) as an Agent Runtime backend alongside Claude Code
body:
> **Rewritten 2026-07-01.** The original issue mistook "Pi" for Raspberry Pi. The actual intent is to support **[pi](https://pi.dev/) ([earendil-works/pi](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi))** — the open-source, BYOK coding-agent harness — as an Agent Runtime backend alongside Claude Code. The original text is preserved at the bottom.

## Background

Cherry Studio's Agent Runtime already has a clean, registry-based backend abstraction (`AgentSessionRuntimeDriver`, keyed by a `type` string, emitting a normalized `AgentRuntimeEvent` stream), but ships exactly **one** driver today: `claude-code`, built on `@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk`.

**pi** is an open-source coding-agent harness (Mario Zechner / earendil-works). Its key differentiator over Claude Code is that it is **provider-agnostic (BYOK)**: through `@earendil-works/pi-ai` it drives 15–20+ LLM providers (Anthropic, OpenAI, Azure, Gemini/Vertex, Bedrock, xAI, DeepSeek, Mistral, Groq, OpenRouter, local models, …) with runtime model switching. Claude Code is locked to Anthropic.

Adding a `pi` runtime driver lets the in-app Agent run on any provider a user already has a key for, without leaving Cherry Studio's agent UI, tool system, or session model.

## Goal

Add **pi as a second Agent Runtime driver**, implementing the existing `AgentSessionRuntimeDriver` interface, so the agent can be backed by either `claude-code` or `pi` — selected per agent/session.

Non-goal: this is **not** about Raspberry Pi / ARM edge deployment. (If remote/LAN runtime hosting is still wanted, it should be a separate issue built on top of this abstraction.)

## Where it plugs in (current architecture)

- Abstraction + registry: `src/main/ai/runtime/types.ts`, `src/main/ai/runtime/registry.ts` (`runtimeDriverRegistry`, `getAgentSessionDriver(type)`).
- Reference driver: `src/main/ai/runtime/claudeCode/` (`ClaudeCodeRuntimeDriver` → `type = 'claude-code'`).
- Host/consumer: `src/main/ai/agentSession/AgentSessionRuntimeService.ts` resolves the driver by `entry.agentType` and calls `driver.connect(...)`.
- Agent `type` is currently pinned to a single value in `src/shared/data/api/schemas/agents.ts` (`z.enum(['claude-code'])`) — this must be widened to include `'pi'`.
- Renderer is a thin IPC client (`src/renderer/pages/agents/**`); no SDK access there. UI needs a runtime/provider selector.

## Integration surface for pi

pi offers two embedding paths; Electron is a Node host, so **SDK-in-process is preferred**, RPC-subprocess is the fallback for isolation.

**Path A — SDK (preferred).** `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent` exposes `createAgentSession()` / `createAgentSessionRuntime()` (`AgentSessionRuntime`) with `AuthStorage`, `ModelRegistry`, `SessionManager`. Embed directly, no subprocess. Docs: `packages/coding-agent/docs/sdk.md`.

**Path B — RPC subprocess (fallback).** Spawn `pi --mode rpc [--provider … --model … --no-session]`. Protocol is **line-delimited JSON (`\n`-separated, NOT JSON-RPC 2.0; do NOT use Node `readline`)**. Client commands: `prompt` (base64 images), `steer`, `follow_up`, `abort`, `get_state`, `set_model`, `cycle_model`, `get_available_models`, `set_thinking_level`, `bash`, `compact`, `fork`, `clone`, `get_entries` (cursor-based incremental history). Server events: `agent_start`, `message_start/update/end` (with `text_delta`/`thinking_delta`/`toolcall_delta`), `tool_execution_start/update/end`, `turn_end`, `agent_end`, `queue_update`, `compaction_start/end`. Docs: `packages/coding-agent/docs/rpc.md`.

Either path maps cleanly onto the existing `AgentRuntimeEvent` union (`chunk` / `resume-token` / `turn-complete` / `compaction-*` / `context-usage` / `error`) and the `AgentRuntimeConnection` contract (`send` / `redirect` (steer) / `close`).

Install: `curl -fsSL https://pi.dev/install.sh | sh`, or npm `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent` (already listed as an installable binary tool in `src/shared/data/presets/binaryTools.ts`, pointing at `github.com/earendil-works/pi`).

## Expected capabilities

1. **`pi` runtime driver** — `PiRuntimeDriver implements AgentSessionRuntimeDriver`, `type = 'pi'`, `capabilities = ['agent-session']`, registered in `runtimeDriverRegistry`.
2. **Event/stream adapter** — translate pi's streaming events (text/thinking/toolcall deltas, tool execution, turn/agent lifecycle, compaction) into Cherry's `AgentRuntimeEvent` / AI-SDK `UIMessageChunk`.
3. **Session lifecycle** — resume tokens (pi session ids ↔ `resume-token`), steering (`redirect()` → pi `steer`), abort, compaction.
4. **Provider/model selection** — surface pi's multi-provider + runtime model switching (`set_model` / `get_available_models`) through the agent config and renderer UI; reuse Cherry's existing provider/key config where possible.
5. **Tool approval & path guards (important)** — pi ships **no built-in permission system** (fs/process/network isolation is external: Docker / Gondolin / OpenShell sandboxes). We must wire tool approval and directory/command restrictions on our side, reusing the existing `ToolApprovalRegistry` / `canUseTool` pattern from the Claude Code driver so pi doesn't run unguarded.
6. **Agent schema + UI** — widen the agent `type` enum to `'claude-code' | 'pi'`; add runtime selection in the agent settings UI.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A `pi` driver is registered and resolvable via `runtimeDriverRegistry.getAgentSessionDriver('pi')`.
- [ ] An agent configured with `type: 'pi'` can run a full session: prompt → streaming (text/thinking/tool-call) → tool execution → turn complete.
- [ ] Steering, abort, resume, and compaction work through the normalized event/connection contract.
- [ ] Provider + model are selectable for pi-backed agents (at least one non-Anthropic provider verified end-to-end).
- [ ] Tool calls are gated by the existing approval/permission mechanism; no unguarded fs/bash execution.
- [ ] Tests cover the pi event→`AgentRuntimeEvent` adapter and session lifecycle.
- [ ] Docs: how to enable/configure a pi-backed agent, provider setup, and the permission/sandbox caveat.

## Open questions

- **SDK vs RPC** as the primary path — SDK is lighter (no subprocess) but couples us to pi's Node API surface and version; RPC gives process isolation and a stable line protocol. Recommend **SDK first**, keep RPC as a documented fallback.
- **Auth/keys** — reuse Cherry's provider key store vs. pi's `AuthStorage`. Prefer feeding Cherry-managed keys into pi rather than a second key store.
- **Sandbox** — do we require a sandbox (Docker/Gondolin/OpenShell) for pi, or rely solely on our tool-approval layer for v1?

## References

- pi.dev — https://pi.dev/
- Repo — https://github.com/earendil-works/pi (mirror: badlogic/pi-mono)
- RPC protocol — https://github.com/badlogic/pi-mono/blob/main/packages/coding-agent/docs/rpc.md
- SDK — https://github.com/badlogic/pi-mono/blob/main/packages/coding-agent/docs/sdk.md
- pi-acp (third-party ACP bridge, spawns `pi --mode rpc`) — https://github.com/svkozak/pi-acp

---
<details>
<summary>Original content (Raspberry Pi interpretation — superseded)</summary>

## Background

We want Cherry Studio Agent Runtime to support running on lightweight local devices like Pi / Raspberry Pi, allowing users to deploy the Agent execution environment to low-power, always-online local machines.

## Requirements

Support Pi as Agent Runtime to host Agent capabilities such as tool calls, task execution, file processing, script running, etc.

## Use Cases

- Users want to run Agent Runtime persistently on Raspberry Pi / Pi-like devices
- Main computer doesn't need to stay on; Agent tasks can continue executing on local low-power devices
- Use Pi as a local Agent execution node in home / studio / intranet environments
- Complete automation tasks with local models, local files, NAS, and intranet services
- Allow Cherry Studio desktop client to connect to remote/LAN Agent Runtime

## Expected Capabilities

### 1. Support deploying Agent Runtime on Pi devices
- Support Linux ARM64 / ARMv7 environments
- Provide deployment instructions for Raspberry Pi / Debian / Ubuntu Server
- Runtime can run as a background service, e.g., systemd service
- Support auto-start on boot

### 2. Desktop client connects to external Runtime
- Cherry Studio can configure Agent Runtime address
- Support LAN connections, e.g., `http://pi.local:xxxx`
- Support connection status detection, version detection, capability detection
- Provide clear error messages when Runtime is unavailable

### 3. Tool and Task Execution Capabilities
- Support executing Agent tool calls in Pi Runtime
- Support basic capabilities like file read/write, command execution, script running
- Support tasks running continuously in Runtime without depending on desktop client
- Support viewing task logs, running status, failure reasons

### 4. Security and Permission Control
- Runtime requires authentication mechanisms like access token / pairing code / API key
- By default only listen on localhost or LAN, avoid exposing to public network
- Support restricting accessible directories, executable commands, tool permissions
- High-risk operations require confirmation or permission configuration

### 5. Lightweight and Resource Adaptation
- Adapt to low memory, low CPU environments
- Support configuring concurrency, task queue, timeout
- Support disabling high resource-consuming capabilities
- Provide clear dependency installation and compatibility instructions for ARM devices

## Suggested Design
- Abstract Agent Runtime as a remotely connectable execution node
- Desktop client handles interaction, configuration, result display
- Pi Runtime handles actual task execution, tool calls, and log storage
- Support both local runtime and remote runtime modes
- Can later extend to NAS, home servers, cloud hosts, etc.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Can install and start Agent Runtime on Raspberry Pi / Linux ARM64
- [ ] Runtime supports background running and auto-start on boot
- [ ] Cherry Studio desktop client can connect to Pi Runtime
- [ ] Agent can execute basic tool calls and tasks on Pi Runtime
- [ ] Can view Runtime status, task logs, and error messages
- [ ] Runtime has basic authentication and permission control, won't expose to public network by default
- [ ] Documentation includes Pi deployment steps, configuration methods, and limitations

</details>

### Platform

### Version

2.0.0-dev

### Bug Description

The chat and topic menu render paths statically import `src/renderer/utils/export.ts`, which pulls provider-specific export stacks before the user invokes any export action.

Exact static paths found during the renderer audit:

- `src/renderer/components/chat/messages/hooks/useMessageExportActions.ts` imports `exportMarkdownToJoplin`, `exportMarkdownToSiyuan`, `exportMarkdownToYuque`, `exportMessageAsMarkdown`, `exportMessageToNotes`, `exportMessageToNotion`, and `messageToMarkdown` from `@renderer/utils/export` at module load.
- `src/renderer/components/chat/messages/frame/messageMenuBarActions.tsx` imports `messageToMarkdown` and `messageToPlainText` from `@renderer/utils/export` at module load.
- `src/renderer/pages/home/Tabs/components/useTopicMenuActions.ts` imports copy/export helpers from `@renderer/utils/export` and `@renderer/utils/copy`; `utils/copy.ts` also imports `topicToMarkdown` and plain-text helpers from `./export`.
- `src/renderer/services/MessagesService.ts` imports only `getTitleFromString` from `@renderer/utils/export`, but that still evaluates the whole export module.
- `src/renderer/utils/export.ts` has top-level imports for `@notionhq/client`, `@tryfabric/martian`, `notion-helper`, `DOMPurify`, and image capture helpers.

This violates the Vercel React best-practices bundle rules for conditional/dynamic heavy dependencies: action-only export provider code should not be in the normal chat render/menu bundle.

Risk: opening chat, rendering message menus, or rendering topic menus can pay parse/evaluation cost for Notion/Yuque/Joplin/markdown export code even when the user never exports anything.

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Inspect `src/renderer/components/chat/messages/hooks/useMessageExportActions.ts`, `src/renderer/components/chat/messages/frame/messageMenuBarActions.tsx`, `src/renderer/pages/home/Tabs/components/useTopicMenuActions.ts`, and `src/renderer/services/MessagesService.ts`.
2. Follow their static imports into `src/renderer/utils/export.ts`.
3. Observe that provider export dependencies are imported at the top of `utils/export.ts` instead of inside the callbacks that need them.

### Expected Behavior

Regular chat/message/topic render paths should only load lightweight formatting helpers. Provider-specific export stacks should load when the corresponding export action runs, or live in narrowly imported modules that are not touched by normal rendering.

Minimal expected fix:

- Move lightweight helpers such as `getTitleFromString` and plain text conversion out of `utils/export.ts`, or split export providers into separate modules.
- Use dynamic imports inside export callbacks for Notion/Yuque/Joplin/Siyuan/Notes actions where appropriate.
- Keep existing export behavior unchanged.

### Relevant Log Output

```shell
N/A
```

### Additional Context

Audit rules used: `vercel-react-best-practices` bundle dynamic-import / conditional dependency rules. This is distinct from #16478, which covers first-screen lazy loading of `ChatMarkdown`, Composer, and Mermaid; this issue covers export utility imports in action/menu paths.

### Platform

macOS

### Version

2.0.0-dev

### Bug Description

`src/renderer/utils/markdown.ts` mixes lightweight render helpers with parser/editing helpers that import markdown parser dependencies at module load.

Exact files:

- `src/renderer/utils/markdown.ts` imports `remark-parse`, `remark-stringify`, `remove-markdown`, `unified`, and `unist-util-visit` at the top level.
- Hot render/action paths import only lightweight helpers from that same module:
  - `src/renderer/components/chat/messages/markdown/ChatMarkdown.tsx` uses `processLatexBrackets`.
  - `src/renderer/components/chat/messages/markdown/CodeBlock.tsx` uses `getCodeBlockId`.
  - `src/renderer/components/chat/messages/markdown/Link.tsx` uses `findCitationInChildren`.
  - `src/renderer/components/chat/messages/frame/messageMenuBarActions.tsx` uses `removeTrailingDoubleSpaces`.
  - `src/renderer/services/ApiService.ts` uses `purifyMarkdownImages`.

Most of those callers do not need `unified`, `remark-parse`, `remark-stringify`, or `remove-markdown`, but the shared module import makes them part of the static dependency path.

This violates the Vercel React best-practices bundle rules for keeping heavy dependencies conditional and avoiding barrel-like utility modules that force unrelated code into render paths.

Risk: normal chat markdown rendering and message menu code can pay parser dependency cost for code-block editing or plain-text export paths that are not currently used.

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Open `src/renderer/utils/markdown.ts` and note the top-level parser imports.
2. Open `src/renderer/components/chat/messages/markdown/ChatMarkdown.tsx`, `CodeBlock.tsx`, and `Link.tsx`.
3. Observe that those files import lightweight helpers from `@renderer/utils/markdown`, forcing the parser imports to load with them.

### Expected Behavior

Lightweight helpers used during rendering should live in a lightweight module with no parser dependencies. Parser/editing helpers such as `updateCodeBlock` and plain-text export helpers should import parser packages only in their own module or dynamically when invoked.

Minimal expected fix:

- Split lightweight helpers (`findCitationInChildren`, `processLatexBrackets`, `convertMathFormula`, `removeTrailingDoubleSpaces`, `getCodeBlockId`, `isHtmlCode`, `purifyMarkdownImages`) away from parser-backed helpers.
- Keep existing behavior and tests for markdown rendering and code-block editing.

### Relevant Log Output

```shell
N/A
```

### Additional Context

Audit rules used: `vercel-react-best-practices` bundle dynamic-import / conditional dependency rules. This complements, but does not duplicate, #16478: even if `ChatMarkdown` is lazy-loaded, message menu and service paths still import lightweight helpers from this mixed module.

### Version

### Bug Description

`src/renderer/utils/image.ts` statically imports both image compression and DOM capture libraries even for callers that only need one small helper.

Exact files:

- `src/renderer/utils/image.ts` imports `browser-image-compression` and `html-to-image` at the top level.
- `src/renderer/components/chat/messages/MessageList.tsx` imports `captureScrollable` and `captureScrollableAsDataURL` from `@renderer/utils/image` for topic image actions.
- `src/renderer/components/chat/messages/frame/messageMenuBarActions.tsx` imports `captureScrollableAsBlob` and `captureScrollableAsDataURL` for copy/export image actions.
- `src/renderer/services/ImageStorage.ts`, `src/renderer/components/Popups/UserPopup.tsx`, and provider/mini-app editors import lightweight conversion/avatar helpers from the same module.

As a result, callers that only need Base64 conversion or avatar compression can pull DOM capture code, and chat message render/action paths can load capture libraries before the user runs an image export/copy action.

This violates the Vercel React best-practices bundle rules for conditional heavy dependencies.

Risk: normal chat rendering and basic image utility users pay parse/evaluation cost for `html-to-image` and/or `browser-image-compression` before the corresponding image action actually runs.

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Open `src/renderer/utils/image.ts`.
2. Note the top-level imports for `browser-image-compression` and `html-to-image`.
3. Follow imports from `src/renderer/components/chat/messages/MessageList.tsx`, `src/renderer/components/chat/messages/frame/messageMenuBarActions.tsx`, and lightweight image utility callers.
4. Observe that the heavy libraries are not isolated to the functions that need them.

### Expected Behavior

Image compression and DOM capture dependencies should load only when the relevant image operation runs, or live in narrowly imported modules.

Minimal expected fix:

- Dynamically import `html-to-image` inside capture functions, or move capture functions to a dedicated module that only action handlers import on demand.
- Dynamically import `browser-image-compression` inside `compressImage`, or move avatar/compression helpers to a dedicated module.

### Platform

macOS

### Version

2.0.0-dev

### Bug Description

Every rendered code fence imports the special preview component map, which statically imports all special preview implementations even when the current code block is not Mermaid, PlantUML, SVG, DOT, or Graphviz.

Exact files:

- `src/renderer/components/chat/messages/markdown/CodeBlock.tsx` imports `CodeBlockView` from `@renderer/components/CodeBlockView` for ordinary code fences.
- `src/renderer/components/CodeBlockView/view.tsx` imports `SPECIAL_VIEW_COMPONENTS` from `./constants`.
- `src/renderer/components/CodeBlockView/constants.ts` statically imports `GraphvizPreview`, `MermaidPreview`, `PlantUmlPreview`, and `SvgPreview` from `@renderer/components/Preview`.
- `src/renderer/components/Preview/PlantUmlPreview.tsx` imports `pako`; `GraphvizPreview` prepares the Graphviz preview path; `MermaidPreview` wires Mermaid rendering hooks.

This violates the Vercel React best-practices bundle dynamic-import rule: optional preview renderers should be loaded when a matching code fence needs them, not for every source code block.

Risk: ordinary code-heavy chats pay parse/evaluation cost for diagram preview UI paths even when no diagram preview is present.

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Open any message containing a normal code block such as `typescript` or `python`.
2. Follow the static import path `CodeBlock.tsx -> @renderer/components/CodeBlockView -> view.tsx -> constants.ts`.
3. Observe that all special preview components are imported unconditionally through `constants.ts`.

### Expected Behavior

Normal code blocks should load the source viewer/editor and toolbar only. Mermaid, PlantUML, SVG, DOT, and Graphviz preview components should be lazy-loaded only when the code block language matches a special view.

Minimal expected fix:

- Keep `SPECIAL_VIEWS` lightweight.
- Replace the eager `SPECIAL_VIEW_COMPONENTS` map with lazy-loaded components or a resolver that imports each preview component only for the matching language.
- Preserve current source/special/split view behavior and toolbar behavior.

N/A

Audit rules used: `vercel-react-best-practices` bundle dynamic-import / conditional dependency rules. This is narrower than #16478; it targets code-block special preview components loaded by all code fences.

title: [Bug]: Citation fetch loads article parsers before citation expansion
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched for existing issues and open PRs to avoid duplicates.
- [x] This is a high-confidence renderer performance issue found by the daily React audit.

### Platform

macOS

### Version

`main` at `a0bf51a1a0380c89defbead778df6e4aef707c39`

### Bug Description

`src/renderer/utils/fetch.ts` imports `@mozilla/readability` and `turndown` at module load time and constructs a `TurndownService` singleton immediately:

- `src/renderer/utils/fetch.ts:2` imports `Readability`
- `src/renderer/utils/fetch.ts:7` imports `TurndownService`
- `src/renderer/utils/fetch.ts:11` constructs `new TurndownService()`

The heavy parser path is only needed when the user expands citation content. Current renderer callers include citation UI paths such as:

- `src/renderer/components/chat/messages/blocks/CitationsList.tsx:6`
- `src/renderer/components/chat/messages/blocks/CitationsList.tsx:184`
- `src/renderer/components/chat/messages/markdown/CitationTooltip.tsx`

This violates `$vercel-react-best-practices` bundle rules for conditional/deferred third-party code: large, feature-specific dependencies should be loaded only when that feature path is actually used. Importing `fetch.ts` for lightweight helpers such as `isValidUrl`, `isXPostUrl`, `fetchXOEmbed`, or `fetchRedirectUrl` should not eagerly load article extraction and HTML-to-markdown conversion code.

### Steps To Reproduce

title: [Bug]: Cherry Studio continuously leaks powershell processes — 188 accumulated in 2 days, bringing down the entire system
body:
> This issue was translated automatically.

## Bug Description

When Cherry Studio v1.9.11 runs in the background on Windows 11, it creates a powershell.exe process approximately every 15 minutes and **never reclaims it**. Over 2 days, **188 zombie powershell processes** accumulated, and together with associated leaked pwsh / conhost processes, a total of ~400+ processes consumed about 26 GB of physical memory. This triggered Windows Memory Compression to spike to 12 GB, causing severe system-wide lag.

## Evidence

### 1. Parent Process Confirmation

```
PS> Get-Process -Id 73072
Process: Cherry Studio (PID: 73072)
Started: 06/27/2026 22:03:57
Memory: 167 MB
Path: D:\Program Files\Cherry Studio\Cherry Studio.exe
```

### 2. Child Process Leak

```
powershell parent process distribution:
  PPID 73072 (Cherry Studio) → 188 processes
  PPID 68772 (Codex)         →   3 processes
  PPID 125364                →   1 process
```

**All 188 powershell processes have Cherry Studio as their parent process.**

### 3. Identical Command Line

All 188 processes execute the same command:

```
powershell "Get-CimInstance -ClassName Win32_LogicalDisk | Select-Object Caption, FreeSpace, Size"
```

### 4. System Impact

| Metric | Before Cleanup | After Cleanup |
|--------|----------------|---------------|
| powershell processes | 193 | 3 |
| pwsh processes | 197 | 2 |
| conhost processes | 211 | 20 |
| Free memory | 13.4 GB | 19.9 GB |
| Memory Compression | **12.2 GB** | 9.7 GB (gradually releasing) |

Memory Compression at 12 GB is a direct signal of system memory pressure. At this point, CPU was maxed out by compression/decompression, and the entire system became unresponsive.

### 5. Timeline

Cherry Studio ran from 6/27 22:03 to 6/29 early morning, approximately 48 hours.
188 processes ÷ 48h ≈ one new powershell every 15 minutes, never reclaimed.

## Environment

- **OS**: Windows 11 (64GB RAM)
- **Cherry Studio Version**: v1.9.11
- **Installation Method**: Manual install (D:\Program Files\Cherry Studio\)
- **User MCP List**: `@cherry/mcp-auto-install` not configured (database mcps list only has 5 other MCPs)
- **Background Runtime**: Approximately 48 hours

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Launch Cherry Studio v1.9.11 on Windows
2. Keep it running in the background for 24+ hours (no active usage required)
3. Open Task Manager → Details → Sort by name and find powershell.exe
4. Observe powershell process count growing linearly over time
5. Use Process Explorer or `Get-CimInstance` to confirm all parent processes are Cherry Studio.exe

## Expected Behavior

Cherry Studio should not leak powershell processes indefinitely in the background. If periodic disk space checks are needed, the same process should be reused or properly reclaimed.

## Additional Information

- A similar situation occurred on June 7 (159 zombie processes at that time), which was cleaned up and then re-accumulated to 188 before being discovered
- User did not enable `@cherry/mcp-auto-install` in MCP settings, indicating this is not an MCP plugin-level issue but rather Cherry Studio core process behavior
- The `Get-CimInstance Win32_LogicalDisk` in the command line is a WMI query for disk free space, suspected to be related to the built-in disk space check for the MCP auto-install feature

2.0.0-dev

### Is your feature request related to an existing issue?

The current file transfer in Channels (`src/main/ai/channels`) is **one-way inbound only**:

- Images/files sent from the IM side are downloaded and saved to the agent's workspace for the agent to read via the Read tool (see "Persisted channel files to workspace" in `ChannelMessageHandler`).
- However, **outbound can only send text**: `ChannelAdapter` only exposes `sendMessage(chatId, text)` / `sendTypingIndicator`, with no capability to send files/documents.

The result: when the agent produces files in workspace/session (code, logs, reports, build artifacts, etc.), these files cannot be sent back to the IM side. Users only receive text and cannot access the files themselves.

### Desired Solution

Enable Channels to support **outbound file forwarding**: send files from workspace/session back to IM clients, as the reverse capability of the existing inbound flow.

Suggested directions:

- Add outbound file capability to the `ChannelAdapter` abstraction (e.g., `sendFile(chatId, file, opts?)` / `sendDocument`), and implement it in each adapter (Telegram / Discord / Slack / Feishu / QQ / WeChat) using their respective SDKs (Telegram `sendDocument`, Discord attachments, Slack `files.upload`, etc.).
- Provide an entry point/mechanism to select and forward files from workspace/session (e.g., automatically push artifact files to the corresponding chat after an agent task completes, or explicitly specify file paths to forward).
- Reuse existing security layers (`security/OutputSanitizer`, `ExternalContentGuard`) to perform necessary validation on outbound files.
- Provide success/failure feedback for forwarding results and write to channel logs (`ChannelLogBuffer`).

### Alternative Solutions

- Only return text + local file path (current status, IM side cannot access the file).
- Upload to external storage and return a share link instead of sending the file directly.

### Additional Information

Design points to confirm:

- Trigger method: automatically forward artifacts when agent task ends, or have agent/user explicitly specify file paths to forward?
- Forwarding scope and security: limit to session.workspace path to prevent unauthorized access to arbitrary files.
- How to uniformly handle and degrade platform-specific file size/type limits (fallback to links or prompts when exceeding limits).
- File body or share link (see above).

Related code: `src/main/ai/channels/ChannelAdapter.ts`, `src/main/ai/channels/ChannelMessageHandler.ts`, `src/main/ai/channels/adapters/*`.

title: [Bug]: Lazy-load chat video player outside the default message render path

## Platform

All renderer platforms (macOS / Windows / Linux)

## Version

`main` at `a77f6f5c9a939f6462fc5c002a71f48b38dec28e`

## Bug Description

The shared chat message rendering path eagerly imports the video player stack even when the current conversation contains no video parts.

Exact path:

- `src/renderer/components/chat/messages/blocks/MessagePartsRenderer.tsx` is the shared message content entry for Home, Agents, History, Quick Assistant, and other chat-like surfaces. It statically imports `../frame/MessageVideo`.
- `src/renderer/components/chat/messages/frame/MessageVideo.tsx` statically imports `react-player`.
- `react-player` is only needed for `data-video` parts, which are rare compared with text, tool, image, and file messages.

This violates the Vercel React performance rule **Dynamic Imports for Heavy Components** from `.agents/skills/vercel-react-best-practices/rules/bundle-dynamic-imports.md`: heavy components that are not needed on the initial render should be lazy-loaded on demand. Because `MessagePartsRenderer` is on the normal message list render path, `react-player` can be pulled into the eager chat bundle even for conversations that never render video.

Risk:

- Higher initial JavaScript cost for the main chat message path.
- Slower startup / message-list TTI for non-video conversations.
- The dependency remains coupled to shared message rendering instead of the specific `data-video` branch that needs it.

## Steps To Reproduce

1. Open `src/renderer/components/chat/messages/blocks/MessagePartsRenderer.tsx`.
2. Note that it statically imports `MessageVideo` from `../frame/MessageVideo`.
3. Open `src/renderer/components/chat/messages/frame/MessageVideo.tsx`.
4. Note that it statically imports `ReactPlayer` from `react-player`.
5. Render a normal chat message with only text/tool/file parts. The shared renderer module graph still includes the video player dependency.

## Expected Behavior

The heavy video player implementation should be loaded only when a `data-video` part is rendered.

Minimal expected fix:

- Keep `MessagePartsRenderer` free of the direct `MessageVideo` import.
- Lazy-load `MessageVideo` (or at least `react-player`) only inside the `data-video` render branch.
- Preserve the existing video rendering behavior and tests.

## Platform

## Is your feature request related to an existing issue?

When using Ollama models, the `contextWindow` value set per model in Cherry Studio is never passed to the Ollama API as the `num_ctx` parameter. This means users cannot control Ollama's context window size through Cherry Studio — the model's metadata `contextWindow` field is only used internally for tool deferral decisions, not sent in API requests.

**Current behavior:**
- Users can edit `contextWindow` in the Model Drawer UI
- This value is stored in the database and displayed in model selectors
- At runtime, it's only used for tool deferral thresholds (`shouldDefer.ts`)
- The `num_ctx` parameter is **never** included in Ollama API request bodies

## Desired Solution

Automatically map the per-model `contextWindow` value to the Ollama `num_ctx` parameter when constructing API requests.

**Implementation:**
- In `buildOllamaProviderOptions()` (at `src/main/ai/utils/options.ts:405-416`), read `model.contextWindow` and populate `ollama.options.num_ctx` if set
- The upstream `ollama-ai-provider-v2` SDK already supports `num_ctx` through `ollamaProviderOptions.options.num_ctx` — no SDK changes needed

**Expected behavior:**
1. User sets `contextWindow` to e.g. `8192` in the Model Drawer for an Ollama model
2. When sending a chat request, the Ollama API receives `options: { num_ctx: 8192 }` in the request body
3. Ollama uses this value to set the context window size for the request

## Alternative Solutions

Users can currently work around this by manually adding `num_ctx` via the assistant's custom parameters mechanism, but this is not a designed or documented path and requires knowledge of the Ollama API structure.

## Additional Information

**Relevant code paths:**
- `src/main/ai/utils/options.ts:405-416` — `buildOllamaProviderOptions()` only passes `think`, not `num_ctx`
- `node_modules/ollama-ai-provider-v2/dist/index.mjs:805-826` — SDK schema supports `num_ctx` in `options` sub-object
- `src/main/ai/tools/adapters/aiSdk/exposition/shouldDefer.ts:24-26` — `FALLBACK_CONTEXT_WINDOW = 32_000` used when contextWindow is undefined
