title: [Discussion]: Server-side topic/session resource lists and removal of unused topic.groupId
body:
### Issue Checklist

- [x] I understand that issues are meant for feedback and problem-solving, not for venting, and I will provide as much detail as possible to help resolve the issue.
- [x] I have checked the pinned issues and searched through the existing open issues, closed issues, and discussions. #16851 is related, but only covers aligning the existing pagination order; this issue intentionally supersedes it with the broader architecture question.
- [x] I confirm that I am here to discuss an architecture adjustment, not to report a product bug or request an unrelated feature.

### Platform

macOS (the architecture is platform-agnostic)

### Version

2.0.0-dev (`main`; review baseline `35f6a8943f`)

### Your Question

Should Topic and Agent Session resource lists move from renderer-side full-data processing to Main/DataApi-owned filtering, ordering, factual aggregation, and cursor pagination? As part of that work, should the unused persisted `topic.groupId` relation be removed while preserving the generic entity types still required by Pin and Tag?

> **Revision note (2026-07-10):** this proposal was rewritten after review against the current frontend behavior, the DataApi/IpcApi boundary, and the relevant known Topic/Session write paths. The revised design keeps keyset pagination, flat list endpoints, server-side stats, and removal of `topic.groupId`, but corrects several errors in the previous draft:
>
> - data freshness now uses the existing DataApi subscription surface, not new row-bearing IpcApi events;
> - the shared `EntityTypeSchema` keeps `topic` and `session` because Pin/Tag still use them;
> - History remains two mode-specific streams and preserves `running | completed | failed`;
> - request count is bounded per surface rather than incorrectly promised as exactly two;
> - search contracts, pinned-count semantics, unlinked/workdir scopes, and remote-list interactions are explicit;
> - `createdAt`, caller-controlled sort direction, and cross-resource k-way merge are removed because there is no current consumer.

#### Confirmed problem

The current resource-list path is effectively:

```text
DataApi cursor pages
  -> renderer automatically loads every page
  -> renderer retains all topics/sessions
  -> renderer searches, groups, sorts, and counts the full arrays
  -> ResourceList slices those arrays for "Show more"
```

Confirmed call sites include:

- `src/renderer/hooks/resourceViewSources.ts`: `useTopics({ loadAll: true })` and `useSessions(..., { loadAll: true })`.
- `src/renderer/hooks/useTopic.ts` and `src/renderer/hooks/agent/useSession.ts`: automatic paging until completion.
- `src/renderer/components/chat/resourceList/base/ResourceListProvider.tsx`: local search/group/sort/count and local-only "Show more".
- `src/renderer/pages/home/Tabs/components/topicsHelpers.ts`: Topic time/assistant grouping and ordering.
- `src/renderer/pages/agents/components/sessionListHelpers.ts`: Session time/agent/workdir grouping and ordering.
- `src/renderer/pages/history/HistoryRecordsPage.tsx`: full-array source/status counts, filtering, and ordering.

Consequences:

- Cursor pagination is currently transport batching rather than a renderer-memory boundary.
- First useful render can wait for complete history (`AgentResourceList.tsx` gates loading on `isFullyLoaded`).
- Renderer memory, search, grouping, and count work scale with complete history.
- Main and renderer ordering semantics can diverge.
- Group counts, classic rails, reveal/delete navigation, and "Show more" implicitly depend on complete arrays.

#### Goals

1. Render the first usable page without loading the complete Topic/Session history.
2. Keep SQLite-backed reads and freshness inside DataApi; keep runtime-only stream state in Cache.
3. Make filtering, supported ordering, pagination, and factual counts consistent across windows.
4. Preserve current pinned sections, grouping modes, History status filters, drag anchors, reveal behavior, and active-item navigation unless a behavior change is called out explicitly.
5. Remove persisted `topic.groupId` residue if no scheduled product requirement owns it.

#### Non-goals

- A combined Topic+Session History stream. Current History selects exactly one mode.
- Arbitrary list sorting. Current consumers need only activity order and manual order.
- Persisting runtime session status in SQLite.
- A UI-shaped nested grouped-list endpoint.
- FTS for short resource names without benchmark evidence.
- Row-level renderer cache merging in the first iteration; invalidation and refetch are the simpler consistency baseline.

#### Proposed DataApi direction

Keep flat collection endpoints. Main/DataApi owns SQL filtering, the two supported ordering profiles, keyset cursor construction, list projections, and factual aggregation. Renderer keeps localized labels, section composition, expanded/collapsed state, locale-derived time boundaries, selection, and navigation policy.

Handlers stay thin. SQL, validation, cursor logic, projections, and transactions live in `TopicService` / `AgentSessionService` and shared data-service utilities. Data change notification extends the existing DataApi subscription path rather than adding a second data channel to IpcApi.

#### Design decisions

**D1. Minimal keyset list contracts**

- Activity surfaces use `updatedAt DESC`; entity-grouped manual order uses `orderKey ASC`.
- The query exposes `sortBy: updatedAt | orderKey`; direction is derived from `sortBy`. There is no `createdAt` or caller-controlled `sortOrder` until a real consumer exists.
- Cursors are opaque `(sortValue, id)` tuples using the shared `keysetCursor.ts` helpers. A cursor is valid only with the same resource/filter/sort query.
- Deleting the former anchor does not invalidate a value cursor. Mutating a sort key between page requests may move a row across the boundary; D2 invalidation refetches the active windows instead of relying on a false wall-clock monotonicity guarantee.
- Responses remain `{ items, nextCursor }`; counts come only from stats.

**D2. DataApi subscription invalidation, after commit**

The renderer and preload already expose `dataApi.subscribe`; `src/main/data/api/core/adapters/IpcAdapter.ts` currently contains the unfinished Main-side handlers. Complete that path and keep SQLite data events out of IpcApi.

- Subscribers receive a typed resource invalidation/reset signal, not a database row used as a second read channel.
- Notification is delivered only to subscribed windows and occurs after the surrounding write transaction commits. Rolled-back writes must not publish.
- One resource invalidation covers list, infinite-list, stats, by-id, and joined pin projections for that resource. Renderer refetch is coalesced/debounced.
- Subscription establishment must close the subscribe-versus-initial-fetch race, for example with a resource revision or an initial reset/refetch handshake.
- Bulk import/migration may emit one reset after completion.

The producer inventory is part of the contract, not an implementation detail:

- Topic writes include `TopicService`, nested Topic mutations from `MessageService`, Temporary Chat promotion, assistant deletion/nulling, seeding/migration/bulk operations, and Topic pin mutations.
- Agent Session writes include `AgentSessionService`, activity touches from `AgentSessionMessageService`, agent/workspace deletion effects, owner/workspace metadata changes that affect joined search or workdir grouping, bulk operations, and Session pin mutations.
- `PinService` must invalidate the corresponding Topic/Session resource because list projections include pin metadata.

Start with invalidation + DataApi refetch. Add row-level window merging only if profiling shows that local aggregate/list refetch is the bottleneck and its transactional/event semantics are specified separately.

**D3. Stats are factual and define pinned semantics**

Stats accept the same record filters as lists, except cursor/limit. Time boundaries are named query values computed by Renderer (`todayStart`, `yesterdayStart`, `weekStart`) rather than an ambiguously ordered tuple; Main applies the same inclusion rules as `getResourceTimeBucket`.

Each breakdown is an array record, not an object map, so null/unlinked scopes are representable. Each entry returns both `count` and `pinnedCount`:

```ts
type CountWithPins = { count: number; pinnedCount: number }

type TopicStats = {
  total: number
  pinnedCount: number
  byAssistant: Array<{ assistantId: string | null } & CountWithPins>
  byUpdatedAtBucket: Record<'today' | 'yesterday' | 'this-week' | 'earlier', CountWithPins>
}
```

ResourceList derives ordinary group counts as `count - pinnedCount`; History source counts use `count`. Session stats follow the same rule for Agent and workdir facts. Missing/dangling owners collapse into the explicit unlinked entry.

Stats and list calls are separate SQLite snapshots, so temporary disagreement during a concurrent mutation is allowed; D2 invalidation reconciles both.

**D4. Group loading is bounded, but not falsely described as query-free**

- Time mode is one `updatedAt DESC` stream with renderer-inserted section headers plus one stats query. The pinned section may use the existing composite pinned/entity cursor generalized for activity order.
- Entity mode uses stats, one global pinned stream, and one stream per expanded entity scope. Initial load requests only the active scope, so first paint remains O(1), but it is normally three resource requests rather than exactly two.
- Topic scopes must distinguish a concrete `assistantId` from `unlinked`.
- Session scopes must distinguish a concrete `agentId` from `unlinked`. Workdir scope uses one centrally defined version of the current path normalization, may represent multiple workspace rows, and exposes system/no-workdir explicitly; Main and Renderer must not maintain separate normalization implementations.
- Existing "Expand all" necessarily creates work proportional to the number of groups. Requests must be queued with bounded concurrency and loaded on demand; this action is not included in the first-paint guarantee. If profiling shows unacceptable fan-out, a bounded first-page batch endpoint or a product change to "expand loaded groups" requires a separate decision.

**D5. Pinned rows remain first-class**

- List items use a fixed projection that includes `pinned`, pin id, and pin order metadata from a SQL JOIN.
- Time/unscoped views may retain the shared composite pinned-then-entity cursor in `pinnedListCursor.ts`.
- Entity views require a global pinned query plus the active scoped unpinned query; scoping the only query to one entity would otherwise hide pins from other entities.
- Pin create/delete/reorder invalidates Topic/Session list and stats windows through D2.
- The generic `/pins` API remains available for other consumers until their migrations are independently proven complete.

**D6. Search behavior is explicit and literal**

- Topic search is a case-insensitive literal substring over Topic name.
- Agent Session resource-list search is a literal substring over Session name.
- Agent History currently searches Session name, description, and Agent name. It uses an explicit closed `searchScope: name | full`; `full` preserves that OR behavior rather than silently reducing History to name-only search.
- Normalization must be the same on stored shadow values and query terms. Changing from current `toLowerCase()` to locale-sensitive casing or NFKC is a deliberate product behavior change, not "exact parity".
- Use literal substring semantics (`instr(normalizedColumn, normalizedTerm) > 0`, or correctly escaped `LIKE`) so `%`, `_`, and `\` are not interpreted as user-supplied wildcards.
- Any internal shadow columns are excluded from public entity/list projections and backfilled during schema generation/migration. `full` search also requires a normalized Agent-name value, and Agent rename must invalidate affected Agent Session queries through D2.
- FTS remains out of scope unless measurements on the agreed dataset justify it.

**D7. History keeps separate resources and all three statuses**

- Assistant History pages `/topics`; Agent History pages `/agent-sessions`. There is no cross-resource k-way merge.
- Runtime maintains typed, disjoint shared-cache sets for active and failed session ids, following the lifecycle of the existing per-session status keys: start/restart, success, error, deletion, and app restart must be defined.
- Running/failed rows are fetched by bounded `ids` pages and then intersected with the active source/search filters.
- `completed = stats.total - matchingActive - matchingFailed`.
- Completed list loading uses the normal SQL cursor and skips active/failed ids in Renderer, over-fetching until the requested visible page is filled; status remains outside DataApi/SQLite.
- History uses infinite-scroll loading. "Select all" selects only the rows displayed at the moment the action is triggered. Pages loaded afterward are not selected automatically, and changing mode, source, status, or search clears the selection so hidden rows cannot be changed accidentally. Bulk actions continue to receive explicit selected ids only.

**D8. Remote ResourceList is a prerequisite, not a follow-up**

Before migrating a surface, ResourceList needs a remote-data contract for:

- controlled search/scope/sort state;
- per-group cursor, loading, empty, and error state;
- real "Show more" requests;
- asynchronous group-header selection that loads the first row before navigating;
- revealing an active id outside the loaded window;
- selecting a valid neighbor after deleting the active row;
- classic entity-rail visibility and first-row navigation;
- create-new seed selection when the latest unpinned row is not loaded;
- stable drag anchors and post-mutation backfill;
- History infinite scroll and bulk selection semantics.

The provider/interaction work must land before Topics, Sessions, or History stop receiving full arrays.

**D9. `topic.groupId` is removed without breaking Pin/Tag entity types**

The active renderer does not consume persisted `Topic.groupId`; displayed Topic groups are derived from pin state, time, or `assistantId`. No live writer assigns a non-null persisted group, migration maps it to null, and the ordering guide defines Topic order as whole-table.

Remove:

1. `Topic.groupId` from the entity and Create/Update DTOs.
2. `topic.group_id`, its FK, and `topic_group_updated_idx` from the throwaway schema/migration artifacts.
3. Group-scoped Topic create/duplicate/reorder logic in favor of whole-table order helpers.
4. Migration, Temporary Chat promotion, seeder, test, and documentation residue.

Do **not** remove `topic` or `session` from the shared `EntityTypeSchema`: Pins and Tags still use those types. Instead introduce/use a Group-specific discriminator (currently only the actively consumed `knowledge` type) in the generic Groups API. The generic group table/API and Knowledge grouping remain.

#### Endpoint contract summary

Exact Zod names can follow existing schema conventions, but the accepted surface is intentionally small:

```text
GET /topics
  filters: search, searchScope(name), assistantId | unlinked, pinned,
           updatedAtFrom, updatedAtTo, ids
  order:   sortBy(updatedAt | orderKey), direction derived by server
  page:    cursor, limit
  result:  { items: TopicListItem[], nextCursor }

GET /topics/stats
  same record filters + todayStart/yesterdayStart/weekStart
  result: total, pinnedCount, assistant and time breakdowns with pinnedCount

GET /agent-sessions
  symmetric filters + agentId | unlinked, workdir scope,
  searchScope(name | full), ids

GET /agent-sessions/stats
  symmetric Agent/workdir/time facts

POST /topics/:id/move
  body: { assistantId: string | null, order: OrderRequest }
  purpose: atomic owner change plus target-anchor ordering
```

`order` on `/topics/:id/move` is required. An optional order would duplicate the existing Topic PATCH operation. Same-owner reorder remains `PATCH /topics/:id/order`.

#### Query-plan and index requirement

Current schemas do not establish that all new scope+sort query shapes are efficient. Before adding indexes:

1. Record `EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN` for activity/manual order under each real scope, pinned JOINs, stats, and History search.
2. Benchmark representative 10k and 100k Topic/Session datasets on the synchronous better-sqlite3 Main thread.
3. Add only the composite indexes justified by those plans, likely around actual owner/workdir + sort + id shapes.
4. Document literal-search full scans if retained and measure their p50/p95 latency instead of assuming a 1 ms aggregate or "milliseconds" search.

#### Acceptance and test matrix

- First usable page renders before the complete history is fetched; ordinary first paint uses a documented O(1) number of resource requests.
- No default Topic/Session/History surface uses `loadAll` or retains every page.
- Cursor tests cover both sort profiles, null scopes, deleted rows, moved rows, and mutation between page requests.
- Search tests cover Unicode case behavior, descriptions/Agent names in History, and literal `%`, `_`, and `\` input.
- Stats tests cover pinned exclusion/derivation, null owners, duplicate workdir paths, exact boundary timestamps, week-start edge cases, and concurrent invalidation reconciliation.
- Subscription tests cover after-commit delivery, rollback, nested writers, PinService, parent deletion/cascade, reset, missed-event recovery, multiple windows, and unsubscribe cleanup.
- Remote-list tests cover expand-all throttling, group first-row loading, Show More, unloaded reveal, active-row deletion, classic rail navigation, drag/move, and window backfill.
- History tests cover running/failed/completed counts and filters, search/source intersections, infinite scrolling, displayed-row-only select-all, later page loading, and selection reset after filter changes.
- `topic.groupId` removal tests prove whole-table ordering and prove Topic/Session pin operations still pass through the shared entity type.

#### Questions to agree on

1. Do we agree that Main/DataApi should own record filtering, the two supported ordering profiles, cursor pagination, and factual aggregation?
2. Do we agree to implement DataApi subscription invalidation first and defer row-level window merging until measurements establish a need?
3. Do we accept per-expanded-group lazy streams with bounded concurrency, with a later batch endpoint only if "Expand all" profiling requires it?
4. Is there any active or scheduled product requirement for persisted `topic.groupId`?
5. If not, can its DB/API/service/migration residue be removed while keeping the generic Pin/Tag entity types?
6. Should this issue supersede and close #16851?

### Context

#16851 aligned the existing Topic/Session pagination contract, but it did not address the root issue: grouped resource surfaces still fully load data before grouping, counts, search, navigation, and local "Show more" are correct.

Suggested implementation phases after agreement:

1. Lock the list/stats/search/status contracts and add service-level regression fixtures.
2. Remove `topic.groupId` in a focused change; add the Group-specific entity discriminator without changing Pin/Tag types.
3. Implement minimal list projections, filters, the two cursor orders, stats, search normalization, query-plan-backed indexes, and required atomic Topic move.
4. Complete transaction-aware DataApi subscription invalidation and the full producer inventory.
5. Add the remote ResourceList provider/interaction contract.
6. Migrate Topic and Agent Session resource panels, then migrate each History mode separately.
7. Remove `loadAll`, `isFullyLoaded`, obsolete full-array derivations, and only the `/pins` composition proven redundant for migrated rows.
8. Update DataApi, pagination, ordering, testing, and breaking-change documentation; attach query plans and benchmark results.

Expected outcome:

- Renderer work and retained rows are bounded by active/expanded windows rather than complete history.
- List ordering, filtering, factual counts, and pin projections have one Main-owned definition.
- Multi-window freshness uses the existing DataApi subsystem and reconciles every committed writer.
- Current Topic/Session grouping, History status/search, reveal, navigation, and drag behavior are either preserved or explicitly changed by an agreed decision.
- Persisted Topic ordering no longer carries an unused group scope, while generic Topic/Session pin and tag types continue to work.

### Platform

macOS

### Version

`main` at `9bb8d78266`

### Bug Description

`src/renderer/components/chat/trace/TraceTree.tsx` stores `usedTime` in state even though it is derived entirely from `node.startTime`, `node.endTime`, and the current time. Its effect runs whenever polling replaces `node`, then calls `setUsedTime`, producing a second render for every visible trace node after each poll. `TracePage.tsx` refreshes trace data every 300 ms, so this compounds for expanded trees and the displayed duration trails the current node by one commit.

This violates the Vercel React rule `rerender-derived-state-no-effect`.

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Open a chat with AI trace enabled.
2. Expand a trace containing multiple spans.
3. Profile `TraceTree` while the trace is running.
4. Observe each polling update followed by another commit caused by the `usedTime` effect.

### Expected Behavior

Compute the formatted duration during render so each polling update needs only one render. The minimal fix should remove the `usedTime` state/effect and derive the value directly from the current node timestamps.

### Relevant Log Output

N/A

### Additional Context

Exact file: `src/renderer/components/chat/trace/TraceTree.tsx`.

Risk: unnecessary commits scale with every visible trace node during 300 ms polling, increasing renderer work while traces are actively updating.

### Platform

macOS

### Version

v2.0.0-dev (main)

### Is your feature request related to an existing issue?

Follow-up from the review of #16867 (built-in Cherry Assistant).

For built-in agents, `instructions === ''` in the database is a sentinel meaning "the bundled definition owns the system prompt" — at session build time the runtime injects the (localized, upgradeable) bundled instructions. This is a deliberate contract, but the UI does not reflect it:

- The agent edit dialog shows an **empty** instructions box while the runtime actually injects a long built-in prompt, so the user cannot see the real effective value.
- Clearing a customized instructions field silently means "restore the built-in default", which is not communicated anywhere.

### Desired Solution

Add an explicit "using built-in default" affordance in the agent edit UI when a built-in agent's stored instructions are empty, e.g.:

- A hint/badge on the instructions field ("Using built-in default instructions — edit to override"), ideally with a way to view the effective bundled prompt.
- On clearing a previously customized value, communicate that this restores the built-in default (hint text or confirmation).

### Alternative Solutions

- Read-only preview of the resolved effective instructions in the edit dialog.
- Replace the empty-string sentinel with an explicit "use built-in default" toggle backed by a dedicated flag (larger change; touches the runtime contract in `buildSystemPrompt`).

### Additional Information

Relevant code: `src/main/ai/runtime/claudeCode/settingsBuilder.ts` (`buildSystemPrompt` — the sentinel contract is documented there), `src/main/ai/agents/builtin/BuiltinAgentProvisioner.ts` (bundled definition loading).

Raised by the reviewer in https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/pull/16867#pullrequestreview-4680090162 as a non-blocking item.

### Platform

macOS

### Version

`main` at `6befb54fa2`

### Bug Description

`src/renderer/hooks/useCodeStyle.ts` documents `CodeStyleProvider` as required and contains a guard that should throw when the provider is missing. However, `CodeStyleContext` is initialized with a complete no-op object, so `use(CodeStyleContext)` can never be null and the guard is unreachable.

If a window or component tree omits `CodeStyleProvider`, consumers silently receive empty highlighting results (`highlightCode()` and `shikiMarkdownIt()` return an empty string) instead of exposing the invalid provider composition. This violates the `state-context-interface` rule because consumers are not guaranteed to receive the provider-injected contract.

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Render a component that calls `useCodeStyle()` outside `CodeStyleProvider`.
2. Call a context action such as `highlightCode()`.
3. Observe that no provider error is thrown and an empty result is returned.

### Expected Behavior

`useCodeStyle()` should fail immediately when used outside `CodeStyleProvider`. The minimal fix is to initialize the context with `null`, preserve the existing guard, and add a focused test asserting that missing-provider usage throws. No consumer or provider API should change.

### Relevant Log Output

N/A

### Additional Context

Exact file: `src/renderer/hooks/useCodeStyle.ts`.

Risk: future window composition mistakes can silently produce blank code or Markdown output and are difficult to diagnose because the intended invariant check never runs.

`main` / PR #16712 (unreleased)

## Is your feature request related to an existing issue?

When a maximized Shell pane is minimized, the live `surfaceRoot` moves to the docked host immediately while the outgoing overlay remains mounted for its 180 ms clip-path exit. The overlay can therefore display only its background during that brief exit.

The current behavior intentionally preserves the expensive preview instance without remounting or reparsing it. This follow-up records the visual trade-off identified in the review of #16712.

## Desired Solution

Add an explicit maximize-to-docked handoff state so the outgoing overlay retains the same live surface until its exit completes, then transfers it to the docked slot without remounting the preview.

Acceptance criteria:

- No blank overlay is visible during minimize.
- Preview components are not remounted or reparsed.
- Reduced-motion behavior remains immediate.
- Close callbacks and docked-pane layout refresh still run exactly once.

## Alternative Solutions

- Keep the current brief blank wipe as the low-complexity baseline.
- Remove the minimize exit animation.
- Fade the overlay background independently, provided it does not expose stale content or introduce extra layout work.

## Additional Information

- Review context: https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/pull/16712#issuecomment-4954688890

- Keep key construction deterministic as `CellStyle` evolves.

Some openpyxl workbooks use the spreadsheet-drawing namespace as a default namespace instead of the `xdr:` prefix expected by ExcelJS. #16712 normalizes those drawing XML parts before loading them with ExcelJS.

JSZip cannot rewrite one entry in the original archive in place, so changing an affected drawing currently calls `generateAsync` and recompresses the whole package. The 256 MiB declared-uncompressed-size preflight bounds well-formed metadata, but full regeneration still raises temporary CPU and memory use; forged ZIP metadata is not a hard decompression bound.

## Desired Solution

Normalize only affected drawing entries while copying unaffected compressed ZIP entries without decompression/recompression, or remove the workaround through an upstream ExcelJS fix.

Acceptance criteria:

- openpyxl charts continue to parse through ExcelJS.
- Unaffected archive entries retain their compressed payloads.
- Peak memory and worker time improve measurably on large workbooks.
- ZIP integrity, size defenses, and error handling remain intact for untrusted input.

## Alternative Solutions

- Contribute namespace-tolerant drawing parsing upstream to ExcelJS.
- Use a streaming/raw-entry ZIP writer for the normalization path.
- Keep the current JSZip regeneration fallback for bounded inputs if alternatives add disproportionate complexity.

title: [Bug]: Direct main-process text fetches can re-resolve hostnames after SSRF preflight
body:
## Issue Checklist

- [x] I understand that issues are for feedback and problem solving, not for complaining in the comment section, and will provide as much information as possible to help solve the problem.
- [x] My issue is not listed in the [FAQ](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/issues/3881).

- [x] I've filled in short, clear headings so that developers can quickly identify a rough idea of what to expect when flipping through the list of issues. And not "a suggestion", "stuck", etc.
- [x] I've confirmed that I am using the latest version of Cherry Studio.

## Platform

macOS (also affects all desktop platforms)

## Version

main / v2 dev

## Scope

This issue tracks the shared, bounded-text direct-fetch safety mechanism and migration of its two current consumers:

- the built-in web-search direct fetch provider;
- the auto-callable MCP fetch server.

It does not track citation-preview UI or IPC changes, binary downloads, uploads, provider-configured endpoints, or a general-purpose `Response`/stream/proxy-compatible fetch abstraction. Those paths have different response, streaming, trust, and proxy requirements and require separate design and tracking. Citation previews can benefit indirectly when they use the in-scope web-search direct provider, without changing citation-preview code or the `web_search.fetch_urls` contract.

## Bug Description

The in-scope main-process text-fetch paths rely on a literal URL SSRF guard before handing the original hostname URL to Electron `net.fetch`. This blocks unsafe literal targets such as `localhost`, private IPs, and link-local addresses, but it does not bind the actual network connection to the address that was checked.

For renderer- or assistant-controlled URL inputs that reach these paths, an attacker-controlled hostname can resolve to a public address during validation and then rebind to a local/private address when `net.fetch` performs its own later DNS resolution. This leaves a DNS time-of-check/time-of-use gap.

The concrete paths are:

```text
web_search.fetch_urls
  -> WebSearchService.fetchUrls
  -> FetchProvider.fetchUrls
  -> fetchWebSearchContent
  -> net.fetch(sanitizeRemoteUrl(url))

MCP fetch tool
  -> Fetcher._fetch
  -> net.fetch(sanitizeRemoteUrl(url))
```

## Steps To Reproduce

1. Invoke either the built-in web-search direct fetch provider or the MCP fetch tool with an attacker-controlled hostname URL.
2. Have that hostname return a public DNS answer during preflight validation.
3. Rebind the hostname to a private/local address before the actual `net.fetch` connection is opened.
4. Observe that the guard validated the original URL, but the actual connection is not constrained to the validated public address.

## Expected Behavior

The in-scope bounded-text fetch paths should enforce address safety at connection time:

- validate the literal URL;
- resolve all hostname DNS answers;
- reject the request if any DNS result is local/private/non-public;
- bind the actual connection to a prevalidated public address;
- preserve the original `Host` header and HTTPS SNI semantics;
- reject redirects unless each hop is independently validated and pinned;
- bound response body buffering in the main process;
- preserve caller-cancellation and timeout semantics for downstream consumers.

## Relevant Log Output

```shell
N/A
```

## Additional Context

This came up while separating the citation-preview freeze fix from the underlying direct text-fetch safety issue. The shared helper should remain intentionally narrow and return bounded text rather than becoming a general network abstraction for incompatible binary, upload, custom-endpoint, or proxy-dependent call sites.

Related review context: CherryHQ/cherry-studio#16835 noted that DNS preflight followed by `net.fetch(originalUrl)` is still vulnerable because the checked address is discarded before the actual connection.

title: # [Feature]: Internal Multi-Agent Group Chat Room
body:
## Problem Statement
Currently, Cherry Studio supports creating multiple AI Agents, each with their own personality and system prompt. However, these agents can only interact with the user **one-on-one** in separate sessions.
There is **no way for multiple agents to converse together in a shared space** — no "group chat" where the user and several agents can chat freely, with agents responding to each other's messages as well as the user's.
## Use Cases
1. **Role-play scenarios**: A user creates several character agents (e.g., different shipgirls from a game) and wants to have a group conversation with all of them simultaneously, where they can banter with each other naturally.
2. **Multi-perspective discussion**: A user wants to discuss a topic with multiple expert agents (e.g., a lawyer agent, an engineer agent, and a product manager agent) in the same room, getting cross-talk and debate.
3. **Storytelling / world-building**: Multiple character agents interact in a shared narrative space, with the user as a participant or observer.
4. **Agent collaboration**: Multiple task-oriented agents discuss and decompose a complex problem together before executing.
## Desired Solution
A **Virtual Group Chat Room** feature built into Cherry Studio:
### Core Mechanism
- User creates a "Group Chat Room" and adds 2+ existing Agents to it
- When the user sends a message, **all agents in the room receive it** (along with previous messages from other agents)
- Agents respond in a configurable order (round-robin, free-for-all, or turn-based)
- The chat history includes messages from the user AND all agents, forming a coherent multi-party conversation
### Configuration Options
| Setting | Description |
|---|---|
| **Response mode** | `sequential` (agents reply one by one), `free` (any agent can jump in), `mentioned-only` (agent only replies when @mentioned) |
| **Max rounds** | Limit how many rounds of agent replies before waiting for user input again |

title: [Feature]: Refactor Topic and Agent Session pagination, grouping, and refresh semantics
body:
### Issue Checklist

- [x] I understand that issues are for reporting problems and requesting features, not for off-topic comments, and I will provide as much detail as possible to help resolve the issue.
- [x] I have checked the pinned issues and searched through the existing open and closed issues, and this issue consolidates the remaining refactor scope.
- [x] I have provided a short and descriptive title so that developers can quickly understand the issue when browsing the issue list.
- [x] The latest `main` branch contains part of the required baseline, but does not include the remaining list, activity, invalidation, and Renderer refactor described below.

### Platform

macOS (the design and implementation are platform-agnostic)

### Version

2.0.0-dev (`main`)

### Is your feature request related to an existing issue?

#### Background

Topic and Agent Session surfaces currently treat DataApi cursor pagination primarily as transport batching. Page-level and legacy consumers still request or derive the complete dataset before performing search, grouping, ordering, counts, pinned composition, owner-rail selection, and local “Show more” behavior.

This creates several related problems:

- First useful render and Renderer memory usage scale with the complete Topic or Session history.
- Sidebar, right-side panel, grouped, and History consumers maintain different list derivations and refresh behavior.
- Main and Renderer can disagree about ordering, filtering, group membership, and pinned semantics.
- A committed write can leave an infinite-query cursor chain stale, causing duplicated, missing, or incorrectly ordered rows.
- Client-side filtering after pagination cannot produce reliable empty states, counts, or `hasNext` values.
- Cross-window and background-originated writes do not currently converge through an authoritative DataApi invalidation path.

#### Document contract

This issue is the **technical architecture** for the product behavior defined in #17025. It contains no product rules of its own: every user-visible behavior is referenced, never restated, and this document adds only the Topic/Session-specific contracts required to implement it. If an implementation constraint exposes a missing or conflicting product decision, resolve it in #17025 first and then update this issue. The architecture must not silently turn an implementation convenience into product behavior.

Related documents:

- #17025 — product source of truth (user-visible behavior and UX acceptance criteria).
- #17144 — generic DataApi data-change notification and bidirectional cursor infrastructure. The change-notification Phase A contract is frozen in [the architecture comment](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/issues/17144#issuecomment-5053757668); bidirectional cursor support remains independent and open.
- #17225 — generic Renderer bidirectional collection, reconciliation, and prepend-scroll-anchoring infrastructure; its concrete API shapes remain under independent review.
- #17095 — already-landed Topic `groupId` removal and global-ordering baseline (see §2).
- #16998 — implementation PR tracking this issue.
#### Resolved product decisions

- **Search matching semantics** follow #17025 and the existing Global Search entity-matching mechanism: deferred automatic search, trimmed escaped literal-substring matching, and no additional NFC-normalization or Unicode case-folding rule introduced by this refactor. §4.5 defines the technical binding.
- **Two-pane unlinked/unknown navigation** follows #17025: the content record may open with no live owner selected and without a scoped right-side reveal. This does not change backend record eligibility.

The pseudo-owner decision is resolved: **Unlinked Assistant** and **Unknown Agent** headers are Renderer-only toggle containers, not live-owner activation targets. This is presentation policy only. Their records remain ordinary backend records and may be returned by global or pseudo-owner-scoped `/latest`, become active, and participate in any row operation the Renderer enables.

### Desired Solution

#### 1. Scope and non-goals

**In scope**: Topic/Session data and query contracts, activity-time semantics, ordering and write semantics, mapping Topic/Session writes to accepted generic change signals, surface migration, preferences, presentation state, migration, and technical verification.

**Non-goals** — this issue deliberately does not include:

- implementation or redesign of the frozen generic DataApi data-change notification protocol in #17144;
- the final generic bidirectional cursor API shape — that remains independently reviewed in #17144;
- the final generic `useInfiniteQuery`, collection-reconciliation, or prepend-scroll-anchoring API shape — those remain independently reviewed in #17225;
- entity-row push or replication between processes: SQLite remains the source of truth;
- any Topic-, Session-, Cache-, or window-specific synchronization channel;
- per-streaming-chunk or per-token database writes for activity time (§4.2);
- offline conflict resolution or multi-device synchronization;
- a global first/last move command (no product surface exists, #17025 §7);
- redesign of Assistant tag organization (#17025 §4);
- v1 list-stack fixes (v1 policy per repository guidelines).
#### 2. Current `main` baseline

PR #17095 has already landed on `main` and is baseline rather than remaining work:

- Topic `groupId`, its foreign key, schema/type/DTO/migrator usage, and response field have been removed.
- Topic manual ordering is one global `orderKey ASC, id ASC` sequence across all Assistants; Agent Session reorder already operates on one global Session sequence.
- Topic create/duplicate and Session create already insert at the first position of their global manual sequences.

This issue must not reintroduce `groupId`, repeat its migration, or treat global Topic/Session ordering as a new schema design. Baseline commit: `2481e959acbc26b0c4476d706ec02a5b189fa3e2`.

#### 3. Traceability: product rule → technical mechanism

| #17025 | Product rule (summary) | Mechanism in this issue |
| --- | --- | --- |
| §1 | Owner activation, default record, and owner fallback use activity time | scoped/global `/latest` selectors (§4.3); stats-driven owner rails (§4.6) |
| §2 | Display mode and sort are independent, persisted, cross-window | Preference keys and migration (§8) |
| §3 | Two visible bands; new pins first; a record appears in exactly one band | independent pinned/ordinary streams (§4.4); pin insert-first write (§5.3) |
| §4 | Groups load, expand, and page independently; empty groups hidden | per-group collection windows (§7); stats-driven group visibility (§4.6) |
| §5 | Search scopes and owner-name matching | SQLite-side filters bound into the cursor family (§4.5) |
| §6 | Active-item reveal without loading everything before the target | anchored entry into the existing collection endpoint (§4.7) |
| §7 | Drag meaning, per-surface eligibility, visible-neighbor drops | global-order write primitives (§5.1–§5.2); Renderer drag policy (§5.2) |
| §8 | Refresh continuity, immediate write feedback, cross-window convergence | generic change signaling and collection reconciliation (§6); removal coordinator (§7.2) |
| §9 | History selection rules | History surface migration (§7); list-only search note (§4.6) |
| §10 | Loading, empty, and error states | error taxonomy (§4.8); per-group load/error isolation (§7) |

#### 4. Data and read-model contracts

##### 4.1 List, latest, stats, anchored collection entry, and move

| Endpoint | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /topics` | Cursor-paged Topic collection projection with pin metadata, search scope, sort, live-Assistant/unlinked owner scope, pinned, cursor, limit, and optional anchored-entry semantics (§4.7). |
| `GET /topics/latest` | Non-paged most-recently-active Topic selector; global when owner scope is omitted, scoped to a live Assistant or the unlinked pseudo-owner scope when provided (§4.3). |
| `GET /agent-sessions` | Cursor-paged Session collection projection with pin metadata, search scope, sort, live-Agent/unknown owner scope, independent user/system workspace scope, pinned, cursor, limit, and optional anchored-entry semantics (§4.7). |
| `GET /agent-sessions/latest` | Non-paged most-recently-active Session selector; global when owner scope is omitted, scoped to a live Agent or the unknown pseudo-owner scope when provided (§4.3). |
| `GET /topics/stats` | Factual aggregates (§4.6). |
| `GET /agent-sessions/stats` | Factual aggregates (§4.6). |
| `POST /topics/:id/move` | Atomic cross-Assistant ownership + required concrete-neighbor placement update (§5.1). |

Topic and Session list items include `pinned` and `pinId`. Entity and list shapes expose `lastActivityAt` as the activity-time field; by-ID reads otherwise keep their normal entity shape. No response is required to carry a resource-wide revision or participate in a cross-endpoint snapshot identity.
##### 4.2 Activity time (`lastActivityAt`)

`updatedAt` and activity time are different contracts. `updatedAt` remains the generic row last-modified timestamp and is advanced by the shared `$onUpdateFn` on any row update, including metadata writes. `lastActivityAt` is the user-visible **activity time** defined in #17025 (Product principles and terminology).

**Core invariant** (the contract — everything else derives from it):

> `lastActivityAt` equals the maximum activity timestamp over the record’s surviving activity-bearing content; when no such content survives, it equals the record’s `createdAt`. Only creation, a response terminal-state transition (completed, failed, or aborted), or deletion of activity-bearing content may change it.

**Activity-bearing content and its timestamps** — the technical mapping of #17025’s “real conversation or task-content activity”:

- a persisted user message / task-interaction start contributes the message row’s `createdAt`;
- a model/agent response contributes two timestamps: the response row’s `createdAt` (response start) and its terminal-state timestamp (completed, failed, or aborted);
- streaming chunks, token deltas, tool-progress deltas, and intermediate persistence contribute no timestamps.

If this mapping is ambiguous for any message or task type, that ambiguity is a #17025 product question, not an implementation choice.

**Consequences** (implementation guidance, not additional contract):

- Writes advance the parent at bounded phases only — interaction start, response start, response terminal. The invariant makes repeated writes idempotent: the update is a monotonic max, so no separate deduplication registry is required.
- Deleting the latest activity-bearing content recomputes `lastActivityAt` from the surviving content, falling back to the parent `createdAt`.
- Metadata writes — opening/viewing, rename, pin/unpin, owner/workspace organization, manual reorder — never touch it; they may still advance generic `updatedAt` through normal row-modification semantics.
- New Topics and Sessions initialize `lastActivityAt` from `createdAt`.
- **Backfill**: existing rows compute the invariant from their surviving messages using the timestamps above, falling back to parent `createdAt`. The same derivation applies in the v1-to-v2 Chat/Agent Session migrators.

##### 4.3 Sort profiles and `/latest`

The ordinary-row sort profiles are:

- `createdAt DESC, id ASC`
- `lastActivityAt DESC, id ASC`
- `orderKey ASC, id ASC`

Pinned-only queries use the pin order (`pin.orderKey`, with the mandatory `id` tie-breaker; new pins insert at the first pin position per #17025 §3). The `id` tie-breaker is mandatory everywhere because timestamps and order keys are not unique.

`/topics/latest` and `/agent-sessions/latest` select `lastActivityAt DESC, id ASC LIMIT 1` across pinned **and** ordinary records. Global selectors include records without a live owner. Scoped selectors accept either a concrete live owner or the corresponding unlinked/unknown pseudo-owner scope. They accept no cursor, search, workspace, pin, or display-sort dimension and never derive selection from the first row of a paged list. Pin state and pseudo-owner presentation affect UI organization, not latest-record eligibility (#17025 §1).

The `/latest` selectors are the single mechanism behind every automatic record choice in #17025 §1 (initial entry, live-owner activation, two-pane owner selection, owner-level fallback after removal, and any record-level selection inside a pseudo-owner group). They fetch or revalidate on demand before committing a selection, and superseded selection requests must not win (§7.1). A pseudo-owner header itself does not invoke owner activation or `/latest`; that distinction belongs exclusively to Renderer presentation policy (§7.1).

##### 4.4 Pinned and ordinary streams

The list service has two explicit and independent paths:

1. a **pinned-only** path selected with `pinned: true`, ordered by pin order;
2. an **ordinary-only** keyset path selected with `pinned: false`, ordered by the requested ordinary sort profile.

Every paged caller selects one stream. A pinned query has no ordinary `sortBy` dimension. An ordinary query that omits `sortBy` defaults to `createdAt`; omission never selects legacy composite behavior. No response or cursor crosses from pinned to ordinary rows or vice versa.

The legacy pinned-then-ordinary composite path and cross-band cursor are removed. A remaining consumer is a migration blocker, not justification for retaining the compatibility path. Existing owner-rail lookups that use `limit: 1` on a paged stream migrate to scoped `/latest`, because neither individual stream can prove the latest record across both pin states.

##### 4.5 Search normalization and filters

Search, live-owner, workspace, and pin filters are applied in SQLite **before** pagination, so counts, empty states, and `hasNext` are authoritative.

- Search reuses the same entity-matching mechanism as Global Search: trim the query, escape `\\`, `%`, and `_`, and apply an SQLite `LIKE` literal-substring predicate before pagination. The refactor adds no separate NFC normalization or Unicode case-folding layer; character-case and Unicode behavior therefore remain aligned with that shared mechanism. The exact trimmed query and `searchScope` bind into the cursor family.
- `name-or-owner` search joins only live Assistant or Agent rows (#17025 §5: a deleted owner’s name is never a match).
- Unlinked/unknown queries include null ownership and references to soft-deleted owners; concrete owner scopes match live owners only.
- Session workspace scope is independent and has no unlinked value.

##### 4.6 Stats and owner rails

Stats are factual database aggregates:

- `GET /topics/stats`: total and pinned counts plus per-live-Assistant `{ count, pinnedCount }`, with every row lacking a live Assistant normalized into the unlinked entry.
- `GET /agent-sessions/stats`: total and pinned counts, per-live-Agent `{ count, pinnedCount }`, and independent per-user/system-workspace counts with the same pinned split; rows lacking a live Agent normalize into the unknown entry.
- Both accept the list search term and owner scope.

Renderer derives ordinary counts as `count - pinnedCount`. How stats drive group visibility, owner-rail membership, and owner fallback is product behavior (#17025 §1, §4); the technical requirements here are only:

- list and stats use identical membership filters and name-search semantics wherever stats determine group visibility or empty state;
- History `name-or-owner` search remains list-only, because History never derives grouped visibility from stats (#17025 §9 keeps History flat);
- mounted list, stats, and `/latest` consumers respond to relevant committed changes through the generic change-signaling and reconciliation capabilities (§6); they are not required to share a resource revision or one cross-endpoint snapshot identity.

##### 4.7 Cursor family and anchored collection entry

Keyset cursors are opaque and bound only to dimensions required to interpret the query and boundary:

- stream;
- sort;
- normalized search and filters;
- owner/workspace scope;
- direction and `(sortValue, id)` boundary;
- cursor-format version.

The cursor contains no resource revision. Changes affecting a mounted collection are handled through generic DataApi change signaling and Renderer reconciliation rather than global cursor invalidation. The generic cursor contract and API shape are owned by #17144.

Anchored reveal enters the existing collection endpoint rather than a dedicated `/window` resource:

```http
GET /topics?anchorId=<topicId>&limit=50
GET /agent-sessions?anchorId=<sessionId>&limit=50
```

Without an anchor, the same endpoint starts from the normal collection head. Around an anchor, the collection can return previous and next cursors so the real ordered window pages in both directions without loading every preceding record.

Topic/Session-specific anchor semantics remain here:

- Main resolves the anchor's existence, actual band, and membership in the current query.
- `FOUND` returns an ordered page containing the anchor, its position in that page, its band, and directional cursors.
- `ANCHOR_OUTSIDE_QUERY` proves the record exists but the current membership query excludes it, allowing Renderer to clear incompatible constraints and retry.
- `RECORD_UNAVAILABLE` means the record no longer exists.
- On `FOUND`, Renderer replaces the owning band/group window, scrolls to the anchor, briefly highlights it, and leaves no injected or floating exception.
- Stale anchored or collection work must not replace a newer result; the generic reconciliation mechanism is decided upstream in #17225.
- Prepending previous pages preserves the visible scroll position through the upstream viewport capability in #17225.

**Rejected alternatives**:

1. *Temporary injected row after a targeted by-ID existence read* — rejected because it leaves a floating exception outside its ordered position and cannot page around the target.
2. *Paging from the collection head through the target boundary* — rejected because cost scales with target depth and violates #17025 §6.
##### 4.8 Domain endpoint outcome taxonomy

| Typed result | Meaning | Product mapping |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ANCHOR_OUTSIDE_QUERY` | reveal target exists but is excluded by the current membership query; non-error control result | clear incompatible constraints only after existence is proven, then retry (#17025 §6) |
| `RECORD_UNAVAILABLE` | reveal/open target no longer exists | unavailable message; current active record and filters unchanged (#17025 §6) |
| `INVALID_ANCHOR` | move/reorder anchor missing or self-referencing, or a Topic `/move` anchor does not belong to the requested target Assistant | operation fails atomically; UI restores the prior visible state (#17025 §8) |
| `INVALID_TARGET_OWNER` | move target Assistant is not live | same |

`ANCHOR_OUTSIDE_QUERY` is **not** an error: it is the existence-proving branch of the constraint-clearing reveal path (§4.7).
#### 5. Ordering and write semantics

##### 5.1 Topic move

`MoveTopicDto` is the minimal atomic contract for one demand only: a cross-Assistant drag with a concrete visible-neighbor placement.

- `assistantId: string` — required live target Assistant;
- `order: { before: string } | { after: string }` — required concrete anchor; no `first` / `last` sentinel.

Within one synchronous write transaction, the service validates the live target Assistant and referenced anchor Topic, requires the anchor to belong to that target Assistant at commit time, updates ownership, and moves the Topic relative to the anchor in the global Topic sequence. Any validation or ordering failure rolls back both changes. The same-owner/target-owner check protects the meaning of the visible insertion line under concurrent writes; it is request-coherence validation, not a general backend restriction on pseudo-owner records.

All other demands use existing contracts:

- same-Assistant and flat-list drags call `/topics/:id/order` or batch reorder and change no ownership;
- the existing Move to Assistant action, a move into an empty target group, History bulk move, explicit unlinking, and other ownership-only changes use `PATCH /topics/:id { assistantId }` and preserve the existing global `orderKey`;
- pseudo-owner membership does not prevent a Topic from being active, deleted, reordered, or moved when the Renderer exposes that operation.

History bulk move remains client-side iteration of atomic ownership-only PATCH calls so partial success, failure, and retry remain per row (#17025 §9). `/topics/:id/order` and batch reorder continue to operate on the already-global Topic sequence and may include Topics from different Assistants. Existing generic ordering internals may retain first/last sentinels for create/duplicate or other non-drag operations, but the narrowed move contract and its UI expose no global first/last command (#17025 §7).

##### 5.2 Grouping-agnostic ordering and Renderer drag policy

Generic Topic and Session `/order` and batch-reorder primitives operate on their respective global `orderKey` sequences. Session reorder never changes Agent or workspace ownership. These generic ordering primitives are **grouping-agnostic**: they do not receive display mode, current group, Agent scope, or workspace scope and do not enforce Renderer drag boundaries. They validate only entity/anchor existence, non-self references, request shape, global-order integrity, and transactional atomicity. A valid global sequence remains valid when adjacent rows belong to different owners or work directories. Topic `/move` (§5.1) is deliberately narrower: because it atomically applies a cross-Assistant ownership change at a visible destination neighbor, it additionally validates that the anchor belongs to the requested target Assistant. That is request-coherence validation for the domain-specific move command, not a grouping restriction on generic ordering.

Renderer implements the #17025 §7 drag rules (per-surface eligibility, same-group vs cross-Assistant drags, work-directory restrictions, visible-neighbor drops, disabled-while-unstable) as projection policy on top of these primitives:

- same-Assistant Topic drags and all Session drags call global reorder with a visible-neighbor anchor;
- cross-Assistant Topic drags with a concrete destination neighbor call atomic Topic move (§5.1) so ownership and placement commit together;
- ownership-only Topic moves use the ordinary Topic PATCH contract and preserve `orderKey`.

Test ownership: Renderer tests cover the #17025 §7 projection rules; Main service tests cover the generic global reorder primitives and Topic move atomicity, not UI grouping modes.

Manual ordering and owner organization do not change `lastActivityAt` (§4.2 invariant; #17025 §7).

##### 5.3 Schema and query plans

- New pins are inserted at the first pin position while preserving idempotency and concurrency behavior (#17025 §3).
- Add mixed-direction `(createdAt DESC, id ASC)` indexes for Topic and Session default ordering.
- Add mixed-direction `(lastActivityAt DESC, id ASC)` indexes for Topic and Session activity ordering and `/latest` selection.
- Do not add owner dimensions to the global manual-order indexes.
- Verify representative global and scoped list/latest queries with `EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN`; add owner-plus-sort indexes only when query-plan evidence demonstrates the need.
- Regenerate Drizzle migration and snapshot artifacts from the final schema.
- Service tests cover stable boundaries, filters, stats, pin ordering, deletes, atomic moves, duplicate sort values, and the `lastActivityAt` invariant.

#### 6. Consuming generic upstream capabilities

#17144 owns the generic DataApi data-change notification and bidirectional cursor infrastructure. Its change-notification Phase A semantics are frozen by [the architecture contract](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/issues/17144#issuecomment-5053757668); bidirectional cursor support remains an independent open capability.

#17225 owns the generic Renderer bidirectional page sequence, collection reconciliation, stale-work protection, and prepend-scroll-anchoring infrastructure. Its concrete API shapes remain under independent review.

#16994 owns only these Topic/Session-specific obligations:

- define and export canonical Topic/Session/Pin membership dimensions and ordering-profile identifiers from the shared schema modules, matching the endpoint query vocabulary;
- derive effect-orthogonal mappings per public write path and per response DTO field, including `/pins`, pin purge, by-ID, stats, and `/latest` effects;
- publish mapped effects only after the outermost public write commits; rollback paths and provable no-ops emit nothing;
- use endpoint-returned primary keys for `entityIds` (`Pin.id`, never `Pin.entityId`, for `/pins`) and omit the hint when those keys are not cheaply available;
- verify mappings, rollback/no-op behavior, canonical dimensions, and entity-id namespaces in service/database tests;
- consume the accepted generic capabilities rather than creating Topic/Session-specific replacements;
- keep SQLite as the source of truth and introduce no entity-row replication;
- retain feature-owned bands, groups, selection, owner fallback, drag policy, optimistic presentation, and rollback;
- make #16998's first notification consumer maximally conservative: revalidate on every relevant endpoint signal; kind/dimension-driven revalidate-versus-rebuild policy remains in #17225.

This issue consumes rather than redefines #17144's frozen payload, routing, publishing, transaction, and delivery semantics. It also does not select the remaining bidirectional cursor or Renderer reconciliation API shapes.

Cross-window convergence follows the frozen delivery contract: best-effort delivery with per-window FIFO to live, continuously subscribed Renderers. A commit between a consumer's first database read and subscription registration may be missed; recovery is the next relevant change, a remount, or another active query. No revision, sequence, replay, acknowledgement, or catch-up handshake is introduced by this issue. #17025's product wording must use the same bounded guarantee.
#### 7. Topic/Session Renderer composition

All migrated surfaces compose Topic/Session product behavior over the generic upstream capabilities in #17144 and #17225. This section specifies feature behavior rather than generic hook or protocol shapes:

- **Per-group collection windows**: each group owns its rows, cursors, loading, errors, expansion, and load-more behavior (#17025 §4).
- **Pinned-band completion**: History completes the pinned band before exposing ordinary rows (#17025 §3).
- **Edge-triggered loading**: list-end detection and viewport auto-fill follow #17025 §10.
- **Shared drag coordination**: Flat and Grouped manual drag uses visible neighbor anchors (§5.2).
- **Top-level section reorder**: peer **Work directory** / **No work directory** section order remains independent from concrete work-directory group order (#17025 §4, §7).

##### 7.1 Owner-aware group headers

Implements the #17025 §1 parent-click contract (inactive-owner activation, active-owner toggle, work-directory toggle-only, non-interactive chevrons):

- owner activation calls scoped `/latest` (§4.3), never the first currently loaded or currently sorted child;
- superseded owner requests cannot overwrite a newer selection;
- **Unlinked Assistant** and **Unknown Agent** headers are Renderer-only toggle containers. Their child records remain ordinary backend records and may still become active or be returned by global/pseudo-owner-scoped `/latest`.

##### 7.2 Removal and owner fallback coordinator

One Topic/Session coordinator implements the #17025 §8 deletion selection rules (next surviving row, previous-row fallback, owner-below/owner-above fallback, empty state, never auto-create):

- preserve the active row's group, band, displayed index, loaded-window size, and current group-window context before optimistic removal;
- after commit, rebuild the affected active group window to its previous visible extent, allowing the following row to fill the deleted position;
- if multiple cursor pages were loaded, rebuild the affected page and its loaded tail so shifted rows cannot remain duplicated;
- do not leave the current group while its refreshed result still contains a candidate;
- stale selection, pagination, or invalidation work cannot re-activate a removed row;
- a deletion observed from another window refreshes that Renderer’s own active group and chooses from its own presentation; Main does not synchronize navigation state;
- direct actions remain optimistic with failure rollback per #17025 §8.
#### 8. Preference, migration, and cleanup

- Persist Topic and Session Sidebar display mode and sort (`topic.display_mode`, `topic.sort_type`, `agent.session.display_mode`, `agent.session.sort_type`, using the repository’s final generated key names) through Preference so one change synchronizes across every open window. Sort defaults to `createdAt` (#17025 §2).
- Cross-window synchronization applies to the shared Sidebar display/sort preference. A scoped right-side panel remains Flat while following the shared sort preference, and History remains the #17025 §2 Flat/`createdAt` product exception.
- Migrate any persisted `updatedAt` activity-sort value to `lastActivityAt`; do not reinterpret generic `updatedAt` elsewhere.
- Persist grouped-Sidebar expansion state per resource and display mode in Renderer persist Cache. Expansion, search text, scroll position, and loaded-page depth remain presentation state rather than part of the shared cross-window display/sort preference. Search, sort, display-mode, and navigation changes do not erase saved expansion state (#17025 §4).
- Persist the peer top-level work-directory section order independently from concrete work-directory group order (#17025 §4).
- Remove obsolete time-bucket expansion keys and Agent History runtime-status/filter/cache-index residue (#17025 §5, §10).
- Add and backfill `lastActivityAt` in the Topic and Agent Session schema and in applicable v1-to-v2 Chat/Agent Session migration paths (§4.2).
- Migrate all in-scope list consumers from composite/load-all derivation to the independent streams, scoped latest selectors, stats, and remote group windows.
- Keep the already-landed #17095 `groupId` removal during rebase; no compatibility column, response field, DTO property, or migration is restored.
- Rebase and update #16998 against current `main`; its implementation and PR description must follow this issue, #17025, #17144's frozen notification contract and remaining cursor capability, and #17225 rather than the older renderer-local/groupId or resource-revision assumptions.

#### 9. Upstream dependencies

#17144 owns:

- DataApi data-change notification — Phase A semantics are frozen by the linked architecture contract;
- generic bidirectional cursor support — independent and still open.

#17225 owns:

- bidirectional `useInfiniteQuery` page sequences;
- Renderer collection reconciliation and stale-work protection;
- prepend scroll anchoring.

#16994 records the Topic/Session consumer vocabulary, mappings, and product policy. It consumes the frozen notification protocol without redefining it and does not select the remaining cursor or Renderer API shapes.
### Alternative Solutions

1. **Composite pinned-then-ordinary stream with a cross-band cursor** — rejected because the two bands have different ordering domains and neither individual stream can prove `/latest` across both pin states.
2. **Reusing `updatedAt` as activity time** — rejected because generic metadata writes advance `updatedAt`; `lastActivityAt` owns the activity invariant instead.
3. **Client-side filtering/grouping after pagination** — rejected because it cannot produce reliable counts, empty states, or `hasNext` and lets Main and Renderer disagree about membership.
4. **Resource revision as the consistency spine** — rejected because it couples change detection, query-impact analysis, and Renderer reconciliation and makes different changes share one global reset.
5. **Dedicated `/topics/window` and `/agent-sessions/window` endpoints** — rejected because anchored reveal is another entry point into the existing collection rather than a separate resource.

The generic DataApi data-change notification protocol is frozen in #17144. Bidirectional cursor support remains open in #17144, while Renderer collection and viewport infrastructure remain open in #17225.
### Additional Information

#### Performance targets and scale assumptions

Proposed defaults — to be validated by measurement and adjusted on this issue:

- Reference scale: 50,000 Topics, 20,000 Sessions, 1,000 pinned records, 200 owners.
- Default collection page size: 30–50 rows (a tuning constant, not product behavior).
- First usable list page (main-process query) at reference scale: < 50 ms; first useful Sidebar render end-to-end: < 300 ms.
- Renderer memory holds only loaded collection windows and does not scale with total history.
- Representative collection, `/latest`, stats, and anchored-entry query plans avoid full table scans and unnecessary temporary B-tree sorts (`EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN`).
#### Rollout sequencing

Topic/Session domain and forward-paging work may be reviewed independently. After #17144's frozen notification capability lands, #16998 adds the domain effect mappings and conservative first consumer defined in §6. Complete anchored reveal and refined collection reconciliation still depend on #17144's bidirectional cursor capability and #17225. This issue does not decide the implementation shape of those remaining upstream workstreams.
#### Technical acceptance criteria

The user-visible acceptance criteria live in #17025. Technical completion additionally requires:

**A. Topic/Session read models (§4)**

- pinned and ordinary streams remain independent;
- SQLite applies search, owner/workspace, and pin filters before pagination;
- list ordering is deterministic with the mandatory `id` tie-breaker;
- `/latest` remains independent from pin state and display sort;
- stats remain factual aggregates with membership semantics matching the corresponding grouped list;
- anchored reveal enters the existing collection endpoint and supports the domain outcomes in §4.7–§4.8.

**B. Activity time (§4.2)**

- the `lastActivityAt` invariant holds under creation, bounded activity phases, deletion, and backfill;
- metadata, owner, pin, and reorder operations do not change activity time;
- existing rows and persisted activity-sort preferences migrate with the documented fallbacks.

**C. Writes and ordering (§5)**

- Topic ownership/order moves remain atomic and grouping-agnostic;
- Renderer drag behavior follows #17025 using visible neighbor anchors;
- required indexes and representative query plans support the documented sort profiles.

**D. Upstream boundary (§6, §9, #17144, #17225)**

- Topic/Session writes map to #17144's frozen generic effects after successful commits, with rollback/no-op and canonical-dimension coverage;
- the first #16998 consumer revalidates every relevant signal; refined kind/dimension reconciliation remains owned by #17225;
- #16994 consumes #17144's accepted generic cursor capability and #17225's page-sequence, reconciliation, and viewport capabilities;
- no Topic/Session-specific synchronization protocol or entity-row replication exists.

**E. Renderer and migration (§7–§8)**

- selection, owner fallback, deletion refill, drag, grouped loading, and continuity follow #17025;
- Preference and Cache retain their documented product responsibilities;
- obsolete list-stack residue is removed without restoring Topic `groupId`.
#### References

- Product source of truth: #17025
- DataApi data-change notification (frozen Phase A) and bidirectional cursor infrastructure: #17144
- Renderer bidirectional collection, reconciliation, and viewport infrastructure: #17225
- Implementation PR: #16998
- Landed baseline: #17095 (`2481e959acbc26b0c4476d706ec02a5b189fa3e2`)

title: [Feature]: Refactor tool rendering into a single typed routing model
body:
- [x] I understand that issues are for reporting problems and requesting features, not for off-topic comments, and I will provide as much detail as possible to help resolve the issue.
- [x] I have checked the pinned issues and searched through the existing [open issues](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/issues), [closed issues](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20state%3Aclosed), and [discussions](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/discussions) and did not find a similar suggestion.
- [x] I have provided a short and descriptive title so that developers can quickly understand the issue when browsing the issue list, rather than vague titles like "A suggestion" or "Stuck."
- [x] The latest version of Cherry Studio does not include the feature I am suggesting.

### Platform

macOS

### Version

2.0.0-dev

### Is your feature request related to an existing issue?

Tool rendering decisions are currently distributed across several layers with overlapping responsibilities:

1. `toolResponse.ts` converts AI SDK message parts into `McpToolResponse` or `NormalToolResponse`, infers protocol/origin, and normalizes MCP wire names into display names.
2. `MessagePartsRenderer` uses different projections for live and completed messages.
3. `MessageTools` chooses between generic MCP rendering and the dedicated-tool path using server allowlists.
4. `chooseTool` selects dedicated cards primarily by the normalized tool name.
5. `AgentExecutionTimeline` and `AgentToolCallCard` perform another selection between the agent renderer registry and `UnknownToolRenderer`.

This makes routing depend on fields that have already lost transport identity. For example, `mcp__cherry-tools__generate_image` becomes the display name `generate_image`; the same logical tool then has two output contracts (chat FileEntry references and agent MCP content blocks). A renderer can be selected correctly by logical name but still reject the runtime-specific response shape.

Additional symptoms:

- MCP responses are cast to `NormalToolResponse` before entering parts of the dedicated renderer path, bypassing useful type checks.
- Full MCP wire names and normalized short names are both handled in routing conditions and tests.
- Protocol selection, runtime/surface selection, logical-tool selection, and presentation selection are coupled.
- Live-process rows and completed tool cards can use unrelated rendering paths.
- Adding a dedicated tool often requires coordinated edits across multiple routers and fallback renderers.
- Unit tests can cover synthetic wire-name inputs while missing the normalized production shape.

### Desired Solution

Introduce one typed tool-rendering decision model and make all tool surfaces consume it.

The normalized descriptor should preserve routing identity separately from presentation metadata, for example:

```ts
interface ToolRenderDescriptor {
  runtime: 'chat' | 'claude-agent'
  protocol: 'builtin' | 'mcp' | 'provider'
  wireName: string
  logicalName: string
  displayName: string
  serverId?: string
  serverName?: string
}
```

The exact type is open to design, but the following properties should hold:

- A single selector determines the tool renderer from stable identity fields; individual components do not re-infer origin from display names.
- Runtime/container policy is separate from content rendering. Agent timeline presentation should not determine how MCP content is parsed, and a logical tool can reuse one presentation with protocol-specific input adapters.
- `McpToolResponse` and `NormalToolResponse` remain type-safe through the routing chain; remove cross-type assertions used only to satisfy router signatures.
- Dedicated renderers declare the response contracts they support. Generic MCP and unknown-agent renderers remain explicit fallbacks.
- Live and completed message projections share the same renderer identity decision, even if their surrounding UI differs.
- Persisted historical messages with legacy `builtin_*`, full `mcp__*`, or normalized names remain renderable through a compatibility adapter at the projection boundary.
- Adding a tool or renderer should require one registry/selector entry plus its renderer, not edits across multiple routing layers.

Add table-driven tests covering the production matrix:

- chat builtin, provider, generic MCP, Claude agent builtin, and Claude agent MCP;
- full wire names, normalized logical names, and persisted legacy names;
- live, completed, error, approval, and restored-message states;
- text, structured JSON, image/audio/resource MCP content, and dedicated logical-tool outputs.

### Alternative Solutions

1. Continue adding name/type/server checks in `chooseTool` and `MessageTools`. This is the smallest option per bug but preserves the distributed routing model and its test gaps.
2. Route every MCP tool through `MessageMcpTool`. This simplifies protocol handling but loses agent timeline behavior and dedicated logical-tool presentations.
3. Route every Claude agent tool through `AgentExecutionTimeline`. This preserves agent styling but forces logical tools to duplicate existing chat presentations and keeps protocol parsing inside fallback renderers.
4. Make each dedicated renderer accept every possible transport shape without centralizing identity. This fixes individual tools but leaves unsafe routing and repeated adapters in place.

### Additional Information

The `generate_image` agent rendering bug is a concrete example, not the scope of this issue. Its minimal fix should remain local: reuse the dedicated image presentation while adapting chat FileEntry references and standard MCP image blocks into the same view.

Likely starting points:

- `src/renderer/components/chat/messages/tools/toolResponse.ts`
- `src/renderer/components/chat/messages/tools/MessageTools.tsx`
- `src/renderer/components/chat/messages/tools/chooseTool.tsx`
- `src/renderer/components/chat/messages/tools/agent/AgentExecutionTimeline.tsx`
- `src/renderer/components/chat/messages/tools/agent/AgentToolCallCard.tsx`
- `src/renderer/components/chat/messages/tools/agent/toolRendererRegistry.tsx`
- `src/renderer/components/chat/messages/blocks/MessagePartsRenderer.tsx`
- `src/renderer/components/chat/messages/blocks/LiveProcessToolList.tsx`

This should be implemented as a focused renderer-routing refactor, without changing tool execution, approval policy, MCP transport, or tool result persistence semantics.
