title: [Feature]: Refactor Claude Code settings builder into explicit materialization stages
body:
## Issue Checklist

- [x] I understand that issues are for reporting problems and requesting features, not for off-topic comments, and I will provide as much detail as possible to help resolve the issue.
- [x] I have checked the pinned issues and searched through the existing open issues, closed issues, and discussions and did not find a similar suggestion.
- [x] I have provided a short and descriptive title so that developers can quickly understand the issue when browsing the issue list, rather than vague titles like "A suggestion" or "Stuck."
- [x] The latest version of Cherry Studio does not include the feature I am suggesting.

## Platform

macOS

## Version

v2.0.0-dev

## Is your feature request related to an existing issue?

`src/main/ai/runtime/claudeCode/settingsBuilder.ts` has accumulated several unrelated responsibilities in one module:

- resolving live agent/session/channel state;
- preparing workspace directories and built-in agent resources;
- creating and updating tool-policy snapshots;
- building system prompts and channel security context;
- materializing MCP servers, skill whitelists, environment variables, and model settings;
- performing asynchronous side effects while constructing a request.

Because settings materialization reads mutable services and performs side effects across a long async flow, callers cannot easily guarantee that every derived value belongs to the same captured session state. PR #16946 had to add an explicit linked-channel snapshot to prevent MCP availability, permission policy, system prompt, source channel, and warm-connection rebuild decisions from observing different channel bindings.

The current shape also makes review and testing difficult: a small change to one concern requires understanding the entire settings construction pipeline and its hidden ordering constraints.

## Desired Solution

Refactor the Claude Code settings pipeline into small, explicit stages while preserving current runtime behavior:

1. Keep a thin orchestration layer that captures all mutable inputs once at the start of materialization.
2. Represent the captured inputs with an immutable materialization context/snapshot.
3. Move prompt, permission/tool policy, MCP, skills, model, and environment derivation into focused builders with explicit inputs.
4. Separate pure derivation from side effects such as workspace preparation, policy persistence, built-in agent provisioning, and network probing.
5. Keep the warm-connection rebuild signature derived from the same captured context used to build the request.
6. Preserve live-first policy update sequencing, fail-closed behavior, and the existing steer/rebuild invariants.

Add focused tests for each builder plus integration tests proving that one materialization uses a single coherent snapshot even when the underlying services change during asynchronous work.

## Alternative Solutions

- Continue adding optional snapshot parameters to the existing builder. This fixes individual races but leaves responsibilities and side effects coupled.
- Cache additional service reads inside `settingsBuilder.ts`. This improves consistency locally but does not make dependencies or ordering constraints explicit.
- Split the file mechanically without changing boundaries. This reduces file size but retains the same hidden coupling, so it should not be the primary goal.

## Additional Information

- Related implementation and review context: #16946.
- The refactor should be behavior-preserving and should not introduce new settings or runtime capabilities.
- Suggested first extraction boundaries: materialization context capture, system prompt/channel security, tool policy, MCP/skills, model settings, and environment construction.

title: [Bug]: Built-in CodeMirror themes load the full theme catalog
body:
### Issue Checklist

- [x] I understand that issues are for feedback and problem solving, not for complaining in the comment section, and will provide as much information as possible to help solve the problem.
- [x] My issue is not listed in the FAQ.
- [x] I've searched pinned, open, and closed issues and discussions; no duplicate was found.
- [x] The title is short and specific.
- [x] This was verified against the latest `main` branch.

### Platform

macOS

### Version

`main` at `30a184a294`

### Bug Description

`packages/ui/src/components/composites/code-editor/utils.ts#getCmThemeByName` awaits `loadCmThemes()` before checking whether the requested theme is the built-in `light`, `dark`, or `none` value. `CodeStyleProvider` calls this on the main-window path, so even the default dark theme downloads and evaluates `@uiw/codemirror-themes-all` before returning the plain string `dark`.

This violates `async-defer-await` and `bundle-conditional`: the production build emits a roughly 98 KiB minified theme chunk containing dozens of themes that a built-in selection does not need.

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Start the main renderer with a built-in CodeMirror theme such as `dark`.
2. Inspect the network/module graph during `CodeStyleProvider` initialization.
3. Observe the `@uiw/codemirror-themes-all` chunk loading before `getCmThemeByName` returns `dark`.

### Expected Behavior

Built-in `light`, `dark`, and `none` values should return before importing the theme catalog. The minimal fix should move that branch before `await loadCmThemes()` and add a focused lazy-boundary test; named catalog themes must continue loading normally.

### Relevant Log Output

N/A

### Additional Context

Renderer entry path: `src/renderer/windows/main/MainApp.tsx` → `CodeStyleProvider.tsx` → upstream UI helper.

Risk: unnecessary startup network, parse, and evaluation cost on the default renderer path.

title: [Bug]: Message enter motion rerenders every visible message
body:
### Issue Checklist

- [x] I understand that issues are for feedback and problem solving, not for complaining in the comment section, and will provide as much information as possible to help solve the problem.
- [x] My issue is not listed in the FAQ.
- [x] I've searched pinned, open, and closed issues and discussions; no duplicate was found.
- [x] The title is short and specific.
- [x] This was verified against the latest `main` branch.

### Platform

macOS

### Version

`main` at `30a184a294`

### Bug Description

`src/renderer/components/chat/motion/messageEnterMotion.tsx` provides the complete `enteringMessageIds` set through context. Every memoized `MessageFrame` consumes that collection. Adding one message replaces the set, then clears it after 380 ms, so every visible message frame rerenders twice although membership changes only for the new message.

This violates bounded provider contracts (`state-context-interface` / `state-decouple-implementation`): consumers need a per-message boolean rather than collection-wide invalidation.

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Open a conversation with multiple visible messages.
2. Start a React profile and add one message.
3. Observe all visible `MessageFrame` consumers rerender when the new ID enters the set and again when it clears after 380 ms.

### Expected Behavior

Only messages whose enter-motion membership changes should rerender. The minimal fix should expose a stable context store and let `useMessageEnterMotionActive(messageId)` subscribe to that ID's boolean snapshot, preserving motion timing and variants.

### Relevant Log Output

N/A

### Additional Context

Exact files: `src/renderer/components/chat/motion/messageEnterMotion.tsx` and consumer `src/renderer/components/chat/messages/frame/MessageFrame.tsx`.

Risk: message arrival cost scales with every visible frame and is paid twice per arrival.

title: [Feature]: Define product behavior for Topic and Agent Session list surfaces
body:
### Issue Checklist

- [x] I understand that issues are for reporting problems and requesting features, not for off-topic comments, and I will provide as much detail as possible to help resolve the issue.
- [x] I reviewed the existing open and closed issues. This issue is intentionally a product-behavior companion to #16994, created in response to its latest product review rather than as an unrelated duplicate.
- [x] I have provided a short and descriptive title so that developers can quickly understand the issue when browsing the issue list.
- [x] The latest `main` branch does not contain a complete, standalone product-behavior contract for these surfaces.

### Platform

macOS (the behavior is platform-agnostic)

### Version

2.0.0-dev (`main`; current behavior also reviewed on `zhangjiadi225/topic-session-pagination`)

### Is your feature request related to an existing issue?

Yes. This is the product source-of-truth companion to #16994, **“Refactor Topic and Agent Session pagination, grouping, and refresh semantics.”**

Issue #16994 currently combines user-facing decisions with API, pagination, refresh, and shared-component design. The [latest product-behavior review comment](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/issues/16994#issuecomment-4970519310) correctly points out that this makes it difficult to distinguish confirmed product requirements from architectural assumptions. It recommends defining the observable product behavior first and requiring later technical contracts to trace back to it.

The current branch already demonstrates much of the intended direction:

- Topic and Agent Session sidebars have independent display and sort controls.
- Right-side lists are scoped to the active Assistant or Agent and use a simplified flat presentation.
- History uses fixed creation-time ordering, owner search/filtering, incremental loading, and bulk actions.
- Pinned and ordinary records are presented as separate bands.
- Grouped views load and retry groups independently.

However, several behaviors are still implicit or inconsistent, including initial group expansion, search-state restoration, active-item reveal, drag meaning at partial-list boundaries, refresh interactions, selection retention, and error recovery. These decisions should be explicit before the shared behavior is considered complete.

One concrete gap is the work-directory hierarchy: the current code already presents **Work directory** and **No work directory** as peer top-level sections, with concrete work-directory groups nested under **Work directory**. The intended product behavior additionally requires users to reorder those two top-level sections by dragging the whole section.

### Desired Solution

## Product Behavior

This section is the source of truth for what users can observe and do. It intentionally contains no implementation design. #16994 should implement these behaviors; it should not redefine them.

### Product principles and terminology

- A **Topic** is presented to users as a conversation. An **Agent Session** is presented as a task.
- **Activity time** is distinct from general metadata modification time. It advances only for real conversation or task-content activity, such as a user message, a model response, or an equivalent task interaction. Merely opening or viewing a record, renaming it, pinning or unpinning it, moving it between owners or work directories, and manually reordering it do not advance activity time.
- Topics and Agent Sessions each have one global manual sequence. Every flat, grouped, and scoped view displays a filtered projection of that sequence; no view maintains a separate manual order.
- A **flat list** means one pinned band followed by one ordinary list. It never means Today, Yesterday, This Week, or Earlier date buckets.
- “Flat list” is the product term. The UI should not describe the display mode as “Time,” because users may sort it by creation time, activity time, or manual order.
- Pinned records and ordinary records are two visible bands with different ordering rules. A record appears in exactly one band.
- Showing useful records quickly is more important than loading a complete history before the surface becomes usable.

### 1. Surface responsibilities

| Surface | Primary responsibility | Product behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Sidebar — flat list | Fast everyday navigation and creation | Shows pinned records first, then an incrementally loaded ordinary list. Supports search and the selected record sort. |
| Sidebar — grouped | Navigation by Assistant, Agent, or work directory | Shows a global pinned section followed by independently expandable owner/work-directory groups. It is not required to load every group or every record. |
| Right-side panel | A deliberately simplified, scoped navigator | Shows only records belonging to the active Assistant or Agent, always as a flat list. It supports search and row actions, but has no display-mode, grouping, or independent sort controls. It follows the same Topic or Session sort preference as the Sidebar. |
| History | Complete long-tail retrieval and batch management | Supports incremental scrolling, search, owner filtering, selection, and bulk actions. It is the only surface intended for systematic retrieval of the full long tail. |

The following behaviors remain consistent across surfaces:

- A record has the same name, pin state, owner, and availability everywhere.
- Pinned records are always before ordinary records.
- Opening, renaming, pinning, unpinning, and deleting a record have the same meaning.
- A committed change automatically converges in every currently open affected surface in every application window, including subwindows and changes originating from the background. The user does not need to reopen the app, navigate away and back, or manually refetch.

Surface-specific creation behavior remains intentional:

- A flat Topic or Session Sidebar creates a new conversation or task from its primary action.
- In Assistant or Agent grouped mode, the primary action creates an Assistant or Agent; a group action creates a conversation or task inside that group.
- In work-directory grouped mode, the primary and group actions create tasks, with the group action using that work directory.
- Right-side panels and History do not add a separate top-level creation workflow.

Parent-level click and default record activation:

- In an Assistant- or Agent-grouped Sidebar, clicking an inactive Assistant or Agent parent row activates that owner, then selects and opens the owner's most recently active Topic or Session. This first click does not change the group's expanded or collapsed state. Clicking the already-active parent row toggles the group between expanded and collapsed states. The chevron is a non-interactive indicator that the group is collapsible and reflects its current expanded state.
- When the Topic or Agent Session page is entered without an explicit record target and at least one record exists, it opens the globally most recently active record.
- In the two-pane Assistant or Agent layout, the left pane is an owner selector rather than a group-disclosure list. Clicking a left-side Assistant or Agent activates that owner, then selects and opens the most recently active Topic or Session in that owner's scoped right-side list.
- If global automatic selection or explicit navigation opens a Topic or Session without a live owner in the two-pane layout, the content area opens that record while the left owner selector has no selected Assistant or Agent. The scoped right-side list is not required to reveal or select the record. This rare presentation state does not remove unlinked/unknown records from normal opening or most-recently-active eligibility.
- All automatic record choices described above use activity time, independently of the current list sort and pinned-band position. Pin state affects presentation, not which record is most recently active.
- An Assistant or Agent appears in the two-pane left owner selector only while it owns at least one Topic or Session; a pinned record still counts as a record.
- In an Assistant- or Agent-grouped presentation, including the two-pane layout, if the active owner loses its last Topic or Session, the next eligible owner below it becomes active; if there is none below, the previous eligible owner above it becomes active. The replacement owner's most recently active record opens. The app never creates a replacement record automatically. If no eligible owner remains, no record is active and the surface shows its empty state.
- Work-directory parent rows do not use this owner-selection behavior; clicking the parent row only toggles its expanded state and never activates an owner or child record. The chevron remains non-interactive.
- **Unlinked Assistant** and **Unknown Agent** are Renderer-managed pseudo-owner groups rather than live owners. Clicking either header only toggles the group; the header does not activate an owner or automatically choose a child record. This header distinction does not restrict the records inside the group: they remain normal conversations/tasks that may be active, opened, renamed, pinned, deleted, or dragged whenever the current surface permits that operation, and they remain eligible for automatic most-recently-active selection.

### 2. Display mode and sort behavior

Topic Sidebar display modes:

- Flat list
- Assistant groups

Agent Session Sidebar display modes:

- Flat list
- Agent groups
- Work-directory groups

Topic and Session ordinary-row sorts:

- Creation time: newest created first; this is the default.
- Activity time: most recently active first.
- Manual order: the user-defined order.

Display mode and sort are independent choices. Changing one never silently changes the other. Topic and Session choices are stored separately and remain selected across navigation and app restarts.

Additional rules:

- Pinned order never changes when the ordinary-row sort changes.
- Changing child-row sort never changes the order of Assistant, Agent, or work-directory groups.
- Right-side panels follow the corresponding Sidebar sort preference but do not expose a second competing preference.
- History is always newest-created-first and does not follow Sidebar sort changes.
- The History time column displays creation time so the visible value agrees with the list order.
- Changing display mode preserves the current search text, selected sort, and active conversation/task.
- Each grouped mode retains its own expansion state. Returning to that mode restores it.
- A structural display-mode change does not promise pixel-identical scroll position. Once the new view is ready, the active record is revealed if it belongs to the current result set.
- Changing sort keeps the current view and scroll anchor stable while the replacement order is prepared.

### 3. Pinned-band behavior

- Pinned records are shown in global pin order, independently of ordinary-row sort and owner/work-directory group order.
- A newly pinned Topic or Session appears first in the pinned band.
- A pinned record is removed from its ordinary group/list, so it never appears twice.
- In grouped Sidebars, pinned records appear in one global pinned section rather than being repeated inside owner/work-directory groups.
- Search applies to both bands, but matching pinned and ordinary results remain visually separated.

Sidebar and right-side panel behavior:

- The pinned and ordinary bands may become usable independently; ordinary records do not wait for every pin to be loaded.
- Any currently loaded pinned records remain above ordinary records.
- A large pinned set has its own “Show more” behavior. Loading more pins does not reset the ordinary list.

History behavior:

- History completes the matching pinned band before displaying ordinary rows. A later pin must never appear below an ordinary History row.
- Pinned History rows are visible and can be unpinned, but they cannot be selected or deleted. The user must unpin them first.

Pin and unpin feedback:

- A successful action moves the row between bands immediately, preserves the active record, and keeps the row visible during the move.
- Pinning a selected History row removes that row from the selection because pinned rows are not selectable.
- If the action fails, the row returns to its previous band and the user receives an error message.
- These rules apply to Topics and Agent Sessions only; they do not define pin behavior for every entity in the application.

### 4. Group loading and expansion

- On first entering a grouped mode, only the active record’s group is expanded when such a group exists; otherwise business groups start collapsed. The pinned section starts expanded.
- Subsequent visits restore the saved expansion state for that display mode.
- Explicitly navigating to a record opens its group and keeps that group expanded.
- Changing child-row sort or starting/clearing a search does not erase the saved expansion state.
- Groups with no ordinary records in the current search/filter are not shown. Clearing the search restores eligible groups and their previous expansion state.
- Expanding a group loads its first visible set of rows. The group becomes usable as soon as those rows are available.
- “Show more” reveals the next set of rows for that group. It never means “load every remaining row.”
- Collapsing a group stops it from requesting additional rows but does not discard already shown rows; reopening it resumes from the previous position.
- Loading or failing in one group does not block already usable sibling groups.
- If a group disappears because its owner/work directory or matching records disappear, retained sibling groups keep their rows and expansion state.

Group identity and order:

- Assistant groups follow Assistant order; Agent groups follow Agent order.
- Work-directory mode has two peer sections at its highest level: **Work directory** (the section for Sessions with a work directory) and **No work directory**.
- **Work directory** contains the concrete work-directory groups. Those concrete groups remain one level below the two top-level sections and keep their own ordering inside **Work directory**.
- **No work directory** directly contains Sessions that do not have a user work directory. It is not a concrete work-directory group and is not nested under **Work directory**.
- Users can drag **Work directory** and **No work directory** to reorder these two top-level sections. Dragging a section moves the entire section, including all nested groups and rows, without changing their internal order.
- Concrete work-directory groups can continue to be reordered within the **Work directory** section; they cannot be dragged out to the top section level.
- The top-level section order and the nested concrete-group order remain stable across navigation, display-mode changes, and app restarts.
- Pinned Assistants or Agents may affect the outer entity presentation but do not change child-row ordering.
- Topics with no live Assistant appear under **Unlinked Assistant**.
- Sessions with no live Agent appear under **Unknown Agent**.
- There is no third unlinked work-directory section or group.
- Unlinked Assistant and Unknown Agent groups appear after normal live owner groups. Work-directory section order follows the user-defined order described above.
- Existing Assistant tag sections remain unchanged; this issue defines record behavior inside the resulting Assistant groups rather than redesigning tag organization.

### 5. Search and filter presentation

- Sidebar, right-panel, and History search updates automatically through the same deferred-input behavior as Global Search; no submit action or fixed debounce duration is part of the product contract.
- Topic and Agent Session list matching uses the same entity-matching mechanism as Global Search: leading and trailing whitespace is ignored, the remaining query is matched as a literal substring, and `%`, `_`, and `\\` are ordinary searchable characters rather than wildcards. This refactor introduces no separate NFC-normalization or Unicode case-folding rule.
- Topic Sidebar and right-panel search match conversation names only.
- Agent Session Sidebar and right-panel search match task names only. Task descriptions are not searched.
- Topic History search matches either the conversation name or the name of its current live Assistant.
- Agent History search matches either the task name or the name of its current live Agent. Task descriptions are not searched.
- A deleted or missing owner name is never a search match, although the record remains searchable by its own name.
- Grouped surfaces stay grouped during search. Pinned and ordinary matches stay in separate bands.
- Groups with no matching ordinary rows are hidden during search.
- History owner filters narrow the results to one live owner or the unlinked/unknown owner group. Agent History has no running/completed/failed status filter.
- If only the owner name matches, the row is displayed normally and its visible owner/source label explains why it matched.
- Applying a new search or owner filter starts at the top of the new result set and clears History selection.
- Clearing search restores the prior group expansion state but does not restore an old pixel scroll offset.
- If the active conversation/task does not match a manually entered search, it remains open in the content area but is not injected into the filtered list.

### 6. Active-item reveal

When a user explicitly navigates to a Topic or Session from History, Global Search, another resource surface, an external target, or an “open” action, the owning list must make that record findable even when it is not currently loaded. This path matters when the owning list already has a manually entered search or filter that did not originate the navigation; a record selected from that same filtered list already satisfies its current query.

- If the target belongs to a collapsed group, that group opens.
- If it is beyond the currently shown rows, enough rows become visible to include it.
- If the current search or filter excludes it, the explicit navigation clears those constraints only after the target is confirmed to exist.
- A History row whose title differs from the query only because its current live Assistant or Agent name matched is already a valid search result; it does not use the excluded-record retry path.
- The owning Assistant or Agent scope becomes active before a scoped right-side panel attempts to reveal the record.
- The list scrolls the row into view and briefly highlights it.
- Reveal does not change the selected sort and does not require loading every record before the target.
- The target appears once in its correct band/group; it is not left as a permanent floating exception.
- After reveal, scrolling upward incrementally loads and prepends the records that precede the revealed window, while scrolling downward continues loading following records. Reveal does not make the target an artificial beginning or end of the list, and prepending earlier records does not jump the visible scroll anchor.
- If the record no longer exists, the current active record and filters remain unchanged and the user receives an unavailable/error message.

### 7. Dragging across partially loaded data

- Record dragging is available only for ordinary rows and only with Manual order selected. Both flat and grouped Sidebars support it.
- Pinned rows, right-side panels, and History do not support row dragging.
- Outer Assistant and Agent group ordering, concrete work-directory group ordering, and top-level work-directory section ordering remain independent from child-row sort.
- In work-directory mode, **Work directory** and **No work directory** support whole-section dragging at the top level. Concrete work-directory groups remain nested inside **Work directory** and use their existing group-level drag ordering there.

Topic behavior:

- All Topics share one global manual sequence, regardless of Assistant.
- Reordering inside an Assistant group changes the corresponding order in the flat Manual-order list.
- A Topic may be dragged between visible live Assistant groups. When the destination provides a concrete visible neighboring Topic, ownership and relative manual position change together.
- A same-Assistant drag changes only manual order. Moving a Topic to an empty Assistant uses the existing “Move to Assistant” action, changes only ownership, and preserves its current global manual position because no neighboring Topic is available.
- **Unlinked Assistant** is not a capability boundary. Its ordinary Topic rows may be active, opened, deleted, reordered inside the pseudo-owner group, or dragged into a visible live Assistant group under the same Renderer-owned surface policy. Pinned rows retain the pinned-band drag restrictions.

Agent Session behavior:

- All Sessions share one global manual sequence, regardless of Agent or work directory.
- Reordering in a flat Session Sidebar changes that global sequence directly. Reordering inside an Agent or work-directory group changes the corresponding filtered subsequence of the same global sequence.
- In grouped mode, a Session may be reordered only within its current Agent group or within its current work-directory group. It cannot be dragged across Agents or across work directories.
- An Unknown Agent Session may be reordered only inside the Unknown Agent group.
- A Session under **No work directory** may be reordered only inside that system section; **No work directory** is not a cross-group drop target.

Boundary behavior:

- A drop is relative to the visible neighboring row at the insertion line.
- Dropping after the last currently visible row means “after this visible row,” not “last in the complete list.” There is no separate command for moving a record to the global first or last position.
- Dragging is disabled while the relevant list or group is loading, refreshing, or unable to provide a stable drop target.
- Reordering and ownership organization do not make a record “recent” and therefore do not change its activity-time position.

### 8. Refresh continuity and immediate write feedback

For a sort change or background update that keeps the same membership:

- Compatible rows remain visible; the surface does not fall back to a full empty skeleton.
- The active row and scroll anchor are preserved by record identity when possible.
- Opening, renaming, pinning, unpinning, and deleting a visible row remain available.
- “Show more,” loading the next ordinary segment, and dragging are disabled until the replacement order is ready.
- If refresh fails, the previous compatible rows remain visible with an inline error and Retry action.

For a membership change such as search, owner, work directory, or pinned scope:

- Rows that cannot belong to the new result disappear when the new query takes effect.
- The surface shows the new loading, empty, or error state rather than presenting incompatible old rows as current results.

For direct user changes:

- Pin/unpin moves the row immediately between bands.
- Delete removes the row immediately after confirmation. If it was active, the current display and grouping mode defines the candidate order: the next surviving record after the deleted row becomes active, or the previous surviving record if no next record exists. Different grouping modes may therefore select different records.
- In an Assistant- or Agent-grouped presentation, if deleting the active record leaves its owner with no records, the next eligible owner below becomes active; if none exists below, the previous eligible owner above becomes active. The replacement owner's most recently active record opens, independently of visible sort and pin position. If no eligible owner remains, no record is active and the surface shows its empty state. Deletion never creates a replacement record automatically.
- Move updates the visible owner group immediately.
- Rename updates the visible title immediately.
- A failed action restores the previous visible state and reports the failure.
- No transition may leave duplicate rows or allow a stale “load more” action to reintroduce old ordering.

### 9. History selection behavior

- Selection exists only in History. Sidebar and right-side lists do not gain bulk-selection state.
- Pinned rows are not selectable.
- “Select all” selects only the ordinary rows currently loaded and displayed.
- Loading another page preserves existing selected rows but does not automatically select newly loaded rows.
- Changing search or owner filter clears selection.
- A compatible background refresh preserves selection by record identity when the row remains in the result.
- A row is removed from selection if it is deleted, pinned, successfully moved out of the current result, or otherwise no longer belongs to the current membership.
- Topic History supports bulk move to a live Assistant and bulk delete. Agent History supports bulk delete.
- After a partial bulk operation, successful rows leave the selection and failed rows remain selected so the user can retry.
- Clicking a checkbox changes selection without opening the record; clicking the title opens the record.
- Group-collapse behavior is not applicable to History because History remains a flat table.

### 10. Loading, empty, and error states

- Initial loading with no rows uses a surface-level loading state.
- Loading additional rows keeps existing rows visible and shows a non-blocking loading-more indicator.
- Flat Sidebar, right-panel, and History lists continue loading as the user approaches the end and may load enough rows to fill an otherwise under-filled viewport.
- Grouped Sidebars use explicit group expansion and “Show more” rather than silently loading every group.
- A group loading for the first time shows a group-level placeholder.
- A group failure shows an error and Retry action inside that group while siblings remain usable.
- If the surface cannot determine its groups or overall result at all, it shows a surface-level error and Retry action.
- “No conversations/tasks yet” is distinct from “No results for this search/filter.” The latter offers a clear-search/filter action.
- If a live Assistant or Agent disappears, its remaining records move to Unlinked Assistant or Unknown Agent without clearing unrelated groups.
- If a work-directory group is removed through the existing delete workflow, its tasks follow that workflow’s existing confirmation and deletion behavior; the app does not invent an unlinked work-directory group.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The four surface responsibilities above are documented in the UI behavior and can be verified independently.
- Default Topic, Session, and History surfaces become useful without loading the complete dataset.
- Flat lists have no date buckets and are not labeled as a “Time” display mode.
- Creation time is the default ordinary-row sort; activity-time and manual sorts remain explicit alternatives.
- Right-side panels are scoped flat lists that follow, but do not redefine, the Sidebar sort preference.
- In Assistant- or Agent-grouped Sidebars, the first click on an inactive parent owner activates it and opens its scoped most recently active Topic or Session without changing expansion state; clicking the already-active parent toggles its group, and chevrons remain non-interactive state indicators.
- Work-directory parent rows only toggle expansion and never activate an owner or child record.
- Initial entry without an explicit record target opens the globally most recently active Topic or Session.
- In the two-pane Assistant or Agent layout, selecting a left-side owner opens that owner's most recently active record by activity time, independently of right-panel display sort and pin position.
- If two-pane navigation opens an unlinked/unknown record, the content area opens it without selecting a left-side owner and without requiring the scoped right-side list to reveal it.
- The two-pane left owner selector contains only Assistants or Agents with at least one record, including pinned records. If the active owner becomes empty, the next owner below becomes active, or the previous owner above if none exists below, and that owner's most recently active record opens. If no owner remains, the surface shows its empty state without creating a record.
- History remains fixed to creation-time order and displays creation time in its time column.
- Pinned records are first, unique, and ordered independently; new pins appear first.
- Sidebar/right-panel ordinary rows do not wait for every pin, while History never shows ordinary rows before its matching pinned band is complete.
- Grouped modes preserve expansion state, expand the active group on first entry, and isolate group loading/errors.
- Search semantics match the rules above, including owner-name matches only in History and no Session-description search.
- Explicit navigation can reveal an unloaded record by opening its group, clearing incompatible constraints, centering it, and briefly highlighting it; subsequent upward and downward scrolling incrementally loads the preceding and following windows without a scroll jump.
- Pseudo-owner headers are toggle-only, while the conversations/tasks inside remain eligible for normal record capabilities and automatic most-recently-active selection.
- Topics and Agent Sessions each use one global manual sequence. Flat Sidebars support manual dragging; grouped dragging changes the filtered subsequence of the same global order. Topic ownership may change through eligible cross-Assistant dragging, while Sessions never cross Agent or work-directory groups.
- **Work directory** and **No work directory** are peer top-level sections and can be reordered by dragging the whole section; concrete work-directory groups remain nested one level below **Work directory**.
- A drop after a visible boundary is relative to that visible row; the product has no separate global first/last command.
- Compatible refreshes retain visible rows and the active/scroll anchor; incompatible membership changes do not retain misleading rows.
- History “Select all” affects only currently loaded ordinary rows, and later rows are not auto-selected.
- Loading, empty, no-match, group-error, and surface-error states are visibly distinguishable and recoverable.
- Agent History has no runtime-status filter.
- Activity-time ordering advances only for real conversation or task-content activity; metadata operations and merely viewing a record do not make it recently active.
- A committed change converges across all affected surfaces in all open application windows, including subwindows and background-originated changes, without requiring navigation or manual refetch.

### Alternative Solutions

1. **Keep product behavior embedded in #16994.** Rejected because confirmed UX requirements remain interleaved with technical design, making review and acceptance ambiguous.
2. **Let each surface define its own behavior independently.** Rejected because it recreates inconsistent search, pin, ordering, and refresh semantics.
3. **Load the complete Topic or Session history before deriving the UI.** Rejected because first useful render and memory usage grow with the user’s full history.
4. **Restore date buckets as the flat display mode.** Rejected because buckets move as time passes, conflict with non-time sorts, and add collapse state without serving the new navigation model.

### Additional Information

This product contract was derived from:

- #16994 and its latest product-behavior review comment.
- The current Topic and Session Sidebar behavior.
- The current scoped right-panel behavior.
- The current Assistant and Agent History behavior.
- Existing tests covering sorting, pinning, grouped loading, reveal, selection, and failure states.

Relevant current-code surfaces reviewed:

- `src/renderer/pages/home/Tabs/components/Topics.tsx`
- `src/renderer/pages/agents/components/Sessions.tsx`
- `src/renderer/components/chat/resourceList/`
- `src/renderer/components/history/`
- `v2-refactor-temp/docs/chat/chat-layout-modes.md`

Once this issue is accepted, product-behavior changes should be discussed here. #16994 remains responsible for technical implementation and should trace its contracts and acceptance checks back to this issue.

title: [Bug]: Paintings — returning during background generation leaves the artboard stuck (completed image never shown)
body:
### Issue Checklist

- [x] I understand issues are for feedback and problem solving, and will provide as much information as possible.
- [x] My issue is not listed in the FAQ.
- [x] I've searched existing open/closed issues and discussions; no similar one was found.
- [x] I've written a short, clear title.
- [x] I'm reporting against the latest code (v2 paintings on `main`).

### Platform

All platforms (platform-independent renderer logic).

### Version

`main` (v2 paintings page); surfaced on PR #17004's branch.

### Bug Description

When a generation is started and the user **leaves the Paintings page and returns while it is still generating**, the completed result is not reflected in the artboard after the background generation finishes. On PR #17004's blurhash-skeleton branch this shows as a **permanent loading skeleton**; more generally the artboard keeps showing the pre-completion state until the user switches to another painting and back, or re-selects the same item.

Root cause (renderer data flow):

- `currentPainting` is a one-time `useState` in `PaintingPage.tsx:25`, bootstrapped once by `usePaintingInitialSelection` (guarded by `bootstrappedRef`). On return-while-running it holds the DB *receipt* with empty `files` and no `generationStatus`.
- `history.items` (`/paintings`) **does** refetch reactively after completion and contains the finished painting with `files`, but nothing syncs that refreshed item back into `currentPainting`.
- The completing background `generate()` belongs to the **old, unmounted** page's `usePaintingGeneration` instance, so its `applyIfVisible` (`usePaintingGeneration.ts:120`) closes over the old `setCurrentPainting` and never reaches the new page.
- There is **no `succeeded`/`completed` terminal** `generationStatus` (only `running | failed | canceled`); success is represented by *absence*. So the reveal state machine in `Artboard.tsx` parks at `{ status: 'awaiting' }` with no dependency left to change.

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Open Paintings, pick a model, enter a prompt, click Generate.
2. While generating, navigate away and return to Paintings.
3. Wait for the background generation to finish.
4. Observe: the finished image doesn't appear in the artboard (permanent skeleton on the #17004 branch); it only shows after switching paintings and back.

### Expected Behavior

When a background generation for the currently-displayed painting completes, the artboard should reactively show the finished image without re-navigating.

### Relevant Log Output

_None (no error thrown — the state machine silently stalls)._

### Additional Context

Surfaced as Blocker **A1** in the review of PR #17004 (by @AtomsH4). Deferred from that PR because the root cause is pre-existing page-state architecture the PR doesn't touch — `PaintingPage.tsx` changes by a single line (`painting={currentPainting}` → `painting={composerPainting}`), and `usePaintingInitialSelection` / `usePaintingGeneration` / `usePaintingList` are untouched.

Proposed fix (either): (1) reactively adopt the refreshed history item's output `files` into `currentPainting` when the local copy lags (files-only merge, preserving in-flight edits) + a return-to-page success test; or (2) a durable completion signal that survives page remount and safely syncs the current record.

title: [Feature]: Cross-process TTL/expiry consistency for the shared cache tier + read-only useSharedCacheValue hook
body:
### Issue Checklist

- [x] I understand that issues are for reporting problems and requesting features, not for off-topic comments, and I will provide as much detail as possible to help resolve the issue.
- [x] I have checked the pinned issues and searched through the existing open issues, closed issues, and discussions and did not find a similar suggestion.
- [x] I have provided a short and descriptive title so that developers can quickly understand the issue when browsing the issue list, rather than vague titles like "A suggestion" or "Stuck."
- [x] The latest version of Cherry Studio does not include the feature I am suggesting.

### Platform

macOS

### Version

2.0.0-dev

### Is your feature request related to an existing issue?

This is the requirement write-up for a shared-cache (`CacheService`) infrastructure change, split out of the knowledge embedding-progress PR #16809 at a reviewer's request ("infrastructure changes should be submitted as a standalone requirement first").

The shared cache tier (`src/main/data/CacheService.ts` + renderer mirror in `src/renderer/data/CacheService.ts`) is the app-wide cross-window store behind `useSharedCache`. While building main-driven, TTL'd progress entries (main writes a value with a TTL, renderer windows observe it read-only), two pre-existing gaps in the shared tier surfaced. They are **platform-agnostic** (all of Windows/macOS/Linux) and affect any feature that puts a TTL'd or main-owned entry into the shared cache — not only knowledge indexing:

1. **A TTL applied on a same-value write never reaches renderer mirrors.** Main's `setShared` skips the cross-window broadcast entirely when the value is unchanged (`isEqual` short-circuit), so a TTL-only refresh updates main's own copy but leaves every renderer mirror holding the value **TTL-free for the rest of the session**. The renderer's own `setSharedInternal` already broadcasts TTL-only changes — the two sides were inconsistent.
2. **Shared-tier expiry deletes silently, and renderers have no GC.** Every expiry site on main — lazy `getShared`/`hasShared` cleanup, the 10-minute GC sweep, and `getAllShared` on new-window init — removes the entry from main's map without broadcasting a deletion. Renderer mirrors have no garbage collection of their own, so a TTL'd entry whose only reader has unmounted is **stranded in every open window until the app restarts**. Under repeated writes (e.g. per-item progress keys) this accumulates unbounded per window.

There is also no read-only way to *observe* a shared key another process owns end-to-end: `useSharedCache` initializes a missing key with the schema default and pins it via `registerHook`, so a passive observer both writes an entry and blocks the owner from deleting it.

### Desired Solution

Fix the shared-cache infrastructure so cross-process TTL/expiry state stays consistent, and add a read-only observer hook:

1. **Broadcast same-value writes whose expiry changed.** `setShared` broadcasts `{ key, value, expireAt }` when only the TTL changed (matching the renderer's existing `setSharedInternal` semantics); main-side subscribers still don't fire for same-value writes (documented `subscribe` contract unchanged).
2. **Broadcast expiry deletions to renderer mirrors.** All four expiry sites evict through a single helper that deletes from main's map **and** broadcasts the deletion, so renderer mirrors drop their copy. Main-side subscribers deliberately don't fire on lazy/GC expiry (contract unchanged).
3. **Add `useSharedCacheValue(key)` — a read-only shared subscription.** It reads the current value (or `undefined` while absent), re-renders on writes/expiry/deletion, and mounts without writing a schema default or pinning the key, so the owner stays free to expire or delete it.

Implementation is ready as a standalone branch/PR (6 files: `CacheService.ts`, `useCache.ts`, their tests, and `docs/references/data/cache-overview.md`), with cross-process mirror-cleanup tests on both the main and renderer sides. It carries no knowledge-feature code.

### Alternative Solutions

- **Downstream workaround (rejected).** The consumer can force propagation with a delete-then-set (delete the entry to reset the equality baseline, then re-set with the TTL so the write broadcasts). This bypasses the infrastructure gap rather than fixing it, fires a spurious deletion event that can briefly blank a mounted UI, and every future TTL'd shared-cache consumer would have to re-discover and re-apply the same hack.
- **Do nothing.** Leaves renderer mirrors accumulating stale entries per window for any TTL'd/main-owned shared key — a latent cross-window memory leak, not specific to the current feature.

### Additional Information

- Split out of PR #16809 (knowledge embedding progress), which consumes this infrastructure and will stack on top of it.
- Reference: `docs/references/data/cache-overview.md` (updated invariants 2/3/4 + API table).

title: [Feature]: Dynamic per-model/per-mode schema for generate_image (accurate size/aspect params + image editing)
body:
### Issue Checklist

- [x] I understand that issues are for reporting problems and requesting features, not for off-topic comments, and I will provide as much detail as possible to help resolve the issue.
- [x] I have checked the pinned issues and searched through the existing open issues, closed issues, and discussions and did not find a similar suggestion.
- [x] I have provided a short and descriptive title so that developers can quickly understand the issue when browsing the issue list.
- [x] The latest version of Cherry Studio does not include the feature I am suggesting.

### Platform

macOS

### Version

2.0.0-dev (follow-up to unreleased branch `feat/painting-tool`)

### Is your feature request related to an existing issue?

Follow-up to #16312 (the `generate_image` builtin tool). Two related gaps, both rooted in the tool using a **fixed, generation-only schema**:

**1. Params (size / aspect ratio) aren't provider-accurate.**
The tool exposes `prompt` + optional `n`. In #16312 we deliberately **dropped `size`** because pixel dimensions are not portable across painting providers, and the tool has no way to know the configured model's valid sizes:

- OpenAI DALL·E 3 → fixed enum (`1024x1024` / `1792x1024` / `1024x1792`)
- Doubao → `1K` / `2K` / `4K` (a separate `imageResolution` vendor field, not the native `size`)
- Imagen / Google → an aspect ratio (`1:1`, …)
- Many diffusion providers → arbitrary `WxH`

`AiService.generateImage` (`src/main/ai/AiService.ts`, `resolveImageRequestSize`) passes `size` through unchanged, so a model-supplied `"WxH"` is frequently rejected and degrades to the `PAINTING_ERROR_NOTE` failure path. Net effect today: the tool only ever generates at the model's **default** size.

**2. Image editing (image-to-image / edit) isn't exposed.**
The engine already supports it — `AiImageRequest` carries `mode`, `inputImages` (base64/URL) and `mask`, and the registry models image generation **per mode** (`ImageGenerationModeSchema = ['generate','edit','remix','upscale','merge']`, each declaring its own `modes[mode].supports`). The Paintings page already does edits. But the `generate_image` tool is generation-only, so an agent/chat model cannot say "edit this image".

### Desired Solution

Build the `generate_image` tool's input schema **dynamically, per-model AND per-mode**, from the configured painting model's `ImageGenerationSupport` spec — the same catalog the Paintings UI already reads:

- `@shared/data/types/model` → `ImageGenerationSupport` / `SupportSpec` / `CanonicalParamKey` / `ImageGenerationMode`
- backed by `@cherrystudio/provider-registry` → `imageParamCatalog`, `buildParamsSchema(support, mode)`

Expose exactly the canonical params the configured model supports for the relevant mode (`size` enum / `aspectRatio` / `imageResolution` / `numImages` / `maxImages`) with their valid options, so the LLM gets accurate, provider-correct choices and `AiService.generateImage` receives canonical `paramValues` guaranteed valid.

**Image editing — extend `generate_image`, do NOT add a new tool.** generate/edit/remix/etc. are variants of one operation (produce an image) and map to the same `AiService.generateImage` method via `mode`; splitting into a separate `edit_image` tool would fight the underlying model and add tool-surface. Instead:

- Add an optional input-image reference param (e.g. `image_ids`: FileEntry ids of images to edit/reference). Under the dynamic schema it only appears for models whose catalog declares an edit-family mode.
- **Presence of `image_ids` → run the model's edit/i2i mode** (`mode: 'edit'`); absence → `mode: 'generate'` (current behavior).
- In the core: verify the model has an edit mode (else a "this model can't edit images" note, like the no-model note); resolve `image_ids` → base64 data URLs via `FileManager.read(id, { encoding: 'base64' })` (capped by the mode's `maxImages`); call `AiService.generateImage({ mode: 'edit', inputImages, prompt, paramValues })`.
- Reference handle: `generate_image`'s text summary already includes the FileEntry id (`… name (id)`), so the model can reference a previously generated image on both the chat and agent paths ("edit the image you just made").
- **Exclude `mask` / inpainting** from the tool — an LLM can't author a pixel mask; that stays in the Paintings page.

AI SDK supports this (dynamic tool / building a per-request `tool()` with a computed schema).

**Implementation notes (what it touches):**

1. **AI-SDK builtin assembly** — `ToolEntry.tool` (`src/main/ai/tools/adapters/aiSdk/builtin/types.ts`) is a **static** `Tool`, and `applies(scope)` only filters include/exclude. This needs a per-request "build tool from scope" hook plus carrying the resolved painting model spec in `ToolApplyScope`. `generate_image` would be the first dynamic-schema builtin, so this is shared assembly infra.
2. **Shared `spec → tool-input zod schema` deriver** — a main-side analog of the renderer's `src/renderer/pages/paintings/form/imageGenerationToFields.ts` + `src/renderer/pages/paintings/model/canonicalGenerate.ts` derivation (mode-aware via `buildParamsSchema(support, mode)`). Extract a shared core rather than duplicate.
3. **Input-image resolution** — resolve `image_ids` (FileEntry ids) → base64 in the `painting.ts` core before calling `AiService.generateImage`.
4. **Claude Code MCP path** — `src/main/ai/mcp/servers/cherryBuiltinTools.ts` advertises a static JSON schema at construction; it must build the `generate_image` schema from the session's painting model spec/mode.

### Alternative Solutions

- **Drop `size`, generation-only (shipped in #16312).** Simplest and always-valid, but the model can't control dimensions/aspect ratio and can't edit images — it always gets a default-size fresh generation.
- **Per-provider size conversion layer** (map `"WxH"` → each provider's format). Rejected: every provider's rules differ, fragile/high-maintenance, and it duplicates knowledge the registry catalog already encodes.
- **A separate `edit_image` tool.** Rejected (discussed on #16312): edit is a `mode` of the same operation and hits the same `AiService.generateImage` method; a second tool splits one capability and adds model-facing surface. Extend `generate_image` with `image_ids` instead.

### Additional Information

- Platform-agnostic: this is a cross-platform, backend/tool-schema enhancement (the Platform field above is required by the template).
- Discussed and evidence-backed during #16312 review — not speculative.
- Sequencing: land the dynamic per-model/per-mode schema first, then editing (the `image_ids` param) falls out as "generate_image but `mode: 'edit'` + `inputImages`".

### Platform

macOS

### Version

2.0.0-dev

### Bug Description

The Anthropic API gateway corrupts multimodal MCP tool results by flattening image content blocks into ordinary base64 text.

The built-in `generate_image` MCP tool correctly returns a standard `CallToolResult` containing one text block followed by one or more `{ type: "image", data, mimeType }` blocks. However, `AnthropicMessageConverter.toolResultToOutput()` converts every image block into a `data:<mime>;base64,<payload>` string and stores the joined string as a `dynamic-tool` output. `convertToModelMessages` then sends the full base64 payload to the downstream model as tool-result text rather than as image content.

With two 1536x1024 generated images, the next model request contained 1,168,516 message tokens and exceeded a 1,048,565-token context window. Besides the overflow, the downstream model does not receive the images with their intended multimodal semantics.

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Configure an agent to use Cherry Studio's Anthropic-compatible gateway and enable the built-in `generate_image` tool.
2. Ask the agent to generate two high-resolution images.
3. Allow the agent to continue after the tool result is returned.
4. Inspect the next request passed through `AnthropicMessageConverter` to the downstream provider.
5. Observe that the image blocks have become full `data:image/...;base64,...` strings inside a text tool result and dramatically inflate the prompt.

### Expected Behavior

The gateway should preserve multimodal tool-result semantics end to end, or keep renderer-only image payloads out of model-visible history and pass a bounded reference instead. A generated image must never be converted into a full base64 text token payload. The renderer should still be able to display generated images without coupling UI delivery to the model prompt representation.

### Relevant Log Output

```shell
This model's maximum context length is 1048565 tokens. However, you requested 1200516 tokens (1168516 in the messages, 32000 in the completion).
```

### Additional Context

Relevant code:

- `src/main/ai/mcp/servers/cherryBuiltinTools.ts`: `readGeneratedImages()` and `toMcpResult()` create the valid MCP image blocks.
- `src/main/features/apiGateway/adapters/converters/AnthropicMessageConverter.ts`: `toolResultToOutput()` turns those image blocks into data-URL strings.

This is downstream of the dynamic `generate_image` input schema work in #17059; changing `dynamicTool()` or its input schema does not address this result-transport bug.

### Bug Description

`POST /v1/messages/count_tokens` undercounts Anthropic messages when an image is nested inside a `tool_result` content array.

`estimateTokenCount()` has a branch for top-level image blocks, but its `tool_result` branch only counts strings and text blocks. Valid image blocks inside `tool_result.content[]` contribute zero tokens. In an observed agent session, Cherry Studio/Claude Agent SDK displayed approximately 339.8K context tokens while the downstream provider measured 1,168,516 message tokens.

Because agent auto-compaction relies on context usage remaining below its configured threshold, this underestimate allows an oversized request to be sent instead of compacting first. `autoCompactEnabled` was already true in the Claude Code runtime settings.

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Send an Anthropic-format conversation containing a `tool_use` followed by a `tool_result` whose content includes one or more base64 image blocks.
2. Call `/v1/messages/count_tokens` with that conversation.
3. Compare the returned `input_tokens` with the token footprint of the request after the gateway's actual message conversion, or with the downstream provider's reported input size.
4. Observe that the nested image payload is absent from the gateway estimate.
5. Continue the agent session until the downstream context limit is exceeded and observe that automatic compaction did not run before the request.

### Expected Behavior

The token-counting route should account for all supported Anthropic content recursively, including images inside `tool_result.content[]`, and should estimate the representation the downstream provider will actually receive. Context-usage UI and auto-compaction decisions should not diverge from the real provider request by hundreds of thousands of tokens.

### Relevant Log Output

```shell
UI / SDK context usage: approximately 339.8K tokens
Provider error: requested 1200516 tokens (1168516 in the messages, 32000 in the completion)
Provider context limit: 1048565 tokens
```

### Additional Context

Relevant code: `src/main/features/apiGateway/routes/messages.ts`. The top-level `block.type === 'image'` branch estimates media, while the nested `block.type === 'tool_result'` loop handles only strings and `item.type === 'text'`.

This should remain an independent gateway-contract issue even if the built-in image tool stops returning full-size image blocks, because any Anthropic-compatible client or external MCP tool can legally send multimodal tool results.

### Platform

macOS

### Version

2.0.0-dev

### Bug Description

The API gateway loses the upstream HTTP status and retryability when an AI SDK provider failure arrives as an in-stream error chunk. A non-retryable provider 400 consequently becomes a gateway 500 `server_error`.

In the observed request, the downstream provider returned an `APICallError` with `statusCode: 400`, `type: invalid_request_error`, and `isRetryable: false` for a context-length overflow. The stream path retained only `chunk.errorText`: `AiSdkToAnthropicSse` threw a new plain `Error`, and `AiStreamManager.errorFromStreamChunk()` produced a `StreamError` containing only name/message/stack. The gateway error transformer therefore had no `statusCode` and defaulted to HTTP 500.

Claude Agent SDK saw the resulting 500 as retryable and replayed the same oversized request through its `max_retries: 10` sequence, extending the turn to roughly 370 seconds and incurring avoidable provider cost.

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Route a Claude Agent SDK request through Cherry Studio's `/v1/messages` gateway.
2. Make the configured downstream provider return a non-retryable 400 from its streaming API, for example by exceeding the model context limit.
3. Inspect the original AI SDK error and confirm `statusCode: 400` and `isRetryable: false`.
4. Inspect the gateway response received by Claude Agent SDK.
5. Observe HTTP 500 / `server_error`, followed by repeated `api_retry` events and identical requests.

### Expected Behavior

Provider error semantics must survive the stream manager and gateway boundary. An upstream 400 `invalid_request_error` should be returned as an Anthropic-compatible HTTP 400 and must not be retried as a server failure. The implementation should preserve structured error metadata rather than reconstructing status from message text.

### Relevant Log Output

```shell
APICallError: maximum context length exceeded
statusCode: 400
isRetryable: false
type: invalid_request_error

[ApiGatewayErrors] API gateway request error { code: 'UNKNOWN', error: { name: 'StreamError', ... } }
[ApiGateway] POST /v1/messages statusCode: 500
[ClaudeCodeStreamAdapter] subtype: api_retry, max_retries: 10, error_status: 500, error: server_error
```

### Additional Context

Relevant code:

- `src/main/features/apiGateway/adapters/stream/AiSdkToAnthropicSse.ts`: throws `new Error(chunk.errorText)`.
- `src/main/ai/streamManager/pipeStreamLoop.ts`: retains only `streamErrorText` for error chunks.
- `src/main/ai/streamManager/AiStreamManager.ts`: `errorFromStreamChunk()` drops status/retryability.
- `src/main/features/apiGateway/errors.ts`: correctly maps `statusCode` when present, but receives none on this path.

### Bug Description

Claude Agent SDK emits structured `system/api_retry` messages, but Cherry Studio deliberately logs and drops them, leaving the agent UI with no indication that a request is waiting for or performing a retry.

The SDK event contains all information needed for a useful status: `attempt`, `max_retries`, `retry_delay_ms`, `error_status`, and `error`. `ClaudeCodeStreamAdapter.handleSystemMessage()` currently groups `api_retry` with unimplemented system subtypes and only writes a debug log. Its unit test explicitly expects no emitted chunks.

In the observed session, generated images were visible, but the turn then appeared idle/busy for roughly six minutes while repeated requests ran. The user only saw the final context-length error; attempts 7 through 10 and their 33-38 second backoffs were visible only in main-process logs.

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Start an agent session using Claude Agent SDK.
2. Trigger a retryable API failure, such as a gateway HTTP 500.
3. Wait for the SDK to emit `system` messages with subtype `api_retry`.
4. Observe the main-process debug log containing attempt/backoff details.
5. Observe that the renderer continues showing only the generic running state with no retry attempt, delay, or error status.

### Expected Behavior

Cherry Studio should expose `api_retry` as a typed, session-scoped runtime event and display an ephemeral status such as “Retrying 7/10 in 36s”. The state should include attempt/max attempts, delay, and a safe error category; it should be cleared on the next request, success, terminal failure, cancellation, or disconnect.

Retry status should not be represented as assistant text or persisted as conversation content. A shared-cache/runtime-state path similar to agent compaction status would keep it observable without polluting message history.

### Relevant Log Output

```shell
[ClaudeCodeStreamAdapter] Received system message subtype: api_retry {
  attempt: 10,
  max_retries: 10,
  retry_delay_ms: 37353.18,
  error_status: 500,
  error: 'server_error'
}
```

### Additional Context

- `src/main/ai/runtime/claudeCode/streamAdapter.ts`: `api_retry` is debug-logged and discarded.
- `src/main/ai/runtime/claudeCode/__tests__/streamAdapter.test.ts`: asserts `parts` remains empty for `api_retry`.
- `src/main/ai/runtime/types.ts` and `src/main/ai/agentSession/AgentSessionRuntimeService.ts`: existing typed runtime-event seam suitable for a non-persistent retry state.

## Is your feature request related to an existing issue?

The current project already has text reading, binary reading, and file metadata querying capabilities, but these capabilities are scattered across legacy preload IPC and batch IpcApi dedicated to the Files page:

- Text and binary reading still accept raw paths via `window.api.fs.readText(path)` and `window.api.fs.read(path)`.
- The legacy `window.api.file.getMetadata(handle)` entry branch is not yet connected, with only `FilePathHandle` available.
- IpcApi currently only provides `file.batch_get_metadata` designed for list scenarios.
- `FileHandle`, `FileHandleSchema`, and `dispatchHandle` already exist, and `file.open` and `file.show_in_folder` already use this model, but single-file read-only access has not yet been fully migrated.

This forces generic renderer callers to continue relying on legacy IPC, or first parse the entry to a path before reading, thereby bypassing `FileManager`'s entry-aware behavior including dangling state observation and version semantics.

## Desired Solution

### What to build

Migrate existing single-file read-only access capabilities to a FileHandle-based IpcApi, forming a common boundary that can be used by Preview, Translate, Composer, Attachment, Artifact, and other modules, rather than adding any preview-specific interfaces.

Need to provide:

- `file.read`: Accepts `FileEntryHandle` or `FilePathHandle`, supports text and binary reading. Text mode preserves current automatic encoding detection behavior.
- `file.get_metadata`: Accepts both `FileHandle` types, returns the latest `PhysicalFileMetadata`; single-file failures propagate to callers through the standard IpcApi error model.

Entry branch should execute through `FileManager`, Path branch should execute through main process path file tools. All input must be validated via `FileHandleSchema` at the IPC boundary.

Also migrate at least one existing non-FilePreview text reader, one binary reader, and one metadata reader to prove the interface is a general capability and verify the complete call chain.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `file.read` accepts `FileEntryHandle` and `FilePathHandle`, supports text and binary modes.
- [ ] Text mode preserves current automatic text encoding detection behavior, does not force UTF-8 assumption.
- [ ] Read results can be transferred via structured clone and contain content, MIME, and version information required by existing reading contracts.
- [ ] `file.get_metadata` accepts both handle types and returns the latest `PhysicalFileMetadata`.
- [ ] Entry reading and metadata queries go through `FileManager`, Path branch goes through path file tools.
- [ ] File not found, permission denied, read failure, and stat failure propagate normally, rather than being converted to `null` in single-file interfaces.
- [ ] Existing `file.batch_get_metadata` remains unchanged, continues serving list scenarios with per-key nullable semantics.
- [ ] Migrate at least one existing non-FilePreview text consumer, one binary consumer, and one metadata consumer.
- [ ] Schema, handler, and migrated renderer calls all have tests covering both handle dispatch and error paths.

### Blocked by

None - can start immediately.

## Alternative Solutions

1. Use single-element call to `file.batch_get_metadata`. This would add extra map keys and convert filesystem errors to `null`, not matching interactive single-file read error semantics.
2. First get physical path via entry, then call `window.api.fs.*`. This would continue relying on legacy IPC and bypass `FileManager`'s entry-aware behavior, unable to complete the `FileHandle` boundary migration.
3. Add dedicated IPC for FilePreview. This would bind common file capabilities to a single UI consumer and should not be adopted.

## Additional Information

Existing non-FilePreview consumers already include Translate, Composer, message attachments, ArtifactPreview, ImageViewer, `useFileSize`, and attachment construction flow, so this capability has general requirements independent of the current FilePreview PR.

This issue explicitly does not include:

- Base64 read mode; no actual consumers in current renderer, can extend when demand arises.
- Migration of `file.get_physical_path` to IpcApi.
- Writing, hashing, streaming reads, file monitoring, or `isTextFile` content detection.
- One-time migration of all legacy File IPC callers.
- Changing FilePreview to accept `FileHandle`; that migration can be done separately after the general IpcApi is in place.

### What to build
