title: [Feature]: Reconcile provider-registry connection-config changes into already-persisted user_provider rows
body:
### Issue Checklist

- [x] I understand that issues are for reporting problems and requesting features, and I will provide as much detail as possible.
- [x] I have searched existing open/closed issues and discussions and did not find a similar suggestion.
- [x] I have provided a short and descriptive title.
- [x] The latest version does not include the mechanism I am suggesting.

### Platform

All (data layer — platform-agnostic)

### Version

2.0.0-dev (v2 / main)

### Is your feature request related to an existing issue?

**There is no mechanism to propagate `provider-registry` changes into already-persisted `user_provider` rows.**

`provider-registry` is the bundled source of truth for provider **connection config** (`endpointConfigs`, `defaultChatEndpoint`, `apiFeatures`, `name`). On startup it is written into the `user_provider` table by `PresetProviderSeeder`, which calls `ProviderService.batchUpsertTx`. Despite the name, that method is **insert-only**:

```ts
// src/main/data/services/ProviderService.ts
batchUpsertTx(tx, providers) {
  const existingIds = new Set(existing.map(r => r.providerId))
  const newProviders = providers.filter(p => !existingIds.has(p.providerId)) // existing skipped
  if (newProviders.length === 0) return 0
  insertManyWithOrderKey(tx, userProviderTable, newProviders, ...)
}
```

`SeedRunner` *does* re-run the seeder when `providers.json`'s content-hash version changes, but because the upsert skips any providerId that already exists, an existing provider row is **never updated**. The read path (`ProviderService.getByProviderId` → `rowToRuntimeProvider` → `resolveAiSdkProviderId`) consumes that persisted row with **no runtime registry merge**.

**Asymmetry that makes this easy to miss:** model-level data (`capabilities`, `endpointTypes`, new preset models) *is* merged from the registry at read time (`ProviderRegistryService.mergePresetModel`), so model updates reach everyone. Only **provider-level connection config** is persisted insert-only and goes stale.

**Concrete instance:** CherryIN under-declared its endpoints, so a Gemini image model's `google-generate-content` endpointType fell through to the generic `openai-compatible` provider and image edits hit `/v1/images/edits` (imagen-only → HTTP 500). The fix adds `google-generate-content` to CherryIN's registry `endpointConfigs`. But that fix only reaches **new installs** — every existing user who already persisted a CherryIN provider keeps the stale `endpointConfigs` and stays broken. Any future upstream change to an existing provider's connection config has the same blind spot (new endpoints, changed `defaultChatEndpoint`, `apiFeatures`, renamed preset providers, etc.).

### Desired Solution

A reconcile mechanism that carries registry connection-config changes into existing `user_provider` rows **without clobbering user data** (API keys, key rotation/enabled state, user-overridden `baseUrl`, enabled/disabled, ordering). Directions to evaluate:

1. **Field-level reconcile on seed re-run** — split preset-owned fields (registry `endpointConfigs` entries keyed by `adapterFamily`, `defaultChatEndpoint`, `apiFeatures`) from user-owned fields (`apiKeys`, custom `baseUrl`, `isEnabled`, order). Merge only preset-owned fields from the registry, preserving user overrides. Requires a rule to distinguish a preset-seeded `endpointConfigs` entry from a user-edited one.
2. **Read-time merge (preferred, mirrors models)** — stop persisting preset connection config in `user_provider`; resolve it from the registry at read time and layer only user overrides on top, exactly like `mergePresetModel` already does for models. This eliminates the whole staleness class instead of patching it per change.
3. **Version-journaled data migrations** — keyed on the `providers.json` content version already tracked in `appState` (`seed:presetProvider`), run idempotent reconcile steps when the version advances.

Whatever the approach, please document the invariant "who owns which field" so future registry edits know whether they reach existing users.

### Alternative Solutions

- **Ad-hoc one-off migration per change** — write a bespoke migration each time an existing provider's config changes. Fragile, easy to forget (the CherryIN fix would need one today), and doesn't generalize.
- **Full re-seed / overwrite existing rows** — clobbers user API keys and customizations. Unacceptable.

### Additional Information

Key code references:
- `src/main/data/services/ProviderService.ts` — `batchUpsertTx` (insert-only), `getByProviderId`
- `src/main/data/db/seeding/seeders/presetProviderSeeder.ts`, `src/main/data/db/seeding/SeedRunner.ts` (version journal in `appState`)
- `src/main/ai/provider/endpoint.ts` — `resolveAiSdkProviderId` (reads persisted `provider.endpointConfigs`)
- `src/main/data/services/ProviderRegistryService.ts` — `mergePresetModel` (the runtime-merge precedent for models)

Motivating fix: adding `google-generate-content` to `packages/provider-registry/src/providers/cherryin.ts`.

title: [Feature]: Refactor Claude runtime driver — extract a single system-message classification seam (content vs session-control)
body:
### Issue Checklist

- [x] I understand that issues are for reporting problems and requesting features, not for off-topic comments, and I will provide as much detail as possible to help resolve the issue.
- [x] I have checked the pinned issues and searched through the existing open issues, closed issues, and discussions and did not find a similar suggestion.
- [x] I have provided a short and descriptive title so that developers can quickly understand the issue when browsing the issue list.
- [x] The latest version of Cherry Studio does not include the feature I am suggesting.

### Platform

macOS

### Version

2.0.0-dev

### Is your feature request related to an existing issue?

Follow-up tech-debt surfaced while implementing #17081 (`api_retry` runtime status).

In `ClaudeCodeRuntimeDriver.runQueryLoop`, the split between **content** SDK messages (→ `adapter` → `CherryUIMessageChunk`, per-turn) and **session-control** SDK messages (→ `AgentRuntimeEvent` → `AgentSessionRuntimeService` → shared cache, per-session) is decided by a growing chain of inline `if (message.type === 'system' && message.subtype === …)` branches:

```
if system init …
if isCompactionSystemMessage && handleSystemControlMessage → continue
if system commands_changed → continue
if system api_retry → continue          // added in #17081
if !adapter → …
adapter.handleMessage(message)           // everything else = content
```

On top of that, `ClaudeCodeStreamAdapter.handleSystemMessage` still carries defensive no-op cases for the same control subtypes (`status`, `compact_boundary`, `api_retry`, …). So **"which subtype is control vs content" has no single source of truth** — it is smeared across the driver loop and the adapter switch. Every new control subtype means one more inline `if` in the hot loop plus another no-op in the adapter.

Key constraint that makes this non-trivial: the two buckets have different **lifetimes**. The `adapter` is per-turn (recreated each turn, cleared on `result`), whereas control messages (compaction between turns, `commands_changed` on a primed/turn-less warm connection) can arrive with **no active turn**. Only `runQueryLoop` spans the whole connection — so control handling genuinely belongs to the session-lived driver layer, not the per-turn adapter. That is also why it cannot simply be folded back into `adapter.handleMessage`.

### Desired Solution

Extract a single **classification seam** — one pure function that is the sole source of truth for content-vs-control:

```ts
// Claude-SDK-specific; lives next to the driver.
// Returns runtime events for session-control messages, or null = "content, hand to the adapter".
function toSessionControlEvents(message: SDKMessage): AgentRuntimeEvent[] | null
```

`runQueryLoop` then collapses the inline chain to one branch:

```ts
const control = toSessionControlEvents(message)
if (control) { for (const e of control) this.eventQueue.push(e); continue }
// genuinely stateful lifecycle cases stay explicit here:
//   init resume-token / pendingInitMessage buffering, steer-boundary message_start detection
// else → adapter.handleMessage(message)   // content, per-turn
```

Outcomes:
- `status` / `compact_boundary` / `commands_changed` / `api_retry` inline branches → one declarative table. Adding a control subtype = one line in the classifier; the driver loop and adapter stay untouched.
- The adapter returns to being a pure content transformer — the defensive no-op cases for control subtypes can be removed (they never reach it).
- The classifier is a pure function → unit-testable without mocking the whole SDK/query stream.

Deliberately **not** moved into the classifier: `init` resume-token update + `pendingInitMessage` buffering, and `steer-boundary` `message_start` detection — these are lifecycle/ordering state, not classification, and should stay explicit in the loop.

### Alternative Solutions

- **Two-sink adapter** (move control handling into `adapter.handleSystemMessage`, routed to a second "control" sink): rejected — the adapter is per-turn, so control messages arriving with no active turn (primed connection, between-turn compaction) would be dropped.
- **Leave the inline `if`s as-is**: acceptable short-term (it is how compaction/`commands_changed` already work), but the branch count keeps growing with each new SDK control subtype.

### Additional Information

- Scope: this is an intentionally **separate** refactor from #17081 — it also touches the existing compaction / `commands_changed` handling, so it should not be bundled into that feature PR (per the repo's "no unrequested refactors of working code" guideline).
- Primary files: `src/main/ai/runtime/claudeCode/ClaudeCodeRuntimeDriver.ts` (`runQueryLoop`, `handleSystemControlMessage`, `isCompactionSystemMessage`), `src/main/ai/runtime/claudeCode/streamAdapter.ts` (`handleSystemMessage`).
- No user-visible behavior change; pure internal restructuring covered by existing + new driver/adapter unit tests.

### Platform

macOS

### Version

v2.0.0-dev

### Is your feature request related to an existing issue?

The runtime `generate_image` tool needs to expose `image_ids` according to the selected model's actual image-editing capability. Provider Registry currently has no field describing how many input/reference images a model accepts.

The existing `maxImages` canonical parameter cannot be reused for this purpose: it controls the number of generated output images and is mapped by DMXAPI/AIHubMix transports to `sequential_image_generation_options.max_images`.

Without an independent input-image capability, the tool must conservatively cap references at one image. This avoids sending multiple images to single-reference transports, but unnecessarily disables multi-reference models.

Related context:

- #17076 introduces a runtime-schema `generate_image` tool and currently uses a temporary one-reference limit.
- #14715 requested selecting multiple reference images in the painting UI, but did not define provider/model capability metadata.
- #9355 tracked general image-input and image-editing support.

### Desired Solution

Add an independent, model-specific input image limit to Provider Registry, for example `maxInputImages` on `ImageModeDef`.

The capability should:

1. Be declared only for modes that accept source/reference images, such as `edit`, `merge`, or `remix` where applicable.
2. Be populated from verified provider/model behavior rather than inferred from output parameters.
3. Drive the runtime `generate_image` input schema so `image_ids.max(...)` matches the selected model.
4. Drive execution-side validation/limiting as defense in depth.
5. Keep `maxImages` exclusively as an output-generation parameter.
6. Include registry invariant tests and real model fixtures covering both single-reference and multi-reference models.

Acceptance criteria:

- Single-reference models expose and accept at most one `image_id`.
- Multi-reference models expose and accept their verified limit.
- Models without an input-image capability do not accidentally inherit an output-image limit.
- AI SDK and MCP `generate_image` tools derive the same runtime schema from the registry capability.

### Alternative Solutions

- Keep a global limit of one. This is safe but permanently disables multi-reference capabilities.
- Infer the limit from `maxImages` or `maxImagesPerCall`. This is incorrect because both describe generated output count.
- Allow an arbitrary array and rely on provider errors. This makes the model see an inaccurate tool contract and fails only after dispatch.

### Additional Information

Relevant code areas:

- `packages/provider-registry/src/schemas/model.ts` (`ImageModeDefSchema`)
- `packages/provider-registry/data/provider-models.json` and provider/creator definitions
- `src/main/ai/tools/generateImageTool.ts`
- `src/main/ai/tools/painting.ts`
- `src/main/ai/provider/custom/dmxapi/dmxapiTransport.ts`
- `src/main/ai/provider/custom/aihubmix/aihubmixImageModel.ts`

title: [Feature]: Redesign Settings "Data Reset" as v2 Factory Reset via preboot wipe gate
body:
## Issue Checklist

- [x] I understand that issues are for reporting problems and requesting features, not for off-topic comments, and I will provide as much detail as possible to help resolve the issue.
- [x] I have checked the pinned issues and searched through the existing open issues, closed issues, and discussions and did not find a similar suggestion.
- [x] I have provided a short and descriptive title so that developers can quickly understand the issue when browsing the issue list.
- [x] The latest version of Cherry Studio does not include the feature I am suggesting.

## Platform

macOS

## Version

2.0.0-dev (`main`). This is a v2 data-layer / preboot design issue and should be treated as cross-platform behavior.

## Is your feature request related to an existing issue?

The "Data Reset" button in Settings → Data is still the v1 implementation, and it is **effectively a no-op today** — worse than "not yet migrated", it silently fails while showing the user a success toast.

Current call chain:

1. Button (`src/renderer/pages/settings/DataSettings/BasicDataSettings.tsx:503`) → `reset()` in `src/renderer/services/BackupService.ts:171` — double confirm, then `localStorage.clear()`.
2. IPC `App_ResetData` (`src/main/ipc.ts:196`) → `LegacyBackupManager.resetData()` (`src/main/services/LegacyBackupManager.ts:923`), which only stages an empty `{userData}/Data.restore` directory.
3. `window.api.application.relaunch()` after a 1s timeout.

The staged `Data.restore` directory was meant to be swapped in at next boot by `LegacyBackupManager.handleStartupRestore()` (`LegacyBackupManager.ts:82`). That method **no longer has any caller** — `src/main/main.ts` only runs the v2 `runBackupRestoreGate()`. So the disk-wipe half of the mechanism is dead code.

What actually happens on "reset" today:

| Data | Result |
|---|---|
| Renderer `localStorage` | ✅ cleared (the only thing that is) |
| v2 SQLite `cherrystudio.sqlite` (all business data **and the Preference table**) | ❌ survives |
| `cache.json` (CacheService persist tier) | ❌ survives |
| `boot-config.json` (`~/.cherrystudio/`) | ❌ survives |
| `{userData}/Data/*` (Files, Notes, KnowledgeBase, Skills, …) | ❌ survives (swap mechanism dead) |
| Chromium session storage / IndexedDB | ❌ survives (only the separate "Clear cache" button touches it) |
| Side effect | orphaned `Data.restore` directory that nothing consumes |

## Desired Solution

Redesign "Data Reset" as **Factory Reset** with a v2-native mechanism. This issue is the plan for review, not an implementation PR.

### Semantics: factory reset

After reset + relaunch, the app behaves like a fresh install. Wipe manifest:

- `cherrystudio.sqlite` + `-wal` / `-shm` (business data + Preference table go together — they are physically one file in v2)
- `{userData}/Data/*` feature directories
- `cache.json` + Chromium session storage (cache = CacheService **and** Chromium storage; factory reset is a strict superset of "Clear cache")
- `boot-config.json` (custom data-dir location, early-boot settings — reset to defaults)
- `~/.cherrystudio` user state: MCP data, copilot token, `memory.json` (see Open Questions for the `bin/` carve-out)

### Mechanism: preboot wipe gate, mirroring `backupRestoreGate`

We cannot safely delete the SQLite file at runtime: better-sqlite3 is a synchronous always-open connection and lifecycle services hold file handles. The v2 backup/restore already solved this shape with a preboot gate (`src/main/core/preboot/backupRestoreGate.ts` + `src/main/data/db/restore/`), so reset mirrors it:

1. Runtime (IPC handler): after double confirmation, write a small **reset marker** file, then `Application.relaunch()` (`src/main/core/application/Application.ts:353` — v2-clean, reusable as-is).
2. Next boot, **before any lifecycle service starts**, a preboot reset gate sees the marker and performs the wipe.
3. Marker is removed last; normal boot continues into fresh-install seeding.

### Failure semantics: idempotent retry, no journal

Unlike restore (which must swap user data in atomically), a wipe is naturally idempotent — deleting an already-deleted file is fine. If the wipe is interrupted, the marker is still present and the next boot re-runs it. No journal, no staging directory.

### v1 cleanup (in scope for the implementing PR)

- `LegacyBackupManager.resetData()` and the dead `handleStartupRestore()` / `*.restore` staging mechanism
- IPC `App_ResetData` registration (`ipc.ts:196`) and preload `resetData` (`preload.ts:81`)
- Renderer `BackupService.reset()` flow including the commented-out Dexie `clearDatabase()` (`BackupService.ts:1025`)

Note: `handleStartupRestore()` being dead also means the **v1 backup-restore flow** (`LegacyBackupManager.ts:530-660`, same `*.restore` staging) is equally broken today. Wholesale deletion of `LegacyBackupManager` is beyond this issue's scope — flagging it here for a separate cleanup issue.

### UI

Keep the existing double-confirm dialog flow in Settings → Data; rename/reword i18n keys from "Data Reset" to factory-reset semantics, and state explicitly in the confirm dialog that settings (including a custom data directory location) are reset too.

## Alternative Solutions

1. **In-process wipe at runtime** — rejected: races against the open synchronous SQLite connection and services holding handles; exactly the problem the preboot gate pattern exists to avoid.
2. **Rewire the v1 `*.restore` swap** (call `handleStartupRestore()` from `main.ts` again) — rejected: it only covers `{userData}/Data`, knows nothing about SQLite/cache.json/boot-config, and the pattern is superseded by v2 preboot gates.
3. **Journal-based staged wipe like v2 restore** — rejected as overkill: wipe is idempotent, so a marker + retry gives the same guarantee with far less machinery.

## Open Questions (review wanted)

1. **`~/.cherrystudio/bin` (BinaryManager downloads: uv, bun, gh, …)** — proposal: **keep it** as the single carve-out from factory reset. Binaries are machine artifacts, not user data; wiping them only forces a re-download of hundreds of MB (especially painful behind the China mirror). Analogy: a phone factory reset doesn't delete the OS. Objections welcome.
2. Should the confirm dialog offer any granularity (e.g. "also clear downloaded tools"), or stay a single all-or-nothing factory reset? Proposal: all-or-nothing, one less decision for a destructive flow.

## Additional Information

- Paths involved (all via `application.getPath` / `pathRegistry.ts`): `app.database.file`, `app.userdata`, `feature.*` Data dirs, `BOOT_CONFIG_PATH` (`src/main/core/paths/constants.ts:22`).
- `BootConfigService` already has a delete-file affordance (`BootConfigService.ts:91`).
- Dev-mode caveat: `Application.relaunch()` does not auto-restart unpackaged builds (shows a dialog and exits) — acceptance testing should use a packaged build or manual restart.
- Related `TODO(v2)`: `App_SetAppDataPath` (`ipc.ts:135`) follows the same "change must go through boot-config + restart" shape and may share the gate infrastructure later.

### Platform

### Bug Description

Environment

Cherry Studio version: 1.9.12 (Windows, installer build)
OS: Windows 11
Rerank provider: gitee (https://ai.gitee.com/v1/rerank)
Rerank model: bge-reranker-v2-m3
Scenario: Web Search + RAG compression (rerank)
Describe the bug
When using Web Search with RAG compression enabled, the compression step calls the rerank API and fails with HTTP 400: Bad Request. Compression returns empty results, so the web search results cannot be properly reranked/filtered.

The raw error returned by gitee is:

documents length must be between '1' and '25'

However, the request body sent by Cherry Studio contains a documents array of length 27 (and 30 in another occurrence), with top_n also set to 27 / 30 — both exceeding the provider's per-request limit of 25.

Root cause analysis
The number of documents sent to rerank is not the "number of search results", but the number of chunks produced after splitting the fetched web page content. Even after lowering "search result count" to 20, the pages were split into 27–30 chunks, all sent in a single documents array. Cherry Studio does not batch the chunks according to each rerank provider's maximum document limit, so whenever the chunk count exceeds 25, the request always fails with 400.

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Set rerank provider to gitee, model bge-reranker-v2-m3
2. Enable Web Search + RAG compression
3. Ask a question that hits multiple long web pages (so chunks > 25 after splitting)
4. Observe compression failure and empty results
5. Expected behavior

### Expected Behavior

Before calling rerank, Cherry Studio should batch the documents array according to the target provider/model's document limit, then merge results across batches and apply top_n — or at least truncate to the limit — instead of failing the whole request.

### Relevant Log Output

```shell
Rerank request failed: HTTP 400: Bad Request
Request details: { ... "top_n": 27 } / { ... "top_n": 30 }
Provider error: documents length must be between '1' and '25'
RAG compression failed, will return empty results
```

### Additional Context

Related issue
After a compression failure, the leftover temporary knowledge-base cache files fail to be cleaned up with EPERM, Permission denied, leaving stale/invalid files in the KnowledgeBase directory. Worth investigating together.

[Feature]: Stream large PDFs via chunked range loading to lift the preview size cap
body:
### Issue Checklist

- [x] I understand that issues are for reporting problems and requesting features, not for off-topic comments, and I will provide as much detail as possible to help resolve the issue.
- [x] I have checked the pinned issues and searched through the existing open issues, closed issues, and discussions and did not find a similar suggestion.
- [x] I have provided a short and descriptive title so that developers can quickly understand the issue when browsing the issue list.
- [x] The latest version of Cherry Studio does not include the feature I am suggesting.

### Platform

All platforms (Windows / macOS / Linux)

### Version

2.0.0-dev (main / v2 development line)

### Is your feature request related to an existing issue?

Follow-up to PR #17149.

That PR fixed the immediate problem — opening a large PDF in the file preview read the whole file into memory (`window.api.fs.read`) before handing it to pdf.js, spiking memory across the IPC boundary + the pdf.js worker copy and freezing the window. The fix (Solution A) preflights the size with `getMetadata` and **hard-caps preview at 50 MiB**, then falls back to "Open with default app".

The remaining limitation: **PDFs above the cap cannot be previewed in-app at all**, even though they are exactly the files users often most want to preview (scanned documents, large reports, e-books can easily exceed 50 MiB). pdf.js is fully capable of rendering them — the bottleneck is not rendering, it's that we read + IPC-transfer the entire file up front instead of streaming it.

### Desired Solution

Load PDF bytes on demand instead of all at once, using pdf.js's built-in random-access loading path, so the hard size cap can be lifted.

**Why this fits PDF specifically:** PDF is a random-access format (xref table + per-object offsets). pdf.js is designed to stream it via `PDFDataRangeTransport` (the same mechanism Firefox's built-in viewer uses for HTTP Range). Only the cross-reference data and the chunks backing currently-visible pages need to be resident, so memory stays flat regardless of total file size.

Proposed shape:

1. **New chunked-read IPC endpoint** — e.g. `fs.readChunk(path, offset, length)` (main-side `fs.open` + positioned `read`). Per `CLAUDE.md`, imperative command IPC like this should go through **IpcApi** (schema + handler), not a new legacy `ipcMain.handle`. This is the "fix upstream" step: the current `fs.read` IPC has no partial-read capability, and other future streaming previews (audio/video seek) would reuse it.
2. **Renderer `PDFDataRangeTransport` subclass** — `requestDataRange(begin, end)` calls the new IPC and feeds bytes back via `onDataRange`. Total length comes from `getMetadata` (the size preflight we already do).
3. **Wire into pdf.js** — `getDocument({ range: transport, length, disableAutoFetch: true, rangeChunkSize: ~1 MiB })`. `disableAutoFetch` prevents pdf.js from silently backfilling the whole file; a ~1 MiB chunk size bounds IPC round-trips.
4. **Lifecycle** — abort the transport and release file handles on unmount / `filePath` change / `refreshKey` change, consistent with the plugin's existing teardown.

Outcome: the 50 MiB hard cap in `PdfFilePreview.tsx` can be removed (or relaxed to a multi-GB sanity limit); large PDFs open smoothly with flat memory.

### Alternative Solutions

- **Just raise the hard cap** (e.g. 50 → 200 MiB). Trivial, but only moves the freeze threshold — a 200 MiB read still blocks the window; it does not solve the underlying "read everything up front" problem.
- **Custom local-file protocol with HTTP Range responses** (`protocol.handle` streaming local files, `getDocument({ url })`). Zero plugin code, pdf.js uses its normal fetch transport — but it opens a "read any local file by URL" surface that needs its own token/allowlist hardening, and the current `ProtocolService` only handles `cherrystudio://` deep links. Over-engineered for one plugin; worth revisiting only if audio/video streaming previews later need the same infrastructure.

### Additional Information

- Scope is intentionally limited to the PDF plugin; other preview plugins keep their existing size guards.
- Suggested acceptance check: open a multi-hundred-MB PDF and confirm the process's resident memory stays roughly constant while scrolling, rather than tracking file size.

title: Register generate_image tool output as a chat_message file ref (fix orphaned files, unblock GC auto-reclaim)
body:
### Problem

Images produced by the builtin `generate_image` agent tool are persisted as `FileEntry` rows but are **never registered in any `*_file_ref` table**. The generated file's id lives only inside the assistant message's `tool-generate_image` part output (`generateImageOutputSchema` = `{ id, name }[]`); the renderer resolves it to a `file://` URL at display time via `getPhysicalPath(id)` (`MessageGenerateImage.tsx`).

The message-save path that materializes chat-message file references — `extractChatMessageFileEntryIds` (`src/main/data/services/MessageService.ts:183-194`) — only scans `part.type === 'file'` parts carrying `cherry.fileEntryId`. Tool parts are skipped, so a `generate_image` result never flows into `chat_message_file_ref`.

Two concrete consequences:

1. **Orphaned files.** When the containing message is deleted, the `chat_message_file_ref` FK cascade cannot reach these images (no row was ever registered), so the image files leak on disk permanently. This holds independent of GC.
2. **Blocks GC auto-reclaim.** The scan-based file GC (#16727) decides "referenced or not" via a ref-table anti-join. Because these outputs have no ref, they must be persisted with `cleanupPolicy: 'manual'` (`src/main/ai/tools/painting.ts`) purely to keep the unreferenced-file sweep from reclaiming them (which would be unrecoverable). That opts them out of automatic reclamation permanently.

### Desired Solution

Register `generate_image` output into the **existing** `chat_message_file_ref` table — its semantics already match (a file owned by a chat message, deleted with the message). No new table is needed.

Recommended (route B): extend `extractChatMessageFileEntryIds` to also recognize the `tool-generate_image` part, parse its output via `generateImageOutputSchema`, and register each id with a new role `'generated'` (distinct from user attachments' `'attachment'`).

Once refs are registered, flip `painting.ts`'s `cleanupPolicy` from `'manual'` to `'delete_when_unreferenced'` — the images then participate in normal GC, and message deletion cascades them away.

**Two output paths must both be covered:**

1. Plain chat via the AI-SDK builtin tool (`PaintingTool.ts`) → lands on a `chat_message` message.
2. Agent session via the Claude Code in-process MCP bridge (`cherryBuiltinTools.ts`) → lands on an agent-session message (separate store + its own ref registration).

### Alternative Solutions

- **Route A:** emit the generated images as `file` parts carrying `cherry.fileEntryId` on the assistant message, so `replaceChatMessageFileRefsTx` picks them up unchanged — but this touches message structure + stream persistence and must be coordinated with the renderer (which currently renders from the tool response, so a duplicate `file` part would double-render).
- **Status quo (`manual`):** no data loss and no misreclaim, but images stay orphaned on message delete and never auto-reclaim.

### Additional Information

Discovered while landing the policy-based file GC (#16727). That PR deliberately keeps `generate_image` output at `cleanupPolicy: 'manual'` to respect the current reference reality; this issue tracks the upstream fix that would let it flip to `delete_when_unreferenced`.

Key references:

- `src/main/ai/tools/painting.ts` — `generateImageFromPrompt`, `cleanupPolicy: 'manual'`
- `src/main/ai/tools/adapters/aiSdk/builtin/PaintingTool.ts` — AI-SDK tool wiring
- `src/main/ai/mcp/servers/cherryBuiltinTools.ts` — Claude Code MCP bridge
- `src/main/data/services/MessageService.ts:183-194` — `extractChatMessageFileEntryIds` (the extractor to extend)
- `src/renderer/components/chat/messages/tools/painting/MessageGenerateImage.tsx` — renderer resolving ids via `getPhysicalPath`

title: [Bug]: Local backup fails on macOS with ENOENT chmod on nested skill schema file (Data/Skills)
body:
### Bug Description

Local backup fails on macOS. `backup:backupToLocalDir` throws `ENOENT` while running `chmod` on a nested skill schema file inside the temp backup directory:

```
Error invoking remote method 'backup:backupToLocalDir': Error: ENOENT: no such file or directory, chmod '/var/folders/7_/4qhthv5d46z1lpq62r6s6bwm0000gn/T/cherry-studio/backup/temp/Data/Skills/docx/scripts/office/schemas/ISO-IEC29500-4_2016/shared-math.xsd'
```

The backup aborts, so no local (or cloud) backup can be produced.

### Platform

macOS

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Have skills installed under `Data/Skills` (e.g. a `docx` skill that ships deeply-nested schema files).
2. Settings → Data Settings → Local backup, choose a directory, click backup.
3. Backup fails with the `ENOENT ... chmod` error above.

### Analysis

The backup copies `Data/Skills` into a temp staging dir and then walks it applying `chmod`/permission fixes. The `chmod` targets a file (`shared-math.xsd`) that no longer exists at the temp path — the file listing and the actual permission pass are out of sync for deeply-nested skill files. Likely the same root area as the closed #14517 (`EPERM symlink` under `Data/Skills` on Windows) and #14360 — the skills-directory copy/permission step in the backup pipeline does not robustly handle nested skill bundles across platforms.

### Expected Behavior

Backup should complete regardless of nested skill files. The permission pass should tolerate files that were moved/removed during staging (skip-if-missing) rather than aborting the whole backup.

### Related

- #14517 (closed/inactive) — same `backupToLocalDir` failure on `Data/Skills`, Windows EPERM symlink
- #14360 — Windows EPERM backup

title: [Discussion]: Make AgentSession a lifecycle-managed runtime entity
body:
### Issue Checklist

- [x] I understand that issues are meant for feedback and problem-solving, not for venting, and I will provide as much detail as possible to help resolve the issue.
- [x] I have checked the pinned issues and searched through the existing open issues, closed issues, and discussions and did not find a discussion at this ownership level.
- [x] I confirm that I am here to ask questions and discuss issues, not to report bugs or request features.

### Platform

macOS

### Version

`main` (`0c472a64`), discussed while reviewing #17143

### Your Question

Should `AgentSession` be promoted from a Data API-managed record plus a separate runtime service into a lifecycle-managed main-process business entity?

The current design exposes session creation, mutation, and deletion through Data API services, while active/idle runtime state and external resources are owned elsewhere. This makes a Data API delete mean only "remove the database rows". Runtime processes, system workspaces, transcripts, and per-session caches then have to be reconciled later by mechanisms such as the periodic mark-and-sweep introduced in #17143.

That sweep is useful as an immediate stopgap and for historical orphan cleanup. The concern is the architectural direction: as more runtimes and external artifacts are added, treating the database as the complete `AgentSession` lifecycle owner may require more GC rules to compensate for lifecycle transitions that no single service owns.

Would the intended direction instead be:

```text
Renderer
  -> typed AgentSession IPC API
  -> lifecycle-managed AgentSessionService
       -> AgentSession persistence service/repository
       -> AgentSessionRuntimeService / runtime drivers
       -> workspace and runtime artifact stores
```

In this model, the owning service would coordinate session commands and state transitions such as create, activate, idle, close, and delete. The persistence layer would remain transaction-composable and free of filesystem/process side effects, but Data API would no longer be the public mutation boundary for a runtime entity.

Deletion could then be modeled explicitly:

```text
active | idle
  -> deleting (persist deletion intent and reject new turns)
  -> stop active and prewarmed runtime resources
  -> remove owned workspace and runtime artifacts
  -> remove persisted session state
  -> deleted
```

A crash while deleting would resume a known lifecycle transition on startup instead of discovering ownership indirectly by scanning the filesystem. Periodic sweeping could remain temporarily for legacy orphan migration, rather than becoming the primary resource-lifetime mechanism.

### Context

PR #17143 correctly identifies a current leak: deleting a session or removing messages only changes SQLite rows, leaving Claude Code transcripts, token-scoped caches, and system workspace directories behind. Its runtime-agnostic GC can reclaim those files without adding side effects to the current Data API services.

The open design concern is why the complete delete operation is constrained to the Data API service in the first place. Keeping transaction-scoped persistence methods DB-only is necessary; requiring the entire business command to be DB-only is a separate policy choice. `AgentSession` has process-local active/idle state, live and prewarmed subprocesses, and externally persisted runtime artifacts, so CRUD over its database representation is not its complete business semantics.

Related discussion #16052 addresses explicit ownership of resources inside a Claude Code connection scope. This issue is intentionally one level higher: which main-process service owns the complete `AgentSession` lifecycle and renderer-facing command boundary.

Points to decide:

1. Should session mutations move from Data API to a typed AgentSession IpcApi surface?
2. Should the existing `AgentSessionRuntimeService` become the lifecycle owner, or should a broader `AgentSessionService` coordinate persistence and runtime components?
3. Which lifecycle states need durable representation? At minimum, is a recoverable `deleting` intent required?
4. How should resume tokens and other artifacts record stable session ownership independently of editable message rows?
5. What migration path keeps #17143 useful for historical cleanup without making periodic GC the permanent primary mechanism?

### Additional Information

```text
Non-goals for this discussion:
- Do not block #17143 from serving as an immediate leak mitigation.
- Do not put filesystem I/O inside a SQLite transaction.
- Do not sweep the user's shared ~/.claude directory without explicit ownership.
- Do not prescribe a separate service for every operation such as deletion.
```

### Priority

Medium (Would like a response soon)

### Platform

Windows

### Version

`main` before the fix (`a26477fe8d`); the original report was reproduced on Windows and the underlying behavior is platform-independent.

### Bug Description

After editing a scheduled task's prompt, workspace, timeout, or channel selection, manually running the task can still enqueue the previous task configuration. The updated configuration only starts taking effect after pausing and resuming the schedule.

The armed schedule callback retains an older execution template, while task actions in the renderer can also race an in-flight save. This makes persisted edits appear successful even though the next manual run uses stale content.

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Open **Settings → Scheduled Tasks** and create a scheduled task.
2. Manually run the task and verify that it uses the initial configuration.
3. Update the task prompt, workspace, or channel selection.
4. Manually run the task again without pausing it.
5. Observe that the queued execution still uses the previous configuration.
6. Pause and resume the task, then run it again.
7. Observe that the updated configuration is now used.

### Expected Behavior

The next manual or automatic fire should read the latest persisted task configuration without requiring pause/resume. Updating execution settings must not reset an Interval schedule's timing cycle, and run/pause/resume actions should wait for pending saves to finish.

### Relevant Log Output

```shell
N/A
```

### Additional Context

This can affect more than Windows because the stale state is held in the in-process scheduler callback rather than in platform-specific code.

title: [Feature]: Support migration failure diagnostic bundles
body:
### Issue Checklist

- [x] I have provided a short and descriptive title so that developers can quickly understand the issue when browsing the issue list, rather than vague titles like "A suggestion" or "Stuck."
- [x] The latest version of Cherry Studio does not include the feature I am suggesting.

### Platform

All platforms.

### Version

2.0.0-dev (`main`)

### Is your feature request related to an existing issue?

The v1-to-v2 migration can stop because the installed data version is incompatible with the supported upgrade path, or fail while migration is running. The existing error surfaces explain the failure and offer recovery choices, but they do not produce a support artifact that users can inspect and share manually.

Some migration failures are reported in the renderer, while others use native dialogs before normal application bootstrap. The diagnostic save flow therefore needs to be available from both surfaces without changing the existing migration decisions.

### Desired Solution

Add a migration failure diagnostic bundle that users can save when either of these conditions is shown:

- The existing data version is incompatible with the supported migration path.
- The migration fails, whether the failure is displayed by the migration window or an existing native preboot dialog.

The flow should:

- Ask the user where to save an atomic ZIP file, use the migration window's current language for renderer-triggered save dialogs, and serialize concurrent save requests.
- Always include compact application and migration metadata.
- Include every regular application log file for the user's local save date, byte-for-byte, when the complete eligible set can be read; if that date has no eligible log for an active run, fall back once to the run's local failure date (or start date when no failure time exists) without combining dates.
- Still save the metadata-only bundle when logs are missing or any eligible log cannot be read.
- Preserve bundles larger than 15 MiB and warn the user instead of failing the save.
- Clearly warn that logs may contain sensitive, unredacted information and that the bundle is never uploaded, attached, or sent automatically.
- Wait for an active save before retrying, exiting, or closing the migration flow, and disable conflicting renderer actions while saving.
- After a renderer save succeeds, let the user open a prefilled support email, reveal the ZIP, or copy the support address without transmitting the file automatically.
- Preserve the existing successful migration path, migration ordering, transactions, and retry, skip, exit, and relaunch decisions.

Migration-specific bundle creation and user-facing behavior should remain under `src/main/data/migration/v2` and `src/renderer/windows/migrationV2`. Core preboot code should only provide the thin native-dialog integration needed before normal bootstrap; it should not gain migration business logic or require lifecycle-managed services.

Acceptance criteria:

1. The version-incompatibility screen and migration error screen offer a save-diagnostic-bundle action.
2. Existing native preboot dialogs for migration failures can offer the same save action before normal application bootstrap.
3. Every saved ZIP contains the metadata JSON; logs come from the complete save-day set, or from the complete active-run failure-day set only when the save day has none. Dates are never combined.
4. Missing or unreadable logs do not prevent saving, and bundles larger than 15 MiB are kept with a warning.
5. Every successful save states that the bundle was not uploaded automatically; renderer support actions never upload, attach, or send it.
6. Saving is single-flight and atomic. Migration-flow actions and cooperative Electron quit/close paths that can be intercepted wait for an active save to settle. Forced process termination, process crashes, and OS session termination that Electron cannot defer are outside the completion guarantee; atomic publication still prevents exposing a partial destination archive.
7. Successful and no-migration startup paths, migration decisions, and transaction behavior remain unchanged.
8. Migration-domain ownership, the thin preboot exception, privacy behavior, renderer save-dialog locale, and the observable save contract are covered by focused tests and documentation.

### Alternative Solutions

- Show only the existing error text: this does not provide a reusable artifact for support diagnosis.
- Upload diagnostics automatically: this would remove the user's opportunity to inspect sensitive logs and explicitly choose whether to share them.
- Add checkpoint persistence, database inspection, or a cross-launch attempt journal: these solve broader recovery and investigation problems but are not required to create the migration failure diagnostic bundle.
- Move the bundle implementation into `src/main/core`: this would make general application infrastructure own migration-specific behavior.

### Additional Information

- Core integration: `src/main/core/preboot/v2MigrationGate.ts` and its focused tests.
- Domain implementation: `src/main/data/migration/v2` and `src/renderer/windows/migrationV2`.

- [x] The latest `main` branch does not include the reviewed generic Renderer capabilities described below.

### Platform

macOS (the architecture is platform-agnostic)

### Version

2.0.0-dev (`main`)

### Is your feature request related to an existing issue?

Yes. #16994 defines the Topic/Agent Session-specific architecture required by the product behavior in #17025. #17144 owns the generic DataApi change-signaling and bidirectional cursor capabilities on which this Renderer infrastructure depends.

This issue tracks the three shared Renderer capabilities previously listed as §4.3–§4.5 in #17144.

### Desired Solution

#### 1. `useInfiniteQuery`

The shared Renderer hook should support:

- `hasPrevious` / `loadPrevious`;
- `hasNext` / `loadNext`;
- prepend and append behavior;
- independent directional loading state;
- existing one-directional consumers.

The current one-way page chain requires an upstream implementation change rather than a Topic/Session wrapper.

#### 2. Renderer collection reconciliation

A shared collection-level capability is needed above raw page fetching to:

- map classified change signals to mounted collection queries;
- choose revalidation versus collection reconstruction;
- prevent stale in-flight work from replacing a newer result;
- preserve compatible presentation state where possible;
- coordinate anchored and head-based reconstruction.

This capability does not encode Topic/Session product policy. Feature layers continue to own bands, groups, selection, owner fallback, and drag behavior.

#### 3. Prepend scroll anchoring

The shared remote-list or virtual-list layer should compensate scroll position when previous pages are prepended. This is a viewport concern and should not be implemented inside the DataApi endpoint or cursor codec.

#### 4. Responsibility of #16994

#16994 consumes these shared capabilities rather than defining feature-specific replacements. It continues to own Topic/Session surface migration, preferences, presentation state, and product-facing and domain-level acceptance criteria from #17025.

### Alternative Solutions

1. **Topic/Session-specific `useInfiniteQuery` wrapper** — not selected because the current one-way page chain requires an upstream implementation change.
2. **Scroll compensation in the DataApi endpoint or cursor codec** — not selected because prepend anchoring is a viewport concern.

### Additional Information

#### Dependencies

- Generic DataApi change signaling and bidirectional cursor infrastructure: #17144

#### References

- First consumer and Topic/Session-specific architecture: #16994
- Product behavior and UX acceptance: #17025
- Implementation consumer: #16998

title: [Feature]: Track retired provider models as registry tombstones
body:
## Issue Checklist

- [x] I understand that issues are for reporting problems and requesting features, not for off-topic comments, and I will provide as much detail as possible to help resolve the issue.
- [x] I have checked the pinned issues and searched through the existing open issues, closed issues, and discussions and did not find a similar suggestion.
- [x] I have provided a short and descriptive title so that developers can quickly understand the issue when browsing the issue list, rather than vague titles like "A suggestion" or "Stuck."
- [x] The latest version of Cherry Studio does not include the feature I am suggesting.

## Platform

macOS

## Version

2.0.0-dev (main / v2 refactor)

## Is your feature request related to an existing issue?

The provider registry currently represents models that are actively selectable, but it cannot retain the identity and lifecycle of models that have been retired by a provider.

This becomes observable during the v1 -> v2 migration:

- The legacy `Model` shape does not contain `presetModelId` or equivalent preset provenance.
- `ProviderModelMigrator` therefore initializes `presetModelId` to `null` and reconstructs it from the registry.
- The reconstruction currently checks the global model catalog first and returns unchanged when no base model exists.
- For a registry-only provider whose model list cannot be reliably inferred from a live endpoint, retired model IDs may no longer exist in the active catalog. Existing SQLite rows then remain with `presetModelId = null`.
- The model-management UI treats those rows as user-defined custom models, so they are neither marked stale/deprecated nor included in stale-model cleanup.

LongCat demonstrates the problem: legacy `LongCat-Flash-*` rows remain in `user_model` after the active provider catalog moves to `LongCat-2.0`, but removing the old IDs from the active catalog also removes the information needed to recognize them as retired provider models.

The runtime `Model` type already has `isDeprecated` and `replaceWith`, but the registry has no durable lifecycle source from which those fields can be derived for historical rows.

## Desired Solution

Add an explicit model lifecycle/tombstone contract to the provider registry while keeping retired models out of normal selectable model lists.

Suggested design:

1. Let exact provider-model records retain retired model IDs as non-selectable tombstones. Direct lookup and migration can still resolve them, while normal catalog listing excludes them by default.
2. Define lifecycle metadata at the correct ownership level:
   - creator model lifecycle for globally released/deprecated models;
   - provider-model lifecycle overrides when availability differs by provider or endpoint.
3. Consider using `releasedAt` and `deprecatedAt` as the source of truth, deriving `isDeprecated` at runtime. If dates are unavailable, an explicit deprecated/disabled state should remain supported.
4. Preserve `replaceWith` so a retired model can point to its supported replacement.
5. Change v1 -> v2 model enrichment to resolve an exact provider-model record before requiring a global base model, and allow a minimal preset to be synthesized from a tombstone.
6. For databases that have already migrated, recognize exact tombstones during read-time registry enrichment and project `isDeprecated`/`replaceWith` without requiring a new SQLite migration.
7. Keep custom models safe: a local row missing from a remote model list must not be considered deprecated unless an exact registry lifecycle record identifies it.

Expected behavior:

- Active catalog/list APIs return only selectable models.
- Exact registry lookup can still resolve retired model IDs.
- Historical provider-backed SQLite rows are marked deprecated even when their original `presetModelId` is null.
- Truly custom models remain unaffected.
- Providers without a reliable runtime model-list source can still express model lifecycle accurately.

## Alternative Solutions

- Hard-code retired LongCat IDs in renderer or migration code. This fixes one provider but duplicates registry knowledge and does not generalize.
- Treat every local model missing from the remote list as stale. This incorrectly deletes or deprecates legitimate custom models.
- Add a one-off SQLite migration that patches known LongCat rows. This does not solve future provider retirements and cannot recover lifecycle for other providers.
- Keep all deprecated models in the normal model catalog. This preserves identity but risks exposing retired models as selectable unless every consumer filters them correctly.

## Additional Information

Relevant code paths:

- `packages/provider-registry/data/models.json`
- `packages/provider-registry/data/provider-models.json`
- `src/main/data/migration/v2/migrators/ProviderModelMigrator.ts`
- `src/main/data/migration/v2/migrators/mappings/ProviderModelMappings.ts`
- `src/main/data/services/ModelService.ts`
- `src/renderer/pages/settings/ProviderSettings/ModelList/useProviderModelPullReconcile.ts`

title: [Privacy Concern]: Agent mode is hard-coded to Claude Code SDK — no user opt-out, no fallback for OpenAI-compatible models
body:
## Problem Statement

Cherry Studio's Agent feature is hard-coded to use `@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk` as the sole execution engine. This creates several issues:

1. **No support for OpenAI-compatible models**: Users who configure OpenAI-compatible providers (like custom self-hosted models) cannot use Agent mode, even though these models work perfectly in Chat mode. The error message is: `Claude Code returned an error result: There's an issue with the selected model...`

2. **Privacy concerns**: Claude Code is a closed-source commercial SDK that may collect user data. Users have no visibility into what data is being sent to Anthropic's servers, and no option to disable this telemetry.

3. **No user choice**: The Agent system does not allow users to opt-out of Claude Code or choose an alternative Agent engine. There's no "local-only" or "OpenAI-compatible" mode.

4. **No graceful degradation**: When Claude Code is unavailable (no API key, network issues, or model incompatibility), Agent mode completely fails instead of falling back to a simpler but functional alternative.

## Context

I understand that:
- Issue #14480, #14861, #14873, and #14918 have reported similar limitations
- PR #15177 added an internal proxy for CherryIN to support OpenAI-compatible providers through Claude Code
- The v2.0.0 milestone (#12980) plans to refactor the Agent architecture

However, these solutions all assume **Claude Code remains the mandatory execution engine** — they just add translation layers. This doesn't address:
- The fundamental lack of user choice
- Privacy concerns about sending all Agent traffic through a closed-source SDK
- The desire for a truly provider-agnostic Agent framework

## Desired Solution

I would like Cherry Studio to:

1. **Make Claude Code optional**: Allow users to explicitly choose whether to enable Claude Code-based Agent mode. If disabled, Agent functionality should gracefully degrade or use an alternative engine.

2. **Support OpenAI-compatible Agent engines**: Either:
   - Use a provider-agnostic Agent framework (like `ai-sdk`'s agent patterns) that supports both Anthropic and OpenAI tool-calling protocols
   - Or provide a clear abstraction layer where users can plug in different Agent runtimes

3. **Be transparent about data flow**: Document what data Claude Code sends to external servers, and allow privacy-conscious users to opt-out.

4. **Provide a local/privacy-first fallback**: Even if limited, a local Agent engine (perhaps using simple ReAct patterns with any model) would be preferable to no Agent functionality at all for users who cannot or don't want to use Claude Code.

## Alternative Workarounds

Currently, the only workaround is:
- Use Chat mode instead of Agent mode (loses tool orchestration, planning, and multi-turn capabilities)
- Run an external proxy like `cc-switch` or `cc-nim` (fragile, adds complexity, not user-friendly)

## Additional Context

This is not just a "feature request" — it's about **user agency and privacy**. Tightly coupling Agent mode to a single closed-source SDK:
- Excludes users who cannot access Anthropic's API (geographic, financial, or compliance reasons)
- Creates a single point of failure
- Prevents community contributions to the Agent runtime
- Goes against the open-source spirit of Cherry Studio

I'm happy to contribute to a more modular Agent architecture if the maintainers are open to this direction.

The exact version was not present in the supplied log. ### Platform Windows ### Version Unknown (log captured from a Windows build on 2026-07-21) ### Bug Description During an Agent run, the task UI can remain indefinitely on an `in_progress` item after the runtime has already failed. In a related failure mode, the assistant message is created but contains no displayable parts, so the conversation shows an empty Agent reply. The reporter confirmed that only one Agent task was running, so concurrent Agent execution is not a direct trigger. The exact page action that triggers the runtime failure is still intermittent and was not captured, but the terminal-state loss is visible in both screenshots and the logs. Log analysis indicates the following sequence: 1. The Agent runtime or query loop fails. 2. A completion result may arrive without an active turn and is dropped. 3. The message/task persistence path can retain an `in_progress` task event or a terminal assistant message without an error part. 4. The renderer therefore shows a permanent spinner or an empty reply instead of a terminal error. The repeated `Failed to persist root span ai.turn` warning appears to be a secondary observability failure. Provider/network errors are also present in the log, but they should not leave the UI in a non-terminal state regardless of their root cause. ### Steps To Reproduce The exact upstream runtime trigger is intermittent. The observed reproduction path is: 1. Start a single Agent task that produces a multi-step task list. 2. Let the Agent runtime fail or disconnect before the active step completes. 3. Return to the task status view and observe that the active task can remain spinning indefinitely. 4. In the affected conversation, send another short message and observe that an assistant row can be created with no visible response content. ### Expected Behavior When the runtime errors, disconnects, or finishes without displayable assistant content: - every active Agent task should transition to a terminal error state; - the assistant message should render a visible error fallback rather than an empty row; - any AI diagnosis attached to the error should persist through the Agent-session message API; - the underlying provider/runtime error should remain available for diagnosis. ### Relevant Log Output ```shell 2026-07-21 20:32:16 WARN Received a result message with no active turn; dropping turn-complete 2026-07-21 20:32:16 ERROR Claude Code query loop failed 2026-07-21 20:32:16 ERROR Agent runtime connection ended without an active turn 2026-07-21 20:33:30 ERROR Claude Code query loop failed subtype=error_during_execution exitCode=1 2026-07-21 20:33:30 ERROR Execution loop error Repeated secondary warning: WARN Failed to persist root span ai.turn TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading '0') at convertSpanToSpanEntity at AiStreamManager.onExecutionError / onExecutionDone ``` Session IDs, local usernames, response cookies, and request identifiers were removed from this excerpt. ### Additional Context - The reporter explicitly confirmed only one Agent task was running. - Original screenshots will be attached to this issue after creation. - Proposed fix: #17264 - The fix terminalizes interrupted task events in persistence, adds a renderer fallback for terminal empty/error messages, and scopes Agent diagnosis persistence by both session ID and message ID.

body:

- [x] I've filled in short, clear headings so that developers can quickly identify a rough idea of what to expect when flipping through the list of issues. And not "a suggestion", "stuck", etc.
- [x] I've confirmed that I am using the latest version of Cherry Studio.

### Platform

macOS

### Version

2.0.0-dev (`main`, migrating a v1.9.12 profile)

### Bug Description

Migrating a v1 profile with a large Dexie `message_blocks` table can fail before the migration engine starts with `RangeError: Invalid string length`.

The legacy exporter loads an entire table with `toArray()` and serializes it into one JSON string. When the serialized table exceeds V8's maximum string length, `JSON.stringify()` throws. Retrying does not help because every attempt reconstructs the same oversized string.

This was originally observed in a migration run captured on July 13 and was reproduced against `main` with an isolated v1 profile containing 513 message blocks of 1 MiB each (537,919,488 content characters in total).

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Prepare a v1.9.12 profile whose Dexie `message_blocks` data serializes to more than the V8 single-string limit.
2. Start the V2 data migration wizard.
3. Click **Start Migration**.
4. Observe that `topics`, `files`, and `knowledge_notes` export successfully.
5. Observe that migration fails while exporting `message_blocks` with `Invalid string length`.

Deterministic fixture used for verification:

- 1 topic
- 513 messages
- 513 message blocks
- 1,048,576 content characters per block
- 537,919,488 content characters total

### Expected Behavior

Dexie tables should be exported with bounded memory usage, migration should complete successfully regardless of aggregate table size, and every source record and message-block payload should be preserved without truncation, duplication, missing IDs, broken parent links, or foreign-key violations.

### Relevant Log Output

```shell
[MigrationIpcHandler] Export file written { tableName: 'topics', ... }
[MigrationIpcHandler] Export file written { tableName: 'files', ... }
[MigrationIpcHandler] Export file written { tableName: 'knowledge_notes', ... }
[MigrationV2::MigrationApp] Failed to start migration [Error: Invalid string length]
RangeError: Invalid string length
    at JSON.stringify (<anonymous>)
    at DexieExporter.exportAll (...)
```

### Additional Context

PR #17273 fixes the root cause by iterating Dexie records in primary-key pages, serializing one record at a time, and streaming bounded JSON chunks through IPC while preserving the existing JSON-array file format.

Manual before/after verification with the deterministic fixture produced these results:

- Before: migration consistently failed with `Invalid string length`.
- After: 15/15 migrators completed in 21.905 seconds.
- Source/target business messages: 513/513.
- Source/resolved message blocks: 513/513; missing blocks: 0.
- Source/target message content characters: 537,919,488/537,919,488.
- Missing expected IDs, broken parent links, foreign-key violations, and skipped messages: all 0.
- Relaunch after completion reported `needsMigration: false` and successfully read the migrated topic through DataApi.

The retry hardening in #16813 does not remove this root cause because the exception occurs while creating the full-table export string before the migration engine can process the data.

title: [Feature]: Add a lean Renderer-only migration diagnostic bundle
body:
### Issue Checklist

- [x] I understand that issues are for reporting problems and requesting features, not for off-topic comments, and I will provide as much detail as possible to help resolve the issue.
- [x] I have checked the pinned issues and searched through the existing [open issues](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/issues), [closed issues](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20state%3Aclosed), and [discussions](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/discussions) and did not find a similar suggestion.
- [x] I have provided a short and descriptive title so that developers can quickly understand the issue when browsing the issue list, rather than vague titles like "A suggestion" or "Stuck."
- [x] The latest version of Cherry Studio does not include the feature I am suggesting.

### Platform

macOS

### Version

2.0.0-dev (`main`)

### Is your feature request related to an existing issue?

When v1-to-v2 migration fails or the stored data version is incompatible, the existing Renderer pages explain the failure and recovery choices but do not provide a small, user-controlled support artifact. Users need a focused way to save relevant local diagnostics without changing the existing migration decisions or automatically transmitting sensitive data.

### Desired Solution

Add a lean diagnostic-bundle action only to the migration error and version-incompatible Renderer pages.

The flow should:

- Warn that application logs may contain file paths, error stacks, user content, or credentials and must not be shared publicly or outside the Cherry Studio support team.
- Open a localized save dialog only after the user clicks the action, and dynamically load the ZIP builder only after a destination is confirmed.
- Save an atomic ZIP containing exact minimal system metadata and a stable snapshot of regular application logs for one date.
- Prefer the failure panel's mount-time local date; when that date has no eligible logs, fall back to the latest eligible on-disk date without combining dates.
- Verify each log with `lstat` / `open` / `fstat`, read a fixed byte snapshot from the opened handle, close all handles, and prevent the destination from overwriting a source log.
- Rebuild a metadata-only ZIP when the complete log snapshot cannot be included, and clearly tell the user that the saved bundle contains only system information.
- State that successful saves remain local and are never uploaded automatically.
- Show exactly two post-save actions: reveal the saved file and copy `support@cherry-ai.com`.
- Validate the sender for the two new pre-bootstrap migration IPC commands while preserving the existing migration lifecycle and decisions.

Acceptance criteria:

1. Save diagnostics is available only on migration error and version-incompatible Renderer pages.
2. The ZIP contains only `migration-diagnostics.json` plus one eligible date's `app.YYYY-MM-DD.log[.N]` files.
3. The JSON contains application version, platform, architecture, OS release, and migration stage; it contains no error details, absolute paths, run identity, process identity, or retry guidance.
4. Append and rotation races cannot change the opened fixed-length snapshot. Any open, identity, short-read, or stream failure results in a metadata-only ZIP rather than a partial log set.
5. Saving is atomic, and the selected destination cannot be the same physical file as a source log.
6. The UI distinguishes bundles with logs from metadata-only bundles and always states that nothing was uploaded automatically.
7. The only follow-up actions reveal the file and copy the support email; there is no upload, attachment, `mailto:`, or prefilled email.
8. There is no native preboot save entry, save-in-flight quit barrier, 15 MiB warning, or change to `MigrationEngine`, `MigrationPaths`, migrators, exporters, or `MigrationWindowManager`.
9. Focused tests cover cross-midnight date selection, stable snapshots, atomic fallback, sender validation, localized dialog payloads, UI isolation, and copy/reveal feedback.

### Alternative Solutions

- Add native preboot diagnostics, exit coordination, structured failure identity, and additional support actions: rejected because they materially broaden this focused Renderer-only flow.
- Upload or attach diagnostics automatically: rejected because users must retain control over sensitive, unredacted application logs.
- Show only existing error text: insufficient because support still lacks a reusable artifact selected and saved by the user.
- Add a public diagnostics framework or extend `MigrationPaths` with application logs: rejected because the bundle is migration-specific and logger output is not v1/v2 migration source data.

### Additional Information

- The requested behavior is cross-platform; macOS records the development environment required by the issue form.
- Main implementation area: `src/main/data/migration/v2`.
- Renderer implementation area: `src/renderer/windows/migrationV2`.
- The implementation PR should close this issue directly.

## Platform

## Version

`main@5b780731f91fb06191cdf9ec31a8280076a5633c`

## Bug Description

`src/renderer/pages/paintings/hooks/usePaintingHistory.ts` re-runs `recordsToPaintingDataList(records)` for the complete loaded history whenever SWR replaces the `pages` array. Painting create and update mutations invalidate `/paintings`, so unchanged history records are repeatedly rehydrated after normal generation updates.

Each record hydration reads every referenced file entry through DataApi and resolves output paths through IPC. With one loaded page of 30 records containing one output each, a generation's two persistence updates can repeat roughly 60 file queries and 60 path IPC calls. The cost grows with the number of loaded pages.

This violates the Vercel `client-swr-dedup` and `js-cache-function-results` rules by repeating expensive client-side work for unchanged records.

## Steps To Reproduce

1. Load a painting history page containing persisted output files.
2. Trigger a painting generation, which persists the pending and completed states and invalidates `/paintings`.
3. Trace `recordToPaintingData`, file-entry DataApi requests, or physical-path IPC calls.
4. Observe that every previously loaded record is rehydrated after each refresh, even when only one record changed.

## Expected Behavior

Painting history should reuse hydrated data for unchanged records and hydrate only new or changed records while preserving query order and stale-effect cancellation.

## Relevant Log Output

```shell
N/A
```

## Additional Context

Minimal expected fix: keep a hook-local cache keyed by a deterministic hydration fingerprint containing the persisted fields consumed by the mapper and the ordered input/output file IDs. Do not key only by `updatedAt`, because files-only writes can replace file refs without updating the painting row. Prune removed records and add focused tests for unchanged revalidation, files-only changes, ordering/deletion, and obsolete async hydration.

This is separate from #17289, which only parallelizes the independent input/output batches within one record; it does not prevent full-list rehydration.
