title: [Bug]: Flaky test — JobManager cancel-timeout smoke test rides on a 400ms scheduling margin
body:
### Issue Checklist

- [x] I understand that issues are for feedback and problem solving, not for complaining in the comment section, and will provide as much information as possible to help solve the problem.
- [x] My issue is not listed in the FAQ.
- [x] I've looked at pinned issues and searched existing Open/Closed Issues and Discussions, no similar issue or discussion was found.
- [x] I've filled in short, clear headings so that developers can quickly identify a rough idea of what to expect when flipping through the list of issues.
- [x] I've confirmed that I am using the latest version of Cherry Studio.

### Platform

macOS

### Version

v2.0.0-rc.3

### Bug Description

**This is a test defect, not a `JobManager` defect.** `JobManager` behaves correctly in both outcomes the test can observe; the test just cannot tell them apart reliably on a loaded runner.

`src/main/core/job/__tests__/JobManager.smoke.test.ts` → *"reports timed-out when the handler ignores the abort past cancelTimeoutMs"* fails intermittently in the `general-test` job:

```
AssertionError: expected { outcome: 'cancelled' } to deeply equal { outcome: 'timed-out' }
```

The test means to assert the force-finalize-after-timeout path. What it actually pins is a race between two wall-clock timers:

| | value |
| --- | --- |
| `dummy.stubborn` handler sleep (un-abortable) | 600 ms |
| `cancelTimeoutMs` | 200 ms |
| test's own wait before calling `cancel()` | 50 ms |

`cancel()` has to be issued **within 400 ms** of the handler entering its sleep. Later than that, the remaining sleep is shorter than the 200 ms grace window, so the handler settles *inside* the window and `JobManager` correctly reports `cancelled` instead of `timed-out` — and the assertion fails.

400 ms of scheduling slack is not a lot on this runner. The run linked below executed 655 test files / 9596 tests in 229 s with `collect 186 s`, i.e. under heavy parallel load. A `setTimeout(…, 50)` landing 400 ms late there is unremarkable.

### Steps To Reproduce

The flake itself is load-dependent, but the mechanism reproduces deterministically:

1. In `src/main/core/job/__tests__/JobManager.smoke.test.ts`, in the test *"reports timed-out when the handler ignores the abort past cancelTimeoutMs"*, change the pre-cancel wait from `setTimeout(r, 50)` to `setTimeout(r, 450)` — this simulates a runner that scheduled the test process 400 ms late.
2. `pnpm vitest run --project main src/main/core/job/__tests__/JobManager.smoke.test.ts -t "reports timed-out"`
3. It fails with exactly the CI assertion — same expected/received values.
4. Restore the `50`, and it passes.

Observed in CI on the branch `eurfelux/feat/file-manager-gc` (PR #16727), whose diff against `main` is empty under `src/main/core/job/` — the test file and `JobManager` are byte-identical to `main` there, so the failure is not branch-specific:
https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/actions/runs/30643555304/job/91199356656

### Expected Behavior

The test should assert `JobManager`'s cancel-timeout behaviour independently of how promptly the test process gets scheduled — a slow runner should not be able to turn "handler ignored the abort" into "handler observed the abort".

### Relevant Log Output

```shell
 FAIL  main src/main/core/job/__tests__/JobManager.smoke.test.ts > JobManager smoke (dummy.echo) > reports timed-out when the handler ignores the abort past cancelTimeoutMs
AssertionError: expected { outcome: 'cancelled' } to deeply equal { outcome: 'timed-out' }

- Expected
+ Received

  {
-   "outcome": "timed-out",
+   "outcome": "cancelled",
  }

 ❯ src/main/core/job/__tests__/JobManager.smoke.test.ts:256:20

 Test Files  1 failed | 655 passed | 2 skipped (658)
      Tests  1 failed | 9484 passed | 111 skipped (9596)
   Duration  229.24s (transform 10.97s, setup 3.86s, collect 186.61s, tests 388.85s, environment 90ms, prepare 33.82s)
```

### Additional Context

Two ways to fix it, in increasing order of how much they actually buy:

1. **Widen the margin.** Give `dummy.stubborn` a much longer sleep relative to `cancelTimeoutMs` (e.g. 3000 ms vs 200 ms). Cheapest change, and it makes the flake very unlikely — but it is still a wall-clock bet, just a longer-odds one, and it adds real seconds to the suite.
2. **Remove the wall-clock dependence.** Have the handler block on a promise the test resolves explicitly, instead of on a duration. "The handler has not yet observed the abort" then becomes a state the test *controls* rather than an interval it *hopes for*, and the assertion holds no matter how the runner schedules anything. This is the shape worth having, since the property under test is ordering, not timing.

Note that the neighbouring `cancels an in-flight job (handler observes abort → outcome cancelled)` test has the same wall-clock shape. It is much less exposed — `makeEchoHandler` sets `cancelTimeoutMs: 2000` and does observe the abort, so its margin is the handler's full 500 ms sleep, and its failure mode would be the job completing before `cancel()` lands (`not-cancellable`) rather than a flipped outcome. Worth converting alongside if someone takes option 2, but it is not what is failing today.

title: [Feature]: Store note images inside the notes folder, not in Cherry's managed file storage
body:
### Issue Checklist

- [x] I understand that issues are for reporting problems and requesting features, not for off-topic comments, and I will provide as much detail as possible to help resolve the issue.
- [x] I have checked the pinned issues and searched through the existing open issues, closed issues, and discussions and did not find a similar suggestion.
- [x] I have provided a short and descriptive title so that developers can quickly understand the issue when browsing the issue list.
- [x] The latest version of Cherry Studio does not include the feature I am suggesting.

### Platform

macOS

### Version

v2.0.0-rc.3

### Is your feature request related to an existing issue?

Images put into a note do not travel with the note. Today there are two entry points and they behave differently — neither stores the image inside the notes tree:

| entry point | what ends up in the `.md` |
| --- | --- |
| paste (`useRichEditor.ts` → `handleImagePaste`) | `![alt](file:///Users/me/Library/.../Data/Files/{uuid}.png)` — an absolute path into Cherry's managed storage |
| toolbar image button (`RichEditor/components/ImageUploader.tsx`) | a base64 `data:` URI inlined into the text |

The notes root is deliberately user-choosable (`feature.notes.path`, folder picker in `NotesSettings.tsx`), and notes themselves are plain `.md` files in it. So the folder is the unit users move, sync, back up and open with other tools — and the paste path leaves the images behind:

1. **Point notes at a synced/Obsidian folder** — the whole reason external roots are supported — open it on another machine or in another editor, and every pasted image is a broken link.
2. **The absolute path embeds the OS user's home directory.** A reinstall, a new machine, or a different OS account breaks every link even without moving anything.
3. **Sharing a single `.md` file** hands the recipient links into your private app storage.
4. **The bytes cannot be reclaimed.** The reference is a substring of user-owned markdown, so nothing in the app is notified when it is removed. #16727 therefore pins these entries with `cleanupPolicy: 'manual'` — correct, but it means paste-then-undo leaks the file permanently.

The base64 path avoids 1–3, but inlines the payload into the note: a 2 MB screenshot becomes ~2.7 MB of base64 sitting in the text, which is slow to load, diff and edit, and unpleasant in any other editor.

### Desired Solution

Do what note apps do: **write the image into the notes tree and reference it relatively.**

- Obsidian — configurable attachment folder (vault root / same folder as the note / a named subfolder)
- Typora — `${filename}.assets/` next to the note, or a global folder, with "copy image to folder" on paste
- Logseq — `assets/`

Concretely: on paste, write the bytes to something like `<notesRoot>/assets/{name}-{shorthash}.{ext}` and insert `![alt](assets/{name}-{shorthash}.png)`. A relative link survives moving, syncing and sharing the folder, because the target moves with it.

The valuable side effect for the file subsystem: **these images stop being `file_entry` rows at all.** They become ordinary files in the user's own tree, exactly like the `.md` files beside them. That takes them out of the GC's scope entirely, removes the `manual` special case, and settles the "should there be a `note_file_ref` table?" question by making it moot.

(For the record on that table, since it is the obvious first idea: it cannot work here. A ref row could never be released soundly — deleting the image from the note text never reaches the app, and copying the markdown line into a second note creates a real reference the table never observed. Releasing on note deletion would then delete a file another note still uses. A table that can only ever accumulate is a more expensive `manual`.)

### Alternative Solutions

- **Keep FileManager, but write a relative link.** Not possible — managed storage lives under `userData`, outside the notes tree, so no relative path from a note reaches it.
- **Keep FileManager, add a `note_file_ref` table and GC.** Unsound, see above.
- **Inline base64 everywhere** (make paste behave like the toolbar button). Portable and simple, but the size cost is real and it makes the `.md` hostile to every other tool.
- **Per-note `<note>.assets/` vs one shared `assets/`.** A genuine trade-off worth deciding rather than defaulting: a per-note folder makes cleanup on note deletion trivial; a shared folder dedups better and keeps the tree flatter. Obsidian and Typora both ship the choice as a setting.

### Additional Information

Open questions this issue should settle before implementation:

- **Migration.** Existing notes already carry `file://.../Data/Files/...` links. Either leave them alone and keep those entries pinned (status quo, zero risk), or rewrite the links and copy the bytes into the notes tree on first open. This is the decision that determines how large the change is.
- **Changing the notes root.** Relative links keep working when the assets folder lives inside the tree — another argument for that layout over anything anchored elsewhere.
- **Unify the two entry points.** Paste and the toolbar button should produce the same thing once a layout is chosen.
- **Cleanup on note deletion.** Per-note folder: delete alongside. Shared folder: needs a scan of the notes tree — cheap, and it reads the actual source of truth rather than a shadow index.
- **Scope.** `useRichEditor`'s paste path is notes-only; the chat composer uses `useRichTextEditorKernel` and a separate attachment flow, so this does not touch chat.

Context: raised while reviewing #16727 (file-manager GC), which keeps `cleanupPolicy: 'manual'` for note images on purpose — that preserves today's behaviour exactly and is not affected by whatever is decided here.

title: [Bug]: RC users' migrated file entries remain permanently manual after cleanup policy rollout
body:
## Issue Checklist

- [x] I understand that issues are for feedback and problem solving, not for complaining in the comment section, and will provide as much information as possible to help solve the problem.
- [x] My issue is not listed in the [FAQ](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/issues/3881).
- [x] I've looked at **pinned issues** and searched for existing [Open Issues](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/issues), [Closed Issues](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20state%3Aclosed), and [Discussions](https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/discussions), no similar issue or discussion was found.
- [x] I've filled in short, clear headings so that developers can quickly identify a rough idea of what to expect when flipping through the list of issues. And not "a suggestion", "stuck", etc.
- [x] I've confirmed that I am using the latest version of Cherry Studio.

## Platform

macOS

## Version

v2.0.0-rc.1 -> v2.0.0-rc.3 / PR #16727 (`d93a4765`)

## Bug Description

PR #16727 introduces `file_entry.cleanup_policy` and classifies newly migrated, reference-backed files as `delete_when_unreferenced`. Part of that classification lives in the one-shot v1-to-v2 domain migrators (`ChatMigrator`, `PaintingMigrator`, and the corresponding fresh-migration creation paths).

Users who completed the v1-to-v2 migration on v2.0.0-rc.1 already have `app_state.key = 'migration_v2_status'` set to `completed`. When they upgrade to rc.3 or a build containing #16727:

1. The appended Drizzle schema migrations run normally.
2. Existing `file_entry` rows receive the database default `cleanup_policy = 'manual'`.
3. `MigrationEngine.needsMigration()` returns false because the one-shot migration is already completed.
4. The updated domain migrators therefore do not run, so their cleanup-policy classification never reaches existing rows.

This does not prevent startup and does not delete data. It creates release-dependent GC behavior: reference-backed files migrated on rc.1 remain permanently `manual`, even after their references are removed, while equivalent files first migrated or created on the newer build become `delete_when_unreferenced` and are reclaimable.

## Steps To Reproduce

1. Start from v2.0.0-rc.1 and complete the v1-to-v2 migration with at least one referenced file, such as a chat attachment, painting file, provider logo, or mini-app logo.
2. Confirm that `app_state.key = 'migration_v2_status'` is `completed` and that the associated `file_entry` and ref-table rows exist.
3. Upgrade directly to v2.0.0-rc.3 or a build containing PR #16727.
4. Let startup apply all pending schema migrations.
5. Query the migrated rows and their references, for example:

   ```sql
   SELECT fe.id, fe.cleanup_policy, cmfr.source_id
   FROM file_entry AS fe
   JOIN chat_message_file_ref AS cmfr ON cmfr.file_entry_id = fe.id;
   ```

6. Observe that the existing rows have `cleanup_policy = 'manual'`. The updated v1-to-v2 migrators are skipped because migration status is already `completed`.

## Expected Behavior

Existing RC databases should receive a deliberate, versioned compatibility treatment for file cleanup policy. Rows whose known owning/ref-table semantics require automatic reclamation should be conservatively backfilled to `delete_when_unreferenced` without blindly reclassifying arbitrary `file_entry` rows.

Equivalent files should not have different lifetime behavior solely based on which RC first performed the v1-to-v2 migration.

## Relevant Log Output

```shell
Direct rc.1 -> PR-head migration harness:

journal: 1785247785125 -> 1785308910164 -> 1785476603915 -> 1785514531244
file_entry.cleanup_policy: manual
existing provider_logo_file_ref: preserved
foreign_key_check: []
integrity_check: ok
```

## Additional Context

- PR: #16727
- The rc.1 and rc.3 releases use the same `Data/cherrystudio.sqlite` path and the same consolidated migration chain, so this is not the earlier beta database relocation issue.
- rc.3 includes #17569, which correctly preserves child ref rows across table-recreate migrations. That runner fix prevents data loss but does not perform cleanup-policy classification.
- `markEntriesAutoCleanup()` is called from the one-shot chat/painting migration paths. It cannot affect users whose `migration_v2_status` was already completed before #16727.
- New files created after the upgrade receive the current runtime policy; the incompatibility is limited to historical rows.
- Related issues #17169 and #17387 concern missing ref registration on specific live creation/persistence paths and do not cover this RC upgrade/backfill gap.
